sourceRange.text: 六月甲戌，任城王彰薨于京都。甲申，太尉賈詡薨。太白晝見。是月大雨，伊、洛溢流，殺人民，壞廬宅。《魏書》曰：七月乙未，大軍當出，使太常以特牛一告祠于郊。臣松之按：魏郊祀奏中，尚書盧毓議祀厲殃事云：「具犧牲祭器，如前後師出告郊之禮。」如此，則魏氏出師，皆告郊也。秋八月丁卯，以廷尉鍾繇爲太尉。《魏書》曰：有司奏改漢氏宗廟安世樂曰正世樂，嘉至樂曰迎靈樂，武德樂曰武頌樂，昭容樂曰昭業樂，雲翹舞曰鳳翔舞，育命舞曰靈應舞，武德舞曰武頌舞，文昭舞曰大昭舞，五行舞曰大武舞。辛未，校獵于熒陽，遂東巡。論征孫權功，諸將已下進爵增戶各有差。九月甲辰，行幸許昌宮。《魏書》曰：十二月丙寅，賜山陽公夫人湯沐邑，公女曼爲長樂郡公主，食邑各五百戶。是冬，甘露降芳林園。臣松之按：芳林園即今華林園，齊王芳即位，改爲華林。

manualTranslations.literal: On the jiashen day, Grand Commandant Jia Xu died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Grand Commandant Jia Xu died.

manualTranslations.literal: Venus was seen in the daytime.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Venus appeared in daylight.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月大雨，伊、洛溢流，殺人民，壞廬宅。
manualTranslations.literal: That month there was heavy rain; the Yi and Luo rivers overflowed, killing people and destroying houses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month torrential rains made the Yi and Luo rivers overflow, killing people and destroying dwellings.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：七月乙未，大軍當出，使太常以特牛一告祠于郊。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book says: In the seventh month, on the yiwei day, the great army was about to march out; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices was sent to announce the sacrifice at the suburban altar with one special ox.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that in the seventh month, on yiwei day, as the main army prepared to march, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices was dispatched to announce the suburban sacrifice with a special ox.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之按：魏郊祀奏中，尚書盧毓議祀厲殃事云：「具犧牲祭器，如前後師出告郊之禮。」
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Songzhi remarks: In the Wei memorial on suburban sacrifices, Minister Lu Yu, debating offerings to avert calamity, said: "Prepare the sacrificial victims and vessels according to the rite of announcing the suburban altar before and after armies march out."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that in a Wei memorial on suburban rites Minister Lu Yu, discussing offerings to ward off disaster, wrote: "Prepare victims and vessels as in the rite of announcing the suburban altar whenever armies march out, before and after."

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，則魏氏出師，皆告郊也。
manualTranslations.literal: From this it follows that whenever Wei dispatched an army, it always announced the sacrifice at the suburban altar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this it appears that every Wei campaign was preceded and followed by announcement at the suburban altar.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋八月丁卯，以廷尉鍾繇爲太尉。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on dingmao day, Court Administrator Zhong Yao was made Grand Commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：有司奏改漢氏宗廟安世樂曰正世樂，嘉至樂曰迎靈樂，武德樂曰武頌樂，昭容樂曰昭業樂，雲翹舞曰鳳翔舞，育命舞曰靈應舞，武德舞曰武頌舞，文昭舞曰大昭舞，五行舞曰大武舞。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book says: the relevant offices memorialized changing Han ancestral temple music—Anshi music to Zhengshi music, Jiazhi music to Yingling music, Wude music to Wusong music, Zhaorong music to Zhaoye music, Yunqiao dance to Fengxiang dance, Yuming dance to Lingying dance, Wude dance to Wusong dance, Wenzhao dance to Dazhao dance, and Wuxing dance to Dawu dance.

manualTranslations.zh: 辛未，校獵于熒陽，遂東巡。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: On xinwei day he reviewed the hunt at Xingyang and then toured east.

manualTranslations.zh: 論征孫權功，諸將已下進爵增戶各有差。

sourceRange.text: 四年春正月，詔曰：「喪亂以來，兵革未戢，天下之人，互相殘殺。今海內初定，敢有私復讎者皆族之。」築南巡臺于宛。三月丙申，行自宛還洛陽宮。癸卯，月犯心中央大星。《魏書》載丙午詔曰：「孫權殘害民物，朕以寇不可長，故分命猛將三道並征。今征東諸軍與權黨呂範等水戰，則斬首四萬，獲船萬艘。大司馬據守濡須，其所禽獲亦以萬數。中軍、征南攻圍江陵，左將軍張郃等舳艫直渡，擊其南渚，賊赴水溺死者數千人，又爲地道攻城，城中外雀鼠不得出入，此几上肉耳！而賊中癘氣疾病，夾江塗地，恐相染污。昔周武伐殷，旋師孟津，漢祖征隗嚻，還軍高平，皆知天時而度賊情也。且成湯解三面之網，天下歸仁。今開江陵之圍，以緩成死之禽。且休力役，罷省繇戍，畜養士民，咸使安息。」丁未，大司馬曹仁薨。是月大疫。

manualTranslations.zh: 四年春正月，詔曰：「喪亂以來，兵革未戢，天下之人，互相殘殺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year, first month of spring, an edict said: "Since the disorders of war, arms have not been laid down, and the people of the realm have slaughtered one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the first month of spring, an edict declared: "Since the age of mourning and chaos arms have never been stilled, and the people of the realm have butchered one another.

manualTranslations.zh: 今海內初定，敢有私復讎者皆族之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now that the realm is newly settled, anyone who dares to take private revenge shall be executed together with his whole clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is newly pacified, whoever dares take private revenge shall be executed to the third degree of kin."

manualTranslations.zh: 築南巡臺于宛。
manualTranslations.literal: The Southern Tour Terrace was built at Wan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Southern Tour Terrace was built at Wan.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月丙申，行自宛還洛陽宮。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month, on the bingchen day, he traveled from Wan back to Luoyang Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingchen day, he returned from Wan to Luoyang Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 癸卯，月犯心中央大星。
manualTranslations.literal: On the guimao day, the moon crossed the central major star of the Heart constellation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao day the moon occulted the central major star of the Heart asterism.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》載丙午詔曰：「孫權殘害民物，朕以寇不可長，故分命猛將三道並征。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book records a bingwu edict: "Sun Quan harms the people; because the banditry cannot be allowed to grow, I have divided my orders among fierce generals to campaign together along three routes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Book preserves a bingwu edict: "Sun Quan ravages the people. Because the enemy must not be indulged, I have ordered fierce generals to advance together on three routes.

manualTranslations.zh: 今征東諸軍與權黨呂範等水戰，則斬首四萬，獲船萬艘。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the armies campaigning east have fought a naval battle with Sun Quan's faction, Lü Fan and others, and beheaded forty thousand and captured ten thousand ships.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eastern armies have already fought Lü Fan and other Sun Quan partisans on the water, beheading forty thousand and taking ten thousand ships.

manualTranslations.zh: 大司馬據守濡須，其所禽獲亦以萬數。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Marshal holding Ruxu has also taken captives numbering in the tens of thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal holding Ruxu has likewise taken prisoners by the ten thousand.

manualTranslations.zh: 中軍、征南攻圍江陵，左將軍張郃等舳艫直渡，擊其南渚，賊赴水溺死者數千人，又爲地道攻城，城中外雀鼠不得出入，此几上肉耳！
manualTranslations.literal: The Central Army and South Campaign forces besieged Jiangling; Left General Zhang He and others crossed directly with warships, striking their southern ford; enemy troops who fled into the water drowned by the thousands; they also dug underground passages to assault the walls—inside and outside the city not even sparrows or mice could come and go—this was meat on the chopping block!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Central Army and the southern expeditionary force besieged Jiangling. Left General Zhang He and others crossed straight over with warships and struck the southern ford; thousands of the enemy drowned fleeing into the water. They also tunneled under the walls until not even sparrows or mice could enter or leave the city—it was meat on the platter!

manualTranslations.zh: 而賊中癘氣疾病，夾江塗地，恐相染污。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet plague and disease spread among the enemy; along both banks of the river bodies littered the ground, and there was fear of mutual contagion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet plague and sickness raged among the enemy; corpses lined both banks of the river, and there was fear of contagion.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔周武伐殷，旋師孟津，漢祖征隗嚻，還軍高平，皆知天時而度賊情也。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly King Wu of Zhou attacked Yin and turned his army back at Mengjin; Emperor Gaozu of Han campaigned against Kui Xiao and returned his army to Gaoping—both knew the heavenly seasons and gauged the enemy's condition.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly King Wu of Zhou turned back at Mengjin after attacking Yin, and Emperor Gaozu withdrew to Gaoping after campaigning against Kui Xiao—both read the seasons of heaven and measured the enemy's state.

manualTranslations.zh: 且成湯解三面之網，天下歸仁。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, Cheng Tang loosened the net on three sides, and the realm submitted to his benevolence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover Cheng Tang opened his net on three sides, and the realm submitted to his humanity.

manualTranslations.zh: 今開江陵之圍，以緩成死之禽。
manualTranslations.literal: Now lift the siege of Jiangling to loosen the grip on birds already as good as dead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now raise the siege of Jiangling and loosen the noose on birds already as good as dead.

manualTranslations.zh: 且休力役，罷省繇戍，畜養士民，咸使安息。」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover cease forced labor, reduce corvée and garrison service, nurture soldiers and civilians, and let all rest in peace."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cease forced labor, reduce corvée and frontier garrison duty, restore soldiers and civilians, and let all rest in peace."

manualTranslations.zh: 丁未，大司馬曹仁薨。
manualTranslations.literal: On the dingwei day, Grand Marshal Cao Ren died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Grand Marshal Cao Ren died.

manualTranslations.zh: 是月大疫。
manualTranslations.literal: That month there was a great epidemic.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That month a great epidemic broke out.

sourceRange.text: 漢帝以衆望在魏，乃召羣公卿士，袁宏《漢紀》載漢帝詔曰：「朕在位三十有二載，遭天下蕩覆，幸賴祖宗之靈，危而復存。然仰瞻天文，俯察民心，炎精之數旣終，行運在乎曹氏。是以前王旣樹神武之績，今王又光曜明德以應其期，是歷數昭明，信可知矣。夫大道之行，天下爲公，選賢與能，故唐堯不私於厥子，而名播於無窮。朕羨而慕焉，今其追踵堯典，禪位于魏王。」告祠高廟。使兼御史大夫張音持節奉璽綬禪位，冊曰：「咨爾魏王：昔者帝堯禪位于虞舜，舜亦以命禹，天命不于常，惟歸有德。漢道陵遲，世失其序，降及朕躬，大亂茲昏，羣兇肆逆，宇內顛覆。賴武王神武，拯茲難于四方，惟清區夏，以保綏我宗廟，豈予一人獲乂，俾九服實受其賜。今王欽承前緒，光于乃德，恢文武之大業，昭爾考之弘烈。皇靈降瑞，人神告徵，誕惟亮采，師錫朕命，僉曰爾度克恊于虞舜，用率我唐典，敬遜爾位。於戲！天之歷數在爾躬，允執其中，天祿永終；君其祗順大禮，饗茲萬國，以肅承天命。」乃爲壇於繁陽。庚午，王升壇即阼，百官陪位。事訖，降壇，視燎成禮而反。改延康爲黃初，大赦。黃初元年十一月癸酉，以河內之山陽邑萬戶奉漢帝爲山陽公，行漢正朔，以天子之禮郊祭，上書不稱臣，京都有事于太廟，致胙；封公之四子爲列侯。追尊皇祖太王曰太皇帝，考武王曰武皇帝，尊王太后曰皇太后。賜男子爵人一級，爲父後及孝悌力田人二級。以漢諸侯王爲崇德侯，列侯爲關中侯。以潁陰之繁陽亭爲繁昌縣。封爵增位各有差。改相國爲司徒，御史大夫爲司空，奉常爲太常，郎中令爲光祿勳，大理爲廷尉，大農爲大司農。郡國縣邑，多所改易。更授匈奴南單于呼廚泉魏璽綬，賜青蓋車、乘輿、寶劔、玉玦。十二月，初營洛陽宮，戊午幸洛陽。臣松之案：諸書記是時帝居北宮，以建始殿朝羣臣，門曰承明，陳思王植詩曰「謁帝承明廬」是也。至明帝時，始於漢南宮崇德殿處起太極、昭陽諸殿。《魏書》曰：以夏數爲得天，故即用夏正，而服色尚黃。《魏略》曰：詔以漢火行也，火忌水，故「洛」去「水」而加「隹」。魏於行次爲土，土，水之牡也，水得土而乃流，土得水而柔，故除「隹」加「水」，變「雒」爲「洛」。

context.beforeSource: 」丙午，行至曲蠡。
context.afterSource: 是歲，長水校尉戴陵諫不宜數行弋獵，帝大怒；
context.beforeLocal: 丙午，行至曲蠡。
context.afterLocal: 是歲，長水校尉戴陵諫不宜數行弋獵，帝大怒；

manualTranslations.zh: 漢帝以衆望在魏，乃召羣公卿士，袁宏《漢紀》載漢帝詔曰：「朕在位三十有二載，遭天下蕩覆，幸賴祖宗之靈，危而復存。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor of Han, because popular expectation rested on Wei, then summoned the assembled lords, ministers, and gentlemen. Yuan Hong's Annals of Han records the Emperor of Han's edict: "I have held the throne for thirty-two years and met with the overturning of the realm; fortunately relying on the spirits of my ancestors, in peril I was restored to existence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because popular expectation rested on Wei, the Emperor of Han summoned the assembled lords, ministers, and gentlemen. Yuan Hong's Annals of Han preserves the emperor's edict: "I have reigned thirty-two years through a world overturned; by the grace of my ancestors I survived peril and was restored.

manualTranslations.zh: 然仰瞻天文，俯察民心，炎精之數旣終，行運在乎曹氏。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet looking up I observe the celestial patterns; looking down I examine the hearts of the people. The tally of the Fiery Essence has already ended; the course of destiny rests with the house of Cao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet looking up at the heavens and down at the hearts of the people, I see that the tally of the Fiery Essence is spent and the course of destiny belongs to the house of Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以前王旣樹神武之績，今王又光曜明德以應其期，是歷數昭明，信可知矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the former king already established achievements of divine martial prowess, and now the King again displays bright virtue in answer to its season—thus the succession of heaven is clear, and indeed it can be known.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The former king already built up divine martial achievement, and now the King again shines with bright virtue in answer to the season—heaven's succession is plain and may be trusted.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫大道之行，天下爲公，選賢與能，故唐堯不私於厥子，而名播於無窮。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Great Way prevails, the realm belongs to all; the worthy and able are chosen. Therefore Tang Yao did not favor his own son, and his name spread without end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Great Way prevails the realm belongs to all and the worthy are chosen; Tang Yao did not favor his own son, and his fame endures without end.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕羨而慕焉，今其追踵堯典，禪位于魏王。」
manualTranslations.literal: I admire and yearn for this; let me now follow in the steps of Yao's precedent and abdicate the throne to the King of Wei."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I admire and long for this; let me now follow Yao's precedent and abdicate the throne to the King of Wei."

manualTranslations.zh: 告祠高廟。
manualTranslations.literal: He announced the sacrifice at the High Temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He announced the sacrifice at the High Temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 使兼御史大夫張音持節奉璽綬禪位，冊曰：「咨爾魏王：昔者帝堯禪位于虞舜，舜亦以命禹，天命不于常，惟歸有德。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent Concurrent Imperial Counselor Zhang Yin, bearing the staff of authority, to present the seal and cord of abdication. The investiture document read: "Consult you, King of Wei: formerly Emperor Yao abdicated the throne to Yu Shun; Shun likewise passed the mandate to Yu. Heaven's mandate is not constant—it rests only on the virtuous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent Concurrent Imperial Counselor Zhang Yin with the staff of authority to present the seal and cord of abdication. The investiture document read: "To you, King of Wei: Emperor Yao once abdicated to Yu Shun, and Shun passed the mandate to Yu. Heaven's mandate is not fixed—it goes only to the virtuous.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢道陵遲，世失其序，降及朕躬，大亂茲昏，羣兇肆逆，宇內顛覆。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Way declined; the age lost its order. Descending to my person, great disorder arose here in darkness; villainous gangs ran wild in rebellion, and the realm was overturned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Way declined and the age lost its order. Upon my person great disorder arose in darkness; villainous gangs rebelled and the realm was overturned.

manualTranslations.zh: 賴武王神武，拯茲難于四方，惟清區夏，以保綏我宗廟，豈予一人獲乂，俾九服實受其賜。
manualTranslations.literal: Relying on King Wu's divine martial prowess, he rescued this peril in the four quarters, clearing and pacifying the central regions, thereby preserving and comforting my ancestral temples. Was it I alone who received governance? The nine domains truly received his bounty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By King Wu's divine martial prowess this peril was rescued in the four quarters, the central regions were cleared and pacified, and my ancestral temples were preserved and comforted. Was it I alone who was governed? The nine domains truly received his bounty.

manualTranslations.zh: 今王欽承前緒，光于乃德，恢文武之大業，昭爾考之弘烈。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the King reverently inherits the former line, makes bright his virtue, restores the great enterprise of Wen and Wu, and manifests your father's lofty achievements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the King reverently inherits the former line, makes his virtue shine, restores the great enterprise of Wen and Wu, and displays your father's lofty achievements.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇靈降瑞，人神告徵，誕惟亮采，師錫朕命，僉曰爾度克恊于虞舜，用率我唐典，敬遜爾位。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial numen sent auspicious signs; men and spirits announced portents; sincerely and brightly you appeared; Heaven bestowed upon me the mandate; all said your measure could match Yu Shun—you should follow my Tang precedent and reverently yield your place.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial numen sent omens, men and spirits announced portents, and you appeared in sincere brilliance. Heaven bestowed the mandate upon me, and all said your measure could match Yu Shun—you should follow my Tang precedent and reverently yield your place.

manualTranslations.zh: 於戲！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 天之歷數在爾躬，允執其中，天祿永終；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's succession rests upon your person; faithfully hold its center; heaven's blessing endures to the end;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven's succession rests upon your person; faithfully hold the center; heaven's blessing endures to the end;

manualTranslations.zh: 君其祗順大禮，饗茲萬國，以肅承天命。」
manualTranslations.literal: O lord, reverently follow the great rite, feast the myriad states, and solemnly receive Heaven's mandate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reverently follow the great rite, feast the myriad states, and solemnly receive Heaven's mandate."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃爲壇於繁陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Then an altar was made at Fanyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An altar was then raised at Fanyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 庚午，王升壇即阼，百官陪位。
manualTranslations.literal: On the gengwu day, the King ascended the altar and took the throne; the hundred officials stood in attendance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the King ascended the altar and took the throne while the hundred officials stood in attendance.

manualTranslations.zh: 事訖，降壇，視燎成禮而反。
manualTranslations.literal: When the rite was finished, he descended the altar, watched the burning offerings to completion, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished he descended the altar, watched the burning offerings to completion, and returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 改延康爲黃初，大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan Kang was changed to Huangchu, and a general amnesty was declared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yan Kang era was redesignated Huangchu, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初元年十一月癸酉，以河內之山陽邑萬戶奉漢帝爲山陽公，行漢正朔，以天子之禮郊祭，上書不稱臣，京都有事于太廟，致胙；
manualTranslations.literal: In Huangchu 1, eleventh month, on the guiyou day, ten thousand households of Shanyang township in Henei were granted to maintain the Emperor of Han as the Shanyang duke; he kept the Han calendar; he performed suburban sacrifices by the Son of Heaven's rite; in memorials to the throne he did not style himself subject; when there were affairs at the Grand Temple in the capital he received sacrificial meat;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 1, eleventh month, on guiyou day, ten thousand households of Shanyang township in Henei were granted to maintain the Emperor of Han as the Shanyang duke. He kept the Han calendar, performed suburban sacrifices by the Son of Heaven's rite, did not style himself subject in memorials to the throne, and when there were affairs at the Grand Temple in the capital received sacrificial meat;

manualTranslations.zh: 封公之四子爲列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His four sons were enfeoffed as marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His four sons were enfeoffed as marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 追尊皇祖太王曰太皇帝，考武王曰武皇帝，尊王太后曰皇太后。
manualTranslations.literal: The royal grandfather, the Grand King, was posthumously honored as Grand Emperor; the father, King Wu, as Martial Emperor; the King's mother was honored as Empress Dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The royal grandfather, the Grand King, was posthumously honored as Grand Emperor; his father, King Wu, as Martial Emperor; and the King's mother as Empress Dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 賜男子爵人一級，爲父後及孝悌力田人二級。
manualTranslations.literal: Men were granted one rank of nobility; those serving as heirs to their fathers and those filially pious, brotherly, and diligent in farming received two ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men received one rank of nobility; heirs to their fathers and those noted for filial piety, brotherliness, and diligence in farming received two.

manualTranslations.zh: 以漢諸侯王爲崇德侯，列侯爲關中侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Former Han princes and kings were made Marquises of Chongde; marquises were made Marquises within the Pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Former Han princes and kings were made Marquises of Chongde, and marquises were made Marquises within the Pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 以潁陰之繁陽亭爲繁昌縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Fanyang pavilion in Yingyin was made Fanchang county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fanyang pavilion in Yingyin was made Fanchang county.

manualTranslations.zh: 封爵增位各有差。
manualTranslations.literal: Enfeoffments, titles, and promotions were granted each according to merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments, titles, and promotions were granted according to merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 改相國爲司徒，御史大夫爲司空，奉常爲太常，郎中令爲光祿勳，大理爲廷尉，大農爲大司農。
manualTranslations.literal: Chancellor of State was changed to Minister over the Masses; Imperial Counselor to Minister of Works; Director of Ceremonies to Grand Master of Splendid Affairs; Director of the Palace Secretariat to Superintendent of the Masters of Writing; Court Administrator to Commandant of Justice; Grand Minister of Agriculture to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State became Minister over the Masses, Imperial Counselor became Minister of Works, Director of Ceremonies became Grand Master of Splendid Affairs, Director of the Palace Secretariat became Superintendent of the Masters of Writing, Court Administrator became Commandant of Justice, and Grand Minister of Agriculture kept his title as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

manualTranslations.zh: 郡國縣邑，多所改易。
manualTranslations.literal: Commanderies, kingdoms, counties, and townships were changed in many places.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commanderies, kingdoms, counties, and townships were changed in many places.

manualTranslations.zh: 更授匈奴南單于呼廚泉魏璽綬，賜青蓋車、乘輿、寶劔、玉玦。
manualTranslations.literal: The Southern Xiongnu chanyu Huchuquan was again invested with Wei's seal and cord; he was granted a green-canopy carriage, imperial equipage, a treasured sword, and a jade ring.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Southern Xiongnu chanyu Huchuquan was reinvested with Wei's seal and cord and granted a green-canopy carriage, imperial equipage, a treasured sword, and a jade ring.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，初營洛陽宮，戊午幸洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, Luoyang Palace was first constructed; on the wuwu day he visited Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month construction of Luoyang Palace began, and on wuwu day he visited Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：諸書記是時帝居北宮，以建始殿朝羣臣，門曰承明，陳思王植詩曰「謁帝承明廬」是也。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: Various books record that at this time the Emperor resided in the Northern Palace, held court with the assembled ministers in the Jianshi Hall, and the gate was called Chenming—as in the verse of Prince Si of Chen, Cao Zhi: "I visited the Emperor at the Chenming lodge."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that various books record that at this time the emperor resided in the Northern Palace, held court in the Jianshi Hall, and used the Chenming gate—as in Cao Zhi's line, "I visited the emperor at the Chenming lodge."

manualTranslations.zh: 至明帝時，始於漢南宮崇德殿處起太極、昭陽諸殿。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time of Emperor Ming, the Taiji, Zhaoyang, and other halls were first raised on the site of Chongde Hall in the Han Southern Palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not until Emperor Ming's reign were the Taiji, Zhaoyang, and other halls first raised on the site of Chongde Hall in the Han Southern Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：以夏數爲得天，故即用夏正，而服色尚黃。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book says: Because the Xia calendar was taken to accord with heaven, the Xia new year was adopted immediately, and yellow was honored for ritual dress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Book says that because the Xia calendar was held to accord with heaven, the Xia new year was adopted at once and yellow was honored for ritual dress.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：詔以漢火行也，火忌水，故「洛」去「水」而加「隹」。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary says: An edict said that Han belonged to the phase of fire; fire dreads water, so in the name Luo the water element was removed and the bird element added.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary says an edict declared that Han belonged to the phase of fire, and because fire dreads water the name of Luo had its water element removed and a bird element added.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏於行次爲土，土，水之牡也，水得土而乃流，土得水而柔，故除「隹」加「水」，變「雒」爲「洛」。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei in the sequence of phases was earth; earth is the mate of water—water encountering earth can flow, earth meeting water becomes soft—so the bird element was removed, water was added, and the old form of the name was changed to the new form of Luo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei in the sequence of phases was earth, and earth is the mate of water: water encountering earth can flow, and earth meeting water becomes soft. Therefore the bird element was removed, water was added, and the old form of the city's name was changed to Luo.

sourceRange.text: 冬十月甲子，表首陽山東爲壽陵，作終制曰：「禮，國君即位爲椑，椑音扶歷反。存不忘亡也。臣松之按：禮，天子諸侯之棺，各有重數；棺之親身者曰椑。昔堯葬穀林，通樹之，禹葬會稽，農不易畝，《呂氏春秋》：堯葬於穀林，通樹之；舜葬於紀，市廛不變其肆；禹葬會稽，不變人徒。故葬於山林，則合乎山林。封樹之制，非上古也，吾無取焉。壽陵因山爲體，無爲封樹，無立寑殿，造園邑，通神道。夫葬也者，藏也，欲人之不得見也。骨無痛痒之知，冢非棲神之宅，禮不墓祭，欲存亡之不黷也，爲棺槨足以朽骨，衣衾足以朽肉而已。故吾營此丘墟不食之地，欲使易代之後不知其處。無施葦炭，無藏金銀銅鐵，一以瓦器，合古塗車、芻靈之義。棺但漆際會三過，飯含無以珠玉，無施珠襦玉匣，諸愚俗所爲也。季孫以璵璠斂，孔子歷級而救之，譬之暴骸中原。宋公厚葬，君子謂華元、樂莒不臣，以爲棄君於惡。漢文帝之不發，霸陵無求也；光武之掘，原陵封樹也。霸陵之完，功在釋之；原陵之掘，罪在明帝。是釋之忠以利君，明帝愛以害親也。忠臣孝子，宜思仲尼、丘明、釋之之言，鑒華元、樂莒、明帝之戒，存於所以安君定親，使魂靈萬載無危，斯則賢聖之忠孝矣。自古及今，未有不亡之國，亦無不掘之墓也。喪亂以來，漢氏諸陵無不發掘，至乃燒取玉匣金縷，骸骨并盡，是焚如之刑也，豈不重痛哉！禍由乎厚葬封樹。『桑、霍爲我戒』，不亦明乎？其皇后及貴人以下，不隨王之國者，有終沒皆葬澗西，前又以表其處矣。蓋舜葬蒼梧，二妃不從，延陵葬子，遠在嬴、博，魂而有靈，無不之也，一澗之閒，不足爲遠。若違今詔，妄有所變改造施，吾爲戮尸地下，戮而重戮，死而重死。臣子爲蔑死君父，不忠不孝，使死者有知，將不福汝。其以此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、祕書、三府。

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十月甲子，表首陽山東爲壽陵，作終制曰：「禮，國君即位爲椑，椑音扶歷反。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiazi day, he designated the east of Mount Shouyang as the site for Shouling and drew up final regulations, saying: "By ritual, when a state's ruler accedes he has a coffin-shell made—bi is pronounced fu-li fan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiazi day, he designated the east of Mount Shouyang as the site for Shouling and issued final regulations: "By ritual, when a ruler accedes a coffin-shell is prepared—bi is read fu-li fan.

manualTranslations.zh: 存不忘亡也。
manualTranslations.literal: While alive one does not forget the dead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While alive one does not forget the dead.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之按：禮，天子諸侯之棺，各有重數；
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Songzhi remarks: By ritual, the coffins of the Son of Heaven and feudal lords each have several layers;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that by ritual the coffins of the Son of Heaven and feudal lords each have several layers;

manualTranslations.zh: 棺之親身者曰椑。
manualTranslations.literal: The innermost coffin that encloses the body is called bi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The innermost coffin that encloses the body is called bi.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔堯葬穀林，通樹之，禹葬會稽，農不易畝，《呂氏春秋》：堯葬於穀林，通樹之；
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Yao was buried at Gulin with trees planted throughout; Yu was buried at Kuaiji and farmers did not change their fields. The Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lu: "Yao was buried at Gulin with trees planted throughout;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Yao was buried at Gulin with trees planted throughout, and Yu was buried at Kuaiji without farmers changing their fields. The Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lu says: "Yao was buried at Gulin with trees planted throughout;

manualTranslations.zh: 舜葬於紀，市廛不變其肆；
manualTranslations.literal: Shun was buried at Ji, and market stalls did not change their shops;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun was buried at Ji, and market stalls did not change their shops;

manualTranslations.zh: 禹葬會稽，不變人徒。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu was buried at Kuaiji, and travelers did not change their routes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu was buried at Kuaiji, and travelers did not change their routes."

manualTranslations.zh: 故葬於山林，則合乎山林。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore burial in mountains and forests accords with mountains and forests.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore burial in mountains and forests accords with mountains and forests.

manualTranslations.zh: 封樹之制，非上古也，吾無取焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The custom of mounding earth and planting trees is not from high antiquity; I do not adopt it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The custom of mounding earth and planting trees is not from high antiquity, and I do not adopt it.

manualTranslations.zh: 壽陵因山爲體，無爲封樹，無立寑殿，造園邑，通神道。
manualTranslations.literal: Shouling takes the mountain as its form; there shall be no mounding or tree-planting, no sleeping hall, no funerary estate, no spirit path.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shouling takes the mountain as its form: no mounding or tree-planting, no sleeping hall, no funerary estate, and no spirit path.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫葬也者，藏也，欲人之不得見也。
manualTranslations.literal: Burial is concealment—one wishes that people cannot see it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Burial is concealment—one wishes that people cannot see it.

manualTranslations.zh: 骨無痛痒之知，冢非棲神之宅，禮不墓祭，欲存亡之不黷也，爲棺槨足以朽骨，衣衾足以朽肉而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Bones have no awareness of pain or itch; a tomb mound is not a dwelling for the spirit; ritual does not sacrifice at the grave—one wishes that living and dead not profane each other. A coffin and outer shell sufficient to decay the bones, and shrouds sufficient to decay the flesh—that is all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bones feel no pain or itch; a mound is no dwelling for the spirit; ritual forbids sacrifice at the grave—living and dead must not profane each other. A coffin and outer shell enough to decay the bones and shrouds enough to decay the flesh—that is all.

manualTranslations.zh: 故吾營此丘墟不食之地，欲使易代之後不知其處。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore I have arranged this barren wasteland where nothing grows, wishing that after dynasties change its location will not be known.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore I have chosen this barren wasteland where nothing grows, wishing that after dynasties change its location will not be known.

manualTranslations.zh: 無施葦炭，無藏金銀銅鐵，一以瓦器，合古塗車、芻靈之義。
manualTranslations.literal: Do not use reed matting and charcoal; do not store gold, silver, copper, or iron; use only earthenware vessels, conforming to the ancient meaning of the clay carriage and straw effigy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Use no reed matting or charcoal; store no gold, silver, copper, or iron; use only earthenware vessels, in keeping with the ancient meaning of the clay carriage and straw effigy.

manualTranslations.zh: 棺但漆際會三過，飯含無以珠玉，無施珠襦玉匣，諸愚俗所爲也。
manualTranslations.literal: The coffin need only have its joints lacquered three times; in mouth-placing rites use no pearls or jade; do not use pearl shrouds or jade cases—these are things done by foolish custom.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The coffin need only have its joints lacquered three times; place no pearls or jade in the mouth; use no pearl shrouds or jade cases—these are the ways of foolish custom.

manualTranslations.zh: 季孫以璵璠斂，孔子歷級而救之，譬之暴骸中原。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ji Sun buried someone with yu and fan jades, Confucius hurried up the steps to stop him, comparing it to exposing the corpse in the central plain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ji Sun buried someone with yu and fan jades, Confucius rushed up the steps to stop him, comparing it to exposing the corpse in the open plain.

manualTranslations.zh: 宋公厚葬，君子謂華元、樂莒不臣，以爲棄君於惡。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Duke of Song had a lavish burial, the gentleman considered Hua Yuan and Yue Ju disloyal ministers, holding that they abandoned their lord to evil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Song received a lavish burial, gentlemen judged Hua Yuan and Yue Ju disloyal for abandoning their lord to evil.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢文帝之不發，霸陵無求也；
manualTranslations.literal: That Emperor Wen of Han's tomb was not opened—Baling had nothing worth seeking;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That Emperor Wen of Han's tomb was never opened—Baling had nothing worth seeking;

manualTranslations.zh: 光武之掘，原陵封樹也。
manualTranslations.literal: That Guangwu's tomb was dug—Yuanling had mounds and trees.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That Guangwu's tomb was dug open—Yuanling had mounds and trees.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸陵之完，功在釋之；
manualTranslations.literal: That Baling remained intact—the credit belongs to Zhang Shi;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That Baling remained intact was Zhang Shi's doing;

manualTranslations.zh: 原陵之掘，罪在明帝。
manualTranslations.literal: That Yuanling was opened—the blame belongs to Emperor Ming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That Yuanling was opened was Emperor Ming's fault.

manualTranslations.zh: 是釋之忠以利君，明帝愛以害親也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Zhang Shi's loyalty benefited his lord; Emperor Ming's affection harmed his kinsman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi's loyalty benefited his lord; Emperor Ming's affection harmed his kinsman.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠臣孝子，宜思仲尼、丘明、釋之之言，鑒華元、樂莒、明帝之戒，存於所以安君定親，使魂靈萬載無危，斯則賢聖之忠孝矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Loyal ministers and filial sons should ponder the words of Zhongni, Qiuming, and Zhang Shi; take warning from Hua Yuan, Yue Ju, and Emperor Ming; keep in mind how to settle their lord and secure their kin, so that the soul for ten thousand generations knows no peril—this is the loyalty and filial piety of the worthy and sage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers and filial sons should ponder the words of Confucius, Qiu Ming, and Zhang Shi, take warning from Hua Yuan, Yue Ju, and Emperor Ming, and keep in mind how to settle their lord and secure their kin so that the soul for ten thousand generations knows no peril—this is the loyalty and filial piety of the worthy and sage.

manualTranslations.zh: 自古及今，未有不亡之國，亦無不掘之墓也。
manualTranslations.literal: From antiquity to the present there has never been a state that did not perish; likewise there is never a tomb that was not dug up.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present no state has failed to perish, and no tomb has escaped being opened.

manualTranslations.zh: 喪亂以來，漢氏諸陵無不發掘，至乃燒取玉匣金縷，骸骨并盡，是焚如之刑也，豈不重痛哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Since the disorders of war, none of the Han tombs have escaped being opened; some were even burned to take jade cases and gold threads, and the bones wholly destroyed—this is the punishment of burning alive. How is this not doubly painful!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the age of chaos none of the Han tombs have escaped being opened; some were even burned to take jade cases and gold threads until the bones were wholly destroyed—this is the punishment of burning alive. How is the pain not doubled!

manualTranslations.zh: 禍由乎厚葬封樹。
manualTranslations.literal: Disaster comes from lavish burial and mounded trees.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Disaster comes from lavish burial and mounded trees.

manualTranslations.zh: 『桑、霍爲我戒』，不亦明乎？
manualTranslations.literal: "Sang and Huo stand as my warning"—is this not clear?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Sang and Huo stand as my warning"—is this not clear?

manualTranslations.zh: 其皇后及貴人以下，不隨王之國者，有終沒皆葬澗西，前又以表其處矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Queens and consorts and those below who do not follow the King's fief—when they reach their end all shall be buried west of the stream; their places have already been marked before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Queens, consorts, and those below who do not follow the King's fief shall, when they reach their end, all be buried west of the stream; their places have already been marked.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋舜葬蒼梧，二妃不從，延陵葬子，遠在嬴、博，魂而有靈，無不之也，一澗之閒，不足爲遠。
manualTranslations.literal: For Shun was buried at Cangwu and the two consorts did not follow; Yanling buried his son far at Ying and Bo—if the soul has awareness, nowhere is beyond reach; the space of one stream is not enough to count as far.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shun was buried at Cangwu and the two consorts did not follow; Yanling buried his son far away at Ying and Bo—if the soul has awareness, nowhere is beyond reach, and the distance of one stream is not far.

manualTranslations.zh: 若違今詔，妄有所變改造施，吾爲戮尸地下，戮而重戮，死而重死。
manualTranslations.literal: If anyone violates this present edict and on his own initiative alters, remodels, or adds works, I will mutilate the corpse underground—mutilated once and mutilated again, dead once and dead again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If anyone violates this edict and on his own initiative alters, remodels, or adds works, I will mutilate the corpse underground—mutilated once and again, dead once and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣子爲蔑死君父，不忠不孝，使死者有知，將不福汝。
manualTranslations.literal: For a minister or son to treat a dead lord or father with contempt is disloyalty and unfilial piety; if the dead have awareness, they will not bless you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For ministers or sons to treat a dead lord or father with contempt is disloyalty and unfilial piety; if the dead have awareness, they will not bless you.

manualTranslations.zh: 其以此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、祕書、三府。
manualTranslations.literal: Let this edict be stored in the ancestral temple, with copies in the Masters of Writing, the Secretariat, and the Three Offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let this edict be stored in the ancestral temple, with copies in the Masters of Writing, the Secretariat, and the Three Offices.

sourceRange.text: 」秋八月，孫權遣使奉章，并遣于禁等還。丁巳，使太常邢貞持節拜權爲大將軍，封吳王，加九錫。冬十月，授楊彪光祿大夫。《魏書》曰：己亥，公卿朝朔旦，并引故漢太尉楊彪，待以客禮，詔曰：「夫先王制几杖之賜，所以賔禮黃耇襃崇元老也。昔孔光、卓茂皆以淑德高年，受茲嘉錫。公故漢宰臣，乃祖已來，世著名節，年過七十，行不踰矩，可謂老成人矣，所宜寵異以章舊德。其賜公延年杖及馮几；謁請之日，便使杖入，又可使著鹿皮冠。」彪辭讓不聽，竟著布單衣、皮弁以見。《續漢書》曰：彪見漢祚將終，自以累世爲三公，恥爲魏臣，遂稱足攣，不復行。積十餘年，帝即王位，欲以爲太尉，令近臣宣旨。彪辭曰：「甞以漢朝爲三公，值世衰亂，不能立尺寸之益，若復爲魏臣，於國之選，亦不爲榮也。」帝不奪其意。黃初四年，詔拜光祿大夫，秩中二千石，朝見位次三公，如孔光故事。彪上章固讓，帝不聽，又爲門施行馬，致吏卒，以優崇之。年八十四，以六年薨。子脩，事見〈陳思王傳〉。以穀貴，罷五銖錢。《魏書》曰：十一月辛未，鎮西將軍曹真命衆將及州郡兵討破叛胡治元多、蘆水、封賞等，斬首五萬餘級，獲生口十萬，羊一百一十一萬口，牛八萬，河西遂平。帝初聞胡決水灌顯美，謂左右諸將曰：「昔隗嚻灌略陽，而光武因其疲弊，進兵滅之。今胡決水灌顯美，其事正相似，破胡事今至不久。」旬日，破胡告檄到，上大笑曰：「吾策之於帷幕之內，諸將奮擊於萬里之外，其相應若合符契。前後戰克獲虜，未有如此也。」己卯，以大將軍曹仁爲大司馬。十二月，行東巡。是歲築陵雲臺。

manualTranslations.zh: 」秋八月，孫權遣使奉章，并遣于禁等還。
manualTranslations.literal: "In the eighth month of autumn, Sun Quan sent envoys bearing tribute, and also sent Yu Jin and others back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "In the eighth month of autumn Sun Quan sent envoys bearing tribute and also returned Yu Jin and the others.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁巳，使太常邢貞持節拜權爲大將軍，封吳王，加九錫。
manualTranslations.literal: On the dingsi day, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Xing Zhen was sent with the staff of authority to invest Sun Quan as Grand General, enfeoff him as King of Wu, and grant the Nine Bestowments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Director of Imperial Sacrifices Xing Zhen was sent with the staff of authority to invest Sun Quan as Grand General, enfeoff him as King of Wu, and grant the Nine Bestowments.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十月，授楊彪光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Yang Biao was appointed Grand Counselor of the Household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Yang Biao was appointed Grand Counselor of the Household.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：己亥，公卿朝朔旦，并引故漢太尉楊彪，待以客禮，詔曰：「夫先王制几杖之賜，所以賔禮黃耇襃崇元老也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book says: On the jihai day, the dukes and ministers attended court at the new moon dawn, and the former Han Grand Commandant Yang Biao was also brought in and treated with guest rites. An edict said: "Former kings instituted the gift of armrest and staff to guest-ritual the hoary-headed and honor and exalt elders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that on jihai day the dukes and ministers attended court at the new-moon dawn and the former Han Grand Commandant Yang Biao was also brought in and treated as a guest. An edict said: "Former kings instituted the gift of armrest and staff to receive the aged with guest rites and honor elders.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔孔光、卓茂皆以淑德高年，受茲嘉錫。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Kong Guang and Zhuo Mao both, by their fine virtue and advanced age, received this fine bestowment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Kong Guang and Zhuo Mao both, by their fine virtue and advanced years, received this honored gift.

manualTranslations.zh: 公故漢宰臣，乃祖已來，世著名節，年過七十，行不踰矩，可謂老成人矣，所宜寵異以章舊德。
manualTranslations.literal: You, sir, are a former minister of Han; from your ancestors onward your house has been famed for integrity; past seventy years, your conduct does not overstep the square—one may call you a mature elder; it is fitting to favor you exceptionally to display your old virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You are a former minister of Han; from your ancestors your house has been famed for integrity; past seventy, your conduct never oversteps the measure—you are truly a mature elder, and it is fitting to honor you exceptionally to display your old virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 其賜公延年杖及馮几；
manualTranslations.literal: Accordingly grant you the staff of prolonged years and a folding armrest;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Accordingly I grant you the staff of prolonged years and a folding armrest;

manualTranslations.zh: 謁請之日，便使杖入，又可使著鹿皮冠。」
manualTranslations.literal: On days of audience and petition, let you enter leaning on the staff, and you may also wear a deerskin cap."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On days when you come to audience you may enter leaning on the staff, and you may also wear a deerskin cap."

manualTranslations.zh: 彪辭讓不聽，竟著布單衣、皮弁以見。
manualTranslations.literal: Biao declined but was not heeded; in the end he wore plain cloth single garments and a leather cap to appear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Biao declined but was not heeded; in the end he appeared wearing plain cloth garments and a leather cap.

manualTranslations.zh: 《續漢書》曰：彪見漢祚將終，自以累世爲三公，恥爲魏臣，遂稱足攣，不復行。
manualTranslations.literal: The Continued Book of Han says: Biao saw that Han's mandate was nearing its end; considering that his house for generations had been among the Three Excellencies, he was ashamed to become a minister of Wei, and therefore claimed crippled feet and no longer walked.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Continued Book of Han says that Biao saw Han's mandate nearing its end; ashamed, as one from a house that for generations had held the Three Excellencies, to become a Wei minister, he claimed crippled feet and would no longer walk.

manualTranslations.zh: 積十餘年，帝即王位，欲以爲太尉，令近臣宣旨。
manualTranslations.literal: For more than ten years this continued; when the Emperor took the royal throne he wished to make him Grand Commandant and ordered a close minister to announce the intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For more than ten years this continued. When the emperor took the royal throne he wished to make him Grand Commandant and ordered a close minister to announce the intent.

manualTranslations.zh: 彪辭曰：「甞以漢朝爲三公，值世衰亂，不能立尺寸之益，若復爲魏臣，於國之選，亦不爲榮也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Biao declined, saying: "I once served Han as one of the Three Excellencies; meeting an age of decline and disorder, I could not establish the slightest benefit. If I were again to become a minister of Wei, in the state's choice it would also not be an honor."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Biao declined, saying: "I once served Han as one of the Three Excellencies in an age of decline and could not achieve the slightest good. To become a Wei minister now would be no honor to the state's choice either."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝不奪其意。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor did not override his intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor did not override his intent.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初四年，詔拜光祿大夫，秩中二千石，朝見位次三公，如孔光故事。
manualTranslations.literal: In Huangchu 4, an edict appointed him Grand Counselor of the Household, with salary of two thousand shi middle grade; at court audiences his place ranked with the Three Excellencies, following Kong Guang's precedent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 an edict appointed him Grand Counselor of the Household at salary of two thousand shi middle grade, with court precedence equal to the Three Excellencies after Kong Guang's precedent.

manualTranslations.zh: 彪上章固讓，帝不聽，又爲門施行馬，致吏卒，以優崇之。
manualTranslations.literal: Biao submitted a memorial firmly declining, but the Emperor would not listen; he also provided gate horses for dismounting, sent officials and soldiers, and honored him with special favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Biao submitted a memorial firmly declining, but the emperor would not listen; he also provided dismounting horses at the gate, posted officials and soldiers, and honored him with special favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 年八十四，以六年薨。
manualTranslations.literal: At age eighty-four, in the sixth year he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At eighty-four he died in the sixth year.

manualTranslations.zh: 子脩，事見
manualTranslations.literal: His son Xiu—account in
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Xiu is treated in

manualTranslations.zh: 〈陳思王傳〉。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Biography of Prince Si of Chen〉.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Prince Si of Chen〉.

manualTranslations.zh: 以穀貴，罷五銖錢。
manualTranslations.literal: Because grain was costly, the five-zhu coin was abolished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because grain was costly, the five-zhu coin was abolished.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：十一月辛未，鎮西將軍曹真命衆將及州郡兵討破叛胡治元多、蘆水、封賞等，斬首五萬餘級，獲生口十萬，羊一百一十一萬口，牛八萬，河西遂平。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Book says: In the eleventh month, on the xinwei day, Guard-West General Cao Zhen ordered the various generals and commandery and district troops to attack and defeat the rebel Hu Zhiyuanduo, Lushui, Fengshang, and others; beheaded more than fifty thousand; captured one hundred thousand living captives, one million one hundred ten thousand sheep, and eighty thousand cattle; and the Hexi region was thereby pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that in the eleventh month, on xinwei day, Guard-West General Cao Zhen ordered the generals and commandery and district troops to defeat the rebel Hu Zhiyuanduo, Lushui, Fengshang, and others, beheading more than fifty thousand, capturing one hundred thousand people, one million one hundred ten thousand sheep, and eighty thousand cattle, and the Hexi region was pacified.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝初聞胡決水灌顯美，謂左右諸將曰：「昔隗嚻灌略陽，而光武因其疲弊，進兵滅之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Emperor first heard that the Hu had breached the waters to flood Xianmei, he said to the generals at his side: "Formerly Kui Xiao flooded Lueyang, and Guangwu, taking advantage of his exhaustion, advanced his army and destroyed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor first heard that the Hu had breached the waters to flood Xianmei, he told the generals at his side: "Formerly Kui Xiao flooded Lueyang, and Guangwu, taking advantage of his exhaustion, advanced and destroyed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 今胡決水灌顯美，其事正相似，破胡事今至不久。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now the Hu have breached the waters to flood Xianmei—the affair is exactly similar; the destruction of the Hu will come before long."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the Hu have breached the waters to flood Xianmei—the affair is exactly similar, and their defeat will come before long."

manualTranslations.zh: 旬日，破胡告檄到，上大笑曰：「吾策之於帷幕之內，諸將奮擊於萬里之外，其相應若合符契。
manualTranslations.literal: Within ten days the victory report on the destruction of the Hu arrived; the Emperor laughed greatly and said: "I plotted it within the curtain, and the generals struck fiercely ten thousand li away—their response matched like joining tally halves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within ten days the victory report arrived. The emperor laughed and said: "I plotted it within the curtain while the generals struck fiercely ten thousand li away—their response matched like joining tally halves.

manualTranslations.zh: 前後戰克獲虜，未有如此也。」
manualTranslations.literal: In battles won and captives taken before and after, there has never been anything like this."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In victories and captives taken before and after, there has never been anything like this."

manualTranslations.zh: 己卯，以大將軍曹仁爲大司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: On the jimao day, Grand General Cao Ren was made Grand Marshal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jimao day Grand General Cao Ren was made Grand Marshal.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，行東巡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, he toured east.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he toured east.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲築陵雲臺。
manualTranslations.literal: That year Lingyun Terrace was built.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Lingyun Terrace was built.

sourceRange.text: 辛巳，立皇子冏爲清河王。吳將諸葛瑾、張霸等寇襄陽，撫軍大將軍司馬宣王討破之，斬霸，征東大將軍曹休又破其別將於尋陽。論功行賞各有差。冬十月，清河王冏薨。十二月，以太尉鍾繇爲太傅，征東大將軍曹休爲大司馬，中軍大將軍曹真爲大將軍，司徒華歆爲太尉，司空王朗爲司徒，鎮軍大將軍陳羣爲司空，撫軍大將軍司馬宣王爲驃騎大將軍。太和元年227年春正月，郊祀武皇帝以配天，宗祀文皇帝於明堂以配上帝。

sourceRange.text: 六年春二月，詔曰：「古之帝王，封建諸侯，所以藩屏王室也。詩不云乎，『懷德維寧，宗子維城』。秦、漢繼周，或彊或弱，俱失厥中。大魏創業，諸王開國，隨時之宜，未有定制，非所以永爲後法也。其改封諸侯王，皆以郡爲國。」三月癸酉，行東巡，所過存問高年鰥寡孤獨，賜穀帛。乙亥，月犯軒轅大星。夏四月壬寅，行幸許昌宮。甲子，初進新果于廟。五月，皇子殷薨，追封謚安平哀王。秋七月，以衞尉董昭爲司徒。九月，行幸摩陂，治許昌宮，起景福、承光殿。冬十月，殄夷將軍田豫帥衆討吴將周賀於成山，殺賀。十一月丙寅，太白晝見。有星孛于翼，近太微上將星。庚寅，陳思王植薨。十二月，行還許昌宮。青龍元年233年春正月甲申，青龍見郟之摩陂井中。二月丁酉，幸摩陂觀龍，於是改年；改摩陂爲龍陂，賜男子爵人二級，鰥寡孤獨無出今年租賦。三月甲子，詔公卿舉賢良篤行之士各一人。夏五月壬申，詔祀故大將軍夏侯惇、大司馬曹仁、車騎將軍程昱於太祖廟庭。《魏書》載詔曰：「昔先王之禮，於功臣存則顯其爵祿，沒則祭于大蒸，故漢氏功臣祠於廟庭。大魏元功之臣功勳優著，終始休明者，其皆依禮祀之。」於是以惇等配饗之。戊寅，北海王蕤薨。閏月庚寅朔，日有蝕之。丁酉，改封宗室女非諸王女皆爲邑主。詔諸郡國山川不在祠典者勿祠。六月，洛陽宮鞠室災。

sourceRange.text: 五年春正月，帝耕于藉田。三月，大司馬曹真薨。諸葛亮寇天水，詔大將軍司馬宣王拒之。自去冬十月至此月不雨，辛巳，大雩。夏四月，鮮卑附義王軻比能率其種人及丁零大人兒禪詣幽州貢名馬。復置護匈奴中郎將。秋七月丙子，以亮退走，封爵增位各有差。《魏書》曰：初，亮出，議者以爲亮軍無輜重，糧必不繼，不擊自破，無爲勞兵；或欲自芟上邽左右生麥以奪賊食，帝皆不從。前後遣兵增宣王軍，又勑使護麥。宣王與亮相持，賴得此麥以爲軍糧。乙酉，皇子殷生，大赦。

sourceRange.text: 二月癸卯，以大中大夫韓曁爲司徒。癸丑，月犯心距星，又犯心中央大星。夏四月庚子，司徒韓曁薨。壬寅，分沛國蕭、相、竹邑、符離、蘄、銍、龍亢、山桑、洨、虹洨音胡交反。虹音絳。十縣爲汝陰郡。宋縣、陳郡苦縣皆屬譙郡。以沛、杼秋、公丘、彭城豐國、廣戚，并五縣爲沛王國。庚戌，大赦。五月乙亥，月犯心距星，又犯中央大星。《魏書》載戊子詔曰：「昔漢高祖創業，光武中興，謀除殘暴，功昭四海，而墳陵崩頹，童兒牧豎踐蹈其上，非大魏尊崇所承代之意也。其表高祖、光武陵四面百步，不得使民耕牧樵採。」六月，省漁陽郡之狐奴縣，復置安樂縣。

sourceRange.text: 秋七月丁卯，司徒陳矯薨。孫權遣將朱然等二萬人圍江夏郡，荊州刺史胡質等擊之，然退走。初，權遣使浮海與高句驪通，欲襲遼東。遣幽州刺史毌丘儉率諸軍及鮮卑、烏丸屯遼東南界，璽書徵公孫淵。淵發兵反，儉進軍討之，會連雨十日，遼水大漲，詔儉引軍還。右北平烏丸單于寇婁敦、遼西烏丸都督王護留等居遼東，率部衆隨儉內附。己卯，詔遼東將吏士民爲淵所脅略不得降者，一切赦之。辛卯，太白晝見。淵自儉還，遂自立爲燕王，置百官，稱紹漢元年。

sourceRange.text: 五年春二月，詔大將軍曹爽率衆征蜀。夏四月朔，日有蝕之。五月癸巳，講尚書經通，使太常以太牢祠孔子於辟雍，以顏淵配；賜太傳、大將軍及侍講者各有差。丙午，大將軍曹爽引軍還。秋八月，秦王詢薨。九月，鮮卑內附，置遼東屬國，立昌黎縣以居之。冬十一月癸卯，詔祀故尚書令荀攸於太祖廟庭。*|臣松之以為故魏氏配饗不及荀彧，蓋以其末年異議，又位非魏臣故也。至於升程昱而遺郭嘉，先鍾繇而後荀攸，則未詳厥趣也。徐謀逆而許褚心動，忠誠之至遠同於日磾，且潼關之危，非褚不濟，褚之功烈有過典韋，今祀韋而不及褚，文所未達也。己酉，復秦國為京兆郡。十二月，司空崔林薨。

manualTranslations.literal: In summer, on the new moon of the fourth month, there was a solar eclipse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse fell on the new moon of the fourth month.

manualTranslations.zh: 五月癸巳，講尚書經通，使太常以太牢祠孔子於辟雍，以顏淵配；
manualTranslations.literal: On guisi in the fifth month, he completed his lectures on the Classic of Documents; he ordered the Minister of Ceremonies with a grand sacrifice to sacrifice to Confucius at the Biyong, with Yan Hui as associate;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guisi in the fifth month, having finished his study of the Documents, he sent the Minister of Ceremonies to offer a bull to Confucius at the Biyong, with Yan Hui as secondary honoree;

manualTranslations.zh: 賜太傳、大將軍及侍講者各有差。
manualTranslations.literal: Gifts to the Grand Tutor, the Grand General, and those who had lectured to him were each according to degree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ranked rewards went to the Grand Tutor, Grand General Cao Shuang, and every lecturer who had instructed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 丙午，大將軍曹爽引軍還。
manualTranslations.literal: On bingwu, Grand General Cao Shuang led the army back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingwu Cao Shuang withdrew his army.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋八月，秦王詢薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, the Prince of Qin, Xun, died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eighth month brought word that Prince of Qin Cao Xun had died.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，鮮卑內附，置遼東屬國，立昌黎縣以居之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, the Xianbei submitted inward; Liaodong Dependent State was established, and Changli County was set up to settle them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month surrendering Xianbei tribes were placed under a new Liaodong dependent state, with Changli county created to house them.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十一月癸卯，詔祀故尚書令荀攸於太祖廟庭。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on guimao, an edict ordered sacrifice to the late Director of the Masters of Writing Xun You in the court of Grand Progenitor's temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eleventh month the court ordered Xun You enshrined in the outer court of Cao Cao's temple.

manualTranslations.zh: *|臣松之以為故魏氏配饗不及荀彧，蓋以其末年異議，又位非魏臣故也。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Your subject Pei Songzhi considers that in the former Wei temple offerings Xun Yu was not included, probably because of his dissenting views in his final years, and also because his position was not that of a Wei minister.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that the Wei shrine never included Xun Yu, likely because his final years brought open disagreement and because he had never formally served as a Wei official.〉

manualTranslations.zh: 至於升程昱而遺郭嘉，先鍾繇而後荀攸，則未詳厥趣也。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈As for elevating Cheng Yu while omitting Guo Jia, and placing Zhong Yao before Xun You, the underlying intent is unclear.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Why Cheng Yu was promoted while Guo Jia was passed over, and Zhong Yao honored before Xun You, Pei Songzhi cannot say.〉

manualTranslations.zh: 徐謀逆而許褚心動，忠誠之至遠同於日磾，且潼關之危，非褚不濟，褚之功烈有過典韋，今祀韋而不及褚，文所未達也。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈When Xu Ta plotted treason Xu Chu was stirred to loyal action; in depth of loyalty he was far akin to Jin Midi; moreover, the peril at Tong Pass was not overcome without Chu—Chu's meritorious achievements surpassed Dian Wei; yet now Wei is sacrificed to and Chu is not—the text has not reached this.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈When Xu Ta plotted assassination Xu Chu proved his loyalty—a devotion Pei Songzhi likens to Jin Midi's; without Chu, Tong Pass would never have been saved, his feats outshining even Dian Wei's—yet Wei receives temple honor while Chu does not, a lacuna Pei Songzhi finds inexplicable.〉

manualTranslations.zh: 己酉，復秦國為京兆郡。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiyou, the State of Qin was restored as Jingzhao Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiyou the Qin principality was converted back into Jingzhao commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，司空崔林薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minister of Works Cui Lin died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Lin died in the twelfth month while holding the Ministry of Works.

localRange.text: 太后詔曰：「夫五刑之罪，莫大於不孝。夫人有子不孝，尚告治之，此兒豈復成人主邪？吾婦人不達大義，以謂濟不得便為大逆也。然大將軍志意懇切，發言惻愴，故聽如所奏。當班下遠近，使知本末也。〈《世語》曰：初，青龍中，石苞鬻鐵於長安，得見司馬宣王，宣王知焉。

sourceRange.text: 三月，詔曰：「」夏五月，命大將軍司馬文王為相國，封晉公，食邑八郡，加之九錫，文王前後九讓乃止。六月丙子，詔曰：「」《楚國先賢傳》曰：余字子正，天姿方毅，志尚仁義，為郡功曹。

localRange.text: 三月，詔曰：「古者克敵，收其屍以為京觀，所以懲昏逆而章武功也。漢孝武元鼎中，改桐鄉為聞喜，新鄉為獲嘉，以著南越之亡。大將軍親總六戎，營據丘頭，內夷羣凶，外殄寇虜，功濟兆民，聲振四海。克敵之地，宜有令名，其改丘頭為武丘，明以武平亂，後世不忘，亦京觀二邑之義也。夏五月，命大將軍司馬文王為相國，封晉公，食邑八郡，加之九錫，文王前後九讓乃止。六月丙子，詔曰：「昔南陽郡山賊擾攘，欲劫質故太守東里衮，功曹應余獨身捍衮，遂免於難。余顛沛殞斃，殺身濟君。其下司徒，署余孫倫吏，使蒙伏節之報。〈《楚國先賢傳》曰：余字子正，天姿方毅，志尚仁義，建安二十三年為郡功曹。

sourceRange.text: 五月己丑，高貴鄉公卒，年二十。《漢晉春秋》曰：帝見威權日去，不勝其忿。乃召侍中王沈、尚書王經、散騎常侍王業，謂曰：「司馬昭之心，路人所知也。吾不能坐受廢辱，今日當與卿等自出討之。」王經曰：「昔魯昭公不忍季氏，敗走失國，為天下笑。今權在其門，為日乆矣，朝廷四方皆為之致死，不顧逆順之理，非一日也。且宿衞空闕，兵甲寡弱，陛下何所資用，而一旦如此，無乃欲除疾而更深之邪！禍殆不測，宜見重詳。」帝乃出懷中版令投地，曰：「行之決矣。正使死，何所懼？況不必死邪！」於是入白太后，沈、業奔走告文王，文王為之備。帝遂帥僮僕數百，鼓譟而出。文王弟屯騎校尉伷入，遇帝於東止車門，左右呵之，伷衆奔走。中護軍賈充又逆帝戰於南闕下，帝自用劒。衆欲退，太子舍人成濟問充曰：「事急矣。當云何？」充曰：「畜養汝等，正謂今日。今日之事，無所問也。」濟即前刺帝，刃出於背。文王聞，大驚，自投於地曰：「天下其謂我何！」太傅孚奔往，枕帝股而哭，哀甚，曰：「殺陛下者，臣之罪也。」臣松之以為習鑿齒書，雖最後出，然述此事差有次第。故先載習語，以其餘所言微異者次其後。《世語》曰：王沈、王業馳告文王，尚書王經以正直不出，因沈、業申意。《晉諸公贊曰：沈、業將出，呼王經。經不從，曰：「吾子行矣！」干寶《晉紀》曰：成濟問賈充曰：「事急矣。若之何？」充曰：「公畜養汝等，為今日之事也。夫何疑！」濟曰：「然。」乃抽戈犯蹕。《魏氏春秋》曰：戊子夜，帝自將宂從僕射李昭、黃門從官焦伯等下陵雲臺，鎧仗授兵，欲因際會，自出討文王。會雨，有司奏却日，遂見王經等出黃素詔於懷曰：「是可忍也，孰不可忍也！今日便當決行此事。」入白太后，遂拔劒升輦，帥殿中宿衞蒼頭官僮擊戰鼓，出雲龍門。賈充自外而入，帝師潰散，猶稱天子，手劒奮擊，衆莫敢逼。充帥厲將士，騎督成倅弟成濟以矛進，帝崩于師。時暴雨雷霆，晦冥。魏末傳曰：賈充呼帳下督成濟謂曰：「司馬家事若敗，汝等豈復有種乎？何不出擊！」倅兄弟二人乃帥帳下人出，顧曰：「當殺邪？執邪？」充曰：「殺之。」兵交，帝曰：「放仗！」大將軍士皆放仗。濟兄弟因前刺帝，帝倒車下。皇太后令曰：「吾以不德，遭家不造，昔援立東海王子髦，以為明帝嗣，見其好書疏文章，兾可成濟，而情性暴戾，日月滋甚。吾數呵責，遂更忿恚，造作醜逆不道之言以誣謗吾，遂隔絕兩宮。其所言道，不可忍聽，非天地所覆載。吾即密有令語大將軍，不可以奉宗廟，恐顛覆社稷，死無面目以見先帝。大將軍以其尚幼，謂當改心為善，殷勤執據。而此兒忿戾，所行益甚，舉弩遙射吾宮，祝當令中吾項，箭親墮吾前。吾語大將軍，不可不廢之，前後數十。此兒具聞，自知罪重，便圖為弒逆，賂遺吾左右人，令因吾服藥，密行酖毒，重相設計。事已覺露，直欲因際會舉兵入西宮殺吾，出取大將軍，呼侍中王沈、散騎常侍王業、《世語》曰：業，武陵人，後為晉中護軍。尚書王經，出懷中黃素詔示之，言今日便當施行。吾之危殆，過於累卵。吾老寡，豈復多惜餘命邪？但傷先帝遺意不遂，社稷顛覆為痛耳。賴宗廟之靈，沈、業即馳語大將軍，得先嚴警，而此兒便將左右出雲龍門，雷戰鼓，躬自拔刃，與左右雜衞共入兵陣間，為前鋒所害。此兒旣行悖逆不道，而又自陷大禍，重令吾悼心不可言。昔漢昌邑王以罪廢為庶人，此兒亦宜以民禮葬之，當令內外咸知此兒所行。又尚書王經，凶逆無狀，其收經及家屬皆詣廷尉。

context.beforeSource: 夏四月，詔有司率遵前命，復進大將軍司馬文王位為相國，封晉公，加九錫。
context.afterSource: 」庚寅，太傅孚、大將軍文王、太尉柔、司徒沖稽首言：「伏見中令，故高貴鄉公悖逆不道，自陷大禍，依漢昌邑王罪廢故事，以民禮葬。

manualTranslations.zh: 五月己丑，高貴鄉公卒，年二十。
manualTranslations.literal: On jichou in the fifth month, the Duke of Gaogui died at age twenty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jichou in the fifth month Cao Mao died at age twenty.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：帝見威權日去，不勝其忿。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Han–Jin Annals states: The emperor saw authority slipping away day by day and could not contain his anger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Han–Jin Annals records that Cao Mao watched real power drain away daily until rage overcame him.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃召侍中王沈、尚書王經、散騎常侍王業，謂曰：「司馬昭之心，路人所知也。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon summoned Palace Attendant Wang Shen, Master of Writing Wang Jing, and Regular Attendant Wang Ye, and said to them: "Sima Zhao's heart is known even to passersby on the road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He summoned Palace Attendant Wang Shen, Master of Writing Wang Jing, and Regular Attendant Wang Ye and said: "Sima Zhao's heart is known even to passersby on the road.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾不能坐受廢辱，今日當與卿等自出討之。」
manualTranslations.literal: I cannot sit and accept deposition and disgrace; today I shall go out with you and strike at him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I will not sit still and accept deposition and disgrace—today I go out with you to strike at him."

manualTranslations.zh: 王經曰：「昔魯昭公不忍季氏，敗走失國，為天下笑。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jing said: "Formerly Duke Zhao of Lu could not bear the Ji clan, failed, fled, and lost his state, becoming the world's laughingstock.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jing said: "When Duke Zhao of Lu could not tolerate the Ji clan he was ruined, fled, and lost his state—the whole world laughed at him.

manualTranslations.zh: 今權在其門，為日乆矣，朝廷四方皆為之致死，不顧逆順之理，非一日也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now power has been in their gate for a long time; court and the four quarters have all given their lives for them, heedless of right and wrong—not for one day only.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Power has sat in the Sima gate for years; every office and every quarter of the realm now serves them without asking whether right or wrong—this did not begin yesterday.

manualTranslations.zh: 且宿衞空闕，兵甲寡弱，陛下何所資用，而一旦如此，無乃欲除疾而更深之邪！
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, the night guard is empty and weak in arms and armor; what resources does Your Majesty have to rely on, and to act so suddenly—are you not trying to remove a disease only to deepen it!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your night guard is hollow, your arms few—what force can Your Majesty actually draw on? To move so suddenly is like trying to cure an illness and only driving it deeper!

manualTranslations.zh: 禍殆不測，宜見重詳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Disaster is hard to measure; Your Majesty should reconsider carefully."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The peril is incalculable; Your Majesty must think again."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝乃出懷中版令投地，曰：「行之決矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor then took the written order from his bosom and cast it to the ground, saying: "My mind is made up.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Mao pulled the written order from his robe and flung it down: "My mind is made up.

manualTranslations.zh: 正使死，何所懼？
manualTranslations.literal: Even if I must die, what is there to fear?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if I die, what is there to fear?

manualTranslations.zh: 況不必死邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: And need it even come to death!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And death may not even be necessary!"

manualTranslations.zh: 於是入白太后，沈、業奔走告文王，文王為之備。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he went in to inform the empress dowager; Shen and Ye ran to tell Prince Wen, and Prince Wen made preparations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then went to inform the empress dowager while Shen and Ye raced to warn Sima Zhao, who at once made preparations.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝遂帥僮僕數百，鼓譟而出。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor then led several hundred pages and attendants, beating drums and clamoring as he went out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Mao then led several hundred household pages and attendants, beating drums and shouting as he marched out.

manualTranslations.zh: 文王弟屯騎校尉伷入，遇帝於東止車門，左右呵之，伷衆奔走。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince Wen's younger brother, Colonel of the Resolute Cavalry Sima You, entered and met the emperor at the East Halting-Carriage Gate; those at the emperor's side shouted at him, and You's followers fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao's younger brother Sima You, Colonel of the Resolute Cavalry, entered and met the emperor at the East Halting-Carriage Gate; the emperor's attendants shouted him down and You's men broke and ran.

manualTranslations.zh: 中護軍賈充又逆帝戰於南闕下，帝自用劒。
manualTranslations.literal: Colonel of the Central Army Jia Chong again met the emperor in battle below the southern gate-tower; the emperor himself wielded a sword.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Central Army Jia Chong met the emperor in battle below the southern gate-tower; Cao Mao himself drew a sword.

manualTranslations.zh: 衆欲退，太子舍人成濟問充曰：「事急矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The mass wished to retreat; Householder to the Heir Apparent Cheng Ji asked Chong: "The matter is urgent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The troops wavered toward retreat; Cheng Ji, householder to the heir apparent, asked Jia Chong: "The crisis is upon us.

manualTranslations.zh: 當云何？」
manualTranslations.literal: What is to be done?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What are we to do?"

manualTranslations.zh: 充曰：「畜養汝等，正謂今日。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong said: "I raised you all for just this day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong answered: "I raised you for this very day.

manualTranslations.zh: 今日之事，無所問也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Today's affair—ask no questions."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's affair—no questions asked."

manualTranslations.zh: 濟即前刺帝，刃出於背。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji at once went forward and stabbed the emperor; the blade came out from his back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji thrust forward at once; the blade came out through the emperor's back.

manualTranslations.zh: 文王聞，大驚，自投於地曰：「天下其謂我何！」
manualTranslations.literal: When Prince Wen heard, he was greatly alarmed and threw himself to the ground, saying: "What will the realm say of me!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao heard, he was stricken and threw himself to the ground: "What will the realm say of me!"

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅孚奔往，枕帝股而哭，哀甚，曰：「殺陛下者，臣之罪也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Tutor Fu ran to him, pillowed the emperor's thigh and wept, grieving deeply, saying: "To kill Your Majesty is this minister's crime."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Fu ran to the body, pillowed the emperor's thigh, and wept in anguish: "Your Majesty's death is my crime."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為習鑿齒書，雖最後出，然述此事差有次第。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi considers that Xi Zuochi's book, though latest to appear, narrates this affair with better order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that although Xi Zuochi's account appeared last, it narrates the affair in clearer sequence.

manualTranslations.zh: 故先載習語，以其餘所言微異者次其後。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore he first records Xi's words, with other slightly differing accounts following after.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He therefore gives Xi's version first and places the slightly differing accounts afterward.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：王沈、王業馳告文王，尚書王經以正直不出，因沈、業申意。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Accounts of the Age states: Wang Shen and Wang Ye galloped to tell Prince Wen; Master of Writing Wang Jing, being upright, did not go out, and Shen and Ye conveyed his meaning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Shiyu records that Wang Shen and Wang Ye galloped to warn Sima Zhao while Wang Jing, standing on principle, refused to join them; Shen and Ye relayed his intent.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉諸公贊曰：沈、業將出，呼王經。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Commendations of the Jin Dukes states: As Shen and Ye were about to go out, they called for Wang Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Jin zhugong zan adds that as Shen and Ye were leaving they called for Wang Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 經不從，曰：「吾子行矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Jing would not follow, saying: "You gentlemen go!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing would not go, saying only: "You gentlemen go!"

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：成濟問賈充曰：「事急矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Annals states: Cheng Ji asked Jia Chong: "The matter is urgent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin ji states: Cheng Ji asked Jia Chong: "The matter is urgent.

manualTranslations.zh: 若之何？」
manualTranslations.literal: What shall be done?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What shall we do?"

manualTranslations.zh: 充曰：「公畜養汝等，為今日之事也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong said: "The Duke raised you all for today's affair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong said: "The Duke raised you for today's affair.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫何疑！」
manualTranslations.literal: What doubt is there!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What doubt remains!"

manualTranslations.zh: 濟曰：「然。」
manualTranslations.literal: Ji said: "So be it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji said: "So be it."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃抽戈犯蹕。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon drew his halberd and violated the imperial train.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then drew his halberd and charged the imperial train.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：戊子夜，帝自將宂從僕射李昭、黃門從官焦伯等下陵雲臺，鎧仗授兵，欲因際會，自出討文王。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Wei Annals of Spring and Autumn states: On the wuzi night the emperor personally led Palace Vice-Director Li Zhao, Yellow Gate attendant Jiao Bo, and others down from Lingyun Terrace, putting on armor and distributing weapons, intending to seize the moment and go out himself to strike at Prince Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei shi chunqiu states that on wuzi night Cao Mao personally led Palace Vice-Director Li Zhao, Yellow Gate attendant Jiao Bo, and others down from Lingyun Terrace, armored and armed, intending to seize the moment and march against Sima Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 會雨，有司奏却日，遂見王經等出黃素詔於懷曰：「是可忍也，孰不可忍也！
manualTranslations.literal: It rained; the bureaus memorialized to postpone the day; then he saw Wang Jing and the others, took the yellow-silk edict from his bosom and said: "If this can be borne, what cannot be borne!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rain fell; the bureaus asked to postpone the day; then, meeting Wang Jing and the others, he took the yellow-silk edict from his bosom and said: "If this can be borne, what cannot be borne!

manualTranslations.zh: 今日便當決行此事。」
manualTranslations.literal: Today this shall be carried out without fail."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today this shall be done without fail."

manualTranslations.zh: 入白太后，遂拔劒升輦，帥殿中宿衞蒼頭官僮擊戰鼓，出雲龍門。
manualTranslations.literal: He entered to inform the empress dowager, then drew his sword, mounted the palanquin, led the palace night guards, household servants, and attendants to beat the war drums, and went out the Cloud Dragon Gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He informed the empress dowager, drew his sword, mounted the palanquin, had palace night guards and household attendants beat the war drums, and marched out the Cloud Dragon Gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 賈充自外而入，帝師潰散，猶稱天子，手劒奮擊，衆莫敢逼。
manualTranslations.literal: Jia Chong entered from outside; the emperor's forces collapsed, yet he still called himself Son of Heaven, sword in hand striking fiercely, and none dared press him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong entered from outside; the emperor's escort collapsed, yet Cao Mao still called himself Son of Heaven, sword in hand, and none dared close on him.

manualTranslations.zh: 充帥厲將士，騎督成倅弟成濟以矛進，帝崩于師。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong rallied and urged the generals and soldiers; Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Zuo's younger brother Cheng Ji advanced with a spear, and the emperor fell among the troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong rallied the officers and men; Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Zuo's younger brother Cheng Ji thrust in with a spear, and the emperor fell among the troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 時暴雨雷霆，晦冥。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time torrential rain, thunder, and lightning; darkness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thunder, lightning, and torrential rain darkened the sky.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏末傳曰：賈充呼帳下督成濟謂曰：「司馬家事若敗，汝等豈復有種乎？
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei End Annals states: Jia Chong called Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Ji and said: "If the Sima family's affair fails, will you still leave descendants?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei mo zhuan states that Jia Chong called Cheng Ji and said: "If the Sima cause fails, will any of you leave descendants?

manualTranslations.zh: 何不出擊！」
manualTranslations.literal: Why not strike out!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why not strike out!"

manualTranslations.zh: 倅兄弟二人乃帥帳下人出，顧曰：「當殺邪？
manualTranslations.literal: The Zuo brothers then led their subordinates out, turned and said: "Are we to kill or seize?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Cheng brothers led their men out, turned back, and asked: "Kill or seize?

manualTranslations.zh: 執邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Seize?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seize?"

manualTranslations.zh: 充曰：「殺之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Chong said: "Kill him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong said: "Kill him."

manualTranslations.zh: 兵交，帝曰：「放仗！」
manualTranslations.literal: In the clash the emperor said: "Lay down your weapons!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As blades crossed the emperor cried: "Lay down your weapons!"

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍士皆放仗。
manualTranslations.literal: All the Grand General's soldiers laid down their weapons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every soldier of the Grand General laid down his arms.

manualTranslations.zh: 濟兄弟因前刺帝，帝倒車下。
manualTranslations.literal: The Ji brothers thereupon advanced and stabbed the emperor; the emperor fell from the carriage below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Cheng brothers rushed forward and stabbed the emperor; he fell from the carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇太后令曰：「吾以不德，遭家不造，昔援立東海王子髦，以為明帝嗣，見其好書疏文章，兾可成濟，而情性暴戾，日月滋甚。
manualTranslations.literal: An empress dowager order said: "By my lack of virtue I met with family misfortune; formerly I raised the Eastern Sea prince's son Mao as Emperor Ming's heir, seeing that he loved books, memorials, and essays, hoping he could succeed—but his temperament was violent and grew worse day by day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An empress dowager order ran: "Lacking virtue I have met family misfortune. I raised Cao Mao, son of the Prince of the Eastern Sea, as Emperor Ming's heir because he loved books and essays and seemed capable of success—but his temperament was violent and worsened daily.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾數呵責，遂更忿恚，造作醜逆不道之言以誣謗吾，遂隔絕兩宮。
manualTranslations.literal: I repeatedly reproved him; he grew angrier, and fabricated foul, rebellious, and unrighteous words to slander me, cutting off communication between the two palaces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I reproved him again and again; he grew angrier still, invented foul and rebellious words to slander me, and cut off all communication between our palaces.

manualTranslations.zh: 其所言道，不可忍聽，非天地所覆載。
manualTranslations.literal: What he said could not be endured to hear—it is not what Heaven and earth cover and bear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What he said could not be endured—it is not what Heaven and earth cover and bear.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾即密有令語大將軍，不可以奉宗廟，恐顛覆社稷，死無面目以見先帝。
manualTranslations.literal: I secretly commanded the Grand General that he could not continue to serve the ancestral temples, fearing the altars would be overturned and I would have no face to meet the late emperor when dead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I secretly told the Grand General that he could no longer serve the ancestral temples, fearing the altars would be overturned and I would have no face to meet the late emperor after death.

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍以其尚幼，謂當改心為善，殷勤執據。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand General, because he was still young, thought he would change his heart and do good, and earnestly held to that hope.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao, because the boy was still young, hoped he would change and do good, and clung earnestly to that hope.

manualTranslations.zh: 而此兒忿戾，所行益甚，舉弩遙射吾宮，祝當令中吾項，箭親墮吾前。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet this boy, angry and perverse, acted ever worse—raising a crossbow he shot at my palace from afar, praying the bolt would strike my neck; an arrow fell before me in person.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet this boy grew angrier and worse—he raised a crossbow and shot at my palace from afar, praying the bolt would strike my neck; an arrow fell at my feet.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾語大將軍，不可不廢之，前後數十。
manualTranslations.literal: I told the Grand General he must not fail to depose him—dozens of times, back and forth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I told the Grand General he must depose him—dozens of times, back and forth.

manualTranslations.zh: 此兒具聞，自知罪重，便圖為弒逆，賂遺吾左右人，令因吾服藥，密行酖毒，重相設計。
manualTranslations.literal: This boy heard it all, knew his guilt was heavy, and plotted regicide, bribing my attendants to use my taking medicine as occasion to secretly administer poison, repeatedly scheming together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The boy heard it all, knew his guilt was grave, and plotted regicide, bribing my attendants to poison my medicine in secret, scheming again and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 事已覺露，直欲因際會舉兵入西宮殺吾，出取大將軍，呼侍中王沈、散騎常侍王業、《世語》曰：業，武陵人，後為晉中護軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When it was discovered, he meant straightway to seize the moment, raise troops, enter the Western Palace to kill me, go out to seize the Grand General, and summon Palace Attendant Wang Shen, Regular Attendant Wang Ye—〈The Accounts of the Age states: Ye was a native of Wuling and later became Jin's Colonel of the Central Army.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed he meant to seize the moment, raise troops, enter the Western Palace to kill me, go out to seize the Grand General, and summon Wang Shen and Wang Ye—〈the Shiyu notes that Wang Ye was from Wuling and later became Jin Colonel of the Central Army.〉

manualTranslations.zh: 尚書王經，出懷中黃素詔示之，言今日便當施行。
manualTranslations.literal: Master of Writing Wang Jing; he took the yellow-silk edict from his bosom to show them, saying today it would be carried out at once.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also summoned Wang Jing, took the yellow-silk edict from his bosom to show them, and said the deed would be done that very day.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾之危殆，過於累卵。
manualTranslations.literal: My peril exceeded a pile of eggs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My peril was greater than a pile of eggs about to topple.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾老寡，豈復多惜餘命邪？
manualTranslations.literal: I am old and alone—would I still cherish what life remains?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am old and widowed—do I still cling to what life remains?

manualTranslations.zh: 但傷先帝遺意不遂，社稷顛覆為痛耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Only it grieves me that the late emperor's intent is not fulfilled and the altars may be overturned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only the late emperor's unfulfilled intent and the fear of overturned altars grieve me.

manualTranslations.zh: 賴宗廟之靈，沈、業即馳語大將軍，得先嚴警，而此兒便將左右出雲龍門，雷戰鼓，躬自拔刃，與左右雜衞共入兵陣間，為前鋒所害。
manualTranslations.literal: By the grace of the ancestral temples, Shen and Ye at once galloped to tell the Grand General, who was able to warn and secure beforehand; yet this boy then led his attendants out the Cloud Dragon Gate, thundered the war drums, personally drew a blade, and with mixed guards entered among the battle ranks, where he was slain by the vanguard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thanks to the ancestral temples, Shen and Ye galloped to warn the Grand General, who secured himself in time; yet the boy still led his attendants out the Cloud Dragon Gate, beat the war drums, drew a blade himself, and with a mixed guard plunged into the battle line, where the vanguard killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 此兒旣行悖逆不道，而又自陷大禍，重令吾悼心不可言。
manualTranslations.literal: This boy, having pursued rebellion and unrighteousness, also brought great calamity on himself, redoubling my grief beyond words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having pursued rebellion and unrighteousness, he also brought ruin on himself, redoubling grief I cannot speak.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔漢昌邑王以罪廢為庶人，此兒亦宜以民禮葬之，當令內外咸知此兒所行。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the Han Prince of Changyi was deposed for crime and made a commoner; this boy too should be buried with commoner rites, so that inside and outside all may know what he did.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the Han Prince of Changyi was deposed for crime and buried as a commoner, this boy too should receive commoner burial so the whole court may know his deeds.

manualTranslations.zh: 又尚書王經，凶逆無狀，其收經及家屬皆詣廷尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, Master of Writing Wang Jing, rebellious and without proper form, is to be seized together with his family and sent to the Commandant of Justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Wang Jing, being viciously rebellious, is to be seized with his entire household and sent to the Commandant of Justice.

sourceRange.text: 乙亥，詔曰：「」七年春二月，幽州刺史毌丘儉討高句驪，夏五月，討濊貊，皆破之。

localRange.text: 乙亥，詔曰：「明日大會羣臣，其令太傅乘輿上殿。七年春二月，幽州刺史毌丘儉討高句驪，夏五月，討濊貊，皆破之。

localRange.text: 正元元年冬十月壬辰，遣侍中持節分適四方，觀風俗，勞士民，察冤枉失職者。

sourceRange.text: 癸未，安西將軍鄧艾大破蜀大將姜維於上邽，詔曰：「」八月庚午，命大將軍司馬文王加號大都督，奏事不名，假黃鉞。

localRange.text: 癸未，安西將軍鄧艾大破蜀大將姜維於上邽，詔曰：「兵未極武，醜虜摧破，斬首獲生，動以萬計，自頃戰克，無如此者。今遣使者犒賜將士，大會臨饗，飲宴終日，稱朕意焉。八月庚午，命大將軍司馬文王加號大都督，奏事不名，假黃鉞。

context.beforeSource: 秋七月己卯，衞將軍胡遵薨。
context.afterSource: 癸酉，以太尉司馬孚為太傅。

sourceRange.text: 丁丑，詔曰：「」己卯，詔曰：「」六月乙巳，詔：「」臣松之以為壹畏逼歸命，事無可嘉，格以古義，欲蓋而名彰者也。

localRange.text: 丁丑，詔曰：「諸葛誕造為凶亂，盪覆揚州。昔黥布逆叛，漢祖親戎，隗嚻違戾，光武西伐，及烈祖明皇帝躬征吳、蜀，皆所以奮揚赫斯，震耀威武也。今宜皇太后與朕暫共臨戎，速定醜虜，時寧東夏。己卯，詔曰：「諸葛誕造構逆亂，迫脅忠義，平寇將軍臨渭亭侯龐會、騎督偏將軍路蕃，各將左右，斬門突出，忠壯勇烈，所宜嘉異。其進會爵鄉侯，蕃封亭侯。六月乙巳，詔：「吳使持節都督夏口諸軍事鎮軍將軍沙羡侯孫壹，賊之枝屬，位為上將，畏天知命，深鑒禍福，翻然舉衆，遠歸大國，雖微子去殷，樂毅遁燕，無以加之。其以壹為侍中車騎將軍、假節、交州牧、吳侯，開府辟召儀同三司，依古侯伯八命之禮，衮冕赤舄，事從豐厚。〈臣松之以為壹畏逼歸命，事無可嘉，格以古義，欲蓋而名彰者也。
