manualTranslations.zh: 河內太守王匡遣泰山兵屯河陽津，將以圖卓。
manualTranslations.literal: Administrator of Henei Wang Kuang dispatched Taishan troops to garrison Heyang Ford, intending thereby to plot against Zhuo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Administrator of Henei Wang Kuang dispatched Taishan troops to garrison Heyang Ford, intending to move against Dong Zhuo.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓遣疑兵若將於平陰渡者，潛遣銳衆從小平北渡，繞擊其後，大破之津北，死者略盡。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo sent decoy troops as if about to cross at Pingyin, secretly sent crack forces to cross north from Xiaoping, circled to strike their rear, and greatly defeated them north of the ford—those who died were nearly all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sent decoy troops as if about to cross at Pingyin, secretly sent crack forces to cross north from Xiaoping, circled to strike their rear, and routed them north of the ford—nearly all were killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓以山東豪傑並起，恐懼不寧。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo, because heroes east of the mountains rose together, was fearful and ill at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because heroes east of the mountains rose together, Dong Zhuo was fearful and ill at ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 初平元年二月，乃徙天子都長安。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Chuping he then moved the Son of Heaven's capital to Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chuping 1 he moved the Son of Heaven's capital to Chang'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 焚燒洛陽宮室，悉發掘陵墓，取寶物。
manualTranslations.literal: He burned Luoyang's palaces, thoroughly excavated imperial tombs, and took precious objects.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He burned Luoyang's palaces, thoroughly excavated imperial tombs, and seized their treasures.

manualTranslations.zh: 華嶠《漢書》曰：卓欲遷都長安，召公卿以下大議。
manualTranslations.literal: Hua Xiao's Han History says: Zhuo wished to move the capital to Chang'an and summoned the Excellencies and ministers down for great deliberation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hua Xiao's Han History says: Dong Zhuo wished to move the capital to Chang'an and summoned the Excellencies and ministers for deliberation.

manualTranslations.zh: 司徒楊彪曰：「昔盤庚五遷，殷民胥怨，故作三篇以曉天下之民。
manualTranslations.literal: Minister of Education Yang Biao said: "Formerly Pan Geng moved the capital five times—the Yin people all resented it—therefore he composed three pieces to enlighten the people of the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Yang Biao said: "Formerly Pan Geng moved the capital five times—the Yin people all resented it—therefore he composed three pieces to enlighten the people of the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 今海內安穩，無故移都，恐百姓驚動，麋沸蟻聚爲亂。
manualTranslations.literal: Now within the seas is stable and settled—to move the capital without cause may startle the people into seething like a boiling cauldron and swarming like ants into rebellion."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the realm is stable—to move the capital without cause may startle the people into seething like a boiling cauldron and swarming like ants into rebellion."

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓曰：「關中肥饒，故秦得并吞六國。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo said: "Guanzhong is rich and fertile—therefore Qin was able to swallow the six states.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said: "Guanzhong is rich and fertile—therefore Qin was able to swallow the six states.

manualTranslations.zh: 今徙西京，設令關東豪彊敢有動者，以我彊兵踧之，可使詣滄海。
manualTranslations.literal: Now moving to the Western Capital—suppose heroes east of the Pass dared stir—I would trample them with my powerful troops and drive them to the eastern sea."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now moving to the Western Capital—suppose heroes east of the Pass dared stir—I would trample them with my powerful troops and drive them to the eastern sea."

manualTranslations.zh: 」彪曰：「海內動之甚易，安之甚難。
manualTranslations.literal: "Biao said: "To move the realm is very easy; to settle it is very hard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Biao said: "To move the realm is very easy; to settle it is very hard.

manualTranslations.zh: 又長安宮室壞敗，不可卒復。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Chang'an's palaces are ruined and broken—they cannot be quickly restored."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover Chang'an's palaces are ruined and broken—they cannot be quickly restored."

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓曰：「武帝時居杜陵南山下，有成瓦窑數千處，引涼州材木東下以作宮室，爲功不難。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo said: "When Emperor Wu dwelt south of Mount Nan at Duling there were thousands of completed tile kilns—draw Liangzhou timber eastward to build palaces—the task is not hard."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said: "When Emperor Wu dwelt south of Mount Nan at Duling there were thousands of completed tile kilns—draw Liangzhou timber eastward to build palaces—the task is not hard."

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓意不得，便作色曰：「公欲沮我計邪？
manualTranslations.literal: "—Zhuo's intent was not obtained; he changed countenance and said: "Do you, sir, wish to thwart my plan?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's intent was not obtained; he changed countenance and said: "Do you, sir, wish to thwart my plan?

manualTranslations.zh: 邊章、韓約有書來，欲令朝廷必徙都。
manualTranslations.literal: Bian Zhang and Han Yue have sent letters wishing to force the court to move the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bian Zhang and Han Yue have sent letters wishing to force the court to move the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 若大兵來下，我不能復相救，公便可與袁氏西行。
manualTranslations.literal: If great troops come down, I cannot again rescue you—sir may go west with the Yuan clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If great troops come down, I cannot again rescue you—sir may go west with the Yuan clan."

manualTranslations.zh: 」彪曰：「西方自彪道徑也，顧未知天下何如耳！
manualTranslations.literal: "Biao said: "The west is naturally Biao's path—but who knows how the realm will turn out!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Biao said: "The west is naturally my path—but who knows how the realm will turn out!"

manualTranslations.zh: 」議罷。
manualTranslations.literal: Deliberation ended.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deliberation ended.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓勑司隷校尉宣璠以災異劾奏，因策免彪。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo ordered Colonel Director of Retainers Xuan Fan to impeach by memorial on portents and anomalies, and thereby dismissed Biao from office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo ordered Colonel Director of Retainers Xuan Fan to impeach Yang Biao on portents and anomalies and thereby dismissed him from office.

manualTranslations.zh: 《續漢書》曰：太尉黃琬、司徒楊彪、司空荀爽俱詣卓，卓言：「昔高祖都關中，十一世後中興，更都洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: The Xu Hanshu says: Grand Commandant Huang Wan, Minister of Education Yang Biao, and Minister of Works Xun Shuang all went to Zhuo; Zhuo said: "Formerly Gaozu made his capital in Guanzhong; eleven generations later came restoration and the capital was moved to Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Xu Hanshu says: Grand Commandant Huang Wan, Minister of Education Yang Biao, and Minister of Works Xun Shuang all went to Dong Zhuo; Dong Zhuo said: "Formerly Gaozu made his capital in Guanzhong; eleven generations later came restoration and the capital was moved to Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 從光武至今復十一世，案石苞室讖，宜復還都長安。
manualTranslations.literal: From Guangwu until now is again eleven generations—according to Shibao's chamber prophecy, the capital ought again to return to Chang'an."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Guangwu until now is again eleven generations—according to Shibao's chamber prophecy, the capital ought again to return to Chang'an."

manualTranslations.zh: 」坐中皆驚愕，無敢應者。
manualTranslations.literal: All present were startled and dumbstruck—none dared reply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All present were startled and dumbstruck—none dared reply.

manualTranslations.zh: 彪曰：「遷都改制，天下大事，皆當因民之心，隨時之宜。
manualTranslations.literal: Biao said: "Moving the capital and changing institutions are great affairs of the realm—all ought to follow the people's hearts and suit the times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Biao said: "Moving the capital and changing institutions are great affairs of the realm—all ought to follow the people's hearts and suit the times.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔盤庚五遷，殷民胥怨，故作三篇以曉之。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Pan Geng moved five times—the Yin people all resented it—therefore he composed three pieces to enlighten them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Pan Geng moved five times—the Yin people all resented it—therefore he composed three pieces to enlighten them.

manualTranslations.zh: 往者王莽篡逆，變亂五常，更始赤眉之時，焚燒長安，殘害百姓，民人流亡，百無一在。
manualTranslations.literal: In former days Wang Mang usurped and rebelled, overturning the Five Constant norms; in the Gengshi and Red Eyebrows era Chang'an was burned and the people harmed—people fled in exile and not one in a hundred remained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In former days Wang Mang usurped and rebelled, overturning the Five Constant norms; in the Gengshi and Red Eyebrows era Chang'an was burned and the people harmed—people fled in exile and not one in a hundred remained.

manualTranslations.zh: 光武受命，更都洛邑，此其宜也。
manualTranslations.literal: Guangwu received the Mandate and moved the capital to Luoyi—this was fitting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangwu received the Mandate and moved the capital to Luoyi—this was fitting.

manualTranslations.zh: 今方建立聖主，光隆漢祚，而無故捐宮廟，棄園陵，恐百姓驚愕，不解此意，必麋沸蟻聚以致擾亂。
manualTranslations.literal: Now when a sage lord is being established and Han's fortune is being glorified—to without cause abandon palace temples and discard park tombs may startle the people who do not understand this intent—they will surely seethe and swarm into disturbance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now when a sage lord is being established and Han's fortune is being glorified—to without cause abandon palace temples and discard park tombs may startle the people who do not understand this intent—they will surely seethe and swarm into disturbance.

manualTranslations.zh: 石苞室讖，妖邪之書，豈可信用？
manualTranslations.literal: Shibao's chamber prophecy is an evil, heterodox book—how can it be trusted?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shibao's chamber prophecy is an evil, heterodox book—how can it be trusted?"

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓作色曰：「楊公欲沮國家計邪？
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo changed countenance: "Does Lord Yang wish to thwart the state's plan?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo changed countenance: "Does Lord Yang wish to thwart the state's plan?

manualTranslations.zh: 關東方亂，所在賊起。
manualTranslations.literal: East of the Pass is in disorder—bandits rise everywhere.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: East of the Pass is in disorder—bandits rise everywhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 崤函險固，國之重防。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao and Han are perilous and firm—the state's great defense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao and Han are perilous and firm—the state's great defense.

manualTranslations.zh: 又隴右取材，功夫不難。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover timber can be taken from Longyou—the labor is not hard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover timber can be taken from Longyou—the labor is not hard.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜陵南山下有孝武故陶處，作塼瓦，一朝可辦。
manualTranslations.literal: South of Mount Nan at Duling are Emperor Xiaowu's old pottery works—making bricks and tiles can be done in one morning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: South of Mount Nan at Duling are Emperor Wu's old pottery works—making bricks and tiles can be done in one morning.

manualTranslations.zh: 宮室官府，蓋何足言！
manualTranslations.literal: Palaces and government offices—how are they worth mentioning!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Palaces and government offices—how are they worth mentioning!

manualTranslations.zh: 百姓小民，何足與議。
manualTranslations.literal: Common people and petty folk—how are they worth debating with?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Common people and petty folk—how are they worth debating with?

manualTranslations.zh: 若有前郤，我以大兵驅之，豈得自在。
manualTranslations.literal: If any hesitate in advance, I will drive them with great troops—how can they remain at ease?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If any hesitate in advance, I will drive them with great troops—how can they remain at ease?"

manualTranslations.zh: 」百寮恐怖失色。
manualTranslations.literal: The hundred offices trembled in terror and changed color.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The hundred offices trembled in terror and changed color.

manualTranslations.zh: 琬謂卓曰：「此大事。
manualTranslations.literal: Wan said to Zhuo: "This is a great affair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huang Wan said to Dong Zhuo: "This is a great affair.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊公之語，得無重思！
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Yang's words—ought you not reconsider!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lord Yang's words—ought you not reconsider!"

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓罷坐，即日令司隷奏彪及琬，皆免官。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo dismissed the session; that same day he ordered the Colonel Director to memorialize against Biao and Wan—both were dismissed from office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo dismissed the session; that same day he ordered the Colonel Director to memorialize against Yang Biao and Huang Wan—both were dismissed from office.

manualTranslations.zh: 大駕即西。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial carriage immediately went west.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage immediately went west.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓部兵燒洛陽城外面百里。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo's subordinate troops burned a hundred li outside Luoyang's walls.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's subordinate troops burned a hundred li outside Luoyang's walls.

manualTranslations.zh: 又自將兵燒南北宮及宗廟、府庫、民家，城內埽地殄盡。
manualTranslations.literal: He also personally led troops to burn the Southern and Northern Palaces, ancestral temples, treasuries, and commoners' homes—within the city everything was swept bare to extinction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also personally led troops to burn the Southern and Northern Palaces, ancestral temples, treasuries, and commoners' homes—within the city everything was swept bare to extinction.

manualTranslations.zh: 又收諸富室，以罪惡沒入其財物；
manualTranslations.literal: He also seized the wealthy houses, confiscating their goods on charges of crime and evil;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also seized the wealthy houses, confiscating their goods on charges of crime and evil;

manualTranslations.zh: 無辜而死者，不可勝計。
manualTranslations.literal: those who died though innocent were beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: those who died though innocent were beyond counting.

manualTranslations.zh: 《獻帝紀》曰：卓獲山東兵，以豬膏塗布十餘匹，用纏其身，然後燒之，先從足起。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian state: Zhuo captured eastern troops, smeared more than ten bolts of cloth with lard, wrapped his body with them, and then burned him—the fire starting from the feet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian state: Dong Zhuo captured eastern troops, smeared more than ten bolts of cloth with lard, wrapped their bodies with them, and then burned them—the fire starting from the feet.

manualTranslations.zh: 獲袁紹豫州從事李延，煑殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: He captured Yuan Shao's Staff Officer of Yuzhou Li Yan and boiled him to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He captured Yuan Shao's Staff Officer of Yuzhou Li Yan and boiled him to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓所愛胡，恃寵放縱，爲司隷校尉趙謙所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: A Hu man Zhuo favored, relying on favor and acting lawlessly, was killed by Colonel Director of Retainers Zhao Qian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A Hu man Dong Zhuo favored, relying on favor and acting lawlessly, was killed by Colonel Director of Retainers Zhao Qian.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓大怒曰：「我愛狗，尚不欲令人呵之，而況人乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo raged: "Even a dog I love—I still do not wish others to scold it—how much more a man!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo raged: "Even a dog I love—I still do not wish others to scold it—how much more a man!

manualTranslations.zh: 」乃召司隷都官撾殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: "He thereupon summoned the Colonel Director's chief officer and beat him to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He thereupon summoned the Colonel Director's chief officer and beat him to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓至西京，爲太師，號曰尚父。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo reached the Western Capital and became Grand Tutor, styled Sire Father.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo reached the Western Capital and became Grand Tutor, styled Sire Father.

manualTranslations.zh: 乘青蓋金華車，爪畫兩轓，時人號曰竿摩車。
manualTranslations.literal: He rode a green-canopied golden-flower carriage with claw patterns on both side boards—people of the time called it the Pole-Brush Carriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rode a green-canopied golden-flower carriage with claw patterns on both side boards—people of the time called it the Pole-Brush Carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：言其逼天子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei says: it spoke of his pressing upon the Son of Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says: it spoke of his pressing upon the Son of Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 《獻帝紀》曰：卓旣爲太師，復欲稱尚父，以問蔡邕。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian state: Zhuo, having become Grand Tutor, again wished to style himself Sire Father and asked Cai Yong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian state: Dong Zhuo, having become Grand Tutor, again wished to style himself Sire Father and asked Cai Yong.

manualTranslations.zh: 邕曰：「昔武王受命，太公爲師，輔佐周室，以伐無道，是以天下尊之，稱爲尚父。
manualTranslations.literal: Yong said: "Formerly when King Wu received the Mandate, the Grand Duke became tutor, aided the Zhou house, and punished the wayless—therefore the realm honored him and called him Sire Father.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cai Yong said: "Formerly when King Wu received the Mandate, the Grand Duke became tutor, aided the Zhou house, and punished the wayless—therefore the realm honored him and called him Sire Father.

manualTranslations.zh: 今公之功德誠爲巍巍，宜須關東悉定，車駕東還，然後議之。
manualTranslations.literal: Now your lordship's merits and virtue are truly towering—but you ought to wait until east of the Pass is entirely settled and the imperial carriage returns east, and then deliberate on it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now your lordship's merits and virtue are truly towering—but you ought to wait until east of the Pass is entirely settled and the imperial carriage returns east, and then deliberate on it."

manualTranslations.zh: 」乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He thereupon stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 京師地震，卓又問邕。
manualTranslations.literal: The capital quaked; Zhuo again asked Yong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The capital quaked; Dong Zhuo again asked Cai Yong.

manualTranslations.zh: 邕對曰：「地動陰盛，大臣踰制之所致也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yong replied: "Earth moves when yin flourishes—it stems from great ministers overstepping their stations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cai Yong replied: "Earth moves when yin flourishes—it stems from great ministers overstepping their stations.

manualTranslations.zh: 公乘青蓋車，遠近以爲非宜。
manualTranslations.literal: Your lordship riding a green-canopied carriage—far and near deem it unsuitable."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your lordship riding a green-canopied carriage—far and near deem it unsuitable."

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓從之，更乘金華皂蓋車也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo followed this and changed to a golden-flower black-canopied carriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo followed this and changed to a golden-flower black-canopied carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓弟旻爲左將軍，封鄠侯；
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo's younger brother Min became General of the Household on the Left and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hu;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's younger brother Min became General of the Household on the Left and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hu;

manualTranslations.zh: 兄子璜爲侍中中軍校尉典兵；
manualTranslations.literal: his elder brother's son Huang became Palace Attendant, Colonel of the Central Army, and held command of troops;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: his elder brother's son Huang became Palace Attendant, Colonel of the Central Army, and held command of troops;

manualTranslations.zh: 宗族內外並列朝廷。
manualTranslations.literal: kinsmen inside and outside all ranked in the court together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: kinsmen inside and outside all ranked in the court together.

manualTranslations.zh: 《英雄記》曰：卓侍妾懷抱中子，皆封侯，弄以金紫。
manualTranslations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Zhuo's concubines held infant sons in their arms—all were enfeoffed as marquises and dressed in gold seals and purple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong Ji says: Dong Zhuo's concubines held infant sons in their arms—all were enfeoffed as marquises and dressed in gold seals and purple.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫女名白，時尚未笄，封爲渭陽君。
manualTranslations.literal: A granddaughter named Bai, not yet come of age, was enfeoffed as Lady of Weiyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A granddaughter named Bai, not yet come of age, was enfeoffed as Lady of Weiyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 於郿城東起壇，從廣二丈餘，高五六尺，使白乘軒金華青蓋車，都尉、中郎將、刺史二千石在郿者，各令乘軒簪筆，爲白導從，之壇上，使兄子璜爲使者授印綬。
manualTranslations.literal: East of Mei city they raised an altar more than two zhang in width and five or six chi in height; they had Bai ride a carriage with rails, golden flowers, and green canopy; commandants, gentlemen-generals, and two-thousand-bushel inspectors at Mei were each ordered to ride carriages with rails and wear writing brushes in their caps as Bai's guides and attendants to the altar; Zhuo's nephew Huang as envoy bestowed seals and ribbons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: East of Mei city they raised an altar more than two zhang in width and five or six chi in height; they had Bai ride a carriage with rails, golden flowers, and green canopy; commandants, gentlemen-generals, and two-thousand-bushel inspectors at Mei were each ordered to ride carriages with rails and wear writing brushes in their caps as Bai's guides and attendants to the altar; Dong Zhuo's nephew Huang as envoy bestowed seals and ribbons.

manualTranslations.zh: 公卿見卓，謁拜車下，卓不爲禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Excellencies and ministers seeing Zhuo bowed and paid respects below his carriage—Zhuo did not return the courtesy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Excellencies and ministers seeing Dong Zhuo bowed and paid respects below his carriage—Dong Zhuo did not return the courtesy.

manualTranslations.zh: 召呼三臺尚書以下自詣卓府啟事。
manualTranslations.literal: He summoned and called the Three Bureau masters of writing down to come themselves to Zhuo's mansion to report affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He summoned the Three Bureau masters of writing down to come themselves to Dong Zhuo's mansion to report affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 《山陽公載記》曰：初卓爲前將軍，皇甫嵩爲左將軍，俱征韓遂，各不相下。
manualTranslations.literal: The Register of the Duke of Shanyang says: At first Zhuo was Forward General and Huangfu Song was General of the Household on the Left—both campaigning against Han Sui and neither yielding to the other.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Register of the Duke of Shanyang says: At first Dong Zhuo was Forward General and Huangfu Song was General of the Household on the Left—both campaigning against Han Sui and neither yielding to the other.

manualTranslations.zh: 後卓徵爲少府并州牧，兵當屬嵩，卓大怒。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Zhuo was summoned as Minister Coachman and Governor of Bing Province; his troops ought to pass to Song—Zhuo raged greatly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Dong Zhuo was summoned as Minister Coachman and Governor of Bing Province; his troops ought to pass to Huangfu Song—Dong Zhuo raged greatly.

manualTranslations.zh: 及爲太師，嵩爲御史中丞，拜於車下。
manualTranslations.literal: When he became Grand Tutor, Song was Censor-in-Chief and bowed below his carriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he became Grand Tutor, Huangfu Song was Censor-in-Chief and bowed below his carriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓問嵩：「義真服未乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo asked Song: "Yizhen, are you convinced yet?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo asked Huangfu Song: "Yizhen, are you convinced yet?

manualTranslations.zh: 」嵩曰：「安知明公乃至於是！
manualTranslations.literal: "Song said: "Who knew Your Excellency would come to this!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song said: "Who knew Your Excellency would come to this!

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓曰：「鴻鵠固有遠志，但燕雀自不知耳。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo said: "The swan indeed has distant ambitions—only sparrows do not know it themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo said: "The swan indeed has distant ambitions—only sparrows do not know it themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 」嵩曰：「昔與明公俱爲鴻鵠，不意今日變爲鳳皇耳。
manualTranslations.literal: "Song said: "Formerly I and Your Excellency were both swans—I never expected today to change into phoenixes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song said: "Formerly I and Your Excellency were both swans—I never expected today to change into phoenixes.

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓笑曰：「卿早服，今日可不拜也。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo laughed: "If you had yielded earlier, today you need not bow."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo laughed: "If you had yielded earlier, today you need not bow."

manualTranslations.zh: 」張璠《漢紀》曰：卓抵其手謂皇甫嵩曰：「義真怖未乎？
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhang Fan's Han Ji says: Zhuo took his hand and said to Huangfu Song: "Yizhen, are you frightened yet?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han Ji says: Dong Zhuo took his hand and said to Huangfu Song: "Yizhen, are you frightened yet?

manualTranslations.zh: 」嵩對曰：「明公以德輔朝廷，大慶方至，何怖之有？
manualTranslations.literal: "Song replied: "Your Excellency aids the court with virtue—great celebration is just arriving—what fear is there?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huangfu Song replied: "Your Excellency aids the court with virtue—great celebration is just arriving—what fear is there?

manualTranslations.zh: 若淫刑以逞，將天下皆懼，豈獨嵩乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If you indulge cruel punishments to gratify yourself, all the realm will fear—how only Song?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you indulge cruel punishments to gratify yourself, all the realm will fear—how only I?

manualTranslations.zh: 」卓默然，遂與嵩和解。
manualTranslations.literal: "Zhuo fell silent and thereupon made peace with Song.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo fell silent and thereupon made peace with Huangfu Song.

manualTranslations.zh: 築郿塢，高與長安城埒，積穀爲三十年儲，《英雄記》曰：郿去長安二百六十里。
manualTranslations.literal: He built the Mei fortress, as high as Chang'an's walls, storing grain for thirty years' provision; the Yingxiong Ji says: Mei was two hundred sixty li from Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He built the Mei fortress, as high as Chang'an's walls, storing grain for thirty years' provision; the Yingxiong Ji says: Mei was two hundred sixty li from Chang'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 云事成，雄據天下，不成，守此足以畢老。
manualTranslations.literal: He said if affairs succeeded he would dominate the realm by force; if not, holding this would suffice to end his days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He said if affairs succeeded he would dominate the realm by force; if not, holding this would suffice to end his days.

manualTranslations.zh: 甞至郿行塢，公卿已下祖道於橫門外。
manualTranslations.literal: Once when he went to Mei to inspect the fortress, the Excellencies down escorted him at farewell outside Heng Gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once when he went to Mei to inspect the fortress, the Excellencies down escorted him at farewell outside Heng Gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 橫音光。
manualTranslations.literal: Heng is pronounced guang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heng is pronounced guang.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓豫施帳幔飲，誘降北地反者數百人，於坐中先斷其舌，或斬手足，或鑿眼，或鑊煑之，未死，偃轉杯案閒，會者皆戰慄亡失匕箸，而卓飲食自若。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuo set up tents and curtains beforehand to drink; he lured several hundred northern rebels to surrender; at the feast he first cut out their tongues, or hacked off hands and feet, or gouged eyes, or boiled them in cauldrons—not yet dead they writhed among cups and platters; those present all trembled and lost spoons and chopsticks—yet Zhuo ate and drank at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo set up tents and curtains beforehand to drink; he lured several hundred northern rebels to surrender; at the feast he first cut out their tongues, or hacked off hands and feet, or gouged eyes, or boiled them in cauldrons—not yet dead they writhed among cups and platters; those present all trembled and lost spoons and chopsticks—yet Dong Zhuo ate and drank at ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 太史望氣，言當有大臣戮死者。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand astrologer read the vapors and said a great minister would be executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand astrologer read the vapors and said a great minister would be executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 故太尉張溫時爲衞尉，素不善卓，卓心怨之，因天有變，欲以塞咎，使人言溫與袁術交關，遂笞殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Former Grand Commandant Zhang Wen was then Minister of the Guards—he had never been on good terms with Zhuo and Zhuo resented him inwardly; because heaven had changes he wished to fill the blame, had men say Wen had covert dealings with Yuan Shu, and thereupon flogged him to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Former Grand Commandant Zhang Wen was then Minister of the Guards—he had never been on good terms with Dong Zhuo and Dong Zhuo resented him inwardly; because heaven had changes he wished to fill the blame, had men say Wen had covert dealings with Yuan Shu, and thereupon flogged him to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 《傅子》曰：靈帝時牓門賣官，於是太尉段熲、司徒崔烈、太尉樊陵、司空張溫之徒，皆入錢上千萬下五百萬以買三公。
manualTranslations.literal: The Fu Zi says: In Emperor Ling's time offices were sold at the palace wall—thereupon Grand Commandant Duan Yong, Minister of Education Cui Lie, Grand Commandant Fan Ling, Minister of Works Zhang Wen and the like all paid money from above ten million down to five million to buy the three excellencies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Fu Zi says: In Emperor Ling's time offices were sold at the palace wall—thereupon Grand Commandant Duan Yong, Minister of Education Cui Lie, Grand Commandant Fan Ling, Minister of Works Zhang Wen and the like all paid money from above ten million down to five million to buy the three excellencies.

manualTranslations.zh: 熲數征伐有大功，烈有北州重名，溫有傑才，陵能偶時，皆一時顯士，猶以貨取位，而況於劉嚻、唐珍、張顥之黨乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Yong had great merit through repeated campaigns; Lie had heavy fame in the Northern Provinces; Wen had outstanding talent; Ling could match the times—all were illustrious men of the age—yet still took office by wealth—how much more the clique of Liu Hao, Tang Zhen, and Zhang Hao!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duan Yong had great merit through repeated campaigns; Cui Lie had heavy fame in the Northern Provinces; Zhang Wen had outstanding talent; Fan Ling could match the times—all were illustrious men of the age—yet still took office by wealth—how much more the clique of Liu Hao, Tang Zhen, and Zhang Hao!

manualTranslations.zh: 風俗通曰：司隷劉嚻以黨諸常侍，致位公輔。
manualTranslations.literal: Fengsu Tong says: Colonel Director Liu Hao, by allying with the various regular attendants, reached the rank of excellency and aide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fengsu Tong says: Colonel Director Liu Hao, by allying with the various regular attendants, reached the rank of excellency and aide.

manualTranslations.zh: 《續漢書》曰：唐珍，中常侍唐衡弟。
manualTranslations.literal: The Xu Hanshu says: Tang Zhen was younger brother of Regular Palace Attendant Tang Heng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Xu Hanshu says: Tang Zhen was younger brother of Regular Palace Attendant Tang Heng.

manualTranslations.zh: 張顥，中常侍張奉弟。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Hao was younger brother of Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Feng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao was younger brother of Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Feng.

manualTranslations.zh: 法令苛酷，愛憎淫刑，更相被誣，冤死者千數。
manualTranslations.literal: Laws were harsh and cruel; favor and hatred drove wanton punishment; they mutually accused one another—and those who died unjustly numbered in the thousands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Laws were harsh and cruel; favor and hatred drove wanton punishment; they mutually accused one another—and those who died unjustly numbered in the thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 百姓嗷嗷，道路以目。
manualTranslations.literal: The people wailed; on the roads they exchanged glances only with their eyes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people wailed; on the roads they exchanged glances only with their eyes.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：卓使司隷校尉劉嚻籍吏民有爲子不孝，爲臣不忠，爲吏不清，爲弟不順，有應此者皆身誅，財物沒官。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Zhuo had Colonel Director Liu Hao register clerks and commoners—those whose sons were unfilial, whose subjects were unloyal, whose officials were unclean, whose younger brothers were uncompliant—whoever matched these were all personally executed and goods confiscated to the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says: Dong Zhuo had Colonel Director Liu Hao register clerks and commoners—those whose sons were unfilial, whose subjects were unloyal, whose officials were unclean, whose younger brothers were uncompliant—whoever matched these were all personally executed and goods confiscated to the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是愛憎互起，民多冤死。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon favor and hatred arose mutually and many people died unjustly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon favor and hatred arose mutually and many people died unjustly.

manualTranslations.zh: 悉椎破銅人、鍾虡，及壞五銖錢。
manualTranslations.literal: He thoroughly smashed the bronze men, bell stands, and also broke the five-zhu coins.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He thoroughly smashed the bronze men, bell stands, and also broke the five-zhu coins.

manualTranslations.zh: 更鑄爲小錢，大五分，無文章，肉好無輪郭，不磨鑢。
manualTranslations.literal: He recast them as small cash—large as five fen, without inscriptions; rim and hole without edge, not ground or filed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He recast them as small cash—large as five fen, without inscriptions; rim and hole without edge, not ground or filed.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是貨輕而物貴，穀一斛至數十萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon goods were cheap and commodities dear—grain reached several hundred thousand per hu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon money was cheap and commodities dear—grain reached several hundred thousand per hu.

manualTranslations.zh: 自是後錢貨不行。
manualTranslations.literal: From this onward coin and currency did not circulate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this onward coin and currency did not circulate.

context.beforeSource: 饑窮稍甚，尚書郎以下自出樵采，或饑死牆壁閒。

sourceRange.text: 呂布之捨袁紹從張楊也，過邈臨別，把手共誓。紹聞之，大恨。邈畏太祖終爲紹擊己也，心不自安。興平元年194年，太祖復征謙，邈弟超，與太祖將陳宮、從事中郎許汜、王楷共謀叛太祖。宮說邈曰：「今雄傑並起，天下分崩，君以千里之衆，當四戰之地，撫劒顧眄，亦足以爲人豪，而反制於人，不以鄙乎！今州軍東征，其處空虛，呂布壯士，善戰無前，若權迎之，共牧兖州，觀天下形勢，俟時事之變通，此亦縱橫之一時也。」邈從之。太祖初使宮將兵留屯東郡，遂以其衆東迎布爲兖州牧，據濮陽。郡縣皆應，唯鄄城、東阿、范爲太祖守。太祖引軍還，與布戰於濮陽，太祖軍不利，相持百餘日。是時歲旱、蟲蝗、少穀，百姓相食，布東屯山陽。二年間，太祖乃盡復收諸城，擊破布於鉅野。布東奔劉備。

context.beforeSource: 其親如此。
context.afterSource: 《英雄記》曰：布見備，甚敬之，謂備曰：「我與卿同邊地人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 呂布之捨袁紹從張楊也，過邈臨別，把手共誓。
manualTranslations.literal: When Bu left Shao to follow Zhang Yang, he passed Miao; at parting they clasped hands and swore together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu left Yuan Shao to follow Zhang Yang, he passed Zhang Miao; at parting they clasped hands and swore together.

manualTranslations.zh: 紹聞之，大恨。
manualTranslations.literal: Shao heard of it and hated it greatly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao heard of it and hated it greatly.

manualTranslations.zh: 邈畏太祖終爲紹擊己也，心不自安。
manualTranslations.literal: Miao feared Grand Progenitor would in the end strike him on Shao's behalf, and his heart was ill at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao feared Cao Cao would eventually strike him for Yuan Shao's sake, and his heart was ill at ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 興平元年194年，太祖復征謙，邈弟超，與太祖將陳宮、從事中郎許汜、王楷共謀叛太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Xingping (194), Grand Progenitor again campaigned against Qian; Miao's younger brother Chao, together with Grand Progenitor's general Chen Gong, Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xu Si, and Wang Kai jointly plotted to rebel against Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xingping 1 (194), while Cao Cao marched again against Tao Qian, Zhang Miao's younger brother Zhang Chao joined Cao Cao's general Chen Gong, Attendant of the Masters of Writing Xu Si, and Wang Kai in a plot to rebel.

manualTranslations.zh: 宮說邈曰：「今雄傑並起，天下分崩，君以千里之衆，當四戰之地，撫劒顧眄，亦足以爲人豪，而反制於人，不以鄙乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Gong said to Miao: "Heroes are rising together now and the realm is splitting apart. With a host of a thousand li in a land fought over from four sides, you need only grip your sword and look about to be a lord among men—yet you submit to another's control. Is that not shameful?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Gong told Zhang Miao: "Heroes are rising everywhere and the realm is splitting apart. With a host of a thousand li in a land fought over from four sides, you need only grip your sword and look about to be a lord among men—yet you submit to another's control. Is that not shameful?

manualTranslations.zh: 今州軍東征，其處空虛，呂布壯士，善戰無前，若權迎之，共牧兖州，觀天下形勢，俟時事之變通，此亦縱橫之一時也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The provincial army is campaigning east and the place is empty. Lü Bu is a fierce warrior, peerless in battle. If you seize the moment and welcome him to jointly govern Yan Province, watch the shape of the realm, and await the shifts of affairs—this too is a season for maneuver."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's army is campaigning east and the province is empty. Lü Bu is a fierce warrior, peerless in battle. Welcome him for the moment, govern Yan Province together, watch the realm's shape, and await shifting fortunes—this too is a season for maneuver."

manualTranslations.zh: 邈從之。
manualTranslations.literal: Miao followed this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖初使宮將兵留屯東郡，遂以其衆東迎布爲兖州牧，據濮陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Progenitor had earlier sent Gong to lead troops and remain garrisoned in Dong Commandery; he now took his forces east to welcome Bu as Governor of Yan Province and seized Puyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had earlier left Chen Gong to garrison Dong Commandery; Chen Gong now led those troops east to welcome Lü Bu as Governor of Yan Province and seized Puyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 郡縣皆應，唯鄄城、東阿、范爲太祖守。
manualTranslations.literal: The counties and districts all responded; only Juancheng, Dong'e, and Fan remained loyal to Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The counties and districts all responded; only Juancheng, Dong'e, and Fan held for Cao Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖引軍還，與布戰於濮陽，太祖軍不利，相持百餘日。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Progenitor brought his army back and fought Bu at Puyang; Grand Progenitor's army fared poorly and they remained locked for over a hundred days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao brought his army back and fought Lü Bu at Puyang; Cao Cao's army fared poorly and they remained locked for over a hundred days.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時歲旱、蟲蝗、少穀，百姓相食，布東屯山陽。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time drought, locusts, and scarce grain drove the people to cannibalism; Bu encamped east at Shanyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Drought, locusts, and famine drove the people to cannibalism; Lü Bu encamped east at Shanyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年間，太祖乃盡復收諸城，擊破布於鉅野。
manualTranslations.literal: Within two years Grand Progenitor recovered every city and defeated Bu at Juye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within two years Cao Cao recovered every city and defeated Lü Bu at Juye.

manualTranslations.zh: 布東奔劉備。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu fled east to Liu Bei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled east to Liu Bei.

sourceRange.text: 備東擊術，布襲取下邳，備還歸布。布遣備屯小沛。布自稱徐州刺史。*|《英雄記》曰：布初入徐州，書與袁術。術報書曰：「昔董卓作亂，破壞王室，禍害術門戶，術舉兵關東，未能屠裂卓。將軍誅卓，送其頭首，爲術掃滅讐耻，使術明目於當世，死生不愧，其功一也。昔將金元休向兖州，甫詣封，爲曹操逆所拒破，流離迸走，幾至滅亡。將軍破兖州，術復明目於遐邇，其功二也。術生年已來，不聞天下有劉備，備乃舉兵與術對戰；術憑將軍威靈，得以破備，其功三也。將軍有三大功在術，術雖不敏，奉以生死。將軍連年攻戰，軍糧苦少，今送米二十萬斛，迎逢道路，非直此止，當駱驛復致；若兵器戰具，佗所乏少，大小唯命。」布得書大喜，遂造下邳。《典略》曰：元休名尚，京兆人也。尚與同郡韋休甫、第五文休俱著名，號爲三休。尚，獻帝初爲兖州刺史，東之郡，而太祖已臨兖州。尚南依袁術。術僭號，欲以尚爲太尉，不敢顯言，私使人諷之，尚無屈意，術亦不敢彊也。建安初，尚逃還，爲術所害。其後尚喪與太傅馬日磾喪俱至京師，天子嘉尚忠烈，爲之咨嗟，詔百官弔祭，拜子瑋郎中，而日磾不與焉。《英雄記》曰：布水陸東下，軍到下邳西四十里。備中郎將丹楊許耽夜遣司馬章誑來詣布，言「張益德與下邳相曹豹共爭，益德殺豹，城中大亂，不相信。丹楊兵有千人屯西白城門內，聞將軍來東，大小踊躍，如復更生。將軍兵向城西門，丹楊軍便開門內將軍矣」。布遂夜進，晨到城下。天明，丹楊兵悉開門內布兵。布於門上坐，步騎放火，大破益德兵，獲備妻子軍資及部曲將吏士家口。建安元年六月夜半時，布將河內郝萌反，將兵入布所治下邳府，詣廳事閤外，同聲大呼攻閤，閤堅不得入。布不知反者爲誰，直牽婦，科頭袒衣，相將從溷上排壁出，詣都督高順營，直排順門入。順問：「將軍有所隱不？」布言「河內兒聲」。順言「此郝萌也」。順即嚴兵入府，弓弩並射萌衆；萌衆亂走，天明還故營。萌將曹性反萌，與對戰，萌刺傷性，性斫萌一臂。順斫萌首，牀輿性，送詣布。布問性，言「萌受袁術謀，謀者悉誰？」性言「陳宮同謀。」時宮在坐上，靣赤，傍人悉覺之。布以宮大將，不問也。性言「萌常以此問，性言呂將軍大將有神，不可擊也，不意萌狂惑不止。」布謂性曰：「卿健兒也！」善養視之。創愈，使安撫萌故營，領其衆。術遣將紀靈等步騎三萬攻備，備求救於布。布諸將謂布曰：「將軍常欲殺備，今可假手於術。」布曰：「不然。術若破備，則北連太山諸將，吾爲在術圍中，不得不救也。」便嚴步兵千、騎二百，馳往赴備。靈等聞布至，皆斂兵不敢復攻。布於沛西南一里安屯，遣鈴下請靈等，靈等亦請布共飲食。布謂靈等曰：「玄德，布弟也。弟爲諸君所困，故來救之。布性不喜合鬬，但喜解鬬耳。」布令門候於營門中舉一隻戟，布言：「諸君觀布射戟小支，一發中者諸君當解去，不中可留決鬬。」布舉弓射戟，正中小支。諸將皆驚，言「將軍天威也」！明日復歡會，然後各罷。

items.acceptedSourceText: 備東擊術，布襲取下邳，備還歸布。布遣備屯小沛。布自稱徐州刺史。〈《英雄記》曰：布初入徐州，書與袁術。術報書曰：「昔董卓作亂，破壞王室，禍害術門戶，術舉兵關東，未能屠裂卓。將軍誅卓，送其頭首，爲術掃滅讐耻，使術明目於當世，死生不愧，其功一也。昔將金元休向兖州，甫詣封，爲曹操逆所拒破，流離迸走，幾至滅亡。將軍破兖州，術復明目於遐邇，其功二也。術生年已來，不聞天下有劉備，備乃舉兵與術對戰；術憑將軍威靈，得以破備，其功三也。將軍有三大功在術，術雖不敏，奉以生死。將軍連年攻戰，軍糧苦少，今送米二十萬斛，迎逢道路，非直此止，當駱驛復致；若兵器戰具，佗所乏少，大小唯命。」布得書大喜，遂造下邳。《典略》曰：元休名尚，京兆人也。尚與同郡韋休甫、第五文休俱著名，號爲三休。尚，獻帝初爲兖州刺史，東之郡，而太祖已臨兖州。尚南依袁術。術僭號，欲以尚爲太尉，不敢顯言，私使人諷之，尚無屈意，術亦不敢彊也。建安初，尚逃還，爲術所害。其後尚喪與太傅馬日磾喪俱至京師，天子嘉尚忠烈，爲之咨嗟，詔百官弔祭，拜子瑋郎中，而日磾不與焉。《英雄記》曰：布水陸東下，軍到下邳西四十里。備中郎將丹楊許耽夜遣司馬章誑來詣布，言「張益德與下邳相曹豹共爭，益德殺豹，城中大亂，不相信。丹楊兵有千人屯西白城門內，聞將軍來東，大小踊躍，如復更生。將軍兵向城西門，丹楊軍便開門內將軍矣」。布遂夜進，晨到城下。天明，丹楊兵悉開門內布兵。布於門上坐，步騎放火，大破益德兵，獲備妻子軍資及部曲將吏士家口。建安元年六月夜半時，布將河內郝萌反，將兵入布所治下邳府，詣廳事閤外，同聲大呼攻閤，閤堅不得入。布不知反者爲誰，直牽婦，科頭袒衣，相將從溷上排壁出，詣都督高順營，直排順門入。順問：「將軍有所隱不？」布言「河內兒聲」。順言「此郝萌也」。順即嚴兵入府，弓弩並射萌衆；萌衆亂走，天明還故營。萌將曹性反萌，與對戰，萌刺傷性，性斫萌一臂。順斫萌首，牀輿性，送詣布。布問性，言「萌受袁術謀，謀者悉誰？」性言「陳宮同謀。」時宮在坐上，靣赤，傍人悉覺之。布以宮大將，不問也。性言「萌常以此問，性言呂將軍大將有神，不可擊也，不意萌狂惑不止。」布謂性曰：「卿健兒也！」善養視之。創愈，使安撫萌故營，領其衆。術遣將紀靈等步騎三萬攻備，備求救於布。布諸將謂布曰：「將軍常欲殺備，今可假手於術。」布曰：「不然。術若破備，則北連太山諸將，吾爲在術圍中，不得不救也。」便嚴步兵千、騎二百，馳往赴備。靈等聞布至，皆斂兵不敢復攻。布於沛西南一里安屯，遣鈴下請靈等，靈等亦請布共飲食。布謂靈等曰：「玄德，布弟也。弟爲諸君所困，故來救之。布性不喜合鬬，但喜解鬬耳。」布令門候於營門中舉一隻戟，布言：「諸君觀布射戟小支，一發中者諸君當解去，不中可留決鬬。」布舉弓射戟，正中小支。諸將皆驚，言「將軍天威也」！明日復歡會，然後各罷。

manualTranslations.zh: 備東擊術，布襲取下邳，備還歸布。
manualTranslations.literal: Bei campaigned east against Shu; Bu raided and seized Xiapi; Bei returned and submitted to Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei marched east against Yuan Shu; Lü Bu seized Xiapi by surprise; Liu Bei returned and submitted to Lü Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 布遣備屯小沛。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu sent Bei to garrison Xiaopei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu sent Liu Bei to garrison Xiaopei.

manualTranslations.zh: 布自稱徐州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu styled himself Inspector of Xu Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu styled himself Inspector of Xu Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：布初入徐州，書與袁術。
manualTranslations.literal: 〈The Yingxiong ji says: When Bu first entered Xu Province, he wrote to Yuan Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈The Record of Heroes says: when Lü Bu first entered Xu Province, he wrote to Yuan Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 術報書曰：「昔董卓作亂，破壞王室，禍害術門戶，術舉兵關東，未能屠裂卓。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu replied in writing: "Formerly Dong Zhuo raised rebellion, destroyed the royal house, and harmed Shu's household; Shu raised troops east of the Pass but could not slaughter Zhuo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu replied: "When Dong Zhuo raised rebellion, he destroyed the royal house and harmed my house. I raised troops east of the mountains but could not destroy him.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍誅卓，送其頭首，爲術掃滅讐耻，使術明目於當世，死生不愧，其功一也。
manualTranslations.literal: The General executed Zhuo and sent his head, sweeping away Shu's feud shame for him, letting Shu hold his head high in the age without shame in life or death—this is your first merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You executed Dong Zhuo and sent me his head, wiping away my blood feud and letting me hold my head high in the age—your first merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔將金元休向兖州，甫詣封，爲曹操逆所拒破，流離迸走，幾至滅亡。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly General Jin Yuansxiu went toward Yan Province; just as he reached Feng he was repulsed and broken by the rebel Cao Cao, fled in disorder, and nearly perished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly General Jin Yuansxiu went toward Yan Province; just as he reached his commandery he was beaten back by Cao Cao, fled in disorder, and nearly perished.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍破兖州，術復明目於遐邇，其功二也。
manualTranslations.literal: The General broke Yan Province and Shu again held his head high far and near—this is your second merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You broke Yan Province and restored my standing far and near—your second merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 術生年已來，不聞天下有劉備，備乃舉兵與術對戰；
manualTranslations.literal: In all the years of Shu's life he had not heard that the realm held Liu Bei; Bei then raised troops to fight Shu;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In all my years I had never heard of Liu Bei in the realm, yet he raised troops to fight me;

manualTranslations.zh: 術憑將軍威靈，得以破備，其功三也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu relied on the General's numinous might and was able to defeat Bei—this is your third merit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I relied on your prestige to defeat him—your third merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍有三大功在術，術雖不敏，奉以生死。
manualTranslations.literal: The General has three great merits toward Shu; though Shu is not clever, he offers life and death in return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have done three great deeds for me; though I am no sage, I offer you my life.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍連年攻戰，軍糧苦少，今送米二十萬斛，迎逢道路，非直此止，當駱驛復致；
manualTranslations.literal: The General has campaigned year after year and military grain is painfully scarce; now I send two hundred thousand hu of rice, meeting you on the road—not only this, but more will follow in relays;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have fought year after year and grain runs short; I now send two hundred thousand hu of rice to meet you on the road—not this alone, but more will follow in relays;

manualTranslations.zh: 若兵器戰具，佗所乏少，大小唯命。」
manualTranslations.literal: if weapons and war gear or anything else you lack, great or small, command as you will."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and for weapons, gear, or anything else you lack, great or small, command as you will."

manualTranslations.zh: 布得書大喜，遂造下邳。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu received the letter and was greatly pleased; he thereupon went to Xiapi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was delighted by the letter and went on to Xiapi.

manualTranslations.zh: 《典略》曰：元休名尚，京兆人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Dianlüe says: Yuansxiu's given name was Shang; he was a man of Jingzhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account says: Yuansxiu's given name was Shang, a native of Jingzhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚與同郡韋休甫、第五文休俱著名，號爲三休。
manualTranslations.literal: Shang, together with Wei Xiufu of the same commandery and Diwu Wenxiu, were all famous and were styled the Three Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shang, Wei Xiufu of the same commandery, and Diwu Wenxiu were all famous and were styled the Three Xiu.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚，獻帝初爲兖州刺史，東之郡，而太祖已臨兖州。
manualTranslations.literal: Shang, at the beginning of Emperor Xian's reign, was Inspector of Yan Province; going east to his commandery, Grand Progenitor had already reached Yan Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xian's reign Shang was Inspector of Yan Province; marching east to take up office, he found Cao Cao already in Yan Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚南依袁術。
manualTranslations.literal: Shang went south and relied on Yuan Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shang went south and relied on Yuan Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 術僭號，欲以尚爲太尉，不敢顯言，私使人諷之，尚無屈意，術亦不敢彊也。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shu usurped the title, he wished to make Shang Grand Commandant; not daring to speak openly, he privately sent men to hint at it; Shang had no yielding intent, and Shu also did not dare force him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu usurped imperial title he wished to make Shang Grand Commandant; not daring to speak openly, he sent private hints, but Shang would not yield and Yuan Shu did not dare force him.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安初，尚逃還，爲術所害。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, Shang fled back and was killed by Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jian'an, Shang fled back and was killed by Yuan Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後尚喪與太傅馬日磾喪俱至京師，天子嘉尚忠烈，爲之咨嗟，詔百官弔祭，拜子瑋郎中，而日磾不與焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward Shang's funeral bier and Grand Tutor Ma Midi's funeral bier both reached the capital; the Son of Heaven praised Shang's loyal martyrdom, sighed over him, ordered the hundred officials to mourn and sacrifice, and appointed his son Wei as Gentleman of the Palace, while Midi was not included.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Shang's funeral train and Grand Tutor Ma Midi's both reached the capital. The emperor praised Shang's loyal martyrdom, ordered court mourning, and appointed his son Wei as a palace gentleman—Midi received no such honor.

manualTranslations.zh: 《英雄記》曰：布水陸東下，軍到下邳西四十里。
manualTranslations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Bu advanced east by water and land; his army reached forty li west of Xiapi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes says: Lü Bu advanced east by water and land until his army stood forty li west of Xiapi.

manualTranslations.zh: 備中郎將丹楊許耽夜遣司馬章誑來詣布，言「張益德與下邳相曹豹共爭，益德殺豹，城中大亂，不相信。
manualTranslations.literal: Bei's Central Gentleman-General Xu Dan of Danyang by night sent Major Zhang Kuang to come to Bu, saying: "Zhang Yide and the Chancellor of Xiapi Cao Bao quarreled; Yide killed Bao; the city is in great disorder and trust is gone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's Central Gentleman-General Xu Dan of Danyang sent Major Zhang Kuang by night to Lü Bu, saying: "Zhang Yide quarreled with Xiapi's chancellor Cao Bao; Yide killed Bao; the city is in chaos and trust is gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 丹楊兵有千人屯西白城門內，聞將軍來東，大小踊躍，如復更生。
manualTranslations.literal: A thousand Danyang troops are garrisoned inside the West White Gate; hearing the General is coming east, great and small leap for joy as if reborn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A thousand Danyang troops hold the West White Gate within; hearing you are coming east, everyone leaps for joy as if reborn.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍兵向城西門，丹楊軍便開門內將軍矣」。
manualTranslations.literal: If the General's troops head for the west gate, the Danyang troops will open the gate and admit the General."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: March on the west gate and the Danyang troops will open it and admit you."

manualTranslations.zh: 布遂夜進，晨到城下。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu thereupon advanced by night and at dawn reached below the walls.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu advanced by night and at dawn reached the walls.

manualTranslations.zh: 天明，丹楊兵悉開門內布兵。
manualTranslations.literal: At daylight the Danyang troops all opened the gates and admitted Bu's troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At daylight the Danyang troops opened the gates and admitted Lü Bu's men.

manualTranslations.zh: 布於門上坐，步騎放火，大破益德兵，獲備妻子軍資及部曲將吏士家口。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu sat atop the gate; infantry and cavalry set fires and greatly defeated Yide's troops, capturing Bei's wife and children, military stores, and the households of his officers, clerks, and soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu sat atop the gate; his foot and horse troops set fires, routed Zhang Yide's men, and seized Liu Bei's wife, children, stores, and the families of his officers and soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安元年六月夜半時，布將河內郝萌反，將兵入布所治下邳府，詣廳事閤外，同聲大呼攻閤，閤堅不得入。
manualTranslations.literal: At midnight in the sixth month of the first year of Jian'an, Bu's general Hao Meng of Henei rebelled, led troops into the Xiapi headquarters where Bu governed, came to the outer doors of the council hall, and all together shouted to attack the doors; the doors held firm and they could not enter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At midnight in the sixth month of Jian'an 1, Lü Bu's general Hao Meng of Henei rebelled, led troops into Lü Bu's Xiapi headquarters, and shouted together to storm the council doors, but the doors held.

manualTranslations.zh: 布不知反者爲誰，直牽婦，科頭袒衣，相將從溷上排壁出，詣都督高順營，直排順門入。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu did not know who the rebel was; he simply took his wife by the hand, bareheaded and with bared torso, went together with her out through the privy by breaking the wall, and went to Colonel-Director Gao Shun's camp, pushing straight through Shun's gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not knowing who had rebelled, Lü Bu seized his wife's hand, bareheaded and shirtless, broke out through the privy wall, and fled straight into Gao Shun's camp.

manualTranslations.zh: 順問：「將軍有所隱不？」
manualTranslations.literal: Shun asked: "General, are you hiding something?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Shun asked, "General, are you hiding something?"

manualTranslations.zh: 布言「河內兒聲」。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu said, "The voice of the fellow from Henei."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said, "The voice of the fellow from Henei."

manualTranslations.zh: 順言「此郝萌也」。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun said, "This is Hao Meng."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Shun said, "That is Hao Meng."

manualTranslations.zh: 順即嚴兵入府，弓弩並射萌衆；
manualTranslations.literal: Shun immediately arrayed troops and entered the headquarters; bows and crossbows shot together at Meng's host;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Shun immediately arrayed troops and entered the headquarters; bows and crossbows shot together at Hao Meng's men;

manualTranslations.zh: 萌衆亂走，天明還故營。
manualTranslations.literal: Meng's host fled in disorder; at daylight they returned to their former camp.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao Meng's men fled in disorder; at daylight they returned to their former camp.

manualTranslations.zh: 萌將曹性反萌，與對戰，萌刺傷性，性斫萌一臂。
manualTranslations.literal: Meng's officer Cao Xing turned against Meng and fought him; Meng stabbed and wounded Xing; Xing hacked off one of Meng's arms.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao Meng's officer Cao Xing turned against him; Hao Meng stabbed Cao Xing, and Cao Xing hacked off one of Hao Meng's arms.

manualTranslations.zh: 順斫萌首，牀輿性，送詣布。
manualTranslations.literal: Shun cut off Meng's head, carried Xing on a litter, and sent them to Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Shun cut off Hao Meng's head, carried Cao Xing on a litter, and brought them to Lü Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 布問性，言「萌受袁術謀，謀者悉誰？」
manualTranslations.literal: Bu questioned Xing, saying, "Meng received Yuan Shu's plot—who were all the plotters?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu questioned Cao Xing: "Hao Meng followed Yuan Shu's plot—who were the plotters?"

manualTranslations.zh: 性言「陳宮同謀。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xing said, "Chen Gong plotted with him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Xing said, "Chen Gong plotted with him."

manualTranslations.zh: 時宮在坐上，靣赤，傍人悉覺之。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Gong was seated in the hall; his face flushed and those beside him all noticed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Gong was seated in the hall; his face flushed and everyone nearby noticed.

manualTranslations.zh: 布以宮大將，不問也。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu, because Gong was a great general, did not question him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Chen Gong was a senior commander, Lü Bu did not question him.

manualTranslations.zh: 性言「萌常以此問，性言呂將軍大將有神，不可擊也，不意萌狂惑不止。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xing said, "Meng often asked this; Xing said General Lü the great commander has a spirit and cannot be attacked—I did not expect Meng's madness would not stop."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Xing added, "Hao Meng often asked me this; I told him General Lü had a guardian spirit and could not be attacked—I never expected his madness would not stop."

manualTranslations.zh: 布謂性曰：「卿健兒也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Bu said to Xing, "You are a stout fellow!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu told Cao Xing, "You are a stout fellow!"

manualTranslations.zh: 善養視之。
manualTranslations.literal: He treated him well and cared for him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He treated him well and cared for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 創愈，使安撫萌故營，領其衆。
manualTranslations.literal: When the wound healed, he had him pacify Meng's former camp and lead his host.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the wound healed, he had Cao Xing pacify Hao Meng's former camp and lead his troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 術遣將紀靈等步騎三萬攻備，備求救於布。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu sent the general Ji Ling and others with thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Bei; Bei begged rescue from Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent Ji Ling and others with thirty thousand foot and horse against Liu Bei; Liu Bei begged Lü Bu for rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 布諸將謂布曰：「將軍常欲殺備，今可假手於術。」
manualTranslations.literal: Bu's generals said to Bu, "The General has always wished to kill Bei; now you can borrow Shu's hand."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's officers told him, "You have always wanted Liu Bei dead—now let Yuan Shu do it for you."

manualTranslations.zh: 布曰：「不然。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu said, "Not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu said, "Not so.

manualTranslations.zh: 術若破備，則北連太山諸將，吾爲在術圍中，不得不救也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If Shu defeats Bei, he will link north with the generals of Mount Tai; I will be within Shu's encirclement and cannot but rescue him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Yuan Shu defeats Liu Bei, he will link north with the Mount Tai generals and I will be trapped in Yuan Shu's net—I must rescue him."

manualTranslations.zh: 便嚴步兵千、騎二百，馳往赴備。
manualTranslations.literal: He thereupon arrayed a thousand infantry and two hundred cavalry and galloped to aid Bei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He arrayed a thousand infantry and two hundred cavalry and galloped to Liu Bei's aid.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈等聞布至，皆斂兵不敢復攻。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling and the others, hearing Bu had arrived, all restrained their troops and did not dare attack again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Ling and the others, hearing Lü Bu had arrived, restrained their troops and dared not attack again.

manualTranslations.zh: 布於沛西南一里安屯，遣鈴下請靈等，靈等亦請布共飲食。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu encamped one li southwest of Pei, sent a bell-man to invite Ling and the others, and Ling and the others also invited Bu to drink and eat together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu encamped one li southwest of Pei, sent an attendant to invite Ji Ling and the others, and they in turn invited him to feast.

manualTranslations.zh: 布謂靈等曰：「玄德，布弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu said to Ling and the others, "Xuande is Bu's younger brother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu told Ji Ling and the others, "Xuande is my younger brother.

manualTranslations.zh: 弟爲諸君所困，故來救之。
manualTranslations.literal: The younger brother is distressed by you gentlemen, therefore I have come to rescue him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My younger brother is in trouble with you, so I have come to rescue him.

manualTranslations.zh: 布性不喜合鬬，但喜解鬬耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Bu by nature does not like joining battle, but only likes resolving battle."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By nature I do not like joining battle—I only like ending it."

manualTranslations.zh: 布令門候於營門中舉一隻戟，布言：「諸君觀布射戟小支，一發中者諸君當解去，不中可留決鬬。」
manualTranslations.literal: Bu ordered the gate warden to raise a single halberd in the camp gate; Bu said, "You gentlemen watch Bu shoot the halberd's small branch—if with one shot he hits it, you gentlemen ought to disperse; if he misses, you may remain and decide the battle."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had a gate warden raise a halberd in the camp gate and said, "Watch me shoot the halberd's side branch—if I hit it with one shot, disperse; if I miss, stay and fight."

manualTranslations.zh: 布舉弓射戟，正中小支。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu raised his bow and shot the halberd, hitting the small branch squarely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu drew his bow and hit the side branch squarely.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸將皆驚，言「將軍天威也」！
manualTranslations.literal: The generals were all astonished and said, "The General's heaven-sent might!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officers were astonished and cried, "Heaven-sent might!"

manualTranslations.zh: 明日復歡會，然後各罷。
manualTranslations.literal: The next day they feasted again in joy, and afterward each dispersed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next day they feasted again, and afterward each went his way.

sourceRange.text: 天子之在河東，楊將兵至安邑，拜安國將軍，封晉陽侯。楊欲迎天子還洛，諸將不聽；楊還野王。建安元年，楊奉、董承、韓暹挾天子還舊京，糧乏。楊以糧迎道路，遂至洛陽。謂諸將曰：「天子當與天下共之，幸有公卿大臣，楊當捍外難，何事京都？」遂還野王。即拜為大司馬。《英雄記》曰：楊性仁和，無威刑。下人謀反，發覺，對之涕泣，輒原不問。楊素與呂布善。太祖之圍布，楊欲救之，不能。乃出兵東市，遙為之勢。其將楊醜，殺楊以應太祖。楊將眭固殺醜，將其眾，欲北合袁紹。太祖遣史渙邀擊，破之於犬城，斬固，盡收其眾也。《典略》曰：固字白兔，既殺楊醜，軍屯射犬。時有巫誡固曰：「將軍字兔而此邑名犬，兔見犬，其勢必驚，宜急移去。」固不從，遂戰死。

context.beforeSource: 卓以楊為建義將軍、河內太守。
context.afterSource: 公孫度字升濟，本遼東襄平人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 天子之在河東，楊將兵至安邑，拜安國將軍，封晉陽侯。
manualTranslations.literal: While the Son of Heaven was in Hedong, Yang led troops to Anyi; he was appointed general who pacifies the state and enfeoffed marquis of Jinyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While the emperor was in Hedong, Yang led troops to Anyi, was named general who pacifies the state, and was enfeoffed marquis of Jinyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊欲迎天子還洛，諸將不聽；
manualTranslations.literal: Yang wished to welcome the emperor back to Luoyang, but the generals would not agree;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang wanted to bring the emperor back to Luoyang; the generals refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊還野王。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang returned to Yewang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang withdrew to Yewang.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安元年，楊奉、董承、韓暹挾天子還舊京，糧乏。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an (196), Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Han Xian escorted the emperor back to the old capital; provisions were scarce.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 1, Yang Feng, Dong Cheng, and Han Xian brought the emperor back to the old capital, but food ran short.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊以糧迎道路，遂至洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang met them on the road with grain, and they reached Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang supplied grain along the route until they reached Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 謂諸將曰：「天子當與天下共之，幸有公卿大臣，楊當捍外難，何事京都？」
manualTranslations.literal: He told the generals, "The Son of Heaven ought to be shared with the empire; fortunately there are eminent ministers—Yang shall ward off external dangers. What need is there for the capital?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He told the generals, "The emperor belongs to the realm; with ministers in the capital, Yang can hold the frontier—why stay in Luoyang?"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂還野王。
manualTranslations.literal: Then he returned to Yewang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then returned to Yewang.

manualTranslations.zh: 即拜為大司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: He was at once appointed grand marshal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grand marshal.

manualTranslations.zh: 《英雄記》曰：楊性仁和，無威刑。
manualTranslations.literal: The Yingxiong ji says: Yang was by nature kind and humane, without harsh penalties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yingxiong ji says Yang was gentle by nature and used no harsh punishments.

manualTranslations.zh: 下人謀反，發覺，對之涕泣，輒原不問。
manualTranslations.literal: When subordinates plotted rebellion and were discovered, he wept facing them and always pardoned them without inquiry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When servants rebelled and were caught, he wept before them and always forgave them.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊素與呂布善。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang had long been on good terms with Lü Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang had long been friendly with Lü Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖之圍布，楊欲救之，不能。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor besieged Bu, Yang wished to rescue him but could not.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao besieged Bu, Yang tried to save him but failed.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃出兵東市，遙為之勢。
manualTranslations.literal: He therefore sent troops out of the eastern market to threaten at a distance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He marched troops out of the eastern market to menace from afar.

manualTranslations.zh: 其將楊醜，殺楊以應太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: His officer Yang Chou killed Yang to answer the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His officer Yang Chou killed Yang to win Cao Cao's favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 楊將眭固殺醜，將其眾，欲北合袁紹。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang's officer Sui Gu killed Chou, took his following, and wished to join Yuan Shao in the north.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang's officer Sui Gu killed Chou, took the host, and planned to join Yuan Shao in the north.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖遣史渙邀擊，破之於犬城，斬固，盡收其眾也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor dispatched Shi Huan to intercept and strike; he defeated them at Quan City, beheaded Gu, and took all his forces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Shi Huan to intercept them, routed them at Quan City, beheaded Gu, and absorbed the whole force.

manualTranslations.zh: 《典略》曰：固字白兔，既殺楊醜，軍屯射犬。
manualTranslations.literal: The Dianlüe says: Gu's courtesy name was White Rabbit; after killing Yang Chou, his army camped at Shequan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe says Gu's courtesy name was White Rabbit; after killing Yang Chou he encamped at Shequan.

manualTranslations.zh: 時有巫誡固曰：「將軍字兔而此邑名犬，兔見犬，其勢必驚，宜急移去。」
manualTranslations.literal: At the time a shaman warned Gu, saying, "The general's courtesy name is Rabbit and this town is named Dog; when a rabbit sees a dog it is sure to be startled—you should move away at once."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A shaman warned him, "Your name is Rabbit and this town is Dog—a rabbit seeing a dog is doomed; move at once."

manualTranslations.zh: 固不從，遂戰死。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu would not follow, and was killed in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gu refused and died in battle.

sourceRange.text: 張燕，常山真定人也，本姓褚。黃巾起，燕合聚少年為群盜，在山澤間轉攻，還真定，眾萬餘人。博陵張牛角亦起眾，自號將兵從事，與燕合。燕推牛角為帥，俱攻癭陶。牛角為飛矢所中。被創且死，令眾奉燕，告曰：「必以燕為帥。」牛角死，眾奉燕，故改姓張。燕剽捍捷速過人，故軍中號曰飛燕。其後人眾寢廣，常山、趙郡、中山、上黨、河內諸山谷皆相通，其小帥孫輕、王當等，各以部眾從燕，眾至百萬，號曰黑山。靈帝不能征，河北諸郡被其害。燕遣人至京都乞降，拜燕平難中郎將。《九州春秋》曰：張角之反也，黑山、白波、黃龍、左校、牛角、五鹿、羝根、苦蝤、劉石、平漢、大洪、司隸、緣城、羅市、雷公、浮雲、飛燕、白爵、楊鳳、於毒等各起兵，大者二三萬，小者不減數千。靈帝不能討，乃遣使拜楊鳳為黑山校尉，領諸山賊，得舉孝廉計吏。後遂瀰漫，不可復數。《典略》曰：黑山、黃巾諸帥，本非冠蓋，自相號字，謂騎白馬者為張白騎，謂輕捷者為張飛燕，謂聲大者為張雷公，其饒須者則自稱於羝根，其眼大者自稱李大目。張璠《漢紀》云：又有左校、郭大賢、左髭丈八三部也。是後，董卓遷天子於長安，天下兵數起，燕遂以其眾與豪傑相結。袁紹與公孫瓚爭冀州，燕遣將杜長等助瓚，與紹戰，為紹所敗，人眾稍散，太祖將定冀州，燕遣使求佐王師，拜平北將軍；率眾詣鄴，封安國亭侯，邑五百戶。燕薨，子方嗣。方薨，子融嗣。陸機《晉惠帝起居注》曰：門下通事令史張林，飛燕之曾孫。林與趙王倫為亂，未及周年，位至尚書令、衛將軍，封郡公。尋為倫所殺。

context.afterSource: 張繡，武威祖厲人，驃騎將軍濟族子也。

manualTranslations.zh: 張燕，常山真定人也，本姓褚。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Yan was a man of Zhending in Changshan; his original surname was Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan of Zhending in Changshan was born Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃巾起，燕合聚少年為群盜，在山澤間轉攻，還真定，眾萬餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Yan gathered youths as bandits, raided among hills and marshes, returned to Zhending, and had more than ten thousand men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans rose he gathered youths into hill bandits, raided the wilds, and mustered over ten thousand at Zhending.

manualTranslations.zh: 博陵張牛角亦起眾，自號將兵從事，與燕合。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Niujiao of Boling also raised a host, styled himself aide who leads troops, and joined Yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Niujiao of Boling also rose, styled himself aide who leads troops, and joined Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 燕推牛角為帥，俱攻癭陶。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan pushed Niujiao as commander and together they attacked Yingtao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan made Niujiao commander and they attacked Yingtao together.

manualTranslations.zh: 牛角為飛矢所中。
manualTranslations.literal: Niujiao was struck by a flying arrow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Niujiao was hit by a stray arrow.

manualTranslations.zh: 被創且死，令眾奉燕，告曰：「必以燕為帥。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wounded and near death, he ordered the host to obey Yan and said, "You must take Yan as commander."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dying, he told the host, "Make Yan commander."

manualTranslations.zh: 牛角死，眾奉燕，故改姓張。
manualTranslations.literal: When Niujiao died the host obeyed Yan, and therefore he changed his surname to Zhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Niujiao died they followed Yan and he took the surname Zhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 燕剽捍捷速過人，故軍中號曰飛燕。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan was fierce, swift, and faster than others; therefore in the army he was called Flying Swallow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Swift and daring, the army called him Flying Swallow.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後人眾寢廣，常山、趙郡、中山、上黨、河內諸山谷皆相通，其小帥孫輕、王當等，各以部眾從燕，眾至百萬，號曰黑山。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward his following grew ever wider; the valleys of Changshan, Zhao, Zhongshan, Shangdang, and Henei all linked; minor chiefs Sun Qing, Wang Dang, and others each brought their hosts to Yan; the host reached a million and was called Black Mountain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His bands spread through Changshan, Zhao, Zhongshan, Shangdang, and Henei; chiefs like Sun Qing and Wang Dang joined until he claimed a million men—the Black Mountain host.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈帝不能征，河北諸郡被其害。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ling could not campaign against him; the commanderies of Hebei suffered from him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling could not suppress him and Hebei suffered.

manualTranslations.zh: 燕遣人至京都乞降，拜燕平難中郎將。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan sent men to the capital to beg surrender and was appointed colonel of the gentlemen cadets who pacify turmoil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan sent envoys to surrender and was named colonel who pacifies turmoil.

manualTranslations.zh: 《九州春秋》曰：張角之反也，黑山、白波、黃龍、左校、牛角、五鹿、羝根、苦蝤、劉石、平漢、大洪、司隸、緣城、羅市、雷公、浮雲、飛燕、白爵、楊鳳、於毒等各起兵，大者二三萬，小者不減數千。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiuzhou chunqiu says: When Zhang Jiao rebelled, Black Mountain, White Wave, Yellow Dragon, Left Colonel, Ox Horn, Five Deer, Ram Root, Bitter Moth, Liu Shi, Pacify Han, Great Flood, Sili, Edge City, Market Luo, Thunder Lord, Floating Cloud, Flying Swallow, White Sparrow, Yang Feng, Yu Du, and others each raised troops—large bands of twenty or thirty thousand, small ones no fewer than several thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu lists dozens of band titles when Zhang Jiao rose—some twenty or thirty thousand strong, none fewer than thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈帝不能討，乃遣使拜楊鳳為黑山校尉，領諸山賊，得舉孝廉計吏。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ling could not punish them and therefore sent envoys appointing Yang Feng colonel of Black Mountain to lead the mountain bandits and qualify for filial-piety and clerk recommendations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ling could not punish them and named Yang Feng Black Mountain colonel to lead the hills and earn recommendation rights.

manualTranslations.zh: 後遂瀰漫，不可復數。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward they spread until they could no longer be counted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They spread beyond counting.

manualTranslations.zh: 《典略》曰：黑山、黃巾諸帥，本非冠蓋，自相號字，謂騎白馬者為張白騎，謂輕捷者為張飛燕，謂聲大者為張雷公，其饒須者則自稱於羝根，其眼大者自稱李大目。
manualTranslations.literal: The Dianlüe says: Black Mountain and Yellow Turban chiefs were not gentry; they gave one another style names—those who rode white horses were Zhang White Horse, the nimble were Zhang Flying Swallow, the loud were Zhang Thunder Lord; the bearded called themselves Yu Ram Root, the big-eyed Li Big Eye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Dianlüe says hill chiefs were not gentry and nicknamed themselves—White Horse, Flying Swallow, Thunder Lord, Ram Root, Big Eye.

manualTranslations.zh: 張璠《漢紀》云：又有左校、郭大賢、左髭丈八三部也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Fan's Han ji says: There were also the three bands Left Colonel, Guo Daxian, and Left Whiskers Zhang Eight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han ji adds Left Colonel, Guo Daxian, and Left Whiskers Zhang Eight.

manualTranslations.zh: 是後，董卓遷天子於長安，天下兵數起，燕遂以其眾與豪傑相結。
manualTranslations.literal: After this Dong Zhuo moved the Son of Heaven to Chang'an; soldiers rose everywhere; Yan then joined his host with heroes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Zhuo moved the court to Chang'an and war spread, Yan allied his bands with warlords.

manualTranslations.zh: 袁紹與公孫瓚爭冀州，燕遣將杜長等助瓚，與紹戰，為紹所敗，人眾稍散，太祖將定冀州，燕遣使求佐王師，拜平北將軍；
manualTranslations.literal: When Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan fought for Jizhou, Yan sent the generals Du Chang and others to aid Zan; fighting Shao they were defeated, and the host gradually scattered; as the Grand Progenitor was about to settle Jizhou, Yan sent envoys asking to aid the royal army and was appointed general who pacifies the north;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shao and Zan fought for Jizhou, Yan sent Du Chang to aid Zan, lost to Shao, then offered service to Cao Cao and was named general who pacifies the north;

manualTranslations.zh: 率眾詣鄴，封安國亭侯，邑五百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: he led his host to Ye and was enfeoffed marquis of Anguo village with a fief of five hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he brought his host to Ye and was enfeoffed marquis of Anguo village, five hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 燕薨，子方嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan died; his son Fang succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan died; his son Fang succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 方薨，子融嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Fang died; his son Rong succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fang died; his son Rong succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 陸機《晉惠帝起居注》曰：門下通事令史張林，飛燕之曾孫。
manualTranslations.literal: Lu Ji's Jin Huidi qiju zhu says: Zhang Lin, attendant clerk for matters at the gate, was Flying Swallow's great-grandson.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's Jin Huidi qiju zhu says attendant clerk Zhang Lin was Flying Swallow's great-grandson.

manualTranslations.zh: 林與趙王倫為亂，未及周年，位至尚書令、衛將軍，封郡公。
manualTranslations.literal: Lin joined Prince of Zhao Lun in rebellion; before a full year he reached minister of writing, general of the guards, and was enfeoffed duke of a commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lin joined Lun's rebellion and within a year reached minister of writing and guards general, enfeoffed commandery duke.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋為倫所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was killed by Lun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lun soon killed him.

sourceRange.text: 魯薨，諡之曰原侯。子富嗣。《魏略》曰：劉雄鳴者，藍田人也。少以採藥射獵為事，常居覆車山下，每晨夜，出行雲霧中，以識道不迷，而時人因謂之能為雲霧。郭、李之亂，人多就之。建安中，附屬州郡，州郡表薦為小將。馬超等反，不肯從，超破之。後詣太祖，太祖執其手謂之曰：「孤方入關，夢得一神人，即卿邪！」乃厚禮之，表拜為將軍，遣令迎其部黨。部黨不欲降，遂劫以反，諸亡命皆往依之，有眾數千人，據武關道口。太祖遣夏侯淵討破之，雄鳴南奔漢中。漢中破，窮無所之，乃復歸降。太祖捉其鬚曰：「老賊，真得汝矣！」復其官，徙勃海。時又有程銀、侯選、李堪，皆河東人也，興平之亂，各有眾千餘家。建安十六年，並與馬超合。超破走，堪臨陳死。銀、選南入漢中，漢中破，詣太祖降，皆复官爵。

context.beforeSource: 為子彭祖取魯女。
context.afterSource: 評曰：公孫瓚保京，坐待夷滅。
context.beforeLocal: 為子彭祖取魯女。
context.afterLocal: 評曰：公孫瓚保京，坐待夷滅。
