manualTranslations.zh: 魯薨，諡之曰原侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Lu died; he was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu died and was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 子富嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Fu succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Fu succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：劉雄鳴者，藍田人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Weilüe says: Liu Xiongming was a man of Lantian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Weilüe says Liu Xiongming was from Lantian.

manualTranslations.zh: 少以採藥射獵為事，常居覆車山下，每晨夜，出行雲霧中，以識道不迷，而時人因謂之能為雲霧。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he gathered medicine and hunted; he constantly dwelt below Mount Fuche, and each dawn and dusk went out in cloud and mist so as to know the road and not lose his way; people therefore called him able to make cloud and mist.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a youth he gathered herbs and hunted below Mount Fuche, walking through mist without losing the path—people said he commanded fog.

manualTranslations.zh: 郭、李之亂，人多就之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the disorders of Guo and Li many people went to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Guo Si and Li Jue's chaos many fled to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安中，附屬州郡，州郡表薦為小將。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jian'an era he attached to the province and commandery; the province and commandery recommended him as a minor general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Jian'an he submitted to local officials who recommended him minor general.

manualTranslations.zh: 馬超等反，不肯從，超破之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ma Chao and others rebelled he would not follow; Chao defeated him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao rebelled he refused and was beaten.

manualTranslations.zh: 後詣太祖，太祖執其手謂之曰：「孤方入關，夢得一神人，即卿邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Later he went to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor took his hand and said, "I had just entered the passes and dreamed of a god—was it you!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later visited Cao Cao, who seized his hand and said, "Entering the passes I dreamed of a god—is it you?"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃厚禮之，表拜為將軍，遣令迎其部黨。
manualTranslations.literal: He therefore treated him generously, memorialized him general, and sent him to welcome his following.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao honored him, named him general, and sent him to summon his band.

manualTranslations.zh: 部黨不欲降，遂劫以反，諸亡命皆往依之，有眾數千人，據武關道口。
manualTranslations.literal: The following would not surrender; they seized him to rebel, and all fugitives went to rely on him—several thousand men—holding Wuguan road mouth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His band seized him to rebel; fugitives gathered by the thousands and held Wuguan pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖遣夏侯淵討破之，雄鳴南奔漢中。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Xiahou Yuan to attack and defeat him; Xiongming fled south to Hanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan to rout him; Xiongming fled south to Hanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢中破，窮無所之，乃復歸降。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hanzhong fell he was destitute with nowhere to go and therefore returned to surrender again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Hanzhong fell he had nowhere to go and surrendered again.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖捉其鬚曰：「老賊，真得汝矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor seized his beard and said, "Old bandit—I truly have got you!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao grabbed his beard and said, "Old bandit—I have got you at last!"

manualTranslations.zh: 復其官，徙勃海。
manualTranslations.literal: His office was restored and he was moved to Bohai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His rank was restored and he was moved to Bohai.

manualTranslations.zh: 時又有程銀、侯選、李堪，皆河東人也，興平之亂，各有眾千餘家。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time there were also Cheng Yin, Hou Xuan, and Li Kan—all men of Hedong; in the Xingping disorders each had a following of more than a thousand households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Also Cheng Yin, Hou Xuan, and Li Kan of Hedong each led over a thousand households in the Xingping chaos.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安十六年，並與馬超合。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an (211) they all joined Ma Chao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 16 they joined Ma Chao.

manualTranslations.zh: 超破走，堪臨陳死。
manualTranslations.literal: When Chao was defeated and fled, Kan died in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Chao fled, Kan died in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 銀、選南入漢中，漢中破，詣太祖降，皆复官爵。
manualTranslations.literal: Yin and Xuan went south into Hanzhong; when Hanzhong fell they went to the Grand Progenitor and surrendered, and all had office and noble rank restored.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yin and Xuan fled to Hanzhong, then surrendered to Cao Cao and regained rank and fief.

sourceRange.text: 明帝於是拜淵大司馬，封樂浪公，持節、領郡如故。《魏名臣奏》載中領軍夏侯獻表曰：「公孫淵昔年敢違王命，廢絕計貢者，實挾兩端。既恃阻險，又怙孫權。故敢跋扈，恣睢海外。宿舒親見賊權軍眾府庫，知其弱少不足憑恃，是以決計斬賊之使。又高句麗、濊貊與淵為仇，並為寇鈔。今外失吳援，內有胡寇，心知國家能從陸道，勢不得不懷惶懼之心。因斯之時，宜遣使示以禍福。奉車都尉鬷弘，武皇帝時始奉使命，開通道路。文皇帝即位，欲通使命，遣弘將妻子還歸鄉里，賜其車、牛，絹百匹。弘以受恩，歸死國朝，無有還意，乞留妻子，身奉使命。公孫康遂稱臣妾。以弘奉使稱意，賜爵關內侯。弘性果烈，乃心於國，夙夜拳拳，念自竭效。冠族子孫，少好學問，博通書記，多所關涉，口論速捷，辯而不俗，附依典誥，若出胸臆，加仕本郡，常在人右，彼方士人素所敬服。若當遣使，以為可使弘行。弘乃自舊土，習其國俗，為說利害，辯足以動其意，明足以見其事，才足以行之，辭足以見信。若其計從，雖酈生之降齊王，陸賈之說尉佗，亦無以遠過也。欲進遠路，不宜釋騏驥；將已篤疾，不宜廢扁鵲。原察愚言也。」使者至，淵設甲兵為軍陳，出見使者，又數對國中賓客出惡言。《吳書》曰：魏遣使者傅容、聶夔拜淵為樂浪公。淵計吏從洛陽還，語淵曰：「使者左駿伯，使皆擇勇力者，非凡人也。」淵由是疑怖。容、夔至，住學館中。淵先以步騎圍之，乃入受拜。容、夔大怖，由是還洛言狀。景初元年，乃遣幽州刺史毌丘儉等齎璽書徵淵。淵遂發兵，逆於遼隧，與儉等戰。儉等不利而還。淵遂自立為燕王，置百官有司。遣使者持節，假鮮卑單于璽，封拜邊民，誘呼鮮卑，侵擾北方。《魏書》曰：淵知此變非獨出儉，遂為備。遣使謝吳，自稱燕王，求為與國。然猶令官屬上書自直於魏曰：大司馬長史臣郭昕、參軍臣柳浦等七百八十九人言：奉被今年七月己卯詔書，伏讀懇切，精魄散越，不知身命所當投措！

localRange.text: 大司馬長史臣郭昕、參軍臣柳浦等七百八十九人言：奉被今年七月己卯詔書，伏讀懇切，精魄散越，不知身命所當投措！

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝於是拜淵大司馬，封樂浪公，持節、領郡如故。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ming thereupon appointed Yuan grand marshal, enfeoffed him duke of Lelang, and let him hold his tally and commandery as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming then named Yuan grand marshal and duke of Lelang, leaving his commission and commandery unchanged.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏名臣奏》載中領軍夏侯獻表曰：「公孫淵昔年敢違王命，廢絕計貢者，實挾兩端。
manualTranslations.literal: The Weimingchen zou records the memorial of Central Army Commander Xiahou Xian, saying, "In former years Gongsun Yuan dared defy the royal command and cut off tribute because he played both sides.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Weimingchen zou quotes Central Army Commander Xiahou Xian: "Yuan once defied the throne and stopped tribute by playing both ends.

manualTranslations.zh: 既恃阻險，又怙孫權。
manualTranslations.literal: He relied on rugged terrain and leaned on Sun Quan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He trusted the terrain and clung to Sun Quan.

manualTranslations.zh: 故敢跋扈，恣睢海外。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore he dared be overbearing and wanton beyond the seas.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So he grew arrogant overseas.

manualTranslations.zh: 宿舒親見賊權軍眾府庫，知其弱少不足憑恃，是以決計斬賊之使。
manualTranslations.literal: Su Shu personally saw the rebel Quan's armies and storehouses and knew they were few and weak and not to be relied on; therefore he resolved to behead the rebel's envoys.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Su Shu saw Quan's armies and stores were weak and chose to kill his envoys.

manualTranslations.zh: 又高句麗、濊貊與淵為仇，並為寇鈔。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Koguryŏ and the Yemaek were Yuan's enemies and together raided and plundered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ and Yemaek were his foes and raided together.

manualTranslations.zh: 今外失吳援，內有胡寇，心知國家能從陸道，勢不得不懷惶懼之心。
manualTranslations.literal: Now he has lost Wu's aid abroad and has barbarian raiders within; knowing the state can advance by land, he cannot but harbor fear and dread.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Losing Wu abroad and facing barbarians within, he knows an overland strike must terrify him.

manualTranslations.zh: 因斯之時，宜遣使示以禍福。
manualTranslations.literal: At such a time one ought to send envoys showing fortune and disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now is the time to send envoys showing reward and ruin.

manualTranslations.zh: 奉車都尉鬷弘，武皇帝時始奉使命，開通道路。
manualTranslations.literal: Chariot Commandant Juan Hong first carried missions in Emperor Wu's time and opened the roads.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chariot Commandant Juan Hong first served as envoy under Emperor Wu and opened the routes.

manualTranslations.zh: 文皇帝即位，欲通使命，遣弘將妻子還歸鄉里，賜其車、牛，絹百匹。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne he wished to renew missions and sent Hong back with wife and children to their home district, granting car, ox, and a hundred bolts of silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Hong home with family, car, ox, and a hundred bolts of silk to renew contact.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘以受恩，歸死國朝，無有還意，乞留妻子，身奉使命。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong, having received grace, wished to die for the court and had no thought of return; he begged to leave wife and children and go on mission himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grateful, Hong asked to leave his family and die on embassy.

manualTranslations.zh: 公孫康遂稱臣妾。
manualTranslations.literal: Gongsun Kang thereupon declared himself subject and concubine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang then submitted as vassal.

manualTranslations.zh: 以弘奉使稱意，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Hong's mission pleased them, he was granted noble rank within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong pleased them and was enfeoffed within the passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘性果烈，乃心於國，夙夜拳拳，念自竭效。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong was resolute and fierce, his heart set on the state; day and night he strained to exhaust himself in service.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong was bold and wholly loyal, straining day and night to serve.

manualTranslations.zh: 冠族子孫，少好學問，博通書記，多所關涉，口論速捷，辯而不俗，附依典誥，若出胸臆，加仕本郡，常在人右，彼方士人素所敬服。
manualTranslations.literal: A noble clan's descendant, in youth fond of learning, broadly versed in records, widely informed, quick in debate, eloquent yet not vulgar, relying on canonical texts as if from his own breast; having served in his home commandery he always stood above others, and the gentlemen there long revered him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A noble-born scholar, widely read, quick-tongued yet sound, long respected in his commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 若當遣使，以為可使弘行。
manualTranslations.literal: If envoys are to be sent, Hong should be the one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If an envoy is needed, send Hong.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘乃自舊土，習其國俗，為說利害，辯足以動其意，明足以見其事，才足以行之，辭足以見信。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong comes from that old land and knows its customs; he can explain advantage and harm, his eloquence enough to move their minds, his clarity enough to see the affair, his talent enough to carry it out, his words enough to win trust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He knows their land and customs, can argue gain and loss, and can move, see, act, and persuade.

manualTranslations.zh: 若其計從，雖酈生之降齊王，陸賈之說尉佗，亦無以遠過也。
manualTranslations.literal: If his plan is followed, even Li Yiji's reduction of the king of Qi or Lu Jia's persuasion of Zhao Tuo could not far surpass it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Success would rival Li Yiji on Qi or Lu Jia on Zhao Tuo.

manualTranslations.zh: 欲進遠路，不宜釋騏驥；
manualTranslations.literal: When one wishes to travel a long road, one should not release a thoroughbred;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On a long road do not spare the thoroughbred;

manualTranslations.zh: 將已篤疾，不宜廢扁鵲。
manualTranslations.literal: when illness is grave, one should not dismiss Bian Que.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: in grave illness do not dismiss the physician Bian Que.

manualTranslations.zh: 原察愚言也。」
manualTranslations.literal: I pray you examine my foolish words."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Please heed this counsel."

manualTranslations.zh: 使者至，淵設甲兵為軍陳，出見使者，又數對國中賓客出惡言。
manualTranslations.literal: When the envoys arrived, Yuan arrayed armored troops in battle lines, came out to see the envoys, and repeatedly spoke evil words to guests in the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When envoys came Yuan paraded armor, received them under arms, and insulted guests.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳書》曰：魏遣使者傅容、聶夔拜淵為樂浪公。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wushu says: Wei sent envoys Fu Rong and Nie Kui to invest Yuan as duke of Lelang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wushu says Wei sent Fu Rong and Nie Kui to invest Yuan duke of Lelang.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵計吏從洛陽還，語淵曰：「使者左駿伯，使皆擇勇力者，非凡人也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan's accounting clerk returned from Luoyang and told Yuan, "The envoys' left groom-warden chose only the bravest men—they are no ordinary people."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A clerk back from Luoyang said, "Their groom-warden picked only the strongest men—not common envoys."

manualTranslations.zh: 淵由是疑怖。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan therefore grew suspicious and afraid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan grew fearful.

manualTranslations.zh: 容、夔至，住學館中。
manualTranslations.literal: Rong and Kui arrived and lodged in the academy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rong and Kui lodged in the academy.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵先以步騎圍之，乃入受拜。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan first surrounded them with infantry and cavalry, then entered to receive investiture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan surrounded them with horse and foot, then accepted the patent.

manualTranslations.zh: 容、夔大怖，由是還洛言狀。
manualTranslations.literal: Rong and Kui were greatly terrified; therefore they returned to Luoyang and reported the situation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Terrified, they fled back to Luoyang and reported.

manualTranslations.zh: 景初元年，乃遣幽州刺史毌丘儉等齎璽書徵淵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu (237), he sent Governor of Youzhou Guanqiu Jian and others bearing imperial writ to summon Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 (237) Guanqiu Jian of Youzhou was sent with imperial writ to summon Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵遂發兵，逆於遼隧，與儉等戰。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan thereupon raised troops and met them at Liaosui and fought.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan marched to meet them at Liaosui and fought.

manualTranslations.zh: 儉等不利而還。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian and the others fared ill and withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian was beaten and withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵遂自立為燕王，置百官有司。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan thereupon declared himself king of Yan and set up the hundred officials and bureaus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan declared himself king of Yan and set up officials.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣使者持節，假鮮卑單于璽，封拜邊民，誘呼鮮卑，侵擾北方。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent envoys bearing tallies, lending the Xianbei chanyu's seal, enfeoffing border people, enticing Xianbei, and harassing the north.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He lent the Xianbei chanyu's seal, enfeoffed border folk, and stirred Xianbei raids.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：淵知此變非獨出儉，遂為備。
manualTranslations.literal: The Weishu says: Yuan knew this change did not come from Jian alone and therefore prepared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Weishu says Yuan knew Jian was not alone and prepared.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣使謝吳，自稱燕王，求為與國。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent envoys apologizing to Wu, called himself king of Yan, and asked to be an allied state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He apologized to Wu, called himself king of Yan, and sought alliance.

manualTranslations.zh: 然猶令官屬上書自直於魏曰：大司馬長史臣郭昕、參軍臣柳浦等七百八十九人言：奉被今年七月己卯詔書，伏讀懇切，精魄散越，不知身命所當投措！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet he still ordered his officials to memorialize Wei in self-defense, saying: Chief clerk of the grand marshal, your subject Guo Xin, aide Liu Pu, and seven hundred eighty-nine others say: We received this year's seventh-month jimao-day edict; prostrate, we read it earnest and cutting—essence and soul scatter beyond bounds; we do not know where body and life should be cast!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he made officials plead to Wei: Guo Xin, Liu Pu, and 789 officers write that the seventh-month edict left them soul-scattered, not knowing where to turn.

sourceRange.text: 初平元年190年，度知中國擾攘，語所親吏柳毅、陽儀等曰：「漢祚將絕，當與諸卿圖王耳。」《魏書》曰：度語毅、儀：「讖書云孫登當為天子，太守姓公孫，字升濟，升即登也。」時襄平延里社生大石，長丈餘，下有三小石為之足。或謂度曰：「此漢宣帝冠石之祥，而裡名與先君同。社主土地，明當有土地，而三公為輔也。」度益喜。故河內太守李敏，郡中知名，惡度所為，恐為所害，乃將家屬入於海。度大怒，掘其父塚，剖棺焚屍，誅其宗族。《晉陽秋》曰：敏子追求敏，出塞，越二十餘年不娶。州里徐邈責之曰：「不孝莫大於無後，何可終身不娶乎！」乃娶妻，生子胤而遣妻，常如居喪之禮，不勝憂，數年而卒。胤生不識父母，及有識，蔬食哀戚亦如三年之喪。以祖父不知存亡，設主奉之。由是知名，仕至司徒。臣松之案：本傳云敏將家入海，而復與子相失，未詳其故。分遼東郡為遼西中遼郡，置太守。越海收東萊諸縣，置營州刺史。自立為遼東侯、平州牧，追封父延為建義侯。立漢二祖廟，承制設壇墠於襄平城南，郊祀天地，藉田，治兵，乘鸞路，九旒，旄頭羽騎。太祖表度為武威將軍，封永寧鄉侯，度曰：「我王遼東，何永寧也！」藏印綬武庫。度死，子康嗣位，以永寧鄉侯封弟恭。是歲建安九年也。

context.beforeSource: 東伐高句驪，西擊烏丸，威行海外。
context.afterSource: 十二年，太祖征三郡烏丸，屠柳城。

manualTranslations.zh: 初平元年190年，度知中國擾攘，語所親吏柳毅、陽儀等曰：「漢祚將絕，當與諸卿圖王耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Chuping (190), Du saw China in turmoil and told his trusted clerks Liu Yi and Yang Yi and others, "The Han mandate will end; I must plot kingship with you."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Chuping 1 (190), seeing China in chaos, Du told Liu Yi, Yang Yi, and other confidants, "Han is ending—we must make ourselves kings."

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：度語毅、儀：「讖書云孫登當為天子，太守姓公孫，字升濟，升即登也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Weishu says: Du told Yi and Yi, "The prophecy books say Sun Deng will be Son of Heaven; the governor's surname is Gongsun and his courtesy name Shengji—sheng means deng."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Weishu says Du told them, "Prophecy names Sun Deng as emperor; the governor is Gongsun Shengji—sheng is deng."

manualTranslations.zh: 時襄平延里社生大石，長丈餘，下有三小石為之足。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time in Yanli of Xiangping a great stone grew at the village altar, more than a zhang long, with three small stones as its feet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A boulder over a zhang tall rose at Yanli altar in Xiangping, standing on three small stones.

manualTranslations.zh: 或謂度曰：「此漢宣帝冠石之祥，而裡名與先君同。
manualTranslations.literal: Someone told Du, "This is the omen of Emperor Xuan's cap-stone, and the hamlet name matches your late father.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some said to Du, "This is Emperor Xuan's cap-stone omen, and the hamlet name matches your father.

manualTranslations.zh: 社主土地，明當有土地，而三公為輔也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The altar lord is lord of the land—clearly there will be land, with the Three Dukes as helpers."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The altar master rules the soil—you will hold territory with the Three Dukes as aides."

manualTranslations.zh: 度益喜。
manualTranslations.literal: Du grew still more pleased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du was delighted.

manualTranslations.zh: 故河內太守李敏，郡中知名，惡度所為，恐為所害，乃將家屬入於海。
manualTranslations.literal: Former governor of Henei Li Min, renowned in the commandery, hated Du's conduct, feared harm, and took his household out to sea.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Min, a noted former Henei governor, loathed Du's ways, feared for his life, and fled by sea with his family.

manualTranslations.zh: 度大怒，掘其父塚，剖棺焚屍，誅其宗族。
manualTranslations.literal: Du in great anger dug up his father's tomb, opened the coffin and burned the corpse, and executed his clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du dug up Li's father's tomb, burned the corpse, and wiped out the clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：敏子追求敏，出塞，越二十餘年不娶。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jinyangqiu says: Min's son pursued Min, went beyond the frontier, and for more than twenty years did not marry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jinyangqiu says Min's son searched for him beyond the passes and remained unmarried for twenty years.

manualTranslations.zh: 州里徐邈責之曰：「不孝莫大於無後，何可終身不娶乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Xu Miao of the province and commandery rebuked him, saying, "Nothing is more unfilial than having no heir—how can you never marry!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xu Miao of his district scolded him: "No greater unfilial act than leaving no heir—how can you never marry?"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃娶妻，生子胤而遣妻，常如居喪之禮，不勝憂，數年而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He then took a wife, had a son Yin and sent his wife away, always observing mourning rites as if in bereavement; unable to bear grief, he died within several years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He married, fathered Yin, then sent his wife away and lived in mourning grief until he died within years.

manualTranslations.zh: 胤生不識父母，及有識，蔬食哀戚亦如三年之喪。
manualTranslations.literal: Yin never knew his parents; once he could understand, he ate plain food and mourned as in three years' mourning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yin never knew his parents; once aware, he ate plainly and mourned three years.

manualTranslations.zh: 以祖父不知存亡，設主奉之。
manualTranslations.literal: Because his grandfather's fate was unknown, he set up a spirit tablet and served it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not knowing whether his grandfather lived or died, he set up a tablet and served it.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是知名，仕至司徒。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereby he became famous and rose to minister over the masses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He became known and rose to minister over the masses.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：本傳云敏將家入海，而復與子相失，未詳其故。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Pei Songzhi notes: The main biography says Min took his family to sea yet also lost his son—the reason is unclear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the biography says Min fled to sea yet also lost his son—the account is unclear.

manualTranslations.zh: 分遼東郡為遼西中遼郡，置太守。
manualTranslations.literal: He divided Liaodong commandery into western Liaodong and central Liaodong commanderies and appointed governors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He split Liaodong into western and central Liaodong commanderies and set governors over them.

manualTranslations.zh: 越海收東萊諸縣，置營州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Crossing the sea he gathered the counties of Donglai and appointed a governor of Yingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He crossed the sea, seized Donglai counties, and appointed a Yingzhou governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 自立為遼東侯、平州牧，追封父延為建義侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He declared himself marquis of Liaodong and governor of Pingzhou, posthumously enfeoffing his father Yan as marquis who establishes righteousness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He made himself marquis of Liaodong and governor of Pingzhou and posthumously enfeoffed his father Yan marquis who establishes righteousness.

manualTranslations.zh: 立漢二祖廟，承制設壇墠於襄平城南，郊祀天地，藉田，治兵，乘鸞路，九旒，旄頭羽騎。
manualTranslations.literal: He built temples to the two Han founders, assumed regal powers, set altar mounds south of Xiangping, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, performed ceremonial plowing, drilled troops, rode the imperial carriage, bore nine tassels, and had plumed-head guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He built temples to Han's founders, set altars south of Xiangping, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, plowed ceremonially, drilled troops, and rode regalia with nine tassels and plumed guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖表度為武威將軍，封永寧鄉侯，度曰：「我王遼東，何永寧也！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized Du as general of martial might and enfeoffed him marquis of Yongning township; Du said, "I am king of Liaodong—what is Yongning?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao nominated him general of martial might and enfeoffed him marquis of Yongning; Du said, "I rule Liaodong—what is Yongning?"

manualTranslations.zh: 藏印綬武庫。
manualTranslations.literal: He stored the seal and ribbon in the armory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He locked the seal and ribbon in the armory.

manualTranslations.zh: 度死，子康嗣位，以永寧鄉侯封弟恭。
manualTranslations.literal: Du died; his son Kang succeeded, enfeoffing his younger brother Gong as marquis of Yongning township.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Du died Kang succeeded and enfeoffed his brother Gong marquis of Yongning.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲建安九年也。
manualTranslations.literal: That year was the ninth year of Jian'an (204).
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That was Jian'an 9 (204).

sourceRange.text: 二年春，遣太尉司馬宣王徵淵。六月，軍至遼東。《漢晉春秋》曰：公孫淵自立，稱紹漢元年。聞魏人將討，復稱臣於吳，乞兵北伐以自救。吳人欲戮其使，羊衜曰：「不可，是肆匹夫之怒而捐霸王之計也。不如因而厚之，遣奇兵潛往以要其成。若魏伐淵不克，而我軍遠赴，是恩結遐夷，義蓋萬里，若兵連不解，首尾離隔，則我虜其傍郡，驅略而歸，亦足以致天之罰，報雪曩事矣。」權曰：「善」。乃勒兵大出。謂淵使曰：「請俟後問，當從簡書，必與弟同休戚，共存亡，雖隕於中原，吾所甘心也。」又曰：「司馬懿所向無前，深為弟憂也。」淵遣將軍卑衍、楊祚等步騎數万屯遼隧，圍塹二十餘里。宣王軍至，令衍逆戰。宣王遣將軍胡遵等擊破之。宣王令軍穿圍，引兵東南向，而急東北，即趨襄平。衍等恐襄平無守，夜走。諸軍進至首山，淵復遣衍等迎軍殊死戰。复擊，大破之，遂進軍造城下，為圍塹。會霖雨三十餘日，遼水暴長，運船自遼口徑至城下。雨霽，起土山、脩櫓，為發石連弩射城中。淵窘急。糧盡，人相食，死者甚多。將軍楊祚等降。八月丙寅夜，大流星長數十丈，從首山東北墜襄平城東南。壬午，淵眾潰，與其子脩將數百騎突圍東南走，大兵急擊之，當流星所墜處，斬淵父子。城破，斬相國以下首級以千數，傳淵首洛陽，遼東、帶方、樂浪、玄菟悉平。

context.beforeSource: 惟陛下恢崇撫育，亮其控告，使疏遠之臣，永有保持。
context.afterSource: 初，淵家數有怪，犬冠幘絳衣上屋，炊有小兒蒸死甑中。

manualTranslations.zh: 二年春，遣太尉司馬宣王徵淵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, spring, the Grand Marshal's major, the Lord of War, was sent to summon Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring of year 2 the Grand Marshal's major—the Lord of War—was dispatched against Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 六月，軍至遼東。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month the army reached Liaodong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the army reached Liaodong.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：公孫淵自立，稱紹漢元年。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Jin chunqiu says: Gongsun Yuan had declared himself and titled his reign Shaohan year 1.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Jin chunqiu says Yuan had declared Shaohan year 1.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞魏人將討，復稱臣於吳，乞兵北伐以自救。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing Wei would punish him, he again submitted to Wu and begged troops for a northern campaign to save himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing of Wei's march, he again bowed to Wu and begged rescue.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳人欲戮其使，羊衜曰：「不可，是肆匹夫之怒而捐霸王之計也。
manualTranslations.literal: The men of Wu wished to kill his envoys; Yang Tao said, "No—this would indulge a common man's wrath and abandon a hegemon's plan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu wanted to kill his envoys; Yang Tao said, "No—that is a commoner's rage, not a hegemon's plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 不如因而厚之，遣奇兵潛往以要其成。
manualTranslations.literal: Better treat him generously and send secret troops to await success.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Treat him well and send secret troops to seize the chance.

manualTranslations.zh: 若魏伐淵不克，而我軍遠赴，是恩結遐夷，義蓋萬里，若兵連不解，首尾離隔，則我虜其傍郡，驅略而歸，亦足以致天之罰，報雪曩事矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: If Wei attacks Yuan and fails while our army goes far, we bind distant peoples in grace spanning ten thousand li; if war drags on and head and tail are cut off, we can seize neighboring commanderies, drive and plunder home, and that is enough to bring Heaven's punishment and avenge old wrongs."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Wei fails and we march far, we win distant hearts; if war stalls, we can raid neighboring counties and carry off spoils—enough for Heaven's punishment and old vengeance."

manualTranslations.zh: 權曰：「善」。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan said, "Good."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Quan said, "Good."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃勒兵大出。
manualTranslations.literal: He then mustered troops on a great scale.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then mobilized on a great scale.

manualTranslations.zh: 謂淵使曰：「請俟後問，當從簡書，必與弟同休戚，共存亡，雖隕於中原，吾所甘心也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He told Yuan's envoys, "Wait for later word; I will follow the brief letter—surely I will share fortune and misfortune with your lord, live and die together; though I fall in the central plains, I am willing."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He told Yuan's envoys, "Await my letter—we will share life and death; though I fall in the heartland, I accept it."

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「司馬懿所向無前，深為弟憂也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He also said, "Sima Yi goes where none can stand before him—I deeply worry for your lord."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He added, "Sima Yi is irresistible—I fear for your lord."

manualTranslations.zh: 淵遣將軍卑衍、楊祚等步騎數万屯遼隧，圍塹二十餘里。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan sent the generals Bei Yan and Yang Zuo with tens of thousands of foot and horse to camp at Liaosui with entrenchments over twenty li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Bei Yan and Yang Zuo with tens of thousands to entrench at Liaosui for over twenty li.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王軍至，令衍逆戰。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord of War's army arrived and ordered Yan to meet battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Lord of War arrived he ordered Yan to fight.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王遣將軍胡遵等擊破之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord of War sent General Hu Zun and others to break them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent Hu Zun and others to rout them.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王令軍穿圍，引兵東南向，而急東北，即趨襄平。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord of War ordered the army to pierce the encirclement, draw troops southeast yet hurry northeast, and press straight for Xiangping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He pierced the ring, feinted southeast, then rushed northeast for Xiangping.

manualTranslations.zh: 衍等恐襄平無守，夜走。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan and the others feared Xiangping was undefended and fled by night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fearing for Xiangping, Yan fled by night.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸軍進至首山，淵復遣衍等迎軍殊死戰。
manualTranslations.literal: The armies advanced to Shoushan; Yuan again sent Yan and others to meet the army in desperate battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Shoushan Yuan sent Yan again in a death fight.

manualTranslations.zh: 复擊，大破之，遂進軍造城下，為圍塹。
manualTranslations.literal: They struck again and routed them greatly, then advanced to the city and made siege trenches.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They beat them again, advanced to the walls, and dug siege lines.

manualTranslations.zh: 會霖雨三十餘日，遼水暴長，運船自遼口徑至城下。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that rain fell more than thirty days; the Liao River swelled, and transport ships came straight from Liaokou to below the city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rain fell thirty days; the Liao flooded and supply ships reached the walls from Liaokou.

manualTranslations.zh: 雨霽，起土山、脩櫓，為發石連弩射城中。
manualTranslations.literal: When the rain cleared they raised earthen hills and repaired siege towers, setting stone-hurlers and repeating crossbows to shoot into the city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the rain they built mounds and towers and battered the city with catapults and repeating crossbows.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵窘急。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan was pressed to extremity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan was desperate.

manualTranslations.zh: 糧盡，人相食，死者甚多。
manualTranslations.literal: Grain was exhausted; men ate one another, and the dead were very many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Food ran out; men cannibalized one another and corpses piled up.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍楊祚等降。
manualTranslations.literal: The general Yang Zuo and others surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Yang Zuo and others surrendered.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月丙寅夜，大流星長數十丈，從首山東北墜襄平城東南。
manualTranslations.literal: On the night of bingyin, the eighth month, a great meteor tens of zhang long fell from northeast of Shoushan to southeast of Xiangping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On bingyin night in the eighth month a great meteor tens of zhang long fell from Shoushan toward southeast Xiangping.

manualTranslations.zh: 壬午，淵眾潰，與其子脩將數百騎突圍東南走，大兵急擊之，當流星所墜處，斬淵父子。
manualTranslations.literal: On renwu Yuan's host collapsed; with his son Xiu he led several hundred horsemen to break out southeast; the great army pressed the attack and, right where the meteor fell, beheaded Yuan father and son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renwu Yuan's force broke; he and his son Xiu fled southeast with hundreds of horse; the army struck where the meteor fell and beheaded them.

manualTranslations.zh: 城破，斬相國以下首級以千數，傳淵首洛陽，遼東、帶方、樂浪、玄菟悉平。
manualTranslations.literal: The city fell; heads of the chancellor of state and below numbered in the thousands; Yuan's head was sent to Luoyang; Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang, and Xuantu were all pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The city fell; over a thousand heads of chancellor and below were taken; Yuan's head went to Luoyang; Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang, and Xuantu were pacified.

sourceRange.text: 尚有愛妾嬖幸，寵奪適室；適室，曹氏女也，故文帝遣人絞殺之。尚悲感，發病怳惚，旣葬埋妾，不勝思見，復出視之。文帝聞而恚之曰：「杜襲之輕薄尚，良有以也。」然以舊臣，恩寵不衰。六年，尚疾篤，還京都，帝數臨幸，執手涕泣。尚薨，謚曰悼侯。《魏書》載詔曰：「尚自少侍從，盡誠竭節，雖云異姓，其猶骨肉，是以入爲腹心，出當爪牙。智略深敏，謀謨過人，不幸早殞，命也柰何！贈征南大將軍、昌陵侯印綬。」子玄嗣。又分尚戶三百，賜尚弟子奉爵關內侯。

manualTranslations.zh: 尚有愛妾嬖幸，寵奪適室；
manualTranslations.literal: Shang still had a favored concubine whom he doted on, and her favor usurped that of the principal wife;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Shang still kept a favored concubine whose attentions displaced those of his principal wife;

manualTranslations.zh: 適室，曹氏女也，故文帝遣人絞殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: the principal wife was a daughter of the Cao clan, so Emperor Wen sent men to strangle her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The principal wife was a Cao clanswoman, so Emperor Wen had her strangled.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚悲感，發病怳惚，旣葬埋妾，不勝思見，復出視之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shang was grieved and moved, fell ill in confusion and delirium; after burying the concubine, unable to bear longing to see her, he went out again to look at her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grief and shock left Shang delirious; after the concubine was buried he could not bear the longing, went out, and looked upon her grave again.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝聞而恚之曰：「杜襲之輕薄尚，良有以也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen heard of it and grew angry, saying: "Du Xi's slighting of Shang was well founded indeed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of it he fumed: "Du Xi was right to look down on Shang."

manualTranslations.zh: 然以舊臣，恩寵不衰。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet because he was an old minister, favor and grace did not decline.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As an old servant of the house, however, Shang's favor never waned.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年，尚疾篤，還京都，帝數臨幸，執手涕泣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year Shang fell gravely ill, returned to the capital, and the emperor repeatedly visited him in person, taking his hand and weeping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, mortally ill, Shang returned to the capital; the emperor visited him again and again, clasped his hand, and wept.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚薨，謚曰悼侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Shang died; his posthumous title was Marquis Dao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shang died and was posthumously titled Marquis Dao.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》載詔曰：「尚自少侍從，盡誠竭節，雖云異姓，其猶骨肉，是以入爲腹心，出當爪牙。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei records an edict saying: "From youth Shang attended and followed, exhausting loyalty and exhausting integrity; though called of another surname, he was like flesh and bone; therefore within he was made heart and belly, without he served as fang and claw.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves an edict: "From boyhood Shang served at my side with utter loyalty. Though not of our surname, he was as close as kin—my confidant within, my talon without.

manualTranslations.zh: 智略深敏，謀謨過人，不幸早殞，命也柰何！
manualTranslations.literal: His wisdom and stratagem were deep and keen, his counsel surpassed other men; unhappily he perished early—fate, what can be done!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mind was keen and his counsel surpassed other men's; that he died young was fate—what can be done?"

manualTranslations.zh: 贈征南大將軍、昌陵侯印綬。」
manualTranslations.literal: He was granted the seals and ribbon of General Who Conquers the South and Marquis of Changling."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He is granted the seals of General Who Conquers the South and Marquis of Changling."

manualTranslations.zh: 子玄嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Xuan succeeded him.

manualTranslations.zh: 又分尚戶三百，賜尚弟子奉爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Again three hundred households of Shang's fief were divided off and given to Shang's younger cousin Feng, enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three hundred households from Shang's fief were also set aside for his younger cousin Feng, who was enfeoffed as a marquis within the passes.

sourceRange.text: 太祖自徐州還，惇從征吕布，爲流矢所中，傷左目。《魏略》曰：時夏侯淵與惇俱爲將軍，軍中號惇爲盲夏侯。惇惡之，每照鏡恚怒，輒撲鏡於地。復領陳留、濟陰太守，加建武將軍，封高安鄉侯。時大旱，蝗蟲起，惇乃斷太壽水作陂，身自負土，率將士勸種稻，民賴其利。轉領河南尹。太祖平河北，爲大將軍後拒。鄴破，遷伏波將軍，領尹如故，使得以便宜從事，不拘科制。建安十二年，錄惇前後功，增封邑千八百户，并前二千五百户。二十一年，從征孫權還，使惇都督二十六軍，留居巢。賜伎樂名倡，令曰：「魏絳以和戎之功，猶受金石之樂，況將軍乎！」二十四年，太祖軍於摩陂，召惇常與同載，特見親重，出入臥内，諸將莫得比也。拜前將軍，《魏書》曰：時諸將皆受魏官號，惇獨漢官，乃上疏自陳不當不臣之禮。太祖曰：「吾聞太上師臣，其次友臣。夫臣者，貴德之人也，區區之魏，而臣足以屈君乎？」惇固請，乃拜爲前將軍。督諸軍還壽春，徙屯召陵。文帝即王位，拜惇大將軍，數月薨。惇雖在軍旅，親迎師受業。性清儉，有餘財輒以分施，不足資之於官，不治產業。諡曰忠侯。子充嗣。帝追思惇功，欲使子孫畢侯，分惇邑千户，賜惇七子二孫爵皆關内侯。惇弟廉及子楙素自封列侯。初，太祖以女妻楙，即清河公主也。楙歷位侍中尚書、安西鎮東將軍，假節。《魏略》曰：楙字子林，惇中子也。文帝少與楙親，及即位，以爲安西將軍、持節，承夏侯淵處都督關中。楙性無武略，而好治生。至太和二年228年，明帝西征，人有白楙者，遂召還爲尚書。楙在西時，多畜伎妾，公主由此與楙不和。其後羣弟不遵禮度，楙數切責，弟懼見治，乃共構楙以誹謗，公主奏之，有詔收楙。帝意欲殺之，以問長水校尉京兆段默，默以爲「此必清河公主與楙不睦，出於譖構，冀不推實耳。且伏波與先帝有定天下之功，宜加三思」。帝意解，曰：「吾亦以爲然。」乃發詔推問爲公主作表者，果其羣弟子臧、子江所構也。充薨，子廙嗣。廙薨，子劭嗣。《晉陽秋》曰：泰始二年266年，高安鄉侯夏侯佐卒，惇之孫也，嗣絕。詔曰：「惇，魏之元功，勳書竹帛。昔庭堅不祀，猶或悼之，況朕受禪於魏，而可以忘其功臣哉！宜擇惇近屬劭封之。」韓浩者，河内人。及沛國史渙與浩俱以忠勇顯。浩至中護軍，渙至中領軍，皆掌禁兵，封列侯。《魏書》曰：韓浩字元嗣。漢末兵起，縣近山藪，多寇，浩聚徒眾爲縣籓衛。太守王匡以爲從事，將兵拒董卓於盟津。時浩舅杜陽爲河陰令，卓執之，使招浩，浩不從。袁术聞而壯之，以爲騎都尉。夏侯惇聞其名，請與相見，大奇之，使領兵從征伐。時大議損益，浩以爲當急田。太祖善之，遷護軍。太祖欲討柳城，領軍史渙以爲道遠深入，非完計也，欲與浩共諫。浩曰：「今兵勢彊盛，威加四海，戰勝攻取，無不如志，不以此時遂除天下之患，將爲後憂。且公神武，舉無遺策，吾與君爲中軍主，不宜沮眾。」遂從破柳城，改其官爲中護軍，置長史、司馬。從討張魯，魯降。議者以浩智略足以綏邊，欲留使都督諸軍，鎮漢中。太祖曰：「吾安可以無護軍？」乃與俱還。其見親任如此。及薨，太祖愍惜之。無子，以養子榮嗣。史渙字公劉。少任俠，有雄氣。太祖初起，以客從，行中軍校尉，從征伐，常監諸將，見親信，轉拜中領軍。十四年薨。子静嗣。

localRange.text: 韓浩、史渙夏侯淵

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖自徐州還，惇從征吕布，爲流矢所中，傷左目。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor returned from Xu province, Dun followed in campaigning against Lü Bu, was struck by a stray arrow, and wounded in the left eye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao withdrew from Xu province, Dun joined the campaign against Lü Bu, took a stray arrow in the left eye, and was badly wounded.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：時夏侯淵與惇俱爲將軍，軍中號惇爲盲夏侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: At that time Xiahou Yuan and Dun were both generals, and in the army they called Dun Blind Xiahou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei notes that he and Xiahou Yuan were then both serving as generals, and the troops nicknamed Dun "Blind Xiahou."

manualTranslations.zh: 惇惡之，每照鏡恚怒，輒撲鏡於地。
manualTranslations.literal: Dun hated this; each time he looked in the mirror he fumed with anger and would dash the mirror to the ground.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dun loathed the sobriquet; whenever he caught his reflection he flew into a rage and smashed the mirror to the floor.

manualTranslations.zh: 復領陳留、濟陰太守，加建武將軍，封高安鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He again headed Chenliu and Jiyin as grand administrator, was promoted to General Who Establishes Martial Might, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Gao'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He resumed the governorship of Chenliu and Jiyin, was advanced to General Who Establishes Martial Might, and received the village marquisate of Gao'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 時大旱，蝗蟲起，惇乃斷太壽水作陂，身自負土，率將士勸種稻，民賴其利。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time there was great drought and locusts arose; Dun then cut off the Taishou River to make a reservoir, himself shouldered earth, led officers and troops to urge planting rice, and the people relied on its benefit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During a severe drought and locust plague he dammed the Taishou River into a reservoir, carried earth on his own back, and drove his soldiers to plant rice; the common people profited from the scheme.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉領河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to head Henan as intendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was then named intendant of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖平河北，爲大將軍後拒。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Hebei, he served as rear guard of the grand general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao subdued Hebei, Dun guarded the army's rear as grand general.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄴破，遷伏波將軍，領尹如故，使得以便宜從事，不拘科制。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ye fell, he was transferred to General Who Calms the Waves, kept the intendant post as before, and was allowed to act at discretion without being bound by regulations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Ye was taken he became General Who Calms the Waves, kept Henan as before, and was empowered to act on his own authority outside the usual statutes.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安十二年，錄惇前後功，增封邑千八百户，并前二千五百户。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jian'an, Dun's merits before and after were recorded; his fief was increased by one thousand eight hundred households, making two thousand five hundred households in all with the previous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 12 his cumulative honors were tallied and his fief enlarged by 1,800 households, bringing the total to 2,500.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十一年，從征孫權還，使惇都督二十六軍，留居巢。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-first year, after returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, he had Dun command the twenty-six armies and remain at Juchao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Cao Cao left Dun in command of twenty-six armies, stationed at Juchao.

manualTranslations.zh: 賜伎樂名倡，令曰：「魏絳以和戎之功，猶受金石之樂，況將軍乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: He bestowed song and dance with famous performers, with an order saying: "Wei Jiang, for the merit of harmonizing the barbarians, still received music of metal and stone; how much more so for a general!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He gave him musicians and celebrated courtesans, declaring: "Wei Jiang won music of bells and drums for pacifying the Rong—surely a general deserves no less!"

manualTranslations.zh: 二十四年，太祖軍於摩陂，召惇常與同載，特見親重，出入臥内，諸將莫得比也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the Grand Progenitor's army was at Mobei, he summoned Dun and often rode with him in the same carriage, showed him special intimacy and weight, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters; no general could compare.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, while Cao Cao camped at Mobei, Dun was constantly summoned to share his carriage, treated with exceptional trust, and admitted to the inner quarters—privilege none of his peers matched.

manualTranslations.zh: 拜前將軍，《魏書》曰：時諸將皆受魏官號，惇獨漢官，乃上疏自陳不當不臣之禮。
manualTranslations.literal: He was appointed General of the Vanguard. The Book of Wei says: At that time all the generals received Wei office titles; Dun alone held a Han office, so he submitted a memorial stating that he ought not follow the rites of one who is not a subject.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was named General of the Vanguard. The Book of Wei records that every other commander had already taken Wei titles while Dun still bore Han rank; he memorialized that he could not accept honors implying he was not a subject of the Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「吾聞太上師臣，其次友臣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "I have heard that the loftiest treats ministers as teachers, next as friends.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied: "They say the sage-emperor treats ministers as teachers, and after that as friends.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫臣者，貴德之人也，區區之魏，而臣足以屈君乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: As for ministers, they are men who esteem virtue; how could a mere Wei make a minister enough to humble a lord?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A minister is a man who honors virtue—how could petty Wei make me your subject and bow you down?"

manualTranslations.zh: 惇固請，乃拜爲前將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Dun firmly petitioned, and thereupon he was appointed general of the vanguard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dun pressed the point until Cao Cao finally confirmed him as General of the Vanguard.

manualTranslations.zh: 督諸軍還壽春，徙屯召陵。
manualTranslations.literal: He supervised the armies returning to Shouchun and moved encampment to Zhaoling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He led the armies back to Shouchun and then shifted the camp to Zhaoling.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝即王位，拜惇大將軍，數月薨。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the royal throne, he appointed Dun grand general; after several months he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended as king of Wei he named Dun grand general; Dun died within months.

manualTranslations.zh: 惇雖在軍旅，親迎師受業。
manualTranslations.literal: Although Dun was amid the army, he personally welcomed teachers and received instruction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even on campaign he sought out tutors and received classical instruction in person.

manualTranslations.zh: 性清儉，有餘財輒以分施，不足資之於官，不治產業。
manualTranslations.literal: His nature was clear and frugal; whenever he had surplus wealth he would distribute it, and what was insufficient he supplied from office, not managing estates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was austere by nature, gave away every surplus, drew on official funds rather than private wealth when funds ran short, and never built up family property.

manualTranslations.zh: 諡曰忠侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was canonized as Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).

manualTranslations.zh: 子充嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Chong succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Chong inherited the title.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝追思惇功，欲使子孫畢侯，分惇邑千户，賜惇七子二孫爵皆關内侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor recalled Dun's merit, wished to make his sons and grandsons all marquises, divided Dun's fief by a thousand households, and bestowed on Dun's seven sons and two grandsons titles, all interior marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor, recalling Dun's service, wished to ennoble the whole line: he carved a thousand households from Dun's fief and made interior marquises of seven sons and two grandsons.

manualTranslations.zh: 惇弟廉及子楙素自封列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Dun's younger brother Lian and his son Mao had long since enfeoffed themselves as ranked marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dun's brother Lian and son Mao had already held ranked marquisates in their own right.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，太祖以女妻楙，即清河公主也。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, the Grand Progenitor gave a daughter in marriage to Mao, namely the Princess of Qinghe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had earlier married his daughter—the Princess of Qinghe—to Mao.

manualTranslations.zh: 楙歷位侍中尚書、安西鎮東將軍，假節。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao successively held the posts of attendant-in-chief and minister of the masters of writing, General Who Pacifies the West and Quiets the East, and was given the credentials of office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mao rose through attendant-in-chief, minister of the masters of writing, and General Who Pacifies the West and Quiets the East, and carried the baton of command.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：楙字子林，惇中子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Mao, courtesy name Zilin, was Dun's middle son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei gives his style as Zilin and identifies him as Dun's second son.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝少與楙親，及即位，以爲安西將軍、持節，承夏侯淵處都督關中。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen in youth was close to Mao; when he took the throne, he made him General Who Pacifies the West, bearing the baton, succeeding Xiahou Yuan's post in commanding Guanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had been close to Mao since boyhood; on his accession he named Mao General Who Pacifies the West with full insignia, succeeding Xiahou Yuan as commander of Guanzhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 楙性無武略，而好治生。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao's nature lacked martial stratagem, but he loved managing livelihood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mao had no talent for war but a passion for moneymaking.

manualTranslations.zh: 至太和二年228年，明帝西征，人有白楙者，遂召還爲尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: By the second year of Taihe, 228, when Emperor Ming campaigned west, someone reported Mao, and he was summoned back as minister of the masters of writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 (228), during Emperor Ming's western expedition, an informer denounced Mao and he was recalled to court as minister of the masters of writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 楙在西時，多畜伎妾，公主由此與楙不和。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mao was in the west, he kept many singing girls and concubines; the princess because of this was not on good terms with Mao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While stationed in the west Mao kept a large household of entertainers and concubines, which alienated the princess.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後羣弟不遵禮度，楙數切責，弟懼見治，乃共構楙以誹謗，公主奏之，有詔收楙。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward his brothers-in-law did not observe the rules of propriety; Mao repeatedly sternly rebuked them; the younger brothers feared punishment and together framed Mao for slander; the princess memorialized it, and there was an edict to arrest Mao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When his wife's brothers flouted decorum, Mao scolded them repeatedly; fearing punishment they conspired to accuse him of slander, the princess petitioned the throne, and an edict went out for his arrest.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝意欲殺之，以問長水校尉京兆段默，默以爲「此必清河公主與楙不睦，出於譖構，冀不推實耳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor intended to kill him, and asked Colonel of the Long River Duan Mo of Jingzhao; Mo thought: "This must be because the Princess of Qinghe and Mao were not on good terms, arising from slanderous framing, hoping it would not be pursued to the facts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor meant to execute him and consulted Colonel of the Long River Duan Mo of Jingzhao, who said: "This surely stems from the princess's quarrel with Mao—a fabricated charge they hope no one will investigate.

manualTranslations.zh: 且伏波與先帝有定天下之功，宜加三思」。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, the Pacifying-the-Waves General and the late Emperor had the merit of settling the realm; one ought to add threefold deliberation."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Besides, Mao's father served the late emperor in conquering the realm—think thrice before acting."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝意解，曰：「吾亦以爲然。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor's mind was eased and he said: "I also think it so."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented: "I believe you are right."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃發詔推問爲公主作表者，果其羣弟子臧、子江所構也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict to pursue inquiry into who had drafted the princess's memorial; indeed it was framed by her brothers-in-law Zizang and Zijiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An investigation traced the memorial to Mao's brothers-in-law Zizang and Zijiang, who had fabricated the case.

manualTranslations.zh: 充薨，子廙嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong died; his son Yi succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Chong died his son Yi inherited.

manualTranslations.zh: 廙薨，子劭嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi died; his son Shao succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yi died his son Shao inherited.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：泰始二年266年，高安鄉侯夏侯佐卒，惇之孫也，嗣絕。
manualTranslations.literal: The Annals of Jin says: In the second year of Taishi, 266, village marquis of Gao'an Xiahou Zuo died, was Dun's grandson, and the succession ended.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals of Jin record that in Taishi 2 (266) Xiahou Zuo, village marquis of Gao'an and Dun's grandson, died without heirs.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「惇，魏之元功，勳書竹帛。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said: "Dun was Wei's paramount merit, his achievements written on bamboo and silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Dun was Wei's founding pillar; his deeds stand inscribed in the annals.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔庭堅不祀，猶或悼之，況朕受禪於魏，而可以忘其功臣哉！
manualTranslations.literal: In former times when Ting Jian had no sacrifices, some still mourned him; how much more, since I received the abdication from Wei, can I forget its meritorious ministers!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ting Jian went without sacrifice men still grieved—how could I, having received the mandate from Wei, forget its champions?

manualTranslations.zh: 宜擇惇近屬劭封之。」
manualTranslations.literal: It is fitting to select Dun's close kinsman Shao and enfeoff him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let Shao, Dun's nearest kin, be chosen to receive the enfeoffment."

manualTranslations.zh: 韓浩者，河内人。
manualTranslations.literal: Han Hao was a man of Henei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Hao came from Henei commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 及沛國史渙與浩俱以忠勇顯。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with Shi Huan of Pei state, Hao became renowned for loyalty and courage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He and Shi Huan of Pei were both famed for loyal daring.

manualTranslations.zh: 浩至中護軍，渙至中領軍，皆掌禁兵，封列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao reached chief of the protectors army, Huan reached commander of the central army, both controlled the forbidden troops, and were enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Hao rose to chief of the protectors army and Shi Huan to commander of the central army; both held the palace guard and received ranked marquisates.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：韓浩字元嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Han Hao, courtesy name Yuansi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei gives his style as Yuansi.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢末兵起，縣近山藪，多寇，浩聚徒眾爲縣籓衛。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Han when troops arose, the county was near mountains and marshes with many bandits; Hao gathered followers to defend the county as a barrier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When war engulfed the Han, his county lay close to wild hills teeming with raiders; Hao rallied a militia to shield the district.

manualTranslations.zh: 太守王匡以爲從事，將兵拒董卓於盟津。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Kuang made him an assistant officer, leading troops to resist Dong Zhuo at Mengjin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand administrator Wang Kuang named him an aide and sent him with troops to block Dong Zhuo at Mengjin.

manualTranslations.zh: 時浩舅杜陽爲河陰令，卓執之，使招浩，浩不從。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Hao's maternal uncle Du Yang was magistrate of Heyin; Zhuo seized him and had him summon Hao; Hao did not comply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo seized Hao's uncle Du Yang, magistrate of Heyin, and used him to summon Hao; Hao refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 袁术聞而壯之，以爲騎都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Shu heard and admired him, and made him commandant of cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu admired his stand and appointed him commandant of cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏侯惇聞其名，請與相見，大奇之，使領兵從征伐。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiahou Dun heard his name, requested to meet him, was greatly struck, and had him lead troops following on campaigns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun sought him out, was mightily impressed, and took him on campaign as a commander.

manualTranslations.zh: 時大議損益，浩以爲當急田。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time there was great discussion of increase and decrease; Hao thought one should urgently farm fields.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Amid debate over fiscal reform, Hao argued that agriculture must come first.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖善之，遷護軍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved it and promoted him to protector of the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved and promoted him to protector of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖欲討柳城，領軍史渙以爲道遠深入，非完計也，欲與浩共諫。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to punish Liucheng; army commander Shi Huan thought the road distant and penetration deep, not a complete plan, and wished together with Hao to remonstrate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao planned an expedition to Liucheng, army commander Shi Huan judged the march too long and deep to be sound policy and urged Hao to join him in counseling against it.

manualTranslations.zh: 浩曰：「今兵勢彊盛，威加四海，戰勝攻取，無不如志，不以此時遂除天下之患，將爲後憂。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao said: "Now military strength is mighty and flourishing, prestige covers the four seas, in battle victorious and in attack taking—nothing fails to accord with intent; if we do not at this time then remove the realm's afflictions, there will be later worry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Hao replied: "Our armies are at their height and nothing resists us—if we do not crush the realm's enemies now, we will rue the delay.

manualTranslations.zh: 且公神武，舉無遺策，吾與君爲中軍主，不宜沮眾。」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the lord is divinely martial; in every move no plan is left out; you and I are masters of the central army—one ought not discourage the host."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lord is invincible in counsel; as chiefs of staff we must not dampen the troops' spirit."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂從破柳城，改其官爲中護軍，置長史、司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he followed in breaking Liucheng; his office was changed to chief of the protectors army, and a chief clerk and marshal were appointed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He joined the victory at Liucheng, was retitled chief of the protectors army, and given chief clerk and marshal.

manualTranslations.zh: 從討張魯，魯降。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed in punishing Zhang Lu; Lu surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Zhang Lu, Lu submitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 議者以浩智略足以綏邊，欲留使都督諸軍，鎮漢中。
manualTranslations.literal: Discussants thought Hao's wisdom and stratagem sufficient to pacify the borderlands, and wished to keep him to command the various armies and guard Hanzhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some urged keeping Han Hao in Hanzhong to command the western armies, trusting his talent for border affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「吾安可以無護軍？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "How can I be without a protector of the army?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered: "How can I do without my protector of the army?"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃與俱還。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they returned together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao returned with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 其見親任如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Such was the intimacy and trust shown him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That was how deeply he was trusted.

manualTranslations.zh: 及薨，太祖愍惜之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, the Grand Progenitor pitied and mourned him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At his death Cao Cao grieved deeply.

manualTranslations.zh: 無子，以養子榮嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: He had no son; his adopted son Rong succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Childless, he was succeeded by his adopted son Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 史渙字公劉。
manualTranslations.literal: Shi Huan, courtesy name Gongliu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Huan, styled Gongliu.

manualTranslations.zh: 少任俠，有雄氣。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he was a knight-errant, with heroic spirit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a youth he lived by the sword and bore a fierce temper.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖初起，以客從，行中軍校尉，從征伐，常監諸將，見親信，轉拜中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first rose, he followed as a guest, acted as colonel of the central army, followed on campaigns, constantly supervised the generals, was seen as intimate and trusted, and was transferred and appointed commander of the central army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first raised his standard, Huan joined as a guest officer, served as acting colonel of the central army, joined every campaign, oversaw the commanders, won close trust, and rose to commander of the central army.

manualTranslations.zh: 十四年薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

manualTranslations.zh: 子静嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Jing succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Jing inherited the title.

sourceRange.text: 仁少時不脩行检，及長爲將，嚴整奉法令，常置科於左右，案以從事。鄢陵侯彰北征烏丸，文帝在東宫，爲書戒彰曰：「爲將奉法，不當如征南邪！」及即王位，拜仁车騎將軍，都督荆、揚、益州諸軍事，進封陳侯，增邑二千，并前三千五百户。追賜仁父炽諡曰陳穆侯，置守冢十家。後召還屯宛。孫權遣將陳邵据襄陽，詔仁討之。仁與徐晃攻破邵，遂入襄陽，使將軍高遷等徙漢南附化民於漢北，文帝遣使即拜仁大將軍。又詔仁移屯临潁，遷大司馬，復督諸軍据烏江，還屯合肥。黃初四年薨，諡曰忠侯。《魏書》曰：仁時年五十六。《傅子》曰：曹大司馬之勇，賁、育弗加也。張辽其次焉。子泰嗣，官至鎮東將軍，假節，轉封甯陵侯。泰薨，子初嗣。又分封泰弟楷、範，皆爲列侯，而牛金官至後將軍。仁弟純，《英雄記》曰：純字子和。

localRange.text: 弟純仁弟純，〈《英雄記》曰：純字子和。

context.beforeSource: 徐晃救至，水亦稍减，晃從外擊羽，仁得溃圍出，羽退走。
context.afterSource: 年十四而喪父，與同產兄仁别居。

manualTranslations.zh: 仁少時不脩行检，及長爲將，嚴整奉法令，常置科於左右，案以從事。
manualTranslations.literal: Ren in youth did not cultivate conduct and discipline; when grown as a general he was strict and orderly in upholding laws and commands, always kept regulations at his side, and judged cases accordingly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a young man Cao Ren was unruly, but once he took command he enforced the code rigorously, kept regulations at hand, and judged every infraction by the book.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄢陵侯彰北征烏丸，文帝在東宫，爲書戒彰曰：「爲將奉法，不當如征南邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis of Yanling Zhang campaigned north against the Wuhuan; Emperor Wen was in the Eastern Palace and wrote a letter admonishing Zhang saying: "As a general upholding law, ought you not be like the general who campaigns south!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Yanling Cao Zhang marched north against the Wuhuan, Crown Prince Wen wrote warning him: "A general who upholds the law should take his cue from the southern expedition commander!"

manualTranslations.zh: 及即王位，拜仁车騎將軍，都督荆、揚、益州諸軍事，進封陳侯，增邑二千，并前三千五百户。
manualTranslations.literal: When he took the royal throne, he appointed Ren General of Chariots and Cavalry, supervisor of military affairs for Jing, Yang, and Yi provinces, advanced him to Marquis of Chen, added two thousand households to his fief, making three thousand five hundred households in all with the previous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On taking the royal throne he named Ren General of Chariots and Cavalry, gave him overall command of Jing, Yang, and Yi, promoted him to Marquis of Chen, and added 2,000 households to his fief for a total of 3,500.

manualTranslations.zh: 追賜仁父炽諡曰陳穆侯，置守冢十家。
manualTranslations.literal: He posthumously bestowed on Ren's father Chi the posthumous title Marquis Mu of Chen and established ten households to guard the tomb.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He canonized Ren's father Cao Chi as Marquis Mu of Chen and assigned ten families to tend the tomb.

manualTranslations.zh: 後召還屯宛。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was summoned back to encamp at Wan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to garrison Wan.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權遣將陳邵据襄陽，詔仁討之。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan sent General Chen Shao to hold Xiangyang; an edict ordered Ren to punish him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan detached Chen Shao to seize Xiangyang, and an edict sent Cao Ren against him.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁與徐晃攻破邵，遂入襄陽，使將軍高遷等徙漢南附化民於漢北，文帝遣使即拜仁大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Ren together with Xu Huang broke Shao, then entered Xiangyang, had General Gao Qian and others move the people who had submitted in the south of the Han to the north of the Han; Emperor Wen sent envoys and immediately appointed Ren grand general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Ren and Xu Huang routed Chen Shao, recovered Xiangyang, resettled submitted peoples from south of the Han to the north, and Emperor Wen's envoys promptly named Ren grand general.

manualTranslations.zh: 又詔仁移屯临潁，遷大司馬，復督諸軍据烏江，還屯合肥。
manualTranslations.literal: Again an edict ordered Ren to move encampment to Linying, transferred him to Grand Marshal, again supervised the armies in holding Wujiang, and returned to encamp at Hefei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Linying, promoted to Grand Marshal, again given overall command to hold the line at Wujiang, and finally garrisoned Hefei.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初四年薨，諡曰忠侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangchu he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Huangchu 4 and was canonized as Marquis Zhong (the Loyal).

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：仁時年五十六。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Ren was then fifty-six years old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei gives his age as fifty-six.

manualTranslations.zh: 《傅子》曰：曹大司馬之勇，賁、育弗加也。
manualTranslations.literal: Master Fu says: Cao the Grand Marshal's courage—Ben and Yu could not surpass it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Master Fu wrote that Grand Marshal Cao's valor exceeded even the legendary strongmen Ben and Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 張辽其次焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Liao was next to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao ranked second.

manualTranslations.zh: 子泰嗣，官至鎮東將軍，假節，轉封甯陵侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Tai succeeded, reached the post of General Who Guards the East, was given credentials of office, and was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Tai inherited, rose to General Who Guards the East with baton of command, and was shifted to Marquis of Ningling.

manualTranslations.zh: 泰薨，子初嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Tai died; his son Chu succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Tai died his son Chu inherited.

manualTranslations.zh: 又分封泰弟楷、範，皆爲列侯，而牛金官至後將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Again Tai's younger brothers Kai and Fan were separately enfeoffed, both becoming ranked marquises, while Niu Jin reached the post of General of the Rear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tai's brothers Kai and Fan were also enfeoffed as marquises, and Niu Jin rose to General of the Rear.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁弟純，《英雄記》曰：純字子和。
manualTranslations.literal: Ren's younger brother Chun—the Records of Heroes says: Chun, courtesy name Zihe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Ren's younger brother Chun—the Records of Heroes gives his style as Zihe.

sourceRange.text: 曹洪字子廉，太祖從弟也。《魏書》曰：洪伯父鼎爲尚書令，任洪爲蕲春長。太祖起義兵討董卓，至荥陽，爲卓將徐榮所敗。太祖失馬，賊追甚急，洪下，以馬授太祖，太祖辞讓，洪曰：「天下可無洪，不可無君。」遂步從到汴水，水深不得渡，洪循水得船，與太祖俱濟，還奔譙。揚州刺史陳温素與洪善，洪將家兵千餘人，就温募兵，得廬江上甲二千人，東到丹楊復得數千人，與太祖會龍亢。太祖征徐州，張邈舉兖州叛迎吕布。時大饑荒，洪將兵在前，先据東平、範，聚糧穀以繼軍。太祖討邈、布於濮陽，布破走，遂据東阿，轉擊濟陰、山陽、中牟、陽武、京、密十餘縣，皆拔之。以前後功拜鹰揚校尉，遷揚武中郎將。天子都许，拜洪諫議大夫。别征劉表，破表别將於舞陽、陰葉、堵陽、博望，有功，遷厉鋒將軍，封國明亭侯。累從征伐，拜都護將軍。文帝即位，爲衛將軍，遷骠騎將軍，進封野王侯，益邑千户，并前二千一百户，位特進；後徙封都陽侯。始，洪家富而性吝啬，文帝少時假求不稱，常恨之，遂以舍客犯法，下狱當死。羣臣并救莫能得。卞太后謂郭后曰：「令曹洪今日死，吾明日敕帝废后矣。」於是泣涕屡請，乃得免官削爵土。《魏略》曰：文帝收洪，時曹真在左右，請之曰：「今誅洪，洪必以真爲譖也。」帝曰：「我自治之，卿何豫也？」會卞太后責怒帝，言「梁、沛之間，非子廉無有今日」。詔乃釋之。猶尚沒入其財產。太后又以爲言，後乃還之。初，太祖爲司空時，以己率下，每歲发调，使本縣平赀。於時譙令平洪赀財與公家等，太祖曰：「我家赀那得如子廉耶！」文帝在東宫，尝從洪贷绢百匹，洪不稱意。及洪犯法，自分必死，既得原，喜，上書谢曰：「臣少不由道，过在人伦，長窃非任，遂蒙含贷。性無检度知足之分，而有豺狼無厌之質，老惛倍贪，触突國网，罪迫三千，不在赦宥，當就辜誅，棄諸市朝，猶蒙天恩，骨肉更生。臣仰视天日，愧負靈神，俯惟愆阙，惭愧怖悸，不能雉經以自裁割，谨涂颜阙門，拜章陳情。」洪先帝功臣，時人多爲觖望。明帝即位，拜後將軍，更封樂城侯，邑千户，位特進，復拜骠騎將軍。太和六年232年薨，諡曰恭侯。子馥，嗣侯。初，太祖分洪户封子震列侯。洪族父瑜，脩慎笃敬，官至衛將軍，封列侯。曹休字文烈，太祖族子也。天下亂，宗族各散去鄉里。休年十餘歲，喪父，獨與一客担喪假葬，携將老母，渡江至吴。《魏書》曰：休祖父尝爲吴郡太守。休於太守舍，見壁上祖父画像，下榻拜涕泣，同坐者皆嘉叹焉。以太祖舉義兵，易姓名轉至荆州，間行北歸，見太祖。太祖謂左右曰：「此吾家千里驹也。」使與文帝同止，見待如子。常從征伐，使領虎豹騎宿衛。劉備遣將吴兰屯下辯，太祖遣曹洪征之，以休爲騎都尉，参洪軍事。太祖謂休曰：「汝雖参軍，其實帥也。」洪聞此令，亦委事於休。備遣張飛屯固山，欲斷軍後。眾議狐疑，休曰：「賊實斷道者，當伏兵潜行。今乃先張声勢，此其不能也。宜及其未集，促擊兰，兰破則飛自走矣。」洪從之，進兵擊兰，大破之，飛果走。太祖拔漢中，諸軍還長安，拜休中領軍。文帝即王位，爲領軍將軍，錄前後功，封東陽亭侯。夏侯惇薨，以休爲鎮南將軍，假節都督諸軍事，车驾临送，上乃下舆執手而别。孫權遣將屯歷陽，休到，擊破之，又别遣兵渡江，燒賊芜湖營數千家。遷征東將軍，領揚州刺史，進封安陽鄉侯。《魏書》曰：休喪母至孝。帝使侍中夺喪服，使饮酒食肉，休受詔而形体益憔悴。乞歸譙葬母，帝復遣越騎校尉薛乔奉詔節其憂哀，使歸家治喪，一宿便葬，葬讫詣行在所。帝見，親自宽慰之。其見愛重如此。帝征孫權，以休爲征東大將軍，假黄钺，督張辽等及諸州郡二十餘軍，擊權大將吕範等於洞浦，破之。拜揚州牧。明帝即位，進封長平侯。吴將审德屯皖，休擊破之，斬德首，吴將韓綜、翟丹等前後率眾詣休降。增邑四百，并前二千五百户，遷大司馬，都督揚州如故。太和二年228年，帝爲二道征吴，遣司馬宣王從漢水下，〔休督〕諸軍向尋陽。賊將僞降，休深入，戰不利，退還宿石亭。軍夜惊，士卒亂，棄甲兵輜重甚多。休上書谢罪，帝遣屯騎校尉楊暨慰谕，禮賜益隆。休因此痈发背薨，諡曰壯侯。子肇嗣。《世語》曰：肇字長思。肇有當世才度，爲散騎常侍、屯騎校尉。明帝寝疾，方與燕王宇等屬以後事。帝意尋变，詔肇以侯歸第。正始中薨。追赠衛將軍。子興嗣。初，文帝分休户三百封肇弟纂爲列侯，後爲殄吴將軍，薨，追赠前將軍。張隐《文士傳》曰：肇孫摅，字颜遠，少厉志操，博學有才藻。仕晉，辟公府，歷洛陽令，有能名。大司馬齊王冏辅政，摅與齊人左思俱爲记室督。從中郎出爲襄陽太守、征南司馬。值天下亂，摅討賊向吴，戰敗死。曹真字子丹，太祖族子也。太祖起兵，真父邵募徒眾，爲州郡所殺。《魏略》曰：真本姓秦，養曹氏。或云其父伯南夙與太祖善。興平末，袁术部党與太祖攻劫，太祖出，爲寇所追，走入秦氏，伯南开門受之。寇問太祖所在，答云：「我是也。」遂害之。由此太祖思其功，故变其姓。《魏書》曰：邵以忠笃有才智，爲太祖所親信。初平中，太祖興義兵，邵募徒眾，從太祖周旋。時豫州刺史黄琬欲害太祖，太祖避之而邵獨遇害。太祖哀真少孤，收養與諸子同，使與文帝共止。常猎，爲虎所逐，顧射虎，應声而倒。太祖壯其鸷勇，使將虎豹騎。討靈丘賊，拔之，封靈壽亭侯。以偏將軍將兵擊劉備别將於下辯，破之，拜中堅將軍。從至長安，領中領軍。是時，夏侯淵沒於陽平，太祖憂之。以真爲征蜀護軍，督徐晃等破劉備别將高详於陽平。太祖自至漢中，拔出諸軍，使真至武都迎曹洪等還屯陳倉。文帝即王位，以真爲鎮西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。錄前後功，進封東鄉侯。張進等反於酒泉，真遣费曜討破之，斬進等。黃初三年還京都，以真爲上軍大將軍，都督中外諸軍事，假節钺。與夏侯尚等征孫權，擊牛渚屯，破之。轉拜中軍大將軍，加給事中。七年，文帝寝疾，真與陳羣、司馬宣王等受遺詔辅政。明帝即位，進封邵陵侯，臣松之案：真父名邵。封邵陵侯，若非書误，則事不可論。遷大將軍。
