manualTranslations.zh: 曹洪字子廉，太祖從弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Hong, courtesy name Zikang, was a younger cousin of the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Hong, styled Zikang, was a younger cousin of Cao Cao on his father's side.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：洪伯父鼎爲尚書令，任洪爲蕲春長。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Hong's paternal uncle Ding was director of the masters of writing and appointed Hong magistrate of Qichun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shu states that Hong's uncle Ding served as director of the masters of writing and secured him the post of Qichun magistrate.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖起義兵討董卓，至荥陽，爲卓將徐榮所敗。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor raised righteous troops to punish Dong Zhuo, he reached Xingyang and was defeated by Zhuo's general Xu Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Dong Zhuo, he was routed at Xingyang by Dong Zhuo's general Xu Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖失馬，賊追甚急，洪下，以馬授太祖，太祖辞讓，洪曰：「天下可無洪，不可無君。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor lost his horse; the enemy pressed close in pursuit. Hong dismounted and offered his horse to the Grand Progenitor. The Grand Progenitor declined, and Hong said, "The realm can do without Hong; it cannot do without my lord."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao lost his mount with pursuers closing in. Hong leapt down and thrust the reins into his cousin's hand. Cao Cao refused; Hong insisted, "The world can spare me—it cannot spare you."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂步從到汴水，水深不得渡，洪循水得船，與太祖俱濟，還奔譙。
manualTranslations.literal: They then went on foot after him to the Bian River. The water was deep and could not be crossed. Hong followed the bank until he found a boat, crossed together with the Grand Progenitor, and fled back to Qiao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They pressed on foot to the Bian River, where the flood was too deep to ford. Hong scouted the bank, found a boat, ferried Cao Cao across, and they raced back to Qiao.

manualTranslations.zh: 揚州刺史陳温素與洪善，洪將家兵千餘人，就温募兵，得廬江上甲二千人，東到丹楊復得數千人，與太祖會龍亢。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen Wen, inspector of Yang province, had long been on good terms with Hong. Hong led more than a thousand household troops, went to Wen to raise soldiers, obtained two thousand first-rate troops from Lujiang, and when he went east to Danyang obtained several thousand more, then joined the Grand Progenitor at Longkang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Inspector Chen Wen of Yang province was an old friend. Hong marched with a thousand-odd household retainers, raised two thousand crack troops from Lujiang through Wen, gathered thousands more in Danyang, and rejoined Cao Cao at Longkang.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖征徐州，張邈舉兖州叛迎吕布。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Xu province, Zhang Miao raised Yan province in rebellion and welcomed Lü Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Cao Cao's campaign against Xu province, Zhang Miao turned Yan province over to Lü Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 時大饑荒，洪將兵在前，先据東平、範，聚糧穀以繼軍。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time there was great famine. Hong led troops in the van, first seized Dongping and Fan, and gathered grain to supply the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the land. Hong pushed ahead, seized Dongping and Fan, and stockpiled grain to keep the host fed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖討邈、布於濮陽，布破走，遂据東阿，轉擊濟陰、山陽、中牟、陽武、京、密十餘縣，皆拔之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor attacked Miao and Bu at Puyang, Bu was broken and fled. Hong then seized Dong'e, turned to strike Jiyin, Shanyang, Zhongmou, Yangwu, Jing, Mi, and more than ten counties, and took them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Puyang Cao Cao shattered Lü Bu's force; Hong then held Dong'e and swept more than ten counties—Jiyin, Shanyang, Zhongmou, Yangwu, Jing, Mi, and others—clearing them one by one.

manualTranslations.zh: 以前後功拜鹰揚校尉，遷揚武中郎將。
manualTranslations.literal: For his successive merits he was appointed colonel who soars and strikes, then promoted to martial might general of the household guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For these services he was made colonel of the soaring hawk, then promoted to martial might general of the household guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子都许，拜洪諫議大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Son of Heaven made his capital at Xu, Hong was appointed remonstrating and consulting grandee.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the emperor moved the court to Xu, Hong received the post of remonstrating and consulting grandee.

manualTranslations.zh: 别征劉表，破表别將於舞陽、陰葉、堵陽、博望，有功，遷厉鋒將軍，封國明亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: On a separate campaign against Liu Biao he defeated Biao's detached generals at Wuyang, Yinye, Duyang, and Bowang. For his merit he was promoted to general who displays the keen edge and enfeoffed as village marquis of Guoming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On detached service against Liu Biao he crushed Biao's lieutenants at Wuyang, Yinye, Duyang, and Bowang, won promotion to general of the keen edge, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Guoming.

manualTranslations.zh: 累從征伐，拜都護將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He repeatedly followed on campaigns and was appointed chief protector general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Campaign after campaign he followed the colors, until he was named chief protector general.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝即位，爲衛將軍，遷骠騎將軍，進封野王侯，益邑千户，并前二千一百户，位特進；
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Hong became general of the guards, was transferred to general of swift cavalry, advanced in fief to marquis of Yewang, had his fief increased by a thousand households to a total of twenty-one hundred with the previous holdings, and was given the eminent position of special advancement;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen made him general of the guards, then general of swift cavalry, advanced his fief to marquis of Yewang with a thousand added households for twenty-one hundred in all, and granted him the eminent rank of special advancement;

manualTranslations.zh: 後徙封都陽侯。
manualTranslations.literal: later his fief was moved to marquis of Duyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: later his fief was transferred to marquis of Duyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 始，洪家富而性吝啬，文帝少時假求不稱，常恨之，遂以舍客犯法，下狱當死。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning Hong's family was wealthy yet his nature was stingy. When Emperor Wen was young he borrowed from him and was not satisfied, and he often resented this. Thereupon on the charge that a retainer had violated the law he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong had been rich and notoriously tight-fisted. The young Cao Pi had borrowed from him and been refused; the grudge lingered. When a guest of Hong's broke the law, Pi seized the chance to have him jailed and condemned to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 羣臣并救莫能得。
manualTranslations.literal: The ministers all pleaded together but could not save him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The whole court interceded, yet none could move the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 卞太后謂郭后曰：「令曹洪今日死，吾明日敕帝废后矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian said to Empress Guo, "If Cao Hong dies today, tomorrow I shall order the emperor to depose you as empress."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian told Empress Guo, "Let Cao Hong die today, and tomorrow I shall command the emperor to depose you."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是泣涕屡請，乃得免官削爵土。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon with tears she repeatedly pleaded, and he was spared execution but stripped of office and fief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She wept and pleaded again and again until Hong was spared the blade but stripped of rank and fief.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：文帝收洪，時曹真在左右，請之曰：「今誅洪，洪必以真爲譖也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei states: When Emperor Wen seized Hong, Cao Zhen was at his side and pleaded for him, saying, "If Hong is executed now, Hong will surely think that Zhen slandered him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe records that when Emperor Wen arrested Hong, Cao Zhen stood at his side and warned, "Execute Hong now, and he will believe I denounced him."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝曰：「我自治之，卿何豫也？」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor said, "I shall handle this myself—what business is it of yours?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "I will judge this myself—what is that to you?"

manualTranslations.zh: 會卞太后責怒帝，言「梁、沛之間，非子廉無有今日」。
manualTranslations.literal: Just then Empress Dowager Bian rebuked the emperor in anger, saying, "Between Liang and Pei, but for Zikang there would be no today."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian then rebuked the emperor: "Between Liang and Pei, without Zikang there would be no you on the throne today."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔乃釋之。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict thereupon released him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict at last set him free.

manualTranslations.zh: 猶尚沒入其財產。
manualTranslations.literal: His property was nevertheless confiscated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even so his estates were seized.

manualTranslations.zh: 太后又以爲言，後乃還之。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress dowager spoke again on his behalf, and afterward they were returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The empress dowager spoke again, and in time his property was restored.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，太祖爲司空時，以己率下，每歲发调，使本縣平赀。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning, when the Grand Progenitor was minister of works, he led subordinates by his own example; each year when levies were issued he had the native county assess property equally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Cao Cao's days as minister of works he set the tone from the top: each year's levy was assessed by the home county on an equal-property basis.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時譙令平洪赀財與公家等，太祖曰：「我家赀那得如子廉耶！」
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Qiao assessed Hong's property as equal to the public household's, and the Grand Progenitor said, "How could my family's wealth match Zikang's!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Qiao rated Hong's wealth equal to the state's own holdings, and Cao Cao laughed, "How could our household ever equal Zikang's!"

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝在東宫，尝從洪贷绢百匹，洪不稱意。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen was in the eastern palace he once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong and was not satisfied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Cao Pi once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong and found the gift wanting.

manualTranslations.zh: 及洪犯法，自分必死，既得原，喜，上書谢曰：「臣少不由道，过在人伦，長窃非任，遂蒙含贷。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hong violated the law he reckoned he would surely die. Once pardoned he rejoiced and submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your servant in youth did not follow the Way; faults lay in human relations. For long I usurped an unfitting post and then received gracious pardon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Hong fell afoul of the law he was sure he would die. Spared, he submitted a grateful memorial: "In youth I strayed from the Way and failed in my duties. Long I held office I did not deserve, yet was shown mercy.

manualTranslations.zh: 性無检度知足之分，而有豺狼無厌之質，老惛倍贪，触突國网，罪迫三千，不在赦宥，當就辜誅，棄諸市朝，猶蒙天恩，骨肉更生。
manualTranslations.literal: My nature lacks the sense of restraint and contentment, yet has the quality of a wolf that knows no satiety. In old age I am doubly muddled and greedy, and I have struck against the laws of the state. My offenses approach three thousand and lie outside amnesty; I ought to suffer execution and be cast out in the marketplace. Yet I still receive Heaven's grace, and flesh and bone are reborn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I never knew moderation, only the hunger of a wolf. Age made me greedier still, and I crashed into the law. My crimes approach three thousand counts and lie beyond pardon; I should die at the execution ground. Yet Heaven spared me, and bone and flesh live again.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣仰视天日，愧負靈神，俯惟愆阙，惭愧怖悸，不能雉經以自裁割，谨涂颜阙門，拜章陳情。」
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant looks up at sun and sky and bears shame before the numinous spirits; looking down on my faults I am ashamed, fearful, and trembling. I cannot hang myself to cut off my own life, and so with face smeared in disgrace I come to your gate and bow in memorial to state my feelings."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I lift my eyes to sun and sky and shame the spirits; looking on my faults I am afraid and ashamed. I cannot take my own life by the cord, and so with smeared face I come to your gate and bow this memorial."

manualTranslations.zh: 洪先帝功臣，時人多爲觖望。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong was a meritorious minister of the former emperor, and at the time many were discontented on his account.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong had been a pillar of the founding reign, and many at court resented his treatment.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，拜後將軍，更封樂城侯，邑千户，位特進，復拜骠騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Hong was appointed general of the rear, had his fief changed to marquis of Lecheng with a thousand households, was given the position of special advancement, and was again appointed general of swift cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming restored him as general of the rear, refiefed him as marquis of Lecheng with a thousand households, granted special advancement, and again named him general of swift cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和六年232年薨，諡曰恭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe (232) he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 6 (232) and was posthumously titled Marquis Gong.

manualTranslations.zh: 子馥，嗣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Fu succeeded to the marquisate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Fu inherited the marquisate.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，太祖分洪户封子震列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning the Grand Progenitor divided households from Hong's fief and enfeoffed his son Zhen as a full marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Cao Cao had carved households from Hong's fief to enfeoff his son Zhen as a full marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 洪族父瑜，脩慎笃敬，官至衛將軍，封列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong's clansman-uncle Yu was cautious, respectful, and sincere in conduct, rose to general of the guards, and was enfeoffed as a full marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong's kinsman Yu was grave and dutiful, rose to general of the guards, and held a full marquisate.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹休字文烈，太祖族子也。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Xiu, courtesy name Wenlie, was a clansman son of the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu, styled Wenlie, was a clansman of Cao Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 天下亂，宗族各散去鄉里。
manualTranslations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos the clans all scattered to their home districts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed, the clan scattered to their native places.

manualTranslations.zh: 休年十餘歲，喪父，獨與一客担喪假葬，携將老母，渡江至吴。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu was just over ten when his father died. Alone with one guest he shouldered the coffin for a provisional burial, then took his aged mother and crossed the river to Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiu was barely into his teens when his father died. With a single companion he shouldered the coffin for a makeshift burial, then crossed the Yangzi with his mother to Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：休祖父尝爲吴郡太守。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Xiu's grandfather had once been grand administrator of Wu commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shu states that Xiu's grandfather had once governed Wu commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 休於太守舍，見壁上祖父画像，下榻拜涕泣，同坐者皆嘉叹焉。
manualTranslations.literal: At the grand administrator's residence Xiu saw his grandfather's portrait on the wall, came down from the couch, bowed, and wept; those seated with him all praised and sighed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the governor's hall he saw his grandfather's portrait on the wall, rose from his seat, bowed, and wept until all present sighed in admiration.

manualTranslations.zh: 以太祖舉義兵，易姓名轉至荆州，間行北歸，見太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the Grand Progenitor had raised righteous troops, he changed his name and made his way to Jing province, traveled secretly north, and saw the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao raised his banner, Xiu changed his name, slipped through Jing province, and made his way north in secret to join him.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖謂左右曰：「此吾家千里驹也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to those at his side, "This is a thousand-league colt of our house."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told his attendants, "Here is a thousand-league colt of our clan."

manualTranslations.zh: 使與文帝同止，見待如子。
manualTranslations.literal: He had him lodge with Emperor Wen and treated him like a son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He lodged him with the heir apparent and treated him as a son.

manualTranslations.zh: 常從征伐，使領虎豹騎宿衛。
manualTranslations.literal: He often followed on campaigns and was made to lead the tiger-and-leopard cavalry as palace guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rode on campaign after campaign and was set to command the tiger-and-leopard cavalry as palace guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 劉備遣將吴兰屯下辯，太祖遣曹洪征之，以休爲騎都尉，参洪軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: Liu Bei sent the general Wu Lan to encamp at Xiabian. The Grand Progenitor sent Cao Hong to campaign against him and made Xiu colonel of cavalry to take part in Hong's military affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei posted Wu Lan at Xiabian, Cao Cao sent Cao Hong against him and attached Xiu as colonel of cavalry on Hong's staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖謂休曰：「汝雖参軍，其實帥也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor told Xiu, "Though you are staff officer, in truth you are commander."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told Xiu, "You hold the title of staff officer, but in truth you are the commander."

manualTranslations.zh: 洪聞此令，亦委事於休。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hong heard this order he also entrusted affairs to Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing that, Hong handed the real command to Xiu.

manualTranslations.zh: 備遣張飛屯固山，欲斷軍後。
manualTranslations.literal: Bei sent Zhang Fei to encamp at Gushan, intending to cut off the army's rear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei to Gushan, aiming to sever the army's line of retreat.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾議狐疑，休曰：「賊實斷道者，當伏兵潜行。
manualTranslations.literal: In council many were doubtful. Xiu said, "If the enemy truly meant to cut the road they would have lain in ambush and moved in secret.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The staff wavered. Xiu said, "Men who mean to cut a road move in ambush and silence.

manualTranslations.zh: 今乃先張声勢，此其不能也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now they have first made a great show of force—this shows they cannot do it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They have blared their intentions first—they cannot do it.

manualTranslations.zh: 宜及其未集，促擊兰，兰破則飛自走矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: We ought to strike Lan before they gather, and when Lan is broken Fei will flee of himself."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Strike Lan before they mass; once Lan falls, Fei will run on his own."

manualTranslations.zh: 洪從之，進兵擊兰，大破之，飛果走。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong followed this plan, advanced and struck Lan, and broke him greatly; Fei indeed fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong agreed, attacked Lan, and routed him; Zhang Fei fled as predicted.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖拔漢中，諸軍還長安，拜休中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took Hanzhong the various armies returned to Chang'an, and Xiu was appointed central leader of the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Hanzhong fell and the armies withdrew to Chang'an, Xiu was named central leader of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝即王位，爲領軍將軍，錄前後功，封東陽亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingship, Xiu became general of the leader of the army, his earlier and later merits were recorded, and he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the kingship, Xiu became general of the leader of the army, his services were entered on the rolls, and he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏侯惇薨，以休爲鎮南將軍，假節都督諸軍事，车驾临送，上乃下舆執手而别。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiahou Dun died, Xiu was made general who guards the south, given the credential and made supervisor of all military affairs. The imperial carriage came to see him off; the emperor descended from the carriage, took his hand, and parted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Xiahou Dun's death Xiu was made general who guards the south with credential and overall command. The emperor came in person to send him off, stepped down from the carriage, took his hand, and bade farewell.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫權遣將屯歷陽，休到，擊破之，又别遣兵渡江，燒賊芜湖營數千家。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan sent a general to encamp at Liyang. When Xiu arrived he defeated him, and separately sent troops across the river to burn several thousand households in the enemy camp at Wuhu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan posted a force at Liyang; Xiu broke it, then sent troops across the river to burn thousands of enemy shelters at Wuhu.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷征東將軍，領揚州刺史，進封安陽鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to general who campaigns east, concurrently inspector of Yang province, and advanced in fief to village marquis of Anyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns east and inspector of Yang province, and advanced to village marquis of Anyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：休喪母至孝。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei states: In mourning for his mother Xiu was supremely filial.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says that in mourning his mother Xiu showed supreme filial devotion.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝使侍中夺喪服，使饮酒食肉，休受詔而形体益憔悴。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor sent an attendant-in-ordinary to take away his mourning garments and had him drink wine and eat meat. Xiu received the edict yet his body grew ever more wasted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an attendant to strip his mourning garb and ordered wine and meat; Xiu obeyed, yet wasted away.

manualTranslations.zh: 乞歸譙葬母，帝復遣越騎校尉薛乔奉詔節其憂哀，使歸家治喪，一宿便葬，葬讫詣行在所。
manualTranslations.literal: He begged to return to Qiao to bury his mother. The emperor again sent Colonel of the Rapid Guard Xue Qiao with an edict to moderate his grief, let him return home to conduct the funeral, buried her after one night's rest, and when the burial was finished went to the emperor's traveling residence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He begged leave to bury his mother at Qiao. The emperor sent Colonel Xue Qiao to temper his grief, let him go home, buried her after a single night, and when the rites were done Xiu presented himself at the traveling palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝見，親自宽慰之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor saw him he personally comforted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and comforted him in person.

manualTranslations.zh: 其見愛重如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Such was the regard in which he was held.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he commanded.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝征孫權，以休爲征東大將軍，假黄钺，督張辽等及諸州郡二十餘軍，擊權大將吕範等於洞浦，破之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Sun Quan he made Xiu grand general who campaigns east, gave him the yellow battle-axe, and had him supervise Zhang Liao and more than twenty armies from the various provinces and commanderies. He struck Sun Quan's great general Lü Fan and others at Dongpu and defeated them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Sun Quan, the emperor named Xiu grand general who campaigns east, gave him the yellow battle-axe, and set him over Zhang Liao and more than twenty provincial hosts. At Dongpu he shattered Sun Quan's great general Lü Fan.

manualTranslations.zh: 拜揚州牧。
manualTranslations.literal: He was appointed governor of Yang province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Yang province.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，進封長平侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Xiu was advanced in fief to marquis of Changping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming advanced his fief to marquis of Changping.

manualTranslations.zh: 吴將审德屯皖，休擊破之，斬德首，吴將韓綜、翟丹等前後率眾詣休降。
manualTranslations.literal: Wu general Shen De encamped at Wan; Xiu defeated him and beheaded De. Wu generals Han Zong, Zhai Dan, and others before and after led their hosts to surrender to Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu general Shen De held Wan; Xiu defeated him and took his head. Wu generals Han Zong, Zhai Dan, and others came over to him in succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 增邑四百，并前二千五百户，遷大司馬，都督揚州如故。
manualTranslations.literal: His fief was increased by four hundred households to a total of twenty-five hundred with the previous holdings, and he was transferred to grand marshal while continuing to supervise Yang province as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Four hundred households were added to his fief for twenty-five hundred in all, and he was made grand marshal while retaining supervision of Yang province.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和二年228年，帝爲二道征吴，遣司馬宣王從漢水下，〔休督〕諸軍向尋陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Taihe (228) the emperor campaigned against Wu on two routes, sending Sima Yi down the Han River while [Xiu supervised] the various armies toward Xunyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 (228) the emperor opened a two-pronged campaign against Wu, sending Sima Yi down the Han while Xiu led the main host toward Xunyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊將僞降，休深入，戰不利，退還宿石亭。
manualTranslations.literal: An enemy general feigned surrender. Xiu advanced deep, the battle went badly, and he withdrew to lodge at Shiting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A Wu officer pretended to defect. Xiu pushed deep, met defeat, and fell back to Shiting.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍夜惊，士卒亂，棄甲兵輜重甚多。
manualTranslations.literal: That night the army was startled; the soldiers fell into disorder and abandoned armor, weapons, and baggage in great quantity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That night panic swept the camp; troops threw away armor, arms, and wagons in heaps.

manualTranslations.zh: 休上書谢罪，帝遣屯騎校尉楊暨慰谕，禮賜益隆。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault. The emperor sent Colonel of the Dappled Cavalry Yang Ji to console and instruct him, and his honors and gifts grew ever greater.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiu submitted a confession of fault. The emperor sent Colonel Yang Ji to console him and heaped fresh honors upon him.

manualTranslations.zh: 休因此痈发背薨，諡曰壯侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu thereupon died of a carbuncle on his back; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A carbuncle on his back killed him; he was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 子肇嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Zhao succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Zhao succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：肇字長思。
manualTranslations.literal: The Accounts of the Age states: Zhao's courtesy name was Changsi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu records that Zhao's courtesy name was Changsi.

manualTranslations.zh: 肇有當世才度，爲散騎常侍、屯騎校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao had the talent and measure of the age and served as attendant cavalier and colonel of the encampment cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhao had talent fit for his generation and served as attendant cavalier and colonel of the encampment cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝寝疾，方與燕王宇等屬以後事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming lay gravely ill he was on the point of entrusting the succession to the Prince of Yan, Yu, and others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Emperor Ming lay dying he was about to entrust the succession to the Prince of Yan, Yu, and others.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝意尋变，詔肇以侯歸第。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor's intent soon changed, and an edict sent Zhao home as a marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind soon shifted, and an edict sent Zhao home with his marquisate.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始中薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the Zhengshi era.

manualTranslations.zh: 追赠衛將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title general of the guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the title general of the guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 子興嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Xing succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Xing succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，文帝分休户三百封肇弟纂爲列侯，後爲殄吴將軍，薨，追赠前將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Wen divided three hundred households from Xiu's fief and enfeoffed Zhao's younger brother Zuan as a full marquis. Later he became general who exterminates Wu, died, and was posthumously granted the title former general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had carved three hundred households from Xiu's fief to enfeoff Zhao's brother Zuan as a full marquis. Zuan later became general who exterminates Wu; at his death he was posthumously named former general.

manualTranslations.zh: 張隐《文士傳》曰：肇孫摅，字颜遠，少厉志操，博學有才藻。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Yin's Account of Literary Men states: Zhao's grandson Shu, courtesy name Yanyuan, in youth set his will on integrity, was broadly learned and had literary talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin's Wenshi zhuan records that Zhao's grandson Shu, styled Yanyuan, was studious, principled, and accomplished in letters.

manualTranslations.zh: 仕晉，辟公府，歷洛陽令，有能名。
manualTranslations.literal: He served Jin, was summoned to the government offices, and successively served as magistrate of Luoyang with a reputation for ability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Jin he entered the bureaucracy, served as magistrate of Luoyang, and won a name for competence.

manualTranslations.zh: 大司馬齊王冏辅政，摅與齊人左思俱爲记室督。
manualTranslations.literal: When Grand Marshal Prince of Qi, Jiong, assisted in government, Shu together with Zuo Si of Qi both served as recorder supervisors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Sima Jiong of Qi held the regency, Shu and the Qi native Zuo Si both served as recorder supervisors.

manualTranslations.zh: 從中郎出爲襄陽太守、征南司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: From gentleman consultant he went out as grand administrator of Xiangyang and marshal of the army campaigning south.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He left office as gentleman consultant to become governor of Xiangyang and marshal of the army campaigning south.

manualTranslations.zh: 值天下亂，摅討賊向吴，戰敗死。
manualTranslations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos Shu campaigned against bandits toward Wu, was defeated in battle, and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the empire dissolved he marched against bandits toward Wu, was defeated, and fell in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹真字子丹，太祖族子也。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Zhen, courtesy name Zidan, was a clansman son of the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen, styled Zidan, was a clansman of Cao Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖起兵，真父邵募徒眾，爲州郡所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor raised troops, Zhen's father Shao recruited followers and was killed by the province and commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao first raised arms, Zhen's father Shao recruited followers and was killed by provincial authorities.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：真本姓秦，養曹氏。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei states: Zhen's original surname was Qin; he was adopted into the Cao clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says Zhen was born a Qin and raised into the Cao clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 或云其父伯南夙與太祖善。
manualTranslations.literal: Some say his father Bonan had long been on good terms with the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some say his father Bonan had been an old friend of Cao Cao's.

manualTranslations.zh: 興平末，袁术部党與太祖攻劫，太祖出，爲寇所追，走入秦氏，伯南开門受之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of the Xingping era, Yuan Shu's faction together with the Grand Progenitor raided and plundered. The Grand Progenitor went out and was pursued by bandits, ran into the Qin household, and Bonan opened the door to receive him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Xingping, partisans of Yuan Shu joined Cao Cao in a raid. Pursued by brigands, he fled into the Qin house; Bonan opened the door.

manualTranslations.zh: 寇問太祖所在，答云：「我是也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The bandits asked where the Grand Progenitor was, and he answered, "I am he."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Asked where Cao Cao was, Bonan answered, "I am he."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂害之。
manualTranslations.literal: They thereupon killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The brigands killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 由此太祖思其功，故变其姓。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of this the Grand Progenitor remembered his merit and therefore changed his surname.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao never forgot the sacrifice and had the boy take the Cao surname.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：邵以忠笃有才智，爲太祖所親信。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Shao was loyal, sincere, and possessed of wisdom and ability, and was trusted by the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shu says Shao was loyal, capable, and trusted by Cao Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 初平中，太祖興義兵，邵募徒眾，從太祖周旋。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Chuping era the Grand Progenitor raised righteous troops; Shao recruited followers and followed the Grand Progenitor in his movements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Chuping, when Cao Cao raised righteous troops, Shao recruited men and rode at his side.

manualTranslations.zh: 時豫州刺史黄琬欲害太祖，太祖避之而邵獨遇害。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Inspector Huang Wan of Yu province wished to harm the Grand Progenitor. The Grand Progenitor avoided it, but Shao alone met disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Inspector Huang Wan of Yu province plotted against Cao Cao. Cao Cao escaped; Shao alone was killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖哀真少孤，收養與諸子同，使與文帝共止。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor pitied Zhen for being orphaned young, took him in and raised him together with his own sons, and had him lodge with Emperor Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pitying the orphan, Cao Cao raised Zhen with his own sons and lodged him with the heir apparent.

manualTranslations.zh: 常猎，爲虎所逐，顧射虎，應声而倒。
manualTranslations.literal: Once while hunting he was chased by a tiger; he turned and shot the tiger, which fell at the sound.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once on the hunt a tiger chased him; he wheeled, shot, and the beast dropped at the crack of the bow.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖壯其鸷勇，使將虎豹騎。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor admired his fierce courage and had him command the tiger-and-leopard cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marveled at his nerve and set him over the tiger-and-leopard cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 討靈丘賊，拔之，封靈壽亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He campaigned against the bandits of Lingqiu, took it, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Lingshou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He reduced the bandits of Lingqiu, took the place, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Lingshou.

manualTranslations.zh: 以偏將軍將兵擊劉備别將於下辯，破之，拜中堅將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: As lieutenant general he led troops and struck Liu Bei's detached general at Xiabian, defeated him, and was appointed general of the resolute center.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As lieutenant general he smashed Liu Bei's detached commander at Xiabian and was made general of the resolute center.

manualTranslations.zh: 從至長安，領中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He followed to Chang'an and led the central army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Chang'an and led the central army.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，夏侯淵沒於陽平，太祖憂之。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Xiahou Yuan perished at Yangping, and the Grand Progenitor was troubled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Yuan fell at Yangping, Cao Cao was deeply troubled.

manualTranslations.zh: 以真爲征蜀護軍，督徐晃等破劉備别將高详於陽平。
manualTranslations.literal: He made Zhen protector general campaigning against Shu, supervised Xu Huang and others, and defeated Liu Bei's detached general Gao Xiang at Yangping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He named Zhen protector general campaigning against Shu, set Xu Huang under him, and broke Liu Bei's lieutenant Gao Xiang at Yangping.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖自至漢中，拔出諸軍，使真至武都迎曹洪等還屯陳倉。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor himself reached Hanzhong he withdrew the various armies and sent Zhen to Wudu to meet Cao Hong and the others and return to encamp at Chencang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao reached Hanzhong himself he pulled the armies back and sent Zhen to Wudu to meet Cao Hong and bring the columns home to Chencang.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝即王位，以真爲鎮西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingship he made Zhen general who guards the west, gave him the credential, and made him supervisor of the military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Cao Pi's accession as king, Zhen became general who guards the west with credential and command over Yong and Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 錄前後功，進封東鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His earlier and later merits were recorded and he was advanced in fief to marquis of Dongxiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His services were entered on the rolls and his fief advanced to marquis of Dongxiang.

manualTranslations.zh: 張進等反於酒泉，真遣费曜討破之，斬進等。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Jin and others rebelled at Jiuquan; Zhen sent Fei Yao to campaign against and defeat them and beheaded Jin and the others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin rebelled at Jiuquan; Zhen sent Fei Yao to crush the revolt and beheaded Jin and his fellows.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初三年還京都，以真爲上軍大將軍，都督中外諸軍事，假節钺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu he returned to the capital and was made grand general of the upper army, supervisor of all military affairs within and without, with credential and battle-axe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he returned to the capital as grand general of the upper army, commander of all forces at court and in the field, with credential and battle-axe.

manualTranslations.zh: 與夏侯尚等征孫權，擊牛渚屯，破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with Xiahou Shang and others he campaigned against Sun Quan, struck the encampment at Niuzhu, and defeated it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Xiahou Shang he campaigned against Sun Quan, stormed Niuzhu, and broke the camp.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉拜中軍大將軍，加給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to grand general of the central army and added as palace attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand general of the central army and added as palace attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年，文帝寝疾，真與陳羣、司馬宣王等受遺詔辅政。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year Emperor Wen lay gravely ill; Zhen together with Chen Qun, Sima Yi, and others received the deathbed edict to assist in government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as Emperor Wen lay dying, Zhen with Chen Qun, Sima Yi, and others received the deathbed charge to govern.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，進封邵陵侯，臣松之案：真父名邵。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Zhen was advanced in fief to marquis of Shaoling. Your subject Songzhi notes: Zhen's father's name was Shao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming advanced his fief to marquis of Shaoling. Your subject Songzhi notes: Zhen's father was named Shao.

manualTranslations.zh: 封邵陵侯，若非書误，則事不可論。
manualTranslations.literal: To enfeoff him as marquis of Shaoling—if this is not a scribal error, then the matter cannot be discussed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A fief named Shaoling for a man whose father was Shao—unless the text is corrupt, the honor is hard to explain.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to grand general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general.

sourceRange.text: 清河王經亦與允俱稱冀州名士。甘露中爲尚書，坐高貴鄉公事誅。始經爲郡守，經母謂經曰：「汝田家子，今仕至二千石，物太過不祥，可以止矣。」經不能從，歷二州刺史，司隷校尉，終以致敗。《世語》曰：經字彥偉，初爲江夏太守。大將軍曹爽附絹二十匹令交市於吳，經不發書，棄官歸。母問歸狀，經以實對。母以經典兵馬而擅去，對送吏杖經五十，爽聞，不復罪。經爲司隷校尉，辟河內向雄爲都官從事，王業之出，不申經，竟以及難。經刑於東市，雄哭之，感動一市。刑及經母，雍州故吏皇甫晏以家財收葬焉。《漢晉春秋》曰：經被收，辭母。母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死？往所以不止汝者，恐不得其所也。以此并命，何恨之有哉？」晉武帝太始元年詔曰：「故尚書王經，雖身陷法辟，然守志可嘉。門戶堙沒，意常愍之，其賜經孫郎中。」允友人同郡崔贊，亦嘗以處世太盛戒允云。荀綽《冀州記》曰：贊子洪，字良伯，清恪有匪躬之志，爲晉吏部尚書、大司農。

context.beforeSource: 猛子式，字儀祖，有才幹，至濮陽內史、平原太守。
context.afterSource: 評曰：夏侯、曹氏，世爲婚姻，故惇、淵、仁、洪、休、尚、真等並以親舊肺腑，貴重於時，左右勳業，咸有効勞。

manualTranslations.zh: 清河王經亦與允俱稱冀州名士。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Jing of Qinghe was also with Yun together called famous gentlemen of Ji province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jing of Qinghe was ranked with Xu Yun among Ji province's celebrated gentlemen.

manualTranslations.zh: 甘露中爲尚書，坐高貴鄉公事誅。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Ganlu era he was secretary; he sat with the affair of the noble township and was executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Ganlu era he served as secretary and was executed in the noble township affair.

manualTranslations.zh: 始經爲郡守，經母謂經曰：「汝田家子，今仕至二千石，物太過不祥，可以止矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: At first when Jing was grand administrator, Jing's mother said to Jing: "You are a farmer's son; now in office reaching two thousand bushels—things too much exceeding is inauspicious; you can stop."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jing first became a commandery governor, his mother warned him: "You are a farmer's son risen to two thousand bushels—excess invites misfortune; stop while you can."

manualTranslations.zh: 經不能從，歷二州刺史，司隷校尉，終以致敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Jing could not follow; he successively served as inspector of two provinces and metropolitan commandant, and in the end thereby met ruin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing would not listen; he served two terms as provincial inspector and as metropolitan commandant, and was ruined.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：經字彥偉，初爲江夏太守。
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Jing's courtesy name was Yanwei; at first he was grand administrator of Jiangxia.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu names him Wang Jing, styled Yanwei; he first governed Jiangxia.

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍曹爽附絹二十匹令交市於吳，經不發書，棄官歸。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand general Cao Shuang attached twenty bolts of silk ordering trade in Wu; Jing did not issue the letter, abandoned office, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand General Cao Shuang sent twenty bolts of silk ordering trade with Wu; Jing refused the order, resigned, and went home.

manualTranslations.zh: 母問歸狀，經以實對。
manualTranslations.literal: His mother asked the circumstances of return; Jing answered with the facts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mother asked why he returned; he told the truth.

manualTranslations.zh: 母以經典兵馬而擅去，對送吏杖經五十，爽聞，不復罪。
manualTranslations.literal: His mother, because Jing commanded troops and horses yet left on his own authority, had the escort clerk beat Jing fifty blows; Shuang heard of it and did not again punish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mother, angry that he had abandoned command without leave, had the escort clerk beat him fifty strokes; Shuang heard and did not punish further.

manualTranslations.zh: 經爲司隷校尉，辟河內向雄爲都官從事，王業之出，不申經，竟以及難。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jing was metropolitan commandant, he recruited Xiang Xiong of Henei as director of capital cases; when Wang Ye went out, he did not report to Jing, and in the end thereby met disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As metropolitan commandant he recruited Xiang Xiong of Henei; when Wang Ye went out without reporting to Jing, disaster followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 經刑於東市，雄哭之，感動一市。
manualTranslations.literal: Jing was executed at the eastern market; Xiong wept for him and moved the whole market.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing was executed at the eastern market; Xiong wept until the whole market was moved.

manualTranslations.zh: 刑及經母，雍州故吏皇甫晏以家財收葬焉。
manualTranslations.literal: When the punishment reached Jing's mother, Huangfu Yan, a former clerk of Yong province, buried her at his household's expense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jing's mother was executed, former Yong clerk Huangfu Yan buried her at his own expense.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：經被收，辭母。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals states: When Jing was seized, he bade farewell to his mother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin chunqiu says Jing took leave of his mother when arrested.

manualTranslations.zh: 母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死？
manualTranslations.literal: His mother's color did not change; smiling she answered: "Who among men does not die?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her color never changed; smiling she answered, "Who does not die?

manualTranslations.zh: 往所以不止汝者，恐不得其所也。
manualTranslations.literal: The reason I before did not stop you was fear you would not obtain your place.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I did not stop you before lest you fail to meet your proper end.

manualTranslations.zh: 以此并命，何恨之有哉？」
manualTranslations.literal: To die together on this account—what regret is there?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To die together now—what regret could there be?"

manualTranslations.zh: 晉武帝太始元年詔曰：「故尚書王經，雖身陷法辟，然守志可嘉。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin's inaugural edict of the first year of Taishi said: "Former Secretary Wang Jing, though his person fell into law's punishment, yet his holding to purpose is praiseworthy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin's Taishi inaugural edict said: "Former Secretary Wang Jing, though punished by law, held firm purpose worth praise.

manualTranslations.zh: 門戶堙沒，意常愍之，其賜經孫郎中。」
manualTranslations.literal: His household gates were buried and extinguished; I constantly pitied it—grant Jing's grandson the post of gentleman of the palace gate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His house was destroyed; I have long pitied it—grant his grandson the post of gentleman of the palace gate."

manualTranslations.zh: 允友人同郡崔贊，亦嘗以處世太盛戒允云。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun's friend Cui Zan of the same commandery also once warned Yun that worldly standing was too full.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xu Yun's friend Cui Zan of the same commandery had also warned that worldly eminence was perilous.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀綽《冀州記》曰：贊子洪，字良伯，清恪有匪躬之志，爲晉吏部尚書、大司農。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Chuo's Record of Ji Province states: Zan's son Hong, courtesy name Liangbo, was pure and scrupulous with a will not to turn his person; he became director of the ministry of personnel and grand minister of agriculture of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Record of Ji Province says Zan's son Hong, styled Liangbo, was pure and scrupulous with unbending integrity, and became Jin's director of the ministry of personnel and grand minister of agriculture.

sourceRange.text: 初，張當私以所擇才人張、何等與爽。疑其有姦，收當治罪。當陳爽與晏等陰謀反逆，並先習兵，須三月中欲發，於是收晏等下獄。會公卿朝臣廷議，以爲「春秋之義，『君親無將，將而必誅』。爽以支屬，世蒙殊寵，親受先帝握手遺詔，託以天下，而包藏禍心，蔑棄顧命，乃與晏、颺及當等謀圖神器，範黨同罪人，皆爲大逆不道」。於是收爽、羲、訓、晏、颺、謐、軌、勝、範、當等，皆伏誅，夷三族。《魏略》曰：鄧颺字玄茂，鄧禹後也。少得士名於京師。明帝時爲尚書郎，除洛陽令，坐事免，拜中郎，又入兼中書郎。初，颺與李勝等爲浮華友，及在中書，浮華事發，被斥出，遂不復用。正始初，乃出爲潁川太守，轉大將軍長史，遷侍中尚書。颺爲人好貨，前在內職，許臧艾授以顯官，艾以父妾與颺，故京師爲之語曰：「以官易婦鄧玄茂。」每所薦達，多如此比。故何晏選舉不得人，頗由颺之不公忠，遂同其罪，蓋由交友非其才。《魏略》曰：丁謐，字彥靖。父斐，字文侯。初，斐隨太祖，太祖以斐鄉里，特饒愛之。斐性好貨，數請求犯法，輒得原宥。爲典軍校尉，總攝內外，每所陳說，多見從之。建安末，從太祖征吳。斐隨行，自以家牛羸困，乃私易官牛，爲人所白，被收送獄，奪官。其後太祖問斐曰：「文侯，印綬所在？」斐亦知見戲，對曰：「以易餅耳。」太祖笑，顧謂左右曰：「東曹毛掾數白此家，欲令我重治，我非不知此人不清，良有以也。我之有斐，譬如人家有盜狗而善捕鼠，盜雖有小損，而完我囊貯。」遂復斐官，聽用如初。後數歲，病亡。謐少不肯交游，但博觀書傳。爲人沈毅，頗有才略。太和中，常住鄴，借人空屋，居其中。而諸王亦欲借之，不知謐已得，直開門入。謐望見王，交脚臥而不起，而呼其奴客曰：「此何等人？促呵使去。」王怒其無禮，還具上言。明帝收謐，繫鄴獄，以其功臣子，原出。後帝聞其有父風，召拜度支郎中。曹爽宿與相親，時爽爲武衞將軍，數爲帝稱其可大用。會帝崩，爽輔政，乃拔謐爲散騎常侍，遂轉尚書。謐爲人外似踈略，而內多忌。其在臺閣，數有所彈駮，臺中患之，事不得行。又其意輕貴，多所忽略，雖與何晏、鄧颺等同位，而皆少之，唯以勢屈於爽。爽亦敬之，言無不從。故於時謗書，謂「臺中有三狗，二狗崖柴不可當，一狗憑默作疽囊。」三狗，謂何、鄧、丁也。默者，爽小字也。其意言三狗皆欲嚙人，而謐尤甚也。奏使郭太後出居別宮，及遣樂安王使北詣鄴，又遣文欽令還淮南，皆謐之計。司馬宣王由是特深恨之。畢軌，字昭先。父字子禮，建安中爲典農校尉。軌以才能，少有名聲。明帝在東宮時，軌在文學中。黃初末，出爲長史。明帝即位，入爲黃門郎，子尚公主，居處殷富。遷并州刺史。其在并州，名爲驕豪。時雜虜數爲暴，害吏民，軌輒出軍擊鮮卑軻比能，失利。中護軍蔣濟表曰：「畢軌前失，旣往不咎，但恐是後難可以再。凡人材有長短，不可彊成。軌文雅志意，自爲美器。今失并州，換置他州，若入居顯職，不毀其德，於國事實善。此安危之要，唯聖恩察之。」至正始中，入爲中護軍，轉侍中尚書，遷司隷校尉。素與曹爽善，每言於爽，多見從之。李勝字公昭。父休字子朗，有智略。張魯前爲鎮北將軍，休爲司馬，家南鄭。時漢中有甘露降，子朗見張魯精兵數萬人，有四塞之固，遂建言赤氣久衰，黃家當興，欲魯舉號，魯不聽。會魯破，太祖以其勸魯內附，賜爵關內侯，署散官騎從，詣鄴。至黃初中，仕歷上黨、鉅鹿二郡太守，後以年老還，拜議郎。勝少游京師，雅有才智，與曹爽善。明帝禁浮華，而人白勝堂有四䆫八達，各有主名。用是被收，以其所連引者多，故得原，禁錮數歲。帝崩，曹爽輔政，勝爲洛陽令。夏侯玄爲征西將軍，以勝爲長史。玄亦宿與勝厚。駱穀之役，議從勝出，由是司馬宣王不恱於勝。累遷熒陽太守、河南尹。勝前後所宰守，未嘗不稱職，爲尹歲餘，廳事前屠蘇壞，令人更治之，小材一枚激墮，正檛受符吏石虎頭，斷之。後旬日，遷爲荊州刺史，未及之官而敗也。桓範字元則，世爲冠族。建安末，入丞相府。延康中，爲羽林左監。以有文學，與王象等典集皇覽。明帝時爲中領軍尚書，遷征虜將軍、東中郎將，使持節都督青、徐諸軍事，治下邳。與徐州刺史鄭岐爭屋，引節欲斬岐，爲岐所奏，不直，坐免還。復爲兖州刺吏，怏怏不得意。又聞當轉爲冀州牧。是時冀州統屬鎮北，而鎮北將軍呂昭才實仕進，本在範後。範謂其妻仲長曰：「我寧作諸卿，向三公長跪耳，不能爲呂子展屈也。」其妻曰：「君前在東，坐欲擅斬徐州刺史，衆人謂君難爲作下，今復羞爲呂屈，是復難爲作上也。」範忿其言觸實，乃以刀環撞其腹。妻時懷孕，遂墮胎死。範亦竟稱疾，不赴冀州。正始中拜大司農。範前在臺閣，號爲曉事，及爲司農，又以清省稱。範嘗抄撮《漢書》中諸雜事，自以意斟酌之，名曰世要論。蔣濟爲太尉，嘗與範會社下，羣卿列坐有數人，範懷其所撰，欲以示濟，謂濟當虛心觀之。範出其書以示左右，左右傳之示濟，濟不肯視，範心恨之。因論他事，乃發怒謂濟曰：「我祖薄德，公輩何似邪？」濟性雖彊毅，亦知範剛毅，睨而不應，各罷。範於沛郡，仕次在曹真後。於時曹爽輔政，以範鄉里老宿，於九卿中特敬之，然不甚親也。及宣王起兵，閉城門，以範爲曉事，乃指召之，欲使領中領軍。範欲應召，而其子諫之，以車駕在外，不如南出。範疑有頃，兒又促之。範欲去而司農丞吏皆止範。範不從，乃突出至平昌城門，城門已閉。門候司蕃，故範舉吏也，範呼之，舉手中版以示之，矯曰：「有詔召我，卿促開門！」蕃欲求見詔書，範呵之，言「卿非我故吏邪，何以敢爾？」乃開之。範出城，顧謂蕃曰：「太傅圖逆，卿從我去！」蕃徒行不能及，遂避側。範南見爽，勸爽兄弟以天子詣許昌，徵四方以自輔。爽疑，羲又無言。範自謂羲曰：「事昭然，卿用讀書何爲邪！於今日卿等門戶倒矣！」俱不言。範又謂羲曰：「卿別營近在闕南，洛陽典農治在城外，呼召如意。今詣許昌，不過中宿，許昌別庫，足相被假；所憂當在穀食，而大司農印章在我身。」羲兄弟默然不從，中夜至五鼓，爽乃投刀於地，謂諸從駕羣臣曰：「我度太傅意，亦不過欲令我兄弟向己也。我獨有以不合於遠近耳！」遂進謂帝曰：「陛下作詔免臣官，報皇太後令。」範知爽首免而己必坐唱義也。範乃曰：「老子今茲坐卿兄弟族矣！」爽等旣免，帝還宮，遂令範隨從。到洛水浮橋北，望見宣王，下車叩頭而無言。宣王呼範姓曰：「桓大夫何爲爾邪！」車駕入宮，有詔範還復位。範詣闕拜章謝，待報。會司蕃詣鴻臚自首，具說範前臨出所道。宣王乃忿然曰：「誣人以反，於法何應？」主者曰：「科律，反受其罪。」乃收範於闕下。時人持範甚急，範謂部官曰：「徐之，我亦義士耳。」遂送廷尉。《世語》曰：初，爽夢二虎銜雷公，雷公若二升椀，放著庭中。爽惡之，以問占者，靈臺丞馬訓曰：「憂兵。」訓退，告其妻曰：「爽將以兵亡，不出旬日。」《漢晉春秋》曰：安定皇甫謐以九年冬夢至洛陽，自廟出，見車騎甚衆，以物呈廟云：「誅大將軍曹爽。」寤而以告其邑人，邑人曰：「君欲作曹人之夢乎！朝無公孫彊如何？且爽兄弟典重兵，又權尚書事，誰敢謀之？」謐曰：「爽無叔振鐸之請，苟失天機則離矣，何恃於彊？昔漢之閻顯，倚母後之尊，權國威命，可謂至重矣，閹人十九人一旦尸之，況爽兄弟乎？」《世語》曰：初，爽出，司馬魯芝留在府，聞有事，將營騎斫津門出赴爽。爽誅，擢爲御史中丞。及爽解印綬，將出，主簿楊綜止之曰：「公挾主握權，捨此以至東巿乎？」爽不從。有司奏綜導爽反，宣王曰：「各爲其主也。」宥之，以爲尚書郎。芝字世英，扶風人也。以後仕進至特進光祿大夫。綜字初伯，後爲安東將軍司馬文王長史。臣松之案：夏侯湛爲芝銘及干寶晉紀並云爽旣誅，宣王即擢芝爲并州刺史，以綜爲安東參軍。與《世語》不同。嘉平中，紹功臣世，封真族孫熙爲新昌亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉真後。干寶《晉紀》曰：蔣濟以曹真之勳力，不宜絕祀，故以熙爲後。濟又病其言之失信於爽，發病卒。

localRange.text: 鄧颺等
