manualTranslations.zh: 初，張當私以所擇才人張、何等與爽。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Zhang Dang privately gave to Shuang the talented women Zhang and He whom he had chosen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first Zhang Dang privately presented to Shuang the talented women Zhang and He whom he had selected.

manualTranslations.zh: 疑其有姦，收當治罪。
manualTranslations.literal: Suspecting he had improper relations, they seized Dang to punish his crime.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Suspecting impropriety, authorities arrested Zhang Dang for punishment.

manualTranslations.zh: 當陳爽與晏等陰謀反逆，並先習兵，須三月中欲發，於是收晏等下獄。
manualTranslations.literal: Dang stated that Shuang with Yan and others secretly plotted rebellion and treason, and all had beforehand practiced troops, intending to rise in the third month; thereupon Yan and others were seized and sent to prison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dang testified that Shuang, He Yan, and others had secretly plotted rebellion, trained troops, and planned to rise in the third month; Yan and the rest were jailed.

manualTranslations.zh: 會公卿朝臣廷議，以爲「春秋之義，『君親無將，將而必誅』。
manualTranslations.literal: The assembled dukes, ministers, and court officials deliberated in court, holding that "the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is, 'The ruler and parent allow no general; if there is a general, he must be executed.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court deliberated under Spring and Autumn principle: "Against ruler or parent, no armed defiance is permitted; defiance demands execution."

manualTranslations.zh: 爽以支屬，世蒙殊寵，親受先帝握手遺詔，託以天下，而包藏禍心，蔑棄顧命，乃與晏、颺及當等謀圖神器，範黨同罪人，皆爲大逆不道」。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang as a branch lineage through generations received extraordinary favor, personally received the late emperor's handclasp testamentary edict, entrusted with All under Heaven, yet harbored treacherous hearts, despised and cast aside the dying charge, and therefore with Yan, Yang, and Dang and others plotted the regalia; Fan's faction were fellow criminals—all were great rebellion without the Way."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang, a collateral kinsman long favored, had received the late emperor's handclasp charge to govern the realm, yet harbored treason, scorned that trust, and with Yan, Yang, Dang, and others sought the throne; Huan Fan's faction shared the crime—all were capital traitors."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是收爽、羲、訓、晏、颺、謐、軌、勝、範、當等，皆伏誅，夷三族。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, Fan, Dang, and others were all seized; all were executed and exterminated to the third degree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, Fan, Dang, and others were seized, executed, and exterminated to the third degree.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：鄧颺字玄茂，鄧禹後也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Deng Yang's courtesy name was Xuanmao; he was a descendant of Deng Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe names Deng Yang, courtesy name Xuanmao, a descendant of Deng Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 少得士名於京師。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he early won gentlemen's fame in the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He won scholarly fame in the capital while young.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝時爲尚書郎，除洛陽令，坐事免，拜中郎，又入兼中書郎。
manualTranslations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, appointed magistrate of Luoyang; because of an affair he was dismissed, appointed central gentleman, and again entered concurrently as gentleman of the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he served as a Masters of Writing gentleman, then Luoyang magistrate; dismissed for an offense, he became a central gentleman and later concurrent Secretariat gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，颺與李勝等爲浮華友，及在中書，浮華事發，被斥出，遂不復用。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Yang with Li Sheng and others were flashy friends; when he was in the Secretariat the flashy affair broke out, he was expelled and dismissed, and thereafter was not again employed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He and Li Sheng had been flashy companions; when the "flashy" scandal broke in the Secretariat he was expelled and never re-employed.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始初，乃出爲潁川太守，轉大將軍長史，遷侍中尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he then went out as grand administrator of Yingchuan, transferred grand general's chief clerk, and was promoted palace attendant and secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhengshi he became governor of Yingchuan, then the grand general's chief clerk, then palace attendant and secretary.

manualTranslations.zh: 颺爲人好貨，前在內職，許臧艾授以顯官，艾以父妾與颺，故京師爲之語曰：「以官易婦鄧玄茂。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yang as a man loved goods; formerly in inner office he promised Zang Ai an eminent office; Ai gave his father's concubine to Yang—therefore the capital made a saying for them: "Trade office for a wife—Deng Xuanmao."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang loved profit; while in inner office he promised Zang Ai a high post in exchange for Ai's father's concubine—hence the capital jingle: "Trade office for a wife—Deng Xuanmao."

manualTranslations.zh: 每所薦達，多如此比。
manualTranslations.literal: Each time he recommended and advanced men, mostly it was of this sort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Most of his promotions followed that pattern.

manualTranslations.zh: 故何晏選舉不得人，頗由颺之不公忠，遂同其罪，蓋由交友非其才。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore He Yan's selections did not obtain worthy men—largely because of Yang's lack of fairness and loyalty; he therefore shared their crime, probably from befriending men not of their talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Yan's appointments failed largely because Yang was unfair; Yang shared their guilt for choosing unworthy friends.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：丁謐，字彥靖。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Ding Mi, courtesy name Yanjing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe names Ding Mi, courtesy name Yanjing.

manualTranslations.zh: 父斐，字文侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Fei, courtesy name Wenhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Fei bore the courtesy name Wenhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，斐隨太祖，太祖以斐鄉里，特饒愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Fei followed the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor because Fei was of his home village especially indulged and loved him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fei had followed Cao Cao, who favored him as a townsman.

manualTranslations.zh: 斐性好貨，數請求犯法，輒得原宥。
manualTranslations.literal: Fei's nature loved goods; he repeatedly requested and committed offenses and always obtained pardon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fei loved profit, repeatedly offended, and was always pardoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 爲典軍校尉，總攝內外，每所陳說，多見從之。
manualTranslations.literal: He was colonel of the army of records, comprehensively controlling inner and outer affairs; each time he stated proposals, mostly they were followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As colonel of the army of records he controlled inner and outer affairs, and his proposals were usually followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安末，從太祖征吳。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of the Jian'an era he followed the Grand Progenitor campaigning against Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Jian'an he followed the campaign against Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 斐隨行，自以家牛羸困，乃私易官牛，爲人所白，被收送獄，奪官。
manualTranslations.literal: Fei followed on the march; thinking his household oxen were weak and weary, he privately exchanged official oxen; someone reported him, he was seized and sent to prison, and his office was stripped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On campaign he swapped his weak household oxen for official ones, was reported, jailed, and stripped of office.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後太祖問斐曰：「文侯，印綬所在？」
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward the Grand Progenitor asked Fei, saying: "Wenhou, where are the seals and ribbon?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao later asked, "Wenhou, where are your seals?"

manualTranslations.zh: 斐亦知見戲，對曰：「以易餅耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Fei also knew he was being teased and answered: "Exchanged for cakes, that's all."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing the jest, Fei answered, "Traded for cakes."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖笑，顧謂左右曰：「東曹毛掾數白此家，欲令我重治，我非不知此人不清，良有以也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor laughed, turned and said to his attendants: "Eastern Bureau Clerk Mao several times reported this family, wishing to have me punish heavily; I am not unaware this man is not clean—there is good reason for it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed and told attendants: "Clerk Mao of the Eastern Bureau keeps denouncing this man; I know he is crooked, yet I keep him.

manualTranslations.zh: 我之有斐，譬如人家有盜狗而善捕鼠，盜雖有小損，而完我囊貯。」
manualTranslations.literal: My having Fei is like a household having a thieving dog that is good at catching rats—the theft though has small loss, yet it completes my bags and stores."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fei is like a thieving dog that catches rats—the petty theft is worth the full granary."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂復斐官，聽用如初。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Fei's office was restored and he was heard and employed as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fei was restored to office.

manualTranslations.zh: 後數歲，病亡。
manualTranslations.literal: Several years later he died of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died of illness several years later.

manualTranslations.zh: 謐少不肯交游，但博觀書傳。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi in youth would not associate; he only broadly viewed books and records.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi in youth shunned company and read widely.

manualTranslations.zh: 爲人沈毅，頗有才略。
manualTranslations.literal: As a man he was deep and resolute, with considerable talent and stratagem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was deep, resolute, and strategically gifted.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和中，常住鄴，借人空屋，居其中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Taihe era he constantly dwelt at Ye, borrowed another's empty house, and lived within it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he lived at Ye in a borrowed empty house.

manualTranslations.zh: 而諸王亦欲借之，不知謐已得，直開門入。
manualTranslations.literal: The various princes also wished to borrow it, not knowing Mi had already obtained it, and went straight in opening the door.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Princes also wanted the house, unaware Mi had it, and walked straight in.

manualTranslations.zh: 謐望見王，交脚臥而不起，而呼其奴客曰：「此何等人？
manualTranslations.literal: Mi saw the prince, lay cross-legged and did not rise, and called his servant-guests, saying: "What sort of people are these?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi saw a prince, lay cross-legged without rising, and shouted to servants, "What sort are these?

manualTranslations.zh: 促呵使去。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hurry—shout and make them leave."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Drive them out!"

manualTranslations.zh: 王怒其無禮，還具上言。
manualTranslations.literal: The prince was angry at his lack of courtesy and on returning fully reported upward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The prince, furious at the insult, reported him.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝收謐，繫鄴獄，以其功臣子，原出。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ming seized Mi and imprisoned him in Ye jail; because he was a meritorious minister's son, he was pardoned and released.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming jailed him at Ye but released him as a hero's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 後帝聞其有父風，召拜度支郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: Later the emperor heard he had his father's manner and summoned and appointed him gentleman of the revenue department.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, hearing he had his father's ways, the emperor made him a revenue-department gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹爽宿與相親，時爽爲武衞將軍，數爲帝稱其可大用。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Shuang for long had been close to him; at that time Shuang was general who guards martial majesty and repeatedly for the emperor praised him as fit for great employment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang, long his friend while general who guards martial majesty, repeatedly praised him to the emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 會帝崩，爽輔政，乃拔謐爲散騎常侍，遂轉尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor died, Shuang assisted government, and thereupon promoted Mi supernumerary cavalry attendant and then transferred him secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor died and Shuang took power, Mi was made supernumerary cavalry attendant, then secretary.

manualTranslations.zh: 謐爲人外似踈略，而內多忌。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi as a man outwardly seemed careless and broad, yet inwardly bore much jealousy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Outwardly careless, Mi was inwardly jealous.

manualTranslations.zh: 其在臺閣，數有所彈駮，臺中患之，事不得行。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was in the terrace offices he repeatedly had impeachments and rebuttals; the terrace offices resented him and affairs could not be carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the central offices he blocked business with constant impeachments.

manualTranslations.zh: 又其意輕貴，多所忽略，雖與何晏、鄧颺等同位，而皆少之，唯以勢屈於爽。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover his intent slighted the honored; he on many occasions neglected them; though with He Yan and Deng Yang he was of equal rank, he all looked down on them—only because of power bowed to Shuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He looked down on peers such as He Yan and Deng Yang, bowing only to Shuang's power.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽亦敬之，言無不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang also respected him; his words were without any not followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang respected him and followed his every word.

manualTranslations.zh: 故於時謗書，謂「臺中有三狗，二狗崖柴不可當，一狗憑默作疽囊。」
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore at the time lampoons said: "In the terrace offices there are three dogs—two dogs cliff firewood cannot be withstood, one dog relying on Mo becomes a carbuncle sack."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A lampoon ran: "Three dogs in the offices—two dogs' cliff firewood none can withstand; one dog leans on Mo and festers like a boil."

manualTranslations.zh: 三狗，謂何、鄧、丁也。
manualTranslations.literal: The three dogs mean He, Deng, and Ding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The three dogs were He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi.

manualTranslations.zh: 默者，爽小字也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mo is Shuang's childhood name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mo was Shuang's childhood name.

manualTranslations.zh: 其意言三狗皆欲嚙人，而謐尤甚也。
manualTranslations.literal: Its meaning said the three dogs all wished to bite men, and Mi was especially so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All three bit at others; Mi most of all.

manualTranslations.zh: 奏使郭太後出居別宮，及遣樂安王使北詣鄴，又遣文欽令還淮南，皆謐之計。
manualTranslations.literal: Memorializing to have Empress Dowager Guo move out to a separate palace, and dispatching Prince of Le'an north to Ye, and also dispatching Wen Qin to order return to Huainan—all were Mi's plans.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi planned the dowager's removal to a separate palace, Prince of Le'an's dispatch north to Ye, and Wen Qin's recall to Huainan.

manualTranslations.zh: 司馬宣王由是特深恨之。
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Yi, King of Xuan, on this account especially deeply hated him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi therefore hated him deeply.

manualTranslations.zh: 畢軌，字昭先。
manualTranslations.literal: Bi Gui, courtesy name Zhaoxian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bi Gui bore the courtesy name Zhaoxian.

manualTranslations.zh: 父字子禮，建安中爲典農校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: His father's courtesy name was Zili; in the Jian'an era he was colonel of the agricultural colonies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Zili had been an agricultural colonel in Jian'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 軌以才能，少有名聲。
manualTranslations.literal: Gui because of talent and ability in youth had reputation and fame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui won early fame for talent.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝在東宮時，軌在文學中。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming was in the Eastern Palace, Gui was in the literary academy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was crown prince, Gui served in the literary academy.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初末，出爲長史。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Huangchu he went out as chief clerk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Huangchu he became a chief clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，入爲黃門郎，子尚公主，居處殷富。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming assumed the throne, he entered as gentleman of the Yellow Gates; his son married an imperial princess and his dwelling was rich.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he became a Yellow Gate gentleman; his son married a princess and his household grew wealthy.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷并州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred inspector of Bing province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Bing.

manualTranslations.zh: 其在并州，名爲驕豪。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was in Bing province he was famed as arrogant and overbearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Bing he earned a name for arrogance.

manualTranslations.zh: 時雜虜數爲暴，害吏民，軌輒出軍擊鮮卑軻比能，失利。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time mixed barbarians repeatedly made raids and harmed officials and commoners; Gui then led troops out to strike the Xianbei Kebineng and suffered defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When barbarians raided, he marched against the Xianbei leader Kebineng and lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 中護軍蔣濟表曰：「畢軌前失，旣往不咎，但恐是後難可以再。
manualTranslations.literal: Protector of the Army Jiang Ji memorialized, saying: "Bi Gui's former fault—what is past is not blamed; only I fear afterward it will be hard to have again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Protector of the Army Jiang Ji memorialized: "Gui's past fault should be forgiven, but repetition would be dangerous.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡人材有長短，不可彊成。
manualTranslations.literal: Human talent has long and short; it cannot be forced to completion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talents differ and cannot be forced.

manualTranslations.zh: 軌文雅志意，自爲美器。
manualTranslations.literal: Gui's literary elegance of intent is in itself a fine vessel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gui's cultivated mind makes him a fine instrument.

manualTranslations.zh: 今失并州，換置他州，若入居顯職，不毀其德，於國事實善。
manualTranslations.literal: Now having lost Bing province, if he is exchanged and placed in another province, if he enters and occupies an eminent post without destroying his virtue, for state affairs it is truly good.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Transfer him from Bing to another post without ruining his gifts, and the state will benefit.

manualTranslations.zh: 此安危之要，唯聖恩察之。」
manualTranslations.literal: This is the crux of safety and peril—may the sage grace examine it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This bears on safety and peril—please consider it."

manualTranslations.zh: 至正始中，入爲中護軍，轉侍中尚書，遷司隷校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: By the Zhengshi era he entered as protector of the army, transferred palace attendant and secretary, and was promoted commandant of Yong and Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By Zhengshi he was protector of the army, then palace attendant and secretary, then metropolitan commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 素與曹爽善，每言於爽，多見從之。
manualTranslations.literal: He for long was on good terms with Cao Shuang; each time he spoke to Shuang, mostly he was followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Long friendly with Shuang, he was usually obeyed.

manualTranslations.zh: 李勝字公昭。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Sheng, courtesy name Gongzhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Sheng bore the courtesy name Gongzhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 父休字子朗，有智略。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Xiu, courtesy name Zilang, had wisdom and stratagem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Xiu, styled Zilang, was a strategist.

manualTranslations.zh: 張魯前爲鎮北將軍，休爲司馬，家南鄭。
manualTranslations.literal: Before Zhang Lu was general who guards the north, Xiu was marshal; his family was at Nanzheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lu was general who guards the north, Xiu served as his marshal at Nanzheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 時漢中有甘露降，子朗見張魯精兵數萬人，有四塞之固，遂建言赤氣久衰，黃家當興，欲魯舉號，魯不聽。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time in Hanzhong sweet dew descended; Zilang saw Zhang Lu's crack troops numbered tens of thousands and had the strength of four passes, and thereupon advised that red vapor had long declined and the Yellow House ought to rise, wishing Lu to assume title; Lu did not listen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When sweet dew fell in Hanzhong, Zilang urged Zhang Lu, with tens of thousands of troops and a fortress in four directions, to declare himself emperor as the Han mandate waned; Lu refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 會魯破，太祖以其勸魯內附，賜爵關內侯，署散官騎從，詣鄴。
manualTranslations.literal: When Lu was broken, the Grand Progenitor because he had urged Lu to submit inward bestowed the rank of marquis within the passes, appointed him supernumerary cavalry follower, and sent him to Ye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Lu's defeat Cao Cao enfeoffed Xiu as a marquis within the passes for urging submission and sent him to Ye.

manualTranslations.zh: 至黃初中，仕歷上黨、鉅鹿二郡太守，後以年老還，拜議郎。
manualTranslations.literal: By the beginning of Huangchu he served successively as grand administrator of Shangdang and Julu commanderies; afterward because of old age he returned and was appointed adviser.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangchu he governed Shangdang and Julu, then retired as an adviser.

manualTranslations.zh: 勝少游京師，雅有才智，與曹爽善。
manualTranslations.literal: Sheng in youth traveled the capital, elegantly had talent and wisdom, and was on good terms with Cao Shuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sheng traveled the capital in youth, showed talent, and befriended Shuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝禁浮華，而人白勝堂有四䆫八達，各有主名。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Ming forbade flashiness, and someone reported Sheng's hall had four-window eight-path openings, each with a master's name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming banned flashy display; someone reported that Sheng's hall had "four windows and eight openings," each named for a patron.

manualTranslations.zh: 用是被收，以其所連引者多，故得原，禁錮數歲。
manualTranslations.literal: On this account he was seized; because those he implicated in succession were many, he obtained pardon, and was confined for several years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was arrested but pardoned because many were implicated; he was confined several years.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝崩，曹爽輔政，勝爲洛陽令。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor died, Cao Shuang assisted government; Sheng was magistrate of Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death Shuang made him Luoyang magistrate.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏侯玄爲征西將軍，以勝爲長史。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiahou Xuan was General Who Conquers the West and made Sheng chief clerk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan as General Who Conquers the West made Sheng his chief clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄亦宿與勝厚。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan also for long had been thick with Sheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan had long been close to Sheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 駱穀之役，議從勝出，由是司馬宣王不恱於勝。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Luogu campaign the deliberation followed Sheng's proposal to advance; on this account Sima Yi, King of Xuan, was not pleased with Sheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Luogu campaign Sheng's plan was adopted, and Sima Yi disliked him for it.

manualTranslations.zh: 累遷熒陽太守、河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted grand administrator of Yingyang and governor of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Yingyang and then Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 勝前後所宰守，未嘗不稱職，爲尹歲餘，廳事前屠蘇壞，令人更治之，小材一枚激墮，正檛受符吏石虎頭，斷之。
manualTranslations.literal: Where Sheng before and after administered and guarded, never was he not called competent; as governor for more than a year, the suzu before the hall office broke; he had men repair it; a small timber piece was struck and fell, just striking the clerk receiving credentials Shi Hutou and breaking him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every post he held won praise; as Henan governor, a repair timber in his hall fell and killed clerk Shi Hutou who was receiving credentials.

manualTranslations.zh: 後旬日，遷爲荊州刺史，未及之官而敗也。
manualTranslations.literal: After ten days he was transferred governor of Jing province; before he could reach office he was ruined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ten days later he was made governor of Jing but fell before taking office.

manualTranslations.zh: 桓範字元則，世爲冠族。
manualTranslations.literal: Huan Fan, courtesy name Yuanze, for generations a leading clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huan Fan, styled Yuanze, came from a leading clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安末，入丞相府。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Jian'an he entered the chancellor's office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Jian'an he entered the chancellor's staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 延康中，爲羽林左監。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Yankang era he was left colonel of the feathered forest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yankang he was left colonel of the feathered forest.

manualTranslations.zh: 以有文學，與王象等典集皇覽。
manualTranslations.literal: Because he had literary learning, together with Wang Xiang and others he directed compilation of the Imperial Overview.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his scholarship he helped Wang Xiang compile the Imperial Overview.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝時爲中領軍尚書，遷征虜將軍、東中郎將，使持節都督青、徐諸軍事，治下邳。
manualTranslations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time he was chief of the palace guard and secretary, transferred General Who Captures Barbarians and east central commander, bearing credentials as commander-in-chief directing Qing and Xu military affairs, administering at Xiapi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was chief of the palace guard and secretary, then general who captures barbarians and east central commander with credentials over Qing and Xu from Xiapi.

manualTranslations.zh: 與徐州刺史鄭岐爭屋，引節欲斬岐，爲岐所奏，不直，坐免還。
manualTranslations.literal: With Inspector of Xu Province Zheng Qi he quarreled over a house; drawing his credentials he wished to behead Qi; Qi memorialized against him; he was not in the right and sat dismissed and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Xu inspector Zheng Qi over a house, drew credentials to behead him, was impeached, found in the wrong, and dismissed.

manualTranslations.zh: 復爲兖州刺吏，怏怏不得意。
manualTranslations.literal: He again became inspector of Yan province, discontent and unhappy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He became inspector of Yan, sullen and unhappy.

manualTranslations.zh: 又聞當轉爲冀州牧。
manualTranslations.literal: He also heard he was about to be transferred provincial shepherd of Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then heard he was to become shepherd of Ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時冀州統屬鎮北，而鎮北將軍呂昭才實仕進，本在範後。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Ji province was under the general who guards the north, and General Who Guards the North Lü Zhao's talent and substance in official advancement originally came after Fan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji was then under General Who Guards the North Lü Zhao, whom Fan outranked in seniority yet resented.

manualTranslations.zh: 範謂其妻仲長曰：「我寧作諸卿，向三公長跪耳，不能爲呂子展屈也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Fan said to his wife Zhongchang: "I would rather be among you gentlemen, facing the three dukes kneeling long, than bow to Lü Zizhan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan told his wife Zhongchang, "I would rather kneel before the Three Excellencies than bow to Lü Zizhan."

manualTranslations.zh: 其妻曰：「君前在東，坐欲擅斬徐州刺史，衆人謂君難爲作下，今復羞爲呂屈，是復難爲作上也。」
manualTranslations.literal: His wife said: "Your lordship before in the east, sitting, wished on his own authority to behead the inspector of Xu province; the multitude said your lordship would be hard to make a subordinate—now again ashamed to bow to Lü, this again is hard to make a superior."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "In the east you nearly beheaded Xu's inspector and were called unfit to serve below—now you refuse to bow to Lü; are you fit to rule above?"

manualTranslations.zh: 範忿其言觸實，乃以刀環撞其腹。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan was angry that her words touched reality and thereupon struck her belly with a knife ring.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enraged that she spoke truth, Fan struck her pregnant belly with a knife ring.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻時懷孕，遂墮胎死。
manualTranslations.literal: His wife at the time was pregnant; thereupon she miscarried and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She miscarried and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 範亦竟稱疾，不赴冀州。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan also in the end claimed illness and did not go to Ji province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan claimed illness and never went to Ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始中拜大司農。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was appointed grand minister of agriculture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he became grand minister of agriculture.

manualTranslations.zh: 範前在臺閣，號爲曉事，及爲司農，又以清省稱。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan before in the terrace offices was called one who understood affairs; when he became minister of agriculture he was again famed for purity and frugality.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once famed in the central offices for knowing affairs, as minister of agriculture he was praised for frugality.

manualTranslations.zh: 範嘗抄撮《漢書》中諸雜事，自以意斟酌之，名曰世要論。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan once copied and gathered miscellaneous matters from the Book of Han, weighed them by his own intent, and titled it Essentials of the Age Treatise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He compiled excerpts from the Book of Han into his Essentials of the Age Treatise.

manualTranslations.zh: 蔣濟爲太尉，嘗與範會社下，羣卿列坐有數人，範懷其所撰，欲以示濟，謂濟當虛心觀之。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiang Ji was grand commandant; he once with Fan met below the altar to the soil god; the assembled ministers sat in rows numbering several men; Fan carried what he had composed and wished to show Ji, thinking Ji ought to view it with an open mind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Jiang Ji met Fan at an earth-god rite, Fan meant to show him his book.

manualTranslations.zh: 範出其書以示左右，左右傳之示濟，濟不肯視，範心恨之。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan took out his book and showed it to his attendants; the attendants passed it to show Ji; Ji would not look; Fan inwardly resented it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan passed the book along; Ji refused to read it, and Fan resented him.

manualTranslations.zh: 因論他事，乃發怒謂濟曰：「我祖薄德，公輩何似邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Because they discussed other matters, he thereupon grew angry and said to Ji: "My ancestor's thin virtue—what are you gentlemen like?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changing the subject in anger, Fan snapped, "My house has thin virtue—what are men like you?"

manualTranslations.zh: 濟性雖彊毅，亦知範剛毅，睨而不應，各罷。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji's nature though was strong and resolute, he also knew Fan was firm and resolute; he glanced and did not answer; each withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, though tough, knew Fan's temper; he glanced away and they parted.

manualTranslations.zh: 範於沛郡，仕次在曹真後。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan in Pei commandery in official seniority came after Cao Zhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Pei commandery Fan ranked after Cao Zhen.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時曹爽輔政，以範鄉里老宿，於九卿中特敬之，然不甚親也。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang assisted government; because Fan was an elder of the home village, among the nine ministers he especially respected him, yet was not very close.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shuang governed he respected Fan as a hometown elder but was not intimate.

manualTranslations.zh: 及宣王起兵，閉城門，以範爲曉事，乃指召之，欲使領中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the King of Xuan raised troops and closed the city gates, because Fan was called one who understood affairs, he was pointed to and summoned, wishing to have him lead the chief of the palace guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi closed the gates, he summoned Fan, famed for knowing affairs, to lead the palace guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 範欲應召，而其子諫之，以車駕在外，不如南出。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan wished to answer the summons, but his son remonstrated, saying the imperial carriage was outside and it was better to go south.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan meant to obey, but his son urged flight south while the emperor was abroad.

manualTranslations.zh: 範疑有頃，兒又促之。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan hesitated a moment; the son again urged him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He hesitated; his son urged again.

manualTranslations.zh: 範欲去而司農丞吏皆止範。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan wished to go but the minister of agriculture's clerks all stopped Fan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Clerks tried to stop him.

manualTranslations.zh: 範不從，乃突出至平昌城門，城門已閉。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan did not follow, and thereupon burst out reaching Pingchang city gate; the city gate was already closed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan broke through to Pingchang Gate, already shut.

manualTranslations.zh: 門候司蕃，故範舉吏也，範呼之，舉手中版以示之，矯曰：「有詔召我，卿促開門！」
manualTranslations.literal: Gate warden Si Fan was formerly Fan's nominated clerk; Fan called him, raised the tablet in his hand to show him, and falsely said: "There is an edict summoning me—you hurry and open the gate!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gate warden Si Fan, once Fan's nominee, was hailed with a forged summons: "Open the gate!"

manualTranslations.zh: 蕃欲求見詔書，範呵之，言「卿非我故吏邪，何以敢爾？」
manualTranslations.literal: Fan wished to see the edict document; Fan shouted at him, saying "Are you not my old clerk—how dare you thus?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Si Fan asked to see the edict, Fan roared, "You were my clerk—how dare you?"

manualTranslations.zh: 乃開之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he opened it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The gate opened.

manualTranslations.zh: 範出城，顧謂蕃曰：「太傅圖逆，卿從我去！」
manualTranslations.literal: Fan left the city, turned and said to Fan: "The Grand Tutor plots rebellion—you follow me and go!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Leaving the city Fan called back, "The Grand Tutor rebels—come with me!"

manualTranslations.zh: 蕃徒行不能及，遂避側。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan went on foot and could not catch up; thereupon he avoided to the side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Si Fan on foot could not catch up and hid aside.

manualTranslations.zh: 範南見爽，勸爽兄弟以天子詣許昌，徵四方以自輔。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan went south and saw Shuang; he urged Shuang's brothers to take the Son of Heaven to Xuchang and summon the four quarters to assist themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan rode south to Shuang and urged him to take the emperor to Xuchang and summon armies from every quarter.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽疑，羲又無言。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang hesitated; Xi again had no words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang hesitated; Xi said nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 範自謂羲曰：「事昭然，卿用讀書何爲邪！
manualTranslations.literal: Fan himself said to Xi: "The affair is obvious—what use is your reading books!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan told Xi, "The case is clear—what good is all your reading?

manualTranslations.zh: 於今日卿等門戶倒矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: On this day your house's gate is overturned!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today your house is finished!"

manualTranslations.zh: 俱不言。
manualTranslations.literal: Both did not speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Neither answered.

manualTranslations.zh: 範又謂羲曰：「卿別營近在闕南，洛陽典農治在城外，呼召如意。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan again said to Xi: "Your separate camp is near south of the palace; Luoyang's agricultural directorate administers outside the city—calling and summoning would be as wished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan added, "Your separate camp lies south of the palace; Luoyang's agricultural office is outside the walls—call them at will.

manualTranslations.zh: 今詣許昌，不過中宿，許昌別庫，足相被假；
manualTranslations.literal: Now going to Xuchang, not passing midnight lodging; Xuchang's separate storehouses are enough to lend to each other;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reach Xuchang by midnight; its storehouses can supply you;

manualTranslations.zh: 所憂當在穀食，而大司農印章在我身。」
manualTranslations.literal: what ought to be worried about is grain food, yet the grand minister of agriculture's seal is on my person."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: grain is the worry, and I hold the minister of agriculture's seal."

manualTranslations.zh: 羲兄弟默然不從，中夜至五鼓，爽乃投刀於地，謂諸從駕羣臣曰：「我度太傅意，亦不過欲令我兄弟向己也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xi's brothers were silent and did not follow; at midnight until the fifth watch Shuang then threw his knife to the ground and said to the various ministers following the carriage: "I gauge the Grand Tutor's intent—nothing more than wishing to have us brothers turn toward himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The brothers stayed silent; at the fifth watch Shuang threw down his sword and told the court, "I think the Grand Tutor only wants us to submit.

manualTranslations.zh: 我獨有以不合於遠近耳！」
manualTranslations.literal: I alone have what does not accord with near and far!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I alone have failed the realm!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂進謂帝曰：「陛下作詔免臣官，報皇太後令。」
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and said to the emperor: "Your Majesty compose an edict dismissing our offices and report the empress dowager's order."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He told the emperor to issue an edict dismissing them and report the dowager's order.

manualTranslations.zh: 範知爽首免而己必坐唱義也。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan knew Shuang would be the first dismissed and he himself would surely sit for advocating righteousness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan knew Shuang would surrender first and he would pay for urging resistance.

manualTranslations.zh: 範乃曰：「老子今茲坐卿兄弟族矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: Fan then said: "Laozi this year sits your brothers' clans!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan cried, "This year I sit with your whole clan!"

manualTranslations.zh: 爽等旣免，帝還宮，遂令範隨從。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shuang and the others were dismissed, the emperor returned to the palace and thereupon ordered Fan to follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shuang surrendered, the emperor returned to the palace with Fan in tow.

manualTranslations.zh: 到洛水浮橋北，望見宣王，下車叩頭而無言。
manualTranslations.literal: Reaching north of the Luoshui floating bridge, he saw the King of Xuan, descended from the carriage, kowtowed, and had no words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: North of the Luoshui floating bridge he saw Sima Yi, descended, and kowtowed in silence.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王呼範姓曰：「桓大夫何爲爾邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: The King of Xuan called Fan's surname, saying: "Grandee Huan—why act thus!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi called, "Grandee Huan—why act thus?"

manualTranslations.zh: 車駕入宮，有詔範還復位。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial carriage entered the palace; there was an edict that Fan return and resume his post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict restored Fan to office.

manualTranslations.zh: 範詣闕拜章謝，待報。
manualTranslations.literal: Fan went to the palace gate, bowed in a memorial apologizing, and awaited reply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan submitted an apology at the palace gate and waited.

manualTranslations.zh: 會司蕃詣鴻臚自首，具說範前臨出所道。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that Si Fan went to the grand herald to surrender himself and fully stated what Fan had said on leaving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Si Fan surrendered to the grand herald and reported Fan's words at the gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王乃忿然曰：「誣人以反，於法何應？」
manualTranslations.literal: The King of Xuan thereupon said in anger: "Falsely accusing a man of rebellion—in law what is the response?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi demanded, "What is the penalty for falsely crying rebellion?"

manualTranslations.zh: 主者曰：「科律，反受其罪。」
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible officer said: "In statute law, the false accuser receives the crime."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officer answered, "The accuser suffers the crime."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃收範於闕下。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Fan was seized below the palace gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan was seized below the palace gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 時人持範甚急，範謂部官曰：「徐之，我亦義士耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Men of the time seized Fan very urgently; Fan said to the office officers: "Slowly—I am also a man of righteousness."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As officers seized him, Fan said, "Slowly—I too am a man of honor."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂送廷尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he was sent to the commandant of justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was sent to the commandant of justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：初，爽夢二虎銜雷公，雷公若二升椀，放著庭中。
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: At first Shuang dreamed two tigers held the Lord of Thunder; the Lord of Thunder was like a two-sheng bowl, placed in the courtyard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Shuang dreamed two tigers holding the Thunder Lord, sized like a two-sheng bowl, set in the courtyard.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽惡之，以問占者，靈臺丞馬訓曰：「憂兵。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang hated it and asked the diviner; Director of the Spirit Terrace Ma Xun said: "Worry over troops."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He asked diviners; Ma Xun of the Spirit Terrace said, "Troops bring trouble."

manualTranslations.zh: 訓退，告其妻曰：「爽將以兵亡，不出旬日。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xun withdrew and told his wife: "Shuang will perish by troops, not outside ten days."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ma Xun told his wife Shuang would die by arms within ten days.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：安定皇甫謐以九年冬夢至洛陽，自廟出，見車騎甚衆，以物呈廟云：「誅大將軍曹爽。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Han–Jin Annals states: Huangfu Mi of Anding in the winter of the ninth year dreamed he reached Luoyang; from the temple he went out and saw chariots and horsemen very numerous; he presented an object to the temple saying: "Execute the grand general Cao Shuang."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin chunqiu says Huangfu Mi of Anding dreamed in winter of the ninth year that he reached Luoyang, left a temple amid vast chariots, and presented an offering: "Execute Grand General Cao Shuang."

manualTranslations.zh: 寤而以告其邑人，邑人曰：「君欲作曹人之夢乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Awakening, he told his townsman; the townsman said: "Your lordship wishes to make a Cao man's dream!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Awake, he told a townsman, who scoffed, "You dream like a Cao man!

manualTranslations.zh: 朝無公孫彊如何？
manualTranslations.literal: At court there is no Gongsun Jiang—how so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Where is there a Gongsun Jiang at court?

manualTranslations.zh: 且爽兄弟典重兵，又權尚書事，誰敢謀之？」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Shuang's brothers control heavy troops and again hold power over the Masters of Writing—who dares plot against them?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang and his brothers hold the army and the Secretariat—who would dare plot?"

manualTranslations.zh: 謐曰：「爽無叔振鐸之請，苟失天機則離矣，何恃於彊？
manualTranslations.literal: Mi said: "Shuang has no uncle Zhen Duo's request; if he loses Heaven's opportunity then he is separated—what reliance on strength?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi replied, "Shuang lacks an uncle's plea for mercy; lose Heaven's moment and power avails nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔漢之閻顯，倚母後之尊，權國威命，可謂至重矣，閹人十九人一旦尸之，況爽兄弟乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: In the past Han's Yan Xian relied on the empress dowager's honor, wielded the state's awesome command—one may say extremely heavy; nineteen eunuchs in one morning made corpses of them—how much more Shuang's brothers?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Xian of Han leaned on the empress dowager yet nineteen eunuchs slew him in a morning—how much less can Shuang rely on force?"

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：初，爽出，司馬魯芝留在府，聞有事，將營騎斫津門出赴爽。
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: At first when Shuang went out, Sima Luzhi remained in the office; hearing there was an affair, he was about to lead camp cavalry to cut through Jinfang Gate and go out to join Shuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says when Shuang marched out, Sima Luzhi in the office heard trouble and prepared to cut through Jinfang Gate with cavalry to join him.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽誅，擢爲御史中丞。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shuang was executed, he was promoted commandant of the censorate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shuang's execution Luzhi was promoted commandant of the censorate.

manualTranslations.zh: 及爽解印綬，將出，主簿楊綜止之曰：「公挾主握權，捨此以至東巿乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: When Shuang removed seals and ribbon and was about to go out, chief clerk Yang Zong stopped him, saying: "Your lordship holds the ruler and wields power—abandon this to reach the eastern market?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As Shuang surrendered his seals, chief clerk Yang Zong stopped him: "You hold the emperor and power—will you abandon this for the execution ground?"

manualTranslations.zh: 爽不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang did not follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang would not listen.

manualTranslations.zh: 有司奏綜導爽反，宣王曰：「各爲其主也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible office memorialized that Zong guided Shuang in rebellion; the King of Xuan said: "Each served his lord."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Authorities accused Zong of abetting rebellion; Sima Yi said, "Each served his lord."

manualTranslations.zh: 宥之，以爲尚書郎。
manualTranslations.literal: He pardoned him and made him gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and made a Masters of Writing gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 芝字世英，扶風人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi's courtesy name was Shiying; he was a man of Fufeng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Luzhi, styled Shiying, was from Fufeng.

manualTranslations.zh: 以後仕進至特進光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: Later in official advancement he reached special advancement and household counsellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later rose to special advancement and household counsellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 綜字初伯，後爲安東將軍司馬文王長史。
manualTranslations.literal: Zong's courtesy name was Chubo; later he was chief clerk to General Who Guards the East Sima Zhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zong, styled Chubo, later became chief clerk to Sima Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：夏侯湛爲芝銘及干寶晉紀並云爽旣誅，宣王即擢芝爲并州刺史，以綜爲安東參軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Commentator Pei Songzhi notes: Xiahou Zhan composed Zhi's epitaph and Gan Bao's Jin Annals both say that when Shuang was already executed, the King of Xuan immediately promoted Zhi inspector of Bing and made Zong an army staff officer to the east.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Xiahou Zhan's epitaph and Gan Bao's Jin ji make Luzhi inspector of Bing and Zong an eastern staff officer immediately after Shuang's fall.

manualTranslations.zh: 與《世語》不同。
manualTranslations.literal: It differs from the Worldly Talk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This differs from the Shiyu.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平中，紹功臣世，封真族孫熙爲新昌亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉真後。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jiaping era the meritorious ministers' lines were continued; Zhen's collateral descendant Xi was enfeoffed village marquis of Xinchang, fief three hundred households, to continue Zhen's line.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Jiaping era Cao Zhen's collateral descendant Xi was enfeoffed village marquis of Xinchang with three hundred households to continue Zhen's sacrifices.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：蔣濟以曹真之勳力，不宜絕祀，故以熙爲後。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Annals states: Jiang Ji because Cao Zhen's meritorious strength ought not to have sacrifices cut off, therefore made Xi his successor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin ji says Jiang Ji secured the enfeoffment lest Cao Zhen's line die out.

manualTranslations.zh: 濟又病其言之失信於爽，發病卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji again was ill that his words had broken faith with Shuang and died of the illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, ashamed that his counsel had misled Shuang, sickened and died.

sourceRange.text: 」淵妻，太祖内妹。長子衡，尚太祖弟海陽哀侯女，恩寵特隆。衡襲爵，轉封安寧亭侯。黄初中，賜中子霸，太和中，賜霸四弟，爵皆關内侯。霸，正始中爲討蜀護軍右將軍，進封博昌亭侯，素爲曹爽所厚。聞爽誅，自疑，亡入蜀。以淵舊勳赦霸子，徙樂浪郡。《魏略》曰：霸字仲權。淵爲蜀所害，故霸常切齒，欲有報蜀意。黄初中爲偏將軍。子午之役，霸召爲前鋒，進至興勢圍，安營在曲谷中。蜀人望知其是霸也，指下兵攻之。霸手戰鹿角間，賴救至，然後解。後爲右將軍，屯隴西，其養士和戎，并得其歡心。至正始中，代夏侯儒爲征蜀護軍，統屬征西。時征西將軍夏侯玄，於霸爲從子，而玄於曹爽爲外弟。及司馬宣王誅曹爽，遂召玄，玄來東。霸聞曹爽被誅而玄又徵，以爲祸必轉相及，心既内恐；又霸先與雍州刺史郭淮不和，而淮代玄爲征西，霸尤不安，故遂奔蜀。南趣陰平而失道，入窮谷中，糧盡，殺馬步行，足破，臥巖石下，使人求道，未知何之。蜀聞之，乃使人迎霸。初，建安五年，時霸從妹年十三四，在本郡，出行樵採，爲張飛所得。飛知其良家女，遂以爲妻，產息女，爲劉禪皇后。故淵之初亡，飛妻請而葬之。及霸入蜀，禪與相見，釋之曰：「卿父自遇害於行間耳，非我先人之手刃也。」指其兒子以示之曰：「此夏侯氏之甥也。」厚加爵寵。霸弟威，官至兖州刺史。《世語》曰：威字季權，任俠。貴歷荆、兖二州刺史。子駿，并州刺史。次莊，淮南太守。莊子湛，字孝若，以才博文章，至南陽相、散騎常侍。莊，晉景陽皇后姊夫也。由此一門侈盛於時。威弟惠，樂安太守。《文章叙錄》曰：惠字稚權，幼以才學見稱，善屬奏議。歷散騎黄門侍郎，與锺毓數有辯駮，事多見從。遷燕相、樂安太守。年三十七卒。惠弟和，河南尹。《世語》曰：和字義權，清辯有才論。歷河南尹、太常。淵第三子稱，第五子榮。從孫湛爲其〈序〉曰：「稱字叔權。自孺子而好合聚童兒，爲之渠帥，戲必爲軍旅戰陣之事，有違者輒嚴以鞭捶，眾莫敢逆。淵陰奇之，使讀《項羽傳》及兵書，不肯，曰：『能則自爲耳，安能學人？』年十六，淵與之田，見奔虎，稱驅馬逐之，禁之不可，一箭而倒。名聞太祖，太祖把其手喜曰：『我得汝矣！』與文帝爲布衣之交，每讌會，氣陵一坐，辯士不能屈。世之高名者多從之游。年十八卒。弟榮，字幼權。幼聰惠，七歲能屬文，誦書日千言，經目輒識之。文帝聞而請焉。賓客百餘人，人一奏刺，悉書其鄉邑名氏，世所謂爵里刺也，客示之，一寓目，使之遍談，不謬一人。帝深奇之。漢中之敗，榮年十三，左右提之走，不肯，曰：『君親在難，焉所逃死！』乃奮劍而戰，遂沒陣。」衡薨，子績嗣，爲虎賁中郎將。績薨，子褒嗣。

manualTranslations.zh: 」淵妻，太祖内妹。
manualTranslations.literal: 」Yuan's wife was the Grand Progenitor's younger sister by marriage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 」She was Cao Cao's sister-in-law.

manualTranslations.zh: 長子衡，尚太祖弟海陽哀侯女，恩寵特隆。
manualTranslations.literal: The eldest son Heng married the daughter of the Grand Progenitor's younger brother, Marquis Ai of Haiyang, and received exceptional grace and favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eldest son Heng married a daughter of Cao Cao's brother, Marquis Ai of Haiyang, and enjoyed exceptional favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 衡襲爵，轉封安寧亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Heng inherited the title and was transferred and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anning village.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heng inherited the line and was shifted to Marquis of Anning village.

manualTranslations.zh: 黄初中，賜中子霸，太和中，賜霸四弟，爵皆關内侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In Huangchu times the middle son Ba was bestowed; in Taihe times Ba's four younger brothers were bestowed; all their titles were interior marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era the middle son Ba was ennobled; in Taihe his four younger brothers followed, all as interior marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸，正始中爲討蜀護軍右將軍，進封博昌亭侯，素爲曹爽所厚。
manualTranslations.literal: Ba, in Zhengshi times served as protector general against Shu and General of the Right, was advanced to Marquis of Bochang village, and had long been favored by Cao Shuang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era Ba served as protector general against Shu and General of the Right, was advanced to Marquis of Bochang village, and had long been a favorite of Cao Shuang.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞爽誅，自疑，亡入蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing of Shuang's execution, he grew suspicious and fled into Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang was executed he panicked and fled to Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 以淵舊勳赦霸子，徙樂浪郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of Yuan's old merit, Ba's sons were pardoned and relocated to Lelang commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of Yuan's old service his sons were spared and exiled to Lelang commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：霸字仲權。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Ba, courtesy name Zhongquan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei gives his style as Zhongquan.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵爲蜀所害，故霸常切齒，欲有報蜀意。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan was harmed by Shu; therefore Ba constantly gnashed his teeth and wished to have the intent of repaying Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Yuan had been killed by Shu, Ba burned to avenge him.

manualTranslations.zh: 黄初中爲偏將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In Huangchu times he was lieutenant general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era he was made lieutenant general.

manualTranslations.zh: 子午之役，霸召爲前鋒，進至興勢圍，安營在曲谷中。
manualTranslations.literal: In the battle of Ziwu, Ba was summoned as vanguard, advanced to the enclosure of Xingshi, and set camp in Qu Valley.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the battle of Ziwu he was called up as vanguard, reached the siege lines at Xingshi, and pitched camp in Qu Valley.

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀人望知其是霸也，指下兵攻之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu men looking afar knew it was Ba and pointed the troops below to attack him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shu scouts recognized Ba and directed an assault against his position.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸手戰鹿角間，賴救至，然後解。
manualTranslations.literal: Ba fought hand-to-hand between the palisades; relying on rescue arriving, only then was he relieved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He fought hand to hand within the palisade until reinforcements arrived and extricated him.

manualTranslations.zh: 後爲右將軍，屯隴西，其養士和戎，并得其歡心。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was General of the Right, encamped in Longxi, nourished soldiers and harmonized with barbarians, and obtained the hearts of all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later as General of the Right stationed in Longxi he won over his troops and pacified the frontier tribes alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 至正始中，代夏侯儒爲征蜀護軍，統屬征西。
manualTranslations.literal: By Zhengshi times, he replaced Xiahou Ru as protector general against Shu and came under the command of the general who campaigns west.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he succeeded Xiahou Ru as protector general against Shu under the western expedition command.

manualTranslations.zh: 時征西將軍夏侯玄，於霸爲從子，而玄於曹爽爲外弟。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time General Who Campaigns West Xiahou Xuan was, to Ba, a nephew by a clanswoman, while Xuan to Cao Shuang was a younger brother by a sister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Who Campaigns West Xiahou Xuan was Ba's clansman-nephew and Cao Shuang's cousin on his mother's side.

manualTranslations.zh: 及司馬宣王誅曹爽，遂召玄，玄來東。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sima the Illustrious King executed Cao Shuang, he then summoned Xuan; Xuan came east.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Illustrious King of Jin executed Cao Shuang he summoned Xuan east to court.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸聞曹爽被誅而玄又徵，以爲祸必轉相及，心既内恐；
manualTranslations.literal: Ba heard that Cao Shuang had been executed and Xuan was also summoned; he thought disaster must spread in succession, and his heart was already inwardly fearful;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing of Cao Shuang's death and Xuan's recall, Ba assumed the purge would reach him and was filled with dread;

manualTranslations.zh: 又霸先與雍州刺史郭淮不和，而淮代玄爲征西，霸尤不安，故遂奔蜀。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Ba had earlier not been on good terms with Inspector of Yong Guo Huai, and when Huai replaced Xuan as commander west, Ba was especially uneasy; therefore he fled to Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had also feuded with Guo Huai, inspector of Yong, who now replaced Xuan in the west—and so he bolted to Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 南趣陰平而失道，入窮谷中，糧盡，殺馬步行，足破，臥巖石下，使人求道，未知何之。
manualTranslations.literal: He headed south toward Yinping but lost the road, entered a remote valley, grain was exhausted, he killed his horse and walked, feet broken, lay beneath cliff rocks, sent men seeking the road, not knowing where to go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He turned south toward Yinping, lost his way in a desolate gorge, ran out of food, killed his horse and went on foot with bleeding feet, and lay under a cliff while messengers searched in vain for a route.

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀聞之，乃使人迎霸。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu heard of it and then sent men to welcome Ba.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shu heard of his plight and sent a party to receive him.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，建安五年，時霸從妹年十三四，在本郡，出行樵採，爲張飛所得。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Jian'an, at that time Ba's cousin by a clanswoman was thirteen or fourteen, in the native commandery, went out to gather firewood and was taken by Zhang Fei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 5, when Ba's cousin was thirteen or fourteen, she was gathering firewood in the district and was seized by Zhang Fei.

manualTranslations.zh: 飛知其良家女，遂以爲妻，產息女，爲劉禪皇后。
manualTranslations.literal: Fei knew she was a good-family girl and then took her as wife; she bore a daughter who became Empress of Liu Shan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing her to be from a respectable house, Zhang Fei married her; their daughter became Empress of Liu Shan.

manualTranslations.zh: 故淵之初亡，飛妻請而葬之。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when Yuan first perished, Fei's wife requested and buried him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan first fell, Zhang Fei's wife obtained leave to bury him.

manualTranslations.zh: 及霸入蜀，禪與相見，釋之曰：「卿父自遇害於行間耳，非我先人之手刃也。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Ba entered Shu, Shan met with him and explained, saying: "Your father himself met harm amid the ranks; it was not my forebears' hands that blade-slaughtered him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ba arrived in Shu, Liu Shan received him and said: "Your father fell in battle—it was not my forebears who killed him with their own hands."

manualTranslations.zh: 指其兒子以示之曰：「此夏侯氏之甥也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Pointing to his son to show him, he said: "This is a nephew of the Xiahou clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He pointed to his son and said: "This boy is your clan's nephew."

manualTranslations.zh: 厚加爵寵。
manualTranslations.literal: He richly added titles and favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Shan heaped honors upon him.

manualTranslations.zh: 霸弟威，官至兖州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: Ba's younger brother Wei reached the post of Inspector of Yan province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ba's brother Wei rose to inspector of Yan province.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：威字季權，任俠。
manualTranslations.literal: A Saying of the Age says: Wei, courtesy name Jiquan, was a knight-errant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A Saying of the Age gives his style as Jiquan and calls him a man of the sword.

manualTranslations.zh: 貴歷荆、兖二州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Gui reign he served as inspector of Jing and Yan provinces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gui he held both Jing and Yan provincial inspectorates.

manualTranslations.zh: 子駿，并州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Jun was Inspector of Bing province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Jun became inspector of Bing.

manualTranslations.zh: 次莊，淮南太守。
manualTranslations.literal: The next, Zhuang, was Grand Administrator of Huainan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next son Zhuang served as grand administrator of Huainan.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊子湛，字孝若，以才博文章，至南陽相、散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuang's son Zhan, courtesy name Xiaoruo, by talent broad and literary compositions, reached Chancellor of Nanyang and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuang's son Zhan, styled Xiaoruo, won fame for learning and prose, rising to chancellor of Nanyang and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 莊，晉景陽皇后姊夫也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhuang was the brother-in-law of Empress Jingyang of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuang was brother-in-law to Jin's Empress Jingyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 由此一門侈盛於時。
manualTranslations.literal: From this the whole clan was extravagant and flourishing in the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From that branch the clan flourished extravagantly.

manualTranslations.zh: 威弟惠，樂安太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei's younger brother Hui was Grand Administrator of Le'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei's brother Hui was grand administrator of Le'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 《文章叙錄》曰：惠字稚權，幼以才學見稱，善屬奏議。
manualTranslations.literal: Collected Sayings on Literature says: Hui, courtesy name Zhiquan, in youth was acclaimed for talent and learning, skilled at composing memorials and deliberations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Collected Sayings on Literature gives his style as Zhiquan, praising his precocious talent and skill at memorial writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷散騎黄門侍郎，與锺毓數有辯駮，事多見從。
manualTranslations.literal: He successively served as Gentleman Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Yellow Gate, had repeated debates with Zhong Yu, and matters were often followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman attendant of scattered cavalry and yellow gate attendant, debated repeatedly with Zhong Yu, and usually prevailed.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷燕相、樂安太守。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Yan and Grand Administrator of Le'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was shifted to chancellor of Yan and grand administrator of Le'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 年三十七卒。
manualTranslations.literal: At age thirty-seven he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-seven.

manualTranslations.zh: 惠弟和，河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's younger brother He was Intendant of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui's brother He was intendant of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：和字義權，清辯有才論。
manualTranslations.literal: A Saying of the Age says: He, courtesy name Yiquan, was clear in debate and had talent for discourse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A Saying of the Age gives his style as Yiquan and describes him as sharp in debate and gifted in argument.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷河南尹、太常。
manualTranslations.literal: He successively served as Intendant of Henan and Minister of Ceremonies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He held the Henan intendant post and the ministry of ceremonials.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵第三子稱，第五子榮。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan's third son Cheng and fifth son Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan's third son was Cheng and his fifth Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 從孫湛爲其
manualTranslations.literal: His clansman-grandson Zhan for him
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His clansman-grandson Zhan composed for him

manualTranslations.literal: 〈Preface〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈Preface〉

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：「稱字叔權。
manualTranslations.literal: says: "Cheng, courtesy name Shuquan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It reads: "Cheng, styled Shuquan.

manualTranslations.zh: 自孺子而好合聚童兒，爲之渠帥，戲必爲軍旅戰陣之事，有違者輒嚴以鞭捶，眾莫敢逆。
manualTranslations.literal: From infancy he loved gathering children, became their chieftain; in play it was always army encampment and battle array matters; whoever disobeyed he immediately severely whipped, and none dared oppose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From childhood he gathered boys about him as a warlord among children; play always meant battle lines, and any rebel he thrashed until none dared defy him.

manualTranslations.zh: 淵陰奇之，使讀《項羽傳》及兵書，不肯，曰：『能則自爲耳，安能學人？』
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan inwardly marveled at him and had him read the biography of Xiang Yu and military books; he refused, saying: 'If able then act on one's own; how can one study others?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan secretly admired him and set him to read the biography of Xiang Yu and the military classics; the boy refused: 'If I have the gift I'll rely on myself—why copy another man?'

manualTranslations.zh: 年十六，淵與之田，見奔虎，稱驅馬逐之，禁之不可，一箭而倒。
manualTranslations.literal: At age sixteen, Yuan with him went to the fields, saw a fleeing tiger; Cheng drove his horse in pursuit; forbidding him was impossible; one arrow and it fell.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At sixteen, out hunting with Yuan, he spurred after a fleeing tiger despite orders to stop and dropped it with a single arrow.

manualTranslations.zh: 名聞太祖，太祖把其手喜曰：『我得汝矣！』
manualTranslations.literal: His name reached the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor grasped his hand delighted and said: 'I have obtained you!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Word reached Cao Cao, who seized his hand in delight and cried: 'I have found my man!'

manualTranslations.zh: 與文帝爲布衣之交，每讌會，氣陵一坐，辯士不能屈。
manualTranslations.literal: With Emperor Wen he was friends as common cloth; at every banquet his spirit towered over the whole seat; debaters could not bend him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was a close friend of the future Emperor Wen; at every feast his presence dominated the room and no wit could best him.

manualTranslations.zh: 世之高名者多從之游。
manualTranslations.literal: Many of the age's high names often associated with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men of the highest reputation sought his company.

manualTranslations.zh: 年十八卒。
manualTranslations.literal: At age eighteen he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at eighteen.

manualTranslations.zh: 弟榮，字幼權。
manualTranslations.literal: Younger brother Rong, courtesy name Youquan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His younger brother Rong, styled Youquan.

manualTranslations.zh: 幼聰惠，七歲能屬文，誦書日千言，經目輒識之。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth clever and gifted; at age seven able to compose prose; recited books a thousand words per day; once seen he always remembered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was precocious: at seven he could compose prose, recited a thousand characters a day, and never forgot what he read.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝聞而請焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and summoned him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wen sent for him.

manualTranslations.zh: 賓客百餘人，人一奏刺，悉書其鄉邑名氏，世所謂爵里刺也，客示之，一寓目，使之遍談，不謬一人。
manualTranslations.literal: More than a hundred guests, each presented a visiting card; he wrote all their native commanderies and surnames—the so-called card of fief and village of the age; when guests showed them, with one glance he had them discuss fully and not one was mistaken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before a hundred guests he was shown the visiting cards known as "fief-and-hometown tablets," glanced once, and named every man without error.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝深奇之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor was deeply struck.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢中之敗，榮年十三，左右提之走，不肯，曰：『君親在難，焉所逃死！』
manualTranslations.literal: In the defeat at Hanzhong, Rong was thirteen; attendants pulled him to flee; he refused, saying: 'Lord and father are in peril; where is flight to death!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the Hanzhong disaster, aged thirteen, attendants tried to drag him away; he refused: 'My lords and kin are in danger—where would I flee and live?'

manualTranslations.zh: 乃奮劍而戰，遂沒陣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he roused his sword and fought, and thereupon perished in the battle line."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He seized a sword, fought, and fell on the field."

manualTranslations.zh: 衡薨，子績嗣，爲虎賁中郎將。
manualTranslations.literal: Heng died; his son Ji succeeded and was Commandant of the Tiger Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Heng died his son Ji inherited and became commandant of the tiger guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 績薨，子褒嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji died; his son Bao succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ji died his son Bao inherited.

sourceRange.text: 真少與宗人曹遵、鄉人朱赞并事太祖。遵、赞早亡，真愍之，乞分所食邑封遵、赞子。詔曰：「大司馬有叔向抚孤之仁，笃晏平久要之分。君子成人之美，听分真邑賜遵、赞子爵關内侯，各百户。」真每征行，與將士同劳苦，軍赏不足，輒以家財班賜，士卒皆原爲用。真病還洛陽，帝自幸其第省疾。真薨，諡曰元侯。子爽嗣。帝追思真功，詔曰：「大司馬蹈履忠節，佐命二祖，内不恃親戚之寵，外不骄白屋之士，可謂能持盈守位，劳謙其德者也。其悉封真五子羲、训、則、彦、皑皆爲列侯。」初，文帝分真邑二百户，封真弟彬爲列侯。爽字昭伯，少以宗室謹重，明帝在東宮，甚親愛之。及即位，爲散騎侍郎，累遷城門校尉，加散騎常侍，轉武衞將軍，寵待有殊。帝寢疾，乃引爽入臥內，拜大將軍，假節鉞，都督中外諸軍事，錄尚書事，與太尉司馬宣王並受遺詔輔少主。明帝崩，齊王即位，加爽侍中，改封武安侯，邑萬二千戶，賜劒履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。丁謐畫策，使爽白天子，發詔轉宣王爲太傅，外以名號尊之，內欲令尚書奏事，先來由己，得制其輕重也。

manualTranslations.zh: 真少與宗人曹遵、鄉人朱赞并事太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth Zhen together with his clansman Cao Zun and his townsman Zhu Zan all served the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth Zhen served Cao Cao alongside his kinsman Cao Zun and his townsman Zhu Zan.

manualTranslations.zh: 遵、赞早亡，真愍之，乞分所食邑封遵、赞子。
manualTranslations.literal: Zun and Zan died early; Zhen pitied them and begged to divide the households of his fief to enfeoff Zun's and Zan's sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zun and Zan died young, Zhen asked to carve from his own fief and enfeoff their sons.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「大司馬有叔向抚孤之仁，笃晏平久要之分。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said, "The grand marshal has the kindness of Shuxiang in nurturing the orphaned and the steadfast friendship of Yan Ping in long-tested bonds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict read, "The grand marshal shows Shuxiang's kindness to the orphaned and Yan Ping's constancy in old friendship.

manualTranslations.zh: 君子成人之美，听分真邑賜遵、赞子爵關内侯，各百户。」
manualTranslations.literal: A gentleman completes another's excellence; permit the division of Zhen's fief to grant Zun's and Zan's sons the rank of secondary marquis within the passes, each with a hundred households."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let a gentleman crown another's merit: divide Zhen's fief and make Zun's and Zan's sons secondary marquises within the passes, a hundred households each."

manualTranslations.zh: 真每征行，與將士同劳苦，軍赏不足，輒以家財班賜，士卒皆原爲用。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever Zhen campaigned he shared hardship and toil with generals and soldiers. When military rewards were insufficient he would distribute his household wealth as gifts, and the soldiers all willingly served him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On campaign Zhen marched and slept as his men did. When bonuses ran short he paid from his own purse, and the ranks followed him willingly.

manualTranslations.zh: 真病還洛陽，帝自幸其第省疾。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhen fell ill and returned to Luoyang the emperor personally visited his residence to inquire after his illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When illness drove him back to Luoyang, the emperor came in person to his house.

manualTranslations.zh: 真薨，諡曰元侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen died; his posthumous title was Marquis Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 子爽嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Shuang succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Shuang succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝追思真功，詔曰：「大司馬蹈履忠節，佐命二祖，内不恃親戚之寵，外不骄白屋之士，可謂能持盈守位，劳謙其德者也。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor recalled Zhen's merit and issued an edict saying, "The grand marshal trod the path of loyal integrity, aided the Mandate of the two founders, inwardly did not rely on favor as kin, outwardly did not exalt himself over men of humble birth—he may be called one who could hold fullness and keep his place, whose merit was labor and whose virtue was humility.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Remembering Zhen's service, the emperor decreed, "The grand marshal walked in loyalty, served both founders, neither traded on kinship nor looked down on humble men—he held his fullness and kept his place through labor and modesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 其悉封真五子羲、训、則、彦、皑皆爲列侯。」
manualTranslations.literal: Let all five of Zhen's sons—Xi, Xun, Ze, Yan, and Kai—be enfeoffed as full marquises."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enfeoff all five sons—Xi, Xun, Ze, Yan, and Kai—as full marquises."

manualTranslations.zh: 初，文帝分真邑二百户，封真弟彬爲列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Wen divided two hundred households from Zhen's fief and enfeoffed Zhen's younger brother Bin as a full marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had earlier carved two hundred households from Zhen's fief to enfeoff his brother Bin as a full marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽字昭伯，少以宗室謹重，明帝在東宮，甚親愛之。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuang, courtesy name Zhaobo, in youth because of his clansmanship was careful and grave. When Emperor Ming was in the eastern palace he was deeply beloved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuang, styled Zhaobo, was grave and dutiful by birth. Emperor Ming cherished him while still heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即位，爲散騎侍郎，累遷城門校尉，加散騎常侍，轉武衞將軍，寵待有殊。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ming ascended the throne Shuang became attendant cavalier, was repeatedly promoted to colonel of the city gates, added as attendant cavalier at the palace, transferred to general of the martial guard, and received extraordinary favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Ming's accession he became attendant cavalier, rose through colonel of the city gates and attendant at the palace to general of the martial guard, with favor beyond the ordinary.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝寢疾，乃引爽入臥內，拜大將軍，假節鉞，都督中外諸軍事，錄尚書事，與太尉司馬宣王並受遺詔輔少主。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emperor lay gravely ill he summoned Shuang into the inner chamber, appointed him grand general, gave him the credential and battle-axe, made him supervisor of all military affairs within and without and recorder of the masters of writing, and together with Grand Commandant Sima Yi he received the deathbed edict to assist the young lord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On his deathbed the emperor drew Shuang to his couch, named him grand general with credential and battle-axe, set him over all armies and the masters of writing, and joined Sima Yi as co-regent for the boy emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝崩，齊王即位，加爽侍中，改封武安侯，邑萬二千戶，賜劒履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming died and the Prince of Qi ascended, Shuang was added as palace attendant, his fief was changed to marquis of Wu'an with twelve thousand households, and he was granted sword and shoes in the hall, exemption from hurrying at court audience, and exemption from having his name spoken in salutation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Ming's death and the Qi king's accession, Shuang became palace attendant, was refiefed as marquis of Wu'an with twelve thousand households, and received sword and shoes in the hall, freedom from hurried court approach, and salutation without naming.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁謐畫策，使爽白天子，發詔轉宣王爲太傅，外以名號尊之，內欲令尚書奏事，先來由己，得制其輕重也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ding Mi devised the plan to have Shuang tell the Son of Heaven to issue an edict transferring Sima Yi to grand tutor—outwardly honoring him by title, inwardly intending that memorials to the masters of writing should first come through himself so that he could control their weight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ding Mi plotted for Shuang to have the emperor name Sima Yi grand tutor—honor in title, but power in routing memorials through Shuang first so he could weigh every matter.

sourceRange.text: 」頃之，爲征西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。《魏略》曰：玄旣遷，司馬景王代爲護軍。護軍總統諸將，任主武官選舉，前後當此官者，不能止貨賂。故蔣濟爲護軍時，有謠言「欲求牙門，當得千匹；百人督，五百匹」。宣王與濟善，聞以問濟，濟無以解之，因戲曰：「洛中市買，一錢不足則不行。」遂相對歡笑。玄代濟，故不能止絕人事。及景王之代玄，整頓法令，人莫犯者。與曹爽共興駱穀之役，時人譏之。爽誅，徵玄爲大鴻臚，數年徙太常。玄以爽抑絀，內不得意。中書令李豐雖宿爲大將軍司馬景王所親待，然私心在玄，遂結皇後父光祿大夫張緝，謀欲以玄輔政。豐旣內握權柄，子尚公主，又與緝俱馮翊人，故緝信之。豐陰令弟兖州刺史翼求入朝，欲使將兵入，并力起。會翼求朝，不聽。嘉平六年254年二月，當拜貴人，豐等欲因御臨軒，諸門有陛兵，誅大將軍，以玄代之，以緝爲驃騎將軍。豐密語黃門監蘇鑠、永寧署令樂敦、宂從僕射劉賢等曰：「卿諸人居內多有不法，大將軍嚴毅，累以爲言，張當可以爲誡。」鑠等皆許以從命。《魏書》曰：玄素貴，以爽故廢黜，居常怏怏不得意。中書令李豐與玄及後父光祿大夫張緝陰謀爲亂，緝與豐同郡，傾巧人也，以東莞太守召，爲後家，亦不得意，故皆同謀。初，豐自以身處機密，息韜又以列侯給事中，尚齊長公主，有內外之重，心不自安。密謂韜曰：「玄旣爲海內重人，加以當大任，年時方壯而永見廢，又親曹爽外弟，於大將軍有嫌。吾得玄書，深以爲憂。緝有才用，棄兵馬大郡，還坐家巷。各不得志，欲使汝以密計告之。」緝嘗病創臥，豐遣韜省病，韜屏人語緝曰：「韜尚公主，父子在機近，大將軍秉事，常恐不見明信，太常亦懷深憂。君侯雖有後父之尊，安危未可知，皆與韜家同慮者也，韜父欲與君侯謀之。」緝默然良久曰：「同舟之難，吾焉所逃？此大事，不捷即禍及宗族。」韜於是往報豐。密語黃門監蘇鑠等，蘇鑠等荅豐：「惟君侯計。」豐言曰：「今拜貴人，諸營兵皆屯門。陛下臨軒，因此便共迫脅，將羣寮人兵，就誅大將軍。卿等當共密白此意。」鑠等曰：「陛下儻不從人，柰何？」豐等曰：「事有權宜，臨時若不信聽，便當劫將去耳。郍得不從？」鑠等許諾。豐曰：「此族滅事，卿等密之。事成，卿等皆當封侯常侍也。」豐復密以告玄、緝。緝遣子邈與豐相結，同謀起事。《世語》曰：豐遣子韜以謀報玄，玄曰「宜詳之耳」，而不以告也。大將軍微聞其謀，請豐相見，豐不知而往，即殺之。《世語》曰：大將軍聞豐謀，舍人王羕請以命請豐：「豐若無備，情屈勢迫，必來，若不來，羕一人足以制之；若知謀泄，以衆挾輪，長戟自衞，徑入雲龍門，挾天子登陵雲臺，臺上有三千人仗，鳴鼓會衆，如此，羕所不及也」。大將軍乃遣羕以車迎之。豐見劫迫，隨羕而至。《魏氏春秋》曰：大將軍責豐，豐知禍及，遂正色曰：「卿父子懷姦，將傾社稷，惜吾力劣，不能相禽滅耳！」大將軍怒，使勇士以刀環築豐腰，殺之。《魏略》曰：豐字安國，故衞尉李義子也。黃初中，以父任召隨軍。始爲白衣時，年十七八，在鄴下名爲清白，識別人物，海內翕然，莫不注意。後隨軍在許昌，聲稱日隆。其父不願其然，遂令閉門，勑使斷客。初，明帝在東宮，豐在文學中。及即尊位，得吳降人，問「江東聞中國名士爲誰」？降人云：「聞有李安國者是。」時豐爲黃門郎，明帝問左右安國所在，左右以豐對。帝曰：「豐名乃被於吳越邪？」後轉騎都尉、給事中。帝崩後，爲永寧太僕，以名過其實，能用少也。正始中，遷侍中尚書僕射。豐在臺省，常多託疾，時臺制，疾滿百日當解祿，豐疾未滿數十日，輒暫起，已復臥，如是數歲。初，豐子韜以選尚公主，豐雖外辭之，內不甚憚也。豐弟翼及偉，仕數歲閒，並歷郡守。豐嘗於人中顯誡二弟，言當用榮位爲□。及司馬宣王久病，偉爲二千石，荒於酒，亂新平、扶風二郡，而豐不召，衆人以爲恃寵。曹爽專政，豐依違二公間，無有適莫，故於時有謗書曰：「曹爽之勢熱如湯，太傅父子冷如漿，李豐兄弟如游光。」其意以爲豐雖外示清淨，而內圖事，有似於游光也。及宣王奏誅爽，住車闕下，與豐相聞，豐怖，遽氣索，足委地不能起。至嘉平四年252年宣王終後，中書令缺，大將軍諮問朝臣：「誰可補者？」或指向豐。豐雖知此非顯選，而自以連婚國家，思附至尊，因伏不辭，遂奏用之。豐爲中書二歲，帝比每獨召與語，不知所說。景王知其議己，請豐，豐不以實告，乃殺之。其事祕。豐前後仕歷二朝，不以家計爲意，仰俸廩而已。韜雖尚公主，豐常約勑不得有所侵取，時得賜錢帛，輒以外施親族；及得賜宮人，多與子弟，而豐皆以與諸外甥。及死後，有司籍其家，家無餘積。《魏氏春秋》曰：夜送豐尸付廷尉，廷尉鍾毓不受，曰：「非法官所治也。」以其狀告，且勑之，乃受。帝怒，將問豐死意，太後懼，呼帝入，乃止。遣使收翼。《世語》曰：翼後妻，散騎常侍荀廙姊，謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及書未至赴吳，何爲坐取死亡！左右可共同赴水火者誰？」翼思未荅，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，去亦不免。」翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去。今但從坐，身死，二兒必免。」果如翼言。翼子斌，楊駿外甥也。晉惠帝初，爲河南尹，與駿俱死，見晉書。事下有司，收玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢等送廷尉。《世語》曰：玄至廷尉，不肯下辭。廷尉鍾毓自臨治玄。玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何辭？卿爲令史責人也，卿便爲吾作。」毓以其名士，節高不可屈，而獄當竟，夜爲作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄。玄視，頷之而已。毓弟會，年少於玄，玄不與交，是日於毓坐狎玄，玄不受。孫盛雜語曰：玄在囹圄，會因欲狎而友玄，玄正色曰：「鍾君何相偪如此也！」廷尉鍾毓奏：「豐等謀迫脅至尊，擅誅冢宰，大逆無道，請論如法。」於是會公卿朝臣廷尉議，咸以爲「豐等各受殊寵，典綜機密，緝承外戚椒房之尊，玄備世臣，並居列位，而苞藏禍心，構圖凶逆，交關閹豎，授以姦計，畏憚天威，不敢顯謀，乃欲要君脅上，肆其詐虐，謀誅良輔，擅相建立，將以傾覆京室，顛危社稷。毓所正皆如科律，報毓施行」。詔書：「齊長公主，先帝遺愛，匄其三子死命。」於是豐、玄、緝、敦、賢等皆夷三族，《魏書》曰：豐子韜，以尚主，賜死獄中。其餘親屬徙樂浪郡。玄格量弘濟，臨斬東巿，顏色不變，舉動自若，時年四十六。《魏略》曰：玄自從西還，不交人事，不蓄華妍。《魏氏春秋》曰：初，夏侯霸將奔蜀，呼玄欲與之俱。玄曰：「吾豈苟存自客於寇虜乎？」遂還京師。太傅薨，許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣。」玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎？此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。」玄嘗著樂毅、張良及本無肉刑論，辭旨通遠，咸傳於世。玄之執也，衞將軍司馬文王流涕請之，大將軍曰：「卿忘會趙司空葬乎？」先是，司空趙儼薨，大將軍兄弟會葬，賔客以百數，玄時後至，衆賔客咸越席而迎，大將軍由是惡之。臣松之案：曹爽以正始五年244年伐蜀，時玄已爲關中都督，至十年，爽誅滅後，方還洛耳。案少帝紀，司空趙儼以六年亡，玄則無由得會儼葬，若云玄入朝，紀、傳又無其事。斯近妄不實。正元中，紹功臣世，封尚從孫本爲昌陵亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉尚後。
