manualTranslations.zh: 」頃之，爲征西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: 」Before long he became General Who Conquers the West, bearing credentials as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 」Shortly afterward he was made General Who Conquers the West, with credentials to command all forces in Yong and Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：玄旣遷，司馬景王代爲護軍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary states: After Xuan was transferred, Sima Shi, King of Jing, replaced him as protector of the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says that after Xuan was moved, Sima Shi replaced him as protector of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 護軍總統諸將，任主武官選舉，前後當此官者，不能止貨賂。
manualTranslations.literal: The protector of the army commands all generals and is charged with military appointments; those who held this office before and after could not stop bribery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The protector commanded all generals and controlled military appointments; none of his predecessors had been able to stop bribery.

manualTranslations.zh: 故蔣濟爲護軍時，有謠言「欲求牙門，當得千匹；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when Jiang Ji was protector of the army there was a saying: "To seek a halberd-bearing gate post, one must have a thousand bolts of silk;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ji held the post, people said, "A halberd gate command costs a thousand bolts of silk;

manualTranslations.zh: 百人督，五百匹」。
manualTranslations.literal: a commander of a hundred men, five hundred bolts."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: a company captain, five hundred."

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王與濟善，聞以問濟，濟無以解之，因戲曰：「洛中市買，一錢不足則不行。」
manualTranslations.literal: The King of Xuan was on good terms with Ji; hearing of it he asked Ji, and Ji had no way to explain it away, so in jest he said: "In Luoyang market trade, if one cash is short nothing moves."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, on good terms with Jiang Ji, asked him about it; Ji could not explain it away and joked, "In Luoyang markets, trade stalls if a single cash is missing."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂相對歡笑。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they laughed together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The two men laughed together.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄代濟，故不能止絕人事。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xuan replaced Ji, therefore he could not stop social obligations entirely.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xuan replaced Ji he still could not shut the door on such obligations.

manualTranslations.zh: 及景王之代玄，整頓法令，人莫犯者。
manualTranslations.literal: When the King of Jing replaced Xuan, he put the laws in order and no one dared offend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sima Shi replaced Xuan he tightened the laws until no one dared transgress.

manualTranslations.zh: 與曹爽共興駱穀之役，時人譏之。
manualTranslations.literal: Together with Cao Shuang he launched the Luogu Valley campaign, and men of the time mocked them for it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He joined Cao Shuang in the Luogu Valley expedition, which contemporaries ridiculed.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽誅，徵玄爲大鴻臚，數年徙太常。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shuang was executed, Xuan was summoned as grand minister of splendid happiness; after several years he was moved to grand minister of worship.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shuang's execution Xuan was recalled as grand minister of splendid happiness, then after several years made grand minister of worship.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄以爽抑絀，內不得意。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan, because Shuang had suppressed and demoted him, inwardly was discontent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Humiliated by Shuang's fall, Xuan brooded in discontent.

manualTranslations.zh: 中書令李豐雖宿爲大將軍司馬景王所親待，然私心在玄，遂結皇後父光祿大夫張緝，謀欲以玄輔政。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng, though long favored by the grand general Sima Shi, King of Jing, in his private heart favored Xuan; he therefore joined the empress's father, Household Counsellor Zhang Ji, plotting to have Xuan assist in government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng had long been favored by Sima Shi, yet privately backed Xuan; he joined the empress's father, Household Counsellor Zhang Ji, in a plot to install Xuan as regent.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐旣內握權柄，子尚公主，又與緝俱馮翊人，故緝信之。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng already held power within; his son had married an imperial princess, and he was a fellow townsman of Ji—therefore Ji trusted him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng already wielded inner power; his son had married a princess, and he shared Zhang Ji's home commandery—so Ji trusted him.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐陰令弟兖州刺史翼求入朝，欲使將兵入，并力起。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng secretly ordered his younger brother Yi, inspector of Yan province, to request audience, wishing to have him lead troops in and join forces to rise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng secretly ordered his brother Yi, inspector of Yan, to request audience so he could march troops in and join the rising.

manualTranslations.zh: 會翼求朝，不聽。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that Yi requested audience and was not permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi's request for audience was denied.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平六年254年二月，當拜貴人，豐等欲因御臨軒，諸門有陛兵，誅大將軍，以玄代之，以緝爲驃騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Jiaping (254), when a noble consort was to be invested, Feng and the others wished to take advantage of the emperor's facing the hall, with gate guards stationed at every door, to execute the grand general, replace him with Xuan, and make Ji general of agile cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jiaping 6 (254), when a noble consort was to be invested, Feng planned to strike during the imperial audience, with gate guards at every portal: kill the grand general, put Xuan in his place, and make Zhang Ji general of agile cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐密語黃門監蘇鑠、永寧署令樂敦、宂從僕射劉賢等曰：「卿諸人居內多有不法，大將軍嚴毅，累以爲言，張當可以爲誡。」
manualTranslations.literal: Feng secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Director of the Eternal Tranquility Office Yue Dun, deputy director of attendants Liu Xian, and others, saying: "You all within often have unlawful conduct; the grand general is stern and severe and has repeatedly spoken of it—Zhang Dang can serve as a warning."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Director of the Office of Eternal Tranquility Yue Dun, deputy director of attendants Liu Xian, and others: "You inside the palace have many offenses; the grand general is stern and has warned you repeatedly—remember Zhang Dang."

manualTranslations.zh: 鑠等皆許以從命。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuo and the others all promised to follow his command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Su Shuo and the rest all pledged obedience.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：玄素貴，以爽故廢黜，居常怏怏不得意。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei states: Xuan had always been honored; because of Shuang he was dismissed and demoted, and in daily life was discontent and unhappy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Xuan had always been eminent; Shuang's fall left him demoted and perpetually sour.

manualTranslations.zh: 中書令李豐與玄及後父光祿大夫張緝陰謀爲亂，緝與豐同郡，傾巧人也，以東莞太守召，爲後家，亦不得意，故皆同謀。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Feng, Xuan, and the empress's father Household Counsellor Zhang Ji secretly plotted rebellion; Ji and Feng were of the same commandery, a man crafty and clever; summoned from grand administrator of Dongguan to serve the empress's family, he too was discontent—therefore all plotted together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Feng, Xuan, and the empress's father Zhang Ji plotted together; Ji, a clever schemer from Feng's home commandery, had been recalled from Dongguan to serve the empress's kin and was equally resentful.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，豐自以身處機密，息韜又以列侯給事中，尚齊長公主，有內外之重，心不自安。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Feng, because he himself stood in confidential affairs, and his son Tao moreover held the rank of full marquis as director of attendants and had married the Princess of Qi the Long, bearing weight within and without, was inwardly ill at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng himself held confidential office, and his son Tao, a full marquis and director of attendants married to the Princess of Qi the Long, gave the family weight at court—yet Feng felt uneasy.

manualTranslations.zh: 密謂韜曰：「玄旣爲海內重人，加以當大任，年時方壯而永見廢，又親曹爽外弟，於大將軍有嫌。
manualTranslations.literal: He secretly told Tao: "Xuan is already a man of weight within the seas, and moreover bears great responsibility; in the prime of life he is forever dismissed; he is also Cao Shuang's cousin by marriage and bears resentment toward the grand general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He secretly told Tao: "Xuan is a man of national stature still in his prime, yet permanently shelved; he is also Cao Shuang's cousin by marriage and bears a grudge against the grand general.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾得玄書，深以爲憂。
manualTranslations.literal: I received a letter from Xuan and deeply took it as a worry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A letter from Xuan has me deeply worried."

manualTranslations.zh: 緝有才用，棄兵馬大郡，還坐家巷。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji has talent and use; he was cast aside from a great commandery of troops and horses and sent back to sit in a home lane.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji has ability, yet was pulled from a major command and left idle at home.

manualTranslations.zh: 各不得志，欲使汝以密計告之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Each is frustrated in ambition; I wish you to tell him the secret plan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each of us is thwarted—I want you to confide the plan to him."

manualTranslations.zh: 緝嘗病創臥，豐遣韜省病，韜屏人語緝曰：「韜尚公主，父子在機近，大將軍秉事，常恐不見明信，太常亦懷深憂。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji once lay ill with a wound; Feng sent Tao to visit him in his illness; Tao dismissed the attendants and spoke to Ji, saying: "Tao has married a princess; father and son stand near the inner secrets; the grand general holds affairs and constantly fears he will not be trusted—Grand Minister of Worship also bears deep worry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Ji lay wounded, Feng sent Tao to visit him; Tao sent servants away and said: "I have married a princess; my father and I stand near the inner secrets. The grand general holds power and we fear we are not trusted; the grand minister of worship is deeply anxious too.

manualTranslations.zh: 君侯雖有後父之尊，安危未可知，皆與韜家同慮者也，韜父欲與君侯謀之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Your lordship, though you have the honor of the empress's father, safety and peril are not yet known; all share the Tao family's concern; Tao's father wishes to plot with your lordship."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though you are the empress's father, your safety is uncertain—we share the same fears, and my father wishes to plot with you."

manualTranslations.zh: 緝默然良久曰：「同舟之難，吾焉所逃？
manualTranslations.literal: Ji was silent a long while and said: "In the same boat in hardship—where can I flee?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji was silent a long while, then said: "We are in the same boat—where could I flee?

manualTranslations.zh: 此大事，不捷即禍及宗族。」
manualTranslations.literal: This is a great affair; if it does not succeed, disaster will reach the clan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is a grave matter; failure means the destruction of our clans."

manualTranslations.zh: 韜於是往報豐。
manualTranslations.literal: Tao thereupon went to report to Feng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tao then reported back to Feng.

manualTranslations.zh: 密語黃門監蘇鑠等，蘇鑠等荅豐：「惟君侯計。」
manualTranslations.literal: He secretly told Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo and others; Su Shuo and the others answered Feng: "Only your lordship's plan."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng again secretly told Su Shuo and the others; they answered, "We follow your plan alone."

manualTranslations.zh: 豐言曰：「今拜貴人，諸營兵皆屯門。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng spoke, saying: "Today when the noble consort is invested, all camp soldiers will be stationed at the gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng said: "When the noble consort is invested today, camp soldiers will mass at the gates.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下臨軒，因此便共迫脅，將羣寮人兵，就誅大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When His Majesty faces the hall, on this occasion together coerce and threaten, take the crowd of ministers and soldiers, and go execute the grand general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor faces the hall we will seize the moment, force the ministers and soldiers with us, and kill the grand general.

manualTranslations.zh: 卿等當共密白此意。」
manualTranslations.literal: You all ought together secretly report this intent."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You must all secretly report this plan."

manualTranslations.zh: 鑠等曰：「陛下儻不從人，柰何？」
manualTranslations.literal: Shuo and the others said: "If His Majesty perchance does not follow men, what then?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Su Shuo asked, "What if the emperor refuses?"

manualTranslations.zh: 豐等曰：「事有權宜，臨時若不信聽，便當劫將去耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng and the others said: "In affairs there is expedient measure; at the moment if he does not believe and listen, then one must seize the general and go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng replied, "There are expedients: if he will not listen, seize the general and go.

manualTranslations.zh: 郍得不從？」
manualTranslations.literal: How could he fail to follow?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Would he not have to obey?"

manualTranslations.zh: 鑠等許諾。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuo and the others promised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐曰：「此族滅事，卿等密之。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng said: "This is a clan-destroying affair; you all must keep it secret.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng warned, "This is a matter of extermination—keep it secret.

manualTranslations.zh: 事成，卿等皆當封侯常侍也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If the affair succeeds, you all will be enfeoffed as marquises and made regular palace attendants."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Succeed, and you will all be enfeoffed marquises and made regular palace attendants."

manualTranslations.zh: 豐復密以告玄、緝。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng again secretly told Xuan and Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng secretly informed Xuan and Ji as well.

manualTranslations.zh: 緝遣子邈與豐相結，同謀起事。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji sent his son Miao to join with Feng and together plot the rising.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji sent his son Miao to join Feng in the plot.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：豐遣子韜以謀報玄，玄曰「宜詳之耳」，而不以告也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Feng sent his son Tao to report the plot to Xuan; Xuan said "It ought to be examined carefully," and did not report it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Feng sent Tao to tell Xuan; Xuan replied only, "This needs careful thought," and reported nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍微聞其謀，請豐相見，豐不知而往，即殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand general faintly heard of the plot, invited Feng to an audience; Feng did not know and went, and was immediately killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The grand general caught wind of the plot, summoned Feng, and killed him when he came unaware.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：大將軍聞豐謀，舍人王羕請以命請豐：「豐若無備，情屈勢迫，必來，若不來，羕一人足以制之；
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: The grand general heard of Feng's plot; attendant Wang Yang requested by order to summon Feng: "If Feng is unprepared, his feelings bent and his situation pressed, he is sure to come; if he does not come, Yang alone is enough to control him;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu adds that attendant Wang Yang proposed summoning Feng: "If he is unprepared, bent by pressure, he will come; if not, I alone can handle him;

manualTranslations.zh: 若知謀泄，以衆挾輪，長戟自衞，徑入雲龍門，挾天子登陵雲臺，臺上有三千人仗，鳴鼓會衆，如此，羕所不及也」。
manualTranslations.literal: if he knows the plot is leaked, with a crowd bearing carriage wheels and long halberds guarding himself, going straight through the Cloud Dragon Gate, seizing the Son of Heaven and ascending the Lingyun Terrace—on the terrace are three thousand men with weapons, beating drums to assemble the crowd—thus Yang could not reach him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: but if he knows the plot is out, he may force his way through Cloud Dragon Gate with an armed escort, seize the emperor, and rally three thousand men on Lingyun Terrace—then I could not stop him."

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍乃遣羕以車迎之。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand general thereupon sent Yang with a carriage to welcome him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sent Wang Yang with a carriage to fetch him.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐見劫迫，隨羕而至。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng, seeing coercion, followed Yang and arrived.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cornered, Feng went with Yang.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：大將軍責豐，豐知禍及，遂正色曰：「卿父子懷姦，將傾社稷，惜吾力劣，不能相禽滅耳！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: The grand general reproached Feng; Feng knew disaster had reached him and thereupon with stern countenance said: "Your lordship and son harbor treachery and will overturn the altars of soil and grain; I regret my strength is weak and cannot seize and destroy you!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says the grand general rebuked Feng, who answered coldly: "You and your father plot treason against the state; I regret I am too weak to destroy you!"

manualTranslations.zh: 大將軍怒，使勇士以刀環築豐腰，殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: The grand general was angry and had warriors strike Feng's waist with knife rings and kill him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enraged, the grand general had warriors beat Feng to death with knife rings.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：豐字安國，故衞尉李義子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary states: Feng's courtesy name was Anguo; he was the son of the former Commandant of the Guard Li Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe gives Feng the courtesy name Anguo; he was son of the former commandant of the guard Li Yi.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初中，以父任召隨軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Huangchu era, through his father's appointment he was summoned to follow the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Huangchu era he entered service through his father's appointment.

manualTranslations.zh: 始爲白衣時，年十七八，在鄴下名爲清白，識別人物，海內翕然，莫不注意。
manualTranslations.literal: When he first was in plain clothes, at seventeen or eighteen, in Ye he was famed as pure and clean, discerning and distinguishing men; within the seas all at once attended to it, none not paying attention.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a young man of seventeen or eighteen in Ye he was famed for integrity and for judging character; the empire took notice.

manualTranslations.zh: 後隨軍在許昌，聲稱日隆。
manualTranslations.literal: Later following the army at Xuchang, his reputation daily grew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, serving at Xuchang, his fame grew daily.

manualTranslations.zh: 其父不願其然，遂令閉門，勑使斷客。
manualTranslations.literal: His father did not wish it so and thereupon ordered the gates closed and commanded that visitors be cut off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father disapproved and shut the gates to visitors.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，明帝在東宮，豐在文學中。
manualTranslations.literal: At first when Emperor Ming was in the Eastern Palace, Feng was in the literary academy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was crown prince, Feng served in the literary academy.

manualTranslations.zh: 及即尊位，得吳降人，問「江東聞中國名士爲誰」？
manualTranslations.literal: When he assumed the honored throne, Wu surrenderers were obtained; he asked, "In Jiangdong whom do they hear are famous gentlemen of China?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After his accession he questioned Wu captives: "Whom do they call China's leading gentlemen?"

manualTranslations.zh: 降人云：「聞有李安國者是。」
manualTranslations.literal: The surrenderer said: "I hear there is one called Li Anguo."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One answered, "I hear of a Li Anguo."

manualTranslations.zh: 時豐爲黃門郎，明帝問左右安國所在，左右以豐對。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Feng was a gentleman of the Yellow Gates; Emperor Ming asked his attendants where Anguo was; the attendants answered with Feng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng was then a gentleman of the Yellow Gates; the emperor asked where Anguo was, and attendants named Feng.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝曰：「豐名乃被於吳越邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor said: "Feng's name is spread even to Wu and Yue?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So Feng's name reaches even Wu and Yue?"

manualTranslations.zh: 後轉騎都尉、給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was transferred cavalry commandant and director of attendants.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was later made cavalry commandant and director of attendants.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝崩後，爲永寧太僕，以名過其實，能用少也。
manualTranslations.literal: After the emperor's death he became grand steward of Eternal Tranquility; because the name exceeded the reality, he was little employed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming's death he became grand steward of Eternal Tranquility but was little used—his reputation outran his role.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始中，遷侍中尚書僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was promoted palace attendant and vice director of the secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he rose to palace attendant and vice director of the secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐在臺省，常多託疾，時臺制，疾滿百日當解祿，豐疾未滿數十日，輒暫起，已復臥，如是數歲。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng in the terrace offices often pleaded illness on many occasions; at that time the terrace regulation was that illness reaching a hundred days should result in dismissal from salary; Feng's illness had not reached several tens of days when he would briefly rise, then lie down again—thus for several years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the central offices Feng often feigned illness; regulations allowed dismissal after a hundred sick days, yet he would rise briefly every few dozen days and then return to bed—for years.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，豐子韜以選尚公主，豐雖外辭之，內不甚憚也。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Feng's son Tao was selected to marry a princess; Feng outwardly declined but inwardly was not very fearful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Tao was chosen to marry a princess, Feng outwardly declined but inwardly was not much alarmed.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐弟翼及偉，仕數歲閒，並歷郡守。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng's younger brothers Yi and Wei, within several years of service, both successively served as grand administrators.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His brothers Yi and Wei both became commandery governors within a few years.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐嘗於人中顯誡二弟，言當用榮位爲□。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng once openly admonished the two younger brothers before people, saying glory and rank ought to be used as □.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng once publicly admonished his brothers before others that rank ought to be used with restraint.

manualTranslations.zh: 及司馬宣王久病，偉爲二千石，荒於酒，亂新平、扶風二郡，而豐不召，衆人以爲恃寵。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sima Yi, King of Xuan, was long ill, Wei held a two-thousand-bushel post, was dissolute in wine, and threw into disorder Xinping and Fufeng commanderies, yet Feng did not summon him; the multitude thought he relied on favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi lay long ill, his brother Wei, a two-thousand-bushel official, drank himself into misrule in Xinping and Fufeng, yet Feng did not recall him—people thought he traded on favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹爽專政，豐依違二公間，無有適莫，故於時有謗書曰：「曹爽之勢熱如湯，太傅父子冷如漿，李豐兄弟如游光。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Cao Shuang monopolized government, Feng wavered between the two lords without fixed preference; therefore at the time there was a lampoon saying: "Cao Shuang's power hot as boiling water, the Grand Tutor and son cold as gruel, the Li Feng brothers like wandering light."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang monopolized power, Feng trimmed between him and the Simas; a lampoon ran: "Shuang's heat boils like soup, the Grand Tutor and son are cold as gruel, the Li Feng brothers drift like will-o'-the-wisp light."

manualTranslations.zh: 其意以爲豐雖外示清淨，而內圖事，有似於游光也。
manualTranslations.literal: Its meaning held that though Feng outwardly showed purity, inwardly he plotted affairs, somewhat like wandering light.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The point was that Feng looked pure outwardly while plotting within—like drifting light.

manualTranslations.zh: 及宣王奏誅爽，住車闕下，與豐相聞，豐怖，遽氣索，足委地不能起。
manualTranslations.literal: When the King of Xuan memorialized to execute Shuang, stopping the carriage below the palace gate, he and Feng were within hearing; Feng was afraid, suddenly his breath failed, his feet gave way to the ground and he could not rise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi memorialized against Shuang and halted below the palace gate, Feng within hearing was terrified—his breath failed and his legs gave way.

manualTranslations.zh: 至嘉平四年252年宣王終後，中書令缺，大將軍諮問朝臣：「誰可補者？」
manualTranslations.literal: By the fourth year of Jiaping (252), after the King of Xuan died, the director of the secretariat was vacant; the grand general consulted the court ministers: "Who can fill it?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi died in Jiaping 4 (252), the directorship fell vacant; the grand general asked the court, "Who can fill it?"

manualTranslations.zh: 或指向豐。
manualTranslations.literal: Some pointed to Feng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some named Feng.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐雖知此非顯選，而自以連婚國家，思附至尊，因伏不辭，遂奏用之。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng though knew this was not a conspicuous selection, yet because he himself was connected by marriage to the imperial house, wished to attach to the supreme lord, and therefore bowed without declining, and memorial was submitted to employ him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng knew it was no glittering appointment, yet through imperial marriage ties he wished to cling to the throne and accepted without demur.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐爲中書二歲，帝比每獨召與語，不知所說。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng was director of the secretariat two years; the emperor repeatedly summoned him alone to speak; what was said is not known.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For two years as director the emperor repeatedly summoned Feng alone—what passed between them is unknown.

manualTranslations.zh: 景王知其議己，請豐，豐不以實告，乃殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: The King of Jing knew he discussed himself, invited Feng; Feng did not tell the truth, and thereupon killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Shi learned Feng had plotted against him, summoned him, and killed him when he would not confess.

manualTranslations.zh: 其事祕。
manualTranslations.literal: The affair was secret.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The affair was kept secret.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐前後仕歷二朝，不以家計爲意，仰俸廩而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Feng through his career served two reigns and did not take household accounts to heart; he relied on salary grain alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Through two reigns Feng cared nothing for household wealth and lived on salary alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 韜雖尚公主，豐常約勑不得有所侵取，時得賜錢帛，輒以外施親族；
manualTranslations.literal: Though Tao had married a princess, Feng constantly restrained and commanded that he must not seize or take anything; when he occasionally received bestowed money and silk, he would outwardly give it to kinsmen;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Tao had married a princess, Feng forbade him to seize anything; gifts of money or silk went to kin;

manualTranslations.zh: 及得賜宮人，多與子弟，而豐皆以與諸外甥。
manualTranslations.literal: and when he received bestowed palace women, he mostly gave them to sons and younger brothers, while Feng all gave them to various nephews.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: palace women given him he passed to nephews and younger kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 及死後，有司籍其家，家無餘積。
manualTranslations.literal: After his death the responsible office inventoried his household; the household had no surplus accumulation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After his death officials inventoried his home and found no surplus.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：夜送豐尸付廷尉，廷尉鍾毓不受，曰：「非法官所治也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: At night Feng's corpse was sent to the commandant of justice; Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu refused it, saying: "It is not what the law office governs."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says Feng's corpse was sent at night to the commandant of justice; Zhong Yu refused, saying, "This is outside the law office's jurisdiction."

manualTranslations.zh: 以其狀告，且勑之，乃受。
manualTranslations.literal: Reporting the circumstances and moreover commanding him, then he accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only after orders were reported and repeated did he accept.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝怒，將問豐死意，太後懼，呼帝入，乃止。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor was angry and was about to question Feng's dying intent; the empress dowager feared it, called the emperor in, and then it stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to interrogate Feng's dying intent; the empress dowager, fearing scandal, called him in and stopped it.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣使收翼。
manualTranslations.literal: An envoy was sent to seize Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to arrest Yi.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：翼後妻，散騎常侍荀廙姊，謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及書未至赴吳，何爲坐取死亡！
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: Yi's later wife, elder sister of Regular Palace Attendant Xun Yi, said to Yi: "The director of the secretariat affair has broken out; while the letter has not yet arrived you can hurry to Wu—why sit and court death!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Yi's second wife, sister of Xun Yi, told him: "The secretariat plot is exposed—you can still reach Wu before the warrant arrives. Why sit here and die?

manualTranslations.zh: 左右可共同赴水火者誰？」
manualTranslations.literal: Among those at hand who can together go through fire and water, who is there?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who among your household would follow you through fire?"

manualTranslations.zh: 翼思未荅，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，去亦不免。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yi thought and had not answered; his wife said: "Your lordship is in a great province and does not know who can live or die with you; go and you still will not escape."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi hesitated; his wife said, "You command a great province yet do not know who would die with you—even flight will not save you."

manualTranslations.zh: 翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi said: "The two sons are small; I will not go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi said, "My two sons are small; I will not flee.

manualTranslations.zh: 今但從坐，身死，二兒必免。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now if I merely suffer joint punishment, though my person dies, the two sons are sure to be spared."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I accept joint punishment, my sons will be spared."

manualTranslations.zh: 果如翼言。
manualTranslations.literal: It turned out as Yi had said.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It happened as Yi predicted.

manualTranslations.zh: 翼子斌，楊駿外甥也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi's son Bin was nephew by marriage to Yang Jun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi's son Bin was Yang Jun's nephew by marriage.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉惠帝初，爲河南尹，與駿俱死，見晉書。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Hui of Jin he was governor of Henan and died together with Jun—see the Book of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin he was governor of Henan and died with Yang Jun—see the Jin shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 事下有司，收玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢等送廷尉。
manualTranslations.literal: The affair was handed to the responsible office; Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, Xian, and others were seized and sent to the commandant of justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The case went to the courts; Xuan, Ji, Shuo, Dun, Xian, and others were sent to the commandant of justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：玄至廷尉，不肯下辭。
manualTranslations.literal: The Worldly Talk states: When Xuan reached the commandant of justice, he refused to submit a confession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Xuan at the commandant of justice refused to confess.

manualTranslations.zh: 廷尉鍾毓自臨治玄。
manualTranslations.literal: Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu himself came to try Xuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu personally tried him.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何辭？
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan with stern countenance reproached Yu, saying: "What confession ought I to make?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan rebuked him: "What confession should I make?

manualTranslations.zh: 卿爲令史責人也，卿便爲吾作。」
manualTranslations.literal: You are a clerk rebuking a man; you just write it for me."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You are a clerk judging a man—write it yourself."

manualTranslations.zh: 毓以其名士，節高不可屈，而獄當竟，夜爲作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu, because he was a famous gentleman whose integrity was high and could not be bent, yet the case was near its end, at night composed the confession, making it attach to the affair, and with tears showed it to Xuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu, knowing Xuan's unbending dignity yet needing to close the case, composed the confession by night, weeping as he showed it to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄視，頷之而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan looked, and merely nodded—that was all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan looked and merely nodded.

manualTranslations.zh: 毓弟會，年少於玄，玄不與交，是日於毓坐狎玄，玄不受。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu's younger brother Hui was younger than Xuan; Xuan did not associate with him; that day at Yu's seat he familiarly pressed Xuan; Xuan did not accept.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Hui, younger than Xuan and not his friend, tried that day at Yu's seat to be familiar; Xuan refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫盛雜語曰：玄在囹圄，會因欲狎而友玄，玄正色曰：「鍾君何相偪如此也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Sheng's Miscellaneous Sayings states: Xuan in prison; Hui thereupon wished to be familiar and befriend Xuan; Xuan with stern countenance said: "Lord Zhong, why press me so!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's zayu says Hui in prison tried to befriend Xuan, who answered coldly, "Lord Zhong, why press me so?"

manualTranslations.zh: 廷尉鍾毓奏：「豐等謀迫脅至尊，擅誅冢宰，大逆無道，請論如法。」
manualTranslations.literal: Commandant of Justice Zhong Yu memorialized: "Feng and others plotted to coerce and threaten the supreme lord, executed the chief minister on their own authority, great rebellion without the Way—request judgment according to law."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu memorialized that Feng and the rest had plotted to coerce the emperor and murder the chief minister without authority—great treason warranting legal judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是會公卿朝臣廷尉議，咸以爲「豐等各受殊寵，典綜機密，緝承外戚椒房之尊，玄備世臣，並居列位，而苞藏禍心，構圖凶逆，交關閹豎，授以姦計，畏憚天威，不敢顯謀，乃欲要君脅上，肆其詐虐，謀誅良輔，擅相建立，將以傾覆京室，顛危社稷。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the assembled dukes, ministers, court officials, and commandant of justice deliberated; all held that "Feng and the others each received special favor, controlled confidential affairs comprehensively; Ji inherited the empress's father's pepper-room honor; Xuan was equipped as a minister of generations, all occupying ranks and posts, yet harbored treacherous hearts, plotted wicked rebellion, associated with eunuch attendants, entrusted with wicked plans, feared Heaven's majesty, dared not plot openly, and therefore wished to coerce the ruler and threaten the sovereign, unleash their fraud and cruelty, plot to execute good assistants, establish others on their own authority, and thereby overturn the capital house and endanger the altars of soil and grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers agreed that Feng and the rest, favored confidants and imperial in-laws, had harbored treason, used eunuchs, and sought to coerce the throne and overturn the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 毓所正皆如科律，報毓施行」。
manualTranslations.literal: What Yu corrected all accorded with statute law; report Yu to carry out."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu's findings matched the statutes; let them be executed."

manualTranslations.zh: 詔書：「齊長公主，先帝遺愛，匄其三子死命。」
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said: "The Princess of Qi the Long, the late emperor's beloved—beg three sons' lives."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict pleaded: "The Princess of Qi the Long was the late emperor's beloved—spare her three sons."

manualTranslations.zh: 於是豐、玄、緝、敦、賢等皆夷三族，《魏書》曰：豐子韜，以尚主，賜死獄中。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Feng, Xuan, Ji, Dun, Xian, and others were all exterminated to the third degree; the Book of Wei states: Feng's son Tao, because he had married a princess, was granted death in prison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Feng, Xuan, Ji, Dun, and Xian were exterminated to the third degree; the Book of Wei adds that Tao, as imperial son-in-law, was granted death in prison.

manualTranslations.zh: 其餘親屬徙樂浪郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The rest of the kin were moved to Lelang commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Other kin were exiled to Lelang.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄格量弘濟，臨斬東巿，顏色不變，舉動自若，時年四十六。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan's measure was broad and sustaining; facing execution at the eastern market, his color did not change and his bearing was as usual; at the time he was forty-six.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan met execution at the eastern market with unchanged color and composed bearing; he was forty-six.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：玄自從西還，不交人事，不蓄華妍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Summary states: From the time Xuan returned from the west he did not engage in human affairs and did not store splendor or beauty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says that after returning from the west Xuan withdrew from public life and kept no luxuries.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：初，夏侯霸將奔蜀，呼玄欲與之俱。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: At first when Xiahou Ba was about to flee to Shu, he called Xuan wishing to go with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu says when Xiahou Ba prepared to flee to Shu he called Xuan to come along.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄曰：「吾豈苟存自客於寇虜乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan said: "How could I basely preserve myself and be a guest among bandit enemies?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "How could I basely save myself by lodging with bandits?"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂還京師。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he returned to the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅薨，許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Tutor died, Xu Yun said to Xuan: "No more worries."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Grand Tutor died, Xu Yun told Xuan, "You need worry no more."

manualTranslations.zh: 玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan sighed and said: "Shizong, why do you not see how things stand?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan sighed: "Shizong, can you not read the times?

manualTranslations.zh: 此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。」
manualTranslations.literal: This man could still treat me as a young man of a connected house; Ziyuan and Zishang will not spare me."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He still treated me as a family friend's son; Ziyuan and Zishang will not spare me."

manualTranslations.zh: 玄嘗著樂毅、張良及本無肉刑論，辭旨通遠，咸傳於世。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan once composed treatises on Yue Yi, Zhang Liang, and on abolishing corporal punishment; their wording and intent were penetrating and far-reaching, all transmitted in the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote treatises on Yue Yi, Zhang Liang, and abolishing corporal punishment that circulated widely.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄之執也，衞將軍司馬文王流涕請之，大將軍曰：「卿忘會趙司空葬乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: When Xuan was seized, General of the Guard Sima Zhao wept and begged for him; the grand general said: "Have you forgotten meeting at Minister of Works Zhao Yan's funeral?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xuan was arrested, Sima Zhao wept and begged for him; the grand general said, "Have you forgotten Minister of Works Zhao Yan's funeral?"

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，司空趙儼薨，大將軍兄弟會葬，賔客以百數，玄時後至，衆賔客咸越席而迎，大將軍由是惡之。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Works Zhao Yan died; the grand general brothers met at the funeral; guests numbered in the hundreds; Xuan at that time arrived later; all the guests alike rose from their mats to welcome him—the grand general on this account hated him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier at Zhao Yan's funeral the Sima brothers saw every guest rise to welcome the late-arriving Xuan—hence their hatred.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：曹爽以正始五年244年伐蜀，時玄已爲關中都督，至十年，爽誅滅後，方還洛耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Commentator Pei Songzhi notes: Cao Shuang in the fifth year of Zhengshi (244) campaigned against Shu; at that time Xuan was already metropolitan protector of Guanzhong; only in the tenth year, after Shuang was destroyed and executed, did he return to Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: Cao Shuang invaded Shu in Zhengshi 5 (244), when Xuan was already metropolitan protector of Guanzhong; he returned to Luoyang only after Shuang's fall in the tenth year.

manualTranslations.zh: 案少帝紀，司空趙儼以六年亡，玄則無由得會儼葬，若云玄入朝，紀、傳又無其事。
manualTranslations.literal: According to the Annals of the Lesser Emperor, Minister of Works Zhao Yan died in the sixth year; Xuan then had no way to meet Yan's funeral; if one says Xuan entered court, the annals and biography again have no such affair.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The annals place Zhao Yan's death in the sixth year, so Xuan could not have attended his funeral; nor do annals or biography record such a court appearance.

manualTranslations.zh: 斯近妄不實。
manualTranslations.literal: This is near to reckless untruth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The story is nearly certainly false.

manualTranslations.zh: 正元中，紹功臣世，封尚從孫本爲昌陵亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉尚後。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Zhengyuan era the meritorious ministers' lines were continued; Shang's collateral descendant Ben was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changling, fief three hundred households, to continue Shang's line.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Zhengyuan era Shang's collateral descendant Ben was enfeoffed village marquis of Changling with three hundred households to continue Shang's sacrifices.

sourceRange.text: 獻帝紀曰：後以煨爲大鴻臚光祿大夫，，以壽終。

localRange.text: 獻帝紀曰：後以煨爲大鴻臚光祿大夫，建安十四年，以壽終。

context.beforeSource: 天子東還，煨迎道貢遺周急。
context.afterSource: 與詡同郡，遂去傕託煨。
context.beforeLocal: 天子東還，煨迎道貢遺周急。
context.afterLocal: 與詡同郡，遂去傕託煨。

sourceRange.text: 十七年，董昭等謂太祖宜進爵國公，九錫備物，以彰殊勳，密以諮彧。彧以爲太祖本興義兵以匡朝寧國，秉忠貞之誠，守退讓之實；君子愛人以德，不宜如此。太祖由是心不能平。會征孫權，表請彧勞軍于譙，因輒留彧，以侍中光祿大夫持節，參丞相軍事。太祖軍至濡須，彧疾留壽春，以憂薨，時年五十。諡曰敬侯。明年，太祖遂爲魏公矣。《魏氏春秋》曰：太祖饋彧食，發之乃空器也，於是飲藥而卒。咸熙二年，贈彧太尉。《彧別傳》曰：彧自爲尚書令，常以書陳事，臨薨，皆焚毀之，故奇策密謀不得盡聞也。是時征役草創，制度多所興復，彧嘗言於太祖曰：「昔舜分命禹、稷、契、皐陶以揆庶績，教化征伐，並時而用。及髙祖之初，金革方殷，猶舉民能善教訓者，叔孫通習禮儀於戎旅之閒，世祖有投戈講藝、息馬論道之事，君子無終食之閒違仁。今公外定武功，内興文學，使干戈戢睦，大道流行，國難方弭，六禮倶治，此姬旦宰周之所以速平也。旣立德立功，而又兼立言，成仲尼述作之意；顯制度於當時，揚名於後世，豈不盛哉！若須武事畢而後制作，以稽治化，於事未敏。宜集天下大才通儒，考論六經，刊定傳記，存古今之學，除其煩重，以一聖眞，並隆禮學，漸敦教化，則王道兩濟。」彧從容與太祖論治道，如此之類甚衆，太祖常嘉納之。彧德行周備，非正道不用心，名重天下，莫不以爲儀表，海内英儁咸宗焉。司馬宣王常稱書傳遠事，吾自耳目所從聞見，逮百數十年間，賢才未有及荀令君者也。前後所舉者，命世大才，邦邑則荀攸、鍾繇、陳羣，海内則司馬宣王，及引致當世知名郗慮、華歆、王朗、荀恱、杜襲、辛毗、趙儼之儔，終爲卿相，以十數人。取士不以一揆，戲志才、郭嘉等有負俗之譏，杜畿簡傲少文，皆以智策舉之，終各顯名。荀攸後爲魏尚書令，亦推賢進士。太祖曰：「二荀令之論人，久而益信，吾沒世不忘。」鍾繇以爲顏子旣沒，能備九德，不貳其過，唯荀彧然。或問繇曰：「君雅重荀君，比之顏子，自以不及，可得聞乎？」曰：「夫明君師臣，其次友之。以太祖之聦明，毎有大事，常先諮之荀君，是則古師友之義也。吾等受命而行，猶或不盡，相去顧不遠邪！」《獻帝春秋》曰：董承之誅，伏后與父完書，言司空殺董承，帝方爲報怨。完得書以示彧，彧惡之，久隱而不言。完以示妻弟樊普，普封以呈太祖，太祖陰爲之備。彧後恐事覺，欲自發之，因求使至鄴，勸太祖以女配帝。太祖曰：「今朝廷有伏后，吾女何得以配上，吾以微功見録，位爲宰相，豈復賴女寵乎！」彧曰：「伏后無子，性又凶邪，往常與父書，言辭醜惡，可因此廢也。」太祖曰：「卿昔何不道之？」彧陽驚曰：「昔已嘗爲公言也。」太祖曰：「此豈小事而吾忘之！」彧又驚曰：「誠未語公邪！昔公在官渡與袁紹相持，恐增内顧之念，故不言爾。」太祖曰：「官渡事後何以不言？」彧無對，謝闕而已。太祖以此恨彧，而外含容之，故世莫得知。至董昭建立魏公之議，彧意不同，欲言之於太祖。及齎璽書犒軍，飲饗禮畢，彧留請閒。太祖知彧欲言封事，揖而遣之，彧遂不得言。彧卒於壽春，壽春亡者告孫權，言太祖使彧殺伏后，彧不從，故自殺。權以露布於蜀，劉備聞之，曰：「老賊不死，禍亂未已。」臣松之案《獻帝春秋》云彧欲發伏后事而求使至鄴，而方誣太祖云「昔已嘗言」。言旣無徴，迴託以官渡之虞，俛仰之間，辭情頓屈，雖在庸人，猶不至此，何以玷累賢哲哉！凡諸云云，皆出自鄙俚，可謂以吾儕之言而厚誣君子者矣。袁暐虚罔之類，此最爲甚也。子惲，嗣侯，官至虎賁中郎將。初，文帝與平原侯植並有擬論，文帝曲禮事彧。及彧卒，惲又與植善，而與夏侯尚不穆，文帝深恨惲。惲早卒，子甝、霬，音翼。以外甥故猶寵待。惲弟俁，御史中丞，俁弟詵，大將軍從事中郎，皆知名，早卒。《荀氏家傳》曰：惲字長倩，俁字叔倩，詵字曼倩，俁子寓，字景伯。《世語》曰：寓少與裴楷、王戎、杜默倶有名京邑，仕晉，位至尚書，名見顯著。子羽嗣，位至尚書。詵弟顗，咸熙中爲司空。《晉陽秋》曰：顗字景倩，幼爲姊夫陳羣所異。博學洽聞，意思愼密。司馬宣王見顗，奇之，曰：「荀令君之子也。近見袁偘，亦曜卿之子也。」擢拜散騎侍郎。顗佐命晉室，位至太尉，封臨淮康公。嘗難鍾會「易無互體」，見稱於世。顗弟粲，字奉倩。何劭爲粲傳曰：粲字奉倩，粲諸兄並以儒術論議，而粲獨好言道，常以爲子貢稱夫子之言性與天道，不可得聞，然則六籍雖存，固聖人之糠粃。粲兄俁難曰：「易亦云聖人立象以盡意，繫辭焉以盡言，則微言胡爲不可得而聞見哉？」粲荅曰：「蓋理之微者，非物象之所舉也。今稱立象以盡意，此非通于意外者也。繫辭焉以盡言，此非言乎繫表者也；斯則象外之意，繫表之言，固蘊而不出矣。」及當時能言者不能屈也。又論父彧不如從兄攸。彧立德髙整，軌儀以訓物，而攸不治外形，愼密自居而已。粲以此言善攸，諸兄怒而不能迴也。太和初，到京邑與傅嘏談。嘏善名理而粲尚玄遠，宗致雖同，倉卒時或有格而不相得意。裴徽通彼我之懷，爲二家騎驛，頃之，粲與嘏善。夏侯玄亦親。常謂嘏、玄曰：「子等在世塗間，功名必勝我，但識劣我耳！」嘏難曰：「能盛功名者，識也。天下孰有本不足而末有餘者邪？」粲曰：「功名者，志局之所獎也。然則志局自一物耳，固非識之所獨濟也。我以能使子等爲貴，然未必齊子等所爲也。」粲常以婦人者，才智不足論，自宜以色爲主。驃騎將軍曹洪女有美色，粲於是娉焉，容服帷帳甚麗，專房歡宴。歴年後，婦病亡，未殯，傅嘏往喭粲；粲不哭而神傷。嘏問曰：「婦人才色並茂爲難。子之娶也，遺才而好色。此自易遇，今何哀之甚？」粲曰：「佳人難再得！顧逝者不能有傾國之色，然未可謂之易遇。」痛悼不能已，歳餘亦亡，時年二十九。粲簡貴，不能與常人交接，所交皆一時俊傑。至葬夕，赴者裁十餘人，皆同時知名士也，哭之，感慟路人。惲子甝，嗣爲散騎常侍，進爵廣陽鄕侯，年三十薨。子頵嗣。《荀氏家傳》曰：頵字温伯，爲羽林右監，早卒。頵子崧，字景猷。《晉陽秋》稱崧少有志操，雅好文學，孝義和愛，在朝恪勤，位至左右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。崧子羨，字令則，淸和有才。尚公主，少歴顯位，年二十八爲北中郎將，徐、兖二州刺史，假節都督徐、兖、靑三州諸軍事。在任十年，遇疾解職，卒於家，追贈驃騎將軍。羨孫伯子，今御史中丞也。霬官至中領軍，薨，諡曰貞侯，追贈驃騎將軍。子愷嗣。霬妻，司馬景王、文王之妹也，二王皆與親善。咸熙中，開建五等，霬以著勳前朝，改封愷南頓子。《荀氏家傳》曰：愷，晉武帝時爲侍中。干寶《晉紀》曰：武帝使侍中荀顗、和嶠倶至東宮，觀察太子。顗還稱太子德識進茂，而嶠云聖質如初。孫盛曰「遣荀勗」，其餘語則同。臣松之案和嶠爲侍中，荀顗亡沒久矣。荀勗位亞台司，不與嶠同班，無縁方稱侍中。二書所云，皆爲非也。考其時位，愷寔當之。愷位至征西大將軍。愷兄憺，少府。弟悝，護軍將軍，追贈車騎大將軍。
