manualTranslations.zh: 十七年，董昭等謂太祖宜進爵國公，九錫備物，以彰殊勳，密以諮彧。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Dong Zhao and others said the Grand Progenitor should be advanced to the rank of Duke of a State, with the nine bestowals and all their appurtenances, to manifest extraordinary merit, and secretly consulted Yu about it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Dong Zhao and others urged that the Grand Progenitor be raised to Duke of a State with the full nine bestowals to honor his exceptional achievements, and they quietly sought Yu's counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧以爲太祖本興義兵以匡朝寧國，秉忠貞之誠，守退讓之實；
manualTranslations.literal: Yu believed that the Grand Progenitor had originally raised righteous troops to rectify the court and pacify the state, holding to the sincerity of loyalty and steadfastness, and keeping to the reality of yielding and modesty;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu held that the Grand Progenitor had originally raised righteous armies to restore the dynasty and pacify the realm, maintaining loyal integrity and the virtue of modest restraint;

manualTranslations.zh: 君子愛人以德，不宜如此。
manualTranslations.literal: A gentleman loves others through virtue; it is not fitting to act thus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A gentleman shows care for others through virtue — such a course was inappropriate.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖由是心不能平。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of this, the Grand Progenitor's heart could not be at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor consequently took this badly at heart.

manualTranslations.zh: 會征孫權，表請彧勞軍于譙，因輒留彧，以侍中光祿大夫持節，參丞相軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that when campaigning against Sun Quan, he memorialized requesting that Yu encourage the troops at Qiao, and on this pretext detained Yu, appointing him Palace Attendant and Household Counsellor bearing credentials of authority, to participate in military affairs of the Chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Sun Quan, he petitioned to have Yu encourage the troops at Qiao, then kept him there — appointing him Palace Attendant and Household Counsellor with credentials of authority to assist the Chancellor in military affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖軍至濡須，彧疾留壽春，以憂薨，時年五十。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor's army reached Ruxu, Yu fell ill and remained at Shouchun; he died of grief, aged fifty at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Grand Progenitor's army reached Ruxu, Yu fell ill and remained at Shouchun, where he died of grief at the age of fifty.

manualTranslations.zh: 諡曰敬侯。
manualTranslations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Marquis Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，太祖遂爲魏公矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year, the Grand Progenitor then became Duke of Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following year, the Grand Progenitor became Duke of Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：太祖饋彧食，發之乃空器也，於是飲藥而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: The Grand Progenitor sent Yu food; when he opened it, it was an empty vessel; whereupon he drank medicine and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wei Clan Annals says that the Grand Progenitor sent Yu food, but when he opened it, the container was empty — whereupon Yu drank poison and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熙二年，贈彧太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Xianxi, Yu was posthumously granted the office of Grand Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianxi, Yu was posthumously awarded the rank of Grand Commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 《彧別傳》曰：彧自爲尚書令，常以書陳事，臨薨，皆焚毀之，故奇策密謀不得盡聞也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Separate Biography of Yu states: From the time Yu served as Director of the Masters of Writing, he often submitted affairs in written memorials; on the verge of death, he burned and destroyed them all; therefore extraordinary plans and secret stratagems could not be fully heard of.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Separate Biography of Yu records that from his time as Director of the Masters of Writing, he habitually submitted affairs in writing; on his deathbed he burned them all, so his most ingenious strategies were never fully known.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時征役草創，制度多所興復，彧嘗言於太祖曰：「昔舜分命禹、稷、契、皐陶以揆庶績，教化征伐，並時而用。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time military campaigns and corvée labor were in their initial stages, and institutions were being widely revived; Yu once said to the Grand Progenitor: "In ancient times Shun separately appointed Yu, Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao to oversee the multitude of achievements; civilizing instruction and military expeditions were employed simultaneously."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time campaigns and corvée were still being organized and many institutions were being revived. Yu once told the Grand Progenitor: "Long ago, Shun separately charged Yu, Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao with governing the people's affairs — civilizing instruction and military campaigns were pursued at the same time."

manualTranslations.zh: 及髙祖之初，金革方殷，猶舉民能善教訓者，叔孫通習禮儀於戎旅之閒，世祖有投戈講藝、息馬論道之事，君子無終食之閒違仁。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of the High Ancestor's reign, the clash of arms and armor was still intense, yet he still elevated those among the people able to teach and instruct well; Shusun Tong became versed in ritual propriety amid military camps; the World Ancestor had occasions for casting aside weapons to lecture on the arts and resting horses to discuss the Way; a gentleman has not even the interval of a single meal in which to depart from benevolence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even at the beginning of the Han, when warfare was still fierce, the court still sought out men capable of teaching and instruction — Shusun Tong mastered ritual amid military encampments, and Emperor Guangwu set aside arms to lecture on the classics and rested horses to discuss the Way. A gentleman does not neglect benevolence even for the span of a single meal."

manualTranslations.zh: 今公外定武功，内興文學，使干戈戢睦，大道流行，國難方弭，六禮倶治，此姬旦宰周之所以速平也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now my lord outwardly settles martial achievements and inwardly raises literary studies, causing weapons and armor to be laid aside in peace, the Great Way to spread, national troubles just to be quelled, and the six rites all to be governed — this is why the Duke of Zhou governed Zhou and brought rapid peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Now you have subdued the realm by force abroad and are fostering scholarship at home — weapons are being laid aside, the Great Way spreads, national crisis is being resolved, and the six rites are being restored. This is how the Duke of Zhou governed Zhou and brought peace so swiftly."

manualTranslations.zh: 旣立德立功，而又兼立言，成仲尼述作之意；
manualTranslations.literal: Having already established virtue and established merit, and furthermore also establishing words, fulfilling the intent of Zhongni's compositions;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "You have established virtue and merit, and by adding literary achievement you fulfill Confucius's purpose in his writings;

manualTranslations.zh: 顯制度於當時，揚名於後世，豈不盛哉！
manualTranslations.literal: displaying institutions in the present age, spreading one's fame in later generations — how could it not be magnificent!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: making your institutions manifest in your own age and your fame endure for posterity — what could be more splendid!"

manualTranslations.zh: 若須武事畢而後制作，以稽治化，於事未敏。
manualTranslations.literal: If one must wait until military affairs are concluded before then undertaking cultural creation, in order to examine governance and transformation, in affairs this lacks keenness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "If you wait until all military matters are finished before turning to cultural institutions in order to examine governance and transformation, you will have been too slow."

manualTranslations.zh: 宜集天下大才通儒，考論六經，刊定傳記，存古今之學，除其煩重，以一聖眞，並隆禮學，漸敦教化，則王道兩濟。」
manualTranslations.literal: It would be fitting to gather the great talents and thoroughly learned Confucians of the empire, examine and discuss the Six Classics, edit and fix the commentarial traditions, preserve the learning of past and present, remove what is cumbersome and redundant, unite them in the one true teaching of the sage, and together elevate the study of ritual, gradually thickening civilizing instruction — then the royal Way would be served on both sides."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "You should assemble the empire's greatest scholars and Confucian experts to examine and discuss the Six Classics, standardize the commentarial traditions, preserve learning ancient and modern while eliminating what is redundant, unify them around the sage's true teaching, and together elevate ritual learning to gradually deepen civilizing instruction — then the royal Way will be fully realized on both fronts."

manualTranslations.zh: 彧從容與太祖論治道，如此之類甚衆，太祖常嘉納之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu calmly discussed principles of governance with the Grand Progenitor; matters of this sort were very numerous; the Grand Progenitor often commended and accepted them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu often discussed principles of governance with the Grand Progenitor in an unhurried manner; the Grand Progenitor frequently approved and adopted his counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧德行周備，非正道不用心，名重天下，莫不以爲儀表，海内英儁咸宗焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu's virtue and conduct were comprehensive and complete; he would not apply his mind except to the correct Way; his renown weighed heavily throughout the realm; none did not regard him as a model; eminent talents within the seas all looked up to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu's virtue and conduct were complete in every respect; he devoted himself only to the right path. His fame resounded throughout the realm, and all regarded him as a model — the most distinguished men in the land looked up to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 司馬宣王常稱書傳遠事，吾自耳目所從聞見，逮百數十年間，賢才未有及荀令君者也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord of Xuan, Sima Yi, often said: "In what is recorded in books and transmitted from distant events, and in what I myself have heard and seen from my own eyes and ears, spanning a hundred and some decades, there has been no talented man who could match Director Xun."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Lord of Xuan (Sima Yi) often said: "In historical records and in what I myself have witnessed over more than a hundred years, I have seen no talent to equal Director Xun."

manualTranslations.zh: 前後所舉者，命世大才，邦邑則荀攸、鍾繇、陳羣，海内則司馬宣王，及引致當世知名郗慮、華歆、王朗、荀恱、杜襲、辛毗、趙儼之儔，終爲卿相，以十數人。
manualTranslations.literal: Those he recommended before and after were world-shaking great talents: within his native region, Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Chen Qun; within the seas, the Lord of Xuan; and he also brought in the well-known men of the age, Xi Lu, Hua Xin, Wang Lang, Xun Yue, Du Xi, Xin Pi, Zhao Yan, and the like — who in the end became ministers and chancellors, numbering more than a dozen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those he recommended over the years were truly exceptional talents: Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Chen Qun from his home region; the Lord of Xuan from across the realm; and he also recruited such celebrated figures as Xi Lu, Hua Xin, Wang Lang, Xun Yue, Du Xi, Xin Pi, and Zhao Yan — more than a dozen in all who rose to ministerial rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 取士不以一揆，戲志才、郭嘉等有負俗之譏，杜畿簡傲少文，皆以智策舉之，終各顯名。
manualTranslations.literal: In selecting scholars he did not use a single standard; Xi Zhicai and Guo Jia and others bore criticisms for violating custom; Du Ji was frugal, proud, and lacking in refinement — all were recommended through their strategic intelligence, and in the end each achieved distinguished fame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He did not select men by a single standard: Xi Zhicai and Guo Jia had reputations for violating convention, and Du Ji was austere, proud, and unpolished — yet he recommended all of them for their strategic brilliance, and each rose to prominence.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀攸後爲魏尚書令，亦推賢進士。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun You later served as Director of the Masters of Writing for Wei and also promoted worthy men and advanced scholars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun You later served as Wei Director of the Masters of Writing and likewise promoted worthy talents.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「二荀令之論人，久而益信，吾沒世不忘。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "The two Directors Xun's judgments of men, the longer they stand the more trustworthy they prove — I shall not forget them while I live."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said: "The two Directors Xun judged men so well that time only confirms their judgment — I shall never forget it."

manualTranslations.zh: 鍾繇以爲顏子旣沒，能備九德，不貳其過，唯荀彧然。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong Yao held that since Yanzi died, only Xun Yu could possess all nine virtues and not stray from his errors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao believed that since Yan Hui's death, only Xun Yu had possessed all nine virtues without wavering from his principles.

manualTranslations.zh: 或問繇曰：「君雅重荀君，比之顏子，自以不及，可得聞乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Someone asked Yao: "You greatly esteem Lord Xun, comparing him to Yanzi, yet consider yourself unequal — may we hear your reasons?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Someone asked Zhong Yao: "You greatly esteem Lord Xun and compare him to Yan Hui, yet say you cannot match him — may we hear why?"

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：「夫明君師臣，其次友之。
manualTranslations.literal: He said: "An enlightened lord treats his minister as a teacher, or at least as a friend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He replied: "An enlightened lord treats his minister as a teacher, or at least as a friend.

manualTranslations.zh: 以太祖之聦明，毎有大事，常先諮之荀君，是則古師友之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: With the Grand Progenitor's brilliance, whenever there was a major affair, he would always first consult Lord Xun — this is the ancient meaning of teacher and friend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Given the Grand Progenitor's brilliance, whenever a major matter arose he always consulted Lord Xun first — that is the ancient ideal of a teacher-friend relationship.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾等受命而行，猶或不盡，相去顧不遠邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: We receive orders and carry them out, yet still sometimes fall short — the distance between us, does it not seem not far!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We merely receive orders and carry them out, and even then we sometimes fall short — are we not rather close to each other in standing!"

manualTranslations.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：董承之誅，伏后與父完書，言司空殺董承，帝方爲報怨。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian states: After Dong Cheng's execution, Empress Fu wrote to her father Wan, saying the Minister of Works had killed Dong Cheng and the Emperor was now seeking revenge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian records that after Dong Cheng's execution, Empress Fu wrote to her father Fu Wan, saying the Minister of Works had killed Dong Cheng and the Emperor was now bent on revenge.

manualTranslations.zh: 完得書以示彧，彧惡之，久隱而不言。
manualTranslations.literal: Wan received the letter and showed it to Yu; Yu hated it and for a long time concealed it without speaking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Wan received the letter and showed it to Yu; Yu was appalled but kept silent about it for a long time.

manualTranslations.zh: 完以示妻弟樊普，普封以呈太祖，太祖陰爲之備。
manualTranslations.literal: Wan showed it to his wife's younger brother Fan Pu; Pu sealed it and presented it to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor secretly made preparations on account of it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Wan showed it to his wife's younger brother Fan Pu, who sealed it and presented it to the Grand Progenitor; Cao Cao secretly began to prepare against the threat.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧後恐事覺，欲自發之，因求使至鄴，勸太祖以女配帝。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu later feared the matter would be discovered and wished to expose it himself; he therefore requested to be sent as envoy to Ye, and urged the Grand Progenitor to marry his daughter to the Emperor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu later feared discovery and wished to expose the matter himself; he requested permission to go to Ye as envoy and urged the Grand Progenitor to marry his daughter to the Emperor.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「今朝廷有伏后，吾女何得以配上，吾以微功見録，位爲宰相，豈復賴女寵乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Now the court has Empress Fu — how could my daughter be matched to ascend the throne? I was recorded for minor achievements and occupy the post of chancellor — would I still depend on my daughter's favor!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said: "The court already has Empress Fu — how can my daughter be made empress? I rose to the chancellorship on modest merit alone — must I rely on my daughter's favor now?"

manualTranslations.zh: 彧曰：「伏后無子，性又凶邪，往常與父書，言辭醜惡，可因此廢也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yu said: "Empress Fu has no son, and her nature is also fierce and wicked; she often wrote to her father with ugly and vile language — she can be deposed on this account."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Empress Fu has no children, and her nature is vicious and depraved. Her letters to her father were full of ugly and vile language — she can be deposed on that basis."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「卿昔何不道之？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why did you not speak of this before?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why didn't you tell me this before?"

manualTranslations.zh: 彧陽驚曰：「昔已嘗爲公言也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yu feigned surprise and said: "In the past I had already spoken to you about it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu feigned surprise and said: "I already told you about it long ago."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「此豈小事而吾忘之！」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "How could this be a minor matter and I have forgotten it!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said: "This is hardly a trifling matter — how could I have forgotten it!"

manualTranslations.zh: 彧又驚曰：「誠未語公邪！
manualTranslations.literal: Yu was surprised again and said: "Truly I did not tell you, my lord!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu feigned surprise again: "Truly I never told you, my lord!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔公在官渡與袁紹相持，恐增内顧之念，故不言爾。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the past when you were at Guandu locked in stalemate with Yuan Shao, I feared increasing thoughts of looking back within — therefore I did not speak of it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When you were at Guandu in stalemate with Yuan Shao, I feared it would distract you with domestic worries, so I said nothing."

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖曰：「官渡事後何以不言？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "After the affair at Guandu, why did you not speak?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why didn't you speak after Guandu?"

manualTranslations.zh: 彧無對，謝闕而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu had no reply; he merely apologized for his lapse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu had no answer and could only apologize for his failure.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖以此恨彧，而外含容之，故世莫得知。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor on this account bore resentment toward Yu, yet outwardly tolerated him; therefore the world did not know of it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor harbored resentment over this but concealed it outwardly, so the world never knew.

manualTranslations.zh: 至董昭建立魏公之議，彧意不同，欲言之於太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: When it came to Dong Zhao's proposal to establish the Grand Progenitor as Duke of Wei, Yu's view differed; he wished to speak of it to the Grand Progenitor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhao proposed establishing the Duke of Wei, Yu disagreed and wished to speak to the Grand Progenitor about it.

manualTranslations.zh: 及齎璽書犒軍，飲饗禮畢，彧留請閒。
manualTranslations.literal: When he brought the imperial edict written on jade to reward the troops and the banquet rites were concluded, Yu remained to request a private audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived bearing the imperial edict to reward the troops and the banquet concluded, he stayed behind to request a private audience.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖知彧欲言封事，揖而遣之，彧遂不得言。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Progenitor knew Yu wished to speak about the enfeoffment matter; he bowed and dismissed him; Yu thus could not speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor knew Yu wanted to discuss the enfeoffment; he bowed and dismissed him, and Yu never got to speak.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧卒於壽春，壽春亡者告孫權，言太祖使彧殺伏后，彧不從，故自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu died at Shouchun; a refugee from Shouchun informed Sun Quan, saying the Grand Progenitor had ordered Yu to kill Empress Fu and Yu refused, therefore killing himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yu died at Shouchun, a refugee from that city told Sun Quan that the Grand Progenitor had ordered Yu to kill Empress Fu, that Yu refused, and therefore killed himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 權以露布於蜀，劉備聞之，曰：「老賊不死，禍亂未已。」
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan broadcast this by open proclamation to Shu; when Liu Bei heard it, he said: "The old villain does not die — calamity and disorder are not yet ended."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan publicized this account to Shu; when Liu Bei heard it, he said: "That old villain is not dead — the turmoil is far from over."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案《獻帝春秋》云彧欲發伏后事而求使至鄴，而方誣太祖云「昔已嘗言」。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian says that Yu wished to expose the Empress Fu matter and therefore requested to be sent to Ye, yet then falsely accused the Grand Progenitor, saying "I had already spoken before."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian says Yu wished to expose the Empress Fu affair and sought an envoy mission to Ye, yet then falsely told the Grand Progenitor "I had already told you."

manualTranslations.zh: 言旣無徴，迴託以官渡之虞，俛仰之間，辭情頓屈，雖在庸人，猶不至此，何以玷累賢哲哉！
manualTranslations.literal: The words had no evidence; he then turned and excused himself with the worry at Guandu; in the lowering and raising of his head, his words and feelings suddenly collapsed — even among ordinary men, it would not reach this point; how could it stain and burden a worthy sage!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His claim had no basis; he then pivoted to the excuse of Guandu — and in that exchange his argument collapsed utterly. Even an ordinary man would not behave so — how could such conduct be imputed to a worthy sage!

manualTranslations.zh: 凡諸云云，皆出自鄙俚，可謂以吾儕之言而厚誣君子者矣。
manualTranslations.literal: All such talk in every case originates from vulgar folk; it may be said to use words of people like us to falsely and heavily accuse a gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All such accounts come from vulgar sources — they use the words of common folk to slander a gentleman most unjustly.

manualTranslations.zh: 袁暐虚罔之類，此最爲甚也。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the false and groundless sorts like Yuan Hui, this is the most extreme.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among fabricators like Yuan Hui, this case is the worst.

manualTranslations.zh: 子惲，嗣侯，官至虎賁中郎將。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Yun succeeded to the marquisate and reached the office of Tiger Guard Commander of the Central.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded to the marquisate and rose to Tiger Guard Commander of the Central.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，文帝與平原侯植並有擬論，文帝曲禮事彧。
manualTranslations.literal: Initially, Emperor Wen and the Marquis of Pingyuan Zhi both had aspirations to succession; Emperor Wen bent to courtesy in serving Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early on, both Emperor Wen and the Marquis of Pingyuan (Cao Zhi) were contenders for succession; Emperor Wen treated Yu with especial courtesy.

manualTranslations.zh: 及彧卒，惲又與植善，而與夏侯尚不穆，文帝深恨惲。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yu died, Yun was again on good terms with Zhi, yet was not harmonious with Xiahou Shang; Emperor Wen deeply resented Yun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Yu's death, Yun remained friendly with Cao Zhi but was on bad terms with Xiahou Shang; Emperor Wen deeply resented him.

manualTranslations.zh: 惲早卒，子甝、霬，音翼。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun died young; his sons Kan and Hui — Hui is pronounced Yi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yun died young, leaving sons Kan and Hui (the latter pronounced Yi).

manualTranslations.zh: 以外甥故猶寵待。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of the connection as nephew by marriage, he was still treated with favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of the family connection by marriage, they were still treated with favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 惲弟俁，御史中丞，俁弟詵，大將軍從事中郎，皆知名，早卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun's younger brother Hou was Censor-in-Chief; Hou's younger brother Shen was Staff Officer to the General-in-Chief — all were well known and died young.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Hou served as Censor-in-Chief; Hou's younger brother Shen served as Staff Officer to the General-in-Chief — all were well known and died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：惲字長倩，俁字叔倩，詵字曼倩，俁子寓，字景伯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Yun's style name was Changqian, Hou's was Shuqian, Shen's was Manqian, and Hou's son Yu's style name was Jingbo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records: Yun styled Changqian, Hou styled Shuqian, Shen styled Manqian, and Hou's son Yu styled Jingbo.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：寓少與裴楷、王戎、杜默倶有名京邑，仕晉，位至尚書，名見顯著。
manualTranslations.literal: The Tales of the Age states: Yu in his youth was together with Pei Kai, Wang Rong, and Du Mo equally famous in the capital; he served Jin and reached the office of Master of Writing; his fame was conspicuous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Tales of the Age records that in youth Yu was as famous in the capital as Pei Kai, Wang Rong, and Du Mo; serving Jin, he rose to Master of Writing with great renown.

manualTranslations.zh: 子羽嗣，位至尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Yu succeeded and reached the office of Master of Writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Yu succeeded him and rose to Master of Writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 詵弟顗，咸熙中爲司空。
manualTranslations.literal: Shen's younger brother Yi, in the Xianxi period served as Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shen's younger brother Yi served as Minister of Works during the Xianxi period.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：顗字景倩，幼爲姊夫陳羣所異。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin states: Yi's style name was Jingqian; in youth he was regarded as extraordinary by his sister's husband Chen Qun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin records that Yi styled Jingqian and was recognized as extraordinary in youth by his brother-in-law Chen Qun.

manualTranslations.zh: 博學洽聞，意思愼密。
manualTranslations.literal: He was broadly learned and well informed; his thoughts were careful and close.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was erudite and well informed, with careful and penetrating judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 司馬宣王見顗，奇之，曰：「荀令君之子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Lord of Xuan saw Yi and marveled at him, saying: "This is the son of Director Xun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Xuan (Sima Yi) met Yi, he was struck by him and said: "He is Director Xun's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 近見袁偘，亦曜卿之子也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Recently I saw Yuan Kan — he too is the son of Lord Yao."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I recently met Yuan Kan — he too is Lord Yao's son."

manualTranslations.zh: 擢拜散騎侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 顗佐命晉室，位至太尉，封臨淮康公。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi assisted in founding the Jin house, reached the office of Grand Commandant, and was enfeoffed as Duke Kang of Linhuai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi assisted in establishing the Jin dynasty, rose to Grand Commandant, and was enfeoffed as Duke Kang of Linhuai.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗難鍾會「易無互體」，見稱於世。
manualTranslations.literal: He once challenged Zhong Hui's proposition that "there is no mutual imagery in the Changes," and was praised by the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once disputed Zhong Hui's claim that the Book of Changes has no mutual imagery, earning renown throughout the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 顗弟粲，字奉倩。
manualTranslations.literal: Yi's younger brother Can's style name was Fengqian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Can styled Fengqian.

manualTranslations.zh: 何劭爲粲傳曰：粲字奉倩，粲諸兄並以儒術論議，而粲獨好言道，常以爲子貢稱夫子之言性與天道，不可得聞，然則六籍雖存，固聖人之糠粃。
manualTranslations.literal: He Shao wrote a biography of Can stating: Can's style name was Fengqian; Can's elder brothers all engaged in Confucian learning and debate, but Can alone delighted in discussing the Way; he often held that when Zigong said the Master's words on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be heard, then although the Six Classics remained, they were truly the chaff of the sage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Shao wrote a biography of Can: Can styled Fengqian. His elder brothers all debated in the Confucian tradition, but Can alone loved to discuss the Way. He often argued that since Zigong said the Master's words on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be fully conveyed, the Six Classics, though preserved, are but the sage's chaff.

manualTranslations.zh: 粲兄俁難曰：「易亦云聖人立象以盡意，繫辭焉以盡言，則微言胡爲不可得而聞見哉？」
manualTranslations.literal: Can's elder brother Hou challenged him, saying: "The Changes also says the sage established images to fully express meaning and attached words to fully express speech — then why could subtle words not be obtained and heard and seen?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can's elder brother Hou objected: "The Book of Changes says the sage established images to fully express meaning and appended words to fully express speech — then why could subtle teachings not be heard?"

manualTranslations.zh: 粲荅曰：「蓋理之微者，非物象之所舉也。
manualTranslations.literal: Can replied: "Principles that are subtle are not what material images can fully express.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can replied: "Subtle principles cannot be fully conveyed through material images.

manualTranslations.zh: 今稱立象以盡意，此非通于意外者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now to say that establishing images fully expresses meaning — this does not penetrate beyond the image.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To say that establishing images fully expresses meaning is not to penetrate beyond the image itself.

manualTranslations.zh: 繫辭焉以盡言，此非言乎繫表者也；
manualTranslations.literal: Attaching words to fully express speech — this is not speaking of what is attached to the surface;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Attaching words to fully express speech is not to speak of what is merely attached to the surface;

manualTranslations.zh: 斯則象外之意，繫表之言，固蘊而不出矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: then the meaning beyond the image and the words attached to the surface are originally hidden and do not emerge."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the meaning beyond the images and the words beyond the surface are inherently contained and do not emerge."

manualTranslations.zh: 及當時能言者不能屈也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time, those skilled in discourse could not refute him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time, none of the leading debaters could defeat him.

manualTranslations.zh: 又論父彧不如從兄攸。
manualTranslations.literal: He also argued that his father Yu was not equal to his cousin You.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also argued that his father Yu was inferior to his cousin Xun You.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧立德髙整，軌儀以訓物，而攸不治外形，愼密自居而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu established virtue that was lofty and ordered, using standards and ceremony to instruct things; You did not cultivate external appearance, merely keeping careful secrecy to himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu's virtue was lofty and orderly, teaching others through standard and ceremony; Xun You did not cultivate appearances outwardly, contenting himself with careful inward reserve.

manualTranslations.zh: 粲以此言善攸，諸兄怒而不能迴也。
manualTranslations.literal: Can with these words praised You; his elder brothers were angry but could not turn him back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can used this argument to praise Xun You; his elder brothers were furious but could not change his mind.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和初，到京邑與傅嘏談。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign, he arrived at the capital and conversed with Fu Gu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign, he came to the capital and discussed philosophy with Fu Gu.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏善名理而粲尚玄遠，宗致雖同，倉卒時或有格而不相得意。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu was skilled in the principles of naming while Can esteemed the abstruse and far-reaching; although their fundamental aims were the same, in hasty moments there were sometimes clashes and mutual incomprehension.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu excelled at logical disputation while Can favored the abstruse and metaphysical; though they shared fundamental aims, in quick exchanges they sometimes clashed and failed to understand each other.

manualTranslations.zh: 裴徽通彼我之懷，爲二家騎驛，頃之，粲與嘏善。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Hui understood the feelings of both sides and served as a relay rider between the two schools; shortly thereafter, Can and Gu became friends.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Hui understood both men's perspectives and mediated between them; before long, Can and Fu Gu became friends.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏侯玄亦親。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiahou Xuan was also close to him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was also close to Xiahou Xuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 常謂嘏、玄曰：「子等在世塗間，功名必勝我，但識劣我耳！」
manualTranslations.literal: He often said to Gu and Xuan: "You gentlemen on the path of worldly life — your fame and achievement will surely surpass mine, but your insight is inferior to mine!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He often told Fu Gu and Xiahou Xuan: "You will surpass me in worldly fame and achievement, but your understanding falls short of mine!"

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏難曰：「能盛功名者，識也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu challenged him, saying: "Those who can flourish in fame and achievement — that is insight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu objected: "It is insight that produces great fame and achievement.

manualTranslations.zh: 天下孰有本不足而末有餘者邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: In all the world, is there anyone whose root is insufficient yet whose branches are abundant?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who in the world has a weak foundation but abundant fruit?"

manualTranslations.zh: 粲曰：「功名者，志局之所獎也。
manualTranslations.literal: Can said: "Fame and achievement are what ambition and design reward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can replied: "Fame and achievement are the rewards of ambition and vision.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則志局自一物耳，固非識之所獨濟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus ambition and design are themselves one thing; they are certainly not what insight alone can accomplish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ambition and vision are one thing — they are not achieved by insight alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 我以能使子等爲貴，然未必齊子等所爲也。」
manualTranslations.literal: I take as my honor that I can make gentlemen like you succeed, yet I am not necessarily equal to what gentlemen like you accomplish."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I take pride in being able to make men like you succeed, yet I may not equal what men like you achieve."

manualTranslations.zh: 粲常以婦人者，才智不足論，自宜以色爲主。
manualTranslations.literal: Can often held that as for women, intellectual talent was not worth discussing; they should naturally take beauty as their main quality.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can often said that a woman's intellect was not worth discussing — beauty was what mattered.

manualTranslations.zh: 驃騎將軍曹洪女有美色，粲於是娉焉，容服帷帳甚麗，專房歡宴。
manualTranslations.literal: The daughter of General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong had beautiful looks; Can therefore married her; her dress, furnishings, and curtains were very sumptuous; he kept her in a private chamber for joyous feasting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The daughter of General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was renowned for her beauty; Can married her, furnishing their private chamber lavishly and devoting himself to her exclusively.

manualTranslations.zh: 歴年後，婦病亡，未殯，傅嘏往喭粲；
manualTranslations.literal: After some years, his wife died of illness; before the burial, Fu Gu went to console Can;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After several years his wife died of illness; before the funeral, Fu Gu came to console Can;

manualTranslations.zh: 粲不哭而神傷。
manualTranslations.literal: Can did not weep but his spirit was wounded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can did not weep outwardly, but his spirit was crushed.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏問曰：「婦人才色並茂爲難。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu asked, saying: "For a woman to possess both talent and beauty in abundance is difficult.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu asked: "It is rare for a woman to possess both talent and beauty.

manualTranslations.zh: 子之娶也，遺才而好色。
manualTranslations.literal: In your marriage, you left aside talent and favored beauty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In marrying, you set aside talent and chose beauty alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 此自易遇，今何哀之甚？」
manualTranslations.literal: This is itself easy to encounter — why grieve so deeply now?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That should be easy to replace — why grieve so deeply?"

manualTranslations.zh: 粲曰：「佳人難再得！
manualTranslations.literal: Can said: "A beautiful woman is hard to obtain again!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can said: "A woman of such beauty cannot be found again!

manualTranslations.zh: 顧逝者不能有傾國之色，然未可謂之易遇。」
manualTranslations.literal: Looking at the departed, she could not possess nation-toppling beauty, yet one still cannot say she was easy to encounter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She may not have had nation-toppling beauty, but one still cannot call her easy to replace."

manualTranslations.zh: 痛悼不能已，歳餘亦亡，時年二十九。
manualTranslations.literal: His grief could not cease; after a little more than a year he also died, aged twenty-nine at the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He could not recover from his grief; a little over a year later he too died, at the age of twenty-nine.

manualTranslations.zh: 粲簡貴，不能與常人交接，所交皆一時俊傑。
manualTranslations.literal: Can was refined and noble; he could not associate with ordinary people; those he associated with were all outstanding talents of the age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Can was refined and aloof; he could not mix with ordinary people and associated only with the age's finest minds.

manualTranslations.zh: 至葬夕，赴者裁十餘人，皆同時知名士也，哭之，感慟路人。
manualTranslations.literal: On the evening of the burial, those who came numbered only a little more than ten — all were well-known scholars of the time; when they wept for him, passersby were moved to grief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the night of his burial, only a dozen or so mourners came — all distinguished men of the day — and their weeping moved passersby to tears.

manualTranslations.zh: 惲子甝，嗣爲散騎常侍，進爵廣陽鄕侯，年三十薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun's son Kan succeeded and served as Regular Attendant of the Central Secretariat; he was advanced to Marquis of Guangyang Township and died at age thirty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yun's son Kan succeeded him as Regular Attendant of the Central Secretariat, was advanced to Marquis of Guangyang Township, and died at thirty.

manualTranslations.zh: 子頵嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Yin succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Yin succeeded him.

manualTranslations.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：頵字温伯，爲羽林右監，早卒。
manualTranslations.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Yin's style name was Wenbo; he served as Right Director of the Forest of Feathers and died young.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records that Yin styled Wenbo, served as Right Director of the Forest of Feathers, and died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 頵子崧，字景猷。
manualTranslations.literal: Yin's son Song's style name was Jingyou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yin's son Song styled Jingyou.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉陽秋》稱崧少有志操，雅好文學，孝義和愛，在朝恪勤，位至左右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin praises Song as having lofty aspirations and conduct from youth, elegantly loving literature, filial, righteous, harmonious, and loving; in court he was diligent and careful, reaching the offices of Left and Right Household Grandee and Grand Master with the Honours of an Imperial Carriage and the Three Dignities.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin praises Song as a youth of noble aspiration, devoted to literature, filial and compassionate; diligent in office, he rose to Household Grandee of the Left and Right and Grand Master with Imperial Carriage Honors.

manualTranslations.zh: 崧子羨，字令則，淸和有才。
manualTranslations.literal: Song's son Xian's style name was Lingze; he was pure and harmonious and possessed talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song's son Xian styled Lingze — refined, harmonious, and talented.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚公主，少歴顯位，年二十八爲北中郎將，徐、兖二州刺史，假節都督徐、兖、靑三州諸軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: He married an imperial princess; from youth he passed through distinguished offices; at age twenty-eight he was General of the North and Central, Governor of Xu and Yan Provinces, and Provisionally bearing credentials of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing Provinces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He married an imperial princess, held distinguished office from youth, and at twenty-eight became General of the North and Central, Governor of Xu and Yan Provinces, with credentials of authority as Commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing.

manualTranslations.zh: 在任十年，遇疾解職，卒於家，追贈驃騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: During ten years in office, he encountered illness and resigned his post; he died at home and was posthumously granted the office of General of Agile Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After ten years in office he fell ill and resigned; he died at home and was posthumously awarded the rank of General of Agile Cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 羨孫伯子，今御史中丞也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xian's grandson Bozi — the present Censor-in-Chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xian's grandson Bozi is the present Censor-in-Chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 霬官至中領軍，薨，諡曰貞侯，追贈驃騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui reached the office of Central Army Inspector; he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhen; he was posthumously granted the office of General of Agile Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui rose to Central Army Inspector; he died and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen and awarded the rank of General of Agile Cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 子愷嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Kai succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Kai succeeded him.

manualTranslations.zh: 霬妻，司馬景王、文王之妹也，二王皆與親善。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's wife was the younger sister of Sima the King of Jing and Sima the King of Wen; both kings were on close and friendly terms with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui's wife was the younger sister of the Kings of Jing and Wen (Sima Shi and Sima Zhao); both Sima brothers were on close terms with the family.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熙中，開建五等，霬以著勳前朝，改封愷南頓子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Xianxi period, when the five ranks of nobility were established, because Hui had displayed merit in the previous dynasty, Kai was changed in enfeoffment to Viscount of Nandun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Xianxi, when the five noble ranks were established, Kai was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nandun in recognition of Hui's merit under the previous dynasty.

manualTranslations.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：愷，晉武帝時爲侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Kai served as Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu of Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records that Kai served as Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu of Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：武帝使侍中荀顗、和嶠倶至東宮，觀察太子。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin states: Emperor Wu sent Palace Attendants Xun Yi and He Qiao together to the Eastern Palace to observe the Crown Prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin records that Emperor Wu sent Palace Attendants Xun Yi and He Qiao together to the Eastern Palace to observe the Crown Prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 顗還稱太子德識進茂，而嶠云聖質如初。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yi returned, he praised the Crown Prince's virtue and insight as advancing and flourishing; He Qiao said his sage-like quality was as at first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On returning, Yi reported that the Crown Prince's virtue and insight were flourishing; He Qiao said his sage-like qualities were unchanged.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫盛曰「遣荀勗」，其餘語則同。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Sheng says "sent Xun Xu"; the rest of the wording is the same.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng writes "sent Xun Xu"; the rest is the same.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案和嶠爲侍中，荀顗亡沒久矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: He Qiao served as Palace Attendant; Xun Yi had long since died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: He Qiao was Palace Attendant, but Xun Yi had long been dead.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀勗位亞台司，不與嶠同班，無縁方稱侍中。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Xu's position was second to the ministers of the Terrace; he was not in the same rank as Qiao; there was no reason he would be called Palace Attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Xu ranked just below the chief ministers and was not in He Qiao's cohort — he could not have been called simply "Palace Attendant."

manualTranslations.zh: 二書所云，皆爲非也。
manualTranslations.literal: What both books say is all incorrect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Both accounts are wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 考其時位，愷寔當之。
manualTranslations.literal: Examining the times and positions, Kai truly should have been the one.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Considering the dates and offices involved, Kai must have been the man.

manualTranslations.zh: 愷位至征西大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai reached the office of General Who Conquers the West.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kai rose to General Who Conquers the West.

manualTranslations.zh: 愷兄憺，少府。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai's elder brother Dan — Minister Steward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kai's elder brother Dan served as Minister Steward.

manualTranslations.zh: 弟悝，護軍將軍，追贈車騎大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: His younger brother Kui — General Who Guards the Army; posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kui served as General Who Guards the Army and was posthumously awarded the rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sourceRange.text: 文帝即位，以詡爲太尉，《魏略》曰：文帝得詡之對太祖，故即位首登上司。荀勗別傳曰：晉司徒闕，武帝問其人於勗。荅曰：「三公具瞻所歸，不可用非其人。昔魏文帝用賈詡爲三公，孫權笑之。」進爵魏壽鄕侯，增邑三百，并前八百戸。又分邑二百，封小子訪爲列侯。以長子穆爲駙馬都尉。帝問詡曰：「吾欲伐不從命以一天下，呉、蜀何先？」對曰：「攻取者先兵權，建本者尚德化。陛下應期受禪，撫臨率土，若綏之以文德而俟其變，則平之不難矣。呉、蜀雖蕞爾小國，依岨山水，劉備有雄才，諸葛亮善治國，孫權識虚實，陸議見兵勢，據險守要，汎舟江湖，皆難卒謀也。用兵之道，先勝後戰，量敵論將，故舉無遺策。臣竊料羣臣，無備、權對，雖以天威臨之，未見萬全之勢也。昔舜舞干戚而有苗服，臣以爲當今宜先文後武。」文帝不納。後興江陵之役，士卒多死。詡年七十七，薨，諡曰肅侯。子穆嗣，歴位郡守。穆薨，子模嗣。《世語》曰：模，晉惠帝時爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍，模子胤，胤弟龕，從弟疋，皆至大官，並顯於晉也。

context.afterSource: 評曰：荀彧淸秀通雅，有王佐之風，然機鑒先識，未能充其志也。

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝即位，以詡爲太尉，《魏略》曰：文帝得詡之對太祖，故即位首登上司。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he made Xu Grand Commandant. The Brief Account of Wei states: Emperor Wen had obtained Xu's reply to the Grand Progenitor, and therefore upon taking the throne first appointed him to the supreme office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne, he named Jia Xu Grand Commandant. The Brief Account of Wei explains that he remembered Jia Xu's counsel to Cao Cao and therefore promoted him first to the highest ministry.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀勗別傳曰：晉司徒闕，武帝問其人於勗。
manualTranslations.literal: The separate biography of Xun Xu states: The Jin office of Minister over the Masses was vacant; Emperor Wu asked Xu about the man for it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A supplementary biography of Xun Xu records that when the Jin Minister over the Masses post fell vacant, Emperor Wu asked Xun Xu whom to appoint.

manualTranslations.zh: 荅曰：「三公具瞻所歸，不可用非其人。
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "The three dukes are what all gaze upon and where they turn; one cannot use someone who is not the right man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Three Excellencies are what the whole court looks to; you cannot fill such a post with the wrong man.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔魏文帝用賈詡爲三公，孫權笑之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Wei used Jia Xu as one of the three dukes, and Sun Quan laughed at it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei once made Jia Xu a Three Excellency, Sun Quan laughed at it."

manualTranslations.zh: 進爵魏壽鄕侯，增邑三百，并前八百戸。
manualTranslations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Marquis of Weishou Township, with three hundred households added to his fief, making eight hundred households together with what came before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His title rose to Marquis of Weishou Township, with three hundred added households in his fief—for eight hundred in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 又分邑二百，封小子訪爲列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Again he divided out two hundred households of the fief and enfeoffed his younger son Fang as a ranked marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He further split off two hundred households and enfeoffed his younger son Fang as a full marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 以長子穆爲駙馬都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: His eldest son Mu was made Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He appointed his eldest son Mu Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝問詡曰：「吾欲伐不從命以一天下，呉、蜀何先？」
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor asked Xu: "I wish to attack those who do not obey orders in order to unify all under Heaven—Wu or Shu, which first?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Jia Xu, "I mean to conquer the disobedient and unite the realm—which should I strike first, Wu or Shu?"

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「攻取者先兵權，建本者尚德化。
manualTranslations.literal: He replied: "Those who seize by attack put military authority first; those who build the foundation esteem civil virtue and transformation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "Conquerors put force first; founders rely on civil virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下應期受禪，撫臨率土，若綏之以文德而俟其變，則平之不難矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty received the abdicated mandate in accord with the season and oversees all the land; if you pacify them with civil virtue and await their change, then pacifying them would not be difficult.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty took the throne at the appointed hour and now rules every province; pacify them with civil virtue and wait for events to turn, and subduing them will not be hard.

manualTranslations.zh: 呉、蜀雖蕞爾小國，依岨山水，劉備有雄才，諸葛亮善治國，孫權識虚實，陸議見兵勢，據險守要，汎舟江湖，皆難卒謀也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wu and Shu, though petty small states, lean on lofty mountains and rivers; Liu Bei has heroic talent, Zhuge Liang excels at governing the state, Sun Quan discerns emptiness and fullness, Lu Yi reads military strength; holding strategic passes in perilous terrain and roaming rivers and lakes—all are difficult to scheme against suddenly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu are small, but they have mountains and rivers to shield them—Liu Bei is formidable, Zhuge Liang governs well, Sun Quan knows his strengths and limits, and Lu Xun reads battlefield odds. They hold defensible passes and move fleets on the rivers and lakes; none can be rushed.

manualTranslations.zh: 用兵之道，先勝後戰，量敵論將，故舉無遺策。
manualTranslations.literal: The Way of employing troops is to secure victory before battle, measure the enemy and weigh the generals—therefore in action nothing is left out of the planning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In war, victory is won before battle is joined—match enemy to commander and every move follows plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣竊料羣臣，無備、權對，雖以天威臨之，未見萬全之勢也。
manualTranslations.literal: I privately reckon among the ministers there is no pair for Bei and Quan; even if Heaven's majesty pressed down upon them, I do not see a fully secure prospect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking at our court, no one measures up to Liu Bei and Sun Quan; even with the throne's full might, I see no safe assurance of victory.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔舜舞干戚而有苗服，臣以爲當今宜先文後武。」
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Shun brandished shield and battle-axe and the Miao submitted; I consider that today one should put civil means first and martial means after."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shun danced with shield and axe, the Miao submitted—I believe we should try civil means before force."

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝不納。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen did not adopt it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Pi would not listen.

manualTranslations.zh: 後興江陵之役，士卒多死。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he launched the Jiangling campaign; soldiers died in great numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later mounted the Jiangling campaign, and many soldiers perished.

manualTranslations.zh: 詡年七十七，薨，諡曰肅侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Xu was seventy-seven when he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Su.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Xu died at seventy-seven and was posthumously titled Marquis Su.

manualTranslations.zh: 子穆嗣，歴位郡守。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Mu succeeded him and held successive posts as commandery governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Mu succeeded him and served as governor of several commanderies.

manualTranslations.zh: 穆薨，子模嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mu died, his son Mo succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mu died, his son Mo took the succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：模，晉惠帝時爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍，模子胤，胤弟龕，從弟疋，皆至大官，並顯於晉也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu states: Mo, during Emperor Hui of Jin, was Regular Attendant Within the Cavalry and General Who Protects the Army; Mo's son Yin, Yin's younger brother Kan, and paternal cousin Pi all rose to high office and were all eminent in Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu adds that under Emperor Hui of Jin, Mo became Regular Attendant Within the Cavalry and General Who Protects the Army; Mo's son Yin, Yin's brother Kan, and cousin Pi all rose to high office and were prominent figures in Jin.

sourceRange.text: 賈詡字文和，武威姑臧人也。少時人莫知，唯漢陽閻忠異之，謂詡有良、平之奇。《九州春秋》曰：中平元年，車騎將軍皇甫嵩旣破黃巾，威震天下。閻忠時罷信都令，説嵩曰：「夫難得而易失者時也，時至而不旋踵者機也，故聖人常順時而動，智者必因機以發。今將軍遭難得之運，蹈易解之機，而踐運不撫，臨機不發，將何以享大名乎？」嵩曰：「何謂也？」忠曰：「天道無親，百姓與能，故有髙人之功者，不受庸主之賞。今將軍授鉞於初春，收功於末冬，兵動若神，謀不再計，旬月之間，神兵電掃，攻堅易於折枯，摧敵甚於湯雪，七州席巻，屠三十六萬方，夷黃巾之師，除邪害之患，或封戸刻石，南向以報德，威震本朝，風馳海外。是以羣雄迴首，百姓企踵，雖湯武之舉，未有髙於將軍者。身建髙人之功，北面以事庸主，將何以圖安？」嵩曰：「心不忘忠，何爲不安？」忠曰：「不然。昔韓信不忍一飱之遇，而棄三分之利，拒蒯通之忠，忽鼎跱之勢，利劒已揣其喉，乃嘆息而悔，所以見烹於兒女也。今主勢弱於劉、項，將軍權重於淮陰，指麾可以振風雲，叱咤足以興雷電；赫然奮發，因危抵頽，崇恩以綏前附，振武以臨後服；徴冀方之士，動七州之衆，羽檄先馳於前，大軍震響於後，蹈蹟漳河，飲馬孟津，舉天網以網羅京都，誅閹宦之罪，除羣怨之積忿，解久危之倒懸。如此則攻守無堅城，不招必影從，雖兒童可使奮空拳以致力，女子可使其褰裳以用命，況厲智能之士，因迅風之勢，則大功不足合，八方不足同也。功業已就，天下已順，乃燎于上帝，告以天命，混齊六合，南面以制，移神器於己家，推亡漢以定祚，實神機之至決，風發之良時也。夫木朽不彫，世衰難佐，將軍雖欲委忠難佐之朝，彫畫朽敗之木，猶逆坂而走丸，必不可也。方今權宦羣居，同惡如市，主上不自由，詔命出左右。如有至聦不察，機事不先，必嬰後悔，亦無及矣。」嵩不從，忠乃亡去。《英雄記》曰：涼州賊王國等起兵，共劫忠爲主，統三十六部，號車騎將軍。忠感慨發病而死。察孝廉爲郎，疾病去官，西還至汧，道遇叛氐，同行數十人皆爲所執。詡曰：「我段公外孫也，汝別埋我，我家必厚贖之。」時太尉段熲，昔久爲邊將，威震西土，故詡假以懼氐。氐果不敢害，與盟而送之，其餘悉死。詡實非段甥，權以濟事，咸此類也。

manualTranslations.zh: 賈詡字文和，武威姑臧人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Jia Xu, styled Wenhe, was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Xu, courtesy name Wenhe, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.

manualTranslations.zh: 少時人莫知，唯漢陽閻忠異之，謂詡有良、平之奇。
manualTranslations.literal: In his youth no one knew him; only Yan Zhong of Hanyang regarded him as extraordinary and said Xu had the marvel of Liang and Ping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth no one noticed him, but Yan Zhong of Hanyang singled him out and said Jia Xu had the genius of a Zhang Liang or Chen Ping.

manualTranslations.zh: 《九州春秋》曰：中平元年，車騎將軍皇甫嵩旣破黃巾，威震天下。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces says: In the first year of Zhongping, General of Chariots and Cavalry Huangfu Song, having already defeated the Yellow Turbans, his prestige shook the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces says: In Zhongping 1, General of Chariots and Cavalry Huangfu Song, having crushed the Yellow Turbans, shook the realm with his prestige.

manualTranslations.zh: 閻忠時罷信都令，説嵩曰：「夫難得而易失者時也，時至而不旋踵者機也，故聖人常順時而動，智者必因機以發。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong at the time had been dismissed as magistrate of Xindu; he urged Song, saying: "What is hard to obtain yet easy to lose is the season; when the season arrives yet one does not turn on his heel—that is the moment missed; therefore sages constantly act in accord with the season, and the wise must surely strike through opportunity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Zhong had just left office as magistrate of Xindu and urged Song: "What is hard to seize and easy to lose is opportunity; when it comes you must not hesitate—that is the decisive moment. Sages move with the times; the wise seize the moment.

manualTranslations.zh: 今將軍遭難得之運，蹈易解之機，而踐運不撫，臨機不發，將何以享大名乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Now the general has encountered a hard-won fortune and treads an easily grasped moment, yet treads fortune without nurturing it and faces the moment without acting—how then will you enjoy a great name?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You stand in a rare fortune and on the brink of an opening you could take—yet you nurture neither fortune nor occasion. How will you win a great name?"

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩曰：「何謂也？」
manualTranslations.literal: Song said: "What do you mean?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song asked, "What do you mean?"

manualTranslations.zh: 忠曰：「天道無親，百姓與能，故有髙人之功者，不受庸主之賞。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong said: "The Way of Heaven is impartial; the people invest ability in the worthy; therefore one who has the achievement of a transcendent man does not receive reward from a mediocre lord.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "Heaven favors merit, not persons; the people raise the capable. One who has done transcendent work does not take his reward from a mediocre master.

manualTranslations.zh: 今將軍授鉞於初春，收功於末冬，兵動若神，謀不再計，旬月之間，神兵電掃，攻堅易於折枯，摧敵甚於湯雪，七州席巻，屠三十六萬方，夷黃巾之師，除邪害之患，或封戸刻石，南向以報德，威震本朝，風馳海外。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the general received the battle-axe in early spring and gathered achievement in late winter; troops moved like a spirit, plans needed no second reckoning; within a month or so divine soldiers swept like lightning; attacking strongholds was easier than breaking dead wood, crushing the enemy more than boiling snow; seven provinces were rolled up like a mat; thirty-six myriad households were slaughtered; the Yellow Turban army was destroyed; the evil harm was removed; some enfeoffed households and carved stone, turning south to repay virtue; prestige shook the present court, wind raced beyond the seas.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You took command in spring and finished the campaign by winter. Your armies moved like spirits; your plans needed no second thought. In a few months they swept the field like lightning—storming fortified places as easily as snapping dry wood, shattering the foe faster than snow melts in boiling water. Seven provinces fell like a mat rolled shut. Three hundred sixty thousand households were put to the sword. The Yellow Turbans were annihilated and the realm cleansed of their poison. Men carved your deeds in stone and turned south to thank Heaven. Your fame shook the court; your renown raced overseas.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以羣雄迴首，百姓企踵，雖湯武之舉，未有髙於將軍者。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the many heroes turned their heads, common folk stood on tiptoe in expectation—even the deeds of Tang and Wu had none higher than the general's.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: War lords everywhere turned to watch; common folk craned their necks in hope. Even Tang and Wu did no greater deeds than yours.

manualTranslations.zh: 身建髙人之功，北面以事庸主，將何以圖安？」
manualTranslations.literal: Having personally built transcendent achievement yet serving a mediocre lord while facing north—how will you scheme for safety?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have built transcendent achievement yet serve a mediocre lord as his subject—how can you hope to stay safe?"

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩曰：「心不忘忠，何爲不安？」
manualTranslations.literal: Song said: "With a heart that does not forget loyalty, why would there be no safety?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song said, "If I keep loyalty in heart, why should I lack safety?"

manualTranslations.zh: 忠曰：「不然。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong said: "It is not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "No.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔韓信不忍一飱之遇，而棄三分之利，拒蒯通之忠，忽鼎跱之勢，利劒已揣其喉，乃嘆息而悔，所以見烹於兒女也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the past Han Xin could not bear to forsake a single meal's favor, yet abandoned the profit of a third of the realm, rejected Kuai Tong's loyal counsel, neglected the posture of tripod standing awry; the sharp sword had already been pressed to his throat—only then did he sigh and regret; therefore he was boiled alive by children and women.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once Han Xin could not bring himself to betray a single meal's kindness. He threw away the chance to divide the realm three ways, spurned Kuai Tong's loyal advice, and ignored the precarious balance of power. The blade was already at his throat before he sighed in regret—so a boy and a girl boiled him alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 今主勢弱於劉、項，將軍權重於淮陰，指麾可以振風雲，叱咤足以興雷電；
manualTranslations.literal: Now the lord's power is weaker than Liu and Xiang; the general's authority is weightier than the Marquis of Huaiyin; a wave of the hand can shake wind and clouds, a shout is enough to raise thunder and lightning;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your sovereign is weaker than Liu Bang and Xiang Yu were; your authority outweighs the Marquis of Huaiyin's. One gesture of your hand can stir wind and cloud; one shout can raise thunder and lightning;

manualTranslations.zh: 赫然奮發，因危抵頽，崇恩以綏前附，振武以臨後服；
manualTranslations.literal: With blazing ardor rise and act; seize crisis to press against collapse; extend grace to soothe those who submit in advance, rouse martial might to overawe those who submit later;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rouse yourself boldly; turn the realm's crisis into your lever. Shower favor on those who submit early; brandish arms against those who hold back;

manualTranslations.zh: 徴冀方之士，動七州之衆，羽檄先馳於前，大軍震響於後，蹈蹟漳河，飲馬孟津，舉天網以網羅京都，誅閹宦之罪，除羣怨之積忿，解久危之倒懸。
manualTranslations.literal: Summon men of Ji region, mobilize the masses of seven provinces; battle proclamations race ahead first, the great army thunders behind; tread the tracks along the Zhang River, water horses at Meng Ford, raise heaven's net to net the capital, punish the crimes of eunuch officials, remove the accumulated resentments of the many, release the long-pending inverted hanging.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Call up the warriors of Ji, mobilize the seven provinces—dispatch your urgent summons ahead and thunder after with the main host. Cross the Zhang River; water your horses at Meng Ford. Cast the net of heaven over the capital. Punish the eunuch criminals, clear the people's stored hatred, and end the peril that has hung the realm upside down for years.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此則攻守無堅城，不招必影從，雖兒童可使奮空拳以致力，女子可使其褰裳以用命，況厲智能之士，因迅風之勢，則大功不足合，八方不足同也。
manualTranslations.literal: If it is thus then attack and defense have no strong city; without summoning, followers must trail like shadows; even children can be made to wield empty fists to exert effort, women can be made to lift their skirts to give their lives—how much more when rousing intelligent and capable men and riding the momentum of swift wind; then great achievement is insufficient to match, the eight directions are insufficient to unite against.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No city could stand against you; men would flock unasked. Children would clench empty fists for you; women would lift their skirts to march. Rouse the able and ride the gale, and no combined merit could rival you, no force in the eight directions could stand united against you.

manualTranslations.zh: 功業已就，天下已順，乃燎于上帝，告以天命，混齊六合，南面以制，移神器於己家，推亡漢以定祚，實神機之至決，風發之良時也。
manualTranslations.literal: When achievement is complete and the realm is already obedient, then offer burnt sacrifice to Supreme Lord, announce the Mandate of Heaven, merge and align the six directions, face south to rule, shift the divine vessel to one's own house, push out the dying Han to fix the imperial seat—it is truly the utmost decision of divine opportunity and the fine season of wind rising.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When your work is done and the realm bows, burn offerings to Heaven and proclaim the Mandate. Unite the six directions, face south and rule, move the imperial regalia to your house, and replace the dying Han to fix the throne—that is the supreme stroke of fate and the perfect hour to strike.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫木朽不彫，世衰難佐，將軍雖欲委忠難佐之朝，彫畫朽敗之木，猶逆坂而走丸，必不可也。
manualTranslations.literal: When wood is rotten it cannot be carved; in a declining age it is hard to assist; though the general wishes to devote loyalty to a hard-to-assist court, carving and painting rotten spoiled wood is like rolling a ball uphill—in every case impossible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rotten wood will not take a carving; a declining age will not take a worthy counselor. Even if you mean to serve this court loyally, you would be painting rotten timber—like rolling a ball uphill. It cannot be done.

manualTranslations.zh: 方今權宦羣居，同惡如市，主上不自由，詔命出左右。
manualTranslations.literal: Just now powerful eunuchs cluster together, sharing evil like a marketplace; the sovereign above is not free; edicts and commands come from those at his side.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today the eunuch faction packs the palace like merchants in a market. The emperor is not his own master; edicts come from whoever stands at his elbow.

manualTranslations.zh: 如有至聦不察，機事不先，必嬰後悔，亦無及矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: If there is utmost intelligence yet no discernment, opportunity matters not seized in advance—one must surely meet regret, and it will also be too late."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Miss this moment while you still have wit enough to see it, and regret will come too late to help."

manualTranslations.zh: 嵩不從，忠乃亡去。
manualTranslations.literal: Song did not follow; Zhong then fled away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Song refused; Zhong fled and never returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 《英雄記》曰：涼州賊王國等起兵，共劫忠爲主，統三十六部，號車騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Records of Heroes says: The Liang Province bandit Wang Guo and others raised troops, together seizing Zhong as lord, controlling thirty-six divisions, styling themselves General of Chariots and Cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Records of Heroes says: The Liang rebel Wang Guo and others rebelled, seized Yan Zhong as their leader, united thirty-six bands, and styled him General of Chariots and Cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠感慨發病而死。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong, moved by emotion, fell ill and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moved to grief, Yan Zhong took ill and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 察孝廉爲郎，疾病去官，西還至汧，道遇叛氐，同行數十人皆爲所執。
manualTranslations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he became a gentleman; illness caused him to leave office; returning west he reached Qian, on the road encountered rebel Di; several tens traveling together were all seized.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, Jia Xu became a palace gentleman but resigned for illness. Returning west to Qian, he met rebel Di on the road; dozens traveling with him were seized.

manualTranslations.zh: 詡曰：「我段公外孫也，汝別埋我，我家必厚贖之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xu said: "I am the outer grandson of Lord Duan; bury me separately; my family will surely ransom me richly."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Xu said, "I am Lord Duan's grandson by his daughter—bury me apart. My kin will pay a heavy ransom."

manualTranslations.zh: 時太尉段熲，昔久爲邊將，威震西土，故詡假以懼氐。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Duan Yong had long served as a border general; his prestige shook the western lands; therefore Xu borrowed this to frighten the Di.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Duan Yong had long served on the frontier; his fame terrified the west—so Jia Xu borrowed the name to frighten them.

manualTranslations.zh: 氐果不敢害，與盟而送之，其餘悉死。
manualTranslations.literal: The Di indeed did not dare harm him; they made alliance and sent him off; the rest all died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Di dared not harm him, swore peace and let him go; all the others died.

manualTranslations.zh: 詡實非段甥，權以濟事，咸此類也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xu was in truth not Duan's nephew; he used expedience to accomplish the affair—all were of this kind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Xu was no relation of Duan Yong; he had improvised to save himself. He often got by this way.

sourceRange.text: 建安元年，太祖撃破黃巾。漢獻帝自河東還洛陽。太祖議奉迎都許，或以山東未平，韓暹、楊奉新將天子到洛陽，北連張楊，未可卒制。彧勸太祖曰：「昔晉文公納周襄王而諸侯景從，髙祖東伐爲義帝縞素而天下歸心。自天子播越，將軍首唱義兵，徒以山東擾亂，未能遠赴關右，然猶分遣將帥，蒙險通使，雖禦難于外，乃心無不在王室，是將軍匡天下之素志也。今車駕旋軫，東京榛蕪，義士有存本之思，百姓感舊而增哀。誠因此時，奉主上以從民望，大順也；秉至公以服雄傑，大略也；扶弘義以致英俊，大德也。天下雖有逆節，必不能爲累，明矣。韓暹、楊奉其敢爲害！若不時定，四方生心，後雖慮之，無及。」太祖遂至洛陽，奉迎天子都許。天子拜太祖大將軍，進彧爲漢侍中，守尚書令。常居中持重，《典略》曰：彧折節下士，坐不累席。其在臺閣，不以私欲撓意。彧有羣從一人，才行實薄，或謂彧：「以君當事，不可不以某爲議郎邪？」彧笑曰：「官者所以表才也，若如來言，衆人其謂我何邪！」其持心平正皆類此。太祖雖征伐在外，軍國事皆與彧籌焉。《典略》曰：彧爲人偉美。又平原禰衡傳曰：衡字正平，建安初，自荊州北游許都，恃才傲逸，臧否過差，見不如己者不與語，人皆以是憎之。唯少府孔融髙貴其才，上書薦之曰：「淑質貞亮，英才卓犖。初渉藝文，升堂覩奧；目所一見，輒誦於口，耳所暫聞，不忘於心。性與道合，思若有神。弘羊心計，安世默識，以衡準之，誠不足恠。」衡時年二十四。是時許都雖新建，尚饒人士。衡嘗書一刺懷之，字漫滅而無所適。或問之曰：「何不從陳長文、司馬伯達乎？」衡曰：「卿欲使我從屠沽兒輩也！」又問曰：「當今許中，誰最可者？」衡曰：「大兒有孔文舉，小兒有楊德祖。」又問：「曹公、荀令君、趙盪寇皆足蓋世乎？」衡稱曹公不甚多；又見荀有儀容，趙有腹尺，因荅曰：「文若可借面吊喪，稚長可使監廚請客。」其意以爲荀但有貌，趙健啖肉也。於是衆人皆切齒。衡知衆不恱，將南還荊州。裝束臨發，衆人爲祖道，先設供帳於城南，自共相誡曰：「衡數不遜，今因其後到，以不起報之。」及衡至，衆人皆坐不起，衡乃號咷大哭。衆人問其故，衡曰：「行屍柩之間，能不悲乎？」衡南見劉表，表甚禮之。將軍黃祖屯夏口，祖子射與衡善，隨到夏口。祖嘉其才，毎在坐，席有異賔，介使與衡談。後衡驕蹇，荅祖言徘優饒言，祖以爲罵己也，大怒，顧伍伯捉頭出。左右遂扶以去，拉而殺之。臣松之以本傳不稱彧容貌，故載《典略》與衡傳以見之。又潘勗爲彧碑文，稱彧「瓌姿奇表」。張衡《文士傳》曰：孔融數薦衡於太祖，欲與相見，而衡疾惡之，意常憤懣。因狂疾不肯往，而數有言論。太祖聞其名，圖欲辱之，乃録爲鼓吏。後至八月朝，大宴，賔客並會。時鼓吏撃鼓過，皆當脱其故服，易着新衣。次衡，衡撃爲漁陽參檛，容態不常，音節殊妙。坐上賔客聽之，莫不慷慨。過不易衣，吏呵之，衡乃當太祖前，以次脱衣，裸身而立，徐徐乃着褌冐畢，復撃鼓參檛，而顏色不怍。太祖大笑，告四坐曰：「本欲辱衡，衡反辱孤。」至今有漁陽參檛，自衡造也。融深責數衡，并宣太祖意，欲令與太祖相見。衡許之，曰：「當爲卿往。」至十月朝，融先見太祖，説「衡欲求見」。至日晏，衡着布單衣，疎巾履，坐太祖營門外，以杖捶地，數罵太祖。太祖勑外廄急具精馬三匹，并騎二人，謂融曰：「禰衡豎子，乃敢爾！孤殺之無異於雀鼠，顧此人素有虚名，遠近所聞，今日殺之，人將謂孤不能容。今送與劉表，視卒當何如？」乃令騎以衡置馬上，兩騎扶送至南陽。《傅子》曰：衡辯於言而剋于論，見荊州牧劉表日，所以自結於表者甚至，表恱之以爲上賔。衡稱表之美盈口，而論表左右不廢繩墨。於是左右因形而譖之，曰：「衡稱將軍之仁，西伯不過也，唯以爲不能斷；終不濟者，必由此也。」是言實指表智短，而非衡所言也。衡以交絶於劉表，智窮於黃祖，身死名滅，爲天下笑者，譖之者有形也。太祖問彧：「誰能代卿爲我謀者？」彧言「荀攸、鍾繇」。先是，彧言策謀士，進戲志才。太祖以彧爲知人，諸所進達皆稱職，唯嚴象爲楊州，韋康爲涼州，後敗亡。《三輔決録》曰：象字文則，京兆人。少聦博，有膽智。以督軍御史中丞詣揚州討袁術，會術病卒，因以爲揚州刺史。建安五年，爲孫策廬江太守李術所殺，時年三十八。象同郡趙岐作三輔決録，恐時人不盡其意，故隱其書，唯以示象。康字元將，亦京兆人。孔融與康父端書曰：「前日元將來，淵才亮茂，雅度弘毅，偉世之器也。昨日仲將又來，懿性貞實，文愍篤誠，保家之主也。不意雙珠，近出老蚌，甚珍貴之。」端從涼州牧徴爲太僕，康代爲涼州刺史，時人榮之。後爲馬超所圍，堅守歴時，救軍不至，遂爲超所殺。仲將名誕，見劉邵傳。

context.afterSource: 自太祖之迎天子也，袁紹内懷不服。
