items.acceptedSourceText: 散騎常侍陳留蘇林、《魏略》曰：林字孝友，博學，多通古今寄指，凡諸書傳文間危疑，林皆釋之。建安中，為五官將文學，甚見禮待。黃初中，為博士給事中。文帝作《典論》所稱蘇林者是也。以老歸第，國家每遣人就問之，數加賜遺。年八十餘卒。光祿大夫京兆韋誕、《文章叙錄》曰：誕字仲將，太僕端之子。有文才，善屬辭章。建安中，為郡上計吏，特拜郎中，稍遷侍中中書監，以光祿大夫遜位，年七十五卒於家。初，邯鄲淳、衞覬及誕並善書，有名。覬孫恒撰《四體書勢》，其序古文曰：「自秦用篆書，焚燒先典，而古文絶矣。漢武帝時，魯恭王壞孔子宅，得《尚書》、《春秋》、《論語》、《孝經》，時人已不復知有古文，謂之「科斗書」，漢世祕藏，希得見之。魏初傳古文者，出於邯鄲淳。敬侯寫淳《尚書》，後以示淳，而淳不別。至正始中，立三字石經，轉失淳法。因科斗之名，遂效其法。太康元年，汲縣民盜發魏襄王冢，得策書十餘萬言。案敬侯所書，猶有髣髴。」敬侯謂覬也。其序篆書曰：「秦時李斯號為工篆，諸山及銅人銘皆斯書也。漢建初中，扶風曹喜少異於斯而亦稱善。邯鄲淳師焉，略究其妙。韋誕師淳而不及也。太和中，誕為武都太守，以能書留補侍中，魏氏寶器銘題皆誕書云。漢末又有蔡邕采斯、喜之法，為古今雜形，然精密簡理不如淳也。」其序錄隷書，已略見《武紀》。又曰：「師宜官為大字，邯鄲淳為小字。梁鵠謂淳得次仲法，然鵠之用筆盡其勢矣。」其序草書曰：「漢興而有草書，不知作者姓名。至章帝時，齊相杜度號善作篇，後有崔瑗、崔寔亦皆稱工。杜氏然字甚安而書體微瘦，崔氏甚得筆勢而結字小疏。弘農張伯英者因而而轉精其巧。凡家之衣帛，必書而後練之，臨池學書，池水盡黑。下筆必為楷則，號『怱怱不暇草』，寸紙不見遺，至今世人尤寶之，韋仲將謂之草聖。伯英弟文舒者，次伯英。又有姜孟潁、梁孔達、田彥和及韋仲將之徒，皆伯英弟子，有名於世，然殊不及文舒也。」樂安太守譙國夏侯惠、惠，淵子。事在〈淵傳〉。陳郡太守任城孫該、《文章叙錄》曰：該字公達。彊志好學。年二十，上計掾，召為郎中。著《魏書》。遷博士司徒右長史，復還入著作。景元二年卒官。郎中令河東杜摯等亦著文賦，頗傳於世。《文章叙錄》曰：摯字德魯。初上笳賦，署司徒軍謀吏。後舉孝廉，除郎中，轉補校書。摯與毌丘儉鄕里相親，故為詩與儉，求仙人藥一丸，欲以感切儉求助也。其詩曰：「騏驥馬不試，婆娑槽櫪間。壯士志未伸，坎軻多辛酸。伊摯為媵臣，呂望身操竿；夷吾困商販，寗戚對牛歎；食其處監門，淮陰飢不餐；買臣老負薪，妻畔呼不還，釋之宦十年，位不增故官。才非八子倫，而與齊其患。無知不在此，袁盎未有言。被此篤病乆，榮衞動不安，聞有韓衆藥，信來給一丸。」儉荅曰：「鳳鳥翔京邑，哀鳴有所思。才為聖世出，德音何不怡！八子未遭遇，今者遘明時。胡康出壟畒，楊偉無根基，飛騰沖雲天，奮迅協光熙。駿驥骨法異，伯樂觀知之，但當養羽翮，鴻舉必有期。體無纖微疾，安用問良醫？聯翩輕栖集，還為燕雀嗤。韓衆藥雖良，或更不能治。悠悠千里情，薄言荅嘉詩。信心感諸中，中實不在辭。」摯竟不得遷，卒于祕書。廬江何氏〈家傳〉曰：明帝時，有譙人胡康，年十五，以異才見送，又陳損益，求試劇縣。詔特引見。衆論翕然，號為神童。詔付祕書，使博覽典籍。帝以問祕書丞何禎：「康才何如？」禎荅曰：「康雖有才，性質不端，必有負敗。」後果以過見譴。臣松之案：魏朝自微而顯者，不聞胡康；疑是孟康。康事見〈杜恕傳〉。楊偉見〈曹爽傳〉。

manualTranslations.zh: 散騎常侍陳留蘇林、《魏略》曰：林字孝友，博學，多通古今寄指，凡諸書傳文間危疑，林皆釋之。
manualTranslations.literal: Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse Su Lin of Chenliu—the Weilue says: Lin, courtesy name Xiaoyou, was broadly learned and thoroughly understood hidden meanings ancient and modern; wherever books and transmitted texts had doubtful passages, Lin explained them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse Su Lin of Chenliu—the Weilue says Lin, courtesy Xiaoyou, was broadly learned in hidden meanings ancient and modern and explained doubtful passages in transmitted texts.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安中，為五官將文學，甚見禮待。
manualTranslations.literal: In Jian'an he was Literary Scholar to the General of the Five Senses and was greatly treated with courtesy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an he was Literary Scholar to the General of the Five Senses and was greatly treated with courtesy.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃初中，為博士給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: In Huangchu he was Erudite Supervising the Center.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Huangchu he was Erudite Supervising the Center.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝作《典論》所稱蘇林者是也。
manualTranslations.literal: He is the Su Lin whom Emperor Wen praised in the Dianlun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He is the Su Lin whom Emperor Wen praised in the Dianlun.

manualTranslations.zh: 以老歸第，國家每遣人就問之，數加賜遺。
manualTranslations.literal: He retired home in old age; the state repeatedly sent men to question him and often added gifts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He retired home in old age; the state repeatedly sent men to question him and often added gifts.

manualTranslations.zh: 年八十餘卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died aged over eighty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died aged over eighty.

manualTranslations.zh: 光祿大夫京兆韋誕、《文章叙錄》曰：誕字仲將，太僕端之子。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei Dan of Jingzhao, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—the Wenzhang xulu says: Dan, courtesy name Zhongjiang, was son of the Grand Herald Duan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Dan of Jingzhao, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness—the Wenzhang xulu says Dan, courtesy Zhongjiang, was son of Grand Herald Duan.

manualTranslations.zh: 有文才，善屬辭章。
manualTranslations.literal: He had literary talent and was skilled at composing literary pieces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had literary talent and was skilled at literary composition.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安中，為郡上計吏，特拜郎中，稍遷侍中中書監，以光祿大夫遜位，年七十五卒於家。
manualTranslations.literal: In Jian'an he was the commandery's accounting clerk sent upward, specially appointed Gentleman, gradually promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat, resigned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died at home aged seventy-five.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jian'an he was the commandery accounting clerk, specially appointed Gentleman, gradually promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat, resigned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died at home at seventy-five.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，邯鄲淳、衞覬及誕並善書，有名。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Handan Chun, Wei Ji, and Dan were all skilled at calligraphy and had fame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first Handan Chun, Wei Ji, and Wei Dan were all skilled at calligraphy and famed.

manualTranslations.zh: 覬孫恒撰《四體書勢》，其序古文曰：「自秦用篆書，焚燒先典，而古文絶矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Ji's grandson Heng compiled the Sitishu shi; its preface on ancient script says: "From the time Qin used seal script and burned the earlier classics, ancient script was cut off.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Ji's grandson Heng compiled the Sitishu shi; its preface on ancient script says: "From the time Qin used seal script and burned earlier classics, ancient script was cut off.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢武帝時，魯恭王壞孔子宅，得《尚書》、《春秋》、《論語》、《孝經》，時人已不復知有古文，謂之「科斗書」，漢世祕藏，希得見之。
manualTranslations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Han's time the Prince of Lu, Gong, destroyed Confucius' house and obtained the Documents, Spring and Autumn, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety; people of the time no longer knew there was ancient script and called it "tadpole writing"; in Han it was secreted in the treasury and rarely seen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu of Han's time the Prince of Lu destroyed Confucius' house and obtained the Documents, Spring and Autumn, Analects, and Filial Piety; people no longer knew ancient script and called it "tadpole writing"; Han secreted it and it was rarely seen.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏初傳古文者，出於邯鄲淳。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Wei those who transmitted ancient script came from Handan Chun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wei those who transmitted ancient script came from Handan Chun.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬侯寫淳《尚書》，後以示淳，而淳不別。
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis Jing copied Chun's Documents and later showed it to Chun, yet Chun could not distinguish it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing copied Chun's Documents and later showed it to Chun, yet Chun could not distinguish it.

manualTranslations.zh: 至正始中，立三字石經，轉失淳法。
manualTranslations.literal: By the Zhengshi era the three-character stone classic was erected and gradually lost Chun's method.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By Zhengshi the three-character stone classic was erected and gradually lost Chun's method.

manualTranslations.zh: 因科斗之名，遂效其法。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of the name "tadpole," they then imitated its form.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of the name "tadpole," they then imitated its form.

manualTranslations.zh: 太康元年，汲縣民盜發魏襄王冢，得策書十餘萬言。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Taikang commoners of Ji County looted the tomb of King Xiang of Wei and obtained bamboo documents of more than one hundred thousand words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taikang 1 commoners of Ji County looted King Xiang of Wei's tomb and obtained more than one hundred thousand words of bamboo documents.

manualTranslations.zh: 案敬侯所書，猶有髣髴。」
manualTranslations.literal: Checking what Marquis Jing wrote, there is still a resemblance."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Checking what Marquis Jing wrote, there is still a resemblance."

manualTranslations.zh: 敬侯謂覬也。
manualTranslations.literal: Marquis Jing means Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing means Wei Ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 其序篆書曰：「秦時李斯號為工篆，諸山及銅人銘皆斯書也。
manualTranslations.literal: Its preface on seal script says: "In Qin times Li Si was styled master of seal script; inscriptions on mountains and bronze men were all in Si's writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its preface on seal script says: "In Qin Li Si was styled master of seal script; mountain and bronze inscriptions were all Si's writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢建初中，扶風曹喜少異於斯而亦稱善。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jianchu era of Han, Cao Xi of Fufeng differed slightly from Si yet was also called skilled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Han Jianchu, Cao Xi of Fufeng differed slightly from Si yet was also called skilled.

manualTranslations.zh: 邯鄲淳師焉，略究其妙。
manualTranslations.literal: Handan Chun studied under him and broadly investigated his subtleties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Handan Chun studied under him and broadly investigated his subtleties.

manualTranslations.zh: 韋誕師淳而不及也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei Dan studied under Chun but did not reach him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Dan studied under Chun but did not reach him.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和中，誕為武都太守，以能書留補侍中，魏氏寶器銘題皆誕書云。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Tahe era Dan was Governor of Wudu; because of his skill at writing he was retained and appointed Palace Attendant; inscriptions on Wei treasured vessels were all Dan's writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tahe, Dan was Governor of Wudu; for skill at writing he was retained as Palace Attendant; Wei treasured vessel inscriptions were all Dan's writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢末又有蔡邕采斯、喜之法，為古今雜形，然精密簡理不如淳也。」
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Han there was also Cai Yong, who took Si's and Xi's methods and made mixed forms ancient and modern, yet in precision and concise order he was not equal to Chun."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Han's end Cai Yong took Si's and Xi's methods and made mixed ancient and modern forms, yet in precision and order he was not equal to Chun."

manualTranslations.zh: 其序錄隷書，已略見《武紀》。
manualTranslations.literal: Its preface recording clerical script has already been briefly seen in the Wu ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its preface recording clerical script has already been briefly seen in the Wu ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「師宜官為大字，邯鄲淳為小字。
manualTranslations.literal: It also says: "Shi Yiguan wrote large characters; Handan Chun wrote small characters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It also says: "Shi Yiguan wrote large characters; Handan Chun wrote small characters.

manualTranslations.zh: 梁鵠謂淳得次仲法，然鵠之用筆盡其勢矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Hu held that Chun obtained Cao Cizhong's method, yet Hu's use of the brush exhausted its momentum."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang Hu held Chun obtained Cao Cizhong's method, yet Hu's brush exhausted its momentum."

manualTranslations.zh: 其序草書曰：「漢興而有草書，不知作者姓名。
manualTranslations.literal: Its preface on cursive script says: "When Han rose there was cursive script; the author's name is not known.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its preface on cursive script says: "When Han rose there was cursive script; the author's name is not known.

manualTranslations.zh: 至章帝時，齊相杜度號善作篇，後有崔瑗、崔寔亦皆稱工。
manualTranslations.literal: By Emperor Zhang's time Du Du of Qi, Chancellor, was styled skilled at composing pieces; afterward Cui Yuan and Cui Shi were also all called masters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By Emperor Zhang's time Du Du, Chancellor of Qi, was styled skilled at composing pieces; afterward Cui Yuan and Cui Shi were also called masters.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜氏然字甚安而書體微瘦，崔氏甚得筆勢而結字小疏。
manualTranslations.literal: The Du clan's characters were very settled yet the script form was slightly thin; the Cui clan greatly obtained brush momentum yet character formation was somewhat sparse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Du clan's characters were very settled yet the form was slightly thin; the Cui clan greatly obtained brush momentum yet formation was somewhat sparse.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘農張伯英者因而而轉精其巧。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Boying of Hongnong thereby refined the craft further.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Boying of Hongnong thereby refined the craft further.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡家之衣帛，必書而後練之，臨池學書，池水盡黑。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever household silk was dyed, he would write on it before boiling; studying calligraphy by the pool, the pool water all turned black.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever household silk was dyed, he wrote on it before boiling; studying by the pool, the pool water all turned black.

manualTranslations.zh: 下筆必為楷則，號『怱怱不暇草』，寸紙不見遺，至今世人尤寶之，韋仲將謂之草聖。
manualTranslations.literal: Every stroke he set down became a model; he was styled "too hurried for cursive"; not a inch of paper was left unused; to this day the world especially treasures it; Wei Zhongjiang called him sage of cursive script.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every stroke became a model; he was styled "too hurried for cursive"; not an inch of paper was wasted; the world still treasures it; Wei Zhongjiang called him sage of cursive script.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯英弟文舒者，次伯英。
manualTranslations.literal: Boying's younger brother Wenshu ranked next after Boying.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Boying's younger brother Wenshu ranked next after Boying.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有姜孟潁、梁孔達、田彥和及韋仲將之徒，皆伯英弟子，有名於世，然殊不及文舒也。」
manualTranslations.literal: There were also Jiang Mengying, Liang Kongda, Tian Yanhe, and followers of Wei Zhongjiang—all disciples of Boying, famed in the world, yet far inferior to Wenshu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There were also Jiang Mengying, Liang Kongda, Tian Yanhe, and followers of Wei Zhongjiang—all Boying's disciples, famed yet far inferior to Wenshu."

manualTranslations.zh: 樂安太守譙國夏侯惠、惠，淵子。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiahou Hui of Qiao, Administrator of Lean—Hui was Yuan's son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiahou Hui of Qiao, Administrator of Lean—Hui was Xiahou Yuan's son.

manualTranslations.zh: 事在
manualTranslations.literal: The account is in
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The account is in

manualTranslations.zh: 〈淵傳〉。
manualTranslations.literal: the biography of Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the biography of Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 陳郡太守任城孫該、《文章叙錄》曰：該字公達。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Gai of Rencheng, Administrator of Chen— the Wenzhang xulu says: Gai, courtesy name Gongda.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Gai of Rencheng, Administrator of Chen—the Wenzhang xulu says Gai, courtesy Gongda.

manualTranslations.zh: 彊志好學。
manualTranslations.literal: Strong in will and fond of learning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Strong in will and fond of learning.

manualTranslations.zh: 年二十，上計掾，召為郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: At twenty he was an accounting clerk sent upward and was summoned as Gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At twenty he was an accounting clerk sent upward and was summoned as Gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 著《魏書》。
manualTranslations.literal: He wrote the Book of Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wrote the Book of Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷博士司徒右長史，復還入著作。
manualTranslations.literal: He was moved to Erudite and Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then returned again to enter the composition office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was moved to Erudite and Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then returned to the composition office.

manualTranslations.zh: 景元二年卒官。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in office in the second year of Jingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in office in Jingyuan 2.

manualTranslations.zh: 郎中令河東杜摯等亦著文賦，頗傳於世。
manualTranslations.literal: Du Zhi of Hedong, Director of the Secretariat, and others also wrote literary rhapsodies, which circulated somewhat in the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Zhi of Hedong, Director of the Secretariat, and others also wrote literary rhapsodies, which circulated in the world.

manualTranslations.zh: 《文章叙錄》曰：摯字德魯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wenzhang xulu says: Zhi, courtesy name Delu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wenzhang xulu says Zhi, courtesy Delu.

manualTranslations.zh: 初上笳賦，署司徒軍謀吏。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he submitted a reed-pipe rhapsody and was appointed Staff Planning Officer to the Minister of Education.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first he submitted a reed-pipe rhapsody and was appointed Staff Planning Officer to the Minister of Education.

manualTranslations.zh: 後舉孝廉，除郎中，轉補校書。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, appointed Gentleman, and transferred to proofreading secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, appointed Gentleman, and transferred to proofreading secretary.

manualTranslations.zh: 摯與毌丘儉鄕里相親，故為詩與儉，求仙人藥一丸，欲以感切儉求助也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi and Guanqiu Jian were fellow townsmen and close; therefore he wrote a poem to Jian seeking one pill of immortal's medicine, wishing to move Jian by feeling and urge him to help.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhi and Guanqiu Jian were fellow townsmen and close; he wrote Jian a poem seeking one pill of immortal medicine, wishing to move him to help.

manualTranslations.zh: 其詩曰：「騏驥馬不試，婆娑槽櫪間。
manualTranslations.literal: The poem says: "The thoroughbred is not tried and sways between manger rails.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The poem says: "The thoroughbred is not tried and sways between manger rails.

manualTranslations.zh: 壯士志未伸，坎軻多辛酸。
manualTranslations.literal: The stalwart man's ambition is not yet fulfilled; rough roads hold much bitter sour.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The stalwart man's ambition is not yet fulfilled; rough roads hold much bitter sour.

manualTranslations.zh: 伊摯為媵臣，呂望身操竿；
manualTranslations.literal: Yi Yin was a secondary consort's minister; Lü Wang himself held a pole;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi Yin was a secondary consort's minister; Lü Wang himself held a pole;

manualTranslations.zh: 夷吾困商販，寗戚對牛歎；
manualTranslations.literal: Guan Zhong was trapped in trade; Ning Qi sighed to an ox;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong was trapped in trade; Ning Qi sighed to an ox;

manualTranslations.zh: 食其處監門，淮陰飢不餐；
manualTranslations.literal: Yishi was at the gatekeeper post; Huaiyin starved without a meal;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yishi was at the gatekeeper post; Huaiyin starved without a meal;

manualTranslations.zh: 買臣老負薪，妻畔呼不還，釋之宦十年，位不增故官。
manualTranslations.literal: Maichén in old age carried firewood; his wife called from the bank and would not return; Shizhi served ten years in office yet rank did not rise from the old post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Maichén in old age carried firewood; his wife called from the bank and would not return; Shizhi served ten years yet rank did not rise.

manualTranslations.zh: 才非八子倫，而與齊其患。
manualTranslations.literal: Talent is not of the Eight Masters' class, yet I share their affliction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talent is not of the Eight Masters' class, yet I share their affliction.

manualTranslations.zh: 無知不在此，袁盎未有言。
manualTranslations.literal: Ignorance is not here; Yuan Ang had no word.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ignorance is not here; Yuan Ang had no word.

manualTranslations.literal: Afflicted by this grave illness long, glory and guard are unsettled; hearing there is Han Zhong's medicine, I trust you to send one pill."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Afflicted by this grave illness long, glory and guard are unsettled; hearing there is Han Zhong's medicine, I trust you to send one pill."

manualTranslations.zh: 儉荅曰：「鳳鳥翔京邑，哀鳴有所思。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian replied: "The phoenix flies over the capital city, wailing with thoughts within.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian replied: "The phoenix flies over the capital city, wailing with thoughts within.

manualTranslations.zh: 才為聖世出，德音何不怡！
manualTranslations.literal: Talent emerges for a sage age—why is virtue's voice not joyful!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Talent emerges for a sage age—why is virtue's voice not joyful!

manualTranslations.zh: 八子未遭遇，今者遘明時。
manualTranslations.literal: The Eight Masters have not yet met fortune; now we encounter a bright time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Eight Masters have not yet met fortune; now we encounter a bright time.

manualTranslations.zh: 胡康出壟畒，楊偉無根基，飛騰沖雲天，奮迅協光熙。
manualTranslations.literal: Hu Kang came from the fields; Yang Wei has no foundation; soaring rushes through heaven, swift vigor joins bright glory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Kang came from the fields; Yang Wei has no foundation; soaring rushes through heaven, swift vigor joins bright glory.

manualTranslations.zh: 駿驥骨法異，伯樂觀知之，但當養羽翮，鴻舉必有期。
manualTranslations.literal: The thoroughbred's bone method differs; Bo Le seeing knows it; one need only nurture wing-feathers and the great flight must have its season.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The thoroughbred's bone method differs; Bo Le seeing knows it; one need only nurture wing-feathers and great flight must have its season.

manualTranslations.zh: 體無纖微疾，安用問良醫？
manualTranslations.literal: The body has no slightest illness—why ask a good physician?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The body has no slightest illness—why ask a good physician?

manualTranslations.zh: 聯翩輕栖集，還為燕雀嗤。
manualTranslations.literal: Fluttering lightly they perch together and in the end are mocked by swallows and sparrows.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fluttering lightly they perch together and in the end are mocked by swallows and sparrows.

manualTranslations.zh: 韓衆藥雖良，或更不能治。
manualTranslations.literal: Han Zhong's medicine though good perhaps again cannot cure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han Zhong's medicine though good perhaps again cannot cure.

manualTranslations.zh: 悠悠千里情，薄言荅嘉詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Far, far the feeling of a thousand li; in brief words I reply to your fine poem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Far, far the feeling of a thousand li; in brief words I reply to your fine poem.

manualTranslations.zh: 信心感諸中，中實不在辭。」
manualTranslations.literal: Trust and feeling move within the heart; the heart's truth is not in words."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Trust and feeling move within the heart; the heart's truth is not in words."

manualTranslations.zh: 摯竟不得遷，卒于祕書。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi in the end was not promoted and died in the Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhi in the end was not promoted and died in the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The He clan of Lujiang

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Family Tradition

manualTranslations.literal: says: In Emperor Ming's time there was Hu Kang of Qiao, aged fifteen, sent up for unusual talent; he also stated gains and losses and asked to be tried in a difficult county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: says: In Emperor Ming's time there was Hu Kang of Qiao, aged fifteen, sent up for unusual talent; he stated gains and losses and asked to be tried in a difficult county.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔特引見。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict specially summoned him for audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict specially summoned him for audience.

manualTranslations.zh: 衆論翕然，號為神童。
manualTranslations.literal: Public discussion was unanimous and styled him a divine child.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Public discussion was unanimous and styled him a divine child.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔付祕書，使博覽典籍。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict assigned him to the Secretariat to make him broadly read the classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict assigned him to the Secretariat to make him broadly read the classics.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝以問祕書丞何禎：「康才何如？」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor asked Secretary Director He Zhen: "How is Kang's talent?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Secretary Director He Zhen: "How is Kang's talent?"

manualTranslations.zh: 禎荅曰：「康雖有才，性質不端，必有負敗。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen replied: "Though Kang has talent, his nature is not upright; he is sure to meet failure."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen replied: "Though Kang has talent, his nature is not upright; he is sure to meet failure."

manualTranslations.zh: 後果以過見譴。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was indeed censured for an offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he was indeed censured for an offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 疑是孟康。
manualTranslations.literal: I suspect this is Meng Kang.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kang's career is seen in

manualTranslations.literal: the biography of Du Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the biography of Du Shu.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Wei is seen in

manualTranslations.literal: the biography of Cao Shuang.

sourceRange.text: 嘏常論才性同異，鍾會集而論之。《傅子》曰：嘏旣達治好正，而有清理識要，好論才性，原本精微，尠能及之。司隷校尉鍾會年甚少，嘏以明智交會。臣松之案：傅子前云嘏了夏侯之必敗，不與之交，而此云與鍾會善。愚以爲夏侯玄以名重致患，釁由外至；鍾會以利動取敗，禍自己出。然則夏侯之危兆難覩，而鍾氏之敗形易照也。嘏若了夏侯之必危，而不見鍾會之將敗，則爲識有所蔽，難以言通；若皆知其不終，而情有彼此，是爲厚薄由于愛憎，奚豫於成敗哉？以愛憎爲厚薄，又虧於雅體矣。傅子此論，非所以益嘏也。嘉平末，賜爵關內侯。高貴鄕公即尊位，進封武鄕亭侯。正元二年春，毌丘儉、文欽作亂。或以司馬景王不宜自行，可遣太尉孚往，惟嘏及王肅勸之。景王遂行。《漢晉春秋》曰曰：嘏固勸景王行，景王未從。嘏重言曰：「淮、楚兵勁，而儉等負力遠鬬，其鋒未易當也。若諸將戰有利鈍，大勢一失，則公事敗矣。」是時景王新割目瘤，創甚，聞嘏言，蹶然而起曰：「我請輿疾而東。」以嘏守尚書僕射，俱東。儉、欽破敗，嘏有謀焉。及景王薨，嘏與司馬文王徑還洛陽，文王遂以輔政。語在〈鍾會傳〉。《世語》曰：景王疾甚，以朝政授傅嘏，嘏不敢受。及薨，嘏祕不發喪，以景王命召文王於許昌，領公軍焉。孫盛評曰：晉宣、景、文王之相魏也，權重相承，王業基矣。豈蕞爾傅嘏所宜間厠？世語所云，斯不然矣。會由是有自矜色，嘏戒之曰：「子志大其量，而勳業難爲也，可不慎哉！」嘏以功進封陽鄕侯，增邑六百戸，并前千二百戸。是歳薨，時年四十七，追贈太常，謚曰元侯。《傅子》曰：初，李豐與嘏同州，少有顯名，早歷大官，內外稱之，嘏又不善也。謂同志曰：「豐飾偽而多疑，矜小失而昧於權利，若處庸庸者可也，自任機事，遭明者必死。」豐後爲中書令，與夏侯玄俱禍，卒如嘏言。嘏自少與兾州刺史裴徽、散騎常侍荀甝善，徽、甝早亡。又與鎮北將軍何曾、司空陳泰、尚書僕射荀顗、後將軍鍾毓並善相友綜朝事，俱爲名臣。子祗嗣。咸熈中開建五等，以嘏著勳前朝，改封祗涇原子。《晉諸公贊》曰：祗字子莊，嘏少子也。晉永嘉中至司空。祗子宣，字世弘。《世語》稱宣以公正知名，位至御史中丞。宣弟暢，字世道，祕書丞，沒在胡中。著《晉諸公贊》及晉公卿禮秩故事。

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏常論才性同異，鍾會集而論之。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu often discussed the sameness and difference of talent and nature; Zhong Hui collected and discoursed on it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu often discussed the sameness and difference of talent and nature; Zhong Hui collected and discoursed on it.

manualTranslations.zh: 《傅子》曰：嘏旣達治好正，而有清理識要，好論才性，原本精微，尠能及之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Fu zi says: Gu was already accomplished, fond of governance and upright action, and had clear judgment and grasp of essentials; he loved to discuss talent and nature, tracing origins to subtle principles—few could match him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Fu zi says Gu was accomplished, fond of upright governance, with clear judgment; he loved discussing talent and nature at a subtle level—few could match him.

manualTranslations.zh: 司隷校尉鍾會年甚少，嘏以明智交會。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of Retainers Zhong Hui was very young; Gu befriended him through insight and wisdom.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Director of Retainers Zhong Hui was very young; Fu Gu befriended him through insight and wisdom.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：傅子前云嘏了夏侯之必敗，不與之交，而此云與鍾會善。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject Songzhi notes: The Fu zi earlier says Gu foresaw Xiahou's certain defeat and would not associate with him, yet here says he was on good terms with Zhong Hui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: The Fu zi earlier says Fu Gu foresaw Xiahou's defeat and would not associate with him, yet here says he was on good terms with Zhong Hui.

manualTranslations.zh: 愚以為夏侯玄以名重致患，釁由外至；
manualTranslations.literal: I think Xiahou Xuan brought trouble through heavy fame, the omen coming from outside;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I think Xiahou Xuan brought trouble through heavy fame, the omen coming from outside;

manualTranslations.zh: 鍾會以利動取敗，禍自己出。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong Hui met defeat through profit-seeking action, disaster issuing from himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui met defeat through profit-seeking action, disaster issuing from himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 然則夏侯之危兆難覩，而鍾氏之敗形易照也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Xiahou's peril was hard to see beforehand, while the Zhong clan's fall was easy to discern.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus Xiahou's peril was hard to see beforehand, while the Zhong clan's fall was easy to discern.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏若了夏侯之必危，而不見鍾會之將敗，則為識有所蔽，難以言通；
manualTranslations.literal: If Gu foresaw Xiahou's certain danger yet did not see Zhong Hui's coming defeat, then his insight was partially blind and hard to reconcile in argument;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Fu Gu foresaw Xiahou's danger yet did not see Zhong Hui's defeat, his insight was partially blind and hard to reconcile;

manualTranslations.zh: 若皆知其不終，而情有彼此，是為厚薄由于愛憎，奚豫於成敗哉？
manualTranslations.literal: if he knew both would not end well yet felt differently toward them, that would mean warmth and coldness arose from love and hate—what has that to do with success or failure?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if he knew both would fail yet felt differently toward them, warmth and coldness arose from love and hate—what has that to do with success or failure?

manualTranslations.zh: 以愛憎為厚薄，又虧於雅體矣。
manualTranslations.literal: To make warmth and coldness depend on love and hate again falls short of elegant form.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To make warmth and coldness depend on love and hate again falls short of elegant form.

manualTranslations.zh: 傅子此論，非所以益嘏也。
manualTranslations.literal: This discussion in the Fu zi is not what would enhance Gu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This discussion in the Fu zi is not what would enhance Fu Gu.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平末，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Jiaping he was given the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of Jiaping he was given the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 高貴鄕公即尊位，進封武鄕亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Duke of Gaogui took the honored throne, Gu was advanced to Marquis of Wuxiang Village.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Gaogui took the honored throne, he was advanced to Marquis of Wuxiang Village.

manualTranslations.zh: 正元二年春，毌丘儉、文欽作亂。
manualTranslations.literal: In spring of the second year of Zhengyuan, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In spring of Zhengyuan 2, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 或以司馬景王不宜自行，可遣太尉孚往，惟嘏及王肅勸之。
manualTranslations.literal: Some held that Sima Jingwang should not go in person and that Grand Commandant Fu could be sent; only Gu and Wang Su urged him to go.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some held Sima Jingwang should not go in person and Grand Commandant Fu could be sent; only Fu Gu and Wang Su urged him to go.

manualTranslations.zh: 景王遂行。
manualTranslations.literal: Jingwang thereupon set out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingwang thereupon set out.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：嘏固勸景王行，景王未從。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Jin chunqiu says: Gu firmly urged Jingwang to go, and Jingwang at first did not follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Jin chunqiu says Fu Gu firmly urged Jingwang to go, and Jingwang at first did not follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏重言曰：「淮、楚兵勁，而儉等負力遠鬬，其鋒未易當也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu spoke again, saying, "The Huai and Chu troops are strong, and Jian and the others rely on their strength to fight far away; their edge is not easy to meet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu spoke again: "Huai and Chu troops are strong; Jian and the others rely on strength to fight far away—their edge is not easy to meet.

manualTranslations.zh: 若諸將戰有利鈍，大勢一失，則公事敗矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: If the generals meet with mixed fortune in battle and the great momentum is once lost, then the lord's affair is ruined."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the generals meet mixed fortune and the great momentum is lost, the lord's affair is ruined."

manualTranslations.zh: 是時景王新割目瘤，創甚，聞嘏言，蹶然而起曰：「我請輿疾而東。」
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Jingwang had newly cut a tumor from his eye; the wound was severe; hearing Gu's words, he started up and said, "I ask to go east in a litter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingwang had newly cut an eye tumor; the wound was severe; hearing Fu Gu, he started up and said, "I ask to go east in a litter."

manualTranslations.zh: 以嘏守尚書僕射，俱東。
manualTranslations.literal: He left Gu as acting Director of the Masters of Writing and went east together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He left Fu Gu as acting Director of the Masters of Writing and went east together.

manualTranslations.zh: 儉、欽破敗，嘏有謀焉。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jian and Qin were defeated, Gu had a share in the planning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jian and Qin were defeated, Fu Gu had a share in the planning.

manualTranslations.zh: 及景王薨，嘏與司馬文王徑還洛陽，文王遂以輔政。
manualTranslations.literal: When Jingwang died, Gu and Sima Wenwang returned directly to Luoyang, and Wenwang thereupon took charge of government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Jingwang died, Fu Gu and Sima Wenwang returned directly to Luoyang, and Wenwang took charge of government.

manualTranslations.zh: 語在
manualTranslations.literal: The account is in
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The account is in

manualTranslations.zh: 〈鍾會傳〉。
manualTranslations.literal: the biography of Zhong Hui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the biography of Zhong Hui.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：景王疾甚，以朝政授傅嘏，嘏不敢受。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu says: When Jingwang was gravely ill, he entrusted court affairs to Fu Gu, and Gu did not dare accept.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says: When Jingwang was gravely ill, he entrusted court affairs to Fu Gu, who did not dare accept.

manualTranslations.zh: 及薨，嘏祕不發喪，以景王命召文王於許昌，領公軍焉。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, Gu kept the death secret, and by Jingwang's order summoned Wenwang from Xuchang to lead the ducal armies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he died, Fu Gu kept the death secret and by Jingwang's order summoned Wenwang from Xuchang to lead the ducal armies.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫盛評曰：晉宣、景、文王之相魏也，權重相承，王業基矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Sheng comments: When the Jin founders Xuan, Jing, and Wenwang assisted Wei, power and weight succeeded one another and the royal enterprise was founded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng comments: When the Jin founders Xuan, Jing, and Wenwang assisted Wei, power succeeded one another and the royal enterprise was founded.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈蕞爾傅嘏所宜間厠？
manualTranslations.literal: How could a mere Fu Gu properly intervene?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How could a mere Fu Gu properly intervene?

manualTranslations.zh: 世語所云，斯不然矣。
manualTranslations.literal: What the Shiyu says is thus not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What the Shiyu says is thus not so.

manualTranslations.zh: 會由是有自矜色，嘏戒之曰：「子志大其量，而勳業難為也，可不慎哉！」
manualTranslations.literal: Hui thereafter had a self-congratulatory air; Gu admonished him, saying, "Your ambition exceeds your measure, yet achievement is hard to accomplish—can you not be careful!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui thereafter looked self-congratulatory; Fu Gu admonished him: "Your ambition exceeds your measure, yet achievement is hard—can you not be careful!"

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏以功進封陽鄕侯，增邑六百戸，并前千二百戸。
manualTranslations.literal: Gu was advanced for merit to Marquis of Yangxiang, with an added fief of six hundred households, twelve hundred in all with the former.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Gu was advanced for merit to Marquis of Yangxiang, with six hundred added households, twelve hundred in all with the former.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歳薨，時年四十七，追贈太常，謚曰元侯。
manualTranslations.literal: That year he died, aged forty-seven; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies with the posthumous title Marquis Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year he died at forty-seven; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies with the posthumous title Marquis Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 《傅子》曰：初，李豐與嘏同州，少有顯名，早歷大官，內外稱之，嘏又不善也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Fu zi says: At first Li Feng was from the same province as Gu and from youth had a bright name; he early held high office and was praised inside and outside; Gu did not think well of him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Fu zi says: Li Feng was Fu Gu's countryman and from youth had a bright name; he early held high office and was praised everywhere; Gu did not think well of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 謂同志曰：「豐飾偽而多疑，矜小失而昧於權利，若處庸庸者可也，自任機事，遭明者必死。」
manualTranslations.literal: He told like-minded men, "Feng adorns falsehood and is much given to suspicion; he prides himself on small gains and is blind to power and profit—if placed among the mediocre it would do, but if he takes charge of critical affairs, meeting a clear-sighted man he is sure to die."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He told like-minded men, "Feng adorns falsehood and is suspicious; he prides himself on small gains and is blind to power—among mediocrity it would do, but in critical affairs, meeting a clear-sighted man he will die."

manualTranslations.zh: 豐後為中書令，與夏侯玄俱禍，卒如嘏言。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Feng became Director of the Secretariat and suffered disaster together with Xiahou Xuan, ending just as Gu had said.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Feng became Director of the Secretariat and suffered disaster with Xiahou Xuan, ending just as Fu Gu said.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘏自少與兾州刺史裴徽、散騎常侍荀甝善，徽、甝早亡。
manualTranslations.literal: From youth Gu was on good terms with Pei Hui, Inspector of Ji Province, and Xun Yi, Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse; Hui and Yi died early.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth Fu Gu was close to Pei Hui, Inspector of Ji Province, and Xun Yi, Regular Attendant of the Fast Horse; both died early.

manualTranslations.zh: 又與鎮北將軍何曾、司空陳泰、尚書僕射荀顗、後將軍鍾毓並善相友綜朝事，俱為名臣。
manualTranslations.literal: He was also on good terms and friendly with General Who Guards the North He Ceng, Minister of Works Chen Tai, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Yi, and Rear General Zhong Yu, jointly discussing court affairs—all were famed ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was also close to He Ceng, Chen Tai, Xun Yi, and Zhong Yu, jointly discussing court affairs—all famed ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 子祗嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熈中開建五等，以嘏著勳前朝，改封祗涇原子。
manualTranslations.literal: When the five ranks were opened in Xianxi, because Gu's merit in the former dynasty was outstanding, Zhi was re-enfeoffed as Baron of Jingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the five ranks opened in Xianxi, because Fu Gu's former merit was outstanding, Zhi was re-enfeoffed as Baron of Jingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：祗字子莊，嘏少子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jin zhugong zan says: Zhi, courtesy name Zizhuang, was Gu's youngest son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin zhugong zan says Zhi, courtesy Zizhuang, was Fu Gu's youngest son.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉永嘉中至司空。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Yongjia era of Jin he reached Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jin Yongjia he reached Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 祗子宣，字世弘。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi's son Xuan, courtesy name Shihong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Xuan, courtesy Shihong.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》稱宣以公正知名，位至御史中丞。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu praises Xuan as famed for fairness and justice and says he reached Censor-in-Chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu praises Xuan as famed for fairness and justice and says he reached Censor-in-Chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣弟暢，字世道，祕書丞，沒在胡中。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Chang, courtesy name Shidao, was Secretary Director and perished among the barbarians.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Chang, courtesy Shidao, was Secretary Director and perished among the barbarians.

manualTranslations.zh: 著《晉諸公贊》及晉公卿禮秩故事。
manualTranslations.literal: He wrote the Jin zhugong zan and the precedents of Jin ranks and ritual for lords and ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wrote the Jin zhugong zan and the precedents of Jin ranks and ritual for lords and ministers.

sourceRange.text: 」毓对曰：帝納其言，即诏作考课法。

localRange.text: 毓对曰：名不足以致異人，而可以得常士。常士畏教慕善，然後有名，非所当疾也。愚臣既不足以识異人，又主者正以循名案常爲职，但当有以验其後。故古者敷奏以言，明试以功。今考绩之法废，而以毁誉相进退，故真伪浑杂，虚实相蒙。帝納其言，即诏作考课法。

sourceRange.text: 羣转爲侍中，领丞相东西曹掾。在朝无適无莫，雅杖名義，不以非道假人。文帝在东宫，深敬器焉，待以交友之礼，常叹曰：「自吾有回，门人日以亲。」及即王位，封羣昌武亭侯，徙爲尚書。制九品官人之法，羣所建也。及践阼，遷尚書仆射，加侍中，徙尚書令，进爵颖鄉侯。帝征孫权，至广陵，使羣领中领軍。帝還，假节，都督水軍。還许昌，以羣爲镇軍大將軍，领中护軍，录尚書事。帝寝疾，羣與曹真、司马宣王等并受遺诏辅政。明帝即位，进封颍阴侯，增邑五百，并前千三百户，與征东大將軍曹休、中軍大將軍曹真、抚軍大將軍司马宣王并开府。顷之，爲司空，故录尚書事。是時，帝初莅政，羣上疏曰：诗称‘仪刑文王，万邦作孚’；

sourceRange.text: 淮薨，泰代爲征西將軍，假节都督雍、凉諸軍事。後年，雍州刺史王经白泰，云姜维、夏侯霸欲三道向祁山、石营、金城，求进兵爲翅，使凉州軍至枹罕，討蜀护軍向祁山。泰量贼勢终不能三道，且兵勢恶分，凉州未宜越境，报经：「审其定问，知所趣向，须东西勢合乃进。」時维等將數万人至枹罕，趣狄道。泰敕经进屯狄道，须軍到，乃規取之。泰进軍陳仓。會经所统諸軍於故關與贼戰不利，经辄渡洮。泰以经不堅据狄道，必有他变。并遣五营在前，泰率諸軍继之。经巳與维戰，大敗，以万餘人還保狄道城，餘皆奔散。维乘胜圍狄道。泰軍上邽，分兵守要，晨夜进前。邓艾、胡奋、王祕亦到，即與艾、祕等分爲三軍，进到陇西。艾等以爲「王经精卒破衄於西，贼众大盛，乘胜之兵既不可当，而將軍以乌合之卒，继敗軍之後，將士失气，陇右倾荡。古人有言：‘蝮蛇螫手，壮士解其腕。’孫子曰：‘兵有所不擊，地有所不守。’盖小有所失而大有所全故也。今陇右之害，过於蝮蛇，狄道之地，非徒不守之謂。姜维之兵，是所辟之锋。不如割险自保，观衅待弊，然後进救，此计之得者也。」泰曰：姜维提轻兵深入，正欲与我争锋原野，求一战之利。

sourceRange.text: 太祖辟矫爲司空掾属，除相令，征南長史，彭城、乐陵太守，魏郡西部都尉。曲周民父病，以牛祷，县結正弃市。矫曰：「此孝子也。」表赦之。遷魏郡太守。時系囚千數，至有历年，矫以爲周有三典之制，汉约三章之法，今惜轻重之理，而忽久系之患，可謂谬矣。悉自览罪状，一時论决。大軍东征，入爲丞相長史。軍還，复爲魏郡，转西曹属。從征汉中，還爲尚書。行前未到鄴，太祖崩洛阳，羣臣拘常，以爲太子即位，当须诏命。矫曰：「王薨于外，天下惶惧。太子宜割哀即位，以系遠近之望。且又爱子在侧，彼此生变，則社稷危矣。」即具官备礼，一日皆办。明旦，以王後令，策太子即位，大赦荡然。文帝曰：「陳季弼臨大节，明略过人，信一時之俊杰也。」帝既践阼，转署吏部，封高陵亭侯，遷尚書令。明帝即位，进爵东鄉侯，邑六百户。车驾尝卒至尚書门，矫跪问帝曰：「陛下欲何之？」帝曰：「欲案行文書耳。」矫曰：「此自臣职分，非陛下所宜臨也。若臣不称其职，則请就黜退。陛下宜還。」帝惭，回车而反。其亮直如此。《世语》曰：刘晔以先进见幸，因谮矫专权。矫惧，以问长子本，本不知所出。次子骞曰：“主上明圣，大人大臣，今若不合，不过不作公耳。”后数日，帝见矫，矫又问二子，骞曰：“陛下意解，故见大人也。”既入，尽日，帝曰：“刘晔构君，朕有以迹君；朕心故已了。”以金五鉼授之，矫辞。帝曰：“岂以为小惠？君已知朕心，顾君妻子未知故也。”帝忧社稷，问矫：“司马公忠正，可谓社稷之臣乎？”矫曰：“朝廷之望；社稷，未知也。”加侍中光禄大夫，遷司徒。景初元年薨，谥曰贞侯。魏氏春秋曰：矫本刘氏子，出嗣舅氏而婚于本族。徐宣每非之，庭议其阙。太祖惜矫才量，欲拥全之，乃下令曰：“丧乱已来，风教彫薄，谤议之言，难用褒贬。自建安五年已前，一切勿论。其以断前诽议者，以其罪罪之。

sourceRange.text: 幽州刺史毌丘俭上疏曰：「陛下即位已來，未有可書。吴、蜀恃险，未可卒平，聊可以此方无用之士克定辽东。」臻曰：「俭所陳皆戰國细术，非王者之事也。吴频岁称兵，寇乱边境，而犹案甲养士，未果寻致討者，诚以百姓疲劳故也。且渊生長海表，相承三世，外抚戎夷，内脩戰射，而俭欲以偏軍長驱，朝至夕卷，知其妄矣。」俭行軍遂不利。臻遷爲司空，徙司徒。正始中，进爵長垣侯，邑千户，封一子列侯。初，太祖久不立太子，而方奇贵臨菑侯。丁儀等爲之羽翼，劝臻自結，臻以大義拒之。及文帝即位，东海王霖有寵，帝问臻：「平原侯何如？」臻称明德美而终不言。曹爽辅政，使夏侯玄宣指，欲引臻入守尚書令，及爲弟求婚，皆不许。固乞逊位。诏曰：「昔干木偃息，義压强秦；留侯颐神，不忘楚事。谠言嘉謀，望不吝焉。」赐宅一区，位特进，秩如三司。薨，追赠太尉，谥曰敬侯。

sourceRange.text: 在官二十三年，轉為太常，旬日遷司空，後徙司徒。太傅司馬宣王奏免曹爽，皇太后詔召柔假節行大將軍事，據爽營。太傅謂柔曰：「君為周勃矣。」爽誅，進封萬歲鄉侯。高貴鄉公即位，進封安國侯，轉為太尉。常道鄉公即位，增邑并前四千，前後封二子亭侯。景元四年，年九十薨，謚曰元侯。孫渾嗣。咸熈中，開建五等，以柔等著勳前朝，改封渾昌陸子。《晉諸公贊》曰：柔長子儁，大將軍掾，次誕，歷三州刺史、太僕。誕放率不倫，而決烈過人。次光，字宣茂，少習家業，明練法理。晉武帝世，為黃沙御史，與中丞同，遷守廷尉，後即真。兄誕與光異操，謂光小節，常輕侮之，而光事誕愈謹。終於尚書令。追贈司空。

localRange.text: 柔上疏曰：「聖王之御世，莫不以廣農為務，儉用為資。夫農廣則穀積，用儉則財畜，畜財積穀而有憂患之虞者，未之有也。古者，一夫不耕，或為之饑；一婦不織，或為之寒。中閒已來，百姓供給衆役，親田者旣減，加頃復有獵禁，羣鹿犯暴，殘食生苗，處處為害，所傷不貲。民雖障防，力不能禦。至如熒陽左右，周數百里，歲略不收，元元之命，實可矜傷。方今天下生財者甚少，而麋鹿之損者甚多。卒有兵戎之役，凶年之災，將無以待之。惟陛下覽先聖之所念，愍稼穡之艱難，寬放民間，使得捕鹿，遂除其禁，則衆庶久濟，莫不恱預矣。〈《魏名臣奏》載柔上疏曰：「臣深思陛下所以不早取此鹿者，誠欲使極蕃息，然後大取以為軍國之用。

context.beforeSource: 是時，殺禁地鹿者身死，財產沒官，有能覺告者厚加賞賜。
context.afterSource: 然臣竊以為今鹿但有日耗，終無從得多也。

localRange.text: 柔上疏曰：「二虜狡猾，潛自講肄，謀動干戈，未圖束手；宜畜養將士，繕治甲兵，以逸待之。而頃興造殿舍，上下勞擾；若使吳、蜀知人虛實，通謀并勢，復俱送死，甚不易也。昔漢文惜十家之資，不營小臺之娛；去病慮匈奴之害，不遑治第之事。況今所損者非惟百金之費，所憂者非徒北狄之患乎？可粗成見所營立，以充朝宴之儀。訖罷作者，使得就農。二方平定，復可徐興。昔軒轅以二十五子，傳祚彌遠；周室以姬國四十，歷年滋多。陛下聦達，窮理盡性，而頃皇子連多夭逝，熊羆之祥又未感應。羣下之心，莫不悒戚。周禮，天子后妃以下百二十人，嬪嬙之儀，旣以盛矣。竊聞後庭之數，或復過之，聖嗣不昌，殆能由此。臣愚以為可妙簡淑媛，以備內官之數，其餘盡遣還家。且以育精養神，專靜為寶。如此，則螽斯之徵，可庶而致矣。帝報曰：「知卿忠允，乃心王室，輒克昌言；

sourceRange.text: 時匈奴王劉靖部衆彊盛，而鮮卑數寇邊，乃以禮為并州刺史，加振武將軍，使持節，護匈奴中郎將。往見太傅司馬宣王，有忿色而無言。宣王曰：「卿得并州，少邪？恚理分界失分乎？今當遠別，何不懽也！」禮曰：「何明公言之乖細也！禮雖不德，豈以官位往事為意邪？本謂明公齊蹤伊、呂，匡輔魏室，上報明帝之託，下建萬世之勳。今社稷將危，天下兇兇，此禮之所以不恱也。」因涕泣橫流。宣王曰：「且止，忍不可忍。」爽誅後，入為司隷校尉，凡臨七郡五州，皆有威信。遷司空，封大利亭侯，邑一百戶。禮與盧毓同郡時輩，而情好不睦。為人雖互有長短，然名位略齊云。嘉平二年250年薨，謚曰景侯。孫元嗣。

manualTranslations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu king Liu Jing's following was strong, while the Xianbei repeatedly raided the borders; thereupon Li was made Inspector of Bing province, given the additional title General Who Inspires Awe, granted staff of authority, and made Protector of the Xiongnu Colonel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With the Xiongnu king Liu Jing powerful and Xianbei raids mounting, Sun Li was named inspector of Bing province, made General Who Inspires Awe with staff of authority, and appointed Protector of the Xiongnu Colonel.

manualTranslations.zh: 往見太傅司馬宣王，有忿色而無言。
manualTranslations.literal: He went to see Grand Tutor Sima Yi with an angry look and without speaking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he went to take leave of Grand Tutor Sima Yi, his face showed anger and he said nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王曰：「卿得并州，少邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Yi said: "You receive Bing province—is that too little?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, "You are getting Bing province—is that too little for you?

manualTranslations.zh: 恚理分界失分乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Are you angry that the boundary settlement lost you ground?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Are you angry that the border settlement cheated you?

manualTranslations.zh: 今當遠別，何不懽也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Now we must part far apart—why are you not pleased!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We part for a long posting—why so glum?"

manualTranslations.zh: 禮曰：「何明公言之乖細也！
manualTranslations.literal: Li said: "How far from the mark your words are, my lord!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Li answered, "My lord, how petty that sounds!

manualTranslations.zh: 禮雖不德，豈以官位往事為意邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Though Li lacks virtue, how could he take office and past affairs to heart?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am no paragon, but surely you do not think I care about rank or old grievances?

manualTranslations.zh: 本謂明公齊蹤伊、呂，匡輔魏室，上報明帝之託，下建萬世之勳。
manualTranslations.literal: I had supposed my lord would match the tracks of Yi Yin and Lü Wang, support and assist the house of Wei, repay above Emperor Ming's entrustment, and below establish merit for ten thousand generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I thought you would walk in the steps of Yi Yin and Lü Wang, shore up Wei, honor Emperor Ming's dying charge, and win eternal fame.

manualTranslations.zh: 今社稷將危，天下兇兇，此禮之所以不恱也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now the altars of state are about to be endangered and All under Heaven is turbulent—this is why Li is not pleased."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the realm totters and the empire seethes—that is why I am not pleased."

manualTranslations.zh: 因涕泣橫流。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon tears streamed across his face.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tears poured down his face as he spoke.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王曰：「且止，忍不可忍。」
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Yi said: "Stop—forbear what cannot be borne."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, "Enough—bear what seems unbearable."

manualTranslations.zh: 爽誅後，入為司隷校尉，凡臨七郡五州，皆有威信。
manualTranslations.literal: After Shuang was executed, he entered as Colonel Director of Retainers; wherever he oversaw seven commanderies and five provinces, he had authority and trust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Shuang's fall he became colonel director of retainers; in seven commanderies and five provinces under his charge he won solid authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷司空，封大利亭侯，邑一百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as village marquis of Dali with a fief of one hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as village marquis of Dali with a hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 禮與盧毓同郡時輩，而情好不睦。
manualTranslations.literal: Li and Lu Yu were contemporaries of the same commandery, yet their feelings and friendship were not harmonious.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Li and Lu Yu were hometown contemporaries, but they did not get along.

manualTranslations.zh: 為人雖互有長短，然名位略齊云。
manualTranslations.literal: As men they each had strengths and shortcomings, yet their fame and rank were roughly equal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each had his faults and virtues, yet their standing was much the same.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Jiaping 2 (250); his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

localRange.text: 又上疏曰：「生有益於民，死猶不害於民。況臣備位台司，在職日淺，未能宣揚聖德以廣益黎庶。寢疾彌留，奄即幽冥。方今百姓農務，不宜勞役，乞不令洛陽吏民供設喪具。懼國典有常，使臣私願不得展從，謹冒以聞，惟蒙哀許。帝得表嗟歎，乃詔曰：「故司徒韓曁，積德履行，忠以立朝，至於黃髮，直亮不虧。旣登三事，望獲毗輔之助，如何奄忽，天命不永！曾參臨沒，易簀以禮；晏嬰尚儉，遣車降制。今司徒知命，遺言卹民，必欲崇約，可謂善始令終者也。其喪禮所設，皆如故事，勿有所闕。時賜溫明祕器，衣一稱，五時朝服，玉具劒佩。

sourceRange.text: 」景初元年，司徒、司空並缺，散騎侍郎孟康薦林曰：「夫宰相者，天下之所瞻效，誠宜得秉忠履正本德杖義之士，足為海內所師表者。竊見司隷校尉崔林，稟自然之正性，體高雅之弘量。論其所長以比古人，忠直不回則史魚之儔，清儉守約則季文之匹也。牧守州郡，所在而治，及為外司，萬里肅齊，誠台輔之妙器，衮職之良才也。」後年遂為司空，封安陽亭侯，邑六百戶。三公封列侯，自林始也。臣松之以為漢封丞相邑，為荀恱所譏。魏封三公，其失同也。頃之，又進封安陽鄉侯。

manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu, the Minister over the Masses and Minister of Works were both vacant; Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Meng Kang recommended Lin, saying: "The chief ministers are what All under Heaven looks to and imitates; truly one ought to obtain men who hold loyalty, tread the upright path, root themselves in virtue, and uphold righteousness—men sufficient to be models for the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 (237), with both the Minister over the Masses and Minister of Works vacant, attendant gentleman Meng Kang recommended Cui Lin: "Chief ministers are what the empire watches and imitates; we need men of loyalty, rectitude, rooted virtue, and upheld righteousness—men fit to be models for the realm.

manualTranslations.literal: I have observed Colonel Director of Retainers Cui Lin, endowed with a naturally upright nature and embodying a lofty and broad capacity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I see Colonel Director of Retainers Cui Lin, endowed with upright nature and lofty, broad capacity.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Measured against antiquity, his blunt loyalty rivals Shi Yu; his purity and frugality match Ji Wen.

items.sourceTextOverride: 景初元年，司徒、司空並缺，散騎侍郎孟康薦林曰：「夫宰相者，天下之所瞻效，誠宜得秉忠履正本德杖義之士，足為海內所師表者。竊見司隷校尉崔林，稟自然之正性，體高雅之弘量。論其所長以比古人，忠直不回則史魚之儔，清儉守約則季文之匹也。牧守州郡，所在而治，及為外司，萬里肅齊，誠台輔之妙器，衮職之良才也。」後年遂為司空，封安陽亭侯，邑六百戶。三公封列侯，自林始也。臣松之以為漢封丞相邑，為荀恱所譏。魏封三公，其失同也。頃之，又進封安陽鄉侯。

localRange.text: 時博士執經，柔上疏曰：「臣聞遵道重學，聖人洪訓；褒文崇儒，帝者明義。昔漢末陵遲，禮樂崩壞，雄戰虎爭，以戰陣為務，遂使儒林之羣，幽隱而不顯。太祖初興，愍其如此，在於撥亂之際，並使郡縣立教學之官。高祖即位，遂闡其業，興復辟雍，州立課試，於是天下之士，復聞庠序之教，親俎豆之禮焉。陛下臨政，允迪叡哲，敷弘大猷，光濟先軌，雖夏啟之承基，周成之繼業，誠無以加也。然今博士皆經明行脩，一國清選，而使遷除限不過長，懼非所以崇顯儒術，帥勵怠惰也。孔子稱『舉善而教不能則勸』，故楚禮申公，學士銳精，漢隆卓茂，搢紳競慕。臣以為博士者，道之淵藪，六藝所宗，宜隨學行優劣，待以不次之位。敦崇道教，以勸學者，於化為弘。帝納之。

localRange.text: 乃詔曰：「昔先聖旣沒，而其遺言餘教，著於六藝。六藝之文，禮又爲急，弗可斯須離者也。末俗背本，所由來乆。故閔子譏原伯之不學，荀卿醜秦世之坑儒，儒學旣廢，則風化曷由興哉？方今宿生巨儒，並各年高，教訓之道，孰爲其繼？昔伏生將老，漢文帝嗣以鼂錯；穀梁寡疇，宣帝承以十郎。其科郎吏高才解經義者三十人，從光祿勳隆、散騎常侍林、博士靜，分受四經三禮，主者具爲設課試之法。夏侯勝有言：『士病不明經術，經術苟明，其取青紫如俯拾地芥耳。今學者有能究極經道，則爵祿榮寵，不期而至。可不勉哉！數年，隆等皆卒，學者遂廢。初，任城棧潛，太祖世歷縣令，〈潛字彥皇，見應璩《書林》。

sourceRange.text: 嘉平元年249年，遷征西將軍，都督雍、涼諸軍事。是歲，與雍州刺史陳泰恊策，降蜀牙門將句安等於翅上。二年，詔曰：「昔漢川之役，幾至傾覆。淮臨危濟難，功書王府。在關右三十餘年，外征寇虜，內綏民夷。比歲以來，摧破廖化，禽虜句安，功績顯著，朕甚嘉之。今以淮爲車騎將軍、儀同三司，持節、都督如故。」進封陽曲侯，邑凡二千七百八十戶，分三百戶，封一子亭侯。《世語》曰：淮妻，王淩之妹。淩誅，妹當從坐，御史往收。督將及羌、胡渠帥數千人叩頭請淮表留妻，淮不從。妻上道，莫不流涕，人人扼腕，欲劫留之。淮五子叩頭流血請淮，淮不忍視，乃命左右追妻。於是追者數千騎，數日而還。淮以書白司馬宣王曰：「五子哀母，不惜其身；若無其母，是無五子；無五子，亦無淮也。今輒追還，若於法未通，當受罪於主者，覲展在近。」書至，宣王亦宥之。正元二年薨，追贈大將軍，謚曰貞侯。子統嗣。統官至荊州刺史，薨。子正嗣。咸熈中，開建五等，以淮著勳前朝，改封汾陽子。《晉諸公贊》曰：淮弟配，字仲南，有重名，位至城陽太守。裴秀、賈充皆配女壻。子展，字泰舒。有器度幹用，歷職著績，終於太僕。次弟豫，字泰寧，相國參軍，知名，早卒。女適王衍。配弟鎮，字季南，謁者僕射。鎮子弈，字泰業。山濤啟事稱弈高簡有雅量，歷位雍州刺史、尚書。

context.afterSource: 評曰：滿寵立志剛毅，勇而有謀。

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平元年249年，遷征西將軍，都督雍、涼諸軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jiaping, 249 CE, he was transferred to general who Conquers the West and supervised all military affairs of Yong and Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiaping 1 (249): Guo Huai became general who Conquers the West and commander of Yong and Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，與雍州刺史陳泰恊策，降蜀牙門將句安等於翅上。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, coordinating plans with inspector of Yong Province Chen Tai, he caused Shu yamen general Gou An and others to surrender at Chishang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year he and Yong inspector Chen Tai forced Shu yamen general Gou An to surrender at Chishang.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，詔曰：「昔漢川之役，幾至傾覆。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year an edict said, "Formerly in the Han River campaign [the state] nearly toppled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year an edict recalled: "At Han River the realm nearly fell.

manualTranslations.zh: 淮臨危濟難，功書王府。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai in peril aided difficulty; his merit was recorded in the royal archives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Huai saved the day; his merit is in the royal archives.

manualTranslations.zh: 在關右三十餘年，外征寇虜，內綏民夷。
manualTranslations.literal: More than thirty years in Guan-you—outwardly campaigning against bandits and barbarians, inwardly soothing the people and tribes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For thirty years west of the pass he fought invaders abroad and soothed tribes at home.

manualTranslations.zh: 比歲以來，摧破廖化，禽虜句安，功績顯著，朕甚嘉之。
manualTranslations.literal: In recent years he has crushed Liao Hua and captured the bandit Gou An—merit conspicuous; We greatly commend this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lately he broke Liao Hua and captured Gou An—splendid service We greatly praise.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以淮爲車騎將軍、儀同三司，持節、都督如故。」
manualTranslations.literal: We now make Huai general of chariots and cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Offices, holding credentials and supervising as before."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We now make Guo Huai general of chariots and cavalry with Three Excellencies protocol, staff and command unchanged."

manualTranslations.zh: 進封陽曲侯，邑凡二千七百八十戶，分三百戶，封一子亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: He was advanced to marquis of Yangqu; his fief totaled two thousand seven hundred eighty households; three hundred households were divided off to enfeoff one son as village marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His fief advanced to marquis of Yangqu with 2,780 households; 300 were set aside to enfeoff a son as village marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：淮妻，王淩之妹。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu states: Huai’s wife was Wang Ling’s younger sister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Guo Huai’s wife was Wang Ling’s sister.

manualTranslations.zh: 淩誅，妹當從坐，御史往收。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ling was executed, the younger sister was to suffer joint punishment; the imperial censor went to seize her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wang Ling was executed his sister faced joint punishment and censors came to seize her.

manualTranslations.zh: 督將及羌、胡渠帥數千人叩頭請淮表留妻，淮不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Supervising generals and Qiang and Hu chieftains numbering several thousand kowtowed begging Huai to memorialize keeping his wife; Huai would not agree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thousands of officers and tribal chiefs begged Guo Huai to petition for his wife; he refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻上道，莫不流涕，人人扼腕，欲劫留之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the wife set out on the road, none failed to weep; every man clenched his wrist, wishing to seize and detain her.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As she was led away men wept and clenched their fists, ready to seize her back.

manualTranslations.zh: 淮五子叩頭流血請淮，淮不忍視，乃命左右追妻。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai’s five sons kowtowed until blood flowed begging Huai; Huai could not bear to look and thereupon ordered attendants to pursue the wife.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His five sons kowtowed until they bled; Guo Huai could not watch and ordered her brought back.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是追者數千騎，數日而還。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon pursuers numbered several thousand riders; in several days they returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thousands of riders chased her down and returned within days.

manualTranslations.zh: 淮以書白司馬宣王曰：「五子哀母，不惜其身；
manualTranslations.literal: Huai by letter informed Sima the King of Announcements, saying, "The five sons grieve for their mother and spare not their persons;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Huai wrote Sima Yi: "My sons mourn their mother and would give their lives;

manualTranslations.zh: 若無其母，是無五子；
manualTranslations.literal: without their mother there are no five sons;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: without her there are no sons;

manualTranslations.zh: 無五子，亦無淮也。
manualTranslations.literal: without the five sons there is also no Huai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: without sons there is no Guo Huai.

manualTranslations.zh: 今輒追還，若於法未通，當受罪於主者，覲展在近。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now I have forthwith pursued and brought her back; if this does not accord with law, I ought to receive punishment from the authorities—Zhan is near at hand."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have brought her back; if the law forbids it, punish me—Zhan is nearby to witness."

manualTranslations.zh: 書至，宣王亦宥之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the letter arrived, the King of Announcements also pardoned him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi pardoned him when the letter arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 正元二年薨，追贈大將軍，謚曰貞侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Zhengyuan he died; posthumously he was gifted the rank of grand general and given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengyuan 2 and was posthumously made grand general with the title Marquis Zhen.

manualTranslations.zh: 子統嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Tong succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Guo Tong succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 統官至荊州刺史，薨。
manualTranslations.literal: Tong reached the office of inspector of Jing Province and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Tong became inspector of Jing Province and died in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 子正嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Guo Zheng succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熈中，開建五等，以淮著勳前朝，改封汾陽子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Xianxi era, when the five ranks were established, because Huai had shown merit in the former dynasty, [Zheng] was changed in enfeoffment to viscount of Fenyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Xianxi’s five-rank system Guo Zheng was re-enfeoffed viscount of Fenyang for his father’s Wei service.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：淮弟配，字仲南，有重名，位至城陽太守。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jin zhugong zan states: Huai’s younger brother Pei, courtesy name Zhongnan, had heavy reputation and reached the post of grand administrator of Chengyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin zhugong zan records his brother Guo Pei, styled Zhongnan, a famed Chengyang governor.

manualTranslations.zh: 裴秀、賈充皆配女壻。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Xiu and Jia Chong were both sons-in-law of Pei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu and Jia Chong married his daughters.

manualTranslations.zh: 子展，字泰舒。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Zhan, courtesy name Taishu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Guo Zhan, styled Taishu.

manualTranslations.zh: 有器度幹用，歷職著績，終於太僕。
manualTranslations.literal: He had capacity and practical ability, served through offices with marked achievement, and ended as minister of the stud.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Capable and effective, he served with distinction and died as minister of the stud.

manualTranslations.zh: 次弟豫，字泰寧，相國參軍，知名，早卒。
manualTranslations.literal: The next younger brother Yu, courtesy name Taining, was aide in the chancellor’s headquarters, renowned, and died young.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Younger brother Guo Yu, styled Taining, was a noted chancellor’s aide who died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 女適王衍。
manualTranslations.literal: A daughter married Wang Yan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A daughter married Wang Yan.

manualTranslations.zh: 配弟鎮，字季南，謁者僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei’s younger brother Zhen, courtesy name Jinan, was supervisor of the gentlemen-at-the-palace gate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Pei’s brother Guo Zhen, styled Jinan, was supervisor of the gentlemen-at-the-palace gate.

manualTranslations.zh: 鎮子弈，字泰業。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen’s son Yi, courtesy name Taiye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Zhen’s son Guo Yi, styled Taiye.

manualTranslations.zh: 山濤啟事稱弈高簡有雅量，歷位雍州刺史、尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Shan Tao’s memorial stated that Yi was lofty, simple, and possessed elegant measure; he served as inspector of Yong Province and secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan Tao praised Guo Yi as lofty and measured; he served as Yongzhou inspector and secretary.

sourceRange.text: 景初二年，以寵年老徵還，遷爲太尉。寵不治產業，家無餘財。詔曰：「君典兵在外，專心憂公，有行父、祭遵之風。賜田十頃，糓五百斛，錢二十萬，以明清忠儉約之節焉。」寵前後增邑，凡九千六百戶，封子孫二人亭侯。正始三年242年薨，謚曰景侯。子偉嗣。偉以格度知名，官至衞尉。《世語》曰：偉字公衡。偉子長武，有寵風，年二十四，爲大將軍掾。高貴鄉公之難，以掾守閶闔掖門，司馬文王弟安陽亭侯幹欲入。幹妃，偉妹也。長武謂幹曰：「此門近，公且來，無有入者，可從東掖門。」幹遂從之。文王問幹入何遲，幹言其故。參軍王羨亦不得入，恨之。旣而羨因王左右啟王，滿掾斷門不內人，宜推劾。壽春之役，偉從文王至許，以疾不進。子從，求還省疾，事定乃從歸，由此內見恨。收長武考死杖下，偉免爲庶人。時人冤之。偉弟子奮，晉元康中至尚書令、司隷校尉。寵、偉、長武、奮，皆長八尺。荀綽《冀州記》曰：奮性清平，有識檢。《晉諸公贊》曰：奮體量通雅，有寵風也。

context.beforeSource: 詔羙之，因以所獲盡爲將士賞。
context.afterSource: 田豫字國讓，漁陽雍奴人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 景初二年，以寵年老徵還，遷爲太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Jingchu, because Chong was aged he was summoned back and transferred to grand commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jingchu 2: recalled as too old, Man Chong was made grand commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵不治產業，家無餘財。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong did not manage estates; his household had no surplus wealth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He kept no estates and left no surplus wealth.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔曰：「君典兵在外，專心憂公，有行父、祭遵之風。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict said, "You commanded troops abroad and devoted your mind to public affairs, with the manner of Xing Fu and Ji Zun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict praised him: "You commanded abroad with single-minded loyalty, in the spirit of Xing Fu and Ji Zun.

manualTranslations.zh: 賜田十頃，糓五百斛，錢二十萬，以明清忠儉約之節焉。」
manualTranslations.literal: We grant ten qing of fields, five hundred hu of grain, and two hundred thousand cash, to make clear the integrity of loyal purity and frugal restraint."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Take ten qing of land, five hundred hu of grain, and two hundred thousand cash as proof of loyal frugality."

manualTranslations.zh: 寵前後增邑，凡九千六百戶，封子孫二人亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong’s fief was increased before and after to nine thousand six hundred households in all; two descendants were enfeoffed as village marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His fief eventually reached 9,600 households and two descendants became village marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始三年242年薨，謚曰景侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, 242 CE, he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi 3 (242) with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 子偉嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Wei succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Man Wei succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 偉以格度知名，官至衞尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei was known for measure and bearing and reached the office of commandant of the guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Man Wei was known for dignity and rose to commandant of the guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：偉字公衡。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu states: Wei’s courtesy name was Gongheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu gives his style as Gongheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 偉子長武，有寵風，年二十四，爲大將軍掾。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei’s son Changwu had Chong’s manner; at age twenty-four he was an aide in the grand general’s headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Man Changwu matched his father’s bearing; at twenty-four he served as an aide in the grand general’s staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 高貴鄉公之難，以掾守閶闔掖門，司馬文王弟安陽亭侯幹欲入。
manualTranslations.literal: During the crisis of the Duke of Gaoguixiang, as an aide he guarded the Changhe side gate; Sima Wenwang’s younger brother Marquis of Anyang village Gan wished to enter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Gaoguixiang crisis he guarded the Changhe side gate while Sima Zhao’s brother Gan, marquis of Anyang village, tried to enter.

manualTranslations.zh: 幹妃，偉妹也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan’s consort was Wei’s younger sister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan’s wife was Man Wei’s sister.

manualTranslations.zh: 長武謂幹曰：「此門近，公且來，無有入者，可從東掖門。」
manualTranslations.literal: Changwu said to Gan, "This gate is near; when you, sir, come there will be no one entering—you may use the eastern side gate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changwu told Gan: "This gate is watched—come by the eastern side gate instead."

manualTranslations.zh: 幹遂從之。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan thereupon followed this advice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan took that route.

manualTranslations.zh: 文王問幹入何遲，幹言其故。
manualTranslations.literal: Wenwang asked Gan why his entry was late; Gan explained the reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked why Gan was late; Gan explained.

manualTranslations.zh: 參軍王羨亦不得入，恨之。
manualTranslations.literal: Adjutant Wang Xian also could not enter and resented this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wang Xian, also barred, bore a grudge.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣而羨因王左右啟王，滿掾斷門不內人，宜推劾。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereafter Xian through the king’s attendants informed the king: "The Man aide blocked the gate and would not admit people—he ought to be impeached."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Xian then told Sima Zhao through attendants that Man’s aide had barred the gate and should be impeached.

manualTranslations.zh: 壽春之役，偉從文王至許，以疾不進。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Shouchun campaign Wei followed Wenwang to Xu but because of illness did not advance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Shouchun campaign Man Wei followed Sima Zhao to Xu but stayed behind ill.

manualTranslations.zh: 子從，求還省疾，事定乃從歸，由此內見恨。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Cong asked to return and visit the illness; only after affairs were settled did he follow back—thereby inwardly incurring resentment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Cong asked leave to tend him and rejoined only after the campaign—earning inner resentment.

manualTranslations.zh: 收長武考死杖下，偉免爲庶人。
manualTranslations.literal: Changwu was seized, examined, and beaten to death; Wei was dismissed and made a commoner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changwu was arrested and beaten to death; Man Wei was reduced to commoner status.

manualTranslations.zh: 時人冤之。
manualTranslations.literal: Men of the time considered this unjust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Contemporaries thought it unjust.

manualTranslations.zh: 偉弟子奮，晉元康中至尚書令、司隷校尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei’s younger brother’s son Fen, in the Yuankang era of Jin, reached Director of the Secretariat and Colonel Director of Retainers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Man Fen, Wei’s nephew, became director of the secretariat and colonel director of retainers under Jin Yuankang.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵、偉、長武、奮，皆長八尺。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong, Wei, Changwu, and Fen were all eight chi in height.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong, Wei, Changwu, and Fen all stood eight chi tall.

manualTranslations.zh: 荀綽《冀州記》曰：奮性清平，有識檢。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Chuo’s Ji Province record states: Fen’s nature was pure and even, with discernment and restraint.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo’s Ji Province record calls Fen even-tempered and judicious.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：奮體量通雅，有寵風也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jin zhugong zan states: Fen’s bearing and capacity were penetrating and refined, with Chong’s manner.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin zhugong zan adds that Fen was broad and refined, with Man Chong’s bearing.

sourceRange.text: 明帝即位，賜爵關內侯。太和二年228年，護烏丸校尉田豫出塞，爲軻比能所圍於故馬邑城，移招求救。招即整勒兵馬，欲赴救豫。并州以常憲禁招，招以爲節將見圍，不可拘於吏議，自表輙行。又並馳布羽檄，稱陳形勢，云當西北掩取虜家，然後東行，會誅虜身。檄到，豫軍踴躍。又遺一通於虜蹊要，虜即恐怖，種類離散。軍到故平城，便皆潰走。比能復大合騎來，到故平州塞北。招潛行撲討，大斬首級。招以蜀虜諸葛亮數出，而比能狡猾，能相交通，表爲防備，議者以爲縣遠，未之信也。會亮時在祁山，果遣使連結比能。比能至故北地石城，與相首尾。帝乃詔招，使從便宜討之。時比能已還漠南，招與刺史畢軌議曰：「胡虜遷徙無常。若勞師遠追，則遲速不相及。若欲潛襲，則山溪艱險，資糧轉運，難以密辦。可使守新興、鴈門二牙門，出屯陘北，外以鎮撫，內令兵田，儲畜資糧，秋冬馬肥，州郡兵合，乘釁征討，計必全克。未及施行，會病卒。招在郡十二年，威風遠振。其治邊之稱，次於田豫，百姓追思之。而漁陽傅容在鴈門有名績，繼招後，在遼東又有事功云。

context.afterSource: 招子嘉嗣。

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, [Zhao] was granted the rank of marquis within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Qian Zhao received a secondary marquisate inside the passes.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和二年228年，護烏丸校尉田豫出塞，爲軻比能所圍於故馬邑城，移招求救。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, 228 CE, colonel protecting the Wuhuan Tian Yu went beyond the barrier and was besieged by Kebineng at old Mayi city; he sent to Zhao seeking rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taihe 2 (228): Wuhuan colonel Tian Yu rode beyond the wall and was trapped by Kebineng at old Mayi; he appealed to Qian Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 招即整勒兵馬，欲赴救豫。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao immediately marshaled troops and horses, intending to hurry to rescue Yu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao mustered troops to relieve him.

manualTranslations.zh: 并州以常憲禁招，招以爲節將見圍，不可拘於吏議，自表輙行。
manualTranslations.literal: Bing Province by standing regulations forbade Zhao; Zhao considered that a frontier general was besieged and one could not be bound by clerks’ debate—he memorialized on his own authority and set out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bingzhou regulations barred him, but Qian Zhao argued a besieged commander could not wait on clerks and marched on his own authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 又並馳布羽檄，稱陳形勢，云當西北掩取虜家，然後東行，會誅虜身。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover he simultaneously dispatched proclamations on urgent feathers, proclaiming and laying out the situation, saying he would first strike northwest to seize the barbarians’ homes, then march east and join in slaying the barbarian leader himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also sent urgent proclamations claiming he would strike the nomad camps northwest, then wheel east to kill Kebineng in person.

manualTranslations.zh: 檄到，豫軍踴躍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the proclamation arrived, Yu’s army leaped for joy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tian Yu’s men cheered when the message arrived.

manualTranslations.zh: 又遺一通於虜蹊要，虜即恐怖，種類離散。
manualTranslations.literal: He also sent another copy to a strategic pass of the barbarians; the barbarians at once grew fearful and their tribes scattered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Another copy reached a nomad choke point; terror scattered the tribes.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍到故平城，便皆潰走。
manualTranslations.literal: When the army reached old Pingcheng, [the enemy] all at once broke and fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At old Pingcheng the enemy broke and ran.

manualTranslations.zh: 比能復大合騎來，到故平州塞北。
manualTranslations.literal: Kebineng again gathered a great host of riders and came to north of the old Pingzhou barrier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kebineng rallied cavalry and returned north of old Pingzhou pass.

manualTranslations.zh: 招潛行撲討，大斬首級。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao moved secretly in a punitive strike and beheaded many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qian Zhao struck secretly and took many heads.

manualTranslations.zh: 招以蜀虜諸葛亮數出，而比能狡猾，能相交通，表爲防備，議者以爲縣遠，未之信也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao, because Shu bandit Zhuge Liang repeatedly came out and Kebineng was crafty and able to communicate with him, memorialized for precaution; debaters thought the commandery too distant and did not believe it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhuge Liang’s repeated raids and Kebineng’s cunning, Qian Zhao warned of collusion; skeptics thought Yanmen too remote.

manualTranslations.zh: 會亮時在祁山，果遣使連結比能。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened Liang was then at Qishan and indeed sent envoys to link with Kebineng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was at Qishan and did send envoys to Kebineng.

manualTranslations.zh: 比能至故北地石城，與相首尾。
manualTranslations.literal: Kebineng reached old Beidi Shicheng and coordinated front and rear with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kebineng reached old Shicheng in Beidi and coordinated with Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝乃詔招，使從便宜討之。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered Zhao to campaign against them as circumstances permitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor authorized Qian Zhao to strike as opportunity allowed.

manualTranslations.zh: 時比能已還漠南，招與刺史畢軌議曰：「胡虜遷徙無常。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Kebineng had already returned south of the desert; Zhao debated with inspector Bi Gui, saying, "Hu barbarians shift camps without fixed pattern.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kebineng had already withdrawn south of the desert; Qian Zhao told Bi Gui: "The tribes move unpredictably.

manualTranslations.zh: 若勞師遠追，則遲速不相及。
manualTranslations.literal: If we weary the army with distant pursuit, swift and slow will not meet.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A distant pursuit will never catch them.

manualTranslations.zh: 若欲潛襲，則山溪艱險，資糧轉運，難以密辦。
manualTranslations.literal: If we wish a secret raid, mountains and streams are perilous and grain transport hard to arrange in secrecy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A secret raid is impossible over rugged streams with long supply lines.

manualTranslations.zh: 可使守新興、鴈門二牙門，出屯陘北，外以鎮撫，內令兵田，儲畜資糧，秋冬馬肥，州郡兵合，乘釁征討，計必全克。
manualTranslations.literal: We may have the garrisons of Xinxing and Yanmen hold the two yamen gates, march out and encamp north of the pass, outwardly to pacify and inwardly order military farming, store provisions, and when autumn and winter bring fat horses and commandery troops combine, strike on opportunity—the plan will surely achieve complete victory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hold Xinxing and Yanmen, camp north of the pass, farm and store grain, then when horses fatten in autumn combine commandery troops and strike—we will win.

manualTranslations.zh: 未及施行，會病卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Before this could be carried out, he happened to die of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died of illness before the plan could be executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 招在郡十二年，威風遠振。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhao was in the commandery twelve years; his awing prestige shook far lands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Twelve years in Yanmen spread his fame far.

manualTranslations.zh: 其治邊之稱，次於田豫，百姓追思之。
manualTranslations.literal: His reputation for governing the frontier was second to Tian Yu; the common people recalled him with longing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His frontier renown ranked just below Tian Yu’s; people mourned him.

manualTranslations.zh: 而漁陽傅容在鴈門有名績，繼招後，在遼東又有事功云。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Fuyang’s Fu Rong had famous achievement at Yanmen; succeeding Zhao, he also had merit in Liaodong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fu Rong of Fuyang followed him at Yanmen with noted success and later served in Liaodong as well.

sourceRange.text: 明帝即位，進封昌邑侯。太和二年228年，領豫州刺史。三年春，降人稱吳大嚴，揚聲欲詣江北獵，孫權欲自出。寵度其必襲西陽而爲之備，權聞之，退還。秋，使曹休從廬江南入合肥，令寵向夏口。寵上疏曰：「曹休雖明果而希用兵，今所從道，背湖旁江，易進難退，此兵之窪地也。若入無彊口，宜深爲之備。」寵表未報，休遂深入。賊果從無彊口斷夾石，要休還路。休戰不利，退走。會朱靈等從後來斷道，與賊相遇。賊驚走，休軍乃得還。是歲休薨，寵以前將軍代都督揚州諸軍事。汝南兵民戀慕，大小相率，奔隨道路，不可禁止。護軍表上，欲殺其爲首者。詔使寵將親兵千人自隨，其餘一無所問。四年，拜寵征東將軍。其冬，孫權揚聲欲至合肥，寵表召兖、豫諸軍，皆集。賊尋退還，被詔罷兵。寵以爲今賊大舉而還，非本意也，此必欲僞退以罷吾兵，而倒還乘虛，掩不備也，表不罷兵。後十餘日，權果更來，到合肥城，不克而還。其明年，吳將孫布遣人詣揚州求降，辭云：「道遠不能自致，乞兵見迎。」刺史王淩騰布書，請兵馬迎之。寵以爲必詐，不與兵，而作報書曰：「知識邪正，欲避禍就順，去暴歸道，甚相嘉尚。今欲遣兵相迎，然計兵少則不足相衞，多則事必遠聞。且先密計以成本志，臨時節度其宜。」寵會被書當入朝，勑留府長史：「若淩欲往迎，勿與兵也。」淩於後索兵不得，乃單遣一督將步騎七百人往迎之。布夜掩擊，督將迸走，死傷過半。初，寵與淩共事不平，淩支黨毀寵疲老悖謬，故明帝召之。旣至，體氣康彊，見而遣還。《世語》曰：王淩表寵年過耽酒，不可居方任。帝將召寵，給事中郭謀曰：「寵爲汝南太守、豫州刺史二十餘年，有勳方岳。及鎮淮南，吳人憚之。若不如所表，將爲所闚。可令還朝，問以方事以察之。」帝從之。寵旣至，進見，飲酒至一石不亂。帝慰勞之，遣還。寵屢表求留，詔報曰：「昔廉頗彊食，馬援據鞌，今君未老而自謂已老，何與廉、馬之相背邪？其思安邊境，惠此中國。」明年，吴將陸遜向廬江，論者以爲宜速赴之。寵曰：「廬江雖小，將勁兵精，守則經時。又賊舍船二百里來，後尾空縣，尚欲誘致，今宜聽其遂進，但恐走不可及耳。」整軍趨楊宜口。賊聞大兵東下，即夜遁。時權歲有來計。青龍元年233年，寵上疏曰：「合肥城南臨江湖，北遠壽春，賊攻圍之，得據水爲勢；

localRange.text: 青龍元年，寵上疏曰：「合肥城南臨江湖，北遠壽春，賊攻圍之，得據水爲勢；
