manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，進封昌邑侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, [Chong] was advanced to marquis of Changyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Man Chong was advanced to marquis of Changyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和二年228年，領豫州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, 228 CE, he concurrently held the post of inspector of Yu Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taihe 2 (228): he took charge as inspector of Yu Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年春，降人稱吳大嚴，揚聲欲詣江北獵，孫權欲自出。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the third year, surrendering men reported that Wu was making great preparations and proclaimed an intent to hunt north of the Yangzi; Sun Quan intended to come out in person.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That spring defectors reported Wu massing troops and claiming a hunt north of the river; Sun Quan meant to march in person.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵度其必襲西陽而爲之備，權聞之，退還。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong judged that [Sun Quan] would surely strike Xiyang and made preparations; when Quan heard of it, he withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong read the move as a strike on Xiyang and prepared; Sun Quan heard and pulled back.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋，使曹休從廬江南入合肥，令寵向夏口。
manualTranslations.literal: In autumn [the court] had Cao Xiu enter Hefei from the south of Lujiang and ordered Chong toward Xiakou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn Cao Xiu was sent into Hefei from south of Lujiang while Chong was ordered toward Xiakou.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵上疏曰：「曹休雖明果而希用兵，今所從道，背湖旁江，易進難退，此兵之窪地也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong submitted a memorial saying, "Though Cao Xiu is bright and resolute, he seldom employs troops; the road he now follows backs onto the lake and runs beside the river—easy to advance, hard to withdraw—this is low ground for an army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized: "Cao Xiu is capable but rarely campaigns; his route hugs lake and river—easy in, hard out—a classic trap.

manualTranslations.zh: 若入無彊口，宜深爲之備。」
manualTranslations.literal: If he enters Wujiangkou, deep preparations ought to be made."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If he enters Wujiangkou, fortify it deeply."

manualTranslations.zh: 寵表未報，休遂深入。
manualTranslations.literal: Before Chong's memorial was answered, Xiu pressed deep inland.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the memorial was answered, Cao Xiu drove deep inland.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊果從無彊口斷夾石，要休還路。
manualTranslations.literal: The enemy indeed cut off Jiashi from Wujiangkou, blocking Xiu's line of retreat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The enemy did cut Jiashi at Wujiangkou and blocked Cao Xiu’s retreat.

manualTranslations.zh: 休戰不利，退走。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu fought unfavorably and retreated in flight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu lost the fight and fled.

manualTranslations.zh: 會朱靈等從後來斷道，與賊相遇。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhu Ling and others came from the rear to cut the road and encountered the enemy,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Ling and others struck from the rear, met the enemy,

manualTranslations.zh: 賊驚走，休軍乃得還。
manualTranslations.literal: the bandits fled in alarm and Xiu’s army was able to return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and the raiders scattered so Cao Xiu’s army escaped.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲休薨，寵以前將軍代都督揚州諸軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: That year Xiu died; Chong replaced him as supervisor of all military affairs of Yang Province with the rank of general of the van.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu died that year; Chong succeeded him as Yang Province commander with the rank of general of the van.

manualTranslations.zh: 汝南兵民戀慕，大小相率，奔隨道路，不可禁止。
manualTranslations.literal: The soldiers and civilians of Runan admired him; great and small led one another along the roads in flight following him—it could not be forbidden.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Runan soldiers and civilians adored him; crowds trailed him along the roads and could not be stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 護軍表上，欲殺其爲首者。
manualTranslations.literal: The protector general memorialized the throne, wishing to execute those who led the way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The protector general urged executing the ringleaders.

manualTranslations.zh: 詔使寵將親兵千人自隨，其餘一無所問。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict had Chong bring a thousand personal troops as escort; concerning the rest, nothing was pursued.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An edict let Chong keep a thousand personal guards and pardoned everyone else.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，拜寵征東將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year Chong was appointed general who Conquers the East.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was named general who Conquers the East.

manualTranslations.zh: 其冬，孫權揚聲欲至合肥，寵表召兖、豫諸軍，皆集。
manualTranslations.literal: That winter Sun Quan proclaimed an intent to reach Hefei; Chong memorialized summoning the armies of Yan and Yu—all assembled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That winter Sun Quan threatened Hefei; Chong called Yan and Yu troops to muster.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊尋退還，被詔罷兵。
manualTranslations.literal: The enemy soon withdrew; [Chong] received an edict dismissing the troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The enemy soon withdrew and an edict ordered the armies stood down.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵以爲今賊大舉而還，非本意也，此必欲僞退以罷吾兵，而倒還乘虛，掩不備也，表不罷兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong judged that the enemy's great host returning now was not their original intent—they must wish to feign withdrawal and dismiss our troops, then wheel about, seize an opening, and strike while we were unprepared; he memorialized not to dismiss the troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong argued the withdrawal was a feint to lure Wei into standing down, then wheel back for a surprise strike; he refused to dismiss the troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 後十餘日，權果更來，到合肥城，不克而還。
manualTranslations.literal: After more than ten days Quan indeed came again, reached the walls of Hefei, could not take it, and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within ten days Sun Quan did return, failed before Hefei, and withdrew.

manualTranslations.zh: 其明年，吳將孫布遣人詣揚州求降，辭云：「道遠不能自致，乞兵見迎。」
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Wu general Sun Bu sent men to Yang Province seeking surrender, saying in his plea, "The road is long and I cannot come of myself—I beg troops to meet and welcome me."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Next year Wu general Sun Bu asked Yang Province for troops to escort his surrender: "The road is long; I cannot come alone—please send men to meet me."

manualTranslations.zh: 刺史王淩騰布書，請兵馬迎之。
manualTranslations.literal: Inspector Wang Ling forwarded Bu's letter and requested troops and horses to welcome him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Ling forwarded the letter and asked for troops to receive Sun Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵以爲必詐，不與兵，而作報書曰：「知識邪正，欲避禍就順，去暴歸道，甚相嘉尚。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong judged it certainly a ruse, gave no troops, yet wrote a reply saying, "I know you distinguish wrong from right, wish to flee disaster and approach obedience, leave violence and return to the Way—I greatly commend this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong smelled a trap, refused troops, and answered: "You know right from wrong, flee harm for loyalty, and leave violence for the Way—I applaud that.

manualTranslations.zh: 今欲遣兵相迎，然計兵少則不足相衞，多則事必遠聞。
manualTranslations.literal: I now wish to dispatch troops to welcome you, yet if the force is few it will not suffice to guard you; if many, the affair will surely be heard from afar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I would send escorts, but a small guard cannot protect you and a large one will be heard far away.

manualTranslations.zh: 且先密計以成本志，臨時節度其宜。」
manualTranslations.literal: First make a secret plan to accomplish your purpose, and at the moment adjust measures as fitting."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Plan in secret first, then act as circumstances require."

manualTranslations.zh: 寵會被書當入朝，勑留府長史：「若淩欲往迎，勿與兵也。」
manualTranslations.literal: It happened Chong received word he was to enter court; he ordered the headquarters chief clerk left behind, "If Ling wishes to go welcome [Sun Bu], give him no troops."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, Chong told his chief clerk: "If Wang Ling tries to welcome Sun Bu, give him no troops."

manualTranslations.zh: 淩於後索兵不得，乃單遣一督將步騎七百人往迎之。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling afterward sought troops and could not obtain them; he then singly dispatched one supervising general with seven hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome [Sun Bu].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Denied troops, Wang Ling sent one commander with seven hundred foot and horse alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 布夜掩擊，督將迸走，死傷過半。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu raided by night; the supervising general bolted in flight—more than half were killed or wounded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Bu struck by night; the commander fled and more than half his men were killed or wounded.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，寵與淩共事不平，淩支黨毀寵疲老悖謬，故明帝召之。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier Chong and Ling serving together were not on good terms; Ling's faction slandered Chong as worn out, aged, perverse, and absurd—therefore Emperor Ming summoned him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong and Wang Ling had long feuded; Ling’s faction called Chong senile and unfit, so Emperor Ming summoned him.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣至，體氣康彊，見而遣還。
manualTranslations.literal: When he arrived, his body and vitality were robust; [the emperor] saw him and sent him back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He arrived vigorous; the emperor sent him back.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：王淩表寵年過耽酒，不可居方任。
manualTranslations.literal: The Shiyu states: Wang Ling memorialized that Chong was advanced in years and addicted to wine and could not hold a frontier post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Shiyu says Wang Ling reported Chong too old and too fond of wine for frontier command.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝將召寵，給事中郭謀曰：「寵爲汝南太守、豫州刺史二十餘年，有勳方岳。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor was about to summon Chong; attendant within the gates Guo Mou said, "Chong has been grand administrator of Runan and inspector of Yu Province for more than twenty years, with merit at the regional level.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to recall Chong, Guo Mou said: "Chong governed Runan and Yu for twenty years with frontier merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 及鎮淮南，吳人憚之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he garrisoned Huainan, the men of Wu feared him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Huainan the Wu armies feared him.

manualTranslations.zh: 若不如所表，將爲所闚。
manualTranslations.literal: If he is not as the memorial says, [Wu] will spy on us.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If he is not as Wang Ling claims, Wu will watch for weakness.

manualTranslations.zh: 可令還朝，問以方事以察之。」
manualTranslations.literal: He may be ordered to return to court and questioned on frontier affairs to test him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recall him, question him on frontier affairs, and judge for yourself."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝從之。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵旣至，進見，飲酒至一石不亂。
manualTranslations.literal: When Chong arrived and had audience, he drank up to one dan [of wine] without disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong appeared at court and drank a full dan of wine without faltering.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝慰勞之，遣還。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor comforted and praised him and sent him back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and sent him back.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵屢表求留，詔報曰：「昔廉頗彊食，馬援據鞌，今君未老而自謂已老，何與廉、馬之相背邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Chong repeatedly memorialized asking to remain; an edict replied, "Formerly Lian Po ate heartily and Ma Yuan gripped his saddle—now you are not old yet call yourself old—how does this differ from Lian and Ma turning their backs on us?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong begged to stay; the reply cited Lian Po’s hearty meals and Ma Yuan in the saddle: "You are not old yet call yourself old—why turn from their example?

manualTranslations.zh: 其思安邊境，惠此中國。」
manualTranslations.literal: Think on securing the frontier and bringing grace to this central realm."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Secure the border and bless the heartland."

manualTranslations.zh: 明年，吴將陸遜向廬江，論者以爲宜速赴之。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year Wu general Lu Xun moved toward Lujiang; debaters thought one ought to hurry to meet him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Next year Lu Xun marched on Lujiang; advisers urged a rapid response.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵曰：「廬江雖小，將勁兵精，守則經時。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong said, "Though Lujiang is small, its generals are strong and troops elite—if defended it will hold for a time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong said: "Lujiang is small but its garrison is tough—it will hold.

manualTranslations.zh: 又賊舍船二百里來，後尾空縣，尚欲誘致，今宜聽其遂進，但恐走不可及耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the bandits left their boats two hundred li away—the rear is empty and dangling; they still wish to lure us—now it is fitting to let them advance, only fearing they may flee beyond reach."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They left their boats two hundred li back with an empty rear—they mean to bait us. Let them advance; I only fear they flee before we catch them."

manualTranslations.zh: 整軍趨楊宜口。
manualTranslations.literal: He marshaled the army and hastened to Yangyikou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He marched the army to Yangyikou.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊聞大兵東下，即夜遁。
manualTranslations.literal: When the bandits heard the great army was coming east, that very night they fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing the host approach, the enemy fled overnight.

manualTranslations.zh: 時權歲有來計。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Quan yearly had plans to come [against Wei].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then plotted yearly incursions.

manualTranslations.zh: 青龍元年233年，寵上疏曰：「合肥城南臨江湖，北遠壽春，賊攻圍之，得據水爲勢；
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, 233 CE, Chong submitted a memorial saying, 'Hefei's south face adjoins the rivers and lakes, while to the north it is far from Shou-chun; when bandits attack and besiege it, they can seize the advantage of the water;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qinglong 1 (233): Chong memorialized: 'Hefei's south face adjoins the rivers and lakes, while to the north it is far from Shou-chun; when bandits attack and besiege it, they can seize the advantage of the water;

sourceRange.text: 」是歲基薨，追贈司空，謚曰景侯。子徽嗣，早卒。咸熈中，開建五等，以基著勳前朝，改封基孫廙，而以東武餘邑賜一子爵關內侯。晉室踐阼，下詔曰：「故司空王基旣著德立勳，又治身清素，不營產業，乆在重任，家無私積，可謂身沒行顯，足用勵俗者也。其以奴婢二人賜其家。

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲基薨，追贈司空，謚曰景侯。
manualTranslations.literal: That year Ji died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji died that year and was posthumously made Minister of Works, styled Marquis Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 子徽嗣，早卒。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Hui succeeded and died young.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Hui succeeded but died young.

manualTranslations.zh: 咸熈中，開建五等，以基著勳前朝，改封基孫廙，而以東武餘邑賜一子爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Xianxi era, when the five ranks were established, because Ji had shown merit in the former dynasty, his grandson Yi was enfeoffed in his place, and one son was given the remaining lands of Dongwu with the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Xianxi, when the five noble ranks were instituted, Ji’s grandson Yi was enfeoffed for his grandfather’s service, and one son received Dongwu’s remaining fief as a secondary marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉室踐阼，下詔曰：「故司空王基旣著德立勳，又治身清素，不營產業，乆在重任，家無私積，可謂身沒行顯，足用勵俗者也。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Jin house ascended the throne, an edict was issued saying, "The late Minister of Works Wang Ji both displayed virtue and established merit, and also kept his person pure and plain, did not pursue property, long held weighty office, and his household had no private hoard—this may be called conduct manifest after death, enough to encourage custom.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Jin took the throne, an edict declared, "The late Minister of Works Wang Ji won merit and lived plainly, held high office for years without private wealth—conduct that outlived him and could edify the age.

manualTranslations.zh: 其以奴婢二人賜其家。
manualTranslations.literal: Let two male and female servants be granted to his household."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grant his household two servants."

sourceRange.text: 性沈實內察，不以其節檢物，所在見思。嘉平二年250年薨，家無餘財，惟有賜衣書篋而已。軍師以聞，追進封陽陵亭侯，邑百戶，謚曰貞侯。子威嗣。六年，詔書褒述質清行，賜其家錢糓。語在〈徐邈傳〉。威，咸熈中官至徐州刺史，《晉陽秋》曰：威字伯虎。少有志尚，厲操清白。質之爲荊州也，威自京都省之。家貧，無車馬童僕，威自驅驢單行，拜見父。停廄中十餘日，告歸。臨辭，質賜絹一匹，爲道路糧。威跪曰：「大人清白，不審於何得此絹？」質曰：「是吾俸祿之餘，故以爲汝糧耳。」威受之，辭歸。每至客舍，自放驢，取樵炊爨，食畢，復隨旅進道，往還如是。質帳下都督，素不相識，先其將歸，請假還家，陰資裝百餘里要之，因與爲伴，每事佐助經營之，又少進飲食，行數百里。威疑之，密誘問，乃知其都督也，因取向所賜絹荅謝而遣之。後因他信，具以白質。質杖其都督一百，除吏名。其父子清慎如此。於是名譽著聞，歷位宰牧。晉武帝賜見，論邊事，語及平生。帝歎其父清，謂威曰：「卿清孰與父清？」威對曰：「臣不如也。」帝曰：「以何爲不如？」對曰：「臣父清恐人知，臣清恐人不知，是臣不如者遠也。」官至前將軍、青州刺史。太康元年卒，追贈鎮東將軍。威弟羆，字季象，征南將軍；威子弈，字次孫，平東將軍；並以潔行垂名。有殊績，歷三郡守，所在有名。卒於安定。王昶字文舒，太原晉陽人也。案〈王氏譜〉：昶伯父柔，字叔優；父澤，字季道。〈郭林宗傳〉曰：叔優、季道幼少之時，聞林宗有知人之鑒，共往候之，請問才行所宜，以自處業。林宗笑曰：「卿二人皆二千石才也，雖然，叔優當以仕宦顯，季道宜以經術進，若違才易務，亦不至也。」叔優等從其言。叔優至北中郎將，季道代郡太守。少與同郡王淩俱知名。淩年長，昶兄事之。文帝在東宮，昶爲太子文學，遷中庶子。文帝踐阼，徙散騎侍郎，爲洛陽典農。時都畿樹木成林，昶斫開荒萊，勤勸百姓，墾田特多。遷兖州刺史。明帝即位，加揚烈將軍，賜爵關內侯。昶雖在外任，心存朝廷，以爲魏承秦、漢之弊，法制苛碎，不大釐改國典以準先王之風，而望治化復興，不可得也。乃著治論，略依古制而合於時務者二十餘篇，又著兵書十餘篇，言奇正之用，《孫子兵法》曰：兵以正合，以奇勝；奇正還相生，若循環之無端。青龍中奏之。

manualTranslations.zh: 性沈實內察，不以其節檢物，所在見思。
manualTranslations.literal: His nature was deep, solid, and inwardly observant; he did not use his standards to judge others, and wherever he served he was missed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deep, steady, and inwardly perceptive, he never judged others by his own standards and was missed wherever he served.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平二年250年薨，家無餘財，惟有賜衣書篋而已。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Jiaping, 250 CE, he died; the household had no surplus wealth, only granted robes and a book chest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Jiaping 2 (250) leaving only court robes and a book chest.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍師以聞，追進封陽陵亭侯，邑百戶，謚曰貞侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The army supervisor reported it, and [the court] advanced him posthumously to Marquis of Yangling village with a fief of one hundred households, posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The army supervisor reported his death; he was posthumously made Marquis of Yangling village, fief of one hundred households, styled Marquis Zhen.

manualTranslations.zh: 子威嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Wei succeeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Hu Wei succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年，詔書褒述質清行，賜其家錢糓。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year an edict praised and recounted Zhi’s pure conduct and granted his household money and grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict praised Hu Zhi’s integrity and granted his household money and grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 語在
manualTranslations.literal: The account is in
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The account appears in

manualTranslations.zh: 〈徐邈傳〉。
manualTranslations.literal: the biography of Xu Miao.〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the biography of Xu Miao.〉

manualTranslations.zh: 威，咸熈中官至徐州刺史，《晉陽秋》曰：威字伯虎。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei, in the Xianxi era, reached office as inspector of Xu Province. The Jin Yang Autumn states: Wei’s courtesy name was Bohu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xianxi, Hu Wei rose to inspector of Xu Province. The Jin Yang Autumn says he was styled Bohu.

manualTranslations.zh: 少有志尚，厲操清白。
manualTranslations.literal: From youth he had aspiration and purpose and cultivated conduct that was pure and white.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth he aimed high and cultivated spotless conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 質之爲荊州也，威自京都省之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhi was in Jing Province, Wei came from the capital to visit him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While Hu Zhi governed Jingzhou, Hu Wei traveled from the capital to visit him.

manualTranslations.zh: 家貧，無車馬童僕，威自驅驢單行，拜見父。
manualTranslations.literal: The household was poor and had no carriage, horses, or servants; Wei himself drove a donkey and went alone to bow and see his father.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Poor and without carriage or servants, Wei drove a donkey alone to see his father.

manualTranslations.zh: 停廄中十餘日，告歸。
manualTranslations.literal: He stayed in the stable more than ten days, then asked to return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He stayed in the stable over ten days, then asked leave to return home.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨辭，質賜絹一匹，爲道路糧。
manualTranslations.literal: As he was leaving, Zhi granted him one bolt of silk as travel provisions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On parting Hu Zhi gave him one bolt of silk for the road.

manualTranslations.zh: 威跪曰：「大人清白，不審於何得此絹？」
manualTranslations.literal: Wei knelt and said, "Father is pure and white—how did you obtain this silk?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei knelt and asked, "You live so plainly—where did this silk come from?"

manualTranslations.zh: 質曰：「是吾俸祿之餘，故以爲汝糧耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi said, "It is the surplus of my salary, so I made it your provisions."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi answered, "It is what remains of my salary, set aside for your journey."

manualTranslations.zh: 威受之，辭歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei accepted it and took leave to return.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei accepted it and went home.

manualTranslations.zh: 每至客舍，自放驢，取樵炊爨，食畢，復隨旅進道，往還如是。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever he reached an inn he himself turned loose the donkey, gathered firewood, cooked, and after eating again followed travelers on the road; going and returning he did thus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At every inn he unsaddled the donkey, gathered firewood, cooked, ate, and rejoined the road—so he traveled both ways.

manualTranslations.zh: 質帳下都督，素不相識，先其將歸，請假還家，陰資裝百餘里要之，因與爲伴，每事佐助經營之，又少進飲食，行數百里。
manualTranslations.literal: A commandant under Zhi’s tent, whom he had never known, before Wei was to return asked leave to go home, secretly prepared supplies, and waited for him more than a hundred li away, then became his companion, assisting and managing every matter, also providing a little food and drink, traveling several hundred li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A commandant in Hu Zhi’s staff, unknown to Wei, took leave, traveled ahead over a hundred li, met him on the road, and for hundreds of li helped with supplies and food.

manualTranslations.zh: 威疑之，密誘問，乃知其都督也，因取向所賜絹荅謝而遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei grew suspicious and secretly questioned him, then learned he was the commandant; he therefore took the silk his father had granted, returned it in thanks, and sent him away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei grew suspicious, questioned him quietly, learned he was the commandant, returned the silk in thanks, and sent him away.

manualTranslations.zh: 後因他信，具以白質。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, through another message, he fully reported it to Zhi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later he reported the whole affair to Hu Zhi in another letter.

manualTranslations.zh: 質杖其都督一百，除吏名。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi had the commandant beaten one hundred strokes and struck his name from the roster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi had the commandant beaten one hundred strokes and removed him from the rolls.

manualTranslations.zh: 其父子清慎如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Father and son were pure and cautious to this degree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Father and son were scrupulous to this degree.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是名譽著聞，歷位宰牧。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon his reputation became renowned, and he held successive posts as chief and governor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His reputation spread, and he served in successive governorships.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉武帝賜見，論邊事，語及平生。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin granted him an audience, discussed border affairs, and spoke of their whole lives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin received him, discussed frontier affairs, and spoke of their lives.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝歎其父清，謂威曰：「卿清孰與父清？」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor sighed at his father’s purity and said to Wei, "Are you purer, or is your father purer?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Hu Zhi’s integrity and asked Wei, "Who is purer—you or your father?"

manualTranslations.zh: 威對曰：「臣不如也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Wei replied, "Your servant is not as good."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei answered, "I am not his equal."

manualTranslations.zh: 帝曰：「以何爲不如？」
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor said, "In what way are you not as good?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How are you not his equal?"

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「臣父清恐人知，臣清恐人不知，是臣不如者遠也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He replied, "My father’s purity feared that people would know; my purity fears that people will not know—that is how far your servant is not as good."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He said, "My father feared people would learn of his integrity; I fear they will not—that is how far I fall short."

manualTranslations.zh: 官至前將軍、青州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In office he reached general of the van and inspector of Qing Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the van and inspector of Qing Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 太康元年卒，追贈鎮東將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in the first year of Taikang and was posthumously appointed general who Stabilizes the East.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Taikang 1 and was posthumously made general who Stabilizes the East.

manualTranslations.zh: 威弟羆，字季象，征南將軍；
manualTranslations.literal: Wei’s younger brother Pi, courtesy name Jixiang, was general who campaigns south;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei’s brother Hu Pi, styled Jixiang, was a south-campaigning general;

manualTranslations.zh: 威子弈，字次孫，平東將軍；
manualTranslations.literal: Wei’s son Yi, courtesy name Cisun, was general who Pacifies the East;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei’s son Hu Yi, styled Cisun, was general who Pacifies the East;

manualTranslations.zh: 並以潔行垂名。
manualTranslations.literal: all were famed for pure conduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: all were famed for spotless conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 有殊績，歷三郡守，所在有名。
manualTranslations.literal: He had outstanding achievement, served as grand administrator of three commanderies, and wherever he was had reputation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He achieved distinction as grand administrator of three commanderies and was renowned wherever he served.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒於安定。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in Anding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Anding.

manualTranslations.zh: 王昶字文舒，太原晉陽人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Chang’s courtesy name was Wenshu; he was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Chang, courtesy Wenshu, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 案
manualTranslations.literal: Investigation
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes

manualTranslations.zh: 〈王氏譜〉
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Genealogy of the Wang clan〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈the Genealogy of the Wang clan〉

manualTranslations.zh: ：昶伯父柔，字叔優；
manualTranslations.literal: : Chang’s father’s elder brother Rou, courtesy name Shuyou;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: : Wang Chang’s uncle Rou, styled Shuyou;

manualTranslations.zh: 父澤，字季道。
manualTranslations.literal: father Ze, courtesy name Jidao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and his father Ze, styled Jidao.

manualTranslations.zh: 〈郭林宗傳〉
manualTranslations.literal: 〈Biography of Guo Linzong〉
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 〈the Biography of Guo Linzong〉

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：叔優、季道幼少之時，聞林宗有知人之鑒，共往候之，請問才行所宜，以自處業。
manualTranslations.literal: states: When Shuyou and Jidao were young they heard that Linzong had the discernment to know men, went together to visit him, and asked what conduct and talent suited them so as to settle their pursuits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: says that in youth Shuyou and Jidao heard Linzong was famed for judging men, visited him together, and asked what paths suited their talents.

manualTranslations.zh: 林宗笑曰：「卿二人皆二千石才也，雖然，叔優當以仕宦顯，季道宜以經術進，若違才易務，亦不至也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Linzong laughed and said, "You two are both talents for two-thousand-shi office; even so, Shuyou ought to become prominent through official service, and Jidao ought to advance through classical learning—if you violate your talents and change your pursuits, you will not reach it either."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Linzong laughed: "Both of you are two-thousand-shi material; Shuyou should rise through office, Jidao through scholarship—swap paths and you will not succeed."

manualTranslations.zh: 叔優等從其言。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuyou and the others followed his words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They took his advice.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔優至北中郎將，季道代郡太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuyou reached North Central Commandant; Jidao became grand administrator of Dai commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuyou became north central commandant; Jidao became grand administrator of Dai.

manualTranslations.zh: 少與同郡王淩俱知名。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he and Wang Ling of the same commandery were both renowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In youth he and Wang Ling of the same commandery were both famed.

manualTranslations.zh: 淩年長，昶兄事之。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling was older, and Chang treated him as an elder brother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ling was older, and Wang Chang treated him as an elder brother.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝在東宮，昶爲太子文學，遷中庶子。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wendi was in the Eastern Palace, Chang was literary aide to the heir apparent and was promoted to palace aide to the heir apparent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wendi was crown prince, Wang Chang served as his literary aide and rose to palace mentor.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝踐阼，徙散騎侍郎，爲洛陽典農。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wendi ascended the throne, [Chang] was shifted to attendant cavalry and served as agricultural intendant of Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wendi took the throne, Wang Chang became attendant cavalry and agricultural intendant of Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 時都畿樹木成林，昶斫開荒萊，勤勸百姓，墾田特多。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time trees in the capital region formed forests; Chang cut open wasteland, urged the people diligently, and opened especially much farmland.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He cleared wooded wastes around the capital, urged the people to farm, and opened unusually much land.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷兖州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to inspector of Yan Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Yan Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，加揚烈將軍，賜爵關內侯。
manualTranslations.literal: When Mingdi ascended the throne, [Chang] was given the additional title General Who Displays Fierce Valor and granted the rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Mingdi took the throne, he was made General Who Displays Fierce Valor and secondary marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 昶雖在外任，心存朝廷，以爲魏承秦、漢之弊，法制苛碎，不大釐改國典以準先王之風，而望治化復興，不可得也。
manualTranslations.literal: Although Chang was in outer office, his heart was with the court; he thought that Wei inherited the defects of Qin and Han, that laws and institutions were harsh and minute, and that without greatly reforming the national canons to align with the style of former kings, hoping for governing transformation to revive was impossible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though serving in the provinces, Wang Chang kept the court in mind and believed Wei inherited Qin and Han abuses; without broad reform to ancient standards, revival was impossible.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃著治論，略依古制而合於時務者二十餘篇，又著兵書十餘篇，言奇正之用，《孫子兵法》曰：兵以正合，以奇勝；
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he composed the Treatise on Governance, more than twenty chapters broadly following ancient institutions and suited to present affairs, and also composed more than ten chapters on military matters discussing the use of orthodox and unorthodox methods. The Art of War of Sunzi states: "An army joins through the orthodox and wins through the unorthodox;"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wrote the Treatise on Governance in more than twenty chapters adapting ancient models to current needs, and more than ten chapters on warfare on orthodox and unorthodox tactics, citing Sunzi: "Join battle in the orthodox way; win by the unorthodox."

manualTranslations.zh: 奇正還相生，若循環之無端。
manualTranslations.literal: orthodox and unorthodox in turn generate each other, like cycling without end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Orthodox and unorthodox generate each other in endless cycle."

manualTranslations.zh: 青龍中奏之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Qinglong era he submitted them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He submitted both works in the Qinglong era.

sourceRange.text: 入爲丞相東曹議令史，州請爲治中。將軍張遼與其護軍武周有隙。遼見刺史溫恢求請質，質辭以疾。遼出謂質曰：「僕委意於君，何以相辜如此？」質曰：「古人之交也，取多知其不貪，奔北知其不怯，聞流言而不信，故可終也。武伯南身爲雅士，往者將軍稱之不容於口，今以睚眦之恨，乃成嫌隙。睚，五賣反。眦，士賣反。況質才薄，豈能終好？是以不願也。」遼感言，復與周平。虞預《晉書》曰：周字伯南，沛國竹邑人。位至光祿大夫。子陔，字元夏。陔及二弟韶、茂，皆總角見稱，並有器望，雖鄉人諸父，未能覺其多少。時同郡劉公榮，名知人，嘗造周。周謂曰：「卿有知人之明，欲使三兒見卿，卿爲目高下，以效郭、許之聽可乎？」公榮乃自詣陔兄弟，與共言語，觀其舉動。出語周曰：「君三子皆國士也。元夏器量最優，有輔佐之風，展力仕宦，可爲亞公。叔夏、季夏，不減常伯、納言也。」陔少出仕宦，歷職內外，泰始初爲吏部尚書，遷左僕射、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，卒於官。陔以在魏已爲大臣，本非佐命之數，懷遜讓，不得已而居位，故在官職，無所荷任，夙夜思恭而已。終始全潔，當世以爲美談。韶歷二官吏部郎。山濤啟事稱韶清白有誠，終於散騎常侍。茂至侍中、尚書。潁川荀愷，宣帝外孫，世祖姑子，自負貴戚，要與茂交。茂拒而不荅，由是見怒。元康元年291年，楊駿被誅。愷時爲尚書僕射，以茂駿之姨弟，陷爲駿黨，遂枉見殺，衆咸冤痛之。

manualTranslations.zh: 入爲丞相東曹議令史，州請爲治中。
manualTranslations.literal: He entered service as a clerk in the eastern bureau of the chancellor’s staff, and the province requested him as aide-de-camp.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He became a clerk in the chancellor’s eastern bureau, and the province wanted him as aide-de-camp.

manualTranslations.zh: 將軍張遼與其護軍武周有隙。
manualTranslations.literal: General Zhang Liao had a rift with his protector-general Wu Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Zhang Liao feuded with his protector-general Wu Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 遼見刺史溫恢求請質，質辭以疾。
manualTranslations.literal: Liao saw Inspector Wen Hui and asked that Zhi be sent; Zhi declined on grounds of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liao asked Inspector Wen Hui to lend him Hu Zhi; Hu Zhi pleaded illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 遼出謂質曰：「僕委意於君，何以相辜如此？
manualTranslations.literal: Liao went out and said to Zhi, "I have entrusted my intent to you—why have you wronged me so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liao confronted Hu Zhi: "I trusted you—why treat me like this?

manualTranslations.zh: 」質曰：「古人之交也，取多知其不貪，奔北知其不怯，聞流言而不信，故可終也。
manualTranslations.literal: " Zhi said, "In the friendship of ancients, taking much showed one knew the other was not greedy; fleeing north showed one knew the other was not cowardly; hearing slander and not believing—thus friendship could last.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Hu Zhi answered, "Ancient friendship endured because generosity proved no greed, retreat proved no cowardice, and slander was not believed.

manualTranslations.zh: 武伯南身爲雅士，往者將軍稱之不容於口，今以睚眦之恨，乃成嫌隙。
manualTranslations.literal: Wu Bonan is a refined gentleman; formerly the general praised him without cease, yet now over the hatred of a trifle a rift has formed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Bonan is a man of refinement whom you once praised endlessly; now a petty grudge has opened a breach.

manualTranslations.zh: 睚，五賣反。
manualTranslations.literal: Ya—fanqie: wu plus mai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ya (fanqie: wu + mai).

manualTranslations.zh: 眦，士賣反。
manualTranslations.literal: Zi—fanqie: shi plus mai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zi (fanqie: shi + mai).

manualTranslations.zh: 況質才薄，豈能終好？
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Zhi’s talent is slight—how could friendship last?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My own talents are slight—how could I keep the peace?

manualTranslations.zh: 是以不願也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore I am unwilling."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is why I refused."

manualTranslations.zh: 」遼感言，復與周平。
manualTranslations.literal: " Liao was moved by the words and made peace with Zhou again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Zhang Liao took the point and reconciled with Wu Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 虞預《晉書》曰：周字伯南，沛國竹邑人。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu Yu’s Jin shu states: Zhou’s courtesy name was Bonan; he was a man of Zhuyi in Pei principality.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu Yu’s Jin shu says Wu Zhou, styled Bonan, came from Zhuyi in Pei.

manualTranslations.zh: 位至光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: He rose to Grand Master for the Imperial Household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master for the imperial household.

manualTranslations.zh: 子陔，字元夏。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Gai, courtesy name Yuanxia.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Wu Gai, styled Yuanxia.

manualTranslations.zh: 陔及二弟韶、茂，皆總角見稱，並有器望，雖鄉人諸父，未能覺其多少。
manualTranslations.literal: Gai and his two younger brothers Shao and Mao were all praised while still youths, all possessed capacity and reputation, and even village elders and fathers could not gauge their measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gai and his brothers Shao and Mao were praised from childhood; even elders in the village could not fully measure them.

manualTranslations.zh: 時同郡劉公榮，名知人，嘗造周。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Liu Gongrong of the same commandery, famed for knowing men, once visited Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Gongrong of the same commandery, famed as a judge of men, once called on Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 周謂曰：「卿有知人之明，欲使三兒見卿，卿爲目高下，以效郭、許之聽可乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou said to him, "You have the clarity to know men; I wish my three sons to meet you—will you appraise them high and low, emulating the judgments of Guo and Xu?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou asked, "You read men well. May my three sons meet you and be ranked as Guo and Xu once did?"

manualTranslations.zh: 」公榮乃自詣陔兄弟，與共言語，觀其舉動。
manualTranslations.literal: " Gongrong thereupon went in person to Gai and his brothers, conversed with them, and observed their conduct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Gongrong visited the brothers, talked with them, and watched their bearing.

manualTranslations.zh: 出語周曰：「君三子皆國士也。
manualTranslations.literal: Coming out he told Zhou, "Your three sons are all men of state caliber.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Afterward he told Zhou, "All three sons are state-caliber men.

manualTranslations.zh: 元夏器量最優，有輔佐之風，展力仕宦，可爲亞公。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuanxia’s capacity is finest; he has the air of one who assists; exerting strength in office, he may serve as a deputy minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuanxia has the greatest breadth and the air of a chief minister’s deputy.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔夏、季夏，不減常伯、納言也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuxia and Jixia are no less than Changbo or Nayin."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuxia and Jixia are the equal of high counselors."

manualTranslations.zh: 」陔少出仕宦，歷職內外，泰始初爲吏部尚書，遷左僕射、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，卒於官。
manualTranslations.literal: " Gai left home young to enter office, served inside and outside the court, in the beginning of Taishi became minister of the personnel bureau, was promoted to left vice director, right grand master for the imperial household, and grand marshal with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and died in office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Wu Gai entered service young, rose through court and field posts, became personnel minister at the start of Taishi, then vice director, right grand master, and grand marshal with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and died in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 陔以在魏已爲大臣，本非佐命之數，懷遜讓，不得已而居位，故在官職，無所荷任，夙夜思恭而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Gai had already been a great minister in Wei and was not originally of the number who aided the mandate, he harbored humility and reluctance and held office only because he could not refuse; therefore in office he undertook no burden of responsibility and only thought of reverence morning and night.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having already been a Wei minister, Gai was not among the founders of Jin; he accepted office reluctantly and took on no real burden, striving only to be reverent.

manualTranslations.zh: 終始全潔，當世以爲美談。
manualTranslations.literal: From beginning to end he preserved his integrity, and his age took it as a fine story.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He preserved his integrity throughout, and his contemporaries praised it.

manualTranslations.zh: 韶歷二官吏部郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Shao served as gentleman of the personnel bureau in two administrations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shao served twice as a personnel gentleman.

manualTranslations.zh: 山濤啟事稱韶清白有誠，終於散騎常侍。
manualTranslations.literal: Shan Tao’s memorial praised Shao as pure, white, and sincere; he ended as regular attendant cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shan Tao praised Shao’s integrity; he ended as regular attendant of the cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 茂至侍中、尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao reached palace attendant and secretary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mao rose to palace attendant and secretary.

manualTranslations.zh: 潁川荀愷，宣帝外孫，世祖姑子，自負貴戚，要與茂交。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun Kai of Yingchuan, the Xuan Emperor’s grandson by a daughter and the Shizu Emperor’s nephew by a sister, relied on his noble kinship and pressed Mao for friendship.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun Kai of Yingchuan, imperial kin by marriage, pressed Mao for friendship on the strength of his rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 茂拒而不荅，由是見怒。
manualTranslations.literal: Mao refused and did not respond, and thereby incurred anger.

sourceRange.text: 及會白鄧艾不軌，文王將西，悌復曰：「鍾會所統，五六倍於鄧艾，但可敕會取艾，不足自行。」文王曰：「卿忘前時所言邪，而更雲可不須行乎？雖爾，此言不可宣也。我要自當以信義待人，但人不負我，我豈可先人生心哉！近日賈護軍問我，言：『頗疑鍾會不？』我答言：『如今遣卿行，寧可復疑卿邪？』賈亦無以易我語也。我到長安，則自了矣。」軍至長安，會果已死，咸如所策。按咸熙元年〈百官名〉：邵悌字元伯，陽平人。《漢晉春秋》曰：文王聞鍾會功曹向雄之收葬會也，召而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭於東市而我不問，今鍾會躬為叛逆而又輒收葬，若復相容，其如王法何！」雄曰：「昔先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後收葬哉？今王誅既加，於法已備，雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。法立於上，教弘於下，以此訓物，雄曰可矣！何必使雄背死違生，以立於時。殿下讎對枯骨，捐之中野，百歲之後，為臧獲所笑，豈仁賢所掩哉？」王悅，與宴談而遣之。習鑿齒曰：向伯茂可謂勇於蹈義也，哭王經而哀感市人，葬鍾會而義動明主，彼皆忠烈奮勁，知死而往，非存生也。況使經、會處世，或身在急難，而有不赴者乎？故尋其奉死之心，可以見事生之情，覽其忠貞之節，足以愧背義之士矣。王加禮而遣，可謂明達。

manualTranslations.zh: 文王曰：「卿忘前時所言邪，而更雲可不須行乎？

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao said: "Have you forgotten what you said before, yet now again say there is no need to go?

manualTranslations.idiomatic: I myself must treat people with trust and righteousness; if others do not betray me, how can I first harbor suspicion in my heart!

manualTranslations.literal: The Annals of Han and Jin says: When the Prince of Wen heard that Zhong Hui's merit officer Xiang Xiong had gathered and buried Hui, he summoned and reproached him, saying: "Formerly when Wang Jing died, you wept at the eastern market and I did not question you; now Zhong Hui personally became a rebel and yet you again gather and bury him—if I again tolerate this, what of the king's law!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals of Han and Jin says: When Sima Zhao heard that Zhong Hui's merit officer Xiang Xiong had gathered and buried Hui, he summoned and reproached him, saying: "Formerly when Wang Jing died, you wept at the eastern market and I did not question you; now Zhong Hui personally became a rebel and yet you again gather and bury him—if I again tolerate this, what of the king's law!"

manualTranslations.zh: 雄曰：「昔先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後收葬哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Xiong said: "Formerly the former kings covered exposed bones and buried flesh remains; benevolence flowed even to decayed bones—did they first divine merit and crime before gathering and burying?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiong said: "Formerly the former kings covered exposed bones and buried flesh remains; benevolence flowed even to decayed bones—did they first divine merit and crime before gathering and burying?

manualTranslations.zh: 今王誅既加，於法已備，雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the king's punishment has already been applied and the law is complete; Xiong, moved by righteousness, gathered and buried—instruction too is not lacking.

manualTranslations.zh: 法立於上，教弘於下，以此訓物，雄曰可矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Law is established above and instruction is spread below; to train the multitude thus—Xiong says it is acceptable!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Law is established above and instruction is spread below; to train the multitude thus—Xiong says it is acceptable!

manualTranslations.zh: 何必使雄背死違生，以立於時。
manualTranslations.literal: Why must Xiong turn his back on the dead and violate life to stand in the age?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why must Xiong turn his back on the dead and violate life to stand in the age?

manualTranslations.zh: 殿下讎對枯骨，捐之中野，百歲之後，為臧獲所笑，豈仁賢所掩哉？」
manualTranslations.literal: Your Highness would face dry bones in enmity and cast them into the wild; a hundred years hence you would be laughed at by slaves—can benevolent worthies cover this up?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Highness would face dry bones in enmity and cast them into the wild; a hundred years hence you would be laughed at by slaves—can benevolent worthies cover this up?"

manualTranslations.zh: 王悅，與宴談而遣之。
manualTranslations.literal: The king was pleased, feasted and talked with him, and sent him away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The prince was pleased, feasted and talked with him, and sent him away.

manualTranslations.zh: 習鑿齒曰：向伯茂可謂勇於蹈義也，哭王經而哀感市人，葬鍾會而義動明主，彼皆忠烈奮勁，知死而往，非存生也。
manualTranslations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: Xiang Bamao may be called brave in treading righteousness; weeping for Wang Jing he moved the market people to grief, burying Zhong Hui he moved the enlightened lord by righteousness—they were all loyal and fierce in exertion, knowing death yet going—not preserving life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi says: Xiang Bamao may be called brave in treading righteousness; weeping for Wang Jing he moved the market people to grief, burying Zhong Hui he moved the enlightened lord by righteousness—they were all loyal and fierce in exertion, knowing death yet going—not preserving life.

manualTranslations.zh: 況使經、會處世，或身在急難，而有不赴者乎？
manualTranslations.literal: How much more if Jing and Hui were in the world—or if one were in urgent peril—would there be any who would not go?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much more if Jing and Hui were in the world—or if one were in urgent peril—would there be any who would not go?

manualTranslations.zh: 故尋其奉死之心，可以見事生之情，覽其忠貞之節，足以愧背義之士矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore tracing their hearts in serving death, one can see their feelings in serving life; viewing their loyal and steadfast integrity, it is enough to shame those who betray righteousness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore tracing their hearts in serving death, one can see their feelings in serving life; viewing their loyal and steadfast integrity, it is enough to shame those who betray righteousness.

manualTranslations.zh: 王加禮而遣，可謂明達。
manualTranslations.literal: The king added courtesy in sending him away—this may be called enlightened judgment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The prince added courtesy in sending him away—this may be called enlightened judgment.

sourceRange.text: 誕既與玄、颺等至親，又王凌、毌丘儉累見夷滅，懼不自安，傾帑藏振施以結眾心，厚養親附及揚州輕俠者數千人為死士。《魏書》曰：誕賞賜過度。有犯死者，虧制以活之。甘露元年256年冬，吳賊欲向徐堨，計誕所督兵馬足以待之，而復請十萬眾守壽春，又求臨淮築城以備寇，內欲保有淮南。朝廷微知誕有自疑心，以誕舊臣，欲入度之。二年五月，徵為司空。誕被詔書，愈恐，遂反。召會諸將，自出攻揚州刺史樂綝，殺之。《世語》曰：司馬文王既秉朝政，長史賈充以為宜遣參佐慰勞四征，於是遣充至壽春。充還啟文王：「誕再在揚州，有威名，民望所歸。今徵，必不來，禍小事淺；不徵，事遲禍大。」乃以為司空。不遣使者，健步齎書，使以兵付樂綝，此必綝所為。」乃將左右數百人至揚州，揚州人欲閉門，誕叱曰：「卿非我故吏邪！」徑入，綝逃上樓，就斬之。魏末傳曰：賈充與誕相見，談說時事，因謂誕曰：「洛中諸賢，皆原禪代，君所知也。君以為云何？」誕厲色曰：「卿非賈豫州子？世受魏恩，如何負國，欲以魏室輸人乎？非吾所忍聞。若洛中有難，吾當死之。」充默然。誕既被徵，請諸牙門置酒飲宴，呼牙門從兵，皆賜酒令醉，謂眾人曰：「前作千人鎧仗始成，欲以擊賊，今當還洛，不復得用，欲蹔出，將見人遊戲，須臾還耳；諸君且止。」乃嚴鼓將士七百人出。樂綝聞之，閉州門。誕歷南門宣言曰：「當還洛邑，蹔出遊戲，揚州何為閉門見備？」前至東門，東門复閉，乃使兵緣城攻門，州人悉走，因風放火，焚其府庫，遂殺綝。誕表曰：「臣受國重任，統兵在東。揚州刺史樂綝專詐，說臣與吳交通，又言被詔當代臣位，無狀日久。臣奉國命，以死自立，終無異端。忿綝不忠，輒將步騎七百人，以今月六日討綝，即日斬首，函頭驛馬傳送。若聖朝明臣，臣即魏臣；不明臣，臣即吳臣。不勝發憤有日，謹拜表陳愚，悲感泣血，哽咽斷絕，不知所如，乞朝廷察臣至誠。」臣松之以為魏末傳所言，率皆鄙陋。疑誕表言曲，不至於此也。斂淮南及淮北郡縣屯田口十餘萬官兵，揚州新附勝兵者四五萬人，聚谷足一年食，閉城自守。遣長史吳綱將小子靚至吳請救。《世語》曰：黃初末，吳人髮長沙王吳芮塚，以其塼於臨湘為孫堅立廟。芮容貌如生，衣服不朽。後豫發者見吳綱曰：「君何類長沙王吳芮，但微短耳。」綱瞿然曰；「是先祖也，君何由見之？」見者言所由，綱曰：「更葬否？」答曰：「即更葬矣。」自芮之卒年至塚發，四百餘年，綱，芮之十六世孫矣。吳人大喜，遣將全懌、全端、唐咨、王祚等，率三萬眾，密與文欽俱來應誕。以誕為左都護、假節、大司徒、驃騎將軍、青州牧、壽春侯。是時鎮南將軍王基始至，督諸軍圍壽春，未合。咨、欽等從城東北，因山乘險，得將其眾突入城。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: When someone deserved death for an offense, he bent the law to spare them.

manualTranslations.zh: 甘露元年256年冬，吳賊欲向徐堨，計誕所督兵馬足以待之，而復請十萬眾守壽春，又求臨淮築城以備寇，內欲保有淮南。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter of the first year of Ganlu (256), Wu bandits intended to move against Xu embankment; reckoning that the troops and horses Dan supervised were sufficient to meet them, yet he again requested one hundred thousand men to guard Shouchun and also asked to build a fortress at Linhuai against raiders—inwardly wishing to keep possession of Huainan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Ganlu (256), Wu forces planned to strike Xu embankment; though the troops under Zhuge Dan were enough to meet them, he again asked for one hundred thousand men to hold Shouchun and to build a fortress at Linhuai against invasion—secretly intending to keep control of Huainan.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷微知誕有自疑心，以誕舊臣，欲入度之。
manualTranslations.literal: The court faintly knew Dan harbored self-doubt; because he was an old minister, they wished to enter and assess him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court had some inkling of Zhuge Dan's unease; as an old servant of the dynasty, they meant to summon him in and take his measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年五月，徵為司空。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, he was summoned to serve as Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Ganlu, he was summoned to the post of Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 誕被詔書，愈恐，遂反。
manualTranslations.literal: Dan received the edict, grew all the more fearful, and thereupon rebelled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan received the edict, his fear deepened and he rebelled.

manualTranslations.zh: 召會諸將，自出攻揚州刺史樂綝，殺之。
manualTranslations.literal: He called the generals together, personally went out to attack Inspector of Yang Province Yue Lin, and killed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He assembled his generals, marched out himself against Yang Province inspector Yue Lin, and killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：司馬文王既秉朝政，長史賈充以為宜遣參佐慰勞四征，於是遣充至壽春。
manualTranslations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: Once Sima Wenwang had taken hold of court government, chief clerk Jia Chong thought aides should be sent to console and encourage the four expeditionary commanders; accordingly Chong was dispatched to Shouchun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Sayings of the Age relates that once Sima Zhao held court power, chief clerk Jia Chong argued that staff should be sent to console the four frontier commanders, and Chong was dispatched to Shouchun.

manualTranslations.zh: 充還啟文王：「誕再在揚州，有威名，民望所歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong returned and reported to Wenwang: "Dan has twice served in Yang Province; he has prestige and is the object of popular hopes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong returned and reported to Sima Zhao: "Zhuge Dan has twice held Yang Province; he has a formidable reputation and the people look to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 今徵，必不來，禍小事淺；
manualTranslations.literal: If summoned now, he will surely not come—the disaster is small and shallow;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Summon him now and he will surely refuse—the harm will be small;

manualTranslations.zh: 不徵，事遲禍大。」
manualTranslations.literal: If not summoned, the affair will be delayed and the disaster great."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: wait, and the trouble will grow far worse."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃以為司空。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed him Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 不遣使者，健步齎書，使以兵付樂綝，此必綝所為。」
manualTranslations.literal: No envoy was sent; a swift runner bore the letter ordering the transfer of troops to Yue Lin—this must be Lin's doing."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No envoy came—only a runner with orders to hand the troops to Yue Lin; this must be Lin's doing."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃將左右數百人至揚州，揚州人欲閉門，誕叱曰：「卿非我故吏邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he took several hundred personal followers to Yang Province; the people of Yang Province wished to shut the gates; Dan shouted: "Are you not my old subordinates!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then took several hundred personal followers to the provincial seat; when the locals tried to shut the gates, Dan shouted: "Are you not my old subordinates!"

manualTranslations.zh: 徑入，綝逃上樓，就斬之。
manualTranslations.literal: He entered straight in; Lin fled upstairs and was beheaded on the spot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went straight in; Yue Lin fled upstairs and was beheaded where he stood.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏末傳曰：賈充與誕相見，談說時事，因謂誕曰：「洛中諸賢，皆原禪代，君所知也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Traditions of Late Wei says: Jia Chong met with Dan and discussed current affairs; thereupon he said to Dan: "The worthies of Luoyang all consent to the transfer of the mandate—you know this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Traditions of Late Wei says that when Jia Chong met Zhuge Dan and discussed current affairs, he said to him: "The worthies of Luoyang all accept the transfer of the mandate—you know this.

manualTranslations.zh: 君以為云何？」
manualTranslations.literal: What do you think?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What is your view?"

manualTranslations.zh: 誕厲色曰：「卿非賈豫州子？
manualTranslations.literal: Dan fiercely colored and said: "Are you not the son of Inspector of Yu Province Jia?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan flushed with anger and said: "Are you not the son of Inspector Jia of Yu Province?

manualTranslations.zh: 世受魏恩，如何負國，欲以魏室輸人乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Your family has received Wei grace for generations—how can you betray the state and wish to hand the house of Wei to others?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your house has enjoyed Wei's favor for generations—how can you betray the state and hand the Wei throne to others?

manualTranslations.zh: 非吾所忍聞。
manualTranslations.literal: This is not what I can bear to hear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is more than I can bear to hear.

manualTranslations.zh: 若洛中有難，吾當死之。」
manualTranslations.literal: If Luoyang faces peril, I shall die for it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Luoyang is in danger, I will die for it."

manualTranslations.zh: 充默然。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong fell silent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Chong said nothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 誕既被徵，請諸牙門置酒飲宴，呼牙門從兵，皆賜酒令醉，謂眾人曰：「前作千人鎧仗始成，欲以擊賊，今當還洛，不復得用，欲蹔出，將見人遊戲，須臾還耳；
manualTranslations.literal: Once Dan had been summoned, he invited all the gate commanders to a drinking feast, called the gate-follower soldiers, gave them all wine and made them drunk, and said to the crowd: "Earlier the thousand suits of armor and weapons were just completed, intended for striking bandits; now we must return to Luoyang and can no longer use them; I wish to go out briefly to let the men parade—I will be back in a moment;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the summons arrived, Zhuge Dan invited the gate commanders to a feast, called up their followers, plied them with wine until they were drunk, and told the assembly: "The thousand suits of armor we finished were meant for fighting bandits; now that we must return to Luoyang they are useless, so I mean to go out briefly and let the men drill for sport—I will be right back;

manualTranslations.zh: 諸君且止。」
manualTranslations.literal: All of you stay here."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All of you wait here."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃嚴鼓將士七百人出。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he beat the drums sternly and led seven hundred officers and soldiers out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then he beat the drums and marched out with seven hundred officers and men.

manualTranslations.zh: 樂綝聞之，閉州門。
manualTranslations.literal: Yue Lin heard of it and shut the provincial gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yue Lin heard of it, he shut the provincial gates.

manualTranslations.zh: 誕歷南門宣言曰：「當還洛邑，蹔出遊戲，揚州何為閉門見備？」
manualTranslations.literal: Dan went through the south gate proclaiming: "We are to return to the capital; we go out briefly for sport—why does Yang Province shut its gates and treat us as enemies?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan passed the south gate proclaiming: "We are returning to the capital and only going out for sport—why does Yang Province shut its gates against us?"

manualTranslations.zh: 前至東門，東門复閉，乃使兵緣城攻門，州人悉走，因風放火，焚其府庫，遂殺綝。
manualTranslations.literal: Advancing to the east gate, the east gate too was shut; thereupon he had troops scale the wall to assault the gate; provincial people all fled; taking advantage of the wind he set fire, burned the government storehouses, and then killed Lin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the east gate the doors were shut again, so he had his men climb the walls to force them; the townspeople fled; he set fire to the government storehouses with the wind at his back and killed Yue Lin.

manualTranslations.zh: 誕表曰：「臣受國重任，統兵在東。
manualTranslations.literal: Dan submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has received the state's heavy charge, commanding troops in the east.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan submitted a memorial: "Your servant bears a weighty charge from the state, commanding troops in the east.

manualTranslations.zh: 揚州刺史樂綝專詐，說臣與吳交通，又言被詔當代臣位，無狀日久。
manualTranslations.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Yue Lin is wholly deceitful; he says your servant communicates with Wu, and also says he was ordered by edict to replace your servant's post—his misconduct has long continued.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Province inspector Yue Lin is wholly treacherous: he claims I am in contact with Wu and says an edict has named him to replace me—his outrages have gone on for some time.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣奉國命，以死自立，終無異端。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant obeys the state's command, establishing himself by death—never will there be disloyalty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I serve the state's command and stand ready to die for it—I will never waver in loyalty.

manualTranslations.zh: 忿綝不忠，輒將步騎七百人，以今月六日討綝，即日斬首，函頭驛馬傳送。
manualTranslations.literal: Angered at Lin's disloyalty, your servant forthwith led seven hundred infantry and cavalry; on the sixth day of this month he campaigned against Lin; that same day he beheaded him, boxed the head, and sent it by post horse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Outraged at Yue Lin's treachery, I led seven hundred foot and horse on the sixth of this month to punish him; that same day I beheaded him, boxed the head, and sent it by relay post.

manualTranslations.zh: 若聖朝明臣，臣即魏臣；
manualTranslations.literal: If the holy court understands your servant, your servant is Wei's minister;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the court understands me, I am Wei's minister;

manualTranslations.zh: 不明臣，臣即吳臣。
manualTranslations.literal: If it does not understand your servant, your servant is Wu's minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if it does not, I am Wu's minister.

manualTranslations.zh: 不勝發憤有日，謹拜表陳愚，悲感泣血，哽咽斷絕，不知所如，乞朝廷察臣至誠。」
manualTranslations.literal: Unable to restrain grievance for days, your servant respectfully bows this memorial stating his earnestness; grief and emotion to tears of blood, choking and cut off, not knowing what to do—begging the court to examine your servant's utmost sincerity."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Long unable to contain my grief, I respectfully submit this memorial; weeping blood with sorrow, choked and overcome, I know not what to do, and beg the court to see my utmost sincerity."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為魏末傳所言，率皆鄙陋。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Songzhi considers that what the Traditions of Late Wei states is on the whole all coarse and vulgar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi holds that what the Traditions of Late Wei reports is on the whole crude and vulgar.

manualTranslations.zh: 疑誕表言曲，不至於此也。
manualTranslations.literal: He doubts Dan's memorial language is twisted—it would not reach this point.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He suspects the wording of Zhuge Dan's memorial was distorted and would not have gone this far.

manualTranslations.zh: 斂淮南及淮北郡縣屯田口十餘萬官兵，揚州新附勝兵者四五萬人，聚谷足一年食，閉城自守。
manualTranslations.literal: He gathered more than one hundred thousand officials and soldiers from military-agriculture households of Huainan and Huaibei commanderies and counties, and forty to fifty thousand victorious soldiers newly attached in Yang Province; stored grain sufficient for a year's food; shut the city and defended himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He mustered more than one hundred thousand officials and soldiers from military-agriculture households across Huainan and Huaibei, plus forty or fifty thousand fit troops newly attached in Yang Province; stockpiled grain for a year; and shut the city to hold it.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣長史吳綱將小子靚至吳請救。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent chief clerk Wu Gang leading his young son Jing to Wu to request rescue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent chief clerk Wu Gang with his young son Jing to Wu to ask for aid.

manualTranslations.zh: 《世語》曰：黃初末，吳人髮長沙王吳芮塚，以其塼於臨湘為孫堅立廟。
manualTranslations.literal: The Sayings of the Age says: At the end of Huangchu, Wu people opened the tomb of King Wu Rui of Changsha, using its bricks at Linxiang to build a temple for Sun Jian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Sayings of the Age relates that near the end of Huangchu, Wu men opened the tomb of King Wu Rui of Changsha and used its bricks at Linxiang to build a temple to Sun Jian.

manualTranslations.zh: 芮容貌如生，衣服不朽。
manualTranslations.literal: Rui's appearance was as if alive; his clothes had not decayed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Rui looked as if alive, and his clothes had not rotted.

manualTranslations.zh: 後豫發者見吳綱曰：「君何類長沙王吳芮，但微短耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Later those about to dig the tomb saw Wu Gang and said: "Sir, how you resemble King Wu Rui of Changsha—only slightly shorter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, those preparing to open the tomb saw Wu Gang and said: "Sir, how you resemble King Wu Rui of Changsha—only a little shorter."

manualTranslations.zh: 綱瞿然曰；
manualTranslations.literal: Gang was startled and said;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Gang started and said;

manualTranslations.zh: 「是先祖也，君何由見之？」
manualTranslations.literal: "He is my ancestor—how did you see him?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "That is my ancestor—how did you see him?"

manualTranslations.zh: 見者言所由，綱曰：「更葬否？」
manualTranslations.literal: The seer told how; Gang said: "Was he reburied or not?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The witness told how; Wu Gang asked: "Was he reburied?"

manualTranslations.zh: 答曰：「即更葬矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: The answer was: "He was reburied at once."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The reply was: "He was reburied immediately."

manualTranslations.zh: 自芮之卒年至塚發，四百餘年，綱，芮之十六世孫矣。
manualTranslations.literal: From the year of Rui's death to the opening of the tomb was more than four hundred years; Gang was Rui's sixteenth-generation descendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Wu Rui's death to the opening of the tomb was more than four hundred years; Wu Gang was his sixteenth-generation descendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳人大喜，遣將全懌、全端、唐咨、王祚等，率三萬眾，密與文欽俱來應誕。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu people were greatly pleased; they sent generals Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and others, leading thirty thousand troops, secretly together with Wen Qin to come and respond to Dan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu court was delighted and sent generals Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Tang Zi, Wang Zuo, and others with thirty thousand men, who secretly joined Wen Qin in coming to Zhuge Dan's aid.

manualTranslations.zh: 以誕為左都護、假節、大司徒、驃騎將軍、青州牧、壽春侯。
manualTranslations.literal: They appointed Dan as left protector-general, with provisional staff of authority, grand minister of education, general of agile cavalry, governor of Qing Province, and marquis of Shouchun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They named Zhuge Dan left protector-general, with provisional authority, grand minister of education, general of agile cavalry, governor of Qing Province, and marquis of Shouchun.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時鎮南將軍王基始至，督諸軍圍壽春，未合。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time General Who Guards the South Wang Ji had just arrived, superintending the various armies to besiege Shouchun—not yet engaged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time General Who Guards the South Wang Ji had just arrived and was directing the armies besieging Shouchun, though the lines were not yet closed.

manualTranslations.zh: 咨、欽等從城東北，因山乘險，得將其眾突入城。
manualTranslations.literal: Zi, Qin, and the others from the northeast of the city, riding the mountains and seizing defiles, were able to lead their troops in a rush into the city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tang Zi, Wen Qin, and the others entered from the northeast, using the mountains and difficult terrain to rush their forces into the city.

sourceRange.text: 冬，以會為鎮西將軍、假節都督關中諸軍事。

localRange.text: 景元三年冬，以會為鎮西將軍、假節都督關中諸軍事。

sourceRange.text: 初，艾為太尉，會為司徒，皆持節、都督諸軍如故，咸未受命而斃。會兄毓，以四年冬薨，會竟未知問。會兄子邕，隨會與俱死，會所養兄子毅及峻、辿敕連反。等下獄，當伏誅。司馬文王表天子下詔曰：「峻等祖父繇，三祖之世，極位臺司，佐命立勳，饗食廟庭。父毓，歷職內外，幹事有績。昔楚思子文之治，不滅斗氏之祀；晉錄成宣之忠，用存趙氏之後。以會、邕之罪，而絕繇、毓之類，吾有愍然！峻、辿兄弟特原，有官爵者如故。惟毅及邕息伏法。」或曰，毓曾密啟司馬文王，言會挾術難保，不可專任，故宥峻等云。《漢晉春秋》曰：文王嘉其忠亮，笑答毓曰：「若如卿言，必不以及宗矣。

manualTranslations.zh: 初，艾為太尉，會為司徒，皆持節、都督諸軍如故，咸未受命而斃。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Ai was Grand Commandant and Hui was Minister of Education; both held the credential insignia and superintended the various armies as before, yet all died before receiving appointment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first Deng Ai was grand commandant and Zhong Hui minister of education; both held the jie staff and superintended the armies as before, yet all died before receiving appointment.

manualTranslations.zh: 會兄毓，以四年冬薨，會竟未知問。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's elder brother Yu died in the winter of the fourth year; Hui to the end did not know the news.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's elder brother Yu died in the winter of the fourth year; Hui to the end did not know the news.

manualTranslations.zh: 會兄子邕，隨會與俱死，會所養兄子毅及峻、辿敕連反。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's elder brother's son Yong died together with Hui; Hui's adopted elder brother's son Yi and Jun and Chan were ordered to rebel in succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui's elder brother's son Yong died together with Hui; Hui's adopted elder brother's son Yi and Jun and Chan were ordered to rebel in succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 等下獄，當伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: They were imprisoned and were to suffer execution.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They were imprisoned and were to suffer execution.

manualTranslations.zh: 司馬文王表天子下詔曰：「峻等祖父繇，三祖之世，極位臺司，佐命立勳，饗食廟庭。
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Zhao, Prince of Wen, memorialized the Son of Heaven, who issued an edict saying: "Jun and the others' grandfather You, in the age of the three founding emperors, reached the highest offices of the terrace and ministers, aided the mandate and established merit, and received sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao, Prince of Wen, memorialized the Son of Heaven, who issued an edict saying: "Jun and the others' grandfather You, in the age of the three founding emperors, reached the highest offices of the terrace and ministers, aided the mandate and established merit, and received sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 父毓，歷職內外，幹事有績。
manualTranslations.literal: Their father Yu served in inner and outer posts and managed affairs with achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their father Yu served in inner and outer posts and managed affairs with achievement.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔楚思子文之治，不滅斗氏之祀；
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Chu, remembering Ziwen's governance, did not extinguish the sacrifices of the Dou clan;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Chu, remembering Ziwen's governance, did not extinguish the sacrifices of the Dou clan;

manualTranslations.zh: 晉錄成宣之忠，用存趙氏之後。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin recorded Cheng Xuan's loyalty and thereby preserved the descendants of the Zhao clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jin recorded Cheng Xuan's loyalty and thereby preserved the descendants of the Zhao clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 以會、邕之罪，而絕繇、毓之類，吾有愍然！
manualTranslations.literal: Because of the crimes of Hui and Yong to cut off the line of You and Yu—I am moved to pity!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of the crimes of Hui and Yong to cut off the line of You and Yu—I am moved to pity!

manualTranslations.zh: 峻、辿兄弟特原，有官爵者如故。
manualTranslations.literal: The brothers Jun and Chan are specially pardoned; those with offices and ranks remain as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The brothers Jun and Chan are specially pardoned; those with offices and ranks remain as before.

manualTranslations.zh: 惟毅及邕息伏法。」
manualTranslations.literal: Only Yi and Yong's son shall suffer the law."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only Yi and Yong's son shall suffer the law."

manualTranslations.zh: 或曰，毓曾密啟司馬文王，言會挾術難保，不可專任，故宥峻等云。
manualTranslations.literal: Some say Yu once secretly reported to Sima Zhao, Prince of Wen, that Hui relied on arts and was hard to keep secure, and could not be entrusted alone—therefore Jun and the others were pardoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some say Yu once secretly reported to Sima Zhao that Hui relied on arts and was hard to keep secure, and could not be entrusted alone—therefore Jun and the others were pardoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：文王嘉其忠亮，笑答毓曰：「若如卿言，必不以及宗矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Annals of Han and Jin says: The Prince of Wen praised his loyalty and candor and smiling answered Yu: "If it were as you say, it would surely not extend to the clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals of Han and Jin says: Sima Zhao praised his loyalty and candor and smiling answered Yu: "If it were as you say, it would surely not extend to the clan.

sourceRange.text: 是時，凌外甥令狐愚以才能為兗州刺史，屯平阿。舅甥並典兵，專淮南之重。凌就遷為司空。司馬宣王既誅曹爽，進凌為太尉，假節鉞。凌、愚密協計，謂齊王不任天位，楚王彪長而才，欲迎立彪都許昌。嘉平元年249年九月，愚遣將張式至白馬，與彪相問往來。凌又遣舍人勞精詣洛陽，語子廣。廣言：「廢立大事，勿為禍先。」《漢晉春秋》曰：凌、愚謀，以帝幼制於強臣，不堪為主，楚王彪長而才，欲迎立之，以興曹氏。凌使人告廣，廣曰：「凡舉大事，應本人情。今曹爽以驕奢失民，何平叔虛而不治，丁、畢、桓、鄧雖並有宿望，皆專競於世。加變易朝典，政令數改，所存雖高而事不下接，民習於舊，眾莫之從。故雖勢傾四海，聲震天下，同日斬戮，名士減半，而百姓安之，莫或之哀，失民故也。今懿情雖難量，事未有逆，而擢用賢能，廣樹勝己，修先朝之政令，副眾心之所求。爽之所以為惡者，彼莫不必改，夙夜匪解，以恤民為先。父子兄弟，並握兵要，未易亡也。」凌不從。臣松之以為如此言之類，皆前史所不載，而猶出習氏。且制言法體不似於昔，疑悉鑿齒所自造者也。其十一月，愚復遣式詣彪，未還，會愚病死。《魏書》曰：愚字公治，本名浚，黃初中，為和戎護軍。烏丸校尉田豫討胡有功，小違節度，愚以法繩之。帝怒，械系愚，免官治罪，詔曰「浚何愚」！遂以名之。正始中，為曹爽長史，後出為兗州刺史。《魏略》曰：愚聞楚王彪有智勇。初東郡有訛言云：「白馬河出妖馬，夜過官牧邊鳴呼，眾馬皆應，明日見其跡，大如斛，行數里，還入河中。」又有謠言：「白馬素羈西南馳，其誰乘者朱虎騎。」楚王小字朱虎，故愚與王凌陰謀立楚王。乃先使人通意於王，言「使君謝王，天下事不可知，原王自愛」！彪亦陰知其意，答言「謝使君，知厚意也。」二年，熒惑守南斗，凌謂：「斗中有星，當有暴貴者。」《魏略》曰：凌聞東平民浩詳知星，呼問詳。詳疑凌有所挾，欲悅其意，不言吳當有死喪，而言淮南楚分也，今吳、楚同佔，當有王者興。故凌計遂定。三年春，吳賊塞塗水。凌欲因此發，大嚴諸軍，表求討賊；詔報不聽。凌陰謀滋甚，遣將軍楊弘以廢立事告兗州刺史黃華，華、弘連名以白太傅司馬宣王。宣王將中軍乘水道討凌，先下赦赦凌罪，又將尚書廣東，使為書喻凌，大軍掩至百尺逼凌。凌自知勢窮，乃乘船單出迎宣王，遣掾王彧謝罪，送印綬、節鉞。軍到丘頭，凌面縛水次。宣王承詔遣主簿解縛反服，見凌，慰勞之，還印綬、節鉞，遣步騎六百人送還京都。凌至項，飲藥死。《魏略》載凌與太傅書曰：「卒聞神軍密發，巳在百尺，雖知命窮盡，遲於相見，身首分離，不以為恨，前後遣使，有書未得還報，企踵西望，無物以譬。昨遣書之後，便乘船來相迎宿丘頭，旦發於浦口，奉被露布赦書，又得二十三日況，累紙誨示，聞命驚愕，五內失守，不知何地可以自處？僕久忝朝恩，歷試無效，統御戎馬，董齊東夏，事有闕廢，中心犯義，罪在三百，妻子同縣，無所禱矣。不圖聖恩天覆地載，橫蒙視息，复睹日月。亡甥令狐愚攜惑群小之言，僕即時呵抑，使不得竟其語。既人已知，神明所鑑，夫非事無陰，卒至發露，知此梟夷之罪也。生我者父母，活我者子也。」又重曰：「身陷刑罪，謬蒙赦宥。今遣掾送印綬，頃至，當如詔書自縛歸命。雖足下私之，官法有分。」及到，如書。太傅使人解其縛。凌既蒙赦，加怙舊好，不復自疑，徑乘小船自趣太傅。太傅使人逆止之，住船淮中，相去十餘丈。凌知見外，乃遙謂太傅曰：「卿直以折簡召我，我當敢不至邪？而乃引軍來乎！」太傅曰：「以卿非肯逐折簡者故也。」凌曰：「卿負我！」太傅曰：「我寧負卿，不負國家。」遂使人送來西。凌自知罪重，試索棺釘，以觀太傅意，太傅給之。凌行到項，夜呼掾屬與決曰：「行年八十，身名並滅邪！」遂自殺。干寶《晉紀》曰：凌到項，見賈逵祠在水側，凌呼曰：「賈梁道，王凌固忠於魏之社稷者，唯爾有神，知之。」其年八月，太傅有疾，夢凌、逵為癘，甚惡之，遂薨。
