manualTranslations.zh: 是時，凌外甥令狐愚以才能為兗州刺史，屯平阿。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time, Ling's nephew Linghu Yu, on account of ability, was made Inspector of Yan Province, stationed at Ping'a.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Ling's nephew Linghu Yu, valued for his talent, served as inspector of Yan Province from a base at Ping'a.

manualTranslations.zh: 舅甥並典兵，專淮南之重。
manualTranslations.literal: Uncle and nephew both commanded troops, monopolizing the weight of Huainan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uncle and nephew both held military command and together controlled the Huainan front.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌就遷為司空。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling was then transferred to serve as Minister of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling was soon transferred to the post of Minister of Works.

manualTranslations.zh: 司馬宣王既誅曹爽，進凌為太尉，假節鉞。
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan, having killed Cao Shuang, advanced Ling to Grand Commandant and granted him the ceremonial staff and battle-axe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan, executed Cao Shuang, he promoted Wang Ling to grand commandant and invested him with the jie staff and battle-axe.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌、愚密協計，謂齊王不任天位，楚王彪長而才，欲迎立彪都許昌。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling and Yu secretly agreed on a plan, saying the Prince of Qi could not bear the heavenly throne, while Prince Cao Biao of Chu was grown and talented; they wished to welcome and enthrone Biao with the capital at Xuchang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu secretly plotted together, arguing that the Prince of Qi was unfit for the throne while Cao Biao, Prince of Chu, was grown and capable; they meant to enthrone Biao and move the capital to Xuchang.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平元年249年九月，愚遣將張式至白馬，與彪相問往來。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jiaping (249), Yu sent general Zhang Shi to Baima to exchange inquiries and messages with Biao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Jiaping (249), Linghu Yu sent General Zhang Shi to Baima to exchange messages with Cao Biao.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌又遣舍人勞精詣洛陽，語子廣。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling also sent houseman Lao Jing to Luoyang to speak with his son Guang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling also sent his attendant Lao Jing to Luoyang to speak with his son Wang Guang.

manualTranslations.zh: 廣言：「廢立大事，勿為禍先。」
manualTranslations.literal: Guang said: "Deposing and enthroning is a great affair; do not be the first to bring disaster."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Guang said, "Deposing and enthroning is a grave matter; do not invite disaster by acting first."

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：凌、愚謀，以帝幼制於強臣，不堪為主，楚王彪長而才，欲迎立之，以興曹氏。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says: Ling and Yu plotted that the emperor was young and controlled by powerful ministers, unfit to be sovereign; Prince Cao Biao of Chu was grown and talented, and they wished to welcome and enthrone him to revive the House of Cao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wang Ling and Linghu Yu plotted that the emperor was still a boy dominated by powerful ministers and unfit to rule; Cao Biao, Prince of Chu, was grown and talented, and they wished to enthrone him to revive the House of Cao.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌使人告廣，廣曰：「凡舉大事，應本人情。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling sent someone to tell Guang, and Guang said: "In every great undertaking one must follow human sentiment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling sent someone to inform Wang Guang, and Guang replied, "Every great undertaking must follow what people will accept.

manualTranslations.zh: 今曹爽以驕奢失民，何平叔虛而不治，丁、畢、桓、鄧雖並有宿望，皆專競於世。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Cao Shuang through arrogance and extravagance lost the people; He Yan was hollow and did not govern; though Ding, Bi, Huan, and Deng all had longstanding repute, they all strove for dominance in the world.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang lost the people through arrogance and extravagance; He Yan was empty talk without real governance; and though Ding, Bi, Huan, and Deng all enjoyed old standing, they competed ruthlessly for power.

manualTranslations.zh: 加變易朝典，政令數改，所存雖高而事不下接，民習於舊，眾莫之從。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover they changed court statutes; policies and orders were frequently altered; what they upheld was lofty but affairs did not reach down in practice; the people were accustomed to the old ways, and the masses would not follow them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They also kept changing court institutions and issuing new orders; their ideals were high but never reached the people below, who clung to old ways and would not follow them.

manualTranslations.zh: 故雖勢傾四海，聲震天下，同日斬戮，名士減半，而百姓安之，莫或之哀，失民故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore though their power tilted the four seas and their fame shook the world, on the day they were beheaded and half the eminent scholars were cut down, yet the common people were at ease and none mourned them—because they had lost the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So although their power shook the realm and their fame resounded across the world, when they were executed on the same day and half the leading men were killed, the common people were untroubled and no one mourned them—they had lost the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 今懿情雖難量，事未有逆，而擢用賢能，廣樹勝己，修先朝之政令，副眾心之所求。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Yi's mind is hard to measure and affairs have not yet turned adverse, yet he promotes worthies and the capable, widely plants men who surpass himself, repairs the policies and orders of the former court, and matches what the masses' hearts seek.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi's intentions may be hard to read and nothing rebellious has yet appeared, but he is promoting able men, surrounding himself with talent, restoring earlier court policies, and giving the people what they want.

manualTranslations.zh: 爽之所以為惡者，彼莫不必改，夙夜匪解，以恤民為先。
manualTranslations.literal: Whatever evils Shuang committed, they all must change them; working day and night without slackening, they put comforting the people first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whatever wrongs Cao Shuang did, they are changing them; they labor day and night and put the people's welfare first.

manualTranslations.zh: 父子兄弟，並握兵要，未易亡也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Father and sons and brothers together hold the keys to military power; they are not easily destroyed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Father, sons, and brothers together hold military power; they will not be easy to overthrow."

manualTranslations.zh: 凌不從。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling did not heed him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling would not listen.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為如此言之類，皆前史所不載，而猶出習氏。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi judges that statements of this sort are nowhere recorded in earlier histories, yet they still come from the house of Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that passages of this kind appear in no earlier history, yet they still come from the Xi clan's compilation.

manualTranslations.zh: 且制言法體不似於昔，疑悉鑿齒所自造者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the structure and style of the language do not resemble the past; I suspect they were entirely fabricated by Xi Zuochi himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover the phrasing and style do not resemble older works; I suspect Xi Zuochi invented them himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 其十一月，愚復遣式詣彪，未還，會愚病死。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yu again sent Shi to Biao; before he returned, Yu happened to die of illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Linghu Yu again sent Zhang Shi to Cao Biao; before Shi returned, Yu died of illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏書》曰：愚字公治，本名浚，黃初中，為和戎護軍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wei says: Yu's courtesy name was Gongzhi; his original name was Jun. In Huangchu he served as Protector of the Army Who Harmonizes with the Rong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Linghu Yu, styled Gongzhi, was originally named Jun; in the Huangchu era he served as protector of the army who harmonizes with the Rong.

manualTranslations.zh: 烏丸校尉田豫討胡有功，小違節度，愚以法繩之。
manualTranslations.literal: Wuhuan colonel Tian Yu had merit in campaigning against the Hu but slightly violated regulations; Yu bound him by law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wuhuan colonel Tian Yu had merit fighting the Hu but slightly exceeded his orders; Linghu Yu punished him according to law.

manualTranslations.zh: 帝怒，械系愚，免官治罪，詔曰「浚何愚」！
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor was angry, had Yu shackled and imprisoned, removed him from office and punished him, and issued an edict saying, 'How foolish is Jun!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had Yu shackled and imprisoned, stripped him of office, and punished him, issuing an edict that said, 'How foolish Jun is!'

manualTranslations.zh: 遂以名之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he was given that as his name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was therefore given that as his name.

manualTranslations.zh: 正始中，為曹爽長史，後出為兗州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In Zhengshi he served as chief clerk to Cao Shuang; later he went out to be Inspector of Yan Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi he served as chief clerk to Cao Shuang, and later went out as inspector of Yan Province.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：愚聞楚王彪有智勇。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Yu heard that Prince Cao Biao of Chu had wisdom and courage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei says Linghu Yu heard that Cao Biao, Prince of Chu, was wise and brave.

manualTranslations.zh: 初東郡有訛言云：「白馬河出妖馬，夜過官牧邊鳴呼，眾馬皆應，明日見其跡，大如斛，行數里，還入河中。」
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier in Dong commandery there was a false rumor saying: "A demonic horse appeared on the White Horse River; at night it passed the government pasture and neighed, all the horses answering; the next day its tracks were seen, as large as a hu measure, going several li before returning into the river."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier in Dong commandery a rumor spread: "A demon horse appeared on the White Horse River; at night it passed the government pasture and neighed, and all the horses answered; the next day tracks as large as a hu measure were seen for several li before they returned into the river."

manualTranslations.zh: 又有謠言：「白馬素羈西南馳，其誰乘者朱虎騎。」
manualTranslations.literal: There was also a ballad: "A white horse with plain bridle gallops southwest—who rides it? Zhu Hu rides."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There was also a ballad: "A white horse with plain bridle gallops southwest—who rides it? Zhu Hu rides."

manualTranslations.zh: 楚王小字朱虎，故愚與王凌陰謀立楚王。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Chu's childhood name was Zhu Hu; therefore Yu and Wang Ling secretly plotted to enthrone the Prince of Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chu's childhood name was Zhu Hu, so Linghu Yu and Wang Ling secretly plotted to enthrone him.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃先使人通意於王，言「使君謝王，天下事不可知，原王自愛」！
manualTranslations.literal: They first sent someone to convey their intentions to the prince, saying, 'The envoy thanks Your Highness; affairs under heaven are unknowable—may Your Highness take care of yourself!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They first sent someone to sound out the prince, saying, 'The envoy thanks Your Highness; affairs under heaven are uncertain—may Your Highness take care of yourself!'

manualTranslations.zh: 彪亦陰知其意，答言「謝使君，知厚意也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Biao also secretly knew their intention and replied, 'Thank the envoy; I know the generous intent.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Biao also understood their meaning in secret and answered, 'Thank the envoy; I understand the generous intent.'

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，熒惑守南斗，凌謂：「斗中有星，當有暴貴者。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, Mars stayed in the Southern Dipper; Ling said: "There is a star within the Dipper—there must be someone who rises swiftly to eminence."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year Mars lingered in the Southern Dipper; Wang Ling said, "There is a star in the Dipper—someone will rise suddenly to great honor."

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》曰：凌聞東平民浩詳知星，呼問詳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei says: Ling heard that Hao Xiang of Dongping understood the stars; he summoned and questioned Xiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei says Wang Ling heard that Hao Xiang of Dongping understood astronomy and summoned him for questioning.

manualTranslations.zh: 詳疑凌有所挾，欲悅其意，不言吳當有死喪，而言淮南楚分也，今吳、楚同佔，當有王者興。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiang suspected Ling had some hidden purpose and wished to please him; he did not speak of Wu having a death and mourning but said Huainan was the Chu asterism's division, and now Wu and Chu shared the same station—there would be a king who rises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hao Xiang suspected Wang Ling had an ulterior motive and wanted to please him; he said nothing about mourning deaths in Wu, but said Huainan lay in the Chu asterism and that Wu and Chu now shared the same station—a king would rise.

manualTranslations.zh: 故凌計遂定。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Ling's plan was settled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling's plan was thus settled.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年春，吳賊塞塗水。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the third year, Wu bandits blocked the Tushui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Wu forces blocked the Tushui.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌欲因此發，大嚴諸軍，表求討賊；
manualTranslations.literal: Ling wished to use this to launch action, greatly mustering the armies, and submitted a memorial requesting to attack the bandits;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling wished to use this as his opening, mustered his forces on a grand scale, and memorialized requesting permission to attack the enemy;

manualTranslations.zh: 詔報不聽。
manualTranslations.literal: An edict responded and did not grant permission.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court replied and refused permission.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌陰謀滋甚，遣將軍楊弘以廢立事告兗州刺史黃華，華、弘連名以白太傅司馬宣王。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling's secret plot grew ever deeper; he sent general Yang Hong to tell Inspector of Yan Province Huang Hua of the deposition and enthronement affair; Hua and Hong jointly signed a memorial reporting it to Grand Tutor Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling's secret plot deepened further; he sent General Yang Hong to reveal the deposition plot to Huang Hua, inspector of Yan Province, and Hua and Hong jointly reported it to Grand Tutor Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王將中軍乘水道討凌，先下赦赦凌罪，又將尚書廣東，使為書喻凌，大軍掩至百尺逼凌。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Xuan led the central army along the water route to attack Ling; he first issued a pardon absolving Ling's crimes, also bringing Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Guang east and having him write to instruct Ling; the great army suddenly arrived at Baichi and pressed upon Ling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan, led the central army by water against Wang Ling; he first issued a pardon absolving Ling's crimes, also brought Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Guang east to write instructing him, and the main force suddenly reached Baichi and pressed Ling.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌自知勢窮，乃乘船單出迎宣王，遣掾王彧謝罪，送印綬、節鉞。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling knew himself powerless, so he took a boat alone to go out and meet the Prince of Xuan; he sent clerk Wang Yu to express apology and sent his seal and ribbon and ceremonial staff and battle-axe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing himself beaten, Wang Ling took a boat out alone to meet Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan; he sent clerk Wang Yu to apologize and surrendered his seal, ribbon, jie staff, and battle-axe.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍到丘頭，凌面縛水次。
manualTranslations.literal: The army reached Qiutou; Ling bound himself with face exposed at the water's edge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the army reached Qiutou, Wang Ling bound himself and waited at the water's edge.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣王承詔遣主簿解縛反服，見凌，慰勞之，還印綬、節鉞，遣步騎六百人送還京都。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Xuan, acting on imperial command, sent the chief clerk to unbind him and restore his proper dress, saw Ling and comforted him, returned seal and ribbon and ceremonial staff and battle-axe, and sent six hundred foot and cavalry to escort him back to the capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial command, Sima Yi, Prince of Xuan, sent his chief clerk to unbind him and restore his dress, received Wang Ling and comforted him, returned his seal, ribbon, jie staff, and battle-axe, and sent six hundred infantry and cavalry to escort him back to the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌至項，飲藥死。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling reached Xiang and drank poison to die.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling reached Xiang and took poison to die.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》載凌與太傅書曰：「卒聞神軍密發，巳在百尺，雖知命窮盡，遲於相見，身首分離，不以為恨，前後遣使，有書未得還報，企踵西望，無物以譬。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei records a letter from Ling to the Grand Tutor, saying: "Suddenly I heard the divine army had secretly set out and was already at Baichi. Though I knew fate was exhausted and meeting was delayed, with body and head separated, I did not consider it a regret. Envoys I sent before and after had letters that received no reply; I stood on tiptoe looking west, with nothing to compare it to.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei records Wang Ling's letter to the Grand Tutor: "Suddenly I heard your divine army had secretly set out and was already at Baichi. Though I knew my fate was spent and our meeting delayed, with body and head separated, I took no offense. Envoys I sent before and after carried letters that received no reply; I stood on tiptoe looking west, with nothing to compare it to.

manualTranslations.zh: 昨遣書之後，便乘船來相迎宿丘頭，旦發於浦口，奉被露布赦書，又得二十三日況，累紙誨示，聞命驚愕，五內失守，不知何地可以自處？
manualTranslations.literal: After I sent my letter yesterday, I took a boat to come meet you and lodged at Qiutou; at dawn I set out from Pukou, received the posted pardon edict, and also received the situation of the twenty-third day, successive papers instructing me; hearing the command I was stunned, my five viscera lost their mooring—I did not know where I could place myself?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After I sent my letter yesterday, I took a boat to meet you and lodged at Qiutou; at dawn I set out from Pukou, received the posted pardon edict, and also received your update of the twenty-third day, successive papers instructing me; hearing your command I was stunned, my inner self lost all bearing—I did not know where I could stand?

manualTranslations.zh: 僕久忝朝恩，歷試無效，統御戎馬，董齊東夏，事有闕廢，中心犯義，罪在三百，妻子同縣，無所禱矣。
manualTranslations.literal: I have long received court favor undeservedly, tested in office without result; I commanded troops and governed the eastern realm, affairs had gaps and failures, my heart transgressed righteousness, crimes numbering in the three hundred; wife and children share my fate, there is nothing to pray for.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have long enjoyed court favor undeservedly and failed in repeated trials of office; I commanded troops and governed the eastern realm, affairs were neglected, my heart transgressed righteousness, and my crimes number in the three hundred statutes; wife and children share my fate, and there is nothing left to pray for.

manualTranslations.zh: 不圖聖恩天覆地載，橫蒙視息，复睹日月。
manualTranslations.literal: I did not expect holy favor covering heaven and earth; I unexpectedly received the breath of life and again beheld sun and moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I never imagined such imperial favor, vast as heaven and earth; I unexpectedly received the gift of life and again beheld sun and moon.

manualTranslations.zh: 亡甥令狐愚攜惑群小之言，僕即時呵抑，使不得竟其語。
manualTranslations.literal: My deceased nephew Linghu Yu carried the words of petty men and deluded me; I immediately rebuked and restrained him, not letting him finish his speech.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My late nephew Linghu Yu was swayed by the talk of petty men; I immediately rebuked and restrained him and would not let him finish.

manualTranslations.zh: 既人已知，神明所鑑，夫非事無陰，卒至發露，知此梟夷之罪也。
manualTranslations.literal: Since men already knew, the spirits bear witness—no affair lacks concealment; when it suddenly came to exposure, I knew this crime of execution and extermination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since men already knew and the spirits witnessed it, no affair lacks concealment; when it was suddenly exposed, I knew this was the crime deserving execution and extermination of kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 生我者父母，活我者子也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Those who bore me were my parents; he who gives me life is you."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who gave me birth were my parents; he who gives me life is you."

manualTranslations.zh: 又重曰：「身陷刑罪，謬蒙赦宥。
manualTranslations.literal: He also reiterated: "Caught in criminal punishment, I wrongly received pardon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also added: "Caught in criminal punishment, I wrongly received pardon.

manualTranslations.zh: 今遣掾送印綬，頃至，當如詔書自縛歸命。
manualTranslations.literal: Now I send a clerk delivering seal and ribbon; when he shortly arrives, I shall as the edict commands bind myself and surrender.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now I send a clerk with my seal and ribbon; when he shortly arrives, I shall as the edict commands bind myself and surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖足下私之，官法有分。」
manualTranslations.literal: Though you may favor me privately, the law of office has its divisions."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though you may favor me privately, the law has its proper divisions."

manualTranslations.zh: 及到，如書。
manualTranslations.literal: When he arrived, it was as in the letter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he did as the letter said.

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅使人解其縛。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Tutor sent someone to loose his bonds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor sent someone to unbind him.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌既蒙赦，加怙舊好，不復自疑，徑乘小船自趣太傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling, having received pardon, trusting additionally in old friendship, no longer doubted himself; he directly took a small boat to hurry to the Grand Tutor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having received pardon, Wang Ling trusted additionally in their old friendship, no longer doubted himself, and took a small boat straight toward the Grand Tutor.

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅使人逆止之，住船淮中，相去十餘丈。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Tutor sent someone to meet and stop him; he kept the boat in the middle of the Huai, more than ten zhang apart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor sent someone to meet and stop him; his boat remained in midstream on the Huai, more than ten zhang apart.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌知見外，乃遙謂太傅曰：「卿直以折簡召我，我當敢不至邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Ling knew he was treated as an outsider; he therefore called out from afar to the Grand Tutor: "You could have simply summoned me with a folded letter—how would I have dared not come?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing he was treated as an outsider, Wang Ling called out from afar to the Grand Tutor: "You could simply have summoned me with a folded letter—how would I have dared not come?

manualTranslations.zh: 而乃引軍來乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Yet you brought an army!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet you brought an army!"

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅曰：「以卿非肯逐折簡者故也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Tutor said: "Because you were not one who would heed a folded letter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor said, "Because you were not one who would heed a folded letter."

manualTranslations.zh: 凌曰：「卿負我！」
manualTranslations.literal: Ling said: "You have wronged me!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ling said, "You have wronged me!"

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅曰：「我寧負卿，不負國家。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Tutor said: "I would rather wrong you than wrong the state."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor said, "I would rather wrong you than wrong the state."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂使人送來西。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he sent men to escort him west.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent men to escort him west.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌自知罪重，試索棺釘，以觀太傅意，太傅給之。
manualTranslations.literal: Ling knew himself guilty and heavy; he tried asking for coffin nails to observe the Grand Tutor's intention; the Grand Tutor supplied them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing his guilt was grave, Wang Ling tried asking for coffin nails to test the Grand Tutor's intention; the Grand Tutor gave them to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 凌行到項，夜呼掾屬與決曰：「行年八十，身名並滅邪！」
manualTranslations.literal: Ling traveled to Xiang; at night he summoned clerks and subordinates to take leave, saying: "Eighty years of life—body and name both destroyed!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wang Ling reached Xiang, he summoned his clerks at night to take leave, saying, "Eighty years of age—body and name both destroyed!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon he killed himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：凌到項，見賈逵祠在水側，凌呼曰：「賈梁道，王凌固忠於魏之社稷者，唯爾有神，知之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin says: When Ling reached Xiang he saw Jia Kui's shrine beside the water; Ling called out: "Jia Liangdao, Wang Ling was truly loyal to Wei's altars of soil and grain—only you spirits know it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin says that when Wang Ling reached Xiang he saw Jia Kui's shrine beside the water and called out, "Jia Liangdao, Wang Ling was truly loyal to the altars of Wei—only you spirits know it."

manualTranslations.zh: 其年八月，太傅有疾，夢凌、逵為癘，甚惡之，遂薨。
manualTranslations.literal: That same year in the eighth month the Grand Tutor fell ill; he dreamed Ling and Kui became plague demons—he found it very hateful—and then died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That same year in the eighth month the Grand Tutor fell ill; he dreamed Wang Ling and Jia Kui had become plague demons, found it deeply hateful, and then died.

sourceRange.text: 毌丘儉作亂，大將軍司馬景王東征，會從，典知密事，衛將軍司馬文王為大軍後繼。景王薨於許昌，文王總統六軍，會謀謨帷幄。時中詔敕尚書傅嘏，以東南新定，權留衛將軍屯許昌為內外之援，令嘏率諸軍還。會與嘏謀，使嘏表上，輒與衛將軍俱發，還到雒水南屯住。於是朝廷拜文王為大將軍、輔政，會遷黃門侍郎，封東武亭侯，邑三百戶。甘露二年257年，徵諸葛誕為司空，時會喪寧在家，策誕必不從命，馳白文王。文王以事已施行，不復追改。會時遭所生母喪。其母傳曰：「夫人性矜嚴，明於教訓，會雖童稚，勤見規誨。年四歲授《孝經》，七歲誦《論語》，八歲誦《詩》，十歲誦《尚書》，十一誦《易》，十二誦《春秋左氏傳》、《國語》，十三誦《周禮》、《禮記》，十四誦《成侯易記》，十五使入太學問四方奇文異訓。謂會曰：『學猥則倦，倦則意怠；吾懼汝之意怠，故以漸訓汝，今可以獨學矣。』雅好書籍，涉曆書，特好易、老子，每讀易孔子說鳴鶴在陰、勞謙君子、籍用白茅、不出戶庭之義，每使會反覆讀之，曰：『易三百餘爻，仲尼特說此者，以謙恭慎密，樞機之發，行己至要，榮身所由故也，順斯術已往，足為君子矣。』正始八年，會為尚書郎，夫人執會手而誨之曰：『汝弱冠見敘，人情不能不自足，則損在其中矣，勉思其戒！』是時大將軍曹爽專朝政，日縱酒沉醉，會兄侍中毓宴還，言其事。夫人曰：『樂則樂矣，然難久也。居不驕，制節謹度，然後乃無危溢之患。今奢僭若此，非長守富貴之道。』嘉平元年249年，車駕朝高平陵，會為中書郎，從行。相國宣文侯始舉兵，眾人恐懼，而夫人自若。中書令劉放、侍郎衛瓘、夏侯和等家皆怪問：『夫人一子在危難之中，何能無憂？』答曰：『大將軍奢僭無度，吾常疑其不安。太傅義不危國，必為大將軍舉耳。吾兒在帝側何憂？聞且出兵無他重器，其勢必不久戰。』果如其言，一時稱明。會歷機密十餘年，頗豫政謀。夫人謂曰：『昔范氏少子為趙簡子設伐邾之計，事從民悅，可謂功矣。然其母以為乘偽作詐，末業鄙事，必不能久。其識本深遠，非近人所言，吾常樂其為人。汝居心正，吾知免矣。但當脩所志以輔益時化，不忝先人耳。常言人誰能皆體自然，但力行不倦，抑亦其次。雖接鄙賤，必以言信。取與之間，分畫分明。』或：『此無乃小乎？』答曰：『君子之行，皆積小以致高大，若以小善為無益而弗為，此乃小人之事耳。希通慕大者，吾所不好。』會自幼少，衣不過青紺，親營家事，自知恭儉。然見得思義，臨財必讓。會前後賜錢帛數百萬計，悉送供公家之用，一無所取。年五十有九，甘露二年257年二月暴疾薨。比葬，天子有手詔，命大將軍高都侯厚加賵贈，喪事無鉅細，一皆供給。議者以為公侯有夫人，有世婦，有妻，有妾，所謂外命婦也。依春秋成風、定姒之義，宜崇典禮，不得總稱妾名，於是稱成侯命婦。殯葬之事，有取於古制，禮也。」及誕反，車駕住項，文王至壽春，會復從行。

manualTranslations.zh: 毌丘儉作亂，大將軍司馬景王東征，會從，典知密事，衛將軍司馬文王為大軍後繼。
manualTranslations.literal: When Guanqiu Jian rebelled, Grand General Sima Shi, Lord of Jing, campaigned east; Hui followed and managed confidential affairs; Guardian General Sima Zhao, Prince of Wen, served as rear support for the main army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian rebelled, Grand General Sima Shi, Lord of Jing, campaigned east; Zhong Hui followed and managed confidential affairs; Guardian General Sima Zhao, Prince of Wen, served as rear support for the main army.

manualTranslations.zh: 景王薨於許昌，文王總統六軍，會謀謨帷幄。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Jing died at Xuchang; the Prince of Wen took overall command of the six armies; Hui planned strategy within the command tent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Shi died at Xuchang; Sima Zhao took overall command of the six armies; Zhong Hui planned strategy within the command tent.

manualTranslations.zh: 時中詔敕尚書傅嘏，以東南新定，權留衛將軍屯許昌為內外之援，令嘏率諸軍還。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time an interim edict instructed Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu that, because the southeast had just been pacified, the Guardian General was provisionally to remain at Xuchang as inner and outer support, and ordered Gu to lead the armies back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time an interim edict instructed Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu that, because the southeast had just been pacified, Sima Zhao was provisionally to remain at Xuchang as inner and outer support, and ordered Fu Gu to lead the armies back.

manualTranslations.zh: 會與嘏謀，使嘏表上，輒與衛將軍俱發，還到雒水南屯住。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui plotted with Gu, had Gu submit a memorial, and then set out together with the Guardian General; returning, they encamped south of the Luo River.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui plotted with Fu Gu, had Fu Gu submit a memorial, and then set out together with Sima Zhao; returning, they encamped south of the Luo River.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是朝廷拜文王為大將軍、輔政，會遷黃門侍郎，封東武亭侯，邑三百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon the court appointed the Prince of Wen Grand General and regent; Hui was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongwu Village with a fief of three hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court appointed Sima Zhao grand general and regent; Zhong Hui was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongwu Village with a fief of three hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 甘露二年257年，徵諸葛誕為司空，時會喪寧在家，策誕必不從命，馳白文王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Ganlu (257), Zhuge Dan was summoned as Excellency of Works; Hui was then at home during mourning observance, judged that Dan would surely refuse the order, and galloped to inform the Prince of Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year of Ganlu (257), Zhuge Dan was summoned as excellency of works; Zhong Hui was then at home during mourning observance, judged that Zhuge Dan would surely refuse the order, and galloped to inform Sima Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 文王以事已施行，不復追改。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Wen said the matter had already been carried out and would not be changed retroactively.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao said the matter had already been carried out and would not be changed retroactively.

manualTranslations.zh: 會時遭所生母喪。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui was then in mourning for his birth mother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was then in mourning for his birth mother.

manualTranslations.zh: 其母傳曰：「夫人性矜嚴，明於教訓，會雖童稚，勤見規誨。
manualTranslations.literal: His mother's biography says: "The lady by nature was stern and dignified and skilled in instruction; though Hui was still a child, she often admonished and taught him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His mother's biography says: "The lady by nature was stern and dignified and skilled in instruction; though Zhong Hui was still a child, she often admonished and taught him.

manualTranslations.zh: 年四歲授《孝經》，七歲誦《論語》，八歲誦《詩》，十歲誦《尚書》，十一誦《易》，十二誦《春秋左氏傳》、《國語》，十三誦《周禮》、《禮記》，十四誦《成侯易記》，十五使入太學問四方奇文異訓。
manualTranslations.literal: At age four she taught him the Classic of Filial Piety; at seven he recited the Analects; at eight the Odes; at ten the Documents; at eleven the Changes; at twelve the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Discourses of the States; at thirteen the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Rites; at fourteen the Accomplished Marquis's Commentary on the Changes; at fifteen he was sent into the Imperial Academy to study remarkable texts and variant readings from all quarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At age four she taught him the Classic of Filial Piety; at seven he recited the Analects; at eight the Odes; at ten the Documents; at eleven the Changes; at twelve the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Discourses of the States; at thirteen the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Rites; at fourteen the Accomplished Marquis's Commentary on the Changes; at fifteen he was sent into the Imperial Academy to study remarkable texts and variant readings from all quarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 謂會曰：『學猥則倦，倦則意怠；
manualTranslations.literal: She said to Hui: 'Learning piled up leads to weariness; weariness leads to slackness of mind;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She said to Zhong Hui: 'Learning piled up leads to weariness; weariness leads to slackness of mind;

manualTranslations.zh: 吾懼汝之意怠，故以漸訓汝，今可以獨學矣。』
manualTranslations.literal: I feared your mind would slacken, therefore I taught you gradually; now you may study on your own.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I feared your mind would slacken, therefore I taught you gradually; now you may study on your own.'

manualTranslations.zh: 雅好書籍，涉曆書，特好易、老子，每讀易孔子說鳴鶴在陰、勞謙君子、籍用白茅、不出戶庭之義，每使會反覆讀之，曰：『易三百餘爻，仲尼特說此者，以謙恭慎密，樞機之發，行己至要，榮身所由故也，順斯術已往，足為君子矣。』
manualTranslations.literal: She loved books by nature and read widely, especially the Changes and Laozi; whenever she read Confucius's explanations of the crane crying in the shade, the noble person who toils yet is humble, white rushes for spreading, and not going beyond the courtyard gate, she had Hui read them over and again, saying: 'The Changes has more than three hundred lines, yet Confucius especially explained these because humility, reverence, and caution are the pivot of conduct, the utmost essentials in deportment, and the means by which one honors oneself; follow this way henceforth, and you will suffice as a noble person.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She loved books by nature and read widely, especially the Changes and Laozi; whenever she read Confucius's explanations of the crane crying in the shade, the noble person who toils yet is humble, white rushes for spreading, and not going beyond the courtyard gate, she had Zhong Hui read them over and again, saying: 'The Changes has more than three hundred lines, yet Confucius especially explained these because humility, reverence, and caution are the pivot of conduct, the utmost essentials in deportment, and the means by which one honors oneself; follow this way henceforth, and you will suffice as a noble person.'

manualTranslations.zh: 正始八年，會為尚書郎，夫人執會手而誨之曰：『汝弱冠見敘，人情不能不自足，則損在其中矣，勉思其戒！』
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengshi, Hui became a gentleman of the Masters of Writing; the lady took Hui's hand and admonished him: 'You have been advanced at your weak-crown years; human feelings cannot but feel self-satisfied—and harm lies within that; strive to ponder this warning!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhengshi, Zhong Hui became a gentleman of the Masters of Writing; the lady took his hand and admonished him: 'You have been advanced at your weak-crown years; human feelings cannot but feel self-satisfied—and harm lies within that; strive to ponder this warning!'

manualTranslations.zh: 是時大將軍曹爽專朝政，日縱酒沉醉，會兄侍中毓宴還，言其事。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized court government and daily abandoned himself to drunkenness; Hui's elder brother Yu, Attendant Within, returned from a banquet and spoke of the matter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized court government and daily abandoned himself to drunkenness; Zhong Hui's elder brother Yu, attendant within, returned from a banquet and spoke of the matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人曰：『樂則樂矣，然難久也。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady said: 'Joy is joy, yet it cannot last long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lady said: 'Joy is joy, yet it cannot last long.

manualTranslations.zh: 居不驕，制節謹度，然後乃無危溢之患。
manualTranslations.literal: Dwelling without arrogance, restraining oneself and observing limits—only then is there no peril of excess and overflow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dwelling without arrogance, restraining oneself and observing limits—only then is there no peril of excess and overflow.

manualTranslations.zh: 今奢僭若此，非長守富貴之道。』
manualTranslations.literal: Now extravagance and presumption such as this are not the way to long keep wealth and rank.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now extravagance and presumption such as this are not the way to long keep wealth and rank.'

manualTranslations.zh: 嘉平元年249年，車駕朝高平陵，會為中書郎，從行。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jiaping (249), the imperial carriage attended at Gaoping Tomb; Hui was a gentleman of the Secretariat and accompanied the journey.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaping (249), the imperial carriage attended at Gaoping Tomb; Zhong Hui was a gentleman of the Secretariat and accompanied the journey.

manualTranslations.zh: 相國宣文侯始舉兵，眾人恐懼，而夫人自若。
manualTranslations.literal: Chancellor Sima Yi, Lord of Xuanwen, first raised troops; everyone was afraid, but the lady was composed as ever.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chancellor Sima Yi, Lord of Xuanwen, first raised troops; everyone was afraid, but the lady was composed as ever.

manualTranslations.zh: 中書令劉放、侍郎衛瓘、夏侯和等家皆怪問：『夫人一子在危難之中，何能無憂？』
manualTranslations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Liu Fang, Attendant Wei Guan, Xiahou He, and their households all wondered and asked: 'The lady has a son in peril—how can she be without worry?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Liu Fang, Attendant Wei Guan, Xiahou He, and their households all wondered and asked: 'The lady has a son in peril—how can she be without worry?'

manualTranslations.zh: 答曰：『大將軍奢僭無度，吾常疑其不安。
manualTranslations.literal: She answered: 'The Grand General is extravagant and presumptuous beyond measure; I have long suspected he would not remain secure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She answered: 'Grand General Cao Shuang is extravagant and presumptuous beyond measure; I have long suspected he would not remain secure.

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅義不危國，必為大將軍舉耳。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Tutor, on grounds of righteousness, would not endanger the state; he is sure to act against the Grand General.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, on grounds of righteousness, would not endanger the state; he is sure to act against the Grand General.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾兒在帝側何憂？
manualTranslations.literal: My son is at the emperor's side—what worry is there?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My son is at the emperor's side—what worry is there?

manualTranslations.zh: 聞且出兵無他重器，其勢必不久戰。』
manualTranslations.literal: I hear the troops about to go out have no other heavy weapons; their force cannot fight for long.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I hear the troops about to go out have no other heavy weapons; their force cannot fight for long.'

manualTranslations.zh: 果如其言，一時稱明。
manualTranslations.literal: It turned out as she said, and for a time she was praised as perceptive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It turned out as she said, and for a time she was praised as perceptive.

manualTranslations.zh: 會歷機密十餘年，頗豫政謀。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui served in confidential affairs for more than ten years and took part considerably in policy deliberations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui served in confidential affairs for more than ten years and took part considerably in policy deliberations.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人謂曰：『昔范氏少子為趙簡子設伐邾之計，事從民悅，可謂功矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The lady said to him: 'Formerly the younger son of the Fan clan devised for Zhao Jianzi a plan to campaign against Zhu; the affair succeeded and the people were pleased—it could be called achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The lady said to him: 'Formerly the younger son of the Fan clan devised for Zhao Jianzi a plan to campaign against Zhu; the affair succeeded and the people were pleased—it could be called achievement.

manualTranslations.zh: 然其母以為乘偽作詐，末業鄙事，必不能久。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet his mother regarded it as relying on fraud and artifice, a base and vulgar pursuit, and that it could not last.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet his mother regarded it as relying on fraud and artifice, a base and vulgar pursuit, and that it could not last.

manualTranslations.zh: 其識本深遠，非近人所言，吾常樂其為人。
manualTranslations.literal: Her insight was in origin deep and far-reaching—not what ordinary people say; I have always delighted in her character.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her insight was in origin deep and far-reaching—not what ordinary people say; I have always delighted in her character.

manualTranslations.zh: 汝居心正，吾知免矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your heart is upright; I know you will escape harm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your heart is upright; I know you will escape harm.

manualTranslations.zh: 但當脩所志以輔益時化，不忝先人耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Only cultivate your aims to assist and improve the age's transformation, and not disgrace your forebears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only cultivate your aims to assist and improve the age's transformation, and not disgrace your forebears.

manualTranslations.zh: 常言人誰能皆體自然，但力行不倦，抑亦其次。
manualTranslations.literal: She often said that who among men can fully embody the natural way; merely to act vigorously without tiring is also next best.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She often said that who among men can fully embody the natural way; merely to act vigorously without tiring is also next best.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖接鄙賤，必以言信。
manualTranslations.literal: Though dealing with the lowly and base, she was sure to keep her word.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though dealing with the lowly and base, she was sure to keep her word.

manualTranslations.zh: 取與之間，分畫分明。』
manualTranslations.literal: In taking and giving, her divisions were clear and distinct.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In taking and giving, her divisions were clear and distinct.'

manualTranslations.zh: 或：『此無乃小乎？』
manualTranslations.literal: Someone said: 'Is this not perhaps too petty?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Someone said: 'Is this not perhaps too petty?'

manualTranslations.zh: 答曰：『君子之行，皆積小以致高大，若以小善為無益而弗為，此乃小人之事耳。
manualTranslations.literal: She answered: 'The conduct of the noble person accumulates small things to achieve greatness; if one regards small goodness as without benefit and does not do it, that is the affair of petty men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She answered: 'The conduct of the noble person accumulates small things to achieve greatness; if one regards small goodness as without benefit and does not do it, that is the affair of petty men.

manualTranslations.zh: 希通慕大者，吾所不好。』
manualTranslations.literal: To hope for far-reaching mastery and admire what is grand—that is what I do not like.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To hope for far-reaching mastery and admire what is grand—that is what I do not like.'

manualTranslations.zh: 會自幼少，衣不過青紺，親營家事，自知恭儉。
manualTranslations.literal: From childhood Hui wore only blue and dark blue; he personally managed household affairs and knew himself to be respectful and frugal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From childhood Zhong Hui wore only blue and dark blue; he personally managed household affairs and knew himself to be respectful and frugal.

manualTranslations.zh: 然見得思義，臨財必讓。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet when he saw gain he considered righteousness; facing wealth he always yielded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet when he saw gain he considered righteousness; facing wealth he always yielded.

manualTranslations.zh: 會前後賜錢帛數百萬計，悉送供公家之用，一無所取。
manualTranslations.literal: The money and silk Hui was granted before and after amounted to millions; he sent it all to supply public use and took not a single item.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The money and silk Zhong Hui was granted before and after amounted to millions; he sent it all to supply public use and took not a single item.

manualTranslations.zh: 年五十有九，甘露二年257年二月暴疾薨。
manualTranslations.literal: At age fifty-nine, in the second month of the second year of Ganlu (257), she suddenly fell ill and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At age fifty-nine, in the second month of the second year of Ganlu (257), she suddenly fell ill and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 比葬，天子有手詔，命大將軍高都侯厚加賵贈，喪事無鉅細，一皆供給。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time of burial, the Son of Heaven had a personal edict ordering Grand General the Marquis of Gaodu to add generously to funeral gifts; matters of the mourning, great and small, were all supplied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the time of burial, the Son of Heaven had a personal edict ordering Grand General the Marquis of Gaodu to add generously to funeral gifts; matters of the mourning, great and small, were all supplied.

manualTranslations.zh: 議者以為公侯有夫人，有世婦，有妻，有妾，所謂外命婦也。
manualTranslations.literal: Deliberators held that lords and marquises have a lady, a mistress of the house, a wife, and concubines—the so-called outer titled ladies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deliberators held that lords and marquises have a lady, a mistress of the house, a wife, and concubines—the so-called outer titled ladies.

manualTranslations.zh: 依春秋成風、定姒之義，宜崇典禮，不得總稱妾名，於是稱成侯命婦。
manualTranslations.literal: According to the principles of Cheng Feng and Ding Si in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ritual norms ought to be honored and one could not simply call her by the name of concubine; therefore she was titled the Accomplished Marquis's lady by ritual investiture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: According to the principles of Cheng Feng and Ding Si in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ritual norms ought to be honored and one could not simply call her by the name of concubine; therefore she was titled the Accomplished Marquis's lady by ritual investiture.

manualTranslations.zh: 殯葬之事，有取於古制，禮也。」
manualTranslations.literal: That the funeral and burial took from ancient institutions was ritual propriety."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That the funeral and burial took from ancient institutions was ritual propriety."

manualTranslations.zh: 及誕反，車駕住項，文王至壽春，會復從行。
manualTranslations.literal: When Dan rebelled, the imperial carriage halted at Xiang; the Prince of Wen reached Shouchun, and Hui again accompanied the campaign.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan rebelled, the imperial carriage halted at Xiang; Sima Zhao reached Shouchun, and Zhong Hui again accompanied the campaign.

context.afterSource: 維退，淮因西擊羌。

sourceRange.text: 毌丘儉字仲恭，河東聞喜人也。父興，黃初中為武威太守，伐叛柔服，開通河右，名次金城太守蘇則。討賊張進及討叛胡有功，封高陽鄉侯。魏名臣奏載雍州刺史張既表曰：「河右遐遠，喪亂彌久，武威當諸郡路道喉轄之要，加民夷雜處，數有兵難。領太守毌丘興到官，內撫吏民，外懷羌、胡，卒使柔附，為官效用。黃華、張進初圖逆亂，扇動左右，興志氣忠烈，臨難不顧，為將校民夷陳說禍福，言則涕泣。於時男女萬口，咸懷感激，形毀髮亂，誓心致命。尋率精兵踧脅張掖，濟拔領太守杜通、西海太守張睦。張掖番和、驪靬二縣吏民及郡雜胡棄惡詣興，興皆安卹，使盡力田。興每所歷，盡竭心力，誠國之良吏。殿下即位，留心萬機，苟有毫毛之善，必有賞錄，臣伏緣聖旨，指陳其事。」入為將作大匠。儉襲父爵，為平原侯文學。明帝即位，為尚書郎，遷羽林監。以東宮之舊，甚見親待。出為洛陽典農。時取農民以治宮室，儉上疏曰：「臣愚以為天下所急除者二賊，所急務者衣食。誠使二賊不滅，士民飢凍，雖崇美宮室，猶無益也。」遷荊州刺史。

manualTranslations.zh: 毌丘儉字仲恭，河東聞喜人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Guanqiu Jian, courtesy name Zhonggong, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian, styled Zhonggong, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 父興，黃初中為武威太守，伐叛柔服，開通河右，名次金城太守蘇則。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Xing, in the early Huangchu era served as Administrator of Wuwei, campaigned against rebels and won their submission, opened communications in the lands west of the Yellow River, and ranked next after Su Ze, Administrator of Jincheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Guanqiu Xing, in early Huangchu served as administrator of Wuwei, subdued rebels, opened the lands west of the Yellow River, and ranked just below Su Ze of Jincheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 討賊張進及討叛胡有功，封高陽鄉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: For merit in campaigning against the bandit Zhang Jin and suppressing rebellious Hu, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang Precinct.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For merit against the bandit Zhang Jin and rebellious Hu tribes, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Gaoyang precinct.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏名臣奏載雍州刺史張既表曰：「河右遐遠，喪亂彌久，武威當諸郡路道喉轄之要，加民夷雜處，數有兵難。
manualTranslations.literal: Memorials of Wei Worthies records a memorial of Zhang Ji, Inspector of Yong Province, saying: "The lands west of the Yellow River are remote, and disorder has long continued; Wuwei lies at the throat of the routes among the commanderies, and moreover Han and tribal peoples are mixed together, with frequent military troubles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Memorials of Wei Worthies records Inspector Zhang Ji of Yong Province memorializing: "The lands west of the Yellow River are remote and long troubled; Wuwei sits at the throat of the routes among the commanderies, with Han and tribal peoples mixed together and frequent military unrest.

manualTranslations.zh: 領太守毌丘興到官，內撫吏民，外懷羌、胡，卒使柔附，為官效用。
manualTranslations.literal: When Acting Administrator Guanqiu Xing took office, he inwardly soothed officials and people and outwardly won over the Qiang and Hu, finally making them gentle and attached so they served the government effectively.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Acting Administrator Guanqiu Xing took office, he soothed officials and people within and won over the Qiang and Hu without, finally making them gentle and attached so they served the government.

manualTranslations.zh: 黃華、張進初圖逆亂，扇動左右，興志氣忠烈，臨難不顧，為將校民夷陳說禍福，言則涕泣。
manualTranslations.literal: When Huang Hua and Zhang Jin first plotted rebellion and stirred those around them, Xing's spirit was loyal and fierce; facing peril he did not flinch, and for generals, officers, and tribal people alike he explained fortune and disaster until he wept as he spoke.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Huang Hua and Zhang Jin first plotted rebellion, Xing's spirit was loyal and fierce; facing peril he did not flinch, and for officers and tribesmen alike he explained fortune and disaster until he wept as he spoke.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時男女萬口，咸懷感激，形毀髮亂，誓心致命。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time men and women by the myriad were all stirred to gratitude; with bodies marred and hair disheveled they vowed their lives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time tens of thousands of men and women were stirred to gratitude; with bodies marred and hair disheveled they vowed their lives.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋率精兵踧脅張掖，濟拔領太守杜通、西海太守張睦。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he led crack troops to press Zhangye and rescued Acting Administrator Du Tong and Administrator of Xihai Zhang Mu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he led crack troops against Zhangye and rescued Acting Administrator Du Tong and Administrator Zhang Mu of Xihai.

manualTranslations.zh: 張掖番和、驪靬二縣吏民及郡雜胡棄惡詣興，興皆安卹，使盡力田。
manualTranslations.literal: The officials and people of Fanhe and Liqian counties in Zhangye and the mixed Hu of the commandery abandoned evil and came to Xing; he comforted them all and had them devote themselves to farming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Fanhe and Liqian in Zhangye and the mixed Hu of the commandery abandoned evil and came to Xing; he comforted them all and had them farm.

manualTranslations.zh: 興每所歷，盡竭心力，誠國之良吏。
manualTranslations.literal: Wherever Xing served, he exhausted heart and strength—truly a fine officer of the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wherever Xing served, he exhausted heart and strength—truly a fine officer of the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 殿下即位，留心萬機，苟有毫毛之善，必有賞錄，臣伏緣聖旨，指陳其事。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Your Highness took the throne you attended to the myriad affairs of state; if there was even the slightest good it was sure to be rewarded and recorded; your servant bows to the sacred intent and points out this matter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Your Highness took the throne you attended to the myriad affairs of state; if there was even the slightest good it was sure to be rewarded and recorded; your servant bows to the sacred intent and points out this matter."

manualTranslations.zh: 入為將作大匠。
manualTranslations.literal: He entered court as Master of Works.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He entered court as master of works.

manualTranslations.zh: 儉襲父爵，為平原侯文學。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian inherited his father's rank and served as literary aide to the Marquis of Pingyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jian inherited his father's rank and served as literary aide to the marquis of Pingyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 明帝即位，為尚書郎，遷羽林監。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he became Attendant of the Masters of Writing and was transferred to Colonel of the Feathered Forest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he became an attendant of the masters of writing and was transferred to colonel of the Feathered Forest.

manualTranslations.zh: 以東宮之舊，甚見親待。
manualTranslations.literal: As an old companion of the eastern palace, he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As an old companion of the eastern palace, he was greatly favored.

manualTranslations.zh: 出為洛陽典農。
manualTranslations.literal: He went out to serve as Agricultural Officer of Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as agricultural officer of Luoyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 時取農民以治宮室，儉上疏曰：「臣愚以為天下所急除者二賊，所急務者衣食。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time peasants were being taken to build palaces; Jian submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant is foolish, but considers that what the realm most urgently needs to eliminate are the two bandits, and what it most urgently needs to attend to are clothing and food.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time peasants were being taken to build palaces; Jian submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant considers that what the realm most urgently needs to eliminate are the two bandits, and what it most urgently needs to attend to are clothing and food.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠使二賊不滅，士民飢凍，雖崇美宮室，猶無益也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If truly the two bandits are not destroyed and officers and people hunger and freeze, even though palaces are lofty and beautiful it is still of no benefit."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the two bandits are not destroyed and officers and people hunger and freeze, even lofty palaces are of no benefit."

manualTranslations.zh: 遷荊州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Jing Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Jing Province.

sourceRange.text: 初，儉與夏侯玄、李豐等厚善。揚州刺史前將軍文欽，曹爽之邑人也，驍果粗猛，數有戰功，好增虜獲，以徼寵賞，多不見許，怨恨日甚。儉以計厚待欽，情好歡洽。欽亦感戴，投心無貳。正元二年正月，有彗星數十丈，西北竟天，起於吳、楚之分。儉、欽喜，以為己祥。遂矯太后詔，罪狀大將軍司馬景王，移諸郡國，舉兵反。迫脅淮南將守諸別屯者，及吏民大小，皆入壽春城，為壇於城西，歃血稱兵為盟，分老弱守城，儉、欽自將五六萬眾渡淮，西至項。儉堅守，欽在外為遊兵。儉、欽等表曰：「故相國懿，匡輔魏室，歷事忠貞，故烈祖明皇帝授以寄託之任。懿戮力盡節，以寧華夏。又以齊王聰明，無有穢德，乃心勤盡忠以輔上，天下賴之。懿欲討滅二虜以安宇內，始分軍糧，克時同舉，未成而薨。齊王以懿有輔己大功，故遂使師承統懿業，委以大事。而師以盛年在職，無疾託病，坐擁強兵，無有臣禮，朝臣非之，義士譏之，天下所聞，其罪一也。懿造計取賊，多舂軍糧，剋期有日。師為大臣，當除國難，又為人子，當卒父業。哀聲未絕而便罷息，為臣不忠，為子不孝，其罪二也。賊退過東關，坐自起眾，三征同進，喪眾敗績，歷年軍實，一旦而盡，致使賊來，天下騷動，死傷流離，其罪三也。賊舉國悉眾，號五十萬，來向壽春，圖詣洛陽，會太尉孚與臣等建計，乃杜塞要險，不與爭鋒，還固新城。淮南將士，衝鋒履刃，晝夜相守，勤瘁百日，死者塗地，自魏有軍已來，為難苦甚，莫過於此。而師遂意自由，不論封賞，權勢自在，無所領錄，其罪四也。故中書令李豐等，以師無人臣節，欲議退之。師知而請豐，其夕拉殺，載屍埋棺。豐等為大臣，帝王腹心，擅加酷暴，死無罪名，師有無君之心，其罪五也。懿每嘆說齊王自堪人主，君臣之義定。奉事以來十有五載，始欲歸政，按行武庫，詔問禁兵不得妄出。師自知姦慝，人神所不祐，矯廢君主，加之以罪。孚，師之叔父，性甚仁孝，追送齊王，悲不自勝。群臣皆怒而師懷忍，不顧大義，其罪六也。又故光祿大夫張緝，無罪而誅，夷其妻子，並及母后，逼恐至尊，強催督遣，臨時哀愕，莫不傷痛；而師稱慶，反以歡喜，其罪七也。陛下踐阼，聰明神武，事經聖心，欲崇省約，天下聞之，莫不歡慶；而師不自改悔脩复臣禮，而方徵兵募士，毀壞宮內，列侯自衛。陛下即阼，初不朝覲。陛下欲臨幸師舍以省其疾，复拒不通，不奉法度，其罪八也。近者領軍許允當為鎮北，以廚錢給賜，而師舉奏加辟，雖云流徙，道路餓殺，天下聞之，莫不哀傷，其罪九也。三方之守，一朝闕廢，多選精兵，以自營衛，五營領兵，闕而不補，多載器杖，充聚本營，天下所聞，人懷憤怨，訛言盈路，以疑海內，其罪十也。多休守兵，以佔高第，以空虛四表，欲擅強勢，以逞姦心，募取屯田，加其復賞，阻兵安忍，壞亂舊法。合聚諸籓王公以著鄴，欲悉誅之，一旦舉事廢主。天不長惡，使目腫不成，其罪十一也。臣等先人皆隨從太祖武皇帝征討凶暴，獲成大功，與高祖文皇帝即受漢禪，開國承家，猶堯舜相傳也。臣與安豐護軍鄭翼、廬江護軍呂宣、太守張休、淮南太守丁尊、督合肥護軍王休等議，各以累世受恩，千載風塵，思盡軀命，以完全社稷安主為效。斯義苟立，雖焚妻子，吞炭漆身，死而不恨也。按師之罪，宜加大辟，以彰姦慝。春秋之義，一世為善，一世宥之。懿有大功，海內所書，依古典議，廢師以侯就弟。弟昭，忠肅寬明，樂善好士，有高世君子之度，忠誠為國，不與師同。臣等碎首所保，可以代師輔導聖躬。太尉孚，忠孝小心，所宜親寵，授以保傅。護軍散騎常侍望，忠公親事，當官稱能，遠迎乘輿，有宿衛之功，可為中領軍。春秋之義，大義滅親，故周公誅弟，石碏戮子，季友鴆兄，上為國計，下全宗族。殛鯀用禹，聖人明典，古今所稱。乞陛下下臣等所奏，朝堂博議。臣言當道，使師遜位避賢者，罷兵去備，如三皇舊法，則天下協同。若師負勢恃眾不自退者，臣等率將所領，晝夜兼行，惟命是授。臣等今日所奏，惟欲使大魏永存，使陛下得行君意，遠絕亡之禍，百姓安全，六合一體，使忠臣義士，不愧於三皇五帝耳。臣恐兵起，天下擾亂，臣輒上事，移三征及州郡國典農，各安慰所部吏民，不得妄動，謹具以狀聞。惟陛下愛養精神，明慮危害，以寧海內。師專權用勢，賞罰自由，聞臣等舉眾，必下詔禁絕關津，使驛書不通，擅复徵調，有所收捕。此乃師詔，非陛下詔書，在所皆不得復承用。臣等道遠，懼文書不得皆通，輒臨時賞罰，以便宜從事，須定表上也。
