manualTranslations.zh: 靖雖年逾七十，愛樂人物，誘納后進，清談不倦。
manualTranslations.literal: Although Jing was past seventy, he delighted in men of talent, drew in the rising generation, and never tired of pure conversation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Xu Jing was past seventy, he delighted in talented men, encouraged the rising generation, and never tired of refined conversation.

manualTranslations.zh: 丞相諸葛亮皆為之拜。
manualTranslations.literal: Chancellor Zhuge Liang all for him bowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even Chancellor Zhuge Liang bowed to him.

manualTranslations.zh: 章武二年卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhangwu era (222).

manualTranslations.zh: 子欽，先靖夭沒。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Qin died before Jing in youth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Qin died young, before Xu Jing himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 欽子游，景耀中為尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin's son You, in the Jingyao era served as Minister of Writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin’s son You served as minister of writing during the Jingyao reign.

manualTranslations.zh: 始靖兄事颍川陳紀，與陳郡袁渙、平原華歆、東海王朗等親善，歆、朗及紀子群，魏初為公輔大臣，咸與靖書，申陳舊好，情義款至，文多故不載。
manualTranslations.literal: At first Jing treated Chen Ji of Yingchuan as an elder brother, and was close with Yuan Huan of Chen commandery, Hua Xin of Pingyuan, Wang Lang of Donghai, and others; Xin, Lang, and Yuan’s son Qun, in the early Wei all became great ministers, and all wrote to Jing, declaring old friendship; affection was warm and sincere, but the texts are many and therefore are not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In his youth Xu Jing had treated Chen Ji of Yingchuan as an elder brother and was close with Yuan Huan of Chen, Hua Xin of Pingyuan, Wang Lang of Donghai, and others. Hua Xin, Wang Lang, and Yuan Huan’s son Qun all became chief ministers of Wei in its early years and wrote to Xu Jing renewing old ties; the letters were warm and full of feeling, but there were so many that they are not reproduced here.

manualTranslations.zh: 《魏略》：王朗與文休書曰：「文休足下：消息平安，甚善甚善。
manualTranslations.literal: The Brief Account of Wei: Wang Lang in a letter to Wenxiu said: "Wenxiu, beneath your feet: news is peaceful—very good, very good.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei records that Wang Lang wrote to Wenxiu: "Wenxiu, my friend: I am glad to hear you are safe and well—very glad indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈意脫別三十餘年而無相見之緣乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Who would have thought that, parted for more than thirty years, we should have no chance to meet!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that after more than thirty years apart we should still have no chance to meet!

manualTranslations.zh: 詩人比一日之別於歲月，豈況悠悠歷累紀之年者哉！
manualTranslations.literal: The poets compare a single day’s parting to months and years—how much more when long years have slowly piled up!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Poets liken a single day’s parting to months and years—how much more when whole decades have slowly passed!

manualTranslations.zh: 自與子別，若沒而復浮，若絕而復連者數矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Since parting from you, it has been as if sinking and then floating again, as if cut off and then joined again, several times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since we parted I have seemed to sink and rise again, to be cut off and joined anew, again and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 而今而後，居昇平之京師，攀附於飛龍之聖主；
manualTranslations.literal: From now on I dwell in the peaceful capital, clinging to a sage lord like a soaring dragon;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From now on I live in the peaceful capital, attached to a sage ruler like a dragon in ascent;

manualTranslations.zh: 儕輩略盡，幸得老與足下併為遺種之叟，而相去數千里，加有邅蹇之隔，時聞消息於風聲，託舊情於思想，眇眇異處，與異世無以異也。
manualTranslations.literal: Our generation is nearly gone; I am fortunate to grow old with you as surviving elders of the remnant, yet we are separated by several thousand li, and there is besides the barrier of hardship and obstruction; at times I hear news on the wind, and entrust old feeling to thought—tiny and far apart, no different from being in different worlds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our generation is nearly gone; I am fortunate to grow old with you as surviving elders of a remnant age, yet we are thousands of li apart, with hardship and obstruction between us. At times I catch news on the wind and nourish old affection in memory—so far apart that it is scarcely different from living in different worlds.

manualTranslations.zh: 往者隨軍到荊州，見鄧子孝、桓元將，粗聞足下動靜，云夫子既在益州，執職領郡，德素規矩，老而不墮。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly, following the army to Jing province, I saw Deng Zixiao and Huan Yuanjiang and roughly heard of your movements; they said the master is already in Yi province, holding office and governing a commandery, his virtue plain and his conduct regular, not declining in old age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I followed the army to Jing province I met Deng Zixiao and Huan Yuanjiang and heard something of your circumstances: they said you were already in Yi province, holding office and governing a commandery, plain in virtue and steady in conduct, not declining with age.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時侍宿武皇帝於江陵劉景升聽事之上，共道足下於通夜，拳拳饑渴，誠無已也。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time I attended and lodged with Emperor Wu at Liu Jingsheng’s audience hall in Jiangling; we spoke of you through the whole night, earnest and eager, truly without end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time I kept night watch with Emperor Wu in Liu Biao’s audience hall at Jiangling; we spoke of you through the whole night, earnest and eager beyond measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 自天子在東宮，及即位之後，每會群賢，論天下髦雋之見在者，豈獨人盡易為英，士鮮易取最，故乃猥以原壤之朽質，感夫子之情聽；
manualTranslations.literal: From when the Son of Heaven was in the Eastern Palace, and after he ascended the throne, whenever the worthies were assembled to discuss the outstanding talents of the realm now living, was it only that men had all become easy to make heroes, and scholars easy to pick as the best? Therefore I presumptuously, with the rotten timber of Yuanrang, moved the master’s sympathetic hearing;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the time the Son of Heaven was crown prince, and after his accession, whenever the court assembled the worthies to discuss the outstanding men of the age, was it that men had all become easy to rank as heroes and scholars easy to choose as the best? I presumptuously, with my own worn-out timber, won your sympathetic ear;

manualTranslations.zh: 每敘足下，以為謀首，豈其注意，乃復過於前世，書曰『人惟求舊』，易稱『同聲相應，同氣相求』，劉將軍之與大魏，兼而兩之，總此二義。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever I spoke of you, I made you the chief of counsel—is not the attention paid to you again greater than in former days? The Documents say, "Men should seek the old"; the Changes say, "Like sounds respond, like qi seek one another"; General Liu and Great Wei—both together embrace these two meanings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever I spoke of you I set you at the head of counsel—is not the regard shown you greater than in former days? The Documents say, "Men should seek the old"; the Changes say, "Like sounds respond, like spirits seek one another." General Liu and Great Wei together fulfill both of these principles.

manualTranslations.zh: 前世邂逅，以同為睽，非武皇帝之旨；
manualTranslations.literal: In former days we met by chance, yet took sameness as estrangement—that was not Emperor Wu’s intent;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In former days we met by chance yet took shared ground as estrangement—that was not Emperor Wu’s intent;

manualTranslations.zh: 頃者蹉跌，其泰而否，亦非足下之意也。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently there was a stumble—from prosperity to decline—and that too was not your intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently there was a stumble—from prosperity to decline—and that was not your intent either.

manualTranslations.zh: 深思書、易之義，利結分於宿好，故遣降者送吳所獻致名馬、貂、罽，得因無嫌。
manualTranslations.literal: Deeply pondering the meaning of the Documents and the Changes, and wishing to bind old friendship with profit, I therefore sent a surrendered man to present famous horses, sable, and felt that Wu had offered, so that we might be without suspicion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reflecting deeply on the meaning of the Documents and the Changes, and wishing to renew old friendship with mutual benefit, I sent a messenger bearing the famous horses, sable, and felt that Wu had presented, so that we might meet without suspicion.

manualTranslations.zh: 道初開通，展敘舊情，以達聲問。
manualTranslations.literal: The road is newly opened; I unfold old feeling to convey voice and inquiry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that the road is newly opened, I unfold old affection to reach you with greetings.

manualTranslations.zh: 久闊情慉，非夫筆墨所能寫陳，亦想足下同其志念。
manualTranslations.literal: Long estranged, feelings pent up—this is not what brush and ink can fully set forth; I also think you share the same thoughts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Long estrangement has pent up feeling that brush and ink cannot fully express; I trust you share the same thoughts.

manualTranslations.zh: 今者，親生男女凡有幾人？
manualTranslations.literal: Now, of children born to you in all, how many are there?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How many children have you now, sons and daughters together?

manualTranslations.zh: 年並幾何？
manualTranslations.literal: And how old are they all?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And how old are they?

manualTranslations.zh: 僕連失一男一女，今有二男：大兒名肅，年二十九，生於會稽；
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant has in succession lost one son and one daughter; now there are two sons: the elder is named Su, twenty-nine years old, born in Kuaiji;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have lost one son and one daughter in succession; I now have two sons: the elder is named Su, twenty-nine, born in Kuaiji;

manualTranslations.zh: 小兒裁歲餘。
manualTranslations.literal: The younger is barely more than a year old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The younger is barely a year old.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨書愴悢，有懷緬然。」
manualTranslations.literal: As I face this letter, grief wells up; my thoughts stretch far away."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As I write, grief wells up and my thoughts reach far across the distance."

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「過聞『受終於文祖』之言於尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: He also said: "I lately heard the words 'He received the end from his cultured ancestor' in the Documents.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I have lately heard in the Documents the words, 'He received the mandate from his cultured ancestor.'

manualTranslations.zh: 又聞『曆數在躬，允執其中』之文於論語。
manualTranslations.literal: I also heard the text 'The cycle of rule is upon his person; sincerely he holds the center' in the Analects.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I also heard in the Analects the passage, 'The cycle of rule is upon his person; sincerely he holds the center.'

manualTranslations.zh: 豈自意得於老耄之齒，正值天命受於聖主之會，親見三讓之弘辭，觀眾瑞之總集，睹升堂穆穆之盛禮，瞻燔燎焜曜之青煙；
manualTranslations.literal: Could I have thought that in my old and white-haired years I would just meet the time when Heaven’s mandate was received from the sage lord, personally see the grand words of thrice yielding, observe the gathering of all auspicious signs, behold the solemn grandeur of ascending the hall, and gaze at the blue smoke blazing bright from the sacrificial fire;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Could I have imagined that in my white-haired old age I would live to see Heaven’s mandate received from the sage ruler, witness the grand ceremony of thrice yielding, behold the gathering of auspicious signs, see the solemn rites of ascending the hall, and watch the blue smoke blaze bright from the sacrificial flames;

manualTranslations.zh: 於時忽自以為處唐、虞之運，際於紫微之天庭也。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time I suddenly thought myself in the fortune of Tang and Yu, arriving at the azure-wei heavenly court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that moment I suddenly felt myself in the age of Tang and Yu, standing in the celestial court of the Purple Palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 徒慨不得攜子之手，共列於
manualTranslations.literal: I can only lament that I cannot take your hand and stand together among
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I can only lament that I cannot take your hand and stand together among

manualTranslations.literal: (shi)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Editor’s emendation: shi.

manualTranslations.zh: 有二子之數，以聽有唐『欽哉』之命也。
manualTranslations.literal: those who have the count of two sons, to hear the Tang command 'Reverently!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: those who have two sons at court, to hear the Tang command, 'Reverently!'

manualTranslations.zh: 子雖在裔土，想亦極目而回望，側耳而遐聽，延頸而鶴立也。
manualTranslations.literal: Although you are in distant lands, I think you too crane your neck and stand like a stork, straining your eyes to look back, your ears to listen far away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though you are in distant borderlands, I imagine you too crane your neck like a stork, straining your eyes to look back and your ears to listen from afar.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔汝南陳公初拜，不依故常，讓上卿於李元禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly when the Lord of Runan first took office, he did not follow old custom and yielded the chief minister’s post to Li Yuanli.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Runan first took office he did not follow custom and yielded the chief minister’s post to Li Yuanli.

manualTranslations.zh: 以此推之，吾宜退身以避子位也。
manualTranslations.literal: Inferring from this, I ought to withdraw and yield place to you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By that measure I ought to withdraw and yield place to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟得避子以竊讓名，然後
manualTranslations.literal: If I could yield to you and borrow the name of yielding, then afterward
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I could step aside for you and borrow the name of yielding, then afterward

manualTranslations.literal: (shou)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Editor’s emendation: shou.

manualTranslations.zh: 帶委質，游談於平、勃之間，與子共陳往時避地之艱辛，樂酒酣宴，高談大噱，亦足遺憂而忘老。
manualTranslations.literal: gird the sash and present my pledge, wander in talk between Ping and Bo, and with you recount the hardships of former days in taking refuge; joyful wine, hearty feasting, lofty talk and great laughter would also be enough to leave sorrow behind and forget old age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I would gird my sash and present my pledge, move freely in conversation between Chen Ping and Zhou Bo, and with you recount the hardships of our days in exile; wine, feasting, lofty talk and loud laughter would be enough to leave sorrow behind and forget old age.

manualTranslations.zh: 捉筆陳情，隨以喜笑。」
manualTranslations.literal: Taking up the brush to set forth feeling, I follow it with joy and laughter."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taking up the brush to pour out my feelings, I end with joy and laughter."

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「前夏有書而未達，今重有書，而並致前問。
manualTranslations.literal: He also said: "Last summer there was a letter that did not arrive; now there is another letter, and with it I send again my former inquiry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Last summer I sent a letter that never reached you; now I write again and repeat my earlier questions.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇帝既深悼劉將軍之早世，又愍其孤之不易，又惜使足下孔明等士人氣類之徒，遂沈溺於羌夷異種之間，永與華夏乖絕，而無朝聘中國之期緣，瞻睎故土桑梓之望也，故復運慈念而勞仁心，重下明詔以發德音，申敕朗等，使重為書與足下等。
manualTranslations.literal: The Emperor has deeply mourned General Liu’s early death, pitied the difficulty of his orphan, and also grieved that you, Kongming, and other men of scholar temperament have sunk among Qiang, Yi, and alien peoples, forever cut off from Huaxia, without the occasion of tribute missions to the Central State or the hope of gazing toward home and native place; therefore he again moved compassionate thought and labored his benevolent heart, again issued a bright edict to send forth virtuous sound, and charged Lang and others to write again to you and the rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Emperor deeply mourns General Liu’s early death, pities the hardship of his orphan, and grieves that you, Kongming, and other men of your kind have sunk among Qiang, Yi, and alien peoples, cut off forever from the Central Realm, without tribute missions to the imperial court or hope of gazing toward home; therefore he has again moved with compassion, issued a bright edict to proclaim his virtue, and charged me and others to write again to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 以足下聰明，揆殷勤之聖意，亦足悟海岱之所常在，知百川之所宜注矣。
manualTranslations.literal: With your intelligence, measuring the sage lord’s earnest intent, you are also sufficient to understand where sea and Mount Tai always stand, and know where the hundred streams ought to flow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With your intelligence you can surely grasp the sage ruler’s earnest intent, understand where sea and Mount Tai always belong, and know where the hundred streams ought to flow.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔伊尹去夏而就殷，陳平違楚而歸漢，猶曜德於阿衡，著功於宰相。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin left Xia and went to Yin; Chen Ping turned from Chu and returned to Han—still they displayed virtue as chief ministers and achieved merit as chancellors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi Yin left Xia for Yin; Chen Ping turned from Chu to Han—yet both displayed virtue as chief ministers and achieved lasting merit as chancellors.

manualTranslations.zh: 若足下能弼人之遺孤，定人之猶豫，去非常之偽號，事受命之大魏，客主兼不世之榮名，上下蒙不朽之常耀，功與事並，聲與勛著，考績效，足以超越伊、呂矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If you can assist a man’s orphaned heir, settle a man’s hesitation, cast off an irregular false title, and serve Great Wei that received the mandate, host and guest together would share unworldly glory; above and below would receive undying splendor; merit would match the task and fame would match achievement; examining achievement and effect, you would be enough to surpass Yi and Lü.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you can assist an orphaned heir, settle a realm’s hesitation, cast off an irregular false title, and serve Great Wei that received the mandate, host and guest would share unexampled glory; above and below would receive undying splendor; merit and fame would match the deed; judged by achievement you would surpass Yi Yin and Lü Wang.

manualTranslations.zh: 既承詔
manualTranslations.literal: Having received the edict
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having received the edict

manualTranslations.literal: (zhi)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Editor’s emendation: zhi.

manualTranslations.zh: ，且服舊之情，情不能已。
manualTranslations.literal: , and moreover yielding to old feeling, feeling cannot stop.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: , and moved by old affection, I cannot restrain my feelings.

manualTranslations.zh: 若不言足下之所能，陳足下之所見，則無以宣明詔命，弘光大之恩，敘宿昔夢想之思。
manualTranslations.literal: If I do not speak of what you are able to do and set forth what you see, then there is no way to proclaim and clarify the edict’s command, enlarge and brighten its great favor, or recount the longing of former days and dreams.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I do not speak of your abilities and set forth your own view, I cannot proclaim the edict, magnify its great grace, or recount the longing of former days.

manualTranslations.zh: 若天啟眾心，子導蜀意，誠此意有攜手之期。
manualTranslations.literal: If Heaven opens the hearts of the multitude and you guide Shu’s intent, truly in this intent there is a time to join hands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Heaven opens men’s hearts and you guide Shu’s will, there may truly be a day when we join hands.

manualTranslations.zh: 若險路未夷，子謀不從，則懼聲問或否，復面何由！
manualTranslations.literal: If the perilous road is not yet level and your counsel is not followed, then I fear voice and inquiry may fail—how then to meet face to face again!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the perilous road is not yet cleared and your counsel is not followed, I fear our messages may fail—how then shall we meet face to face again!

manualTranslations.zh: 前後二書，言每及斯，希不切然有動於懷。
manualTranslations.literal: In the two letters before and after, whenever the words reach this point, I hope you are deeply moved in your breast.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In both letters, whenever I come to this point, I hope you are deeply moved.

manualTranslations.zh: 足下周游江湖，以暨南海，歷觀夷俗，可謂遍矣；
manualTranslations.literal: You have wandered the rivers and lakes, reaching even the southern sea, and observed barbarian customs throughout—one may say you have seen broadly;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have traveled the rivers and lakes, even to the southern sea, and observed foreign customs throughout—you have seen broadly;

manualTranslations.zh: 想子之心，結思華夏，可謂深矣。
manualTranslations.literal: I think your heart is bound in thought to Huaxia—one may say it is deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I believe your heart is bound to the Central Realm—your longing runs deep.

manualTranslations.zh: 為身擇居，猶原中土；
manualTranslations.literal: In choosing where to dwell for yourself, you still prefer the central lands;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In choosing where to live, you still prefer the central lands;

manualTranslations.zh: 為主擇
manualTranslations.literal: in choosing for your lord
manualTranslations.idiomatic: in choosing for your lord

manualTranslations.literal: (ju)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Editor’s emendation: ju.

manualTranslations.zh: 安，豈可以不系意於京師，而持疑於荒裔乎？
manualTranslations.literal: security, how can you not fix your mind on the capital and yet hold doubt in distant borderlands?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: security, how can you fail to fix your mind on the capital and still hesitate in distant borderlands?

manualTranslations.zh: 詳思愚言，速示還報也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Consider carefully my foolish words and quickly show your reply."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Consider my words carefully and send a swift reply."

manualTranslations.zh: 麋竺字子仲，東海朐人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Mi Zhu, courtesy name Zizhong, was a man of Ju in Donghai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu, styled Zizhong, came from Ju in Donghai commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖世貨殖，僮客萬人，貲產鉅億。
manualTranslations.literal: For generations his family traded and accumulated wealth; he had ten thousand retainers and assets of hundreds of millions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His family had traded and accumulated wealth for generations; he had ten thousand retainers and assets reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

manualTranslations.zh: 《搜神記》曰：竺嘗從洛歸，未達家數十里，路傍見一婦人，從竺求寄載。
manualTranslations.literal: In Search of the Supernatural says: Zhu once returned from Luoyang; when he was still several tens of li from home, he saw a woman by the roadside who asked Zhu to give her a ride.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Search of the Supernatural records that Mi Zhu was returning from Luoyang when, still several tens of li from home, he saw a woman by the roadside who asked him for a ride.

manualTranslations.zh: 行可數里，婦謝去，謂竺曰：「我天使也，當往燒東海麋竺家，感君見載，故以相語。」
manualTranslations.literal: After traveling several li, the woman thanked him and left, saying to Zhu: "I am a heavenly messenger and am going to burn the house of Mi Zhu of Donghai; moved by your giving me a ride, I therefore tell you."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a few li she thanked him and prepared to leave, saying to Mi Zhu: "I am a heavenly messenger sent to burn the house of Mi Zhu of Donghai; moved by your giving me a ride, I tell you this."

manualTranslations.zh: 竺因私請之，婦曰：「不可得不燒。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu therefore privately begged her; the woman said: "It cannot be that it will not burn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu privately begged her, but the woman said: "It cannot be avoided.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，君可馳去，我當緩行，日中火當發。」
manualTranslations.literal: If so, you may gallop away; I shall go slowly, and at midday the fire will break out."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If so, you may ride away at once; I shall go slowly, and at midday the fire will break out."

manualTranslations.zh: 竺乃還家，遽出財物，日中而火大發。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu then returned home, hurriedly removed his goods, and at midday a great fire broke out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu hurried home, rushed his goods out of the house, and at midday a great fire broke out.

manualTranslations.zh: 后徐州牧陶謙辟為別駕從事。
manualTranslations.literal: Later the provincial governor of Xu, Tao Qian, summoned him as aide-de-camp on the staff.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Tao Qian, governor of Xu province, recruited him as aide-de-camp on the staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 謙卒，竺奉謙遺命，迎先主于小沛。
manualTranslations.literal: When Qian died, Zhu carried out Qian’s final command and welcomed the First Lord at Xiaopei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Tao Qian died, Mi Zhu carried out his final command and welcomed Liu Bei at Xiaopei.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安元年，呂布乘先主之出拒袁術，襲下邳，虜先主妻子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jian’an, Lü Bu, taking advantage of the First Lord’s going out to resist Yuan Shu, raided Xiapi and captured the First Lord’s wife and children.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jian’an, while Liu Bei was away resisting Yuan Shu, Lü Bu seized Xiapi and captured Liu Bei’s wife and children.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主轉軍廣陵海西，竺于是進妹于先主為夫人，奴客二千，金銀貨幣以助軍資，于時困匱，賴此複振。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Lord shifted his army to Guangling and Haixi; Zhu thereupon presented his younger sister to the First Lord as consort, with two thousand retainers and gold, silver, and currency to aid military supplies; at the time, pressed by want, he relied on this to revive again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei shifted his army to Guangling and Haixi; Mi Zhu then offered his younger sister to Liu Bei as consort, along with two thousand retainers and gold, silver, and currency to support the army; at that desperate hour Liu Bei relied on this to recover his strength.

manualTranslations.zh: 后曹公表竺領嬴郡太守，曹公集載公表曰：「泰山郡界廣遠，舊多輕悍，權時之宜，可分五縣為嬴郡，揀選清廉以為守將。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Lord Cao memorialized that Zhu should head Ying commandery as grand warden; the Collected Documents of Lord Cao record the memorial: "The borders of Taishan commandery are broad and far; formerly there were many light and fierce men; as the time’s expedient requires, five counties may be separated to form Ying commandery, and the pure and honest selected as defending commander.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao memorialized that Mi Zhu should serve as grand warden of Ying commandery. Cao Cao’s collected documents record the memorial: "Taishan commandery’s borders are broad and its people were formerly unruly; as the times require, five counties may be separated to form Ying commandery, and a pure and honest man chosen as its defender.

manualTranslations.zh: 偏將軍麋竺，素履忠貞，文武昭烈，請以竺領嬴郡太守，撫慰吏民。」
manualTranslations.literal: Lieutenant General Mi Zhu, by nature upright and loyal, civil and martial, splendid and fierce—please let Zhu head Ying commandery as grand warden and comfort clerks and people."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lieutenant General Mi Zhu is by nature loyal and upright, accomplished in civil and military affairs—let Mi Zhu head Ying commandery as grand warden and comfort officials and people."

manualTranslations.zh: 竺弟芳為彭城相，皆去官，隨先主周旋。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu’s younger brother Fang was chancellor of Pengcheng; both left office and followed the First Lord in his turns of fortune.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu’s younger brother Fang was chancellor of Pengcheng; both brothers resigned their posts and followed Liu Bei through every turn of fortune.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主將適荊州，遣竺先與劉表相聞，以竺為左將軍從事中郎。
manualTranslations.literal: When the First Lord was about to go to Jing province, he sent Zhu ahead to communicate with Liu Biao, and made Zhu administrative clerk on the staff of the General of the Left.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei prepared to move into Jing province, he sent Mi Zhu ahead to open contact with Liu Biao and appointed him administrative clerk on the staff of the general of the left.

manualTranslations.zh: 益州既平，拜為安漢將軍，班在軍師將軍之右。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yi province was pacified, he was invested as General Who Pacifies Han, ranking to the right of the General of the Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Yi province was pacified, he was named general who pacifies Han, ranking just to the right of the general of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 竺雍容敦雅，而干翮非所長。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu was easy and dignified, refined and elegant, but practical administration was not his strength.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mi Zhu was unhurried, dignified, and refined, but practical administration was not his strength.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以待之以上賓之禮，未嘗有所統御。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore he was treated with the ritual of a chief guest and never given command over anything.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei therefore treated him with the ceremony due a chief guest and never gave him command over troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 然賞賜優寵，無與為比。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet in bounty and favor he had no equal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet in bounty and favor he had no equal.

items.acceptedSourceText: 靖雖年逾七十，愛樂人物，誘納后進，清談不倦。丞相諸葛亮皆為之拜。章武二年卒。子欽，先靖夭沒。欽子游，景耀中為尚書。始靖兄事颍川陳紀，與陳郡袁渙、平原華歆、東海王朗等親善，歆、朗及紀子群，魏初為公輔大臣，咸與靖書，申陳舊好，情義款至，文多故不載。《魏略》：王朗與文休書曰：「文休足下：消息平安，甚善甚善。豈意脫別三十餘年而無相見之緣乎！詩人比一日之別於歲月，豈況悠悠歷累紀之年者哉！自與子別，若沒而復浮，若絕而復連者數矣。而今而後，居昇平之京師，攀附於飛龍之聖主；儕輩略盡，幸得老與足下併為遺種之叟，而相去數千里，加有邅蹇之隔，時聞消息於風聲，託舊情於思想，眇眇異處，與異世無以異也。往者隨軍到荊州，見鄧子孝、桓元將，粗聞足下動靜，云夫子既在益州，執職領郡，德素規矩，老而不墮。是時侍宿武皇帝於江陵劉景升聽事之上，共道足下於通夜，拳拳饑渴，誠無已也。自天子在東宮，及即位之後，每會群賢，論天下髦雋之見在者，豈獨人盡易為英，士鮮易取最，故乃猥以原壤之朽質，感夫子之情聽；每敘足下，以為謀首，豈其注意，乃復過於前世，書曰『人惟求舊』，易稱『同聲相應，同氣相求』，劉將軍之與大魏，兼而兩之，總此二義。前世邂逅，以同為睽，非武皇帝之旨；頃者蹉跌，其泰而否，亦非足下之意也。深思書、易之義，利結分於宿好，故遣降者送吳所獻致名馬、貂、罽，得因無嫌。道初開通，展敘舊情，以達聲問。久闊情慉，非夫筆墨所能寫陳，亦想足下同其志念。今者，親生男女凡有幾人？年並幾何？僕連失一男一女，今有二男：大兒名肅，年二十九，生於會稽；小兒裁歲餘。臨書愴悢，有懷緬然。」又曰：「過聞『受終於文祖』之言於尚書。又聞『曆數在躬，允執其中』之文於論語。豈自意得於老耄之齒，正值天命受於聖主之會，親見三讓之弘辭，觀眾瑞之總集，睹升堂穆穆之盛禮，瞻燔燎焜曜之青煙；於時忽自以為處唐、虞之運，際於紫微之天庭也。徒慨不得攜子之手，共列於（世）有二子之數，以聽有唐『欽哉』之命也。子雖在裔土，想亦極目而回望，側耳而遐聽，延頸而鶴立也。昔汝南陳公初拜，不依故常，讓上卿於李元禮。以此推之，吾宜退身以避子位也。苟得避子以竊讓名，然後（綬）帶委質，游談於平、勃之間，與子共陳往時避地之艱辛，樂酒酣宴，高談大噱，亦足遺憂而忘老。捉筆陳情，隨以喜笑。」又曰：「前夏有書而未達，今重有書，而並致前問。皇帝既深悼劉將軍之早世，又愍其孤之不易，又惜使足下孔明等士人氣類之徒，遂沈溺於羌夷異種之間，永與華夏乖絕，而無朝聘中國之期緣，瞻睎故土桑梓之望也，故復運慈念而勞仁心，重下明詔以發德音，申敕朗等，使重為書與足下等。以足下聰明，揆殷勤之聖意，亦足悟海岱之所常在，知百川之所宜注矣。昔伊尹去夏而就殷，陳平違楚而歸漢，猶曜德於阿衡，著功於宰相。若足下能弼人之遺孤，定人之猶豫，去非常之偽號，事受命之大魏，客主兼不世之榮名，上下蒙不朽之常耀，功與事並，聲與勛著，考績效，足以超越伊、呂矣。既承詔（直），且服舊之情，情不能已。若不言足下之所能，陳足下之所見，則無以宣明詔命，弘光大之恩，敘宿昔夢想之思。若天啟眾心，子導蜀意，誠此意有攜手之期。若險路未夷，子謀不從，則懼聲問或否，復面何由！前後二書，言每及斯，希不切然有動於懷。足下周游江湖，以暨南海，歷觀夷俗，可謂遍矣；想子之心，結思華夏，可謂深矣。為身擇居，猶原中土；為主擇（居）安，豈可以不系意於京師，而持疑於荒裔乎？詳思愚言，速示還報也。」麋竺字子仲，東海朐人也。祖世貨殖，僮客萬人，貲產鉅億。《搜神記》曰：竺嘗從洛歸，未達家數十里，路傍見一婦人，從竺求寄載。行可數里，婦謝去，謂竺曰：「我天使也，當往燒東海麋竺家，感君見載，故以相語。」竺因私請之，婦曰：「不可得不燒。如此，君可馳去，我當緩行，日中火當發。」竺乃還家，遽出財物，日中而火大發。后徐州牧陶謙辟為別駕從事。謙卒，竺奉謙遺命，迎先主于小沛。建安元年，呂布乘先主之出拒袁術，襲下邳，虜先主妻子。先主轉軍廣陵海西，竺于是進妹于先主為夫人，奴客二千，金銀貨幣以助軍資，于時困匱，賴此複振。后曹公表竺領嬴郡太守，曹公集載公表曰：「泰山郡界廣遠，舊多輕悍，權時之宜，可分五縣為嬴郡，揀選清廉以為守將。偏將軍麋竺，素履忠貞，文武昭烈，請以竺領嬴郡太守，撫慰吏民。」竺弟芳為彭城相，皆去官，隨先主周旋。先主將適荊州，遣竺先與劉表相聞，以竺為左將軍從事中郎。益州既平，拜為安漢將軍，班在軍師將軍之右。竺雍容敦雅，而干翮非所長。是以待之以上賓之禮，未嘗有所統御。然賞賜優寵，無與為比。

sourceRange.text: 祗字奉宗，汝南人，許靖兄之外孫也。少孤，長於靖家。弱冠知名，稍遷至選曹郎，矜厲有威容。多技藝，挾數術，費禕甚異之，故超繼允內侍。呂乂卒，祗又以侍中守尚書令，加鎮軍將軍，大將軍姜維雖班在祗上，常率眾在外，希親朝政。祗上承主指，下接閹豎，深見信愛，權重於維。景耀元年卒，後主痛惜，發言流涕，乃下詔曰：「祗統職一紀，柔嘉惟則，幹肅有章，和義利物，庶績允明。命不融遠，朕用悼焉。夫存有令問，則亡加美諡，諡曰忠侯。」賜子粲爵關內侯，拔次子裕為黃門侍郎。自祗之有寵，後主追怨允日深，謂為自輕，由祗媚茲一人，皓構間浸潤故耳。允孫宏，晉巴西太守。臣松之以為陳群子泰，陸遜子抗，傳皆以子系父，不別載姓，及王肅、杜恕、張承、顧劭之流，莫不皆然，惟董允獨否，未詳其意，當以允名位優重，事蹟逾父故邪？夏侯玄、陳表並有騂角之美，而亦如泰者，《魏書》總名此卷云《諸夏侯曹傳》，故不復稍加品藻。陳武與表俱至偏將軍，以位不相過故也。

manualTranslations.zh: 祗字奉宗，汝南人，許靖兄之外孫也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Fengzong, was a man of Runan; he was the maternal grandson of Xu Jing's elder brother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi, styled Fengzong, came from Runan and was the maternal grandson of Xu Jing's elder brother.

manualTranslations.zh: 少孤，長於靖家。
manualTranslations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised in Jing's household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised in Xu Jing's household.

manualTranslations.zh: 弱冠知名，稍遷至選曹郎，矜厲有威容。
manualTranslations.literal: At capping age he was already known; he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Selection Bureau, stern and imposing in bearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was already known at capping age and was gradually promoted to gentleman of the selection bureau, stern and imposing in bearing.

manualTranslations.zh: 多技藝，挾數術，費禕甚異之，故超繼允內侍。
manualTranslations.literal: Skilled in many arts and versed in numerology, Fei Yi greatly regarded him as extraordinary; therefore he was promoted ahead of Yun into inner service.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Skilled in many arts and versed in divination, he greatly impressed Fei Yi, who therefore had him leapfrog Dong Yun into inner court service.

manualTranslations.zh: 呂乂卒，祗又以侍中守尚書令，加鎮軍將軍，大將軍姜維雖班在祗上，常率眾在外，希親朝政。
manualTranslations.literal: When Lü Yi died, Zhi again served as palace attendant while acting as Director of the Masters of Writing, and was further given the title General Who Stabilizes the Army; Grand General Jiang Wei, though ranking above Zhi, usually led troops outside and seldom attended to court governance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Lü Yi died, Chen Zhi again served as palace attendant while acting as director of the masters of writing and was further named general who stabilizes the army. Grand General Jiang Wei, though ranking above him, usually led troops in the field and seldom attended to court governance.

manualTranslations.zh: 祗上承主指，下接閹豎，深見信愛，權重於維。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi carried out the sovereign's intent above and cultivated ties with eunuch attendants below; he was deeply trusted and favored, and his authority outweighed Wei's.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chen Zhi carried out the sovereign's intent above and cultivated ties with eunuch attendants below; he was deeply trusted and favored, and his authority outweighed Jiang Wei's.

manualTranslations.zh: 景耀元年卒，後主痛惜，發言流涕，乃下詔曰：「祗統職一紀，柔嘉惟則，幹肅有章，和義利物，庶績允明。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jingyao he died; the Later Lord grieved deeply, wept as he spoke, and issued an edict saying: "Zhi held office for a full twelve years; gentle and good, he was a model; dignified and orderly, his conduct was manifest; harmonious and righteous, he benefited things and men; his many achievements were bright and clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Jingyao era. The Later Lord grieved deeply, wept as he spoke, and issued an edict: "Zhi held office for a full twelve years; gentle and good, he was a model; dignified and orderly, his conduct was manifest; harmonious and righteous, he benefited things and men; his many achievements were clear and bright.

manualTranslations.zh: 命不融遠，朕用悼焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Fate did not grant him long life; We mourn him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fate did not grant him long life, and We mourn him.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫存有令問，則亡加美諡，諡曰忠侯。」
manualTranslations.literal: When one in life has a fine reputation, in death an honorable posthumous title is added; his posthumous title is Loyal Marquis."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When one in life has a fine reputation, in death an honorable posthumous title is added; his posthumous title is Loyal Marquis."

manualTranslations.zh: 賜子粲爵關內侯，拔次子裕為黃門侍郎。
manualTranslations.literal: He granted Zhi's son Can noble rank as marquis within the passes and promoted his second son Yu to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Chen Zhi's son Can as marquis within the passes and promoted his second son Yu to gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

manualTranslations.zh: 自祗之有寵，後主追怨允日深，謂為自輕，由祗媚茲一人，皓構間浸潤故耳。
manualTranslations.literal: From the time Zhi gained favor, the Later Lord's resentment toward Yun grew daily deeper; he thought himself undervalued—because Zhi flattered this one man and Hao wove intrigues and gradually poisoned his ear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the time Chen Zhi gained favor, the Later Lord's resentment toward Dong Yun grew daily deeper; he thought himself undervalued—because Chen Zhi flattered this one man and Huang Hao wove intrigues and gradually poisoned his ear.

manualTranslations.zh: 允孫宏，晉巴西太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Yun's grandson Hong, under Jin, was Administrator of Brazil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Yun's grandson Hong served Jin as administrator of Brazil.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為陳群子泰，陸遜子抗，傳皆以子系父，不別載姓，及王肅、杜恕、張承、顧劭之流，莫不皆然，惟董允獨否，未詳其意，當以允名位優重，事蹟逾父故邪？
manualTranslations.literal: Pei Songzhi considers that for Chen Qun's son Tai, Lu Xun's son Kang, and others, the biographies all treat sons under fathers without separately recording the surname; Wang Su, Du Shu, Zhang Cheng, Gu Shao, and the like were all the same—only Dong Yun was not. The reason is unclear; perhaps because Yun's name and rank were exalted and his achievements surpassed his father's?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that for Chen Qun's son Tai, Lu Xun's son Kang, and others, the biographies all attach sons under fathers without separately recording the surname; Wang Su, Du Shu, Zhang Cheng, Gu Shao, and the like all follow this pattern—only Dong Yun does not. The reason is unclear; perhaps because Yun's name and rank were exalted and his achievements surpassed his father's?

sourceRange.text: 章武二年，先主徵嚴詣永安宮，拜尚書令。三年，先主疾病，嚴與諸葛亮並受遺詔輔少主；以嚴為中都護，統內外軍事，留鎮永安。建興元年，封都鄉侯，假節，加光祿勳。四年，轉為前將軍。以諸葛亮欲出軍漢中，嚴當知後事，移屯江州，留護軍陳到駐永安，皆統屬嚴。嚴與孟達書曰：「吾與孔明俱受寄託，憂深責重，思得良伴。」亮亦與達書曰：「部分如流，趨舍罔滯，正方性也。」其見貴重如此。諸葛亮集有嚴與亮書，勸亮宜受九錫，進爵稱王。亮答書曰：「吾與足下相知久矣，可不復相解！足下方誨以光國，戒之以勿拘之道，是以未得默已。吾本東方下士，誤用於先帝，位極人臣，祿賜百億，今討賊未效，知己未答，而方寵齊、晉，坐自貴大，非其義也。若滅魏斬叡，帝還故居，與諸子併升，雖十命可受，況於九邪！」八年，遷驃騎將軍。以曹真欲三道向漢川，亮命嚴將二萬人赴漢中。亮表嚴子豐為江州都督督軍，典嚴後事。亮以明年當出軍，命嚴以中都護署府事。嚴改名為平。

context.beforeSource: 加輔漢將軍，領郡如故。
context.afterSource: 九年春，亮軍祁山，平催督運事。

manualTranslations.zh: 章武二年，先主徵嚴詣永安宮，拜尚書令。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu, the Former Lord summoned Yan to Yong’an Palace and appointed him Director of the Ministry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhangwu 2 (222) the Former Lord summoned Li Yan to Yong’an Palace and named him director of the ministry.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，先主疾病，嚴與諸葛亮並受遺詔輔少主；
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year the Former Lord fell ill; Yan together with Zhuge Liang both received the testamentary edict to assist the young lord;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next year, as the Former Lord lay dying, Li Yan and Zhuge Liang received the deathbed charge to guide the young emperor;

manualTranslations.zh: 以嚴為中都護，統內外軍事，留鎮永安。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan was made Director of the Retainers, commanding internal and external military affairs, remaining to garrison Yong’an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Yan was made director of the retainers with command over all armies and remained at Yong’an.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年，封都鄉侯，假節，加光祿勳。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dou Village, granted the staff of authority, and added Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223) he was enfeoffed as marquis of Dou village, granted the staff of authority, and made grandee of splendid happiness.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，轉為前將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Former General.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 4 (226) he became former general.

manualTranslations.zh: 以諸葛亮欲出軍漢中，嚴當知後事，移屯江州，留護軍陳到駐永安，皆統屬嚴。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Zhuge Liang wished to lead the army out to Hanzhong, Yan should manage rear affairs; he moved camp to Jiangzhou, leaving Protector of the Army Chen Dao garrisoned at Yong’an—all under Yan’s command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang prepared to march on Hanzhong, Li Yan was to manage affairs in the rear; he moved to Jiangzhou and left Chen Dao at Yong’an, both under his command.

manualTranslations.zh: 嚴與孟達書曰：「吾與孔明俱受寄託，憂深責重，思得良伴。
manualTranslations.literal: Yan wrote to Meng Da, saying: “I together with Kongming both received the entrustment—worry is deep and responsibility heavy; I wish to gain a good companion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Yan wrote Meng Da: “Kongming and I share this burden—deep worry and heavy duty—and I long for a worthy partner.

manualTranslations.zh: 」亮亦與達書曰：「部分如流，趨舍罔滯，正方性也。
manualTranslations.literal: ”Liang also wrote to Da, saying: “Disposition and assignment flow like water; advance and withdrawal without delay—this is Zhengfang’s nature.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”Zhuge Liang also wrote Meng Da: “Li Yan assigns duties smoothly and moves without hesitation—that is his nature.

manualTranslations.zh: 」其見貴重如此。
manualTranslations.literal: ”Thus was he seen to be honoured and esteemed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”Such was the esteem in which he was held.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸葛亮集有嚴與亮書，勸亮宜受九錫，進爵稱王。
manualTranslations.literal: In Zhuge Liang’s collected works there is Yan’s letter to Liang, urging Liang to accept the Nine Bestowals and advance in rank to king.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang’s collected works preserve Li Yan’s letter urging him to accept the Nine Bestowals and proclaim himself king.

manualTranslations.zh: 亮答書曰：「吾與足下相知久矣，可不復相解！
manualTranslations.literal: Liang replied in a letter, saying: “I with you, sir, have known each other long—can we not understand each other again!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang answered: “We have known each other long—you need not lecture me!

manualTranslations.zh: 足下方誨以光國，戒之以勿拘之道，是以未得默已。
manualTranslations.literal: You, sir, just now instructed me to glorify the state and warned me with the Way of not being constrained—therefore I could not keep silent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You urge me to glorify the state and warn me against restraint, so I cannot stay silent.

manualTranslations.zh: 吾本東方下士，誤用於先帝，位極人臣，祿賜百億，今討賊未效，知己未答，而方寵齊、晉，坐自貴大，非其義也。
manualTranslations.literal: I am originally an eastern lowly scholar, mistakenly employed by the Former Lord, rank reaching the utmost among ministers, salary and gifts in the hundreds of millions; now striking the bandits has not succeeded, repaying the knowing lord has not been answered—yet you would ennoble me like Qi and Jin and sit self-exalted and great; this is not the right meaning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I was a humble eastern scholar whom the late emperor raised to the summit of office with boundless honours; the campaign against Wei is unfinished and my debt to him unpaid—yet you would have me take rank like the lords of Qi and Jin and sit in self-importance. That is not right.

manualTranslations.zh: 若滅魏斬叡，帝還故居，與諸子併升，雖十命可受，況於九邪！
manualTranslations.literal: If Wei is destroyed and Rui beheaded, the emperor returns to his old residence, and I rise together with the various lords—even ten commands could be received, how much more nine!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Wei were destroyed and Cao Rui slain, the emperor restored to his old capital, and I advanced with the other lords—even ten commands I might accept; how much less nine!

manualTranslations.zh: 以曹真欲三道向漢川，亮命嚴將二萬人赴漢中。

manualTranslations.zh: 亮表嚴子豐為江州都督督軍，典嚴後事。

sourceRange.text: 魏延字文長，義陽人也。以部曲隨先主入蜀，數有戰功，遷牙門將軍。先主爲漢中王，遷治成都，當得重將以鎮漢川，眾論以爲必在張飛，飛亦以心自許。先主乃拔延爲督漢中鎮遠將軍，領漢中太守，一軍盡驚。先主大會群臣，問延曰：「今委卿以重任，卿居之欲云何？」延對曰：「若曹操舉天下而來，請爲大王拒之；偏將十萬之眾至，請爲大王吞之。」先主稱善，眾咸壯其言。先主踐尊號，進拜鎮北將軍。建興元年223年，封都亭侯。五年，諸葛亮駐漢中，更以延爲督前部，領丞相司馬、涼州刺史，八年，使延西入羌中，魏後將軍費瑤、雍州刺史郭淮與延戰於陽谿，延大破淮等，遷爲前軍師、征西大將軍，假節，進封南鄭侯。延每隨亮出，輒欲請兵萬人，與亮異道會於潼關，如韓信故事，亮制而不許。

manualTranslations.zh: 魏延字文長，義陽人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei Yan, courtesy name Wenchang, was a man of Yiyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Yan, styled Wenchang, came from Yiyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 以部曲隨先主入蜀，數有戰功，遷牙門將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: With his private troops he followed the Former Lord into Shu; repeatedly had battle achievements; was promoted to General of the Household of the Yamen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Bei into Shu with his own troops, won repeated victories, and was made general of the household of the yamen.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主爲漢中王，遷治成都，當得重將以鎮漢川，眾論以爲必在張飛，飛亦以心自許。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Former Lord became King of Hanzhong and moved his seat to govern Chengdu, a heavy general was needed to garrison Han River; public opinion thought it must be Zhang Fei, and Fei also in his heart took it for granted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong and moved the capital to Chengdu, everyone expected Zhang Fei to hold Hanzhong—and Fei expected it too.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主乃拔延爲督漢中鎮遠將軍，領漢中太守，一軍盡驚。
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Lord thereupon elevated Yan to General Who Supervises Hanzhong and Pacifies the Distance, concurrently Governor of Hanzhong—the whole army was startled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei instead named Wei Yan general who supervises Hanzhong and pacifies the distance, with the governorship of Hanzhong—the whole army was astonished.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主大會群臣，問延曰：「今委卿以重任，卿居之欲云何？
manualTranslations.literal: The Former Lord greatly assembled the host of ministers and asked Yan, saying: “Now I entrust you with a heavy responsibility—living in this post, what do you wish to say?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei gathered the court and asked Wei Yan: “I give you a grave charge—what say you to holding this post?

manualTranslations.zh: 」延對曰：「若曹操舉天下而來，請爲大王拒之；
manualTranslations.literal: ”Yan replied, saying: “If Cao Cao brings all Under Heaven and comes, I ask to reject him for the Great King;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”Wei Yan answered: “If Cao Cao brings all the realm, I will hold him off for you;

manualTranslations.zh: 偏將十萬之眾至，請爲大王吞之。
manualTranslations.literal: If partial generals with a host of a hundred thousand arrive, I ask to swallow them for the Great King.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if lesser generals bring a hundred thousand men, I will swallow them for you.

manualTranslations.zh: 」先主稱善，眾咸壯其言。
manualTranslations.literal: ”The Former Lord praised it as good; the host all admired his words as bold.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: ”Liu Bei approved, and the court admired his bold words.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主踐尊號，進拜鎮北將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Former Lord assumed the exalted title, Yan was advanced and appointed General Who Guards the North.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took the imperial title, Wei Yan was promoted to general who guards the north.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年，封都亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing, 223 CE, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Du Village.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223) he was enfeoffed as marquis of Du village.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，諸葛亮駐漢中，更以延爲督前部，領丞相司馬、涼州刺史，八年，使延西入羌中，魏後將軍費瑤、雍州刺史郭淮與延戰於陽谿，延大破淮等，遷爲前軍師、征西大將軍，假節，進封南鄭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year Zhuge Liang garrisoned Hanzhong and further made Yan Supervisor of the Front Section, concurrently Chancellor’s Major and Inspector of Liang Province; in the eighth year he sent Yan west into the Qiang lands; Wei’s General of the Rear Fei Yao and Inspector of Yong Province Guo Huai fought Yan at Yang Creek; Yan greatly defeated Huai and the others; was transferred to Former Army Adviser and Grand General Who Conquers the West, granted the staff of authority, and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Nan Zheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 5 (227) Zhuge Liang garrisoned Hanzhong and made Wei Yan supervisor of the front section with the posts of the chancellor’s major and inspector of Liang province; in Jianxing 8 (230) he sent Wei Yan into the Qiang country, where Fei Yao and Guo Huai met him at Yang Creek and were routed; Wei Yan became former army adviser and grand general who conquers the west, received the staff of authority, and was advanced to marquis of Nan Zheng.

sourceRange.text: 朗兄子寵，先主時為牙門將。秭歸之敗，寵營特完。建興元年223年封都亭侯，後為中部督，典宿衛兵。諸葛亮當北行，表與後主曰：「將軍向寵，性行淑均，曉暢軍事，試用於昔，先帝稱之曰能，是以眾論舉寵為督。愚以為營中之事，悉以咨之，必能使行陳和睦，優劣得所也。」遷中領軍。延熙三年，征漢嘉蠻夷，遇害。寵弟充，歷射聲校尉、尚書。《襄阳记》曰：魏咸熙元年六月，镇西将军卫瓘至於成都，得璧玉印各一枚，文似“成信”字，魏人宣示百官，藏于相国府。充闻之曰：“吾闻谯周之言，先帝讳备，其训具也，后主讳禅，其训授也，如言刘已具矣，当授与人也。今中抚军名炎，而汉年极於炎兴，瑞出成都，而藏之於相国府，此殆天意也。”是岁，拜充为梓潼太守，明年十二月而晋武帝即尊位，炎兴於是乎徵焉。孙盛曰：昔公孙自以起成都，号曰成氏，二玉之文，殆述所作乎！

manualTranslations.literal: Lang's elder brother's son Chong, in the Former Lord's time served as general of the household yamen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang's elder brother's son Xiang Chong served as general of the household yamen under the Former Lord.

manualTranslations.zh: 秭歸之敗，寵營特完。
manualTranslations.literal: At the defeat at Zigui, Chong's camp alone remained intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 建興元年223年封都亭侯，後為中部督，典宿衛兵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing, 223, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and directed the palace guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223) he was enfeoffed marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and commanded the palace guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸葛亮當北行，表與後主曰：「將軍向寵，性行淑均，曉暢軍事，試用於昔，先帝稱之曰能，是以眾論舉寵為督。
manualTranslations.literal: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the Later Lord, saying: "General Xiang Chong is even and fair in nature and conduct, well versed in military affairs; tested in former days, the late Emperor praised him as capable, and so by common counsel Chong was recommended as supervisor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the emperor: "General Xiang Chong is even-tempered and fair, and well versed in military affairs. The late emperor tested him in earlier days and praised his ability, and the court therefore recommended him as camp supervisor.

manualTranslations.zh: 愚以為營中之事，悉以咨之，必能使行陳和睦，優劣得所也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant thinks that in camp affairs, if you consult him on all, you will surely make the ranks harmonious and assign merit and fault to their proper places."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I believe that in camp affairs, if you consult him on everything, the ranks will stay harmonious and each man will be placed according to his worth."

manualTranslations.zh: 遷中領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to director of the central army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the central army.

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙三年，征漢嘉蠻夷，遇害。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Yanxi he campaigned against the Hanjia barbarians and met with harm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 3 (240) he campaigned against the Hanjia tribes and was killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 寵弟充，歷射聲校尉、尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong's younger brother Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Xiang Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：魏咸熙元年六月，镇西将军卫瓘至於成都，得璧玉印各一枚，文似“成信”字，魏人宣示百官，藏于相国府。
manualTranslations.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianxi in Wei, General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and obtained one jade seal each, the inscription resembling the characters for "completed faith"; the men of Wei displayed them to the hundred officials and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji records that in the sixth month of Wei Xianxi 1 (264), General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and found a pair of jade seals inscribed with characters resembling "completed faith"; Wei officials displayed them to the court and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.

manualTranslations.zh: 充闻之曰：“吾闻谯周之言，先帝讳备，其训具也，后主讳禅，其训授也，如言刘已具矣，当授与人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chong heard of it and said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's words: the Former Lord's taboo name Bei, its gloss is 'complete'; the Later Lord's taboo name Shan, its gloss is 'hand over'; as if saying the Liu house is already complete and should be handed to another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiang Chong said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's remark—the Former Lord's taboo name Bei means 'complete,' and the Later Lord's taboo name Shan means 'hand over,' as though the Liu house were finished and due to be handed on.

manualTranslations.zh: 今中抚军名炎，而汉年极於炎兴，瑞出成都，而藏之於相国府，此殆天意也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, and the Han years end in Yanxing; the omen appeared at Chengdu yet is stored in the chancellor's mansion—this is perhaps heaven's intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, Han's years end in Yanxing, the omen appeared at Chengdu and was stored in the chancellor's mansion—surely this is heaven's intent.

manualTranslations.zh: "是岁，拜充为梓潼太守，明年十二月而晋武帝即尊位，炎兴於是乎徵焉。
manualTranslations.literal: "That year Chong was appointed Administrator of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin assumed the exalted position, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "That year Xiang Chong was appointed governor of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.

manualTranslations.zh: 孙盛曰：昔公孙自以起成都，号曰成氏，二玉之文，殆述所作乎！

sourceRange.text: 先主既稱尊號，征吳不克，還住永安。漢嘉太守黃元素為諸葛亮所不善，聞先主疾病，懼有後患，舉郡反，燒臨邛城。時亮東行省疾，成都單虛，是以元益無所憚。洪即啟太子，遣其親兵，使將軍陳曶、鄭綽討元。眾議以為元若不能圍成都，當由越囗據南中。洪曰：「元素信凶暴，無他恩信，何能辦此？不過乘水東下，冀主上平安，面縛歸死；如其有異，奔吳求活耳。敕曶、綽但於南安峽口遮即便得矣。」曶、綽承洪言，果生獲元。洪建興元年223年賜爵關內侯，復為蜀郡太守、忠節將軍，後為越騎校尉，領郡如故。

manualTranslations.zh: 漢嘉太守黃元素為諸葛亮所不善，聞先主疾病，懼有後患，舉郡反，燒臨邛城。
manualTranslations.literal: Huang Yuan, Administrator of Hanjia, was ill regarded by Zhuge Liang; hearing the Former Lord was ill, he feared future trouble, raised the whole commandery in rebellion, and burned Linqiong city.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huang Yuan, governor of Hanjia, had fallen foul of Zhuge Liang; hearing Liu Bei was gravely ill, he feared what might follow, rebelled across the district, and burned Linqiong.

manualTranslations.zh: 時亮東行省疾，成都單虛，是以元益無所憚。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Liang was traveling east to attend to the illness; Chengdu stood largely empty, and Yuan therefore grew all the more brazen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was then away east tending the emperor's illness; Chengdu lay nearly bare, and Yuan grew bolder.

manualTranslations.zh: 洪即啟太子，遣其親兵，使將軍陳曶、鄭綽討元。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong immediately notified the Crown Prince, dispatched his personal troops, and had Generals Chen Hu and Zheng Chuo punish Yuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yang Hong immediately alerted the crown prince, sent his personal guard, and had Generals Chen Hu and Zheng Chuo attack Huang Yuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 眾議以為元若不能圍成都，當由越囗據南中。
manualTranslations.literal: The multitude in council held that if Yuan could not encircle Chengdu, he would pass through Yuexi and seize the southern interior.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Most advisers thought that if Yuan could not take Chengdu he would head through Yuexi into the southern tribes.

manualTranslations.zh: 洪曰：「元素信凶暴，無他恩信，何能辦此？
manualTranslations.literal: Hong said: "Yuan by nature is fierce and violent, without other kindness and trust—how could he accomplish this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong said: "Yuan is brutal by nature, with no other hold over men—how could he manage that?

manualTranslations.zh: 不過乘水東下，冀主上平安，面縛歸死；
manualTranslations.literal: He would only ride the waters east, hoping the sovereign above would be safe and well, then come bound to die;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He will only flee downriver, hoping the emperor recovers so he can bind himself and await death;

manualTranslations.zh: 如其有異，奔吳求活耳。
manualTranslations.literal: if he has other intent, he will run to Wu to seek life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if not, he will flee to Wu for his life.

manualTranslations.zh: 敕曶、綽但於南安峽口遮即便得矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Only order Hu and Chuo to intercept at Nan'an Gorge, and he can be taken at once."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Simply have Hu and Chuo ambush him at Nan'an Gorge and he is ours."

manualTranslations.zh: 曶、綽承洪言，果生獲元。
manualTranslations.literal: Hu and Chuo followed Hong's words; indeed they captured Yuan alive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hu and Chuo followed Hong's plan and captured Yuan alive.

sourceRange.text: 」李譔字欽仲，梓潼涪人也。父仁，字德賢，與同縣尹默懼遊荊州，從司馬徽、宋忠等學。譔具傳其業，又默講論義理，五經、諸子，無不該覽，加博好技藝，算術、卜數，醫藥、弓弩、機械之巧，皆致思焉。始為州書佐、尚書令史。延熙元年238年，後主立太子，以譔為庶子，遷為僕射，轉中散大夫、右中郎將，猶侍太子。太子愛其多知，甚悅之。然體輕脫，好戲啁，故世不能重也。著古文《易》、《尚書》、《毛詩》、《三禮》、《左氏傳》、《太玄指歸》，皆依準賈、馬，異於鄭玄。與王氏殊隔，初不見其所述，而意歸多同。景耀中卒。時又有漢中陳術，字申伯，亦博學多聞，著《釋部》七篇、《益部耆舊傳》及《志》，位歷三郡太守。

manualTranslations.literal: Zuan fully transmitted his father's craft; moreover Mo lectured on principles of meaning—the Five Classics and various masters, none not covered in reading—additionally broadly loved skills and arts: calculation, divination, medicine, bow and crossbow, mechanical ingenuity—all he devoted thought to.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zuan fully inherited his father's learning, while Yin Mo lectured on doctrine; he read the Five Classics and all the masters, and also pursued arithmetic, divination, medicine, archery, and mechanical arts with equal zeal.

manualTranslations.zh: 始為州書佐、尚書令史。
manualTranslations.literal: At first served as provincial clerk and Secretariat recorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He first served as a provincial clerk and Secretariat recorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 延熙元年238年，後主立太子，以譔為庶子，遷為僕射，轉中散大夫、右中郎將，猶侍太子。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yanxi (238), the Later Lord installed the crown prince and appointed Zuan as junior tutor; he was promoted to steward, then transferred to palace attendant and right commander of the gentlemen of the interior, still attending the crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 238, when the Later Ruler established the crown prince, Zuan was made junior tutor, then promoted to steward, palace attendant, and right commander of the gentlemen of the interior, continuing to attend the heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 太子愛其多知，甚悅之。
manualTranslations.literal: The crown prince loved his great knowledge and was very pleased with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The crown prince delighted in his wide learning and favored him greatly.

manualTranslations.zh: 然體輕脫，好戲啁，故世不能重也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet his bearing was light and unserious; he loved jesting and mockery—therefore the age could not esteem him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he was frivolous and fond of banter, so the world could not take him seriously.

manualTranslations.zh: 著古文《易》、《尚書》、《毛詩》、《三禮》、《左氏傳》、《太玄指歸》，皆依準賈、馬，異於鄭玄。
manualTranslations.literal: He authored Old Text commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Three Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Directions to the Supreme Mystery—all following Jia and Ma, differing from Zheng Xuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He wrote Old Text commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Three Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Directions to the Supreme Mystery, following Jia Kui and Ma Rong rather than Zheng Xuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 與王氏殊隔，初不見其所述，而意歸多同。
manualTranslations.literal: With the Wang lineage he was utterly separate; at first he did not see what they expounded, yet the intent returned mostly the same.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had no contact with the Wang school and had not read their commentaries, yet his conclusions largely agreed with theirs.

manualTranslations.zh: 景耀中卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in the Jingyao era.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died during the Jingyao reign.

manualTranslations.zh: 時又有漢中陳術，字申伯，亦博學多聞，著《釋部》七篇、《益部耆舊傳》及《志》，位歷三郡太守。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time there was also Chen Shu of Hanzhong, courtesy name Shenbo, likewise broad in learning and famed in hearing; he authored seven chapters of Explanatory Categories, Records of Elders of Yibu, and a Gazetteer, and his posts spanned three commandery governorships.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: About the same time Chen Shu of Hanzhong, styled Shenbo, was also widely learned; he wrote seven chapters of Explanatory Categories, Records of Elders of Yibu, and a gazetteer, and served as governor of three commanderies.

sourceRange.text: 李恢字德昂，建寧俞元人也，仕郡督郵，姑夫爨習為建伶令，有違犯之事，恢坐習免官。太守董和以習方土大姓，寢而不許。《華陽國志》曰：習後官至領軍。後貢恢於州，涉道末至，聞先主自葭萌還攻劉璋。恢知璋之必敗，先主必成也，乃託名郡使，北詣先主，遇於綿竹。先主嘉之，從至洛城，遣恢至漢中交好馬超，超遂從命。成都既定，先主領益州牧，以恢為功曹書佐、主簿。後為亡虜所誣，引恢謀反，有司執送。先主明其不然，更遷恢為別駕從事。章武元年，庲降都督鄧方卒，先主問恢：「誰可代者？」恢對曰：「人之才能，各有長短，故孔子曰『其使人也器之』。且夫明主在上，則臣下盡情，是以先零之役，趙充國曰『莫若老臣』。臣竊不自量，惟陛下察之。」先主笑曰：「孤之本意，亦已在卿矣！」遂以恢為庲降都督，使持節領交州刺史，住平夷縣。臣松之訊之蜀人，云庲降地名，去蜀二千餘里，時未有寧州，號為南中，立此職以總攝之。晉泰始中，始分為寧州。

context.beforeSource: 會艾長驅而前，瞻卻戰綿竹，祟帥厲軍士，期於必死，臨陣見殺。
context.afterSource: 先主薨，高定恣睢於越巂，雍闓跋扈於建寧，朱褒反叛於牂牁。

manualTranslations.zh: 李恢字德昂，建寧俞元人也，仕郡督郵，姑夫爨習為建伶令，有違犯之事，恢坐習免官。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Hui, courtesy name De'ang, was a man of Yuyuan in Jianning. He served as commandery postal inspector. His uncle by marriage Cuan Xi was chief of Jianling; when Xi committed offenses, Hui was implicated and dismissed from office because of Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Hui, styled De'ang, came from Yuyuan in Jianning Commandery. He served as the commandery postal inspector. His uncle by marriage Cuan Xi was magistrate of Jianling; when Xi committed offenses, Hui was dismissed from office on account of Xi.

manualTranslations.zh: 太守董和以習方土大姓，寢而不許。
manualTranslations.literal: Administrator Dong He, because Xi was a great clan of the region, shelved the matter and would not approve [the dismissal].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Administrator Dong He, considering Xi a leading local clan, set the matter aside and refused to approve it.

manualTranslations.zh: 《華陽國志》曰：習後官至領軍。
manualTranslations.literal: The Huayang guo zhi states: Xi later reached office as leader of the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Huayang guo zhi notes that Xi later rose to leader of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 後貢恢於州，涉道末至，聞先主自葭萌還攻劉璋。
manualTranslations.literal: Later [the commandery] recommended Hui to the province. He was on the road but had not yet arrived when he heard that the First Sovereign had returned from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The commandery later recommended Hui to the provincial government. While still on the road he learned that Liu Bei had marched back from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 恢知璋之必敗，先主必成也，乃託名郡使，北詣先主，遇於綿竹。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui knew Zhang would certainly be defeated and the First Sovereign would certainly prevail; therefore he posed as a commandery envoy, went north to the First Sovereign, and met him at Mianzhu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing that Liu Zhang was doomed and Liu Bei would prevail, Hui posed as a commandery envoy, went north to meet Liu Bei, and encountered him at Mianzhu.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主嘉之，從至洛城，遣恢至漢中交好馬超，超遂從命。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign praised him. [Hui] followed him to Luocheng, and the First Sovereign sent Hui to Hanzhong to cultivate friendship with Ma Chao; Chao thereupon followed his orders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was pleased and took him along to Luocheng, then sent him to Hanzhong to win over Ma Chao, who thereupon submitted.

manualTranslations.zh: 成都既定，先主領益州牧，以恢為功曹書佐、主簿。
manualTranslations.literal: When Chengdu was settled, the First Sovereign took charge as Governor of Yi Province and appointed Hui recorder-clerk and chief registrar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell Liu Bei became governor of Yi Province and named Hui recorder-clerk and chief registrar.

manualTranslations.zh: 後為亡虜所誣，引恢謀反，有司執送。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he was slandered by defeated enemies who implicated Hui in plotting rebellion; the authorities arrested and sent him [to the capital].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later defeated enemies accused him of plotting rebellion; officials arrested him and sent him up for trial.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主明其不然，更遷恢為別駕從事。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign knew this was not so and transferred Hui to the post of vice administrator attendant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei knew the charge was false and reassigned him as vice administrator attendant.

manualTranslations.zh: 章武元年，庲降都督鄧方卒，先主問恢：「誰可代者？」
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhangwu, Area Commander of Laixiang Deng Fang died. The First Sovereign asked Hui: "Who can replace him?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhangwu 1, Laixiang area commander Deng Fang died. Liu Bei asked Li Hui, "Who should succeed him?"

manualTranslations.zh: 恢對曰：「人之才能，各有長短，故孔子曰『其使人也器之』。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui replied: "Human talent each has strengths and shortcomings; therefore Confucius said, 'He employs men according to their capacities.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Hui answered, "Every man has his strengths and limits, as Confucius said: 'He employs men according to their capacities.'"

manualTranslations.zh: 且夫明主在上，則臣下盡情，是以先零之役，趙充國曰『莫若老臣』。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, when an enlightened lord is above, then ministers below give their full effort; thus in the campaign against the Xianling, Zhao Chongguo said, "None is better than this old minister."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the ruler is wise, ministers serve wholeheartedly—at the Xianling campaign Zhao Chongguo said, "None is better than this old minister."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣竊不自量，惟陛下察之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant ventures not to measure himself; may Your Majesty examine it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I hardly dare measure myself against the task; may Your Majesty judge."

manualTranslations.zh: 先主笑曰：「孤之本意，亦已在卿矣！」
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign laughed and said: "My original intent was already upon you, sir!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei laughed and said, "You were already in my mind!"

manualTranslations.zh: 遂以恢為庲降都督，使持節領交州刺史，住平夷縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Hui Area Commander of Laixiang, granted him credential insignia and concurrent office as Inspector of Jiao Province, and stationed him at Pingyi County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then made Li Hui area commander at Laixiang with credential insignia and concurrent rank as inspector of Jiao Province, stationed at Pingyi County.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之訊之蜀人，云庲降地名，去蜀二千餘里，時未有寧州，號為南中，立此職以總攝之。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi inquired of Shu people, who said Laixiang is a place name more than two thousand li from Shu; at that time there was not yet Ning Province—it was called the Southern Center—and this office was established to oversee it in general.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi asked Shu natives and learned that Laixiang was a place name more than two thousand li from Shu; Ning Province did not yet exist—the region was called the Southern Center—and this post was created to govern it.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉泰始中，始分為寧州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Taishi era of Jin it was first divided off as Ning Province.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Taishi reign it was first carved out as Ning Province.

sourceRange.text: 呂凱字季平，永昌不韋人也，孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：初，秦徙呂不韋子弟宗族於蜀漢。漢武帝時，開西南夷，置郡縣，徙呂氏以充之，因曰不韋縣。仕郡五官掾、功曹。時雍闓等聞先主薨於永安，驕黠滋甚。都護李嚴與闓書六紙，解喻利害，闓但答一紙曰：「蓋聞天無二日，土無二王，今天下鼎立，正朔有三，是以遠人惶惑，不知所歸也。」其桀慢如此。闓又降於吳，吳遙署凱為永昌太守。永昌既在益州郡之西，道路壅塞，與蜀隔絕，而郡太守改易。凱與府丞蜀郡王伉帥厲吏民，閉境拒闓。闓數移檄永昌，稱說云云。凱答檄曰：天降喪亂，奸雄乘釁，天下切齒，萬國悲悼，臣妾大小，莫不思竭筋力，肝腦塗地，以除國難。

manualTranslations.zh: 呂凱字季平，永昌不韋人也，孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：初，秦徙呂不韋子弟宗族於蜀漢。
manualTranslations.literal: Lü Kai, courtesy name Jiping, was a man of Buwei in Yongchang. Sun Sheng's Shu shifu states: At first Qin relocated the sons, younger brothers, and clansmen of Lü Buwei to Shu-Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Kai, styled Jiping, came from Buwei in Yongchang Commandery. Sun Sheng's Shu shifu records that Qin first relocated Lü Buwei's kin to Shu-Han.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢武帝時，開西南夷，置郡縣，徙呂氏以充之，因曰不韋縣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Han, when the southwestern Yi were opened and commanderies and counties were established, the Lü clan was moved to fill them; therefore [the place] was called Buwei County.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han, when the southwest was opened and counties were established, the Lü clan was settled there and the county took the name Buwei.

manualTranslations.zh: 仕郡五官掾、功曹。
manualTranslations.literal: He served as the commandery's five-offices clerk and merit clerk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served as the commandery's five-offices clerk and merit clerk.

manualTranslations.zh: 時雍闓等聞先主薨於永安，驕黠滋甚。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Yong Kai and others heard that the First Sovereign had died at Yong'an; they grew ever more arrogant and cunning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yong Kai and his allies learned that Liu Bei had died at Yong'an, they grew bolder and more insolent.

manualTranslations.zh: 都護李嚴與闓書六紙，解喻利害，闓但答一紙曰：「蓋聞天無二日，土無二王，今天下鼎立，正朔有三，是以遠人惶惑，不知所歸也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Chief Controller Li Yan sent Kai six sheets of correspondence explaining advantages and harms; Kai replied with only one sheet, saying: "I have heard that heaven has no two suns and earth has no two kings. Now the realm stands like a tripod and there are three orthodox calendars; therefore distant men are fearful and confused and do not know where to turn."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chief Controller Li Yan sent Yong Kai six letters explaining the stakes; Kai answered with one: "Heaven has but one sun and earth but one king. With three rival calendars abroad, frontier folk are lost and do not know whom to follow."

manualTranslations.zh: 其桀慢如此。
manualTranslations.literal: His arrogance and insolence were like this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such was his arrogance.

manualTranslations.zh: 闓又降於吳，吳遙署凱為永昌太守。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai again submitted to Wu, and Wu at a distance appointed Kai Administrator of Yongchang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yong Kai then submitted to Wu, which at a distance named Lü Kai administrator of Yongchang.

manualTranslations.zh: 永昌既在益州郡之西，道路壅塞，與蜀隔絕，而郡太守改易。
manualTranslations.literal: Yongchang lay west of Yi Province; the roads were blocked and cut off from Shu, and the commandery administrator was changed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yongchang lay west of Yi Province; roads were blocked and Shu was cut off, while the commandery magistrate had been replaced.

manualTranslations.zh: 凱與府丞蜀郡王伉帥厲吏民，閉境拒闓。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai with assistant administrator Wang Kang of Shu Commandery led and exhorted officials and people, closed the borders, and resisted Kai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Kai and assistant administrator Wang Kang of Shu Commandery rallied officials and people, sealed the borders, and refused Yong Kai.

manualTranslations.zh: 闓數移檄永昌，稱說云云。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai repeatedly issued proclamations to Yongchang, making claims of every sort.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yong Kai sent manifesto after manifesto to Yongchang full of grand claims.

manualTranslations.zh: 凱答檄曰：天降喪亂，奸雄乘釁，天下切齒，萬國悲悼，臣妾大小，莫不思竭筋力，肝腦塗地，以除國難。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai answered the proclamation, saying: Heaven has sent mourning and chaos; treacherous heroes seize every opening; all under heaven gnash their teeth; myriad states grieve; subjects great and small—none do not wish to exhaust sinew and strength and smear liver and brains on the ground to remove the state's calamity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Kai answered the manifesto: "Heaven has sent calamity; usurpers exploit every crack; all under heaven grit their teeth in grief. Every subject longs to spend sinew and blood to lift the nation's woes."

sourceRange.text: 先主為漢中王，猶領益州牧，以權為治中從事，及稱尊號，將東伐吳，權諫曰：「吳人悍戰，又水軍順流，進易退難，臣請為先驅以當寇，陛下宜為後鎮。」先主不從，以權為鎮北將軍，督江北軍以防魏師。先主自在江南。及吳將軍陸議乘流斷圍，南軍敗績，先主引退。而道隔絕，權不得還，故率將所領降於魏。有司執法，白收權妻子。先主曰：「孤負黃權，權不負孤也。」待之如初。臣松之以為漢武用虛罔之言，滅李陵之家，劉主拒憲司所執，宥黃權之室，二主得失縣邈遠矣。詩云「樂只君子，保艾爾後」，其劉主之謂也。魏文帝謂權曰：「君捨逆效順，欲追從陳、韓邪？」權對曰：「臣過受劉主殊遇，降吳不可。還蜀無路，是以歸命。且敗軍之將，免死為幸，何古人之可慕也！」文帝善之，拜為鎮南將軍，封育陽候，加侍中，使之陪乘。蜀降人或云誅權妻子，權知其虛言，未便發喪，《漢魏春秋》曰：文帝詔令發喪，權答曰：「臣與劉、葛推誠相信，明臣本志。疑惑未實，請須後問。」後得審問，果如所言。及先主薨問至，魏群臣咸賀而權獨否。文帝察權有局量，欲試驚之，遣左右詔權，末至之間，累催相屬，馬使奔馳，交錯於道，官屬侍從莫不辟魄，而權舉止顏色自若。

context.beforeSource: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。
context.afterSource: 後領益州刺史，徙佔河南。

manualTranslations.zh: 先主為漢中王，猶領益州牧，以權為治中從事，及稱尊號，將東伐吳，權諫曰：「吳人悍戰，又水軍順流，進易退難，臣請為先驅以當寇，陛下宜為後鎮。」
manualTranslations.literal: When the First Sovereign became King of Hanzhong he still concurrently held the governorship of Yi Province and appointed Quan director of the headquarters staff. When he assumed the imperial title and was about to campaign east against Wu, Quan remonstrated, saying: "Wu men fight fiercely, and with the navy flowing downstream advance is easy but retreat is hard. Your servant asks to serve as vanguard to meet the enemy; Your Majesty should hold the rear guard."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong while still governing Yi Province, he named Huang Quan director of the headquarters staff. As he prepared to march east against Wu after taking the imperial title, Huang Quan urged, "Wu fighters are fierce and the fleet has the current at its back—advance is easy, retreat hard. Let me lead the vanguard while Your Majesty holds the rear."

manualTranslations.zh: 先主不從，以權為鎮北將軍，督江北軍以防魏師。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign did not follow [his advice] and appointed Quan General Who Guards the North, supervising the army north of the river to guard against Wei forces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei refused and made him general who guards the north, commanding troops north of the Yangzi against Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主自在江南。
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign himself was south of the river.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei himself remained south of the Yangzi.

manualTranslations.zh: 及吳將軍陸議乘流斷圍，南軍敗績，先主引退。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wu General Lu Yi exploited the current to cut off the encirclement, the southern army suffered defeat and the First Sovereign withdrew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wu general Lu Yi used the current to sever the encirclement, the southern army was routed and Liu Bei pulled back.

manualTranslations.zh: 而道隔絕，權不得還，故率將所領降於魏。
manualTranslations.literal: But the roads were cut off and Quan could not return; therefore he led the troops he commanded and submitted to Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cut off from retreat, Huang Quan led his command and surrendered to Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 有司執法，白收權妻子。
manualTranslations.literal: The authorities enforced the law and reported that Quan's wife and children should be seized.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials invoked the law and urged seizing Huang Quan's family.

manualTranslations.zh: 先主曰：「孤負黃權，權不負孤也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The First Sovereign said: "I failed Huang Quan; Huang Quan did not fail me."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said, "I failed Huang Quan; Huang Quan did not fail me."

manualTranslations.zh: 待之如初。
manualTranslations.literal: They were treated as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His family was treated as before.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以為漢武用虛罔之言，滅李陵之家，劉主拒憲司所執，宥黃權之室，二主得失縣邈遠矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Han Wudi believed empty false words and destroyed Li Ling's household, while Lord Liu rejected what the law officers urged and pardoned Huang Quan's household—the gains and losses of the two lords are vastly far apart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that Han Wudi believed slander and destroyed Li Ling's family, while Liu Bei rejected the prosecutors and spared Huang Quan's household—a vast gulf between the two rulers.

manualTranslations.zh: 詩云「樂只君子，保艾爾後」，其劉主之謂也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Odes say, "How blessed the gentleman—may he protect and comfort your posterity"; this applies to Lord Liu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Happy is the noble lord who shelters your heirs"—that fits Liu Bei.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏文帝謂權曰：「君捨逆效順，欲追從陳、韓邪？」
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei said to Quan: "Sir, you abandoned rebellion and turned to obedience—do you wish to follow Chen and Han?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei asked Huang Quan, "You abandoned rebellion for loyalty—do you mean to rival Chen Ping and Han Xin?"

manualTranslations.zh: 權對曰：「臣過受劉主殊遇，降吳不可。
manualTranslations.literal: Quan replied: "Your servant excessively received special favor from Lord Liu; to submit to Wu was impossible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huang Quan answered, "I owed Liu Bei extraordinary favor and could not submit to Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 還蜀無路，是以歸命。
manualTranslations.literal: To return to Shu there was no road; therefore I submitted my allegiance [to Wei].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With no road back to Shu, I turned to Wei."

manualTranslations.zh: 且敗軍之將，免死為幸，何古人之可慕也！」
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, a defeated army's general—escape from death is fortune; what ancients are there to admire!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A beaten general is lucky to live—what ancient hero should I emulate?"

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝善之，拜為鎮南將軍，封育陽候，加侍中，使之陪乘。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen approved of this, appointed him General Who Guards the South, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuyang, added him as Palace Attendant, and had him ride in the accompanying chariot.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Pi was pleased, named him general who guards the south, enfeoffed him as marquis of Yuyang, made him palace attendant, and had him ride in the imperial escort.

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀降人或云誅權妻子，權知其虛言，未便發喪，《漢魏春秋》曰：文帝詔令發喪，權答曰：「臣與劉、葛推誠相信，明臣本志。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu surrenderers said Quan's wife and children had been executed; Quan knew this was empty talk and did not yet hold mourning. The Han-Wei chunqiu states: Emperor Wen ordered mourning to be proclaimed. Quan replied: "Your servant and Liu and Zhuge extend sincerity and trust one another; they understand your servant's original intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shu defectors claimed Huang Quan's family had been executed; he knew it was rumor and would not mourn. The Han-Wei chunqiu records that Cao Pi ordered mourning proclaimed. Huang Quan replied, "Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang know my heart and trust me.

manualTranslations.zh: 疑惑未實，請須後問。」
manualTranslations.literal: The doubt is not yet verified; I ask to await further inquiry."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Until the facts are clear, I beg to wait for confirmation."

manualTranslations.zh: 後得審問，果如所言。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he obtained careful inquiry; it was indeed as stated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later inquiry proved the report false.

manualTranslations.zh: 及先主薨問至，魏群臣咸賀而權獨否。
manualTranslations.literal: When news arrived of the First Sovereign's death, all Wei ministers congratulated [Cao Pi], but Quan alone did not.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When word of Liu Bei's death arrived, Wei ministers congratulated Cao Pi, but Huang Quan alone did not.

manualTranslations.zh: 文帝察權有局量，欲試驚之，遣左右詔權，末至之間，累催相屬，馬使奔馳，交錯於道，官屬侍從莫不辟魄，而權舉止顏色自若。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen perceived that Quan had composure and breadth, wished to test and startle him, and sent attendants to summon Quan. Before [the summons] arrived, repeated urgent orders followed one after another; mounted messengers galloped, crisscrossing on the road. Officials and attendants were all terrified, yet Quan's bearing and complexion remained as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Pi saw Huang Quan's composure and tested him with repeated urgent summons, messengers galloping past one another until attendants trembled—yet Huang Quan's bearing never changed.
