manualTranslations.zh: 」徐州牧陶謙深忌策。
manualTranslations.literal: The Governor of Xu Province, Tao Qian, deeply envied Ce.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tao Qian, Governor of Xu Province, deeply resented Sun Ce.

manualTranslations.zh: 策舅呉景，時爲丹楊太守，策乃載母徙曲阿，與呂範，孫河俱就景。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce's maternal uncle Wu Jing was then Administrator of Danyang; Ce then carried his mother and moved to Qu'a, and with Lü Fan and Sun He together went to Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce's uncle Wu Jing was then Administrator of Danyang. Sun Ce moved his mother to Qu'a and went with Lü Fan and Sun He to join Wu Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 因緣召募得數百人。
manualTranslations.literal: By opportunity he recruited and obtained several hundred men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of local connections, he recruited several hundred men.

manualTranslations.zh: 興平元年194年，從袁術。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Xingping, 194, he followed Yuan Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xingping 1 (194), he joined Yuan Shu.

manualTranslations.zh: 術甚奇之，以堅部曲還策。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu greatly marveled at him and returned to Ce the troops of Jian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu was greatly impressed and returned Sun Jian's former troops to Sun Ce.

manualTranslations.zh: 呉暦曰：「初策在江都時，張紘有母喪。
manualTranslations.literal: Wu Li says: 'At first when Ce was at Jiangdu, Zhang Hong was in mourning for his mother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Li records: "When Sun Ce was at Jiangdu, Zhang Hong was in mourning for his mother.

manualTranslations.zh: 策數詣紘，咨以世務，曰：『方今漢祚中微，天下擾攘，英雄俊傑各擁衆營私，未有能扶危濟亂者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce repeatedly visited Hong and consulted him on affairs of the age, saying: 'Now the fortune of Han is in mid-decline; the realm is in turmoil; heroes and outstanding men each hold troops and pursue private ends—there is none able to support the endangered and rescue disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce visited Zhang Hong repeatedly to consult him on public affairs, saying, 'The Han dynasty is in decline, the realm is in turmoil, and heroes and men of talent each hold troops for private ends. None can rescue the state from crisis.

manualTranslations.zh: 先君與袁氏共破董卓，功業未遂，卒爲黃祖所害。
manualTranslations.literal: My late father together with the Yuan clan broke Dong Zhuo; his achievement was not completed, and in the end he was harmed by Huang Zu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My late father joined the Yuan clan in defeating Dong Zhuo, but his mission was cut short when Huang Zu killed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 策雖暗稚，竊有微志，欲從袁揚州求先君餘兵，就舅氏於丹楊，收合流散，東據呉會，報讎雪恥，爲朝廷外籓。
manualTranslations.literal: Although Ce is young and immature, he secretly has a slight ambition: he wishes to go to Governor of Yang Province Yuan to request my late father's remaining troops, join my maternal uncle in Danyang, gather the scattered, hold Wu and Kuaiji in the east, avenge wrongs and wipe away shame, and be an outer bulwark for the court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though I am young and inexperienced, I harbor a modest ambition: to ask Yuan Shu for my father's remaining troops, join my uncle in Danyang, gather scattered forces, seize Wu and Kuaiji in the east, avenge my father, and serve the court as a frontier bulwark.

manualTranslations.zh: 君以爲何如？』
manualTranslations.literal: What does my lord think?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What do you think?'

manualTranslations.zh: 紘答曰：『旣素空劣，方居衰絰之中，無以奉贊盛略。』
manualTranslations.literal: Hong answered: 'Being by nature empty and inferior, and just now in the midst of mourning garb, I have no means to serve and assist a grand design.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong replied, 'I am a man of little talent, and I am still in mourning. I have nothing to offer such a grand plan.'

manualTranslations.zh: 策曰：『君高名播越，遠近懷歸。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce said: 'My lord's lofty name spreads far; near and far yearn to return to you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, 'Your reputation is far-reaching, and men near and far look to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 今日事計，決之於君，何得不紆慮啓告，副其高山之望？
manualTranslations.literal: Today's plan is decided by my lord—how can you not bend your thoughts and open and tell, matching the hope placed in one of lofty mountain stature?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's decision rests with you. How can you withhold your counsel and fail the hopes men place in you?

manualTranslations.zh: 若微志得展，血讎得報，此乃君之勛力，策心所望也。』
manualTranslations.literal: If my slight ambition can be fulfilled and blood vengeance obtained, this will be my lord's meritorious effort—what Ce's heart hopes for.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If my humble ambition succeeds and my father's blood debt is paid, that will be your achievement, and it is what I most desire.'

manualTranslations.zh: 因涕泣橫流，顔色不變。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon tears flowed freely, yet his countenance did not change.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As he spoke, tears streamed down his face, yet his expression did not change.

manualTranslations.zh: 紘見策忠壯內發，辭令慷慨，感其志言，乃答曰：『昔周道陵遲，齊晉並興；
manualTranslations.literal: Hong saw Ce's loyalty and valor welling within, his words and commands impassioned; moved by his intent and speech, he then answered: 'Formerly the Way of Zhou declined; Qi and Jin both rose together;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong saw Sun Ce's loyal fervor and impassioned speech, was moved by his purpose, and answered, 'In antiquity when the Zhou dynasty declined, Qi and Jin rose together;

manualTranslations.zh: 王室已寧，諸侯貢職。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the royal house was settled, the feudal lords paid tribute and performed duty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: once the royal house was secure, the feudal lords resumed their tribute duties.

manualTranslations.zh: 今君紹先侯之軌，有驍武之名，若投丹楊，收兵呉會，則荆揚可一，讎敵可報。
manualTranslations.literal: Now my lord follows the track of the former marquis and has a name for fierce valor; if you go to Danyang and gather troops in Wu and Kuaiji, then Jing and Yang can be united and the enemy of vengeance can be repaid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You follow your father's path and bear a name for martial prowess. If you go to Danyang and gather forces in Wu and Kuaiji, you can unite Jing and Yang and avenge your enemy.

manualTranslations.zh: 據長江，奮威德，誅除群穢，匡輔漢室，功業侔於桓文，豈徒外籓而已哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Hold the Yangzi, exert authority and virtue, execute and remove the multitude of filth, support and assist the house of Han—achievement matching Huan and Wen; how could it be merely an outer bulwark?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hold the Yangzi River, wield authority and virtue, purge the corrupt, and restore the Han house. Your achievement could rival Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi. How could that be merely a frontier post?

manualTranslations.zh: 方今世亂多難，若功成事立，當與同好俱南濟也。』
manualTranslations.literal: Just now the age is disorderly with many hardships; if achievement is completed and affairs established, I should together with those of like mind cross south to aid.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These are troubled times. If you succeed, I shall cross south with you and like-minded men to do our part.'

manualTranslations.zh: 策曰：『一與君同符合契，
manualTranslations.literal: Ce said: 'Once with my lord sharing tally and covenant,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, 'From this moment we share the same purpose,

manualTranslations.literal: (same)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (same)

manualTranslations.zh: 有永固之分，今便行矣，以老母弱弟委付於君，策無復回顧之憂。』」
manualTranslations.literal: there is an everlasting bond; now I shall depart at once. Entrusting my aged mother and young brother to my lord, Ce will have no further worry of looking back.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: with an enduring bond between us. I depart at once, leaving my mother and young brother in your care, and I shall have no further worries.'"

manualTranslations.zh: 江表傳曰：「策徑到壽春見袁術，涕泣而言曰：『亡父昔從長沙入討董卓，與明使君會於南陽，同盟結好；
manualTranslations.literal: Jiang Biao Zhuan says: 'Ce went straight to Shouchun to see Yuan Shu, weeping as he spoke, saying: 'My deceased father formerly came from Changsha to join the campaign against Dong Zhuo; he met the Illustrious Envoy at Nanyang and formed alliance and friendship;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Biao Zhuan records: "Sun Ce went directly to Shouchun to see Yuan Shu and, weeping, said, 'My late father came from Changsha to campaign against Dong Zhuo, met Your Excellency at Nanyang, and formed an alliance;

manualTranslations.zh: 不幸遇難，勛業不終。
manualTranslations.literal: Unhappily he met disaster; his meritorious work was not completed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: unhappily he met disaster and his mission was left unfinished.

manualTranslations.zh: 策感惟先人舊恩，欲自憑結，原明使君垂察其誠。』
manualTranslations.literal: Ce, moved by remembrance of the former kindness of our forebear, wishes to rely on and bind himself; I pray the Illustrious Envoy will look down and examine his sincerity.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moved by my father's old bond with you, I wish to place myself under your patronage. I pray you will look upon my sincerity.'

manualTranslations.zh: 術甚貴異之，然未肯還其父兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu greatly honored and marveled at him, yet was unwilling to return his father's troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu held him in high regard but would not return his father's troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 術謂策曰：『孤始用貴舅爲丹楊太守，賢從伯陽爲都尉，彼精兵之地，可還依召募。』
manualTranslations.literal: Shu said to Ce: 'I have just employed your honored uncle as Administrator of Danyang and your worthy clansman Boyang as Commandant—that is a land of picked troops; you may return and rely on it to recruit.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu told Sun Ce, 'I have just appointed your uncle Administrator of Danyang and your kinsman Boyang as Commandant. That is rich in troops. You may return there to recruit.'

manualTranslations.zh: 策遂詣丹楊依舅，得數百人，而爲涇縣大帥祖郎所襲，幾至危殆。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce then went to Danyang to rely on his uncle and obtained several hundred men, but was attacked by Zu Lang, chief bandit of Jing County, and nearly reached peril.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce then went to Danyang to join his uncle and gathered several hundred men, but was attacked by Zu Lang, the bandit chief of Jing County, and nearly perished.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是復往見術，術以堅餘兵千餘人還策。」
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he again went to see Shu; Shu returned to Ce more than a thousand of Jian's remaining troops.'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then returned to Yuan Shu, who at last returned to him more than a thousand of Sun Jian's remaining troops."

manualTranslations.zh: 太傅馬日磾杖節安集關東，在壽春以禮辟策，表拜懷義校尉，術大將喬蕤、張勳皆傾心敬焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Tutor Ma Midi, bearing the staff to pacify and gather the east, at Shouchun ceremonially recruited Ce and memorialized to appoint him Colonel Who Cherishes Righteousness; Yuan Shu's great generals Qiao Rui and Zhang Xun all gave their hearts and showed respect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Ma Midi, bearing imperial credentials to pacify the east, ceremonially recruited Sun Ce at Shouchun and memorialized his appointment as Colonel Who Cherishes Righteousness. Yuan Shu's senior generals Qiao Rui and Zhang Xun all respected him warmly.

manualTranslations.zh: 術常歎曰：「使術有子如孫郎，死復何恨！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shu often sighed, saying: 'If Shu had a son like Master Sun, what regret would there be in death!'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu often sighed, "If I had a son like Master Sun, I could die without regret!"

manualTranslations.zh: 策騎士有罪，逃入術營，隱於內廄。
manualTranslations.literal: A cavalryman of Ce committed an offense, fled into Shu's camp, and hid in the inner stable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One of Sun Ce's horsemen committed a crime, fled into Yuan Shu's camp, and hid in the inner stables.

manualTranslations.zh: 策指使人就斬之，訖，詣術謝。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce pointed and sent men to go and behead him; when finished, he went to Shu to apologize.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent men to execute him on the spot, then went to Yuan Shu to apologize.

manualTranslations.zh: 術曰：「兵人好叛，當共疾之，何爲謝也？」
manualTranslations.literal: Shu said: 'Soldiers are prone to rebellion; we should together abhor it—why apologize?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu said, "Soldiers are prone to desertion. We should despise that together. Why apologize?"

manualTranslations.zh: 由是軍中益畏憚之。
manualTranslations.literal: From this the army increasingly feared and respected him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From then on the army feared and respected him all the more.

manualTranslations.zh: 術初許策爲九江太守，已而更用丹楊陳紀。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu at first promised Ce the post of Administrator of Jiujiang, but afterward instead employed Chen Ji of Danyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu had first promised Sun Ce the post of Administrator of Jiujiang, but later gave it to Chen Ji of Danyang instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 後術欲攻徐州，從廬江太守陸康求米三萬斛。
manualTranslations.literal: Later Shu wished to attack Xu Province and requested thirty thousand hu of grain from Lu Kang, Administrator of Lujiang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuan Shu wished to attack Xu Province, he asked Lu Kang, Administrator of Lujiang, for thirty thousand hu of grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 康不與，術大怒。
manualTranslations.literal: Kang would not give it; Shu was greatly angered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Kang refused, and Yuan Shu was furious.

manualTranslations.zh: 策昔曾詣康，康不見，使主簿接之。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce had formerly visited Kang; Kang did not see him and had the Chief Clerk receive him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had once visited Lu Kang, who refused to see him and sent a chief clerk to receive him instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 策常銜恨。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce constantly harbored resentment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had long nursed resentment over this.

manualTranslations.zh: 術遣策攻康，謂曰：「前錯用陳紀，每恨本意不遂。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu dispatched Ce to attack Kang, saying to him: 'Formerly I wrongly employed Chen Ji and always regretted that my original intent was not fulfilled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack Lu Kang, saying, "I wrongly gave the post to Chen Ji before and have always regretted failing to carry out my original plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 今若得康，廬江眞卿有也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now if we obtain Kang, Lujiang truly will have its proper lord.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you take Lu Kang now, Lujiang will truly have its rightful administrator."

manualTranslations.zh: 策攻康，拔之。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce attacked Kang and captured it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce attacked Lu Kang and captured the city.

manualTranslations.zh: 術復用其故吏劉勳爲太守，策益失望。
manualTranslations.literal: Shu again employed his former clerk Liu Xun as Administrator; Ce grew all the more disappointed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu then appointed his former subordinate Liu Xun as administrator, and Sun Ce grew still more disillusioned.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，劉繇爲揚州刺史，州舊治壽春。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Liu Yao was Inspector of Yang Province; the province's former seat was Shouchun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Previously Liu Yao had been Inspector of Yang Province, and the provincial seat had been at Shouchun.

items.acceptedSourceText: 」徐州牧陶謙深忌策。策舅呉景，時爲丹楊太守，策乃載母徙曲阿，與呂範，孫河俱就景。因緣召募得數百人。興平元年194年，從袁術。術甚奇之，以堅部曲還策。呉暦曰：「初策在江都時，張紘有母喪。策數詣紘，咨以世務，曰：『方今漢祚中微，天下擾攘，英雄俊傑各擁衆營私，未有能扶危濟亂者也。先君與袁氏共破董卓，功業未遂，卒爲黃祖所害。策雖暗稚，竊有微志，欲從袁揚州求先君餘兵，就舅氏於丹楊，收合流散，東據呉會，報讎雪恥，爲朝廷外籓。君以爲何如？』紘答曰：『旣素空劣，方居衰絰之中，無以奉贊盛略。』策曰：『君高名播越，遠近懷歸。今日事計，決之於君，何得不紆慮啓告，副其高山之望？若微志得展，血讎得報，此乃君之勛力，策心所望也。』因涕泣橫流，顔色不變。紘見策忠壯內發，辭令慷慨，感其志言，乃答曰：『昔周道陵遲，齊晉並興；王室已寧，諸侯貢職。今君紹先侯之軌，有驍武之名，若投丹楊，收兵呉會，則荆揚可一，讎敵可報。據長江，奮威德，誅除群穢，匡輔漢室，功業侔於桓文，豈徒外籓而已哉？方今世亂多難，若功成事立，當與同好俱南濟也。』策曰：『一與君同符合契，（同）有永固之分，今便行矣，以老母弱弟委付於君，策無復回顧之憂。』」江表傳曰：「策徑到壽春見袁術，涕泣而言曰：『亡父昔從長沙入討董卓，與明使君會於南陽，同盟結好；不幸遇難，勛業不終。策感惟先人舊恩，欲自憑結，原明使君垂察其誠。』術甚貴異之，然未肯還其父兵。術謂策曰：『孤始用貴舅爲丹楊太守，賢從伯陽爲都尉，彼精兵之地，可還依召募。』策遂詣丹楊依舅，得數百人，而爲涇縣大帥祖郎所襲，幾至危殆。於是復往見術，術以堅餘兵千餘人還策。」太傅馬日磾杖節安集關東，在壽春以禮辟策，表拜懷義校尉，術大將喬蕤、張勳皆傾心敬焉。術常歎曰：「使術有子如孫郎，死復何恨！」策騎士有罪，逃入術營，隱於內廄。策指使人就斬之，訖，詣術謝。術曰：「兵人好叛，當共疾之，何爲謝也？」由是軍中益畏憚之。術初許策爲九江太守，已而更用丹楊陳紀。後術欲攻徐州，從廬江太守陸康求米三萬斛。康不與，術大怒。策昔曾詣康，康不見，使主簿接之。策常銜恨。術遣策攻康，謂曰：「前錯用陳紀，每恨本意不遂。今若得康，廬江眞卿有也。」策攻康，拔之。術復用其故吏劉勳爲太守，策益失望。先是，劉繇爲揚州刺史，州舊治壽春。

sourceRange.text: 」中平元年，黃巾賊師張角起於魏郡。託有神靈，遣八使以善道教化天下，而潛相連結，自稱黃天泰平。三月甲子，三十六（萬）一旦俱發，天下響應，燔燒郡縣，殺害長吏。獻帝春秋曰：「角稱天公將軍，角弟寶稱地公將軍，寶弟梁稱人公將軍。」漢朝遣車騎將軍皇甫崧、中郎將朱儁將兵討擊之。儁表請堅爲佐軍司馬，鄕里少年隨在下邳者皆願從。堅又募諸商旅及淮泗精兵，合千許人，與儁並力奮擊，所向無前。呉書曰：「堅乘勝深入，於西華失利。堅被創墮馬，臥草中。軍衆分散，不知堅所在。堅所騎驄馬馳還營，踣地呼鳴，將士隨馬於草中得堅。堅還營十數日，創少愈，乃復出戰。」汝穎賊困迫，走保宛城。堅身當一面，登城先入，衆乃蟻附，遂大破之。儁具以狀聞上，拜堅別部司馬。續漢書曰：「儁字公偉，會稽人，少好學，爲郡功曹，察孝廉，舉進士。漢朝以討黃巾功拜車騎將軍，累遷河南尹。董卓見儁，外甚親納，而心忌之，儁亦陰備焉。關東兵起，卓議移都，儁輒止卓。卓雖憚儁，然貪其名重，乃表拜太僕以自副。儁被召不肯受拜，因進曰：「國不宜遷，必孤天下望，成山東之結，臣不見其可也。」有司詰曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，何也？」儁曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也。遷都非計，臣之所急也。辭所不堪，進臣所急，臣之所宜也。」有司曰：「遷都之事，初無此計也，就有，未露，何所受聞？」儁曰：「相國董卓爲臣説之，臣聞之於相國。」有司不能屈，朝廷稱服焉。後爲太尉。李傕、郭汜相攻，劫質天子公卿，儁性剛，卽發病而卒。

context.beforeSource: 鄕里知舊，好事少年，往來者常數百人，堅接撫待養，有若子弟焉。
context.afterSource: 邊章、韓遂作亂涼州，中郎將董卓拒討無功。

manualTranslations.zh: 」中平元年，黃巾賊師張角起於魏郡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhongping, the Yellow Turban bandit leader Zhang Jiao rose up in Wei Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Zhongping 1 (184), the Yellow Turban rebel leader Zhang Jiao rose in Wei Commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 託有神靈，遣八使以善道教化天下，而潛相連結，自稱黃天泰平。
manualTranslations.literal: Claiming to have divine spirits, he sent eight emissaries to teach and transform the realm with the Way of goodness, while secretly linking together, calling himself Yellow Heaven and Great Peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Claiming supernatural authority, he sent eight agents to spread his doctrine of virtue throughout the empire while secretly organizing his followers, proclaiming the era of Yellow Heaven and Great Peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 三月甲子，三十六
manualTranslations.literal: On the jiazi day of the third month, thirty-six
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month, thirty-six

manualTranslations.literal: (ten thousand)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (ten thousand)

manualTranslations.zh: 一旦俱發，天下響應，燔燒郡縣，殺害長吏。
manualTranslations.literal: At once all rose together; the realm responded; they burned commanderies and counties and killed chief officials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They all rose at once; the empire answered their call; they burned cities and counties and killed local officials.

manualTranslations.zh: 獻帝春秋曰：「角稱天公將軍，角弟寶稱地公將軍，寶弟梁稱人公將軍。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: 'Jiao styled himself General of Heaven; Jiao's younger brother Bao styled himself General of Earth; Bao's younger brother Liang styled himself General of Man.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian records: "Zhang Jiao called himself General of Heaven; his younger brother Bao called himself General of Earth; Bao's younger brother Liang called himself General of Man."

manualTranslations.zh: 漢朝遣車騎將軍皇甫崧、中郎將朱儁將兵討擊之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han court dispatched General of Chariots and Cavalry Huangfu Song and General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhu Jun to lead troops to attack them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han court sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Huangfu Song and General of the Gentlemen of the Household Zhu Jun with troops to suppress them.

manualTranslations.zh: 儁表請堅爲佐軍司馬，鄕里少年隨在下邳者皆願從。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jun memorialized requesting Jian as Assistant Army Major; the young men of the district who were at Xiapi all wished to follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun submitted a memorial asking that Sun Jian serve as Assistant Army Major; all the local youths at Xiapi volunteered to join him.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅又募諸商旅及淮泗精兵，合千許人，與儁並力奮擊，所向無前。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian also recruited merchants and travelers and picked troops of the Huai and Si, totaling about a thousand men; with Zhu Jun he joined strength and struck fiercely, wherever they went none could stand before them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jian also recruited merchants and elite troops from the Huai and Si regions, gathering about a thousand men; fighting alongside Zhu Jun, they swept forward without opposition.

manualTranslations.zh: 呉書曰：「堅乘勝深入，於西華失利。
manualTranslations.literal: The Book of Wu says: 'Jian, riding victory, pressed deep in; at Xihua he met defeat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu records: "Sun Jian pressed his advantage deep into enemy territory and suffered a setback at Xihua.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅被創墮馬，臥草中。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian was wounded and fell from his horse, lying in the grass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jian was wounded and thrown from his horse, lying hidden in the grass.

manualTranslations.zh: 軍衆分散，不知堅所在。
manualTranslations.literal: The army masses scattered, not knowing where Jian was.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His troops scattered, not knowing where Sun Jian was.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅所騎驄馬馳還營，踣地呼鳴，將士隨馬於草中得堅。
manualTranslations.literal: The piebald horse Jian had ridden galloped back to camp, fell to the ground and neighed; officers and soldiers followed the horse and found Jian in the grass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jian's piebald horse galloped back to camp, collapsed, and whinnied; the soldiers followed it and found Sun Jian in the grass.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅還營十數日，創少愈，乃復出戰。」
manualTranslations.literal: Jian returned to camp for ten-odd days; when his wound had somewhat healed, he then went out to battle again.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After returning to camp for more than ten days and recovering somewhat from his wounds, he went back into battle."

manualTranslations.zh: 汝穎賊困迫，走保宛城。
manualTranslations.literal: The bandits of Runan and Ying were hard pressed and fled to hold Wancheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rebels of Runan and Ying, pressed hard, fled and fortified themselves in Wancheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 堅身當一面，登城先入，衆乃蟻附，遂大破之。
manualTranslations.literal: Jian personally faced one side, climbed the wall and entered first; the masses then swarmed up like ants, and so he utterly defeated them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Jian personally led the assault on one face of the city, was first over the wall, and his men swarmed after him like ants, routing the enemy completely.

manualTranslations.zh: 儁具以狀聞上，拜堅別部司馬。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jun fully reported the situation to the throne; Jian was appointed Separate Division Major.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun reported the full account to the court, and Sun Jian was appointed Separate Division Major.

manualTranslations.zh: 續漢書曰：「儁字公偉，會稽人，少好學，爲郡功曹，察孝廉，舉進士。
manualTranslations.literal: The Continuation of the Book of Han says: 'Zhu Jun, styled Gongwei, was a man of Kuaiji; in youth he loved learning; he served as Commandery Merit Officer, was nominated Filial and Incorrupt, and was recommended as Presented Scholar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Continuation of the Book of Han states: "Zhu Jun, styled Gongwei, was from Kuaiji. In his youth he loved learning. He served as a commandery merit officer, was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, and was recommended as a Presented Scholar.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢朝以討黃巾功拜車騎將軍，累遷河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han court, for merit in suppressing the Yellow Turbans, appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry; he was promoted in succession to Intendant of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For his service against the Yellow Turbans, the Han court appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry, and he was later promoted to Intendant of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 董卓見儁，外甚親納，而心忌之，儁亦陰備焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Dong Zhuo saw Zhu Jun and outwardly was very intimate and accepting, but inwardly envied him; Zhu Jun also secretly guarded against him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo treated Zhu Jun with outward warmth but secretly resented him; Zhu Jun likewise kept his guard up.

manualTranslations.zh: 關東兵起，卓議移都，儁輒止卓。
manualTranslations.literal: When the armies of the east rose, Zhuo discussed moving the capital; Zhu Jun repeatedly stopped Zhuo.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the eastern coalition rose in arms, Dong Zhuo proposed moving the capital, and Zhu Jun repeatedly blocked him.

manualTranslations.zh: 卓雖憚儁，然貪其名重，乃表拜太僕以自副。
manualTranslations.literal: Although Zhuo feared Zhu Jun, yet he coveted his great reputation, and so memorialized to appoint him Grand Steward as his deputy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Dong Zhuo feared Zhu Jun, he still coveted his prestige and memorialized the court to appoint him Grand Steward as his deputy.

manualTranslations.zh: 儁被召不肯受拜，因進曰：「國不宜遷，必孤天下望，成山東之結，臣不見其可也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jun, summoned, refused to accept the appointment, and therefore advanced saying: 'The state should not be moved; it will surely estrange the hopes of the realm and complete the bond of the eastern mountains; your servant does not see that it can be done.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Summoned to accept the post, Zhu Jun refused and said: "The capital should not be moved. It would alienate the hopes of the empire and strengthen the eastern coalition. I see no merit in it."

manualTranslations.zh: 有司詰曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，何也？」
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible officials questioned him, saying: 'You were summoned to accept appointment and you refused; we did not ask about the matter of relocation yet you presented it—why?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials demanded: "You were summoned to accept office and refused. We did not ask about moving the capital, yet you raised it. Why?"

manualTranslations.zh: 儁曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jun said: 'Serving as deputy to the Chancellor is not what your servant can bear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun replied: "Serving as deputy to the Chancellor is beyond my capacity.

manualTranslations.zh: 遷都非計，臣之所急也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moving the capital is no plan—it is what your servant urgently addresses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moving the capital is ill-advised, and that is what I urgently wished to address.

manualTranslations.zh: 辭所不堪，進臣所急，臣之所宜也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Declining what one cannot bear and advancing what your servant urgently addresses—that is what your servant ought to do.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To decline what I cannot accept and advance what I urgently consider important—that is what I ought to do."

manualTranslations.zh: 有司曰：「遷都之事，初無此計也，就有，未露，何所受聞？」
manualTranslations.literal: The officials said: 'The matter of moving the capital—at first there was no such plan; even if there were, it had not been revealed—what did you hear it from?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials said: "There was no plan to move the capital. Even if there had been, it had not been disclosed. How did you hear of it?"

manualTranslations.zh: 儁曰：「相國董卓爲臣説之，臣聞之於相國。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhu Jun said: 'Chancellor Dong Zhuo told it to your servant; your servant heard it from the Chancellor.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun answered: "Chancellor Dong Zhuo told me himself. I heard it from the Chancellor."

manualTranslations.zh: 有司不能屈，朝廷稱服焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The officials could not refute him; the court praised and admired him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The officials could not overcome him, and the court admired his stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 後爲太尉。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he became Grand Commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 李傕、郭汜相攻，劫質天子公卿，儁性剛，卽發病而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Jue and Guo Si attacked each other and held the Son of Heaven and the high ministers hostage; Zhu Jun's nature was stern, and he immediately fell ill and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Jue and Guo Si fought each other and held the emperor and high officials hostage, Zhu Jun's stern nature could not bear it; he fell ill at once and died.

items.acceptedSourceText: 」中平元年，黃巾賊師張角起於魏郡。託有神靈，遣八使以善道教化天下，而潛相連結，自稱黃天泰平。三月甲子，三十六（萬）一旦俱發，天下響應，燔燒郡縣，殺害長吏。獻帝春秋曰：「角稱天公將軍，角弟寶稱地公將軍，寶弟梁稱人公將軍。」漢朝遣車騎將軍皇甫崧、中郎將朱儁將兵討擊之。儁表請堅爲佐軍司馬，鄕里少年隨在下邳者皆願從。堅又募諸商旅及淮泗精兵，合千許人，與儁並力奮擊，所向無前。呉書曰：「堅乘勝深入，於西華失利。堅被創墮馬，臥草中。軍衆分散，不知堅所在。堅所騎驄馬馳還營，踣地呼鳴，將士隨馬於草中得堅。堅還營十數日，創少愈，乃復出戰。」汝穎賊困迫，走保宛城。堅身當一面，登城先入，衆乃蟻附，遂大破之。儁具以狀聞上，拜堅別部司馬。續漢書曰：「儁字公偉，會稽人，少好學，爲郡功曹，察孝廉，舉進士。漢朝以討黃巾功拜車騎將軍，累遷河南尹。董卓見儁，外甚親納，而心忌之，儁亦陰備焉。關東兵起，卓議移都，儁輒止卓。卓雖憚儁，然貪其名重，乃表拜太僕以自副。儁被召不肯受拜，因進曰：「國不宜遷，必孤天下望，成山東之結，臣不見其可也。」有司詰曰：「召君受拜而君拒之，不問徙事而君陳之，何也？」儁曰：「副相國，非臣所堪也。遷都非計，臣之所急也。辭所不堪，進臣所急，臣之所宜也。」有司曰：「遷都之事，初無此計也，就有，未露，何所受聞？」儁曰：「相國董卓爲臣説之，臣聞之於相國。」有司不能屈，朝廷稱服焉。後爲太尉。李傕、郭汜相攻，劫質天子公卿，儁性剛，卽發病而卒。

sourceRange.text: 臣松之以爲張昭雖名重，然不如紘之文也，此書必紘所作。曹公表策爲討逆將軍，封爲呉侯。江表傳曰：「建安二年夏，漢朝遣議郎王誧奉戊辰詔書曰：『董卓逆亂，凶國害民。先將軍堅念在平討，雅意未遂，厥美著聞。策遵善道，求福不回。今以策爲騎都尉，襲爵烏程侯，領會稽太守。』又詔敕曰：『故左將軍袁術不顧朝恩，坐創凶逆，造合虛僞，欲因兵亂，詭詐百姓，聞其言以爲不然。定得使持節、平東將軍、領徐州牧、温侯布上術所造惑衆妖妄，知術鴟梟之性，遂其無道，修治王宮，署置公卿，郊天祀地，殘民害物，爲禍深酷。布前後上策乃心本朝，欲還討術，爲國效節，乞加顯異。夫縣賞俟功，惟勤是與，故便寵授，承襲前邑，重以大郡，榮耀兼至，是策輸力竭命之秋也。其亟與布及行呉郡太守、安東將軍陳瑀戮力一心，同時赴討。』策自以統領兵馬，但以騎都尉領郡爲輕，欲得將軍號，（及）使人諷誧，誧便承制假策明漢將軍。是時，陳瑀屯海西，策奉詔治嚴，當與布瑀參同形勢。行到錢塘，瑀陰圖襲策，遣都尉萬演等密渡江，使持印傳三十餘紐與賊丹楊、宣城、涇、陵陽、始安、黟、歙諸險縣大帥祖郎、焦已及呉郡烏程嚴白虎等，使爲內應，伺策軍發，欲攻取諸郡。策覺之，遣呂範、徐逸攻瑀於海西，大破瑀，獲其吏士妻子四千人。山陽公載記曰：『瑀單騎走冀州，自歸袁紹，紹以爲故安都尉。』呉録載策上表謝曰：『臣以固陋，孤持邊陲。陛下廣播高澤，不遺細節，以臣襲爵，兼典名郡。仰榮顧寵，所不克堪。興平二年十二月二十日，於呉郡曲阿得袁術所呈表，以臣行殄寇將軍；至被詔書，乃知詐擅。雖輒捐廢，猶用悚悸。臣年十七，喪失所怙，懼有不任堂構之鄙，以忝析薪之戒，誠無去病十八建功，世祖列將弱冠佐命。臣初領兵，年未弱冠，雖駑懦不武，然思竭微命。惟術狂惑，爲惡深重。臣憑威靈，奉辭罰罪，庶必獻捷，以報所授。』臣松之案：本傳云孫堅以初平三年卒，策以建安五年卒，策死時年二十六，計堅之亡，策應十八，而此表云十七，則爲不符。張璠張璠後漢紀漢紀及呉歷並以堅初平二年死，此爲是而本傳誤也。江表傳曰：『建安三年，策又遣使貢方物，倍於元年所獻。其年，制書轉拜討逆將軍，改封呉侯。

localRange.text: 臣松之以为张昭虽名重，然不如纮之文也，此书必纮所作。

context.beforeSource: 」典略云張昭之辭。
context.afterSource: 』後術死，長史楊弘、大將張勳等將其衆欲就策，廬江太守劉勳要擊，悉虜之，收其珍寶以歸。
context.beforeLocal: 《典略》云张昭之辞。
context.afterLocal: 後術死，長史楊弘、大將張勳等將其眾欲就策，廬江太守劉勳要擊，悉虜之，收其珍寶以歸。

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以爲張昭雖名重，然不如紘之文也，此書必紘所作。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that although Zhang Zhao's name is weighty, yet he is not the equal of Hong in literary composition; this text must have been written by Hong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that although Zhang Zhao was renowned, his writing was inferior to Zhang Hong's; this text must be Hong's work.

manualTranslations.zh: 曹公表策爲討逆將軍，封爲呉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Cao memorialized Ce as General Who Punishes Rebels and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lord Cao memorialized Sun Ce's appointment as General Who Punishes Rebels and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 江表傳曰：「建安二年夏，漢朝遣議郎王誧奉戊辰詔書曰：『董卓逆亂，凶國害民。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiang Biao Zhuan says: 'In summer of the second year of Jian'an, the Han court dispatched Consultant Wang Fu bearing the wuchen edict, saying: 'Dong Zhuo was rebellious and disorderly, harming the state and injuring the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Biao Zhuan records: "In the summer of Jian'an 2 (197), the Han court dispatched Consultant Wang Fu with an edict dated wuchen, stating, 'Dong Zhuo rebelled against the dynasty and brought ruin upon the state and people.

manualTranslations.zh: 先將軍堅念在平討，雅意未遂，厥美著聞。
manualTranslations.literal: The former General Jian's intent in leveling and punishing was not yet fulfilled; his fine merit is renowned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Sun Jian's purpose in suppressing rebellion was cut short, yet his merit is widely known.

manualTranslations.zh: 策遵善道，求福不回。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce follows the good Way and seeks blessing without turning aside.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce follows the righteous path and seeks the dynasty's welfare without wavering.

manualTranslations.zh: 今以策爲騎都尉，襲爵烏程侯，領會稽太守。』
manualTranslations.literal: Now Ce is appointed Commandant of Cavalry, succeeding to the title Marquis of Wucheng, and leading as Administrator of Kuaiji.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce is hereby appointed Commandant of Cavalry, succeeding to the title Marquis of Wucheng, and made Administrator of Kuaiji.'

manualTranslations.zh: 又詔敕曰：『故左將軍袁術不顧朝恩，坐創凶逆，造合虛僞，欲因兵亂，詭詐百姓，聞其言以爲不然。
manualTranslations.literal: Another edict and command said: 'The former General of the Left Yuan Shu disregarded court grace, sat and created rebellion and treachery, fabricated and assembled falsehood, wished to take advantage of military disorder, and deceived the people with fraud—hearing his words one would think it not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A further edict stated: 'The former General of the Left Yuan Shu spurned the court's favor, raised rebellion, fabricated false claims, and sought to exploit the chaos to deceive the people. At first hearing, one might doubt it.

manualTranslations.zh: 定得使持節、平東將軍、領徐州牧、温侯布上術所造惑衆妖妄，知術鴟梟之性，遂其無道，修治王宮，署置公卿，郊天祀地，殘民害物，爲禍深酷。
manualTranslations.literal: But it is confirmed: the Bearer of Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Xu Province, Marquis of Wen Bu reported the falsehoods Yuan Shu created to delude the masses; knowing Shu's owl-and-eagle nature, he followed his lawless course—repairing a royal palace, appointing dukes and ministers, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs, harming the people and injuring things—his calamity was deep and cruel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But it is confirmed: Lü Bu, Bearer of Staff, General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xu Province, reported Yuan Shu's deceptions and demagoguery. Knowing Yuan Shu's vicious nature, he has pursued his lawless course—building a palace, appointing ministers, performing imperial sacrifices, and ravaging the people. His crimes are grave indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 布前後上策乃心本朝，欲還討術，爲國效節，乞加顯異。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu repeatedly reported that Ce's heart is loyal to the court, that he wishes to turn and attack Shu and serve the state with fidelity, and requested special distinction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lü Bu has repeatedly reported that Sun Ce's heart is loyal to the court, that he wishes to turn against Yuan Shu and serve the state, and has asked that he be specially honored.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫縣賞俟功，惟勤是與，故便寵授，承襲前邑，重以大郡，榮耀兼至，是策輸力竭命之秋也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now rewards are hung awaiting merit, and only diligence is granted; therefore favor is bestowed: succeeding to the former fief and additionally granted a great commandery—glory arriving together—this is the season for Ce to pour forth his strength and exhaust his life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rewards await merit and honor goes to the diligent. Therefore he is granted succession to his former fief and additionally entrusted with a great commandery. Glory has come together; this is the time for Sun Ce to devote his full strength and life to the cause.

manualTranslations.zh: 其亟與布及行呉郡太守、安東將軍陳瑀戮力一心，同時赴討。』
manualTranslations.literal: Let him quickly join with Bu and Acting Administrator of Wu Commandery, General Who Pacifies the East Chen Yu, exerting one heart, and at the same time go to attack.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let him promptly join Lü Bu and Chen Yu, Acting Administrator of Wu Commandery and General Who Pacifies the East, in united effort to campaign against Yuan Shu at once.'

manualTranslations.zh: 策自以統領兵馬，但以騎都尉領郡爲輕，欲得將軍號，
manualTranslations.literal: Ce considered that he himself commanded troops and horses, yet to hold the commandery merely as Commandant of Cavalry was too light; he wished to obtain a general's title,
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce felt that commanding troops while holding only the rank of Commandant of Cavalry over a commandery was too modest; he wanted a general's title,

manualTranslations.literal: (and)
manualTranslations.idiomatic: (and)

manualTranslations.zh: 使人諷誧，誧便承制假策明漢將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: and sent men to hint to Fu; Fu then, by imperial commission, provisionally appointed Ce General of the Bright Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and sent envoys to hint as much to Wang Fu, who then provisionally appointed him General of the Bright Han by imperial commission.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，陳瑀屯海西，策奉詔治嚴，當與布瑀參同形勢。
manualTranslations.literal: At this time Chen Yu was stationed at Haixi; Ce received the edict and prepared his forces, and was to join with Bu and Yu in assessing the situation together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Yu was encamped at Haixi. Sun Ce received the edict, marshaled his forces, and was to coordinate with Lü Bu and Chen Yu.

manualTranslations.zh: 行到錢塘，瑀陰圖襲策，遣都尉萬演等密渡江，使持印傳三十餘紐與賊丹楊、宣城、涇、陵陽、始安、黟、歙諸險縣大帥祖郎、焦已及呉郡烏程嚴白虎等，使爲內應，伺策軍發，欲攻取諸郡。
manualTranslations.literal: When he reached Qiantang, Yu secretly plotted to surprise Ce; he sent Commandant Wan Yan and others secretly to cross the river, giving more than thirty seals and credentials to the bandit chiefs Zu Lang, Jiao Yi, and Yan Baihu of Wucheng in Wu Commandery, and the chiefs of the perilous counties of Danyang, Xuancheng, Jing, Lingyang, Shi'an, Yi, and She, making them inner collaborators; watching for Ce's army to set out, he wished to attack and seize the commanderies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce reached Qiantang, Chen Yu secretly plotted to ambush him. He sent Commandant Wan Yan and others to cross the river in secret with more than thirty seals and credentials for the bandit chiefs Zu Lang, Jiao Yi, Yan Baihu of Wucheng, and others in the strategic counties of Danyang, Xuancheng, Jing, Lingyang, Shi'an, Yi, and She, intending them as inside collaborators to seize the commanderies when Sun Ce's army marched out.

manualTranslations.zh: 策覺之，遣呂範、徐逸攻瑀於海西，大破瑀，獲其吏士妻子四千人。
manualTranslations.literal: Ce discovered it and dispatched Lü Fan and Xu Yi to attack Yu at Haixi; they greatly defeated Yu and captured four thousand of his clerks, soldiers, wives, and children.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Ce discovered the plot and sent Lü Fan and Xu Yi to attack Chen Yu at Haixi. They routed him and captured four thousand of his officials, soldiers, and their families.

manualTranslations.zh: 山陽公載記曰：『瑀單騎走冀州，自歸袁紹，紹以爲故安都尉。』
manualTranslations.literal: The Records of the Duke of Shanyang say: 'Yu fled alone on horseback to Ji Province, surrendered himself to Yuan Shao, and Shao made him Commandant of Gu'an.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Records of the Duke of Shanyang record: "Chen Yu fled alone on horseback to Ji Province, surrendered to Yuan Shao, and was made Commandant of Gu'an."

manualTranslations.zh: 呉録載策上表謝曰：『臣以固陋，孤持邊陲。
manualTranslations.literal: Wu Lu records Ce's memorial of thanks, saying: 'Your servant, being stubborn and lowly, alone holds the frontier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu Lu records Sun Ce's memorial of thanks: "Your servant, being unworthy, holds a remote frontier post alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下廣播高澤，不遺細節，以臣襲爵，兼典名郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty broadly spreads lofty grace and does not overlook small details, granting your servant succession to the title and additionally entrusting a renowned commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace is far-reaching and overlooks no detail, granting me succession to my title and additionally entrusting me with a great commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 仰榮顧寵，所不克堪。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking up to glory and turning to favor, I am unable to bear it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am overwhelmed by such honor and favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 興平二年十二月二十日，於呉郡曲阿得袁術所呈表，以臣行殄寇將軍；
manualTranslations.literal: On the twentieth day of the twelfth month of the second year of Xingping, at Qu'a in Wu Commandery I received the memorial Yuan Shu presented, appointing your servant Acting General Who Exterminates Bandits;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the twelfth month of Xingping 2, at Qu'a in Wu Commandery I received the memorial Yuan Shu had submitted appointing me Acting General Who Exterminates Bandits;

manualTranslations.zh: 至被詔書，乃知詐擅。
manualTranslations.literal: Only upon receiving the edict did I know of the fraudulent usurpation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: only upon receiving the imperial edict did I learn of this fraudulent usurpation of authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖輒捐廢，猶用悚悸。
manualTranslations.literal: Although I immediately discarded and abolished it, I still feel fear and trembling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Although I immediately renounced it, I remain fearful and uneasy.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣年十七，喪失所怙，懼有不任堂構之鄙，以忝析薪之戒，誠無去病十八建功，世祖列將弱冠佐命。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant is seventeen years old, bereft of those I relied upon; I fear I may not bear the humble task of building the hall and beam, and may disgrace the warning of splitting firewood—truly I do not have Huo Qubing at eighteen achieving merit, nor the lieutenant generals of Emperor Guangwu assisting fate at the capping age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am only seventeen, bereft of my father, and fear I am unfit for the responsibility of upholding the family enterprise and unworthy of the charge to carry on my father's work. I am no Huo Qubing achieving glory at eighteen, nor one of Emperor Guangwu's generals who aided the throne in his youth.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣初領兵，年未弱冠，雖駑懦不武，然思竭微命。
manualTranslations.literal: When your servant first took command of troops, I had not yet reached the capping age; although dull and timid and not martial, yet I think to exhaust my slight life.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I first took command I had not yet reached my majority. Though untested and unwarlike, I am resolved to devote my life to service.

manualTranslations.zh: 惟術狂惑，爲惡深重。
manualTranslations.literal: Only Shu is mad and deluded, his evil deep and heavy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu alone is mad and deluded, and his crimes are grave.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣憑威靈，奉辭罰罪，庶必獻捷，以報所授。』
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant, relying on majesty and spirit, receives the charge to punish crime; I hope surely to present victory and repay what has been granted.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Relying on Your Majesty's authority, I accept the charge to punish his crimes and hope to bring victory in return for the honor you have granted me.'

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之案：本傳云孫堅以初平三年卒，策以建安五年卒，策死時年二十六，計堅之亡，策應十八，而此表云十七，則爲不符。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: the main biography says Sun Jian died in the third year of Chuping; Ce died in the fifth year of Jian'an at age twenty-six; calculating Jian's death, Ce should have been eighteen, yet this memorial says seventeen—thus it does not match.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes: the main biography says Sun Jian died in Chuping 3 (192); Sun Ce died in Jian'an 5 (200) at age twenty-six. By that reckoning Sun Ce should have been eighteen when his father died, yet this memorial says seventeen—a discrepancy.

manualTranslations.zh: 張璠張璠後漢紀漢紀及呉歷並以堅初平二年死，此爲是而本傳誤也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Fan—Zhang Fan's Hou Han Ji and Han Ji, as well as Wu Li, all say Jian died in the second year of Chuping; this is correct and the main biography is in error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Hou Han Ji (where the name Zhang Fan appears duplicated in the source) and Han Ji, as well as Wu Li, all say Sun Jian died in Chuping 2 (191); that is correct and the main biography is mistaken.

manualTranslations.zh: 江表傳曰：『建安三年，策又遣使貢方物，倍於元年所獻。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiang Biao Zhuan says: 'In the third year of Jian'an, Ce again sent envoys to present local products, twice what had been offered in the first year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiang Biao Zhuan records: "In Jian'an 3 (198), Sun Ce again sent envoys with local tribute, twice the amount offered in the first year.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年，制書轉拜討逆將軍，改封呉侯。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, an imperial document transferred his appointment to General Who Punishes Rebels and changed his enfeoffment to Marquis of Wu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That same year an imperial edict promoted him to General Who Punishes Rebels and changed his enfeoffment to Marquis of Wu.

sourceRange.text: 偕乃報勛，具説形狀，使勛來襲取之。勛得偕書，使潛軍到海昏邑下。宗帥知之，空壁逃匿，勛了無所得。時策西討黃祖，行及石城，聞勛輕身詣海昏，便分遣從兄賁、輔率八千人於彭澤待勛，自與周瑜率二萬人歩襲皖城，卽克之，得術百工及鼓吹部曲三萬餘人，並術勛妻子。賁、輔又於彭澤破勛。勛走入楚江，從尋陽歩上到置馬亭，聞策等已克皖，乃投西塞。至沂，築壘自守，告急於劉表，求救於黃祖。祖遣太子射船軍五千人助勛。策復就攻，大破勛。勛與偕北歸曹公，射亦遁走。策收得勛兵二千餘人，船千艘，遂前進夏口攻黃祖。時劉表遣從子虎、南陽韓晞將長矛五千，來爲黃祖前鋒。

localRange.text: 權乃參分天下，豫、青、徐、幽屬吳，兗，冀，并州，涼屬蜀。其司州之土，以函谷關為界，造為盟曰："天降喪亂，皇綱失敘，逆臣乘釁，劫奪國柄，始於董卓，終於曹操，窮凶極惡，以覆四海。至令九州幅裂，普天無統，民神痛怨，靡所戾止。及操子丕，桀逆遺丑，薦作奸回，偷取天位。而睿么麼，尋丕凶跡，阻兵盜土，未伏厥誅。昔共工亂象而高辛行師，三苗干度虞舜征焉。今日滅曹，禽其徒黨，非蜀漢與東吳，將復誰任?夫討惡剪暴，必聲其罪。

sourceRange.text: 臣松之按《禮記》曾子問子夏曰：『三年之喪，金革之事無避也者，禮與？初有司與？』孔子曰：『吾聞諸老摐曰，昔者魯公伯禽有爲爲之也。』鄭玄注曰：『周人卒哭而致事。時有徐戎作難，伯禽卒哭而徵之，急王事也。』昭所云『伯禽不師』，蓋謂此也。況今奸宄競逐，豺狼滿道，乃欲哀親戚，顧禮制，是猶開門而揖盜，未可以爲仁也。

sourceRange.text: 孫盛曰：「昔伯夷、叔齊不屈有周，魯仲連不爲秦民。夫以匹夫之志，猶義不辱，況列國之君三分天下，而可二三其節，或臣或否乎？餘觀吳、蜀，咸稱奉漢，至於漢代，莫能固秉臣節，君子是以知其不能克昌厥後，卒見吞於大國也。曏使權從群臣之議，終身稱漢將，豈不義悲六合，仁感百世哉！」是歳，劉備師軍來伐，至巫山、秭歸，使使誘導武陵蠻夷，假與印傳，許之封賞。於是諸縣及五谿民皆反爲蜀。權以陸遜爲督，督朱然、潘璋等以拒之。

sourceRange.text: 」壬申，王濬最先到，於是受皓之降，解縛焚櫬，延請相見。《晉陽秋》曰：濬收其圖籍，領州四，郡四十三，縣三百一十三，戶五十二萬三千，吏三萬二千，兵二十三萬，男女口二百三十萬，米穀二百八十萬斛，舟船五千餘艘，後宮五千餘人。伷以皓致印綬於己，遣使送皓。皓舉家西遷，以太康元年五月丁亥集于京邑。四月甲申，詔曰：「孫皓窮迫歸降，前詔待之以不死，今皓垂至，意猶愍之，其賜號爲歸命侯。進給衣服車乘，田三十頃，歲給穀五千斛，錢五十萬，絹五百匹，緜五百斤。」皓太子瑾拜中郎，諸子爲王者，拜郎中。《搜神記》曰：吳以草創之國，信不堅固，邊屯守將皆質其妻子，名曰保質。童子少年，以類相與嬉游者，日有十數。永安二年259年三月，有一異兒，長四尺餘，年可六七歲，衣青衣，來從羣兒戲，諸兒莫之識也。皆問曰：「爾誰家小兒，今日忽來？」荅曰：「見爾羣戲樂，故來耳。」詳而視之，眼有光芒，爚爚外射。諸兒畏之，重問其故。兒乃荅曰：「爾惡我乎？我非人也，乃熒惑星也。將有以告爾：三公鉏，司馬如。」諸兒大驚，或走告大人，大人馳往觀之。兒曰：「舍爾去乎！」竦身而躍，即以化矣。仰而視之，若引一匹練以登天。大人來者，猶及見焉，飄飄漸高，有頃而沒。時吳政峻急，莫敢宣也。後五年而蜀亡，六年而晉興，至是而吳滅，司馬如矣。干寶《晉紀》曰：王濬治船於蜀，吳彥取其流柹以呈孫皓，曰：「晉必有攻吳之計，宜增建平兵。建平不下，終不敢渡江。」皓弗從。陸抗之克步闡，皓意張大，乃使尚廣筮并天下，遇同人之頤，對曰：「吉。庚子歲，青蓋當入洛陽。」故皓不脩其政，而恒有窺上國之志。是歲也，實在庚子。五年，皓死于洛陽。《吳錄》曰：皓以四年十二月死，時年四十二，葬河南縣界。

manualTranslations.zh: 」壬申，王濬最先到，於是受皓之降，解縛焚櫬，延請相見。
manualTranslations.literal: " On renshen Wang Jun arrived first; thereupon he received Hao's surrender, untied bonds and burned the coffin, extended invitation and met him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " On renshen Wang Jun arrived first, accepted Sun Hao's surrender, cut his bonds, burned the coffin of shame, and received him in audience.

manualTranslations.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：濬收其圖籍，領州四，郡四十三，縣三百一十三，戶五十二萬三千，吏三萬二千，兵二十三萬，男女口二百三十萬，米穀二百八十萬斛，舟船五千餘艘，後宮五千餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jin Yang Chunqiu states: Jun collected their maps and registers: four provinces, forty-three commanderies, three hundred thirteen counties, five hundred twenty-three thousand households, thirty-two thousand clerks, two hundred thirty thousand soldiers, two million three hundred thousand men and women, two million eight hundred thousand hu of grain, more than five thousand boats, more than five thousand palace women.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang Chunqiu records Wang Jun's inventory: four provinces, forty-three commanderies, 313 counties, 523,000 households, 32,000 officials, 230,000 troops, 2.3 million people, 2.8 million hu of grain, 5,000+ ships, and 5,000+ palace women.

manualTranslations.zh: 伷以皓致印綬於己，遣使送皓。
manualTranslations.literal: You, because Hao presented the seal and sash to himself, sent envoys to escort Hao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima You, having received Sun Hao's seal and sash, dispatched envoys escorting him north.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓舉家西遷，以太康元年五月丁亥集于京邑。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao moved his whole family west; on the day dinghai of the fifth month of the first year of Taikang (280) he assembled at the capital metropolis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao and his household reached the capital on dinghai in the fifth month of Taikang 1 (280).

manualTranslations.zh: 四月甲申，詔曰：「孫皓窮迫歸降，前詔待之以不死，今皓垂至，意猶愍之，其賜號爲歸命侯。
manualTranslations.literal: On jiashen of the fourth month an edict stated: "Sun Hao, driven to extremity, returned and submitted; the former edict treated him with not dying; now Hao is about to arrive—our mind still pities him; let him be granted the title Marquis Who Submits to the Mandate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the fourth month an edict declared, "Sun Hao, cornered, has surrendered; though we promised his life, we still pity him—let him be styled Marquis Who Submits to the Mandate.

manualTranslations.zh: 進給衣服車乘，田三十頃，歲給穀五千斛，錢五十萬，絹五百匹，緜五百斤。」
manualTranslations.literal: Advance and give clothes and carriages, thirty qing of fields, five thousand hu of grain each year, five hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of silk, five hundred jin of cotton."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grant robes and carriages, thirty qing of land, five thousand hu of grain yearly, five hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of silk, and five hundred jin of cotton."

manualTranslations.zh: 皓太子瑾拜中郎，諸子爲王者，拜郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao's crown prince Jin was appointed palace cadet; the sons who were kings were appointed gentlemen of the palace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jin became palace cadet; princely sons became gentlemen of the palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 《搜神記》曰：吳以草創之國，信不堅固，邊屯守將皆質其妻子，名曰保質。
manualTranslations.literal: The Soushen Ji states: Wu, being a state founded in grass and creation, faith was not firm and solid; border garrison defending generals all hostage their wives and children, called hostage guarantors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Soushen Ji notes Wu, a young state, distrusted frontier commanders and held their families as hostages—"guarantee hostages."

manualTranslations.zh: 童子少年，以類相與嬉游者，日有十數。
manualTranslations.literal: Boys and youths, those who played together by kind, daily were more than ten.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Local boys played together in groups of a dozen or more.

manualTranslations.zh: 永安二年259年三月，有一異兒，長四尺餘，年可六七歲，衣青衣，來從羣兒戲，諸兒莫之識也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Yong'an (259), there was one strange child, more than four chi tall, age about six or seven sui, wearing green clothes, who came to follow the host of children in play; the various children did not know him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 2, third month, a strange boy over four chi tall, seemingly six or seven, in green robes joined their games unrecognized.

manualTranslations.zh: 皆問曰：「爾誰家小兒，今日忽來？」
manualTranslations.literal: All asked: "Whose household little child are you, that today you suddenly come?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They asked, "Whose child are you, appearing so suddenly?"

manualTranslations.zh: 荅曰：「見爾羣戲樂，故來耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "Seeing you host of children playing happily, therefore I came."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "I saw you playing and came to join."

manualTranslations.zh: 詳而視之，眼有光芒，爚爚外射。
manualTranslations.literal: Examining him and looking at him, his eyes had light rays, blazing and shooting outward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking closely, his eyes blazed with outward-shooting light.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸兒畏之，重問其故。
manualTranslations.literal: The various children feared him; they again asked the reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Terrified, the boys pressed him again.

manualTranslations.zh: 兒乃荅曰：「爾惡我乎？
manualTranslations.literal: The child then answered: "Do you hate me?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The child said, "Do you fear me?

manualTranslations.zh: 我非人也，乃熒惑星也。
manualTranslations.literal: I am not a person—I am the Sparkling Deluder star.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am not human—I am the Sparkling Deluder star.

manualTranslations.zh: 將有以告爾：三公鉏，司馬如。」
manualTranslations.literal: There will be something to tell you: the three dukes are hoes; Sima like."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hear my warning: the three excellencies are but hoes; the Sima clan prevails."

manualTranslations.zh: 諸兒大驚，或走告大人，大人馳往觀之。
manualTranslations.literal: The various children were greatly startled; some ran to tell grown men; grown men galloped to go observe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some boys fled to tell adults, who rushed to see.

manualTranslations.zh: 兒曰：「舍爾去乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: The child said: "Leave you and go!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The child cried, "I leave you!"

manualTranslations.zh: 竦身而躍，即以化矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Drawing up his body he leaped; immediately he transformed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sprang upward and vanished.

manualTranslations.zh: 仰而視之，若引一匹練以登天。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking up to observe him, it was like drawing a bolt of silk to ascend heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking up, he seemed to trail silk as he rose into heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 大人來者，猶及見焉，飄飄漸高，有頃而沒。
manualTranslations.literal: Grown men who came still caught sight of it; drifting drifting it gradually rose high; after a moment it disappeared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Latecomers still saw him float upward until he vanished.

manualTranslations.zh: 時吳政峻急，莫敢宣也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Wu government was severe and urgent; none dared proclaim it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu's harsh rule silenced witnesses.

manualTranslations.zh: 後五年而蜀亡，六年而晉興，至是而吳滅，司馬如矣。
manualTranslations.literal: After five years Shu perished; after six years Jin rose; reaching this time Wu perished—Sima like indeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Five years later Shu fell, six years later Jin rose, and now Wu fell—the Sima prophecy was fulfilled.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：王濬治船於蜀，吳彥取其流柹以呈孫皓，曰：「晉必有攻吳之計，宜增建平兵。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: Wang Jun built ships in Shu; Wu Yan took their floating timbers and presented them to Sun Hao, saying: "Jin surely has a plan to attack Wu—it is fitting to increase Ping's garrison troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin Ji records Wu Yan showing Sun Hao timbers from Wang Jun's Shu shipyards and warning, "Jin plans to attack Wu—increase the Jianping garrison.

manualTranslations.zh: 建平不下，終不敢渡江。」
manualTranslations.literal: If Jianping is not taken, in the end they will not dare cross the river."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Jianping holds, they will never dare cross the Yangzi."

manualTranslations.zh: 皓弗從。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao did not follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored him.

manualTranslations.zh: 陸抗之克步闡，皓意張大，乃使尚廣筮并天下，遇同人之頤，對曰：「吉。
manualTranslations.literal: When Lu Kang took Bu Chan, Hao's intent swelled greatly; thereupon he had Shang Guang divine the whole realm with the hexagrams; he encountered Tongren's Yi; he answered: "Auspicious.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Lu Kang crushed Bu Chan, Sun Hao grew arrogant and had Shang Guang divine the realm, drawing the hexagram Tongren changing to Yi—"auspicious,

manualTranslations.zh: 庚子歲，青蓋當入洛陽。」
manualTranslations.literal: In the gengzi year, the green canopy will enter Luoyang."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: in the gengzi year the green-canopy carriage will enter Luoyang."

manualTranslations.zh: 故皓不脩其政，而恒有窺上國之志。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Hao did not cultivate his government, yet constantly had the ambition of peering at the upper state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So Sun Hao neglected governance while dreaming of conquering the north.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲也，實在庚子。
manualTranslations.literal: This year indeed was gengzi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year was indeed gengzi (280).

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，皓死于洛陽。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year Hao died in Luoyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao died at Luoyang in the fifth year after surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳錄》曰：皓以四年十二月死，時年四十二，葬河南縣界。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Hao died in the twelfth month of the fourth year; at the time he was forty-two sui; he was buried at the border of Henan county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu dates his death to the twelfth month of the fourth year at age forty-two, buried on Henan county's border.

sourceRange.text: 鳳皇元年272年秋八月，徵西陵督步闡。闡不應，據城降晉。遣樂鄉都督陸抗圍取闡，闡衆悉降。闡及同計數十人皆夷三族。大赦。是歲右丞相萬彧被譴憂死，徙其子弟於廬陵。《江表傳》曰：初皓游華里，彧與丁奉、留平密謀曰：「此行不急，若至華里不歸，社稷事重，不得不自還。」此語頗泄。皓聞知，以彧等舊臣，且以計忍而陰銜之。後因會，以毒酒飲彧，傳酒人私減之。又飲留平，平覺之，服他藥以解，得不死。彧自殺。平憂懣，月餘亦死。何定姦穢發聞，伏誅。皓以其惡似張布，追改定名爲布。《江表傳》曰：定，汝南人，本孫權給使也，後出補吏。定佞邪僭媚，自表先帝舊人，求還內侍，皓以爲樓下都尉，典知酤糴事，專爲威福。而皓信任，委以衆事。定爲子求少府李勗女，不許。定挾忿譖勗於皓，皓尺口誅之，焚其尸。定又使諸將各上好犬，皆千里遠求，一犬至直數千匹。御犬率具纓，直錢一萬。一犬一兵，養以捕兎供厨。所獲無幾。吳人皆歸罪於定，而皓以爲忠勤，賜爵列侯。《吳歷》曰：中書郎奚熙譖宛陵令賀惠。惠，劭弟也。遣使者徐粲訊治，熙又譖粲顧護不即決斷。皓遣使就宛陵斬粲，收惠付獄。會赦得免。

manualTranslations.zh: 鳳皇元年272年秋八月，徵西陵督步闡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the first year of Fenghuang (272), Xiling area commander Bu Chan was summoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn's eighth month, Fenghuang 1 (272), Xiling area commander Bu Chan was recalled to court.

manualTranslations.zh: 闡不應，據城降晉。
manualTranslations.literal: Chan did not respond; he held the city and surrendered to Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bu Chan refused, held the fortress, and defected to Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣樂鄉都督陸抗圍取闡，闡衆悉降。
manualTranslations.literal: [The court] sent Lexiang area commander Lu Kang to surround and take Chan; Chan's host all surrendered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent Lexiang commander Lu Kang to invest the city until Bu Chan's entire force surrendered.

manualTranslations.zh: 闡及同計數十人皆夷三族。
manualTranslations.literal: Chan and several tens who shared the plot were all exterminated to the third degree of kin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bu Chan and dozens of conspirators were executed to the third degree of kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲右丞相萬彧被譴憂死，徙其子弟於廬陵。
manualTranslations.literal: This year Right Chancellor Wan Yu was reprimanded, died in worry, and his sons and younger brothers were moved to Luling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Right Chancellor Wan Yu, rebuked by the emperor, died in despair and his kin were exiled to Luling.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：初皓游華里，彧與丁奉、留平密謀曰：「此行不急，若至華里不歸，社稷事重，不得不自還。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: At the beginning, when Hao toured Huali, Yu with Ding Feng and Liu Ping secretly plotted: "This journey is not urgent; if when we reach Huali we do not return, the altars of soil and grain are weighty—we must not fail to return ourselves."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says that during a tour of Huali, Wan Yu, Ding Feng, and Liu Ping privately agreed they must turn back if Sun Hao lingered—state affairs could not wait.

manualTranslations.zh: 此語頗泄。
manualTranslations.literal: This speech leaked somewhat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The remark leaked.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓聞知，以彧等舊臣，且以計忍而陰銜之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao heard and knew; because Yu and the others were old ministers, and moreover because of the plan he bore it and secretly harbored resentment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, hearing it, tolerated the old ministers for the moment but nursed a grudge.

manualTranslations.zh: 後因會，以毒酒飲彧，傳酒人私減之。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, at a gathering, he had Yu drink poisoned wine; the wine-passer privately reduced it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet he gave Wan Yu poisoned wine, but the cupbearer diluted it.

manualTranslations.zh: 又飲留平，平覺之，服他藥以解，得不死。
manualTranslations.literal: Again he had Liu Ping drink; Ping perceived it; he took other medicine to resolve it and obtained not dying.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He tried the same on Liu Ping, who detected it, took antidote, and survived.

manualTranslations.zh: 彧自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Yu killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wan Yu killed himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 平憂懣，月餘亦死。
manualTranslations.literal: Ping was worried and resentful; after more than a month he also died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Ping died of grief a month later.

manualTranslations.zh: 何定姦穢發聞，伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: He Ding's wickedness and filth having been exposed and heard, he was executed by law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Ding's corruption was exposed and he was executed.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓以其惡似張布，追改定名爲布。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao, because his wickedness resembled Zhang Bu's, pursued changing Ding's name to Bu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, likening him to Zhang Bu, posthumously renamed He Ding to He Bu.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：定，汝南人，本孫權給使也，後出補吏。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ding was a Runan man; originally Sun Quan's attendant runner; later he went out to fill an official post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan identifies He Ding of Runan as a former personal runner of Sun Quan who later entered official service.

manualTranslations.zh: 定佞邪僭媚，自表先帝舊人，求還內侍，皓以爲樓下都尉，典知酤糴事，專爲威福。
manualTranslations.literal: Ding was fawning, wicked, and presumptuously flattering; on his own memorial he said he was an old man of the late emperor and begged return to inner attendance; Hao made him commandant of the lower pavilion, in charge of knowing the sale of wine and grain affairs, exclusively wielding authority and blessing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Ding flattered his way back to palace service as lower-pavilion commandant controlling wine and grain monopolies, abusing power for personal gain.

manualTranslations.zh: 而皓信任，委以衆事。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet Hao trusted him and entrusted him with the multitude of affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao trusted him with sweeping authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 定爲子求少府李勗女，不許。
manualTranslations.literal: Ding sought for his son the daughter of Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Li Xu; [Xu] did not consent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Ding sought Chamberlain Li Xu's daughter for his son and was refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 定挾忿譖勗於皓，皓尺口誅之，焚其尸。
manualTranslations.literal: Ding, holding resentment, slandered Xu before Hao; Hao with a foot-length mouth executed him and burned his corpse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Ding slandered Li Xu until Sun Hao had him dismembered and his corpse burned.

manualTranslations.zh: 定又使諸將各上好犬，皆千里遠求，一犬至直數千匹。
manualTranslations.literal: Again Ding had various generals each present fine dogs; all sought them from a thousand li away; one dog arriving was worth several thousand bolts of silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Ding forced generals to procure fine hounds from afar at costs of thousands of bolts of silk per dog.

manualTranslations.zh: 御犬率具纓，直錢一萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Imperial hounds mostly wore full bridles; straight price ten thousand cash.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Palace hounds wore full bridles worth ten thousand cash each.

manualTranslations.zh: 一犬一兵，養以捕兎供厨。
manualTranslations.literal: One dog one soldier, reared to catch rabbits to supply the kitchen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each dog had a dedicated soldier to hunt rabbits for the kitchen.

manualTranslations.zh: 所獲無幾。
manualTranslations.literal: What was obtained was not several.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The yield was negligible.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳人皆歸罪於定，而皓以爲忠勤，賜爵列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The people of Wu all attributed the blame to Ding, yet Hao considered him loyal and diligent and granted him noble rank as a ranked marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wu blamed He Ding, yet Sun Hao called him loyal and enfeoffed him as marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳歷》曰：中書郎奚熙譖宛陵令賀惠。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu li states: Palace Secretary Xi Xi slandered Wanling Magistrate He Hui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu li records Palace Secretary Xi Xi denouncing Wanling magistrate He Hui.

manualTranslations.zh: 惠，劭弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui was Younger Brother Shao's younger brother.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Hui was the younger brother of He Shao.

manualTranslations.zh: 遣使者徐粲訊治，熙又譖粲顧護不即決斷。
manualTranslations.literal: [Hao] sent envoy Xu Can to investigate and try; Xi again slandered Can for looking to protect and not immediately deciding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao sent Xu Can to try the case; Xi Xi then accused Xu Can of shielding He Hui.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓遣使就宛陵斬粲，收惠付獄。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao sent an envoy to Wanling to behead Can and take Hui into prison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao had Xu Can beheaded at Wanling and threw He Hui in prison.

manualTranslations.zh: 會赦得免。
manualTranslations.literal: Meeting an amnesty he obtained release.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He Hui was freed when an amnesty followed.

items.acceptedSourceText: 鳳皇元年272年秋八月，徵西陵督步闡。闡不應，據城降晉。遣樂鄉都督陸抗圍取闡，闡衆悉降。闡及同計數十人皆夷三族。大赦。是歲右丞相萬彧被譴憂死，徙其子弟於廬陵。《江表傳》曰：初皓游華里，彧與丁奉、留平密謀曰：「此行不急，若至華里不歸，社稷事重，不得不自還。」此語頗泄。皓聞知，以彧等舊臣，且以計忍而陰銜之。後因會，以毒酒飲彧，傳酒人私減之。又飲留平，平覺之，服他藥以解，得不死。彧自殺。平憂懣，月餘亦死。何定姦穢發聞，伏誅。皓以其惡似張布，追改定名爲布。《江表傳》曰：定，汝南人，本孫權給使也，後出補吏。定佞邪僭媚，自表先帝舊人，求還內侍，皓以爲樓下都尉，典知酤糴事，專爲威福。而皓信任，委以衆事。定爲子求少府李勗女，不許。定挾忿譖勗於皓，皓尺口誅之，焚其尸。定又使諸將各上好犬，皆千里遠求，一犬至直數千匹。御犬率具纓，直錢一萬。一犬一兵，養以捕兎供厨。所獲無幾。吳人皆歸罪於定，而皓以爲忠勤，賜爵列侯。《吳歷》曰：中書郎奚熙譖宛陵令賀惠。惠，劭弟也。遣使者徐粲訊治，熙又譖粲顧護不即決斷。皓遣使就宛陵斬粲，收惠付獄。會赦得免。

sourceRange.text: 元興元年264年八月，以上大將軍施績、大將軍丁奉爲左右大司馬，張布爲驃騎將軍，加侍中，諸增位班賞，一皆如舊。九月，貶太后爲景皇后，追謚父和曰文皇帝，尊母何爲太后。十月，封休太子𩅦爲豫章王，次子汝南王，次子梁王，次子陳王，立皇后滕氏。《江表傳》曰：皓初立，發優詔，恤士民，開倉廩，振貧乏，科出宮女以配無妻，禽獸擾於苑者皆放之。當時翕然稱爲明主。皓旣得志，麤暴驕盈，多忌諱，好酒色，大小失望。興、布竊悔之。或以譖皓，十一月，誅興、布。十二月，孫休葬定陵。封后父滕牧爲高密侯，《吳歷》曰：牧本名密，避丁密，改名牧，丁密避牧，改名爲固。舅何洪等三人皆列侯。是歲，魏置交阯太守之郡。晉文帝爲魏相國，遣昔吳壽春城降將徐紹、孫彧銜命齎書，陳事勢利害，以申喻皓。《漢晉春秋》載晉文王與皓書曰：「聖人稱有君臣然後有上下禮義，是故大必字小，小必事大，然後上下安服，羣生獲所。逮至末塗，純德旣毀，勦民之命，以爭彊於天下，違禮順之至理，則仁者弗由也。方今主上聖明，覆帱無外，僕備位宰輔，屬當國重。唯華夏乖殊，方隅圮裂，六十餘載，金革亟動，無年不戰，暴骸喪元，困悴罔定，每用悼心，坐以待旦。將欲止戈興仁，爲百姓請命，故分命偏師，平定蜀漢，役未經年，全軍獨克。于時猛將謀夫，朝臣庶士，咸以奉天時之宜，就旣征之軍，藉吞敵之勢，宜遂回旗東指，以臨吳境。舟師汎江，順流而下，陸軍南轅，取徑四郡，兼成都之械，漕巴漢之粟，然後以中軍整旅，三方雲會，未及浹辰，可使江表厎平，南夏順軌。然國朝深惟伐蜀之舉，雖有靜難之功，亦悼蜀民獨罹其害，戰於緜竹者，自元帥以下並受斬戮，伏尸蔽地，血流丹野。一之於前，猶追恨不忍，況重之於後乎？是故旋師案甲，思與南邦共全百姓之命。夫料力忖勢，度資量險，遠考古昔廢興之理，近鑒西蜀安危之効，隆德保祚，去危即順，屈己以寧四海者，仁哲之高致也；履危偷安，隕德覆祚，而不稱於後世者，非智者之所居也。今朝廷遣徐紹、孫彧獻書喻懷，若書御於前，必少留意，回慮革筭，結歡弭兵，共爲一家，惠矜吳會，施及中土，豈不泰哉！此昭心之大願也，敢不承受。若不獲命，則普天率土，期於大同，雖重干戈，固不獲已也。」甘露元年265年三月，皓遣使隨紹、彧報書曰：「知以高世之才，處宰輔之任，漸導之功，勤亦至矣。孤以不德，階承統緒，思與賢良共濟世道，而以壅隔未有所緣，嘉意允著，深用依依。今遣光祿大夫紀陟、五官中郎將弘璆宣明至懷。」《江表傳》曰：皓書兩頭言白，稱名言而不著姓。《吳錄》曰：陟字子上，丹楊人。初爲中書郎，孫峻使詰南陽王和，令其引分。陟密使令正辭自理，峻怒。陟懼，閉門不出。孫休時，父亮爲尚書令，而陟爲中書令，每朝會，詔以屏風隔其座。出爲豫章太守。干寶《晉紀》曰：陟、璆奉使如魏，入境而問諱，入國而問俗。壽春將王布示之馬射，旣而問之曰：「吳之君子亦能斯乎？」陟曰：「此軍人騎士肄業所及，士大夫君子未有爲之者矣。」布大慙。旣至，魏帝見之，使儐問曰：「來時吳王何如？」陟對曰：「來時皇帝臨軒，百寮陪位，御膳無恙。」晉文王饗之，百寮畢會，使儐者告曰：「某者安樂公也，某者匈奴單于也。」陟曰：「西主失土，爲君王所禮，位同三代，莫不感義，匈奴邊塞難羈之國，君王懷之，親在坐席，此誠威恩遠著。」又問：「吳之戍備幾何？」對曰：「自西陵以至江都，五千七百里。」又問曰：「道里甚遠，難爲堅固？」對曰：「疆界雖遠，而其險要必爭之地，不過數四，猶人雖有八尺之軀靡不受患，其護風寒亦數處耳。」文王善之，厚爲之禮。臣松之以爲人有八尺之體靡不受患，防護風寒豈唯數處？取譬若此，未足稱能。若曰譬如金城萬雉，所急防者四門而已。方陟此對，不猶愈乎！《吳錄》曰：皓以諸父與和相連及者，家屬皆徙東冶，唯陟以有密旨，特封子孚都亭侯。孚弟瞻，字思遠，入仕晉驃騎將軍。弘璆，曲阿人，弘咨之孫，權外甥也。璆後至中書令、太子少傅。紹行到濡須，召還殺之，徙其家屬建安，始有白紹稱美中國者故也。夏四月，蔣陵言甘露降，於是改年大赦。秋七月，皓逼殺景后朱氏，亡不在正殿，於苑中小屋治喪，衆知其非疾病，莫不痛切。又送休四子於吳小城，尋復追殺大者二人。九月，從西陵督步闡表，徙都武昌，御史大夫丁固、右將軍諸葛靚鎮建業。陟、璆至洛，遇晉文帝崩，十一月，乃遣還。皓至武昌，又大赦。以零陵南部爲始安郡，桂陽南部爲始興郡。十二月，晉受禪。寶鼎元年正月，遣大鴻臚張儼、五官中郎將丁忠弔祭晉文帝。及還，儼道病死。《吳錄》曰：儼字子節，吳人也。弱冠知名，歷顯位，以博聞多識，拜大鴻臚。使于晉，皓謂儼曰：「今南北通好，以君爲有出境之才，故相屈行。」對曰：「皇皇者華，蒙其榮耀，無古人延譽之美，磨厲鋒鍔，思不辱命。」旣至，車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、侍中荀勗等欲傲以所不知而不能屈。尚書僕射羊祜、尚書何楨並結縞帶之好。忠說皓曰：「北方守戰之具不設，弋陽可襲而取。」皓訪羣臣，鎮西大將軍陸凱曰：「夫兵不得已而用之耳，且三國鼎立已來，更相侵伐，無歲寧居。今彊敵新并巴蜀，有兼土之實，而遣使求親，欲息兵役，不可謂其求援於我。今敵形勢方彊，而欲徼幸求勝，未見其利也。」車騎將軍劉纂曰：「天生五才，誰能去兵？譎詐相雄，有自來矣。若其有闕，庸可棄乎？宜遣閒諜，以觀其勢。」皓陰納纂言，且以蜀新平，故不行，然遂自絕。八月，所在言得大鼎，於是改年，大赦。以陸凱爲左丞相，常侍萬彧爲右丞相。冬十月，永安山賊施但等聚衆數千人，《吳錄》曰：永安今武康縣也。劫皓庶弟永安侯謙出烏程，取孫和陵上鼓吹曲蓋。比至建業，衆萬餘人。丁固、諸葛靚逆之於牛屯，大戰，但等敗走。獲謙，謙自殺。《漢晉春秋》曰：初望氣者云荊州有王氣破揚州而建業宮不利，故皓徙武昌，遣使者發民掘荊州界大臣名家冢與山岡連者以厭之。旣聞但反，自以爲徙土得計也。使數百人鼓譟入建業，殺但妻子，云天子使荊州兵來破揚州賊，以厭前氣。分會稽爲東陽郡，分吳、丹楊爲吳興郡。皓詔曰：「古者分土建國，所以襃賞賢能，廣樹藩屏。秦毀五等爲三十六郡，漢室初興，闓立乃至百五，因事制宜，蓋無常數也。今吳郡陽羨、永安、餘杭、臨水及丹楊故鄣、安吉、原鄉、於潛諸縣，地勢水流之便，悉注烏程，旣宜立郡以鎮山越，且以藩衞明陵，奉承大祭，不亦可乎！其亟分此九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程。」以零陵北部爲邵陵郡。十二月，皓還都建業，衞將軍滕牧留鎮武昌。

context.afterSource: 二年春，大赦。
