manualTranslations.zh: 元興元年264年八月，以上大將軍施績、大將軍丁奉爲左右大司馬，張布爲驃騎將軍，加侍中，諸增位班賞，一皆如舊。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanxing (264), Senior General Shi Ji and Grand General Ding Feng were made left and right grand marshals; Zhang Bu was made general of agile cavalry with added status as palace attendant; all additions of rank and rewards were entirely as before.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yuanxing 1 (264) Senior General Shi Ji and Grand General Ding Feng became left and right grand marshals, Zhang Bu was named general of agile cavalry with palace attendant status, and other promotions followed precedent.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，貶太后爲景皇后，追謚父和曰文皇帝，尊母何爲太后。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month the empress dowager was demoted to Empress Jing; the father He was posthumously titled Emperor Wen; the mother He was honored as empress dowager.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the former empress dowager was reduced to Empress Jing, Sun He was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, and Lady He was elevated as empress dowager.

manualTranslations.zh: 十月，封休太子𩅦爲豫章王，次子汝南王，次子梁王，次子陳王，立皇后滕氏。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month Sun Xiu's crown prince (whose name uses the rare graph) was enfeoffed as prince of Yuzhang; the second son as prince of Runan; the third son as prince of Liang; the fourth son as prince of Chen; Empress Teng was established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Sun Xiu's crown prince (whose name uses the rare graph) became prince of Yuzhang, three younger sons received princely titles, and Lady Teng was crowned empress.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓初立，發優詔，恤士民，開倉廩，振貧乏，科出宮女以配無妻，禽獸擾於苑者皆放之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: When Hao had first been established, he issued a generous edict, showed compassion to scholars and commoners, opened granaries, relieved the poor and exhausted, assessed palace women to match the wifeless, and birds and beasts troubling the park were all released.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says that at his accession Sun Hao issued benevolent edicts, opened granaries, paired palace women with unmarried men, and freed park animals—measures that briefly won praise.

manualTranslations.zh: 當時翕然稱爲明主。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time there was unanimous acclaim calling him a enlightened ruler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For a moment the court hailed him as an enlightened sovereign.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓旣得志，麤暴驕盈，多忌諱，好酒色，大小失望。
manualTranslations.literal: Once Hao had obtained his aim, he was coarse, violent, arrogant, and overbearing, with many taboos, fond of wine and women; great and small were disappointed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once secure on the throne he turned coarse, arrogant, jealous, and debauched, and hope collapsed high and low.

manualTranslations.zh: 興、布竊悔之。
manualTranslations.literal: Xing and Bu secretly regretted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu privately regretted their choice.

manualTranslations.zh: 或以譖皓，十一月，誅興、布。
manualTranslations.literal: Some slandered Hao; in the eleventh month Xing and Bu were executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When rivals denounced them to Sun Hao, both men were executed in the eleventh month.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，孫休葬定陵。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month Sun Xiu was buried at Dingling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Sun Xiu was interred at Dingling.

manualTranslations.zh: 封后父滕牧爲高密侯，《吳歷》曰：牧本名密，避丁密，改名牧，丁密避牧，改名爲固。
manualTranslations.literal: The empress's father Teng Mu was enfeoffed as marquis of Gaomi; the Wu li states: Mu's original name was Mi; to avoid Ding Mi he changed his name to Mu; Ding Mi avoided Mu and changed his name to Gu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Teng's father Teng Mu received Gaomi marquisate; the Wu li notes taboo-name swaps between Teng Mu (originally Mi) and Ding Mi (who renamed himself Gu).

manualTranslations.zh: 舅何洪等三人皆列侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The maternal uncles He Hong and three others were all made ranked marquises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Three maternal uncles of the He clan, including He Hong, were all enfeoffed as marquises.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，魏置交阯太守之郡。
manualTranslations.literal: This year Wei established the commandery of the administrator of Jiaozhi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Wei re-established the Jiaozhi commandery administration.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉文帝爲魏相國，遣昔吳壽春城降將徐紹、孫彧銜命齎書，陳事勢利害，以申喻皓。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin Emperor Wen was chancellor of state for Wei and sent the former Wu Shouchun garrison defectors Xu Shao and Sun Yu bearing credentials with a letter, setting forth the situation's advantages and harms, to admonish Hao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao, as Wei's chancellor of state, dispatched former Wu defectors Xu Shao and Sun Yu from Shouchun with a letter explaining the strategic stakes to warn Sun Hao.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》載晉文王與皓書曰：「聖人稱有君臣然後有上下禮義，是故大必字小，小必事大，然後上下安服，羣生獲所。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu carries Jin Emperor Wen's letter to Hao, which states: "The sages say that only when there are ruler and minister are there thereafter upper and lower and ritual and righteousness; therefore the great must title the small, the small must serve the great—only then do upper and lower rest secure and the multitude obtain their places.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Jin Chunqiu preserves Sima Zhao's letter to Sun Hao: "The sages teach that hierarchy begins with ruler and minister—the great must shelter the small, the small must serve the great—so that order prevails and the people find their place.

manualTranslations.zh: 逮至末塗，純德旣毀，勦民之命，以爭彊於天下，違禮順之至理，則仁者弗由也。
manualTranslations.literal: Reaching the final paths, pure virtue was already destroyed; the lives of the people were cut down in striving for strength in all under Heaven, violating the utmost principle of according with ritual—then the benevolent will not go that way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In these last days pure rule has collapsed and armies squander civilian lives across the realm, defying the way of ritual—no benevolent man can endorse that course.

manualTranslations.zh: 方今主上聖明，覆帱無外，僕備位宰輔，屬當國重。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the sovereign above is sagely and enlightened, covering and sheltering without exclusion; I, humble, fill the place of chief minister and am entrusted with the weight of the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our emperor is sage and his canopy shelters all; I stand as chancellor bearing the nation's weight.

manualTranslations.zh: 唯華夏乖殊，方隅圮裂，六十餘載，金革亟動，無年不戰，暴骸喪元，困悴罔定，每用悼心，坐以待旦。
manualTranslations.literal: Only the Central States are sundered and apart; territories and corners collapse and split—more than sixty years; metal and leather move urgently; no year without battle; exposed corpses lose heads; the weary and emaciated are unsettled; each time I use a grieving heart and sit awaiting dawn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For sixty years the heartland has been riven, war never ceasing, corpses heaped and the people broken—I grieve nightly until dawn.

manualTranslations.zh: 將欲止戈興仁，爲百姓請命，故分命偏師，平定蜀漢，役未經年，全軍獨克。
manualTranslations.literal: Wishing to halt weapons and raise benevolence, to plead for the people's lives, therefore [we] divided orders to partial armies and pacified Shu-Han; the campaign had not passed a year when the whole army alone conquered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeking to sheathe swords and plead for the people, we sent armies westward and conquered Shu within a year.

manualTranslations.zh: 于時猛將謀夫，朝臣庶士，咸以奉天時之宜，就旣征之軍，藉吞敵之勢，宜遂回旗東指，以臨吳境。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time fierce generals and planners, court ministers and common scholars, all considered that, conforming to Heaven's season's fitness, joining the army already on campaign, borrowing the momentum of swallowing the enemy, it was fitting to turn the banners east and come to the Wu border.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our generals and ministers then urged that, with Heaven's mandate, victorious armies, and Shu's arsenals in hand, we should wheel east against Wu.

manualTranslations.zh: 舟師汎江，順流而下，陸軍南轅，取徑四郡，兼成都之械，漕巴漢之粟，然後以中軍整旅，三方雲會，未及浹辰，可使江表厎平，南夏順軌。
manualTranslations.literal: The fleet floated on the river, flowing downstream; the land army turned its shafts south, taking the direct route through the four commanderies, combining Chengdu's engines, transporting Ba and Han grain—then with the central army ordering the hosts, the three directions cloud-gathering, before a full cycle of days one could make the lands beyond the river level, and southern Xia follow the track.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fleets could descend the Yangzi while armies marched south through four commanderies, hauling Shu weapons and Ba-Han grain until a converging strike flattened the south bank in weeks.

manualTranslations.zh: 然國朝深惟伐蜀之舉，雖有靜難之功，亦悼蜀民獨罹其害，戰於緜竹者，自元帥以下並受斬戮，伏尸蔽地，血流丹野。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the court deeply reflected that the campaign against Shu, though it had the merit of quelling calamity, also grieved that the Shu people alone suffered its harm; those who fought at Mianzhu, from the commander-in-chief down, all received beheading and slaughter; corpses lay covering the ground; blood flowed over cinnabar fields.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the court reflected that although the Shu campaign restored order, the Shu people alone bore its cost—from commanders down to soldiers slaughtered at Mianzhu until blood soaked the fields.

manualTranslations.zh: 一之於前，猶追恨不忍，況重之於後乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Once before was already enough to pursue regret and not bear it—how much more a second time?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once was tragedy enough to haunt us—how could we repeat it?

manualTranslations.zh: 是故旋師案甲，思與南邦共全百姓之命。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore [we] turned the army and set aside armor, thinking to join the southern state in preserving the people's lives together.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So we halted the advance and sheathed our arms, hoping to preserve Wu's people together with you.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫料力忖勢，度資量險，遠考古昔廢興之理，近鑒西蜀安危之効，隆德保祚，去危即順，屈己以寧四海者，仁哲之高致也；
manualTranslations.literal: To estimate strength and weigh momentum, measure resources and gauge danger, examine from afar the principles of rise and fall in antiquity, and reflect near at hand on the effects of Western Shu's safety and peril—preserving lofty virtue and securing the mandate, leaving danger and taking accord, humbling oneself to settle the four seas: this is the lofty aim of the benevolent and wise;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Weighing power and precedent, the wise choose magnanimity over conquest—preserving virtue, accepting submission, and humbling oneself to pacify the realm;

manualTranslations.zh: 履危偷安，隕德覆祚，而不稱於後世者，非智者之所居也。
manualTranslations.literal: treading danger and stealing peace, losing virtue and overturning the mandate, yet not being praised by later generations: this is not where the wise dwell.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: while clinging to peril for a false peace and losing moral standing wins no praise from posterity.

manualTranslations.zh: 今朝廷遣徐紹、孫彧獻書喻懷，若書御於前，必少留意，回慮革筭，結歡弭兵，共爲一家，惠矜吳會，施及中土，豈不泰哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Now the court sends Xu Shao and Sun Yu presenting letters to explain our hearts; if the letter is received before you, you will surely give it slight attention, turn your thoughts and change your plans, join in friendship and cease weapons, become one family together, extend favor and pity to Wu and Hui, reaching to the central lands—would that not be great peace!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We send Xu Shao and Sun Yu with this letter; read it carefully, reconsider your course, make peace, and join as one household extending mercy to Wu and the central provinces—would that not be sublime peace!

manualTranslations.zh: 此昭心之大願也，敢不承受。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the great wish made manifest in the heart; how dare [I] not receive it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is our heartfelt wish, and I dare not refuse it.

manualTranslations.zh: 若不獲命，則普天率土，期於大同，雖重干戈，固不獲已也。」
manualTranslations.literal: If [I] do not obtain the mandate, then throughout Heaven and the lands within the seas the term is set on great unity; though weapons be heavy, indeed [I] cannot avoid it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But if you reject us, all under Heaven will still march toward unity—and war, however bitter, will be unavoidable."

manualTranslations.zh: 甘露元年265年三月，皓遣使隨紹、彧報書曰：「知以高世之才，處宰輔之任，漸導之功，勤亦至矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Ganlu (265), Hao sent envoys following Shao and Yu with a reply stating: "Knowing that with talent surpassing the age you occupy the place of chief minister, the merit of gradual guidance—your diligence has also reached the utmost.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third month of Ganlu 1 (265) Sun Hao replied through envoys escorted by Xu Shao and Sun Yu: "Knowing your transcendent ability as chief minister and the tireless guidance you have shown,

manualTranslations.zh: 孤以不德，階承統緒，思與賢良共濟世道，而以壅隔未有所緣，嘉意允著，深用依依。
manualTranslations.literal: I, solitary, with lacking virtue, stepwise inherit the line and succession; I think to join with the worthy and good to ferry the age's way together; yet because of blockage and separation there has been no connection; your fine intent is clearly granted—deeply I am attached.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I, lacking virtue, have inherited the throne and wish to work with worthy men to steady the age, yet distance has blocked us—your gracious intent moves me deeply.

manualTranslations.zh: 今遣光祿大夫紀陟、五官中郎將弘璆宣明至懷。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now I send Household Counsellor Ji Zhi and Palace Cadet-General Hong Qiu to declare and make clear the utmost heart."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I now send Household Counsellor Ji Zhi and Palace Cadet-General Hong Qiu to convey my sincere regard."

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓書兩頭言白，稱名言而不著姓。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Hao's letter at both ends said bai; it used the personal name and did not write the surname.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan notes Sun Hao's letter opened and closed with "bai" and used his personal name without surname—an assertion of equality.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳錄》曰：陟字子上，丹楊人。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Zhi, courtesy name Zishang, was a Danyang man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu identifies Ji Zhi, courtesy Zishang, as a native of Danyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 初爲中書郎，孫峻使詰南陽王和，令其引分。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he was palace secretary; Sun Jun sent him to interrogate the prince of Nanyang He, ordering him to cite grounds for suicide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He first served as palace secretary until Sun Jun ordered him to interrogate Prince He of Nanyang and force a confession of guilt.

manualTranslations.zh: 陟密使令正辭自理，峻怒。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi secretly had him use upright words to explain himself; Jun was angry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi secretly coached Prince He to answer with righteous defense, enraging Sun Jun.

manualTranslations.zh: 陟懼，閉門不出。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi was afraid and closed his door and did not go out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisal, Ji Zhi barricaded himself at home.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫休時，父亮爲尚書令，而陟爲中書令，每朝會，詔以屏風隔其座。
manualTranslations.literal: In Sun Xiu's time, his father Liang was director of the masters of writing while Zhi was director of the palace secretariat; at each court assembly an edict used a screen to separate their seats.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under Sun Xiu, when his father Teng Liang headed the Secretariat and Ji Zhi headed the palace secretariat, edicts ordered a screen between their seats at court.

manualTranslations.zh: 出爲豫章太守。
manualTranslations.literal: He went out as administrator of Yuzhang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi later went out to govern Yuzhang.

manualTranslations.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：陟、璆奉使如魏，入境而問諱，入國而問俗。
manualTranslations.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: Zhi and Qiu, on mission to Wei, upon entering the border inquired about taboo names; upon entering the state inquired about customs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's Jin Ji records that Ji Zhi and Hong Qiu, entering Wei, first asked about taboo names and local customs.

manualTranslations.zh: 壽春將王布示之馬射，旣而問之曰：「吳之君子亦能斯乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: Shouchun general Wang Bu showed them horse archery; afterward he asked them: "Can the gentlemen of Wu also do this?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shouchun commander Wang Bu demonstrated mounted archery and asked, "Can Wu gentlemen match this?"

manualTranslations.zh: 陟曰：「此軍人騎士肄業所及，士大夫君子未有爲之者矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi said: "This is what military riders and knights practice in training; scholar-gentlemen and junzi have not yet done it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi replied, "That is cavalry drill—court scholars do not perform such feats."

manualTranslations.zh: 布大慙。
manualTranslations.literal: Bu was greatly ashamed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Bu flushed with embarrassment.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣至，魏帝見之，使儐問曰：「來時吳王何如？」
manualTranslations.literal: Having arrived, the Wei emperor saw them and had attendants ask: "When you came, what was the king of Wu like?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At audience the Wei emperor's attendants asked, "What was the Wu sovereign like when you departed?"

manualTranslations.zh: 陟對曰：「來時皇帝臨軒，百寮陪位，御膳無恙。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi answered: "When we came the emperor faced the hall; the hundred officials attended in place; imperial meals were without ailment."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi answered, "When we left, the emperor held court in good health with the full bureaucracy in attendance."

manualTranslations.zh: 晉文王饗之，百寮畢會，使儐者告曰：「某者安樂公也，某者匈奴單于也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Jin Emperor Wen feasted them; the hundred officials all assembled; he had attendants announce: "So-and-so is Duke of Peace and Joy; so-and-so is the Xiongnu chanyu."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao entertained them before the full court, introducing guests as "the Duke of Peace and Joy" and "the Xiongnu chanyu."

manualTranslations.zh: 陟曰：「西主失土，爲君王所禮，位同三代，莫不感義，匈奴邊塞難羈之國，君王懷之，親在坐席，此誠威恩遠著。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi said: "The western lord lost his lands and is treated with ritual by the king; his rank equals the Three Dynasties—none are not moved by righteousness; the Xiongnu are a border state hard to restrain—the king cherishes them; [they are] personally at the seat—this truly is majesty and favor reaching far and showing."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi replied, "Liu Shan lost his realm yet receives royal courtesy like a Three Dynasties sovereign—an act of righteous majesty; the Xiongnu are unruly border folk yet sit here as honored guests—your grace reaches far indeed."

manualTranslations.zh: 又問：「吳之戍備幾何？」
manualTranslations.literal: He again asked: "How much is Wu's frontier defense?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They asked again, "How long is Wu's frontier defense?"

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「自西陵以至江都，五千七百里。」
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "From Xiling to Jiangdu, five thousand seven hundred li."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "From Xiling to Jiangdu, five thousand seven hundred li."

manualTranslations.zh: 又問曰：「道里甚遠，難爲堅固？」
manualTranslations.literal: He again asked: "The roads and li are very far—how can it be firm and solid?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They pressed, "Such distances—how can defenses hold?"

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「疆界雖遠，而其險要必爭之地，不過數四，猶人雖有八尺之軀靡不受患，其護風寒亦數處耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "Though the border is far, yet among its strategic defiles the places that must be contested are no more than several score of four; it is like a man who though having an eight-chi body nowhere escapes affliction—his guarding against wind and cold is also only several places."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He answered, "Distance matters less than choke points—only a handful of strongholds decide the frontier, as a man needs but a few garments against the cold."

manualTranslations.zh: 文王善之，厚爲之禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen approved of this and richly bestowed rites upon them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao was pleased and treated them generously.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣松之以爲人有八尺之體靡不受患，防護風寒豈唯數處？
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: A man with an eight-chi body nowhere escapes affliction—against wind and cold is it only several places?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments: If a man's whole body feels the cold, can protection be limited to a few spots?

manualTranslations.zh: 取譬若此，未足稱能。
manualTranslations.literal: Taking a comparison like this is not sufficient to be called able.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such a simile hardly proves skill.

manualTranslations.zh: 若曰譬如金城萬雉，所急防者四門而已。
manualTranslations.literal: If one said it is like a golden city with ten thousand battlements—the places urgently defended are only the four gates—that would suffice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Better to say a golden city relies on only four gates—now that would be apt.

manualTranslations.zh: 方陟此對，不猶愈乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Compared with Zhi's this reply—is it not still better!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That image would have served Ji Zhi better than his own.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳錄》曰：皓以諸父與和相連及者，家屬皆徙東冶，唯陟以有密旨，特封子孚都亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Hao, because paternal uncles connected with He were implicated, their families were all moved to Dongye; only Zhi, because he had secret instructions, was specially enfeoffed with his son Fu as marquis of Duting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu notes Sun Hao exiled kinsmen linked to Sun He to Dongye but enfeoffed Ji Zhi's son Fu as marquis of Duting for carrying secret credentials.

manualTranslations.zh: 孚弟瞻，字思遠，入仕晉驃騎將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu's younger brother Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, entered service in Jin as general of agile cavalry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi's younger son Zhan, courtesy Siyuan, later served Jin as general of agile cavalry.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘璆，曲阿人，弘咨之孫，權外甥也。
manualTranslations.literal: Hong Qiu was a Qu'e man, grandson of Hong Zi, Sun Quan's sister's son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong Qiu of Qu'e was grandson of Hong Zi and nephew of Sun Quan.

manualTranslations.zh: 璆後至中書令、太子少傅。
manualTranslations.literal: Qiu later reached director of the palace secretariat and junior tutor to the crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hong Qiu later became director of the palace secretariat and junior tutor to the crown prince.

manualTranslations.zh: 紹行到濡須，召還殺之，徙其家屬建安，始有白紹稱美中國者故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Shao, traveling as far as Ruxu, was summoned back and killed; his family was moved to Jian'an—because at the beginning there were those who said Shao praised the Central States.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xu Shao, recalled from Ruxu, was executed and his family exiled to Jian'an for earlier praise of the north.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏四月，蔣陵言甘露降，於是改年大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Jiangling reported sweet dew descending; thereupon the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That summer's fourth month Jiangling reported sweet dew, prompting a new reign title and general amnesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋七月，皓逼殺景后朱氏，亡不在正殿，於苑中小屋治喪，衆知其非疾病，莫不痛切。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Hao forced Empress Jing Lady Zhu to death; she died not in the main hall; in a small house in the park they managed the mourning; the multitude knew it was not illness and none did not grieve bitterly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn's seventh month Sun Hao murdered Empress Jing Lady Zhu in a park hut rather than the palace hall—a killing every courtier mourned.

manualTranslations.zh: 又送休四子於吳小城，尋復追殺大者二人。
manualTranslations.literal: Again he sent Sun Xiu's four sons to the small city of Wu; soon afterward he again pursued and killed the two eldest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He banished Sun Xiu's four sons to Wu's minor fortress, then hunted down and killed the two eldest.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，從西陵督步闡表，徙都武昌，御史大夫丁固、右將軍諸葛靚鎮建業。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month, following the memorial of Xiling area commander Bu Chan, the capital was moved to Wuchang; Imperial Counselor Ding Gu and Right General Zhuge Jing guarded Jianye.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, heeding Xiling commander Bu Chan's memorial, Sun Hao moved the capital to Wuchang while Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing held Jianye.

manualTranslations.zh: 陟、璆至洛，遇晉文帝崩，十一月，乃遣還。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi and Qiu reached Luoyang; they encountered Jin Emperor Wen's death; in the eleventh month they were then sent back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ji Zhi and Hong Qiu reached Luoyang as Sima Zhao died and were sent home in the eleventh month.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓至武昌，又大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hao reached Wuchang, again a general amnesty was proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Wuchang Sun Hao declared another general amnesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 以零陵南部爲始安郡，桂陽南部爲始興郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The southern part of Lingling was made Shian commandery; the southern part of Guiyang was made Shixing commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Southern Lingling became Shian commandery and southern Guiyang became Shixing commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，晉受禪。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month Jin received the abdication.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jin accepted Wei's abdication.

manualTranslations.zh: 寶鼎元年正月，遣大鴻臚張儼、五官中郎將丁忠弔祭晉文帝。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Baoding, Grand Herald Zhang Yan and Palace Cadet-General Ding Zhong were sent to mourn and sacrifice to Jin Emperor Wen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Baoding 1, first month, Grand Herald Zhang Yan and Palace Cadet-General Ding Zhong were dispatched to mourn Sima Zhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 及還，儼道病死。
manualTranslations.literal: Upon returning, Yan died of illness on the road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan died en route home.

manualTranslations.zh: 《吳錄》曰：儼字子節，吳人也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wu lu states: Yan, courtesy name Zijie, was a Wu man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wu lu identifies Zhang Yan, courtesy Zijie, as a Wu native.

manualTranslations.zh: 弱冠知名，歷顯位，以博聞多識，拜大鴻臚。
manualTranslations.literal: In weak cap he was famed; he passed through prominent positions; because of broad learning and much knowledge he was appointed grand herald.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Famed from youth and widely learned, he rose to grand herald.

manualTranslations.zh: 使于晉，皓謂儼曰：「今南北通好，以君爲有出境之才，故相屈行。」
manualTranslations.literal: On mission to Jin, Hao told Yan: "Now north and south are in good relations; because you have talent for going beyond the border, therefore [we] bend to send you on the journey."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before his Jin mission Sun Hao told him, "With peace between north and south I rely on your diplomatic skill for this embassy."

manualTranslations.zh: 對曰：「皇皇者華，蒙其榮耀，無古人延譽之美，磨厲鋒鍔，思不辱命。」
manualTranslations.literal: He answered: "Splendid is the flower; [I] receive its glory and splendor—without the ancients' extension of reputation's beauty, [I] hone sharp blades, thinking not to disgrace the mandate."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He replied with a classical flourish, vowing to sharpen his wit and not dishonor the mission.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣至，車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、侍中荀勗等欲傲以所不知而不能屈。
manualTranslations.literal: Having arrived, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Director of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Palace Attendant Xun Xu and others wished to condescend with what he did not know yet could not bend him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Jia Chong, Pei Xiu, and Xun Xu tried to stump him and failed.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚書僕射羊祜、尚書何楨並結縞帶之好。
manualTranslations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Hu and Master of Writing He Zhen both formed friendships tied with white silk sashes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Hu and Master of Writing He Zhen befriended him warmly.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠說皓曰：「北方守戰之具不設，弋陽可襲而取。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhong urged Hao: "The north's defensive war equipment is not set up—Yiyang can be raided and taken."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ding Zhong urged Sun Hao that northern defenses were slack and Yiyang could be seized.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓訪羣臣，鎮西大將軍陸凱曰：「夫兵不得已而用之耳，且三國鼎立已來，更相侵伐，無歲寧居。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao consulted the host of ministers; General Who Guards the West Lu Kai said: "Arms are used only when there is no alternative; moreover since the three states stood as tripods, they have mutually invaded and attacked—no year of peaceful dwelling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao asked his ministers; Lu Kai answered, "Arms are the last resort; since the three kingdoms rose, war has never ceased.

manualTranslations.zh: 今彊敵新并巴蜀，有兼土之實，而遣使求親，欲息兵役，不可謂其求援於我。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the strong enemy has newly annexed Ba-Shu and has the substance of combining lands; yet it sends envoys seeking kinship, wishing to rest military service—it cannot be said that it seeks aid from us.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The northern power has just swallowed Ba-Shu and seeks peace by marriage—not because it needs our help.

manualTranslations.zh: 今敵形勢方彊，而欲徼幸求勝，未見其利也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now the enemy's form and momentum are just strong, yet wishing to rely on chance to seek victory—its profit is not seen."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To gamble on victory while they are strongest would bring no gain."

manualTranslations.zh: 車騎將軍劉纂曰：「天生五才，誰能去兵？
manualTranslations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Liu Zuan said: "Heaven produces the five talents—who can dispense with arms?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Liu Zuan said, "Heaven grants five talents—who can renounce war?

manualTranslations.zh: 譎詐相雄，有自來矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Deception and craft contend as heroes—this has existed from of old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rivalry through stratagem is as old as history.

manualTranslations.zh: 若其有闕，庸可棄乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If they have gaps, how can [we] abandon them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the enemy shows weakness, should we ignore it?

manualTranslations.zh: 宜遣閒諜，以觀其勢。」
manualTranslations.literal: It is fitting to send secret scouts to observe their momentum."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Send spies to probe their condition."

manualTranslations.zh: 皓陰納纂言，且以蜀新平，故不行，然遂自絕。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao secretly accepted Zuan's words, and because Shu was newly pacified, therefore did not act; yet thereupon he broke off relations on his own.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao secretly favored Liu Zuan's view but, with Shu just pacified, held off—yet still cut ties with Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 八月，所在言得大鼎，於是改年，大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month, everywhere reported obtaining great tripods; thereupon the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth month reports of great bronze tripods prompted a new reign title and amnesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 以陸凱爲左丞相，常侍萬彧爲右丞相。
manualTranslations.literal: Lu Kai was made left chancellor; Regular Attendant Wan Yu was made right chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Kai became left chancellor and Regular Attendant Wan Yu right chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 冬十月，永安山賊施但等聚衆數千人，《吳錄》曰：永安今武康縣也。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, bandits of Yong'an mountain Shi Dan and others gathered a host of several thousand; the Wu lu states: Yong'an is now Wukang county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In winter's tenth month Yong'an bandit Shi Dan rallied thousands; the Wu lu notes Yong'an is modern Wukang county.

manualTranslations.zh: 劫皓庶弟永安侯謙出烏程，取孫和陵上鼓吹曲蓋。
manualTranslations.literal: They seized Hao's common-born younger brother Marquis of Yong'an Qian and went out from Wucheng, taking the drum-and-pipe canopy from Sun He's tomb mound.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They kidnapped Sun Hao's younger brother Marquis of Yong'an Qian from Wucheng and stole the ceremonial canopy from Sun He's tomb.

manualTranslations.zh: 比至建業，衆萬餘人。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time they reached Jianye, the host exceeded ten thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their ranks swelled past ten thousand by the time they neared Jianye.

manualTranslations.zh: 丁固、諸葛靚逆之於牛屯，大戰，但等敗走。
manualTranslations.literal: Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing met them at Niutun; a great battle; Dan and the others were defeated and fled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing met them at Niutun and routed the rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 獲謙，謙自殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Qian was captured; Qian killed himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qian was captured and took his own life.

manualTranslations.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：初望氣者云荊州有王氣破揚州而建業宮不利，故皓徙武昌，遣使者發民掘荊州界大臣名家冢與山岡連者以厭之。
manualTranslations.literal: The Han Jin Chunqiu states: At the beginning a reader of qi said Jing province had royal qi that broke Yang province and that the Jianye palace was unpropitious; therefore Hao moved to Wuchang and sent envoys to mobilize the people to dig the tombs of great clans of Jing province's border connected with mountain ridges to suppress it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han Jin Chunqiu says geomancers claimed Jing's royal qi undermined Yang and Jianye's palace, so Sun Hao moved to Wuchang and ordered tombs of Jing nobles on mountain ridges desecrated to break the omen.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣聞但反，自以爲徙土得計也。
manualTranslations.literal: Having heard of Dan's rebellion, he himself considered that moving the earth had obtained the plan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Shi Dan rebelled Sun Hao decided the capital move had been prescient.

manualTranslations.zh: 使數百人鼓譟入建業，殺但妻子，云天子使荊州兵來破揚州賊，以厭前氣。
manualTranslations.literal: He sent several hundred men drumming and clamoring into Jianye, killing Dan's wife and children, saying the Son of Heaven sent Jing troops to break Yang bandits, to suppress the former qi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent hundreds of men into Jianye to massacre Dan's family, claiming imperial Jing troops had crushed Yang rebels to dispel the omen.

manualTranslations.zh: 分會稽爲東陽郡，分吳、丹楊爲吳興郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Kuaiji was divided into Dongyang commandery; Wu and Danyang were divided into Wuxing commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kuaiji was split into Dongyang commandery and Wu-Danyang into Wuxing commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓詔曰：「古者分土建國，所以襃賞賢能，廣樹藩屏。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao's edict stated: "In antiquity enfeoffment by land established states—thereby to praise and reward the worthy and able and broadly plant screens and shields.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's edict read, "Ancient enfeoffment rewarded merit and planted feudal shields for the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦毀五等爲三十六郡，漢室初興，闓立乃至百五，因事制宜，蓋無常數也。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin destroyed the five ranks into thirty-six commanderies; when the Han house first rose, [enfeoffments] opened and stood reaching even to one hundred five—according with affairs and making measures, there was basically no constant number.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin abolished the five ranks for thirty-six commanderies; Han created as many as one hundred five—forms shift with need.

manualTranslations.zh: 今吳郡陽羨、永安、餘杭、臨水及丹楊故鄣、安吉、原鄉、於潛諸縣，地勢水流之便，悉注烏程，旣宜立郡以鎮山越，且以藩衞明陵，奉承大祭，不亦可乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Now Wu commandery's Yangxian, Yong'an, Yuhang, Linshui and Danyang's former Zhang, Anji, Yuanxiang, Yuqian various counties—the convenience of terrain and water flow all pour into Wucheng; it is already fitting to establish a commandery to secure the mountain Yue, and moreover to screen and guard the bright tomb and attend the great sacrifices—is it not also fitting!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The counties around Wucheng—Yangxian, Yong'an, Yuhang, Linshui, Zhang, Anji, Yuanxiang, Yuqian—drain to Wucheng and should form a commandery to control mountain Yue, guard the imperial tomb, and supply the great sacrifices.

manualTranslations.zh: 其亟分此九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hasten to divide these nine counties into Wuxing commandery, administering from Wucheng."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Divide these nine counties into Wuxing commandery with its seat at Wucheng."

manualTranslations.zh: 以零陵北部爲邵陵郡。
manualTranslations.literal: The northern part of Lingling was made Shaoling commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Northern Lingling became Shaoling commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 十二月，皓還都建業，衞將軍滕牧留鎮武昌。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month Hao returned the capital to Jianye; General of the Guard Teng Mu remained to guard Wuchang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Sun Hao returned to Jianye, leaving General of the Guard Teng Mu at Wuchang.

items.acceptedSourceText: 元興元年264年八月，以上大將軍施績、大將軍丁奉爲左右大司馬，張布爲驃騎將軍，加侍中，諸增位班賞，一皆如舊。九月，貶太后爲景皇后，追謚父和曰文皇帝，尊母何爲太后。十月，封休太子𩅦爲豫章王，次子汝南王，次子梁王，次子陳王，立皇后滕氏。《江表傳》曰：皓初立，發優詔，恤士民，開倉廩，振貧乏，科出宮女以配無妻，禽獸擾於苑者皆放之。當時翕然稱爲明主。皓旣得志，麤暴驕盈，多忌諱，好酒色，大小失望。興、布竊悔之。或以譖皓，十一月，誅興、布。十二月，孫休葬定陵。封后父滕牧爲高密侯，《吳歷》曰：牧本名密，避丁密，改名牧，丁密避牧，改名爲固。舅何洪等三人皆列侯。是歲，魏置交阯太守之郡。晉文帝爲魏相國，遣昔吳壽春城降將徐紹、孫彧銜命齎書，陳事勢利害，以申喻皓。《漢晉春秋》載晉文王與皓書曰：「聖人稱有君臣然後有上下禮義，是故大必字小，小必事大，然後上下安服，羣生獲所。逮至末塗，純德旣毀，勦民之命，以爭彊於天下，違禮順之至理，則仁者弗由也。方今主上聖明，覆帱無外，僕備位宰輔，屬當國重。唯華夏乖殊，方隅圮裂，六十餘載，金革亟動，無年不戰，暴骸喪元，困悴罔定，每用悼心，坐以待旦。將欲止戈興仁，爲百姓請命，故分命偏師，平定蜀漢，役未經年，全軍獨克。于時猛將謀夫，朝臣庶士，咸以奉天時之宜，就旣征之軍，藉吞敵之勢，宜遂回旗東指，以臨吳境。舟師汎江，順流而下，陸軍南轅，取徑四郡，兼成都之械，漕巴漢之粟，然後以中軍整旅，三方雲會，未及浹辰，可使江表厎平，南夏順軌。然國朝深惟伐蜀之舉，雖有靜難之功，亦悼蜀民獨罹其害，戰於緜竹者，自元帥以下並受斬戮，伏尸蔽地，血流丹野。一之於前，猶追恨不忍，況重之於後乎？是故旋師案甲，思與南邦共全百姓之命。夫料力忖勢，度資量險，遠考古昔廢興之理，近鑒西蜀安危之効，隆德保祚，去危即順，屈己以寧四海者，仁哲之高致也；履危偷安，隕德覆祚，而不稱於後世者，非智者之所居也。今朝廷遣徐紹、孫彧獻書喻懷，若書御於前，必少留意，回慮革筭，結歡弭兵，共爲一家，惠矜吳會，施及中土，豈不泰哉！此昭心之大願也，敢不承受。若不獲命，則普天率土，期於大同，雖重干戈，固不獲已也。」甘露元年265年三月，皓遣使隨紹、彧報書曰：「知以高世之才，處宰輔之任，漸導之功，勤亦至矣。孤以不德，階承統緒，思與賢良共濟世道，而以壅隔未有所緣，嘉意允著，深用依依。今遣光祿大夫紀陟、五官中郎將弘璆宣明至懷。」《江表傳》曰：皓書兩頭言白，稱名言而不著姓。《吳錄》曰：陟字子上，丹楊人。初爲中書郎，孫峻使詰南陽王和，令其引分。陟密使令正辭自理，峻怒。陟懼，閉門不出。孫休時，父亮爲尚書令，而陟爲中書令，每朝會，詔以屏風隔其座。出爲豫章太守。干寶《晉紀》曰：陟、璆奉使如魏，入境而問諱，入國而問俗。壽春將王布示之馬射，旣而問之曰：「吳之君子亦能斯乎？」陟曰：「此軍人騎士肄業所及，士大夫君子未有爲之者矣。」布大慙。旣至，魏帝見之，使儐問曰：「來時吳王何如？」陟對曰：「來時皇帝臨軒，百寮陪位，御膳無恙。」晉文王饗之，百寮畢會，使儐者告曰：「某者安樂公也，某者匈奴單于也。」陟曰：「西主失土，爲君王所禮，位同三代，莫不感義，匈奴邊塞難羈之國，君王懷之，親在坐席，此誠威恩遠著。」又問：「吳之戍備幾何？」對曰：「自西陵以至江都，五千七百里。」又問曰：「道里甚遠，難爲堅固？」對曰：「疆界雖遠，而其險要必爭之地，不過數四，猶人雖有八尺之軀靡不受患，其護風寒亦數處耳。」文王善之，厚爲之禮。臣松之以爲人有八尺之體靡不受患，防護風寒豈唯數處？取譬若此，未足稱能。若曰譬如金城萬雉，所急防者四門而已。方陟此對，不猶愈乎！《吳錄》曰：皓以諸父與和相連及者，家屬皆徙東冶，唯陟以有密旨，特封子孚都亭侯。孚弟瞻，字思遠，入仕晉驃騎將軍。弘璆，曲阿人，弘咨之孫，權外甥也。璆後至中書令、太子少傅。紹行到濡須，召還殺之，徙其家屬建安，始有白紹稱美中國者故也。夏四月，蔣陵言甘露降，於是改年大赦。秋七月，皓逼殺景后朱氏，亡不在正殿，於苑中小屋治喪，衆知其非疾病，莫不痛切。又送休四子於吳小城，尋復追殺大者二人。九月，從西陵督步闡表，徙都武昌，御史大夫丁固、右將軍諸葛靚鎮建業。陟、璆至洛，遇晉文帝崩，十一月，乃遣還。皓至武昌，又大赦。以零陵南部爲始安郡，桂陽南部爲始興郡。十二月，晉受禪。寶鼎元年正月，遣大鴻臚張儼、五官中郎將丁忠弔祭晉文帝。及還，儼道病死。《吳錄》曰：儼字子節，吳人也。弱冠知名，歷顯位，以博聞多識，拜大鴻臚。使于晉，皓謂儼曰：「今南北通好，以君爲有出境之才，故相屈行。」對曰：「皇皇者華，蒙其榮耀，無古人延譽之美，磨厲鋒鍔，思不辱命。」旣至，車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、侍中荀勗等欲傲以所不知而不能屈。尚書僕射羊祜、尚書何楨並結縞帶之好。忠說皓曰：「北方守戰之具不設，弋陽可襲而取。」皓訪羣臣，鎮西大將軍陸凱曰：「夫兵不得已而用之耳，且三國鼎立已來，更相侵伐，無歲寧居。今彊敵新并巴蜀，有兼土之實，而遣使求親，欲息兵役，不可謂其求援於我。今敵形勢方彊，而欲徼幸求勝，未見其利也。」車騎將軍劉纂曰：「天生五才，誰能去兵？譎詐相雄，有自來矣。若其有闕，庸可棄乎？宜遣閒諜，以觀其勢。」皓陰納纂言，且以蜀新平，故不行，然遂自絕。八月，所在言得大鼎，於是改年，大赦。以陸凱爲左丞相，常侍萬彧爲右丞相。冬十月，永安山賊施但等聚衆數千人，《吳錄》曰：永安今武康縣也。劫皓庶弟永安侯謙出烏程，取孫和陵上鼓吹曲蓋。比至建業，衆萬餘人。丁固、諸葛靚逆之於牛屯，大戰，但等敗走。獲謙，謙自殺。《漢晉春秋》曰：初望氣者云荊州有王氣破揚州而建業宮不利，故皓徙武昌，遣使者發民掘荊州界大臣名家冢與山岡連者以厭之。旣聞但反，自以爲徙土得計也。使數百人鼓譟入建業，殺但妻子，云天子使荊州兵來破揚州賊，以厭前氣。分會稽爲東陽郡，分吳、丹楊爲吳興郡。皓詔曰：「古者分土建國，所以襃賞賢能，廣樹藩屏。秦毀五等爲三十六郡，漢室初興，闓立乃至百五，因事制宜，蓋無常數也。今吳郡陽羨、永安、餘杭、臨水及丹楊故鄣、安吉、原鄉、於潛諸縣，地勢水流之便，悉注烏程，旣宜立郡以鎮山越，且以藩衞明陵，奉承大祭，不亦可乎！其亟分此九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程。」以零陵北部爲邵陵郡。十二月，皓還都建業，衞將軍滕牧留鎮武昌。

sourceRange.text: 春《吳歷》曰：正月，爲權立廟，稱太祖廟。

localRange.text: 太平元年春〈《吳歷》曰：正月，爲權立廟，稱太祖廟。

sourceRange.text: 四年夏五月，大雨，水泉涌溢。秋八月，遣光祿大夫周弈、石偉巡行風俗，察將吏清濁，民所疾苦，爲黜陟之詔。《楚國先賢傳》曰：石偉字公操，南郡人。少好學，脩節不怠，介然獨立，有不可奪之志。舉茂才、賢良方正，皆不就。孫休即位，特徵偉，累遷至光祿勳。及皓即位，朝政昏亂，偉乃辭老耄痼疾乞身，就拜光祿大夫。吳平，建威將軍王戎親詣偉。太康二年，詔曰：「吳故光祿大夫石偉，秉志清白，皓首不渝，難處危亂，廉節可紀。年已過邁，不堪遠涉，其以偉爲議郎，加二千石秩，以終厥世。」偉遂陽狂及盲，不受晉爵。年八十三，太熙元年卒。九月，布山言白龍見。是歲，安吳民陳焦死，埋之，六日更生，穿土中出。

context.beforeSource: 《吳歷》曰：是歲得大鼎於建德縣。
context.afterSource: 五年春二月，白虎門北樓災。
context.beforeLocal: 〈《吳歷》曰：是歲得大鼎於建德縣。
context.afterLocal: 五年春二月，白虎門北樓災。

manualTranslations.zh: 四年夏五月，大雨，水泉涌溢。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the fourth year, great rain fell; springs and streams overflowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, summer's fifth month, torrential rains flooded springs and streams.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋八月，遣光祿大夫周弈、石偉巡行風俗，察將吏清濁，民所疾苦，爲黜陟之詔。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the court sent Household Counsellor Zhou Yi and Shi Wei to tour and inspect customs, examine whether generals and officials were pure or corrupt and what hardships the people suffered, with an edict for dismissal and promotion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn's eighth month Household Counsellor Zhou Yi and Shi Wei were sent to inspect local customs, judge officials' integrity, hear popular grievances, and recommend promotions and dismissals.

manualTranslations.zh: 《楚國先賢傳》曰：石偉字公操，南郡人。
manualTranslations.literal: The Chu Kingdom Xianxian Zhuan states: Wei, courtesy name Gongcao, was a Nan commandery man.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chu Kingdom Xianxian Zhuan records Shi Wei, courtesy Gongcao, from Nan commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 少好學，脩節不怠，介然獨立，有不可奪之志。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he loved learning; he cultivated conduct without slackening; upright and independent, he had a will that could not be wrested away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He loved learning from youth, lived uprightly, and could not be swayed.

manualTranslations.zh: 舉茂才、賢良方正，皆不就。
manualTranslations.literal: Recommended as flourishing talent and as worthy and upright, he all did not accept.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He declined nominations as flourishing talent and worthy-and-upright.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫休即位，特徵偉，累遷至光祿勳。
manualTranslations.literal: When Sun Xiu assumed the throne, Wei was specially summoned; he was repeatedly promoted to superintendent of the imperial household.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu specially summoned him and promoted him to superintendent of the imperial household.

manualTranslations.zh: 及皓即位，朝政昏亂，偉乃辭老耄痼疾乞身，就拜光祿大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: When Hao assumed the throne, court government was benighted and chaotic; Wei then resigned on grounds of old age and chronic illness begging his person; he was then appointed household counsellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took power and the court decayed, Shi Wei pleaded age and illness, accepting appointment as household counsellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 吳平，建威將軍王戎親詣偉。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wu was pacified, General Who Establishes Might Wang Rong personally visited Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Wu's fall General Who Establishes Might Wang Rong visited him in person.

manualTranslations.zh: 太康二年，詔曰：「吳故光祿大夫石偉，秉志清白，皓首不渝，難處危亂，廉節可紀。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Taikang, an edict stated: "Wu's former Household Counsellor Shi Wei, holding his will pure and white, white-haired without change, hard to be in peril and chaos—his integrity can be recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Taikang 2 an edict praised former Wu Household Counsellor Shi Wei for spotless integrity maintained through chaos.

manualTranslations.zh: 年已過邁，不堪遠涉，其以偉爲議郎，加二千石秩，以終厥世。」
manualTranslations.literal: His years already passed the threshold; he cannot bear long journeying; let Wei be made gentleman consultant with added rank of two thousand dan to end his generation."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Too aged to travel, he was named gentleman consultant at two-thousand-dan rank for life."

manualTranslations.zh: 偉遂陽狂及盲，不受晉爵。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei then feigned madness and blindness and did not accept Jin nobility.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shi Wei feigned madness and blindness and refused Jin honors.

manualTranslations.zh: 年八十三，太熙元年卒。
manualTranslations.literal: At age eighty-three, in the first year of Taixi, he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three in Taixi 1.

manualTranslations.zh: 九月，布山言白龍見。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month Bushan reported a white dragon appearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bushan reported a white dragon.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，安吳民陳焦死，埋之，六日更生，穿土中出。
manualTranslations.literal: This year Anwu commoner Chen Jiao died; after burial, on the sixth day he revived again, piercing out from within the earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Chen Jiao of Anwu was buried, revived on the sixth day, and clawed up through the soil.

sourceRange.text: 天璽元年276年，吳郡言臨平湖自漢末草穢壅塞，今更開通。長老相傳，此湖塞，天下亂，此湖開，天下平。又於湖邊得石函，中有小石，青白色，長四寸，廣二寸餘，刻上作皇帝字，於是改年，大赦。會稽太守車浚、湘東太守張詠不出筭緡，就在所斬之，徇首諸郡。《江表傳》曰：浚在公清忠，值郡荒旱，民無資糧，表求振貸。皓謂浚欲樹私恩，遣人梟首。又尚書熊睦見皓酷虐，微有所諫，皓使人以刀環撞殺之，身無完肌。秋八月，京下督孫楷降晉。鄱陽言歷陽山石文理成字，凡二十，云「楚九州渚，吳九州都，揚州士，作天子，四世治，太平始」。《江表傳》曰：歷陽縣有石山臨水，高百丈，其三十丈所，有七穿駢羅，穿中色黃赤，不與本體相似，俗相傳謂之石印。又云，石印封發，天下當太平。下有祠屋，巫祝言石印神有三郎。時歷陽長表上言石印發，皓遣使以太牢祭歷山。巫言，石印三郎說「天下方太平」。使者作高梯，上看印文，詐以朱書石作二十字，還以啟皓。皓大喜曰：「吳當爲九州作都、渚乎！從大皇帝逮孤四世矣，太平之主，非孤復誰？」重遣使，以印綬拜三郎爲王，又刻石立銘，襃贊靈德，以荅休祥。又吳興陽羨山有空石，長十餘丈，名曰石室，在所表爲大瑞。乃遣兼司徒董朝、兼太常周處至陽羨縣，封襌國山。明年改元，大赦，以恊石文。

context.beforeSource: 天冊元年，吳郡言掘地得銀，長一尺，廣三分，刻上有年月字，於是大赦，改年。
context.afterSource: 天紀元年夏，夏口督孫慎出江夏、汝南，燒略居民。

context.afterLocal: 天紀元年夏，夏口督孫慎出江夏、汝南，燒略居民。

manualTranslations.zh: 天璽元年276年，吳郡言臨平湖自漢末草穢壅塞，今更開通。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Tian Shi (276), Wu commandery reported that Linping Lake, since the end of Han overgrown and choked with weeds, was now again opened and connected.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Tian Shi 1 (276) Wu commandery reported Linping Lake, choked since Han's fall, had reopened.

manualTranslations.zh: 長老相傳，此湖塞，天下亂，此湖開，天下平。
manualTranslations.literal: The elders transmitted by tradition: when this lake is blocked, all under Heaven is chaotic; when this lake opens, all under Heaven is peaceful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Local tradition held: a blocked lake meant chaos; an open lake meant peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 又於湖邊得石函，中有小石，青白色，長四寸，廣二寸餘，刻上作皇帝字，於是改年，大赦。
manualTranslations.literal: Again at the lake shore a stone casket was obtained; inside was a small stone, blue-white in color, four cun long and a bit more than two cun wide; carved on top were the characters for emperor—thereupon the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A stone box found lakeside held a pale green tablet inscribed with the character for emperor, prompting a new reign title and amnesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 會稽太守車浚、湘東太守張詠不出筭緡，就在所斬之，徇首諸郡。
manualTranslations.literal: Kuaiji Administrator Che Jun and Xiangdong Administrator Zhang Yong did not issue the coin surtax; they were beheaded on the spot and their heads displayed through the commanderies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kuaiji governor Che Jun and Xiangdong governor Zhang Yong, refusing the coin levy, were executed on the spot and their heads displayed across the provinces.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：浚在公清忠，值郡荒旱，民無資糧，表求振貸。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Jun was public-spirited, pure, and loyal; encountering famine and drought in the commandery, the people had no resources or grain; he memorialized requesting relief loans.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Che Jun was incorruptible; during famine he petitioned for relief grain.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓謂浚欲樹私恩，遣人梟首。
manualTranslations.literal: Hao considered that Jun wished to plant private favor and sent men to display his head.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao accused him of currying favor and had him beheaded.

manualTranslations.zh: 又尚書熊睦見皓酷虐，微有所諫，皓使人以刀環撞殺之，身無完肌。
manualTranslations.literal: Again Master of Writing Xiong Mu, seeing Hao's cruelty and tyranny, subtly offered some remonstrance; Hao sent men to kill him by striking with a knife ring; his body had no whole flesh.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Xiong Mu, remonstrating against Sun Hao's cruelty, was beaten to death with a knife pommel until no flesh remained intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 秋八月，京下督孫楷降晉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Capital-area Supervisor Sun Kai surrendered to Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In autumn's eighth month capital-area supervisor Sun Kai defected to Jin.

manualTranslations.zh: 鄱陽言歷陽山石文理成字，凡二十，云「楚九州渚，吳九州都，揚州士，作天子，四世治，太平始」。
manualTranslations.literal: Poyang reported that on Liyang mountain the stone's grain patterns formed characters—in all twenty—saying: "Chu nine provinces islets, Wu nine provinces capital, Yang province gentry, makes Son of Heaven, four generations rule, great peace begins."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Poyang reported twenty characters naturally formed in Liyang rock: "Chu holds the islets of nine provinces, Wu the capital of nine provinces; a Yangzhou man becomes Son of Heaven; four reigns rule—great peace begins."

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：歷陽縣有石山臨水，高百丈，其三十丈所，有七穿駢羅，穿中色黃赤，不與本體相似，俗相傳謂之石印。
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Liyang county has a stone mountain facing the water, a hundred zhang high; at about thirty zhang there are seven perforations ranged side by side; within the perforations the color is yellow-red, not similar to the main body; popular tradition calls it the stone seal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan describes Liyang's hundred-zhang riverside cliff with seven yellow-red holes locals called the Stone Seal.

manualTranslations.zh: 又云，石印封發，天下當太平。
manualTranslations.literal: Again it is said: when the stone seal's seal breaks open, all under Heaven will be greatly peaceful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tradition also said when the Stone Seal opened, universal peace would follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 下有祠屋，巫祝言石印神有三郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Below there is a shrine house; shaman priests say the stone seal spirit has three lords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A shrine below housed shamans who claimed the spirit had three lords.

manualTranslations.zh: 時歷陽長表上言石印發，皓遣使以太牢祭歷山。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the Liyang chief memorialized upward that the stone seal had opened; Hao sent envoys with the great offering to sacrifice at Li mountain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Liyang magistrate reported the seal had opened, Sun Hao sent envoys with great sacrifices to Li mountain.

manualTranslations.zh: 巫言，石印三郎說「天下方太平」。
manualTranslations.literal: The shamans said the stone seal's three lords stated: "All under Heaven is just now greatly peaceful."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shamans declared the three lords announced, "The realm is entering great peace."

manualTranslations.zh: 使者作高梯，上看印文，詐以朱書石作二十字，還以啟皓。
manualTranslations.literal: The envoys made a high ladder, looked up at the seal text, falsely used cinnabar to write on stone twenty characters, returned and reported to Hao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Envoys climbed a ladder, forged twenty cinnabar characters on the stone, and reported back to Sun Hao.

manualTranslations.zh: 皓大喜曰：「吳當爲九州作都、渚乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Hao was greatly pleased and said: "Will Wu be made capital and islet of the nine provinces!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Hao rejoiced: "So Wu shall be capital of the nine provinces!

manualTranslations.zh: 從大皇帝逮孤四世矣，太平之主，非孤復誰？」
manualTranslations.literal: From the Great Emperor down to me, solitary, it is four generations; the lord of great peace—if not I, solitary, then who?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the Great Emperor to me is four generations—who but I could be the lord of great peace?"

manualTranslations.zh: 重遣使，以印綬拜三郎爲王，又刻石立銘，襃贊靈德，以荅休祥。
manualTranslations.literal: Again he sent envoys, with seal and sash enfeoffing the three lords as kings; again he carved stone and set up an inscription, praising and rewarding spiritual virtue, to answer the auspicious omen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to enfeoff the three lords as kings with seals and sashes, carved commemorative stone, and hailed the omen.

manualTranslations.zh: 又吳興陽羨山有空石，長十餘丈，名曰石室，在所表爲大瑞。
manualTranslations.literal: Again in Wuxing Yangxian mountain there was an empty stone more than ten zhang long, named the stone chamber; the place memorialized it as a great auspice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wuxing's Yangxian mountain held a hollow boulder over ten zhang long called the Stone Chamber, reported as a great omen.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃遣兼司徒董朝、兼太常周處至陽羨縣，封襌國山。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon [the court] sent Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing Dong Chao and Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhou Chu to Yangxian county to enfeoff and perform the feng rite at Tianshan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Concurrent Secretariat Director Dong Chao and Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhou Chu to Yangxian to perform the feng rite at Tianshan.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年改元，大赦，以恊石文。
manualTranslations.literal: The next year the era name was changed, a general amnesty proclaimed, to accord with the stone text.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following year brought a new reign title and amnesty to match the stone prophecy.

items.acceptedSourceText: 天璽元年276年，吳郡言臨平湖自漢末草穢壅塞，今更開通。長老相傳，此湖塞，天下亂，此湖開，天下平。又於湖邊得石函，中有小石，青白色，長四寸，廣二寸餘，刻上作皇帝字，於是改年，大赦。會稽太守車浚、湘東太守張詠不出筭緡，就在所斬之，徇首諸郡。《江表傳》曰：浚在公清忠，值郡荒旱，民無資糧，表求振貸。皓謂浚欲樹私恩，遣人梟首。又尚書熊睦見皓酷虐，微有所諫，皓使人以刀環撞殺之，身無完肌。秋八月，京下督孫楷降晉。鄱陽言歷陽山石文理成字，凡二十，云「楚九州渚，吳九州都，揚州士，作天子，四世治，太平始」。《江表傳》曰：歷陽縣有石山臨水，高百丈，其三十丈所，有七穿駢羅，穿中色黃赤，不與本體相似，俗相傳謂之石印。又云，石印封發，天下當太平。下有祠屋，巫祝言石印神有三郎。時歷陽長表上言石印發，皓遣使以太牢祭歷山。巫言，石印三郎說「天下方太平」。使者作高梯，上看印文，詐以朱書石作二十字，還以啟皓。皓大喜曰：「吳當爲九州作都、渚乎！從大皇帝逮孤四世矣，太平之主，非孤復誰？」重遣使，以印綬拜三郎爲王，又刻石立銘，襃贊靈德，以荅休祥。又吳興陽羨山有空石，長十餘丈，名曰石室，在所表爲大瑞。乃遣兼司徒董朝、兼太常周處至陽羨縣，封襌國山。明年改元，大赦，以恊石文。

sourceRange.text: 詔曰：「」二年春正月，震電。三月，備九卿官，詔曰：「」三年春三月，西陵言赤烏見。

localRange.text: 詔曰：「古者建國，教學爲先，所以道世治性，爲時養器也。自建興以來，時事多故，吏民頗以目前趨務，去本就末，不循古道。夫所尚不惇，則傷化敗俗。其案古置學官，立五經博士，核取應選，加其寵祿，科見吏之中及將吏子弟有志好者，各令就業。一歲課試，差其品第，加以位賞。使見之者樂其榮，聞之者羨其譽。以敦王化，以隆風俗。二年春正月，震電。三月，備九卿官，詔曰：「朕以不德，託于王公之上，夙夜戰戰，忘寢與食。今欲偃武脩文，以崇大化。推此之道，當由士民之贍，必須農桑。管子有言：『倉廩實，知禮節；衣食足，知榮辱。夫一夫不耕，有受其饑，一婦不織，有受其寒；饑寒並至而民不爲非者，未之有也。自頃年已來，州郡吏民及諸營兵，多違此業，皆浮船長江，賈作上下，良田漸廢，見穀日少，欲求大定，豈可得哉？亦由租入過重，農人利薄，使之然乎！今欲廣開田業，輕其賦稅，差科彊羸，課其田畝，務令優均，官私得所，使家給戶贍，足相供養，則愛身重命，不犯科法，然後刑罰不用，風俗可整。以羣僚之忠賢，若盡心於時，雖太古盛化，未可卒致，漢文升平，庶幾可及。及之則臣主俱榮，不及則損削侵辱，何可從容俯仰而已？諸卿尚書，可共咨度，務取便佳。田桑已至，不可後時。事定施行，稱朕意焉。三年春三月，西陵言赤烏見。

sourceRange.text: 孫休字子烈，權第六子。年十三，從中書郎射慈、郎中盛冲受學。太元二年252年正月，封琅邪王，居虎林。四月，權薨，休弟亮承統，諸葛恪秉政，不欲諸王在濵江兵馬之地，徙休於丹楊郡。太守李衡數以事侵休，休上書乞徙他郡，詔徙會稽。居數歲，夢乘龍上天，顧不見尾，覺而異之。孫亮廢，己未，孫綝使宗正孫楷與中書郎董朝迎休。休初聞問，意疑，楷、朝具述綝等所以奉迎本意，留一日二夜，遂發。十月戊寅，行至曲阿，有老公干休叩頭曰：「事乆變生，天下喁喁，願陛下速行。」休善之，是日進及布塞亭。武衞將軍恩行丞相事，率百僚以乘輿法駕迎於永昌亭，築宮，以武帳爲便殿，設御座。己卯，休至，望便殿止住，使孫楷先見恩。楷還，休乘輦進，羣臣再拜稱臣。休升便殿，謙不即御坐，止東廂。戶曹尚書前即階下讚奏，丞相奉璽符。休三讓，羣臣三請。休曰：「將相諸侯咸推寡人，寡人敢不承受璽符。」羣臣以次奉引，休就乘輿，百官陪位，綝以兵千人迎於半野，拜于道側，休下車荅拜。即日，御正殿，大赦，改元。是歲，於魏甘露三年258年也。永安元年258年冬十月壬午，詔曰：「夫襃德賞功，古今通義。其以大將軍綝爲丞相、荊州牧，增食五縣。武衞將軍恩爲御史大夫、衞將軍、中軍督，封縣侯。威遠將軍授爲右將軍、縣侯。偏將軍幹雜號將軍、亭侯。長水校尉張布輔導勤勞，以布爲輔義將軍，封永康侯。董朝親迎，封爲鄉侯。」又詔曰：「丹陽太守李衡，以往事之嫌，自拘有司。夫射鉤斬袪，在君爲君，遣衡還郡，勿令自疑。」《襄陽記》曰：衡字叔平，本襄陽卒家子也，漢末入吳爲武昌庶民。聞羊衜有人物之鑒，往干之，衜曰：「多事之世，尚書劇曹郎才也。」是時校事呂壹操弄權柄，大臣畏偪，莫有敢言，衜曰：「非李衡無能困之者。」遂共薦爲郎。權引見，衡口陳壹姦短數千言，權有愧色。數月，壹被誅，而衡大見顯擢。後常爲諸葛恪司馬，幹恪府事。恪被誅，求爲丹楊太守。時孫休在郡治，衡數以法繩之。妻習氏每諫衡，衡不從。會休立，衡憂懼，謂妻曰：「不用卿言，以至於此。」遂欲奔魏。妻曰：「不可。君本庶民耳，先帝相拔過重，旣數作無禮，而復逆自猜嫌，逃叛求活，以此北歸，何面見中國人乎？」衡曰：「計何所出？」妻曰：「琅邪王素好善慕名，方欲自顯於天下，終不以私嫌殺君明矣。可自囚詣獄，表列前失，顯求受罪。如此，乃當逆見優饒，非但直活而已。」衡從之，果得無患，又加威遠將軍，援以棨戟。衡每欲治家，妻輙不聽，後密遣客十人於武陵龍陽汎洲上作宅，種甘橘千株。臨死，勑兒曰：「汝母惡我治家，故窮如是。然吾州里有千頭木奴，不責汝衣食，歲上一匹絹，亦可足用耳。」衡亡後二十餘日，兒以白母，母曰：「此當是種甘橘也，汝家失十戶客來七八年，必汝父遣爲宅。汝父恒稱太史公言，『江陵千樹橘，當封君家』。吾荅曰：『且人患無德義，不患不富，若貴而能貧，方好耳，用此何爲！』」吳末，衡甘橘成，歲得絹數千匹，家道殷足。晉咸康中，其宅止枯樹猶在。己丑，封孫皓爲烏程侯，皓弟德錢唐侯，謙永安侯。《江表傳》曰：羣臣奏立皇后、太子，詔曰：「朕以寡德，奉承洪業，莅事日淺，恩澤未敷，加后妃之號，嗣子之位，非所急也。」有司又固請，休謙虛不許。

manualTranslations.zh: 孫休字子烈，權第六子。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Xiu, courtesy name Zilie, was Sun Quan's sixth son.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, whose courtesy name was Zilie, was the sixth son of Sun Quan.

manualTranslations.zh: 年十三，從中書郎射慈、郎中盛冲受學。
manualTranslations.literal: At age thirteen he studied under Palace Secretary She Ci and Gentleman Sheng Chong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At thirteen he took instruction from Palace Secretary She Ci and Gentleman Sheng Chong.

manualTranslations.zh: 太元二年252年正月，封琅邪王，居虎林。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taiyuan (252), he was enfeoffed as prince of Langye and resided at Hulin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taiyuan 2 (252) he was made prince of Langye and established his household at Hulin.

manualTranslations.zh: 四月，權薨，休弟亮承統，諸葛恪秉政，不欲諸王在濵江兵馬之地，徙休於丹楊郡。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month Sun Quan died; Xiu's younger brother Liang succeeded to the line; Zhuge Ke held government; not wishing princes to remain in riverside regions of troops and horses, he moved Xiu to Danyang commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan died that fourth month, Sun Liang took the throne under Zhuge Ke's regency. Ke refused to let imperial princes linger along the militarized Yangzi corridor and transferred Sun Xiu to Danyang commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 太守李衡數以事侵休，休上書乞徙他郡，詔徙會稽。
manualTranslations.literal: Administrator Li Heng repeatedly used affairs to encroach on Xiu; Xiu submitted a memorial begging transfer to another commandery; an edict moved him to Kuaiji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Governor Li Heng kept finding pretexts to harass him, so Sun Xiu petitioned for reassignment and was ordered to Kuaiji.

manualTranslations.zh: 居數歲，夢乘龍上天，顧不見尾，覺而異之。
manualTranslations.literal: After residing several years, he dreamed of riding a dragon up to heaven; looking back he could not see its tail; on waking he regarded it as strange.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Years later he dreamed he rode a dragon skyward yet could not see its tail when he glanced back—a omen that unsettled him when he woke.

manualTranslations.zh: 孫亮廢，己未，孫綝使宗正孫楷與中書郎董朝迎休。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Liang was deposed; on jiwei, Sun Lin sent Director of the Imperial Clan Sun Kai and Palace Secretary Dong Chao to welcome Xiu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Sun Liang's deposition, on jiwei Sun Lin dispatched Imperial Clan Director Sun Kai and Palace Secretary Dong Chao to escort Sun Xiu to the capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 休初聞問，意疑，楷、朝具述綝等所以奉迎本意，留一日二夜，遂發。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiu first heard the inquiry he was suspicious in mind; Kai and Chao fully set forth Lin and the others' purpose in welcoming him; he stayed one day and two nights, then set out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was wary at first, but Kai and Chao explained the full rationale for the summons; he waited a day and two nights, then departed.

manualTranslations.zh: 十月戊寅，行至曲阿，有老公干休叩頭曰：「事乆變生，天下喁喁，願陛下速行。」
manualTranslations.literal: On the tenth month, day wuyin, traveling as far as Qu'e, an old man intercepted Xiu and kowtowed, saying: "Matters long delayed breed change; all under Heaven murmurs—may Your Majesty hasten on."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the tenth month, nearing Qu'e, an old man threw himself before Sun Xiu and kowtowed: "Delay invites upheaval—the realm is restless. Hurry, Your Majesty!"

manualTranslations.zh: 休善之，是日進及布塞亭。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu approved of this; that day he advanced as far as Busei pavilion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu took the warning to heart and pushed on that same day to Busei pavilion.

manualTranslations.zh: 武衞將軍恩行丞相事，率百僚以乘輿法駕迎於永昌亭，築宮，以武帳爲便殿，設御座。
manualTranslations.literal: General of the Martial Guard En acted as chancellor, leading the hundred officials with the imperial carriage and full regalia to welcome him at Yongchang pavilion; they built a palace, using a military tent as the convenience hall, and set up the imperial seat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Sun En, acting chancellor, led the bureaucracy with the imperial carriage and full regalia to receive him at Yongchang pavilion, erecting a camp palace with a military tent as provisional hall and installing the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 己卯，休至，望便殿止住，使孫楷先見恩。
manualTranslations.literal: On jimao Xiu arrived, gazed at the convenience hall and halted; he sent Sun Kai first to see En.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jimao Sun Xiu arrived, paused before the tent-hall, and sent Sun Kai ahead to notify Sun En.

manualTranslations.zh: 楷還，休乘輦進，羣臣再拜稱臣。
manualTranslations.literal: Kai returned; Xiu entered in the imperial carriage; the host of ministers twice bowed and styled themselves subjects.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Kai returned, Sun Xiu entered in the imperial carriage while the assembled ministers bowed twice and hailed him as sovereign.

manualTranslations.zh: 休升便殿，謙不即御坐，止東廂。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu ascended the convenience hall, modestly not immediately taking the imperial seat, stopping in the east wing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He mounted the tent-hall but refused the throne at once, standing aside in the east wing.

manualTranslations.zh: 戶曹尚書前即階下讚奏，丞相奉璽符。
manualTranslations.literal: The director of the household bureau advanced before the steps and intoned the presentation; the chancellor bore the seal and tally.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Director of the Household Bureau stepped to the foot of the stairs to chant the investiture; the chancellor presented the imperial seal and tally.

manualTranslations.zh: 休三讓，羣臣三請。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu thrice declined; the host of ministers thrice requested.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu declined three times; the ministers pressed him three times.

manualTranslations.zh: 休曰：「將相諸侯咸推寡人，寡人敢不承受璽符。」
manualTranslations.literal: Xiu said: "Generals, ministers, and feudal lords all push upon me—how dare I not receive the seal and tally?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu said, "When generals, ministers, and feudal lords all urge me on, how can I refuse the seal and tally?"

manualTranslations.zh: 羣臣以次奉引，休就乘輿，百官陪位，綝以兵千人迎於半野，拜于道側，休下車荅拜。
manualTranslations.literal: The host of ministers in order led and guided him; Xiu took the imperial carriage; the hundred officials attended in place; Lin with a thousand troops welcomed him in the half-wilds, bowing at the roadside; Xiu descended from the carriage and returned the bow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ministers guided him to the carriage; officials took their stations; Sun Lin met him midway with a thousand troops and bowed from the roadside—Sun Xiu stepped down to bow in return.

manualTranslations.zh: 即日，御正殿，大赦，改元。
manualTranslations.literal: That same day he took the main hall, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That same day he entered the main palace, declared a general amnesty, and proclaimed a new reign title.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，於魏甘露三年258年也。
manualTranslations.literal: This year was, in Wei, the third year of Ganlu (258).
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On Wei's calendar the year was the third of Ganlu (258).

manualTranslations.zh: 永安元年258年冬十月壬午，詔曰：「夫襃德賞功，古今通義。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of winter of the first year of Yong'an (258), day renwu, an edict stated: "To praise virtue and reward merit is the universal principle of antiquity and the present."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On renwu in the tenth month of winter, Yong'an 1 (258), an edict declared: "Honoring merit and rewarding service is the constant law of every age."

manualTranslations.zh: 其以大將軍綝爲丞相、荊州牧，增食五縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Let Grand General Lin be made chancellor and governor of Jing province, with an added fief of five counties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand General Sun Lin is appointed chancellor and governor of Jing province, with five additional counties added to his fief.

manualTranslations.zh: 武衞將軍恩爲御史大夫、衞將軍、中軍督，封縣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: General of the Martial Guard En is made imperial counselor, general of the guard, and director of the central army, enfeoffed as a district marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General of the Martial Guard Sun En becomes imperial counselor, general of the guard, and director of the central army, and is enfeoffed as district marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 威遠將軍授爲右將軍、縣侯。
manualTranslations.literal: General Who Manifests Distant Might Shou is made right general and district marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: General Who Manifests Distant Might Sun Shou is named right general and district marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 偏將軍幹雜號將軍、亭侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Adjutant General Gan is made miscellaneous-numbered general and precinct marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Adjutant General Sun Gan is promoted to miscellaneous-numbered general and precinct marquis.

manualTranslations.zh: 長水校尉張布輔導勤勞，以布爲輔義將軍，封永康侯。
manualTranslations.literal: Colonel of the Chang River Zhang Bu guided and assisted with diligence and toil; Bu is made general who assists righteousness and enfeoffed as marquis of Yongkang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Chang River Zhang Bu, who guided the succession with tireless loyalty, is made general who assists righteousness and enfeoffed as marquis of Yongkang.

manualTranslations.zh: 董朝親迎，封爲鄉侯。」
manualTranslations.literal: Dong Chao personally welcomed [me]; he is enfeoffed as a township marquis."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dong Chao, who came in person to escort me, is enfeoffed as township marquis."

manualTranslations.zh: 又詔曰：「丹陽太守李衡，以往事之嫌，自拘有司。
manualTranslations.literal: Another edict stated: "Danyang Administrator Li Heng, because of suspicions over past affairs, has confined himself before the authorities.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A second edict ran: "Danyang Administrator Li Heng, troubled by old grievances, has turned himself in to the magistrates.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫射鉤斬袪，在君爲君，遣衡還郡，勿令自疑。」
manualTranslations.literal: Shooting the hook and cutting the hem—in serving one's lord one serves one's lord; send Heng back to his commandery and do not let him doubt himself."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, whoever holds the lord's hook or hem serves that lord—send Li Heng back to his post and put his fears to rest."

manualTranslations.zh: 《襄陽記》曰：衡字叔平，本襄陽卒家子也，漢末入吳爲武昌庶民。
manualTranslations.literal: The Xiangyang Ji states: Heng, courtesy name Shuping, was originally the son of a conscript household of Xiangyang; at the end of Han he entered Wu and became a commoner of Wuchang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Ji records that Li Heng, courtesy name Shuping, came from a military household in Xiangyang and drifted into Wu at the end of Han as an ordinary resident of Wuchang.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞羊衜有人物之鑒，往干之，衜曰：「多事之世，尚書劇曹郎才也。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing that Yang Yi had discernment of men's qualities, he went to seek him; Yi said: "In a time of many affairs, he has the talent of an intendant of the intense bureau of the Masters of Writing."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Learning that Yang Yi was famed for judging character, Li Heng sought him out; Yang Yi said, "In turbulent times this man has the makings of an intendant in the Secretariat's busiest office."

manualTranslations.zh: 是時校事呂壹操弄權柄，大臣畏偪，莫有敢言，衜曰：「非李衡無能困之者。」
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the investigator Lü Yi manipulated the handle of power; great ministers feared coercion and none dared speak; Yi said: "None but Li Heng can corner him."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Investigator Lü Yi then monopolized power and terrified the court into silence until Yang Yi declared, "Only Li Heng can bring him down."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂共薦爲郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon they jointly recommended him as gentleman.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They jointly recommended Li Heng for a secretariat post.

manualTranslations.zh: 權引見，衡口陳壹姦短數千言，權有愧色。
manualTranslations.literal: Sun Quan summoned him for an audience; Heng orally set forth Yi's wicked shortcomings in several thousand words; Sun Quan showed a ashamed countenance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received him and listened as Li Heng denounced Lü Yi's crimes at length, leaving the emperor visibly ashamed.

manualTranslations.zh: 數月，壹被誅，而衡大見顯擢。
manualTranslations.literal: Several months later Yi was executed, and Heng was greatly advanced and promoted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within months Lü Yi was executed and Li Heng rocketed up the ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 後常爲諸葛恪司馬，幹恪府事。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he often served as Zhuge Ke's marshal and managed Ke's headquarters affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later served as Zhuge Ke's chief of staff and ran the regent's headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 恪被誅，求爲丹楊太守。
manualTranslations.literal: When Ke was executed, he requested to be administrator of Danyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Ke's execution he sought appointment as governor of Danyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 時孫休在郡治，衡數以法繩之。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Sun Xiu was in the commandery seat; Heng repeatedly bound him with the law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was then living in the commandery capital, and Li Heng repeatedly cited regulations against him.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻習氏每諫衡，衡不從。
manualTranslations.literal: His wife Lady Xi often remonstrated with Heng; Heng did not follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Xi, pleaded with him to relent; he refused.

manualTranslations.zh: 會休立，衡憂懼，謂妻曰：「不用卿言，以至於此。」
manualTranslations.literal: When Xiu was established, Heng was anxious and fearful; he said to his wife: "I did not use your words and have come to this."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Li Heng was terrified and told his wife, "You warned me, and now look."

manualTranslations.zh: 遂欲奔魏。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he wished to flee to Wei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He prepared to defect north to Wei.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻曰：「不可。
manualTranslations.literal: His wife said: "You must not.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His wife said, "You cannot.

manualTranslations.zh: 君本庶民耳，先帝相拔過重，旣數作無禮，而復逆自猜嫌，逃叛求活，以此北歸，何面見中國人乎？」
manualTranslations.literal: You were originally a commoner; the late emperor elevated you beyond measure; having repeatedly acted without propriety, yet again turning to suspicion on your own account, fleeing in rebellion to seek life—returning north thus, with what face would you see the people of the Central States?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You were a commoner whom the late emperor raised too high; you already insulted him repeatedly, and now you would flee in guilty panic—what face could you show the Central Plains?"

manualTranslations.zh: 衡曰：「計何所出？」
manualTranslations.literal: Heng said: "What plan do you propose?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Heng asked, "What course do you advise?"

manualTranslations.zh: 妻曰：「琅邪王素好善慕名，方欲自顯於天下，終不以私嫌殺君明矣。
manualTranslations.literal: His wife said: "The prince of Langye has always loved goodness and prized reputation; he is just now wishing to display himself to all under Heaven—he will certainly not kill you over a private grudge; this is clear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She answered, "The prince of Langye loves virtue and craves a good name; he wants the realm to see him as magnanimous and will never execute you over a private quarrel.

manualTranslations.zh: 可自囚詣獄，表列前失，顯求受罪。
manualTranslations.literal: You can imprison yourself and go to jail, set forth in a memorial your former faults, and openly request punishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Turn yourself in, list your offenses in a memorial, and beg for punishment.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此，乃當逆見優饒，非但直活而已。」
manualTranslations.literal: Thus you will instead meet with generous treatment—not merely escape with your life."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do that and he will treat you with favor—not merely spare your life."

manualTranslations.zh: 衡從之，果得無患，又加威遠將軍，援以棨戟。
manualTranslations.literal: Heng followed this; indeed he suffered no trouble, and was further made General Who Manifests Distant Might, presented with halberds of office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Heng followed her counsel, escaped harm, was even promoted to General Who Manifests Distant Might, and received ceremonial halberds.

manualTranslations.zh: 衡每欲治家，妻輙不聽，後密遣客十人於武陵龍陽汎洲上作宅，種甘橘千株。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever Heng wished to manage the household, his wife always would not listen; later he secretly sent ten retainers to Longyang islet on the Fan River in Wuling to build a residence and plant a thousand sweet-orange trees.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever he tried to build up the family estate his wife blocked him; instead he secretly sent ten retainers to Longyang islet on the Fan River in Wuling to build a house and plant a thousand sweet-orange trees.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨死，勑兒曰：「汝母惡我治家，故窮如是。
manualTranslations.literal: Facing death, he charged his sons: "Your mother dislikes my managing the household—therefore we are poor like this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his sons, "Your mother hated my household management, so we ended poor.

manualTranslations.zh: 然吾州里有千頭木奴，不責汝衣食，歲上一匹絹，亦可足用耳。」
manualTranslations.literal: Yet in our district there are a thousand-headed wooden slaves; they will not demand food and clothing from you; each year they yield one bolt of silk—that can also suffice."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But I left you a thousand wooden slaves in the district—they need no food or clothes and pay one bolt of silk a year, enough to live on."

manualTranslations.zh: 衡亡後二十餘日，兒以白母，母曰：「此當是種甘橘也，汝家失十戶客來七八年，必汝父遣爲宅。
manualTranslations.literal: More than twenty days after Heng's death, the sons reported this to the mother; the mother said: "This must be planting sweet oranges; your household lost ten retainers who came seven or eight years ago—they must be the residence your father sent them to build.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Twenty-odd days after Li Heng died the sons told their mother, who said, "That can only be the orange grove—remember the ten missing retainers of seven or eight years ago? Your father sent them to build that estate.

manualTranslations.zh: 汝父恒稱太史公言，『江陵千樹橘，當封君家』。
manualTranslations.literal: Your father always cited Master Taishi's words: 'A thousand orange trees at Jiangling will ennoble your clan.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He always quoted Sima Qian: 'A thousand orange trees at Jiangling will make your house noble.'

manualTranslations.zh: 吾荅曰：『且人患無德義，不患不富，若貴而能貧，方好耳，用此何爲！』」
manualTranslations.literal: I answered: 'Yet people worry over lacking virtue and righteousness, not over lacking wealth; if noble yet able to be poor, that is best—what use is this!'"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I replied, 'Men fear want of virtue, not want of wealth; better to be honored yet poor—what need of that!'"

manualTranslations.zh: 吳末，衡甘橘成，歲得絹數千匹，家道殷足。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Wu, Heng's sweet oranges matured; each year they yielded several thousand bolts of silk; the family's condition was ample.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By Wu's final years the grove bore fruit worth thousands of bolts of silk yearly and the family grew prosperous.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉咸康中，其宅止枯樹猶在。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Xian Kang era of Jin, at his residence only the withered trees still remained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Jin's Xian Kang era only the dead trees still stood at the old homestead.

manualTranslations.zh: 己丑，封孫皓爲烏程侯，皓弟德錢唐侯，謙永安侯。
manualTranslations.literal: On jichou Sun Hao was enfeoffed as marquis of Wucheng; Hao's younger brother De as marquis of Qiantang; Qian as marquis of Yong'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On jichou Sun Hao was enfeoffed as marquis of Wucheng, his brother De as marquis of Qiantang, and Qian as marquis of Yong'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 《江表傳》曰：羣臣奏立皇后、太子，詔曰：「朕以寡德，奉承洪業，莅事日淺，恩澤未敷，加后妃之號，嗣子之位，非所急也。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: The host of ministers memorialized to establish an empress and crown prince; an edict stated: "We, with meager virtue, inherit the great enterprise; our days in office are shallow and grace has not yet spread—adding titles of empress and consorts and the position of heir is not what is urgent."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan records that ministers urged him to name an empress and heir; Sun Xiu replied, "My virtue is slight and my reign young—honors for consorts and an heir can wait."

manualTranslations.zh: 有司又固請，休謙虛不許。
manualTranslations.literal: The responsible officials again firmly requested; Xiu modestly declined and did not consent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When officials pressed again, Sun Xiu modestly refused.

items.acceptedSourceText: 孫休字子烈，權第六子。年十三，從中書郎射慈、郎中盛冲受學。太元二年252年正月，封琅邪王，居虎林。四月，權薨，休弟亮承統，諸葛恪秉政，不欲諸王在濵江兵馬之地，徙休於丹楊郡。太守李衡數以事侵休，休上書乞徙他郡，詔徙會稽。居數歲，夢乘龍上天，顧不見尾，覺而異之。孫亮廢，己未，孫綝使宗正孫楷與中書郎董朝迎休。休初聞問，意疑，楷、朝具述綝等所以奉迎本意，留一日二夜，遂發。十月戊寅，行至曲阿，有老公干休叩頭曰：「事乆變生，天下喁喁，願陛下速行。」休善之，是日進及布塞亭。武衞將軍恩行丞相事，率百僚以乘輿法駕迎於永昌亭，築宮，以武帳爲便殿，設御座。己卯，休至，望便殿止住，使孫楷先見恩。楷還，休乘輦進，羣臣再拜稱臣。休升便殿，謙不即御坐，止東廂。戶曹尚書前即階下讚奏，丞相奉璽符。休三讓，羣臣三請。休曰：「將相諸侯咸推寡人，寡人敢不承受璽符。」羣臣以次奉引，休就乘輿，百官陪位，綝以兵千人迎於半野，拜于道側，休下車荅拜。即日，御正殿，大赦，改元。是歲，於魏甘露三年258年也。永安元年258年冬十月壬午，詔曰：「夫襃德賞功，古今通義。其以大將軍綝爲丞相、荊州牧，增食五縣。武衞將軍恩爲御史大夫、衞將軍、中軍督，封縣侯。威遠將軍授爲右將軍、縣侯。偏將軍幹雜號將軍、亭侯。長水校尉張布輔導勤勞，以布爲輔義將軍，封永康侯。董朝親迎，封爲鄉侯。」又詔曰：「丹陽太守李衡，以往事之嫌，自拘有司。夫射鉤斬袪，在君爲君，遣衡還郡，勿令自疑。」《襄陽記》曰：衡字叔平，本襄陽卒家子也，漢末入吳爲武昌庶民。聞羊衜有人物之鑒，往干之，衜曰：「多事之世，尚書劇曹郎才也。」是時校事呂壹操弄權柄，大臣畏偪，莫有敢言，衜曰：「非李衡無能困之者。」遂共薦爲郎。權引見，衡口陳壹姦短數千言，權有愧色。數月，壹被誅，而衡大見顯擢。後常爲諸葛恪司馬，幹恪府事。恪被誅，求爲丹楊太守。時孫休在郡治，衡數以法繩之。妻習氏每諫衡，衡不從。會休立，衡憂懼，謂妻曰：「不用卿言，以至於此。」遂欲奔魏。妻曰：「不可。君本庶民耳，先帝相拔過重，旣數作無禮，而復逆自猜嫌，逃叛求活，以此北歸，何面見中國人乎？」衡曰：「計何所出？」妻曰：「琅邪王素好善慕名，方欲自顯於天下，終不以私嫌殺君明矣。可自囚詣獄，表列前失，顯求受罪。如此，乃當逆見優饒，非但直活而已。」衡從之，果得無患，又加威遠將軍，援以棨戟。衡每欲治家，妻輙不聽，後密遣客十人於武陵龍陽汎洲上作宅，種甘橘千株。臨死，勑兒曰：「汝母惡我治家，故窮如是。然吾州里有千頭木奴，不責汝衣食，歲上一匹絹，亦可足用耳。」衡亡後二十餘日，兒以白母，母曰：「此當是種甘橘也，汝家失十戶客來七八年，必汝父遣爲宅。汝父恒稱太史公言，『江陵千樹橘，當封君家』。吾荅曰：『且人患無德義，不患不富，若貴而能貧，方好耳，用此何爲！』」吳末，衡甘橘成，歲得絹數千匹，家道殷足。晉咸康中，其宅止枯樹猶在。己丑，封孫皓爲烏程侯，皓弟德錢唐侯，謙永安侯。《江表傳》曰：羣臣奏立皇后、太子，詔曰：「朕以寡德，奉承洪業，莅事日淺，恩澤未敷，加后妃之號，嗣子之位，非所急也。」有司又固請，休謙虛不許。

sourceRange.text: 春正月，立子瑾爲太子，及淮陽、東平王。

localRange.text: 建衡元年春正月，立子瑾爲太子，及淮陽、東平王。

sourceRange.text: 《吳錄》載休詔曰：「」臣松之以爲傳稱「名以制義，義以出禮，禮以體政，政以正民。

localRange.text: 〈《吳錄》載休詔曰：「人之有名，以相紀別，長爲作字，憚其名耳。禮，名子欲令難犯易避，五十稱伯仲，古或一字。今人競作好名好字，又令相配，所行不副，此瞽字伯明者也，孤常哂之。或師友父兄所作，或自己爲；師友尚可，父兄猶非，自爲最不謙。孤今爲四男作名字：太子名𩅦，𩅦音如『湖水灣澳』之灣，字莔，莔音如『迄今』之迄；次子名𩃙，𩃙音如『兕觥』之觥，字𧟨，𧟨音如『玄礥首』之礥；次子名壾，壾音如『草莽』之莽，字昷，昷音如『舉物』之舉；次子名𠅬，𠅬音如『襃衣下寬大』之襃，字㷏，㷏音如『有所擁持』之擁。此都不與世所用者同，故鈔舊文會合作之。夫書八體損益，因事而生，今造此名字，旣不相配，又字但一，庶易棄避，其普告天下，使咸聞知。臣松之以爲傳稱「名以制義，義以出禮，禮以體政，政以正民。

context.beforeSource: 戊子，立子𩅦爲太子，大赦。
context.afterSource: 是以政成而民聽，易則生亂」。
